### Out-of-band fix: cold-start retry gave up at ~101s even though the real budget was ~220s (urgent live-bug report, between rounds 399 and 400)

**Not a numbered autonomous round.** שלומי sent a direct message mid-session ("מעירים את השרת זה באג כל הזמן זה מופיע והאפ לא עובד בכלל" -- "waking the server, this bug keeps appearing, the app doesn't work at all") -- a genuine, live, reported failure, so per the Routine's own standing rule this took absolute priority over the hourly autonomous cycle and was handled immediately, out of sequence.

**Investigation**: the live Render URL isn't reachable from this sandbox's network policy, so this was pure code review, same constraint round 163 worked under. Read `wakeRetry.ts`'s `fetchWithWakeRetry` and confirmed `DEFAULT_DELAYS_MS` sums to exactly 101,000ms (`3000+5000+8000+12000+18000+25000+30000`). Read `api.ts`'s `fetchApi` and confirmed it always passes its own `AbortController`'s signal into `fetchWithWakeRetry`, with that controller's timer set to `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` = 220,000ms. The bug: the retry loop's `if (attempt >= delays.length) throw err;` check fires the moment the fixed 7-entry array is exhausted, regardless of whether the caller's own signal has fired yet -- so the *real* ceiling the caller negotiated (220s) was never actually used past 101s of it. A cold start landing between 101s and 220s -- entirely plausible now, since the server has grown substantially since round 163 added this 101s figure (real auth, the multi-agent build pipeline, WhatsApp/baileys, Business Twin, codegen) -- would throw a hard `NETWORK_ERROR` with over 100s of legitimately-available budget still sitting unused.

**Why this matches her exact report despite round 163 already widening the budget once**: round 163's own fix doubled the retry budget from ~49s to ~101s and added a dedicated test enforcing `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS > retry budget + 60s Anthropic call + 30s margin` -- but that test only ever checked the *numbers* were consistent with each other, never that the retry loop actually *used* the full ceiling it was handed. The structural gap (a fixed small array silently becoming the real ceiling, with the larger negotiated budget sitting unused) was never closed; it was only given enough headroom that it took this long to resurface as the server grew.

**The fix**: `fetchWithWakeRetry` now treats `DEFAULT_DELAYS_MS` as a backoff *shape*, not a hard ceiling. Once the array is exhausted, if the caller supplied its own `AbortSignal` (every real call through `api.ts` does), the loop keeps retrying using the array's last delay (30s), repeated, until that signal itself fires -- so `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`'s full 220s is what actually bounds retrying, not the smaller 101s sub-budget. A caller with no signal at all still throws once the array is exhausted (per the pre-existing test for that case), since nothing else would ever stop it. Updated `fetchApi`'s own doc comment in `api.ts` to describe this corrected relationship.

**codegen.ts (exported standalone app)**: checked before assuming anything needed porting (the round-384 lesson) -- confirmed via grep that `codegen.ts` has no `wakeRetry`/`fetchWithWakeRetry`/`waking`/cold-start equivalent at all, so there's nothing to port this into.

**Tests**: two new tests in `wakeRetry.test.ts`. One proves retries continue past a deliberately short 2-entry `delaysMs` array (failing 3 times, succeeding on the 4th call) when a non-aborted `AbortSignal` is present, and that the 3rd retry reuses the array's own last delay. A companion test proves the extended retrying still actually *stops* once that signal fires mid-retry, so "keeps retrying" doesn't silently become "retries forever." All five pre-existing `wakeRetry.test.ts` tests pass completely unchanged.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both changed implementation files (`wakeRetry.ts`, `api.ts`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted both to HEAD (keeping the two new/updated tests). The predicted failure occurred exactly: the new "keeps retrying past the array" test failed with the old code's `TypeError("Load failed")` rethrown right at the array boundary (3rd call), instead of succeeding on the 4th call as the fix guarantees. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full build and both affected workspaces' full suites clean.

Full suite green: **780 tests** in `@forge/web` (+2 new), **383 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged, confirmed unaffected), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed immediately as its own commit (`d9171b4`) rather than waiting for the next hourly round's usual batching, given the urgency of a live, reported failure -- matching round 163's own precedent for exactly this situation.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed, but the standing round-114 keep-alive/default-branch issue remains open and unresolved -- the app will continue cold-starting on every single visit (no keep-alive ping can run) until that's fixed. This change gives a slow cold start a real chance to actually finish within the budget already negotiated; it does not make cold starts faster or less frequent. Reported honestly to שלומי with that exact caveat, matching round 163's own precedent for not overstating a mitigation as a cure.

### Round 400: a boolean field could be grouped by but never filtered to just its true (or false) rows

**The survey**: a fresh Explore general-survey, primed with the full closed-topics list through round 399 and the out-of-band `wakeRetry.ts` fix, plus the standing "sibling-consumer-gap" pattern (rounds 395-398: when a shared predicate or data structure widens for one consumer, check whether a sibling consumer built from the same original predicate widened to match). The subagent's candidate: `entityFormatting.ts`'s `isGroupableField` treats `enum` and `boolean` fields as the same "small fixed value space" category for table grouping, but `EntityPanel.tsx`'s per-field filter dropdown only offered enum fields.

**Independent verification**: read `entityFormatting.ts` directly and confirmed `isGroupableField` (used for the group-by control) accepts both `enum` and `boolean`, while `findFilterableEnumFields` (used for the filter dropdown, extracted in round 286 from `findBoardField`'s Kanban-column predicate) only accepts `enum`. Read `EntityPanel.tsx`'s toolbar and confirmed it calls `findFilterableEnumFields`, not `isGroupableField`, to build the filter dropdowns, and that the filter-apply logic itself (`Object.entries(fieldFilters).every(...) => !value || String(r[fieldName] ?? "") === value`) already works unchanged for a stringified `"true"`/`"false"` value -- only the dropdown's option list was missing boolean fields entirely. Read round 286's own roadmap entry and confirmed `findFilterableEnumFields`'s enum-only scope was deliberately copied from `findBoardField`'s Kanban-grouping needs ("a board still groups by exactly one field... inherent to what a board is"), not from `isGroupableField`'s broader scope -- so this is a genuine, unintentional gap, not a documented design boundary.

**Why this wasn't already closed**: `findFilterableEnumFields` is also used internally by `findBoardField` for Kanban column picking, which must stay enum-only by design. Widening `findFilterableEnumFields` itself to include booleans would risk a boolean field being auto-picked for Kanban board grouping -- an unrelated, unrequested behavior change to a different consumer of the same function.

**Reachable through real UI usage**: any entity with a boolean field (e.g. `IsUrgent`, `IsBillable`) could be grouped by that field in the table view, but a person wanting to narrow the table down to just the `true` (or just the `false`) rows had no filter control to do it with -- the free-text search box matches every field as a substring match, not an exact value, so it can't substitute.

**The fix**: added a new function, `findFilterableFields`, that unions `findFilterableEnumFields`'s own enum fields with every boolean field, leaving `findFilterableEnumFields` itself and its Kanban-picking dependent (`findBoardField`) completely untouched. `EntityPanel.tsx`'s toolbar now calls `findFilterableFields` and renders a `Yes`/`No` option pair for a boolean field's dropdown instead of raw `enumValues`/`enumLabels` (which a boolean field has neither of).

**codegen.ts (exported standalone app)**: checked before assuming this needed porting (the round-384 lesson) -- confirmed via grep that `codegen.ts`'s embedded plain-JS template has its own copy of `findFilterableEnumFields` and the same toolbar filter-dropdown JSX, so it does need porting. Added the identical `findFilterableFields` function and the same boolean branch to the toolbar JSX, using hardcoded `"Yes"`/`"No"` strings (matching the existing convention elsewhere in `codegen.ts`, e.g. `groupRecordsByField`'s own `label: "Yes"`/`label: "No"`). Build verified clean (no nested-backtick esbuild errors in the embedded template).

**Tests**: a new unit test in `entityFormatting.test.ts` for `findFilterableFields` (asserts it returns a qualifying enum field plus a boolean field, in that order, excluding text/date/too-large-enum fields -- the same exclusions `findFilterableEnumFields` already enforces). A new full-DOM test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` with a `Task` entity carrying both an enum (`status`) and a boolean (`isUrgent`) field, confirming two filter dropdowns render, the boolean one shows `Yes`/`No` (never raw `true`/`false`), filtering by `true` narrows the record set correctly, and combining the boolean filter with the enum filter narrows via AND (both conditions). A new test in `codegen.test.ts` confirms the exported app's own generated `entityViewJsx` carries the same boolean branch and the `findFilterableFields` function definition. The pre-existing round-286 structural test in `codegen.test.ts` was updated to assert against the renamed `filterableFields` variable and the new function alongside the still-present `findFilterableEnumFields`.

### Round 404: leaving a shared project (self-service) left its own client-side preferences behind forever

**The survey**: a fresh Explore general-survey, primed with the full closed-topics list through round 403, explicitly including round 403's own "N convergent paths to the same end result, one path forgotten" framing. **Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/CollaboratorsPanel.tsx:107-128`'s `handleLeave` directly and confirmed its own doc comment states "once this succeeds, the caller has no access to this project at all any more" -- it calls `removeCollaborator(projectId, currentUserId)` then `onLeft()`, with no arguments. Read `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s `CollaboratorsPanel` usage (`project.id`/`project.ownerId` passed as sibling props, confirming `project` is non-null in that JSX scope since it's nested inside `view === "preview" && project && (...)`) and confirmed the pre-fix `onLeft` callback only called `setShowCollaborators(false)` and `handleGoHome()` -- no `purgeProjectPreferences` anywhere. Grepped `docs/roadmap.md` for `Leave project`/`handleLeave`/`onLeft` and found round 213's own design note (`onLeft` wired to "the same `handleGoHome` cleanup the account-deletion flow and the topbar logo already use") -- written roughly 170 rounds before `projectPreferenceCleanup.ts` existed (round 390), and never revisited by any round that wired that sweep into the other three paths. No test or comment anywhere claims this exclusion is intentional.

**Why it's a genuine gap, not deliberate**: a user who collaborates on several projects and leaves some of them accumulates orphaned entries across all eighteen `projectPreferenceCleanup.ts` stores forever, since leaving typically means never regaining access to that project id to trigger any other cleanup path. The end state (no access, from this browser, ever again) is identical to the three already-fixed paths; only the trigger (a `removeCollaborator` self-targeted call, not a `deleteProject` cascade) differs.

**The fix**: added `purgeProjectPreferences(project.id)` to the `onLeft` callback in `App.tsx`, right alongside the existing `setShowCollaborators`/`handleGoHome` calls. `project.id` was already in scope (it's the same value passed as the sibling `projectId` prop on the same JSX element), so unlike round 403's `DeleteAccountPanel` fix, no prop-signature widening was needed anywhere.

**Tests**: a new `App.test.ts` extraction test, sliced straight out of the `onLeft={() => {...}}` JSX attribute itself -- round 350's own "slice between JSX attributes" technique, here applied to a multi-statement inline callback rather than a single expression. Hit one real mechanical snag: esbuild's `transformSync` appends a trailing `;` to a bare arrow-function expression it transforms (`() => {...}` becomes `() => {...};`), so wrapping the regex-captured text in an extra `return (${code});` produced a dangling `);` after that semicolon and a syntax error; fixed by using `return ${code}` directly, since the transformed text already ends in its own semicolon. The test confirms `purgeProjectPreferences` is called with exactly the left project's id, and that the existing panel-close/navigate-home behavior still runs unchanged.

### Round 405: the "New share" chip never reappeared after a collaborator was removed and later re-invited to the same project

**The survey**: round 404's own trigger-prompt note warned against a 5th trivial instance of the `purgeProjectPreferences` "N convergent paths" pattern, so this round's Explore general-survey was pointed at genuinely unexamined areas instead (search edge cases, validation, timezones, pagination, concurrent-edit scenarios, TODO/FIXME comments). The subagent's single candidate was a correctness bug in round 401's own same-day feature, not a 5th instance of the already-4x-closed pattern: `sharedProjectSeen.ts` marked a shared project id "seen" forever the instant it was opened once, with no way to tell "this exact share grant was acknowledged" from "this project id was ever opened." A collaborator removed (`DELETE /projects/:id/collaborators/:userId`, a real `DELETE FROM project_collaborators`) and later re-invited (`addCollaborator`, a fresh `INSERT`) gets a brand-new share -- but their browser still has the project id in `forge.seenSharedProjects` from the first time, so the "New share" chip (round 401) silently never shows for exactly the case it exists to catch.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/sharedProjectSeen.ts` directly and confirmed `markSharedProjectSeen`/`getSeenSharedProjectIds` operated on a flat `string[]` of ids with no timestamp of any kind. Read `packages/db/src/collaborators.ts`: `addCollaborator` does `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO project_collaborators (projectId, userId, addedAt) VALUES (...)` with `addedAt = new Date().toISOString()` computed fresh on every call; `removeCollaborator` is a real `DELETE`, so a remove-then-re-add sequence frees the `(projectId, userId)` primary key and the second `addCollaborator` is a genuine `INSERT` with a new `addedAt`, not an `OR IGNORE` no-op. Read `packages/db/src/projects.ts`'s `listProjectsForUser`: its query selected only `projects.*` from the `LEFT JOIN project_collaborators` -- `addedAt` was never exposed to the client at all, confirming there was no signal available today to distinguish one share grant from the next. Confirmed via `grep` that `ProjectSchema`/`Project` (in `packages/shared/src/index.ts`) is never run through `.parse()` anywhere except for type inference, so adding an optional field to it is a pure type-level change with no runtime validation to break.

**Why it's a genuine gap, not deliberate**: round 401 built the chip to solve exactly this problem ("surface a share the user hasn't yet acknowledged"), and a stale "Shared" project silently reappearing with access restored, unannounced, is the single most confusing instance of the problem the feature was built to prevent. Nothing suggests this was an intentional simplification -- the flat id-set design simply never considered that the same project id could represent more than one distinct share grant over time.

**The fix**: `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s `ProjectSchema` gained an optional `sharedAt: z.string().optional()` field (documented as "only present for a project the requesting user is a collaborator on"). `packages/db/src/projects.ts`'s `listProjectsForUser` query now selects `project_collaborators.addedAt AS sharedAt` alongside `projects.*`, and `rowToProject` normalizes the resulting SQL `NULL` (present for every owned project, whose `LEFT JOIN` side never matches) to `undefined` rather than leaving it as `null`, keeping it consistent with the schema's `.optional()` (not `.nullable()`) and letting `JSON.stringify` omit the key entirely for owned projects. `sharedProjectSeen.ts` was rewritten to store `projectId -> last-acknowledged sharedAt` (a `Record<string, string>` under the same `forge.seenSharedProjects` key) instead of a flat id array; `getSeenSharedProjectIds()` became `getSeenSharedTimestamps(): Map<string, string>`, `markSharedProjectSeen(projectId, sharedAt)` now takes the timestamp to record, and a new `isNewShare(seen, projectId, sharedAt)` helper centralizes the "is this worth showing as new" comparison (`sharedAt !== undefined && seen.get(projectId) !== sharedAt`) for both the `App.tsx` call sites that used to do this inline. `App.tsx`'s `openExistingProject` now calls `markSharedProjectSeen(p.id, p.sharedAt)` only when `p.sharedAt` is defined, and the home screen's "New share" chip condition became `isNewShare(seenShared, p.id, p.sharedAt)`. Round 401's old flat-array-shaped `forge.seenSharedProjects` value is treated as "nothing acknowledged yet" by the new reader (it's neither `null` nor a plain object) -- a one-time, harmless reset of every already-seen chip the first time a browser loads this round's code, not a crash or data-loss risk, and explicitly called out as such in the function's own comment.

**codegen.ts (exported standalone app)**: checked first (the round-384 lesson) -- `collaborator`/`ownerId`/`sharedAt` all returned zero matches; the exported app has no collaborator concept, so nothing to port.

### Round 406: /refine silently discarded the AI-vs-heuristic provider signal that /projects and /ideas/enhance already surface

**The survey**: round 405's own trigger-prompt note explicitly steered this round's Explore general-survey away from the `purgeProjectPreferences` pattern and toward genuinely unexamined areas (search edge cases, validation, timezones, pagination, concurrent-edit scenarios, TODO/FIXME comments), and also explicitly excluded re-touching `sharedProjectSeen.ts`/the "New share" chip area round 405 had just re-verified correct. The subagent's top candidate was a second, independent instance of round 402's own "provider signal discarded" gap -- not a re-opening of round 405's fix, and not the already-4x-closed purge pattern.

**Independent verification**: grepped `generateSpec`/`providerName` across `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` directly. `POST /projects` (project creation, line 340) and `POST /ideas/enhance` (round 402, line 327) both destructure `providerName` from their respective `generateSpec()`/`enhancePrompt()` calls and return it in the JSON response. `POST /projects/:id/refine` (line 660, pre-fix) called the identical `generateSpec(combinedDescription, provider)` but destructured only `{ spec: nextSpec }`, discarding `providerName` outright before handing `nextSpec` to `streamPipeline`. Confirmed `generateSpec()`'s own return type in `packages/spec-engine/src/index.ts` (`Promise<{ spec: ProductSpec; providerName: string }>`) and its test file's explicit assertions that a failed Anthropic call returns `providerName: "anthropic-fallback"` rather than throwing or silently looking identical to the heuristic path -- confirming the signal genuinely exists and is genuinely silenced at this one call site. (The subagent's `/answers` runner-up turned out, on inspection of `handleBuild`'s own flow, to have no safe render location -- that route's view transitions straight to `"building"` the instant it succeeds, so there's no screen left on which a captured `specProvider` would ever be shown; left open as a smaller, separately-scoped follow-up rather than folded into this fix.)

**Why it's a genuine gap, not deliberate**: the app's own stated design intent for this seam (quoted in round 402's commit message) is "nothing hidden or silently substituted." That already holds for the initial build and the enhance step, both because round 402 closed the second of those two gaps. `/refine` is the single most-repeated AI-regeneration action in the app (a project can be refined dozens of times, per the existing unbounded refine-history list), and a silent Anthropic failure mid-refine falling back to the crude keyword heuristic is exactly as consequential to the resulting spec as a build-time fallback -- round 398's own "tightened constraints" work already treats refine-time spec correctness as seriously as build-time. There was simply no render location wired up for `/refine`'s copy of this signal before now.

**The fix**: `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s `PipelineOptions` gained an optional `providerName?: string` field, documented as "/build has no such call, so this stays undefined there." `runBuildPipeline`'s very first yielded event (`{agent: "Architect", status: "running", ...}`, emitted exactly once per pipeline run, for both `/build` and `/refine`) now spreads `...(providerName ? { detail: { providerName } } : {})` onto itself -- a `detail` key only when there's a provider name to carry, rather than always setting one to `undefined`, so `/build`'s copy of this same event keeps its exact pre-fix shape (no new own key at all) for any strict `deepEqual` elsewhere. `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `/refine` route now destructures `providerName` from its `generateSpec()` call and passes it through to `streamPipeline`'s opts. On the client, `apps/web/src/App.tsx` gained `extractRefineProviderName(events)`, which finds that same first `agent === "Architect" && status === "running"` event in a completed refine's raw event list and reads `providerName` off its `detail` (mirroring `summarizeRefineImpact`'s own convention of scanning the raw list rather than `BuildProgress.tsx`'s per-agent-latest map, since nothing else ever needs this transient event once the pipeline's second, "success" Architect event supersedes it there). `RefineHistoryEntry` gained a `providerName: string | null` field, set in `handleBuildComplete` via `extractRefineProviderName(refineEvents.current)`, and the refine-history list now renders it via the pre-existing `specProviderLabel(entry.providerName, t)` (reused as-is, not duplicated into a third near-identical label function or i18n key set) right below each entry's own impact summary, using the same `"error"` CSS class convention for the `"anthropic-fallback"` case that `specProviderLabel`'s other two call sites already use.

**codegen.ts (exported standalone app)**: checked first (the round-384 lesson) -- `AgentStepEvent`/`runBuildPipeline`/`PipelineOptions`/`specProviderLabel`/`RefineHistoryEntry` all returned zero matches; the exported app has no AI-build-pipeline or provider-seam concept at all, so nothing to port.

**Tests**: `apps/api/src/pipeline.test.ts` gained two tests -- one confirming `providerName` lands on the first event's `detail` when `PipelineOptions.providerName` is set, and one confirming the first event has no `detail` key at all (not even one holding `undefined`) when it's omitted, matching every other "running"-status event in that file. `apps/web/src/App.test.ts` gained three direct `extractRefineProviderName` unit tests (reads off the first running event, returns `null` when that event has no detail, returns `null` for an empty list) plus a new `handleBuildComplete` extraction-test case (refineRunning `true` this time, unlike the file's existing case) confirming the real `RefineHistoryEntry` pushed via `setRefineHistory` carries the `providerName` extracted from a fixture event list -- and the two existing `RefineHistoryEntry`-typed test fixtures (`filterRefineHistory`/`removeRefineHistoryEntry`'s own tests) picked up an explicit `providerName: null` once the interface's new field stopped being optional.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the three changed implementation files (`apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`, `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`, `apps/web/src/App.tsx`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted them to HEAD (keeping the two updated test files). Both predicted failures occurred: `pipeline.test.ts`'s new "attaches providerName" test failed with `actual: undefined` vs `expected: {providerName: 'anthropic-fallback'}` (its sibling "no detail key when omitted" test correctly kept passing even reverted, since that's a guard against a *different*, already-pre-existing behavior, not this round's own change), and `App.test.ts` failed with a module-load error (`extractRefineProviderName` not exported) -- a strong confirmation per the round-381 convention. Restored all three files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and the full `@forge/api` and `@forge/web` suites clean. ### Round 407: /answers' own copy of round 406's provider-signal gap, closed with a new BuildProgress render location

**The survey**: round 406's own trigger-prompt note flagged its exact follow-up candidate -- `/answers` discards `generateSpec()`'s `providerName` the identical way `/refine` did before that round, but has no existing render location (its view switches straight to `"building"` on success, unlike `/refine`'s persistent refine-history list). This round picked that already-identified, already-scoped candidate up directly rather than running a fresh Explore survey, since the prior round had already done the hard work of locating and verifying it.

**Independent re-verification before starting**: re-read `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `/answers` handler directly and confirmed it still destructured only `{ spec }` from `generateSpec(combinedDescription, provider)`, discarding `providerName` exactly as round 406 described; confirmed `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s `handleBuild` (the only caller of `answerQuestions()`) calls `setView("building")` as its very next statement after the `answerQuestions` call succeeds, with no `return`/early-exit in between -- so the spec-review screen (where `specProviderLabel(specProvider, t)` already renders, right under the project summary) is genuinely gone by the time any such signal could be read, confirming the "no render location" claim rather than assuming it.

**The fix**: `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `/answers` route now destructures `providerName` alongside `spec` from its `generateSpec()` call and returns it in `res.json({ project: updated, providerName })`, mirroring `/projects` and `/ideas/enhance` exactly (the early-return "nothing to answer" branch above it never calls `generateSpec()` at all, so it still returns no `providerName` key, left alone). `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `answerQuestions()` return type widened to `Promise<{ project: Project; providerName?: string }>` (optional, matching that same no-op case). `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s `handleBuild` now does `if (providerName) setSpecProvider(providerName)` right after `setProject(updated)` -- deliberately overwriting the existing `specProvider` state (set at project-creation time) with this second, more-recent `generateSpec()` call's own result when the user actually answered something, since that's the spec about to be built. The new render location is `apps/web/src/BuildProgress.tsx`'s own new optional `specProviderNotice?: ReactNode` prop, rendered right under the `<h1>{title}</h1>` (only when `!compact`, matching the existing title-suppression rule for the inline/refine usage) -- a plain already-rendered node rather than a raw `providerName` string or a new label function, so `BuildProgress.tsx` needs no i18n keys of its own and never duplicates `specProviderLabel`'s logic. The initial-build `<BuildProgress>` call in `App.tsx` now passes `specProviderNotice={specProviderLabel(specProvider, t) && (<p className={...}>{...}</p>)}` -- the exact same JSX fragment the spec-review screen already renders, just handed down as a prop instead of re-implemented. The refine screen's own, separate `<BuildProgress compact>` usage passes nothing new, so it renders exactly as before (its `compact` flag already suppresses the title and, now, this notice too).

**A side effect worth naming explicitly, not a bug**: because `specProvider` is already set from project creation even when the user answers nothing, this notice now also appears on every initial build, not only after answering questions -- a strictly larger application of the same "nothing hidden or silently substituted" intent round 402's commit message stated, not a narrower one. Nothing in prior rounds' history documents a deliberate choice to hide this signal during the build screen specifically, so this isn't reversing an intentional design decision.

### Round 408: a whitespace-only value for a required number/relation field silently stored 0 instead of being rejected

**The survey**: with the `generateSpec()`-providerName pattern now closed 4/4 (round 407) and the `purgeProjectPreferences` pattern closed 4/4 (round 404), a fresh Explore general-survey was explicitly steered toward genuinely unexplored territory -- data-validation edge cases on the record create/update path specifically, an area the prompt had been flagging as under-examined for several rounds. The subagent found and reproduced (via a direct call to `coerceValue`, not just reasoning about it) a real JS quirk: `Number(" ")` is `0`, not `NaN`.

**Independent verification**: read `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` (lines 31-46) directly and confirmed its required/emptiness check was exactly `raw === undefined || raw === null || raw === ""` -- a whitespace-only string like `" "` or `"\t\n"` satisfies none of those three, so it fell straight through into the `"number"`/`"relation"` branch's `Number(raw)`. Ran `node -e 'console.log(Number(" "), Number("\t\n"))'` directly and confirmed both print `0`, not `NaN` -- so `Number.isNaN(num)` never catches it either. Confirmed `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` passes `req.body` into `insertRecord`/`updateRecord` with no trimming anywhere above this layer, and that a `relation` field's column carries a real `REFERENCES ... (id)` constraint (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`), so a fabricated foreign key `0` would hit that constraint and throw a bare, untranslated SQLite error for a *required* relation field specifically (a `0` row essentially never exists) -- a different failure mode from round 394's own fix (which translated an FK violation from a syntactically-valid-but-nonexistent id into a clean 409; round 394 never touched the required/emptiness check itself, so this gap survived that round untouched). Grepped `entityFormatting.ts`'s CSV import (`buildImportRecords`) and confirmed it already trims each cell before checking for emptiness -- so the codebase already had the right instinct in one of two places that needed it, just not in the data layer every caller (including any future bulk-edit feature or a direct API client) ultimately funnels through.

**The fix**: `coerceValue` now computes `isEmpty` as the existing three-way check `||` `(typeof raw === "string" && raw.trim() === "")`, and uses that for the required-field branch -- a whitespace-only value is now treated exactly like an already-empty one: a `ValidationError` for a required field, `null` for an optional one. Nothing below that branch changed; a real, non-whitespace value (including one with incidental leading/trailing padding like `" 42 "`) still coerces exactly as before, since `Number(" 42 ")` already correctly returns `42`.

**codegen.ts (exported standalone app)**: checked first (the round-384 lesson) -- found a second copy of the identical logic, `coerce()` (lines 361-384), a verbatim copy-pasted duplicate of `coerceValue` baked into the exported standalone app's generated `server.js` template (same pattern already called out by this file's own comments for round 62's date-validation gap). Applied the identical one-line fix there too.

**Tests**: `packages/db/src/repository.test.ts` gained three tests -- a required `number` field rejects four different whitespace-only inputs (`" "`, `"\t"`, `"\n"`, `"  \t  "`) while still accepting a real `500`; a required `relation` field rejects a whitespace-only value with a clean `ValidationError` rather than hitting the FK constraint as a fabricated id `0` (new `Customer`/`Order` fixture, mirroring `migrate.test.ts`'s own relation-fixture convention since none existed in this file yet); an *optional* number field and an optional text field both turn a whitespace-only value into `null`, not a fabricated `0` or the literal whitespace string. `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts` gained one new test following this file's own established "spawn the real generated server.js and hit it over HTTP" convention (the same standard it already uses for this exact function's date-validation and foreign-key-enforcement tests) -- POSTs a whitespace-only `amount` to a required number field and confirms a `400`, then confirms a real `500` value is still accepted and stored correctly.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the two changed implementation files (`packages/db/src/repository.ts`, `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted them to HEAD (keeping the updated test files). All four predicted failures occurred exactly: the required-number-field test failed with "Missing expected exception"; the required-relation-field test failed on its own assertion message; the optional-fields test failed with `0 !== null`; and the spawned-server test failed with `201 !== 400` (the record was created instead of rejected). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and the full `@forge/db` and `@forge/api` suites clean.

Full suite green: **106 tests** in `@forge/db` (+3 new), **387 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1 new), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/web` and `@forge/shared` (untouched this round, no re-run needed) stayed at their round-407 counts. Pushed as commit `995155b`.

### Round 409: `deleteProject` orphaned a table whose entity only ever appeared in a checkpoint that fails to parse under today's schema

**The survey**: with the whitespace-emptiness gap (round 408), the `purgeProjectPreferences` pattern (4/4), and the `generateSpec()` providerName pattern (4/4) all closed, a fresh Explore general-survey was steered explicitly away from those three and toward genuinely unexplored areas: `identifiers.ts`, `migrate.ts`'s less-common diff paths, `checkpoints.ts` restore/diff edge cases, `users.ts`, and cross-cutting concerns. It found a narrow, previously-unidentified repeat of a bug this project had already fixed once before (round 389's "`deleteProject` orphaned data table" fix), occurring one layer further down than that fix reached.

**Independent verification**: read `packages/db/src/projects.ts`'s `deleteProject` (lines 198-211) directly and confirmed it computes the set of tables to drop by unioning `project.spec.entities` with every checkpoint's own entities, read via `listCheckpoints(db, project.id)` -- exactly the fix round 389's own doc-comment describes (entities removed from the spec via refine still need their real data table dropped, since `migrate.ts`'s `diffAndMigrate` is deliberately additive-only). Read `packages/db/src/checkpoints.ts`'s `listCheckpoints` (lines 66-78) and its `tryRowToCheckpoint` helper (lines 45-53) and confirmed it wraps `ProductSpecSchema.parse` in a try/catch and silently excludes (with only a `console.error`) any checkpoint row whose stored `spec_json` no longer satisfies today's schema -- explicitly documented in that function's own comment as "a real, expected future case," since `ProductSpecSchema` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts` lines 143-160) can only get stricter over time by design (a new `.min(1)`, a field going from optional to required, etc.), never looser. That exclusion is the right behavior for `listCheckpoints`'s only other caller (the History panel's user-facing checkpoint list, `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` line 677) -- one bad row shouldn't take down the whole list -- but `deleteProject` was reusing that same tolerant function for a completeness-critical computation: a checkpoint that fails to parse is excluded from `deleteProject`'s accounting too, so any entity that only ever appeared in *that* checkpoint's spec (and was later refined back out of the current spec) never gets its table dropped. Confirmed `listCheckpoints` has exactly one other call site in the whole repo (grepped all non-test usages) and it's the History panel route, so narrowing `deleteProject`'s own behavior couldn't affect anything else. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no checkpoint/project concept at all (grepped for "checkpoint" -- zero matches), so there was nothing to port there, unlike most prior rounds' fixes.

**The fix**: added `listAllCheckpointedEntityNames(db, projectId)` to `checkpoints.ts`, which reads each checkpoint row's raw `spec_json` directly (not via `rowToCheckpoint`/`ProductSpecSchema.parse`) and pulls out just the `entities[].name` strings, tolerating a `spec_json` that fails full schema validation as long as its `entities` array itself is still shaped sensibly (an array of objects with a string `name`) -- a far weaker, narrower requirement than the full checkpoint schema, and the right one for this specific need. `deleteProject` now calls this instead of `listCheckpoints` to build its entity-name set; `listCheckpoints` itself is untouched, so the History panel keeps its existing (correct) tolerant behavior.

**Tests**: `packages/db/src/projects.test.ts` gained one test, placed directly after round 389's own "entity added then removed from spec" test and explicitly modeled on it: builds a project, adds an "Order" entity via a real `diffAndMigrate` + a real inserted row, but writes that refine's checkpoint via a raw SQL `INSERT` (bypassing `insertCheckpoint`, which would require a valid spec) with a `spec_json` missing the required `roles` field -- standing in for a checkpoint written by an older app version. A sanity assertion confirms `listCheckpoints` really does exclude that row (so the test is actually exercising the gap, not a false positive), then refines "Order" back out of the spec and calls `deleteProject`, asserting the `entity_..._Order` table is still dropped.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the two changed implementation files (`packages/db/src/checkpoints.ts`, `packages/db/src/projects.ts`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted them to HEAD (keeping the new test). The predicted failure occurred exactly: 106 passed, 1 failed (the new test, with the `entity_proj_stale_cp_Order` table still present instead of throwing "no such table"). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and the full `@forge/db` and `@forge/api` suites clean.

Full suite green: **107 tests** in `@forge/db` (+1 new), **387 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged -- no files in that workspace touched this round), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/web` and `@forge/shared` (untouched, no re-run needed) stayed at their round-408 counts. Pushed as commit `7bea832`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It is a narrower, one-layer-deeper variant of round 389's already-closed "orphaned data table" fix -- round 389 fixed the case where `deleteProject` didn't consider checkpoint history *at all*; this fix closes the remaining gap where it considers checkpoint history but through a lens (`listCheckpoints`) that silently drops some of it. Both are now closed. Everything else still open from rounds 378-408 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 410: two fields on the same entity differing only by case passed validation, then crashed the real database layer with a raw SQLite error

**The survey**: with the `purgeProjectPreferences` pattern (4/4), the `generateSpec()` providerName pattern (4/4), the whitespace-emptiness gap (408), and the `deleteProject` checkpoint-orphan gap (389+409, two layers) all closed, a fresh Explore general-survey was explicitly pointed at genuinely unexplored territory and specifically asked to watch for round 409's own lesson: a completeness-critical computation relying on a tolerant, best-effort helper designed for a different purpose. It instead found a close structural cousin of an *already-closed* guard, one level down: `ProductSpecSchema` guards against two **entities** whose names collide case-insensitively, but has no equivalent guard for two **fields on the same entity**.

**Independent verification**: read `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s two existing entity-level guards directly -- `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames` (then at lines 44-56) and `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` (then at lines 78-90), both wired into `ProductSpecSchema`'s own `.refine()` calls (then at lines 171-176), both scoped only to `spec.entities`. Read `FieldSchema` (then at lines 92-113) and confirmed its only name-collision guard is `RESERVED_FIELD_NAMES` (`id`/`createdat`, the two built-in columns) -- nothing checks one field's name against another field's name within the same entity. Read `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`'s `generateCreateTableStatements` (lines 28-47, builds the live preview's `CREATE TABLE` from `entity.fields` with no case-folding) and `diffAndMigrate`'s `new_column` branch (the `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` path), and confirmed both build raw SQL straight from field names with no dedup. Reproduced directly against this project's actual `node:sqlite` binding (`node --experimental-sqlite`): `CREATE TABLE t ("Email" TEXT, "email" TEXT)` throws `duplicate column name: email`, and (given an existing `email` column) `ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN "Email" TEXT` throws `duplicate column name: Email` the same way -- the identical failure class the entity-name guards already exist to prevent, just one level down. Confirmed `routes/projects.ts`'s `deriveFieldName` (the manual "add field" UI path) already de-duplicates case-insensitively against an entity's existing field names (its own doc-comment says so explicitly) -- so this gap is specific to an AI- or heuristic-generated spec, the one path with no equivalent guard: a `/refine` that regenerates an entity from prose alone (the AI provider never sees the previous spec's structure -- the same blind spot `pipeline.ts`'s own `computeImpact` comment already documents for entity/field removal) can plausibly emit a second, differently-cased field on an entity that already has one. Traced what actually happens when `diffAndMigrate` throws this raw SQLite error: `pipeline.ts`'s `runBuildOrRefine` (lines ~288-334) catches it and routes to the Debug Agent's automatic repair path -- a real, paid Anthropic API call -- or, with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` configured, fails the build outright and surfaces the raw `duplicate column name: Email` string to the end user, instead of the clean, pre-DB validation message the entity-name case already gets. Confirmed no test anywhere in the repo (`index.test.ts`, `migrate.test.ts`, `App.test.ts`, `pipeline.test.ts`) exercises two same-entity fields differing only by case. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicated schema-validation logic to port -- unlike `coerceValue`/`coerce` (round 408), `codegen.ts` only ever consumes an already-`ProductSpecSchema`-validated spec (every stored project re-validates on read, per that schema's own doc-comment), so fixing the schema in `@forge/shared` alone protects both the live preview and the exported app's codegen path.

**The fix**: added `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateFieldNames`, structurally identical to `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames` but scoped to a single entity's own `fields` array, and wired it into a new `.refine()` on `EntitySchema` itself (not `ProductSpecSchema`) -- unlike entity names, two fields can only collide within the *same* entity, since fields are scoped per-table, not per-spec (the exact same field name reused across two different entities, e.g. `name` on both `Customer` and `Vendor`, is two entirely separate columns and must stay accepted).

**Tests**: `packages/shared/src/index.test.ts` gained three tests, placed directly after the existing "`EntitySchema` rejects an entity with zero fields" test: two same-entity fields differing only by case (`email`/`Email`) are rejected with a message matching `/collide when compared case-insensitively/`; two genuinely distinct field names on the same entity are still accepted; and the same field name (`name`) reused across two different entities in a full `ProductSpecSchema` still passes, confirming the check is correctly entity-scoped and not spec-wide.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the one changed implementation file (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted it to HEAD (keeping the new tests). The predicted failure occurred exactly: 15 passed, 1 failed (the new case-collision rejection test, with `result.success` true instead of false). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and the full test chain (`@forge/shared` → `@forge/spec-engine` → `@forge/db` → `@forge/api` → `@forge/web`) clean end to end -- confirming no existing fixture anywhere in the monorepo happens to rely on two same-entity fields colliding case-insensitively.

Full suite green: **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (+3 new), **93** in `@forge/spec-engine`, **107** in `@forge/db`, **387** in `@forge/api`, **801** in `@forge/web` (all four unchanged -- no files in those workspaces touched this round), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `7fedfad`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It closes the field-level counterpart to the already-closed entity-level case-insensitive-name guard; the entity-level `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` check has no field-level counterpart added here, since field names go through `assertSafeIdentifier`'s strict ASCII-only pattern rather than `tableNameFor`'s silent non-ASCII sanitization, so that specific failure mode (two different names sanitizing to the same identifier) doesn't apply the same way to fields -- a separate question, not evaluated this round, and not claimed closed. Everything else still open from rounds 378-409 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 411: deleting your account silently orphaned a project whose own stored spec failed to re-parse

**The survey**: with round 410's field-level guard closed, a fresh Explore general-survey was pointed away from it and explicitly asked to watch for two recurring patterns from recent rounds: (1) a completeness-critical computation routed through a tolerant, best-effort listing function (round 409's own lesson), and (2) a validation guard existing at one level with a missing sibling at a neighboring level (round 410's own lesson) -- but told to discount the one candidate round 410 itself had already surfaced and evaluated (a non-ASCII field name, which would require the AI to violate its own prompt's explicit, emphatic "MUST stay ASCII... no matter what" instruction, confirmed by reading `packages/spec-engine/src/anthropic.ts` line 39 and `domainEntities.ts`'s hardcoded English field names -- too speculative to treat as a real bug). The survey instead found a direct structural repeat of round 409's own pattern, one level up: `deleteProject` orphaning a single entity's table because of an unparseable *checkpoint* (409) has a twin where `DELETE /auth/account` orphans an *entire project* -- every table, every checkpoint, every WhatsApp row, and the project row itself -- because of an unparseable *project*.

**Independent verification**: read `packages/db/src/projects.ts`'s `tryRowToProject` (lines 43-59) and confirmed its doc-comment explicitly frames a project whose `spec_json` fails `ProductSpecSchema.parse` as "a real, expected future case" -- the identical framing `tryRowToCheckpoint` already uses for checkpoints, and for the identical reason (the schema only ever gets stricter). Read `listProjectsForUser` and `listProjectsForOwner` (lines 89-100, 112-122) and confirmed both run every row through `tryRowToProject` and filter out any `undefined` -- correct for a user-facing project list, exactly as round 409 already established for `listCheckpoints`. Read `apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts`'s `DELETE /auth/account` handler (lines 179-195, before this round's fix) and confirmed it computed `ownedProjects` via `listProjectsForUser(db, req.userId!).filter((p) => p.ownerId === req.userId)`, then looped `deleteProject(db, project)` over exactly that filtered list, then unconditionally called `deleteUser(db, req.userId!)` regardless. Traced the consequence directly: a project whose spec fails to re-parse is silently absent from `ownedProjects`, so `deleteProject` is never called for it -- its real data tables, checkpoints, and WhatsApp connection/message rows are never dropped, and the `projects` row itself (with its now-nonexistent `ownerId`) is never deleted -- while the route still returns a clean `204` and the user row is gone, so there is no login path left to ever reach that project again through any route. This is a strictly worse outcome than round 409's own bug: round 409 orphaned one entity's table within an otherwise-intact, still-owned project; this orphans the *entire* project, permanently, with the deleting user's own request reporting success. Confirmed `deleteProject`'s *other* call site (`DELETE /projects/:id`, `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` line 480) already goes through `requireProjectOwner`/`getProject`, which has no try/catch and fails loudly for a single unparseable project -- an accepted, narrower cost for a single, user-initiated single-project delete (per `tryRowToProject`'s own comment), deliberately left unchanged this round since it's a different, already-accepted tradeoff, not the bug being fixed here.

**The fix**: added `listOwnedProjectIds(db, ownerId)` to `projects.ts` -- a raw query selecting only the `id` column, so it never touches `spec_json` and can never miss a project this way. `DELETE /auth/account` now uses it directly instead of `listProjectsForUser(...).filter(...)`. `deleteProject` itself had the identical problem one level down -- its signature required a parsed `Project` (specifically for `project.spec.entities`), which is exactly what's unavailable for a project that fails to parse -- so its signature changed from `(db, project: Project)` to `(db, projectId: string)`, and it now reads its own `spec_json` directly via a newly-exported `extractEntityNamesFromSpecJson` (factored out of round 409's `listAllCheckpointedEntityNames`, now shared by both: a checkpoint's `spec_json` and a project's own `spec_json` need the exact same tolerant extraction, for the exact same reason). Updated `deleteProject`'s other call site (`DELETE /projects/:id`) to pass `project.id` instead of the full object -- no behavior change there, since that route already had a valid `Project` in hand.

**Tests**: `packages/db/src/projects.test.ts` gained two tests, placed directly after round 409's own checkpoint-parse-failure test. The first (`listOwnedProjectIds still returns a project whose stored spec no longer parses...`) inserts one valid project via `insertProject` and one "stale" project via a raw SQL `INSERT` missing `roles` (mirroring every prior round's convention for simulating an older app version's row), then asserts `listProjectsForOwner` excludes the stale one (sanity check) while `listOwnedProjectIds` returns both. The second (`deleteProject still drops the real data table, checkpoints, collaborators, and WhatsApp history of a project whose own stored spec no longer parses...`) builds a project's real table/row/checkpoint/collaborator/WhatsApp-connection entirely through `applyMigrations`/`insertRecord`/`insertCheckpoint`/`addCollaborator`/`recordWhatsAppConnected` *before* ever writing its `projects` row (confirmed no `FOREIGN KEY` ties any of those tables to a real `projects` row, by reading `collaborators.ts`'s and `whatsapp.ts`'s own schemas), then writes that stale `projects` row via raw SQL, confirms `getProject` throws on it (sanity check), calls `deleteProject(db, "proj-stale-own")`, and asserts the project row, its real data table, its checkpoint, its collaborator grant, and its WhatsApp connection are all gone.

**Regression-proof**: backed up all five changed files (`apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts`, `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`, `packages/db/src/checkpoints.ts`, `packages/db/src/index.ts`, `packages/db/src/projects.ts`) to the session scratchpad (into separate subdirectories, since two of them share the basename `projects.ts`), `git checkout --` reverted all five to HEAD (keeping the updated test file). The predicted failure occurred, just in a stronger form than a per-assertion failure: `projects.test.ts`'s own `import { listOwnedProjectIds } from "./projects.js"` now names an export that no longer exists on the reverted file, crashing that entire test file's module load (96 tests ran instead of 109, with the whole file's test count missing rather than individually failing) -- a module-load crash, per this project's own established convention, counts as a strong confirmation. Restored all five files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q` on each, then reran the full monorepo build and the full `@forge/db` and `@forge/api` suites clean.

Full suite green: **109 tests** in `@forge/db` (+2 new), **387 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged -- the route changes are a straightforward drop-in swap with no new API-level test needed), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/web` and `@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` (untouched, no re-run needed) stayed at their round-410 counts. Pushed as commit `0909361`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It is round 409's exact pattern repeated one level up (a tolerant project-listing function reused by a completeness-critical cleanup, instead of a tolerant checkpoint-listing function) -- both are now closed. `DELETE /projects/:id`'s own narrower "fails loudly for a single unparseable project" behavior (via `getProject`) is a separate, already-accepted tradeoff and was deliberately left unchanged. Everything else still open from rounds 378-410 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 412: GlobalSearch's "Show all" had no staleness guard, unlike its own sibling `runSearch`

**The survey**: with the project-level `deleteProject` tolerant-listing pattern closed (411, mirroring 409 one layer up), a fresh Explore general-survey was pointed at genuinely unexhausted areas and asked to watch for the same general "does this caller need completeness/consistency and actually get it" question, but told explicitly not to restate 409/411 itself. It surfaced a candidate round 394's own survey had already found and named -- a staleness-guard gap in `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s `handleShowAll` -- but explicitly deprioritized at the time as "low impact" (see round 394's closing notes). Per the round-407 lesson (a candidate a previous round identified but didn't implement is "ready" for the next round to pick up, after independent re-verification), this was re-verified from scratch rather than taken on faith from the old note.

**Independent verification**: read `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s `runSearch` (lines 113-165) and confirmed it captures `const requestId = ++searchRequestId.current;` before its own `await`, then checks `if (searchRequestId.current !== requestId) return;` immediately after -- a deliberate, commented guard against a slower, now-stale search's results clobbering a faster, newer one's. Read `handleShowAll` (lines 188-210, before this round's fix) and confirmed it makes its own independent async `listRecords` call and then unconditionally calls `setExpandedSamples((prev) => ({ ...prev, [entityName]: full?.sample ?? [] }))` once that call resolves -- no equivalent check against `searchRequestId` at all, even though it's the exact same shape of race (an async fetch writing into state the UI reads back). Traced the concrete failure: a user searches "apple", clicks "Show all" on a "Customers" result group (`handleShowAll("Customers")` starts), then edits the query to "banana" and resubmits before the first fetch resolves -- `handleSubmit` resets `expandedSamples` to `{}` and calls `runSearch("banana")`, which bumps `searchRequestId` past what `handleShowAll` captured. When the stale "apple"-era fetch finally resolves, it merges its (irrelevant) sample back into `expandedSamples`, and if the new "banana" search also produced a "Customers" group, the render (`expandedSamples[result.entityName] ?? result.sample`) shows the wrong, apple-matched records under a banana search, with a `remaining` count that no longer matches `totalMatches` and "jump to record" targets that don't correspond to anything the current search actually matched. Confirmed `codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has a verbatim duplicate of this same `handleShowAll`/`runSearch` pair in its `GlobalSearch.jsx` template (round 326's own porting work), with the identical gap.

**The fix**: `handleShowAll` now captures `const requestId = searchRequestId.current;` before its `await listRecords(...)`, and checks `if (searchRequestId.current !== requestId) return;` right after -- mirroring `runSearch`'s own guard exactly, reusing the same ref rather than introducing a second one. The early return sits inside the existing `try` block, so the `finally` clause still clears the entity from `showAllLoading` regardless (a stale fetch's own loading spinner should disappear; only the stale *data* must not land). Ported the identical fix to `codegen.ts`'s plain-JS duplicate.

**Tests**: `apps/web/src/GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` gained one test, placed directly after the existing stale-`runSearch` regression test and built the same way (regex-extracts the real `handleShowAll` from the `.tsx` source, strips TypeScript via `esbuild`'s `transformSync`, runs it via `new Function` with a `listRecords` mock that holds its promise open): starts a "Show all" fetch, lets it reach its held-open `listRecords` call, bumps `searchRequestId` (standing in for a newer search completing), then resolves the held promise and asserts `setExpandedSamples` was never called. `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts` gained the identical test against the real generated `GlobalSearch.jsx`/`EntityView.jsx` output (extracting the generated `matchesSearch` and `handleShowAll` together), following the file's own existing convention for the stale-`runSearch` test right above it.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both changed implementation files (`apps/web/src/GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`, `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted both to HEAD (keeping the new tests). Both predicted failures occurred exactly: `@forge/web` reported 801 passed / 1 failed, `@forge/api` reported 387 passed / 1 failed -- in each case the one new test, with `setExpandedSamples`/the captured sample list showing the stale write had gone through. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran a full monorepo build, the full `@forge/api` suite, and the full `@forge/web` suite clean.

Full suite green: **802 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1 new), **388 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1 new), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/shared`, `@forge/spec-engine`, and `@forge/db` (untouched, no re-run needed) stayed at their round-411 counts. Pushed as commit `e448f11`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It closes the one remaining runner-up candidate round 394's own survey had surfaced and explicitly left open. Everything else still open from rounds 378-411 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 413: a field removed and later re-added under the same name could silently reuse a stale, mismatched physical column

**The survey**: with round 412's staleness-guard gap closed (the last runner-up round 394 had surfaced), a fresh Explore general-survey was pointed at genuinely unexhausted territory and explicitly told to discount both round 409/411's "tolerant listing used where completeness is needed" pattern and round 410/412's "a staleness/race guard present in one function but missing in a sibling doing the same shape of async work" pattern, since both families are now fully closed. It surfaced a third, structurally different category of defect in `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`'s `diffAndMigrate`: a field removed from an entity on one refine, then re-added under the *same name* on a *later* refine, with a different type.

**Independent verification**: read `diffAndMigrate` in full (then lines 1-224) and confirmed `previousSpec` is always exactly the immediately-preceding stored spec (every call site passes `project.spec`, never the full checkpoint history or the live SQL schema) -- so `prevFieldsByName`, built fresh from `prevEntity.fields` on each call, has no entry at all for a field that existed two-or-more refines ago but not in the one right before this one. Traced the consequence: such a field falls past both the `type_changed` and `relation_target_changed` checks (both require a truthy `prevField`) straight to the `new_column` branch. But this migration engine is additive-only by its own explicit design (the file's own doc-comment: "Never drops or renames anything, even if a field or entity was removed from the new spec"), so the physical column from the field's earlier life was never dropped -- `currentColumns.has(columnName)` is true, the `ALTER TABLE` is skipped, and the stale column's real SQL type and `REFERENCES` clause silently carry over with zero change reported, even when they now completely disagree with what the field claims. Reproduced the concrete repro directly against this project's own `node:sqlite` binding: a relation column (`INTEGER REFERENCES ...`) left behind after its field is removed, then a same-named `text` field added back two refines later, reports a clean `new_column` today with no indication the real column is still `INTEGER` with a live foreign key a plain-text field was never meant to have -- any write success/failure for that column now depends on an invisible leftover `REFERENCES` constraint the current spec has no way of knowing about. Confirmed `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s existing messaging code (lines ~335-346) already filters `changes` by `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed` and renders a note for each with zero change needed there, if the fix reuses those same two shapes. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no `diffAndMigrate` equivalent at all (its one mention of "migrate" is a comment describing the live app's behavior, not a competing implementation) -- consistent with round 395's own prior finding that the exported app's codegen is a single static snapshot with no incremental-migration concept, so this fix needs no counterpart there.

**The fix**: added `physicalColumnShape(db, table)` (reads `PRAGMA table_info` and `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` for the table, returning each existing column's real SQL type and, if any, its FK target table -- verified directly against a real SQLite binding that `table_info.type` echoes back the exact declared type string and `foreign_key_list.table` the exact referenced table name, both already written by this same file's own `sqlTypeFor`/`tableNameFor`), `entityNameForTable` (best-effort reverse lookup from a physical table name to an entity name for a user-facing message, falling back to the raw table name rather than ever rendering "undefined"), and `fieldTypeLabelForSqlType` (reverses `sqlTypeFor`'s own REAL/INTEGER/TEXT mapping for a column with no surviving `Field` to read `field.type` from -- INTEGER is resolved to "relation" or "boolean" by checking for an actual FK, since that's the one ambiguity in the mapping that's actually resolvable without the original Field). In the main per-field loop, added a check right after the existing `prevField`-truthy branch (which still handles the one-step-back case unchanged): when a field has no `prevField` but its column name already exists physically, compare the column's real shape against what the field now claims, using the identical two change shapes (`type_changed` for any cross-SQL-type-bucket mismatch; `relation_target_changed` for a same-INTEGER-bucket relation pointing at a different table) the `prevField` branch already produces. A benign reuse (same name, same type, same FK target) stays silent, same as if the field had never left. Scope note, an explicit judgment call this round: this covers any cross-bucket mismatch and any relation-to-different-relation mismatch, but deliberately does not add a check for the narrower residual case where both sides share the INTEGER bucket but one is a stale relation (with a leftover FK) and the new field is a boolean -- reasoned as a genuine edge-within-an-edge, analogous to this same file's own acknowledged, deliberate type_changed limitation in general, not attempted this round.

**Tests**: `packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts` gained three tests, placed directly after the existing `relation_target_changed` test. The first drives two sequential `diffAndMigrate` calls (remove the relation field, confirming zero changes and an untouched physical column; then re-add a same-named `text` field) and asserts a `type_changed` entry (`relation` → `text`) is now reported alongside the baseline `new_column` entry, and that the real column is still untouched (`INTEGER`, still FK-bound to `Customer`). The second proves the benign twin: re-adding the same name with the *same* type (relation to the same entity) stays silent -- only the baseline `new_column`, no spurious `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed` -- confirming the check only fires on a genuine mismatch. The third proves the `relation_target_changed` side: a relation field removed then re-added pointing at a *different* existing entity reports `relation_target_changed` (not `type_changed`, since both sides are INTEGER), with the real FK proven still bound to the original target.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the one changed implementation file (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted it to HEAD (keeping the new tests). The predicted failures occurred exactly: 110 passed, 2 failed -- the first and third new tests, each showing the actual `changes` array missing its `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed` entry and only ever containing the plain `new_column`, exactly the silent-misreport this round fixes; the second (benign-reuse) test passed even without the fix, correctly confirming it doesn't distinguish behavior for the no-mismatch case. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and the full `@forge/db` and `@forge/api` suites clean (the latter since `pipeline.ts` consumes `MigrationChange[]`, though that file itself was not touched).

Full suite green: **112 tests** in `@forge/db` (+3 new), **388 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged -- no files in that workspace touched this round), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/web`, `@forge/shared`, and `@forge/spec-engine` (untouched, no re-run needed) stayed at their round-412 counts. Pushed as commit `1b04541`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It is a third, independent category of defect in the migration diff path, distinct from both the type_changed/relation_target_changed gaps for a field that persists by name across exactly one step (already closed well before this round) and from rounds 409/411's and 410/412's own two patterns (both explicitly excluded from this round's survey and confirmed still fully closed, not reopened by this work). The deliberately-deferred same-INTEGER-bucket relation-vs-boolean residual case (see "The fix" above) remains open, as a documented, intentional scope boundary, not a bug. Everything else still open from rounds 378-412 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 414: a reused column that never had a FK could become a relation field with zero referential-integrity protection, forever

**The survey**: with round 413's own stale-column-reuse fix just pushed, a fresh Explore general-survey was pointed away from all three now-closed families (tolerant-listing completeness [409/411], staleness/race guards missing in a sibling [394/412], and the migration-diff one-step-back blind spot [413]) and asked to find a genuinely distinct gap. It found one sitting one asymmetric branch inside round 413's own new code: round 413's `relation_target_changed` check for a reused column requires a truthy `shape.fkTable` to compare against (`if (shape.fkTable && expectedFkTable && shape.fkTable !== expectedFkTable)`), so it only ever catches a stale FK pointing at the *wrong* table -- never a reused column that has *no* FK at all.

**Independent verification**: reproduced directly against this project's own `node:sqlite` binding (not just read through): built an entity with a plain `boolean` field (`isUrgent`, stored as INTEGER, no FK -- `sqlTypeFor` maps both `boolean` and `relation` to the same INTEGER bucket). Removed it on one refine (physical column survives untouched, additive-only). Re-added a field also named `isUrgent`, but now typed `relation` pointing at `Customer`, on the next refine. `diffAndMigrate` returned only `[{ type: "new_column", ... }]` -- no `type_changed` (same INTEGER bucket, no mismatch to trigger it) and no `relation_target_changed` (its own condition's `shape.fkTable` is falsy, so the whole check short-circuits). `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` on the real table confirmed: completely empty. Inserting a record with `isUrgent: 999999` -- a value with no corresponding `Customer` row at all -- succeeded silently via `insertRecord`, with no error anywhere. Confirmed this is the opposite, previously-unexamined direction from round 413's own documented scope note (which named only "old: relation+FK, new: boolean" as a deferred residual case) -- here it's "old: boolean, no FK ever existed; new: relation, needs one" -- and confirmed `twin.ts`'s `computeRelationHubObservation` explicitly documents and relies on "a dangling id can't happen through this app's own code paths" as its own justification for skipping its own extra protection; this is exactly a case where that invariant is silently false, with nothing to explain why.

**The fix**: added a new `relation_missing_fk` entry to `MigrationChange`'s type union in `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`, with a new `else if (!shape.fkTable && expectedFkTable)` branch alongside the existing `relation_target_changed` check (same parent `else if (field.type === "relation" && shape)` block) -- fires when the field now claims a real relation target but the physical column has no FK to compare at all. Reusing `relation_target_changed`'s own shape wasn't a good fit here (there's no real `fromRelationTo` to report, and its pipeline.ts message text, "kept pointing at the original related table," would be actively misleading when nothing was ever pointed anywhere), so this is a genuinely new, minimal shape instead: `{ type: "relation_missing_fk", table, column, toRelationTo }`. `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s existing Database-agent message gained one more filter + note clause, parallel to the two it already has for `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed`, warning that the field is a relation reusing a column that was never linked to anything and isn't protected against pointing at a nonexistent record. Consistent with this file's own established limitation for `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed`, this reports the gap rather than attempting to repair it -- SQLite can't add a FOREIGN KEY to an existing column any more than it can retype one, so an actual fix would require a full create-new-table-and-copy rebuild, out of scope for a reporting-only change.

**Tests**: `packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts` gained one test, placed directly after round 413's own `relation_target_changed` test and built the same way: a `boolean` field removed then re-added under the same name as a `relation` to `Customer` now reports `relation_missing_fk` (alongside the baseline `new_column`), and the real proof mirrors the file's established convention for this limitation -- `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` confirms the column still has zero FK, and inserting a record with a completely nonexistent `Customer` id in that field succeeds without error, documenting the exact gap this change type now surfaces instead of hiding.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both changed implementation files (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`, `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`) to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted both to HEAD (keeping the new test). The predicted failure occurred exactly: 112 passed, 1 failed -- the new test, showing the actual `changes` array missing its `relation_missing_fk` entry and only containing the plain `new_column`. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q` on each, then reran the full monorepo build and the full `@forge/db` and `@forge/api` suites clean. `codegen.ts` was re-confirmed (via `grep`) to have no `diffAndMigrate` equivalent at all, so no porting was needed there, consistent with round 395's and round 413's own prior findings.

Full suite green: **113 tests** in `@forge/db` (+1), **388 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged -- `pipeline.ts`'s message-construction code for these three change types has no dedicated unit test in `pipeline.test.ts`, consistent with the file's existing convention for `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed`, neither of which has one either), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/web`, `@forge/shared`, and `@forge/spec-engine` (untouched, no re-run needed) stayed at their round-413 counts. Pushed as commit `2d40055`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It closes the specific asymmetric gap left by round 413's own new relation-check branch -- the no-FK-at-all direction, which is strictly more severe than the documented, still-deliberately-deferred stale-FK-vs-boolean residual case (a spurious-but-real leftover constraint vs. total silent loss of referential integrity). Everything else still open from rounds 378-413 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 415: matchesSearch didn't match a number field's own displayed, comma-formatted value

**The survey**: with three rounds in a row (395, 413, 414) all landing inside `migrate.ts`'s relation-FK/type comparison logic, this round's Explore survey was explicitly told to broaden out to genuinely different files before proposing a fourth fix there, and to discount all four now-closed families (tolerant-listing completeness [409/411], staleness/race guards missing in a sibling [394/412], migration-diff one-step-back blindness [413], and asymmetric new-branch coverage [414]). It surfaced a candidate in `packages/shared/src/index.ts`: no refine anywhere validates that a `relation` field's `relationTo` actually names a real entity in the spec, which `migrate.ts`/`codegen.ts` both silently tolerate by just omitting the `REFERENCES` clause -- reproduced directly (schema accepts `relationTo: "customer"` against an entity named `Customer`; the resulting column has no FK at all, and a nonexistent id inserts cleanly).

**Independent verification turned up a conflict, not a bug**: before implementing the suggested fix (a new `ProductSpecSchema` refine rejecting any spec with an unresolvable `relationTo`), ran the full `@forge/spec-engine` test suite against it and got 10 failures, not the clean pass a correctness fix should get. Tracing the first one (`heuristic.test.ts`'s own "Order gets an optional courierId relation field pointing to Courier" test) led straight to `domainEntities.ts` lines 237-241: `Order.courierId`'s `relationTo: "Courier"` is **deliberately** present even when the `Courier` entity itself isn't included in the generated spec, with the file's own comment explicitly reasoning that "Required here would either force an invalid reference or block the build; null is a legitimate, honest value for 'not assigned yet' regardless." `docs/roadmap.md`'s own history (rounds 59-60 onward) confirms this is a long-standing, heavily-tested, intentional design decision, not an oversight -- a relation field is allowed to legitimately name an entity that doesn't (yet) exist in a given generated spec, trading a genuine but low-stakes integrity gap for not blocking the build or forcing an awkward required field. A blanket schema-level rejection can't distinguish this deliberate placeholder from an AI's accidental typo/case-mismatch, since both look identical structurally (a `relationTo` string with no matching entity name) -- so the validation-layer fix was reverted in full (confirmed via `git status`/`git checkout --` back to a clean tree, and the full `@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` suites green again) rather than risk breaking this established feature. This is the same "check if the 'problem' is a deliberate feature before fixing" lesson this Routine has carried since rounds 356-407, just encountered firsthand this round instead of caught by a stale note.

**The fix actually implemented** (a different, already-identified-but-not-yet-done "ready" candidate from the trigger's own small-candidates list, picked up after the above detour): `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s `matchesSearch` stringified a `number` field via bare `String(value)` (e.g. `"1500"`) when checking it against the search query, while the exact same value's table cell (`EntityPanel.tsx`, via `formatNumberValue`) renders with locale thousands separators (`"1,500"`) -- confirmed directly that both `en-US` and `he-IL` locales produce a comma separator here, so this isn't locale-specific. A user typing back precisely the digits they can see on screen, comma included, got zero matches for a record they're looking right at. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported-app copy of `matchesSearch` had the identical gap (its own table cell renders via plain `.toLocaleString()`), confirmed by direct read, consistent with round-384's standing check.

**The fix**: for a `number` field, `matchesSearch` now checks the query against both the plain and the locale-formatted representation (space-joined into one display string), so either "1500" or "1,500" still finds the row -- no regression for the existing plain-digit habit, and the new gap closed. Added an optional `lang: Lang = "en"` parameter to `matchesSearch` and `searchEntityRecords` (both appended at the end, so no existing positional call site needed to pass it to keep compiling) and threaded the real value through from `EntityPanel.tsx` and `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s two `searchEntityRecords` calls, both of which already had `lang` in scope. Ported the equivalent fix to `codegen.ts`'s plain-JS `matchesSearch`, with no `lang` parameter at all since the exported standalone app has no locale/i18n concept anywhere (confirmed by grep -- its number formatting is a bare, unparameterized `.toLocaleString()`).
