### Round 470: finally produced the `wakeRetry.ts` idempotency design -- grounded in every mutating route's real code, no implementation yet

**The candidate**: round 469's own closing note confirmed no small candidate was left after the buildWarning leak closed, and pointed at the one standing large candidate deferred since round 387 across many subsequent rounds (387 → 468 → 469): `wakeRetry.ts`'s retry-on-any-method duplicate-write risk, each time correctly deferred rather than rushed, given round 163's own history as a live warning about careless changes to this exact file.

**Independent verification/investigation**: read `wakeRetry.ts`'s actual retry condition directly and confirmed its own doc comment's safety claim ("a connection failure means the request was never received by the server at all") is accurate for the dominant case (a cold-start connection refusal, before any request bytes are sent) but not universally true for every way `fetch()` can throw -- a connection can also drop after the server fully received and processed a request but before the response made it back, which `fetch()` surfaces identically. Then read every mutating route in `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` and the client call sites in `apps/web/src/api.ts` to classify each one by REAL risk rather than guessing: confirmed `POST /projects/:id/build` is already double-guarded (`activePipelines` plus `project.status === "built"`), confirmed `POST /projects/:id/collaborators`'s `addCollaborator` (`packages/db/src/collaborators.ts:25-32`) is naturally safe via `INSERT OR IGNORE` against a `(projectId, userId)` primary key, confirmed every `DELETE` and value-overwrite `PATCH` route is naturally idempotent by HTTP semantics -- but confirmed `POST /projects` (create), `POST /projects/from-template`, and `POST /projects/:id/clone` have NO guard of any kind (`insertProject(db, { id: randomUUID(), ... })` runs unconditionally), and that `POST /projects/:id/refine` and `POST /projects/:id/answers`'s existing `activePipelines` guard only protects against a retry landing *while* the original is still running, not one landing after it already fully finished.

**The deliverable**: a new `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`, grounded in the file/line references above rather than abstract reasoning, recommending a client-generated idempotency key (one per logical user action, reused automatically across that action's own retries since `fetchWithWakeRetry`'s loop already re-sends the same `init`/headers on every attempt -- requiring zero changes to `wakeRetry.ts`'s own retry loop or to `fetchApi()`) checked server-side against a new, short-lived `idempotency_keys` table via a small opt-in helper mirroring `activePipelines`'s own existing guard-and-record shape. Explicitly scopes which specific routes would opt in (the unguarded creates, and the residual gap in refine/answers) versus which need nothing at all (everything already proven naturally safe above) -- deliberately avoiding a blanket middleware, matching this codebase's own established discipline against validating for scenarios that can't cause harm. Recommends starting implementation with `POST /projects` alone (highest real value: a wasted AI call plus a confusing orphaned duplicate draft project) rather than all routes at once, with a real test simulating "server fully processed the request, client never saw the response, client retries" before extending further. Lists three open product/review questions (TTL length, multi-tab/multi-user key scoping, and what to return on a replayed "done" key) for whoever picks up implementation.

**Regression-proof**: not applicable -- no runtime code changed this round (confirmed via `git status` showing only the new `.md` file). Ran a sanity `npm run build` anyway to confirm nothing else was inadvertently touched; it passed clean as expected for a docs-only change.

**Topic status**: design is closed; implementation remains open and is now a concrete, reviewable, incrementally-adoptable plan rather than an open-ended deferred worry. Everything else still open from rounds 378-469 (AI-label language mismatch, checkpoint pruning, render.yaml disk stanza, `listRecords` pagination, non-ASCII field name, `diffAndMigrate`'s `type_changed` oscillation, `CollaboratorsPanel` email enumeration, `calendarIcs.ts`'s `UID:` field skipping `icsEscapeText`) remains open and unchanged.

### Round 471: implemented idempotency keys for `POST /projects`, the narrow scope round 470's design doc recommended starting with

**The candidate**: round 470's own closing note explicitly recommended round 471 consider starting a real, narrowly-scoped implementation of the design it had just produced -- `POST /projects` alone, the single highest-value route (`docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`'s own "real, unguarded risk" section), rather than every route the design doc identified at once.

**Independent verification before implementing**: re-read the design doc in full and re-confirmed directly against the current code that `POST /projects` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:364-382` at the time) still had no guard of any kind -- `generateSpec()` followed by an unconditional `insertProject(db, { id: randomUUID(), ... })`. Read `packages/db/src/collaborators.ts`'s `addCollaborator` and `apps/api/src/store.ts`'s existing `ensureXTable` wiring pattern to model the new table/module on an established precedent rather than inventing a new shape.

**The implementation**: a new `idempotency_keys` table (`key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, userId, route, status, responseStatus, responseBody, createdAt`) and its CRUD functions in `packages/db/src/idempotency.ts`, wired into `apps/api/src/store.ts` the same way every other table is. A new `withIdempotency()` helper in `apps/api/src/idempotency.ts` mirrors `activePipelines`'s own guard-and-record shape exactly as the design doc specified: no key supplied -> runs the work directly (today's behavior, completely unchanged for every other route); key still `"in_progress"` -> throws `HttpError(409, ..., "DUPLICATE_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS")`; key already `"done"` -> replays the stored response without running the work again. One addition beyond the design doc's own helper sketch: when the guarded work throws, the key's row is deleted rather than left `"in_progress"` forever -- without this, a single real failure (e.g. the AI call erroring) would permanently brick every future retry with that same key, since it would always see a stuck "already in progress" row that will never actually finish. `POST /projects` now generates/reads `X-Idempotency-Key` and wraps its existing body in this helper with no other behavior change. The client (`apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `createProject`) generates one `crypto.randomUUID()` key per call via `request()`'s own `headers` override -- `fetchWithWakeRetry`'s retry loop already resends the same `init` object (headers included) on every attempt, so this required zero changes to `wakeRetry.ts` or `fetchApi()` themselves, exactly matching the design doc's central point about why this approach is safe to implement without touching the file round 163 warns against.

**Tests**: `packages/db/src/idempotency.test.ts` covers the raw table CRUD. `apps/api/src/idempotency.test.ts` unit-tests `withIdempotency` directly: no-key passthrough, first-call-persists-the-real-response, a same-key second call replaying the cached response without re-running the work, a same-key call while the first is still `"in_progress"` getting rejected with 409, and a failed first attempt's key being cleared so a retry can still succeed. `apps/api/src/app.test.ts` adds the real end-to-end repro the design doc called for: signs up a user, POSTs to `/api/projects` twice with the identical `X-Idempotency-Key` header (simulating the exact scenario -- "server fully processed the request, client never saw the response, client retries" -- since the guard can't tell a genuine network retry apart from this), and asserts the second response returns the exact same project id and that exactly one project exists afterward, not two. A second test confirms the no-key path is completely unaffected (two separate requests still create two separate projects). A third, using the existing `createGatedProvider()` test double (originally built for the `/refine` concurrency test), fires a same-key request while the first is still genuinely blocked mid-`generateSpec()`-call and confirms the real concurrent case gets 409 `DUPLICATE_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` instead of running a second AI call.

**A real regression caught mid-round**: the first full `@forge/web` suite run (837 tests) came back with exactly one failure -- the existing i18n error-code completeness scanner (`apps/web/src/i18n/language.test.ts`, itself round 425's own fix) correctly flagged that the new `DUPLICATE_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` error code had no Hebrew/English translation in `apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts`. Added both, modeled directly on the existing `PIPELINE_IN_PROGRESS` entry (the closest analog -- both are "a previous attempt is still running, wait and retry" 409s), and reran the scanner test alone to confirm it passed before rerunning the full suite.

**Regression-proof**: backed up every changed/new implementation file, reverted the modified ones via `git checkout --` and removed the two brand-new `idempotency.ts` files (kept all new/updated test files in place), then confirmed the exact predicted failures: the `POST /projects` retry test returned a *different* project id than the first attempt (proving a second project was wrongly created), the concurrent-collision test got `201` instead of the expected `409`, and both new `idempotency.test.ts` files failed to even load (`Cannot find module './idempotency.js'`) -- the module-load-crash pattern this session treats as a strong confirmation signal. Restored every file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran `@forge/db` (135, +5), `@forge/api` (424, +8), and the full `@forge/web` suite (837, clean after the i18n fix) plus a full `npm run build` from the repo root -- all green. Confirmed via direct inspection that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no project-creation route of any kind to duplicate this fix into -- creating a new Forge project is a platform-only concept that doesn't exist in an already-built exported app.

**Topic status**: `POST /projects` is now guarded; this is intentionally only the first of the several routes `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md` identified (`POST /projects/from-template`, `POST /projects/:id/clone`, the residual gap in `/refine` and `/answers`, and the append-only gap in `/roles`/`/assumptions`/`/entities`) -- matching the design doc's own explicit recommendation to prove the mechanism on the highest-value route first rather than rolling it out everywhere at once. Everything else still open from rounds 378-470 (AI-label language mismatch, checkpoint pruning, render.yaml disk stanza, `listRecords` pagination, non-ASCII field name, `diffAndMigrate`'s `type_changed` oscillation, `CollaboratorsPanel` email enumeration, `calendarIcs.ts`'s `UID:` field skipping `icsEscapeText`) remains open and unchanged.

### Round 474: extended idempotency keys to `POST /projects/:id/answers` -- the design doc's "SSE" grouping turned out to be only half right

**The candidate**: round 473's own closing note pointed at `POST /refine`/`POST /answers` as the one remaining gap, grouped together since round 470's design doc described both as SSE-streaming responses that wouldn't fit `withIdempotency()`'s plain `{status, body}` contract without adaptation.

But reading `/answers` directly (rather than trusting the design doc's grouping of the two together) showed it does no such thing: it calls `generateSpec()` then `updateProjectSpec()` then a plain `res.json({project: updated, providerName})`, confirmed further by the client side -- `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `answerQuestions` uses the ordinary `request()`/`fetchApi()` JSON path, while only `streamBuild`/`streamRefine` use the dedicated SSE `streamPipeline()` client helper. The original design doc's "residual gap" section had simply described `/refine` and `/answers` together as sharing the same `activePipelines`-only-protects-during-execution gap, without separately checking whether `/answers`'s *response shape* also matched `/refine`'s -- it doesn't.

The `activePipelines` add/remove moved inside `withIdempotency()`'s `run()` callback, so a cached replay (the key is already `"done"`) never touches `activePipelines` at all -- only a request that actually executes the work does, exactly matching the route's pre-existing concurrency semantics. The client (`apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `answerQuestions`) generates one `crypto.randomUUID()` key per call, the same as the six other routes already converted.

**Tests**: a new end-to-end test wraps `HeuristicSpecProvider` in a call-counting provider, since the heuristic provider is a pure function of its input -- a second real `generateSpec()` call on the retry would produce byte-identical output anyway, so comparing response bodies alone couldn't prove whether the work actually ran twice. The call count is what proves it: sends the identical `X-Idempotency-Key` twice for the same answers submission, and asserts `generateSpec()` was only invoked once while the retry's response is deep-equal to the first's.

Read `matchesSearch` directly (confirmed the ternary chain ended at `enum -> relation -> number -> String(value)` with no date case) and confirmed the existing `formatDateValue`/`parseFieldDate` helpers already used elsewhere in the same file for display rendering, with zero existing test coverage of `matchesSearch` against a `date`-typed field. This closes the one field type round 195's original search-matching diagnosis named alongside number/relation/enum but that was never actually fixed when those three were fixed in rounds 271/415/enum-sort.

**The implementation**: added a `field.type === "date"` branch to both copies of `matchesSearch`, in the same ternary-chain position as the existing `enum`/`relation`/`number` branches -- `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s copy reuses `formatDateValue(String(value), lang)`; `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated copy reuses the file's own hoisted `parseFieldDate` + `date.toLocaleDateString()` (no `lang` argument, matching `Cell()`'s own call). Both now match a record against `` `${value} ${formatted}` `` the same way the existing number/relation branches already did, so either the raw value or the displayed value matches.

### Round 476: fixed a WhatsApp log duplicate-message race in `handleLoadMore`

**The candidate**: round 475's closing note left round 476 open to either a real design for `/refine`'s SSE idempotency or a fresh Explore general-survey, given round 163's standing precedent against rushing any wakeRetry.ts-adjacent change without new information making it safer. No new information emerged, so dispatched an Explore survey instead, with an explicit denylist of everything already closed through round 475 so it wouldn't waste time rediscovering fixed issues.

**Independent verification before implementing**: the Explore agent flagged that `apps/web/src/WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s `handleLoadMore` (its "Load older messages" handler) reads `messages.length` as the offset for a server-side `OFFSET` query over a DESC-ordered log, then appends the result with an undeduplicated `[...prev, ...older]` concat -- unlike every other fetch-then-setMessages call site in the file, which goes through `mergeFreshMessages`'s own id-based dedup. Read `handleLoadMore` (`WhatsAppPanel.tsx:541-555` at the time) directly and confirmed the plain concat. Read `mergeFreshMessages` (lines 99-106) and confirmed its dedup pattern. Read `packages/db/src/whatsapp.ts`'s `listWhatsAppMessages` (`ORDER BY createdAt DESC, rowid DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`) and confirmed the offset-over-a-growing-head mechanism is real: a genuine incoming WhatsApp message landing between the client reading `messages.length` and the server running the query shifts the true order, so the returned "older" page's leading item(s) can already be in `prev`. Checked the existing round-432 regression test (`messagesVersionRef`, bumped only by `handleDeleteMessage`/`handleClearHistory`) and confirmed it guards a different race entirely (a delete/clear landing mid-fetch) -- nothing bumps that ref on a new incoming message, so this race had no existing guard. Confirmed via `grep` that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no WhatsApp integration at all (platform-only feature, no duplicate-copy risk).

**The implementation**: `handleLoadMore` now dedupes the fetched `older` page against `prev` by id before appending, mirroring `mergeFreshMessages`'s own approach (just appending the non-duplicate tail instead of prepending), with no change to `mergeFreshMessages`, `messagesVersionRef`, or any other call site.

**Tests**: a new end-to-end test simulates the race by having the mocked `offset=2` response return a page whose first item is already shown (as if a new message's insertion had shifted the true offset by one) followed by a genuinely new one, and asserts the rendered log settles at the correct count with no duplicate. First draft of this test waited on the "Load older messages" button's text disappearing, which also matches its own transient "Loading…" label the instant the click fires -- before the fetch's result (and the fix's dedup) had actually landed in `messages`. Caught by running the test for real (not just reasoning about it) and fixed by waiting on the actual rendered row count instead, matching this file's own established convention in the adjacent round-432 test.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the implementation file, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place), confirmed the exact predicted failure (`waitForCondition: condition never became true` -- the list stuck at the duplicated count, never reaching the expected deduped count). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite green: `@forge/db` 135 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 432 (unchanged -- this fix is web-only), `@forge/web` 841 (+1), full `npm run build` clean from the repo root.

**Topic status**: this `handleLoadMore` duplicate-message race is closed. ### Round 477: fixed the Architect build message's self-contradictory "gaining fields" headline

**The candidate**: round 476's closing note recommended round 477 either continue the same low-risk Explore-survey pattern (two consecutive rounds had each found a small, safe fix this way) or take on a dedicated `/refine` SSE idempotency design round. Read `architectEvent` (`pipeline.ts:149-178` at the time) directly and confirmed line 167 used the raw `changedEntities.length` with no filter. Confirmed the concrete contradiction: an entity that only lost a field (e.g. a refine dropping `Order.notes`, with nothing added) produces a message reading "...1 existing entities gaining fields. Warning: Order lost field(s): notes..." -- the headline and the very next sentence directly contradict each other for the same entity. Read the existing round-397 regression test (`pipeline.test.ts`, the "...not as 'gaining fields'" test) and confirmed its `assert.doesNotMatch` used a regex with a negative lookahead for `" Warning"` immediately after `"gaining fields."` -- since the real message always has `" Warning"` right there, the lookahead never matched, so `doesNotMatch` passed vacuously and never actually checked the count. Confirmed via `grep` that `apps/web/src/BuildProgress.tsx`'s own structured detail renderer (`AgentDetail`) already correctly guards its "gained fields" line with `newFieldNames.length > 0`, so only the plain-text `message` string (shown verbatim above that detail) was wrong -- the two parts of the same event visibly disagreed. **The implementation**: added `entitiesWithNewFields` (`impact.changedEntities.filter((e) => e.newFieldNames.length > 0)`) alongside the existing `entitiesWithRemovedFields`/`entitiesWithTightenedFields` filters, and used its `.length` in the headline sentence instead of the raw `changedEntities.length`. No change to `computeImpact` itself or to any other call site.

**Tests**: strengthened the existing round-397 test's vacuous assertion -- replaced the no-op `assert.doesNotMatch` with a direct `assert.match` against the correct headline text (`/\+0 new entities \(none\), 0 existing entities gaining fields\./`), which actually fails against the old, unfixed code instead of passing regardless.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `pipeline.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the strengthened test in place), confirmed the exact predicted failure (the round-397 test failed, every other test in the file still passed: 22/23). ### Round 480: the `idempotency_keys` table had no TTL/cleanup, growing unbounded forever — closed the design doc's own open question

**The candidate**: a fifth consecutive fresh Explore survey (explicitly denylisted against every closed topic from rounds 475-479) found that `idempotency_keys` -- the table backing `withIdempotency()` (wired into 8 routes across rounds 471-474) -- has no expiry mechanism at all. `completeIdempotencyRecord` (`packages/db/src/idempotency.ts`) flips a row to `"done"` and stores the full JSON response body *permanently*; only the failure path (`deleteIdempotencyRecord`) ever removes a row, and nothing sweeps a successful row afterward. Grepping across `packages/db` and `apps/api` for "TTL"/"expire"/"cleanup"/"prune" turned up nothing outside `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`'s own prose. That design doc (round 470) explicitly flagged this: *"A short TTL cleanup (e.g. rows older than 24h deleted on a schedule, or opportunistically on each insert) is enough,"* then listed **"TTL length"** as the first of three **"Open questions for whoever implements this"** -- an open question the four rounds (471-474) that actually wired the mechanism into real routes never answered. This is a materially different kind of gap than anything in the wakeRetry denylist (those are all about per-route *retry correctness*, already closed): this is about the storage mechanism's own *lifecycle*, never addressed.

**Independent verification**: read `packages/db/src/idempotency.ts` and `apps/api/src/idempotency.ts` in full. Confirmed `ensureIdempotencyKeysTable`'s own doc comment already calls the table "deliberately short-lived, not a permanent audit log" -- but that claim was only ever true for the *failure* path (`deleteIdempotencyRecord`, called from `withIdempotency`'s `catch` block); a `"done"` row from a successful request has no code path that ever removes it. Confirmed `withIdempotency` has no age check anywhere -- `getIdempotencyRecord` returns a `"done"` row of any age and it gets replayed forever, turning what the design doc calls a short retry-window mechanism into a permanent cache that also leaks storage.

**The implementation**: added `pruneExpiredIdempotencyRecords(db, maxAgeMs)` to `packages/db/src/idempotency.ts` -- a single `DELETE FROM idempotency_keys WHERE createdAt < ?` against an ISO-string cutoff (ISO 8601 with a `Z` suffix sorts correctly as a plain string, so no date parsing needed). Deliberately prunes *both* `"done"` and `"in_progress"` rows by age, not just `"done"` ones: this also self-heals a row orphaned `"in_progress"` by a server crash mid-request, a case `deleteIdempotencyRecord`'s own catch-path can never reach (the process died before the catch block could run) and the design doc's TTL discussion didn't call out by name but which falls out of the same age cutoff for free. Exported it from `packages/db/src/index.ts`. Wired it into `apps/api/src/idempotency.ts`'s `withIdempotency`, called opportunistically at the top -- before the existing-record lookup, not after -- with a new `IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS = 24h` constant, using the design doc's own suggested default and its own suggested implementation strategy ("opportunistically on each insert," chosen over a scheduled sweep since this app has no cron/scheduler infrastructure at all -- adding one would be a disproportionate architectural addition for a single-table cleanup). Running it before the lookup (not just before the insert) matters: it's what makes an aged-out key for a `"done"` response stop being replayed and instead get treated as brand-new, not just stop the table from growing. Updated `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`'s own "Open questions" section to mark item 1 (TTL length) resolved, pointing at the new function -- so a future round reading that doc doesn't re-open a question this round actually answered.

**Tests**: a new unit test in `packages/db/src/idempotency.test.ts` backdates two rows (one `"done"`, one `"in_progress"`) via the same raw-SQL `UPDATE ... SET createdAt = ?` pattern `apps/api/src/twin.test.ts` already uses to simulate an old record, prunes with a 24h cutoff, and confirms both old rows are gone while a freshly-inserted third row survives. A new test in `apps/api/src/idempotency.test.ts` runs `withIdempotency` once to get a real `"done"` row, backdates it the same way, then calls `withIdempotency` again with the same key and confirms the guarded work actually runs a second time (not replayed from the stale cached response) -- the flip side of the existing "replays the cached response" test two tests above it.

### Round 481: a blank/unnamed CSV import column silently bound itself to the first unlabeled field instead of being ignored

**The candidate**: a seventh consecutive fresh Explore survey (explicitly denylisted against every closed topic from rounds 475-480) found a real data-correctness bug in `matchesHeader` (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`): `return normalized === field.name.toLowerCase() || normalized === (field.label ?? "").toLowerCase();`. When a field has no `label` set, `(field.label ?? "").toLowerCase()` evaluates to `""` -- so a genuinely blank CSV header cell (a stray trailing comma, an unlabeled spreadsheet column) matches that condition and gets claimed by the *first* unlabeled field in the entity, instead of being ignored the way a column with real, unmatched text already correctly is (see the pre-existing `"buildImportRecords ignores an unmatched CSV column instead of erroring on it"` test, which only ever exercised a *non-empty* unmatched header). This is reachable in real usage, not just a contrived edge case: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s entity field definitions never set `.label` at all in the English-mode path (`withLabels` only applies labels under the Hebrew path), so most generated entities have unlabeled fields by default.

**Independent verification**: read `matchesHeader` and `buildImportRecords` in full and confirmed the logic directly rather than trusting the agent's description. Reproduced with a tiny standalone script: fields `[{name:"name",required:true}, {name:"notes",required:false}]` (neither labeled), CSV `"name,\nDana,this is garbage from an unrelated blank column\n"` -- the blank second header column bound itself to `notes` and the garbage text landed in the imported record. Confirmed via `grep` that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s duplicated `matchesImportHeader`/`buildImportRecords` has the identical bug (`(field.label || "")`), since it mirrors `entityFormatting.ts`'s CSV-import logic line for line.

**The implementation**: added a one-line guard to both `matchesHeader` (`entityFormatting.ts`) and `matchesImportHeader` (`codegen.ts`) -- `if (!normalized) return false;` right after trimming/lowercasing the header, before either comparison. A blank header can never legitimately refer to any field by name or label, so this makes a blank column fall through to the existing "unmatched column is ignored" path instead of ever being considered a match.

**Tests**: a new test in `entityFormatting.test.ts`, placed right after the existing "ignores an unmatched CSV column" test, using two unlabeled fields and a blank second header cell; confirms the imported record keeps `notes: null` (the same value any other unmatched optional field already gets) rather than the blank column's garbage text. A parallel test in `codegen.test.ts` uses this file's own established regex-extraction technique (`matchesImportHeader`/`buildImportRecords` pulled out of the real generated `EntityView.jsx` via regex, executed via `new Function`, not reimplemented) with the same unlabeled-fields setup, confirming the same behavior in the exported app's own duplicated CSV import logic.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both implementation files (`entityFormatting.ts`, `codegen.ts`), reverted them via `git checkout --` (keeping both new and all pre-existing tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failures in isolation: both new tests failed with the blank column's garbage text (`"this is garbage from an unrelated blank column"`) showing up in `notes` instead of `null`, every other test in both files (139/139 and 157/157) still green. Restored both from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite green across all five test packages: `@forge/db` 136 (unchanged), `@forge/shared` 16 (unchanged), `@forge/spec-engine` 109 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 437 (+1), `@forge/web` 843 (+1), full `npm run build` clean from the repo root.

**Topic status**: a blank/unnamed CSV column is now correctly ignored in both the live preview and the exported app, matching the already-documented behavior for a column with real, unmatched text. The wakeRetry candidate's remaining gap (`/refine`/`/build` SSE) is unchanged and still deliberately deferred. ### Round 482: design-only round — a concrete, reviewed plan for closing `/refine`'s remaining idempotency gap (no code changed)

**The candidate**: an eighth consecutive fresh Explore survey (explicitly denylisted against every closed topic from rounds 475-481) came back with an honest **nothing found** -- a legitimate result this session's own standing process explicitly allows, not a forced weak finding. With the small-bug vein genuinely thin after eight rounds of harvesting it, and the one large standing candidate (`docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`'s `/refine`/`/build` SSE gap, deferred every round since 475) still open, this round did real work on it in the one safe way the trigger's own standing caution allows: a design-only round, mirroring round 470's own original approach, with zero code changes to the request path round 163's incident lives in.

**The investigation**: re-read `routes/projects.ts`'s `/build` and `/refine` handlers and `streamPipeline` line by line, and `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s client-side `streamPipeline`/`fetchApi`/`fetchWithWakeRetry` wiring, rather than trusting the existing design doc's own framing at face value. Two concrete findings sharpened and corrected that doc:
1. **`/build` has no gap at all** (confirms the doc's existing verdict, now verified fresh): `project.status === "built"` rejects a delayed retry landing after a first `/build` already succeeded, on top of `activePipelines` rejecting one landing during. Nothing to design for `/build`.
2. **`/refine`'s real reachable window is narrower than the doc's original framing, but still real**: `streamPipeline`'s client-side read loop (`api.ts:460-474`) does NOT re-enter `fetchWithWakeRetry` on a mid-stream network failure -- it just throws. The actual risk is specifically a retry of `/refine`'s *initial* POST (which does go through `fetchWithWakeRetry`, same as every other request) landing after the original attempt already ran to completion server-side, with nothing analogous to `/build`'s status check to catch it. This is the single most expensive route in the whole inventory to hit if it does.

**The design produced**: an addendum to `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md` proposing `withIdempotencyStream` -- a direct generalization of the existing `withIdempotency` helper from a single `{status, body}` JSON value to an ordered array of `AgentStepEvent`s, reusing every existing piece (the `idempotency_keys` table, its TTL prune, the insert/complete/delete helpers) unchanged. A "done" replay writes every recorded event back-to-back with no artificial delay, matching the client's own event-driven (not timing-dependent) consumption. Two new open questions were added for a future implementer: re-verifying the "`/build` needs no changes" verdict before trusting it secondhand, and how to test a stream-shaped idempotency guard (asserting replayed events match the original ones byte-for-byte, not just that some events came back).

**Why this stays design-only**: `/refine`'s request path is the exact family of code round 163's own incident lives in, and every round since 475 has repeated the same standing caution against touching it in haste. This addendum exists so a future round that does implement it starts from a reviewed plan instead of reasoning it out from scratch under time pressure -- exactly the service round 470's original document provided for the six routes (471-474, 480) that have since been safely shipped from it.

**Regression-proof**: not applicable in the usual sense (no implementation code changed -- `git status` shows only `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`). Ran the full test suite across all five packages and the root build anyway, as a sanity check that a documentation-only change left everything else untouched: `@forge/db` 136, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 437, `@forge/web` 843 (all unchanged from round 481), `npm run build` clean.

### Round 483: four of five copied "click-to-rename" inline editors were keyboard-unreachable

**The candidate**: a ninth consecutive fresh Explore survey (denylisted against every closed topic through round 482) found a genuine, demonstrable gap: `ProjectNameEditor.tsx`, `ProjectDescriptionEditor.tsx`, `EntityLabelEditor.tsx`, and `CheckpointLabelEditor.tsx` -- four near-identical "click the display text to rename it" components, each copied from the last (their own doc comments say so explicitly) -- all rendered their edit trigger as a bare `<h1>`/`<p>`/`<h3>`/`<strong>` with only an `onClick` handler: no `tabIndex`, no `role`, no `onKeyDown`. A keyboard-only or screen-reader user could never focus, let alone activate, any of them. The fifth sibling in the same copied family, `FieldLabelEditor.tsx`, already used a real `<button type="button">` for its own trigger and never had this gap -- making this a concrete inconsistency within one tightly-related component family, not a vague "could be more accessible" observation.

**The investigation**: read all five components' full source directly (not just the subagent's excerpt), and grepped `App.tsx`/`EntityPanel.tsx`/`HistoryPanel.tsx` to confirm each of the four is genuinely the *only* way to trigger that rename -- no overflow menu, no alternate button, no keyboard shortcut exists anywhere else. Also grepped `codegen.ts` for all five component names: no matches, confirming these are live-preview-only (no exported-app duplicate to carry the same fix, unlike most prior rounds' findings).

**The fix**: added `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}`, and an `onKeyDown` handler (`Enter`/`Space` calls `startEditing()`, with `e.preventDefault()`) to each of the four bare trigger elements -- mirroring the identical pattern already used by `EntityPanel.tsx`'s calendar-day cells (`tabIndex`/`role="button"`/`onKeyDown` on `Enter`/`Space`). Kept each element's existing tag (`h1`/`p`/`h3`/`strong`) and visual styling untouched rather than swapping in a `<button>`, since unlike `FieldLabelEditor`'s standalone icon-button these elements wrap the entire display text plus a decorative edit-icon span, and the ARIA role/tabIndex addition is sufficient and minimal.

**Regression-proof**: added one new test per component (`ProjectNameEditor.test.ts`, `ProjectDescriptionEditor.test.ts`, `EntityLabelEditor.test.ts`, `CheckpointLabelEditor.test.ts`) asserting `role="button"`/`tabIndex="0"` on the trigger and that firing a `keyDown` with `key: "Enter"` opens edit mode. Backed up the 4 implementation files, reverted them via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests), ran just those 4 test files: all 4 new tests failed with exactly the predicted outcome (Enter never opened edit mode) while all 10 pre-existing tests in those files still passed. Restored the 4 files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build: `@forge/db` 136, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 437, `@forge/web` 847 (+4), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this specific gap is closed. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open, implementation still deliberately deferred pending an explicit future decision. Everything else still open from rounds 378-482 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 485: j/k keyboard row-navigation could silently focus, then edit/delete/duplicate, a record hidden inside a collapsed group

**The candidate**: an eleventh consecutive fresh Explore survey was given two tasks: first, proactively re-check the whole of `apps/web/src/*.tsx` for any further instance of round 483/484's exact pattern (a non-interactive `onClick`-only trigger with no keyboard path) -- that systematic grep (159 `onClick`s in `apps/web/src`, cross-checked against `codegen.ts`'s 56 duplicates) came back genuinely clean, a good-faith confirmation that the specific accessibility pattern is now fully closed everywhere it appears. Falling back to a general survey, it found a different, real bug in the same neighborhood: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s j/k row-navigation (round 188) computes its navigable row list from the flat `visibleRecords` array, with no awareness of table grouping (round 344) or group-collapse (round 419). When a group is collapsed, its records are skipped from the `<tbody>` entirely, but the flat `visibleIds` list still contained their ids.

**The investigation**: read `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `handleKeyDown` effect (lines 1474-1507) and the grouped-table body render (lines 2771-2812) directly, confirming the exact mechanism: `visibleIds = visibleRecords.map(...)` versus the `<tbody>`'s own `{!collapsed && group.records.map(renderRecordRow)}`, which genuinely omits a collapsed group's rows from the DOM. `computeNextFocusedRowId` (entityFormatting.ts) walks `visibleIds` by plain array index, so "j"/"k" could land `focusedRowId` on a record with no rendered `<tr>` at all -- no highlight appears (nothing has the `record-row-focused` class), but Enter/"x"/Delete/Backspace/"d" all branch on `focusedRowId != null` alone and call `startEdit`/`toggleSelected`/`handleDelete`/`handleDuplicate` directly by id, with no visibility check, so they'd silently act on a record the user never saw land under the cursor. Grepped every `setFocusedRowId(` call site (only the two j/k handlers) and confirmed nothing resets focus when `groupFieldName`/`collapsedGroups` changes. Grepped `codegen.ts` and found the identical duplicated bug in its own copy of this exact feature (`visibleIds = visibleRecords.map((r) => r.id)` at the equivalent line), confirming both live preview and exported app needed the fix.

**Why this isn't on the denylist**: round 462 fixed a different bug in the same area -- the jump-to-record *highlight* effect not clearing `groupFieldName` -- but never touched `visibleIds`/`focusedRowId`/`computeNextFocusedRowId`, a separate code path from an earlier round (188) that round 344's later collapse feature never revisited.

**The fix**: `visibleIds` is now derived from the actual rendered set (`recordGroups.flatMap((g) => collapsedGroups.has(g.key) ? [] : g.records)` when grouped, the flat array otherwise) in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, so j/k can no longer land on an invisible row at all. Additionally guarded the Enter/x/Delete/d branches with `focusedRowId != null && visibleIds.includes(focusedRowId)` instead of a bare null check, closing the narrower follow-on case where a group is collapsed by mouse while it already holds the keyboard focus.

**Regression-proof**: added one new test to each of `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts` (the latter using the real generated `EntityView.jsx`, not a reimplementation) confirming j/k clamps at the one visible record instead of landing on either of two records hidden inside a collapsed "Won" group. A first full-suite run surfaced one unrelated failure in `BuildProgress.test.ts` (an `onComplete` warning-message assertion); re-ran that file alone (31/31 passed) and the full web suite again cleanly (852/852) confirming it was a parallel-run flake, not a real regression, before proceeding. Backed up both implementation files, reverted via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests): both new tests failed with exactly the predicted outcome (focus still landed on a hidden record) while all 105 pre-existing `EntityPanel.test.ts` tests and all 158 pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` tests still passed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build: `@forge/db` 136, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 438 (+1), `@forge/web` 852 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed in both the live preview and the exported app. The round 483/484 accessibility-pattern re-scan came back clean, so that specific topic is considered fully closed unless a future round finds a genuinely new instance. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-484 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 486: "select all" silently included records hidden inside a collapsed group -- the same staleness pattern as round 485, in a different code path

**The candidate**: a twelfth consecutive fresh Explore survey was pointed at round 485's own pattern explicitly -- a newer feature (table grouping/collapse) added without reconciling an existing feature that shares the same "which records are visible" concept -- and asked to look for other instances of it, since j/k navigation was only one of several features built on top of `visibleRecords`. It found one: `toggleSelectAllVisible` and the header "select all" checkbox's own `checked`/`indeterminate` computation (`EntityPanel.tsx`) both read `visibleRecords` directly, the same staleness class round 485 fixed for keyboard navigation, but in the bulk-selection code path instead -- a feature built earlier (round ~53) that table grouping/collapse (rounds 344/419) never revisited, just like j/k wasn't.

**The investigation**: read `toggleSelectAllVisible` (`EntityPanel.tsx`) and the header checkbox's `checked`/`ref` logic directly, confirming both iterate `visibleRecords` in full with no `collapsedGroups` awareness, while the `<tbody>` itself (same render block round 485 already read) skips a collapsed group's rows entirely. Traced the consequence forward: `selectedIds` (populated by "select all") feeds the bulk-actions bar's own count, `handleBulkDelete`/`handleBulkDuplicate`/`handleBulkUpdate` (which intentionally act on raw `selectedIds` regardless of search/filter, per their own documented rationale), and `selectedOrAllRecords` (used by CSV export-selected and print-selected) -- so a stale `selectedIds` silently propagates into four different bulk operations, not just the checkbox's own visual state. [] : g.records)` when grouped, the flat array otherwise -- the same expression round 485 wrote inline for the keyboard handler, now a reusable value) in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, and used it in place of `visibleRecords` in `toggleSelectAllVisible` and the header checkbox's `checked`/`indeterminate` logic. `selectedOrAllRecords`'s own contract didn't need to change: once "select all" itself never adds a hidden group's ids to `selectedIds`, every downstream consumer (bulk actions, CSV export-selected, print-selected) is automatically correct too.

**Regression-proof**: added one new test to each of `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts` (the latter using the real generated `EntityView.jsx`) confirming "select all" while "Won" is collapsed only selects the one visible record, and that re-expanding "Won" afterward shows its own two records still unselected. Backed up both implementation files, reverted via `git checkout --`: both new tests failed with exactly the predicted outcome (the header checkbox and `selectedIds` both still included the hidden group's records) while all 106 pre-existing `EntityPanel.test.ts` tests and all 159 pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` tests still passed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build: `@forge/db` 136, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 439 (+1), `@forge/web` 853 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

### Round 488: seed data generated a 0-day date range for checkInDate/checkoutDate-style field pairs

**The candidate**: a fourteenth consecutive fresh Explore survey (denylisted against every closed topic through round 487) found that `packages/db/src/seed.ts`'s `seedValueFor` determines whether a `date`-type field is an "end of range" field (which needs to land chronologically after its sibling date field, not collapse to the same day) via `const isEndLike = /end/i.test(field.name);` -- a literal-substring check that only ever matches a field genuinely named something containing "end" (like `endDate`). A field named `checkoutDate`, `returnDate`, `untilDate`, or `toDate` -- all equally plausible, common choices for a booking/rental-style entity, and arguably more natural than "startDate/endDate" for a hotel, car-rental, or venue-booking app -- doesn't contain that substring, so both fields in the pair seed to the identical date: every demo record becomes a visibly wrong 0-day stay.

**Independent verification**: read `seed.ts` line 95 directly and confirmed the literal regex. Read `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` (`["enddate", "returndate", "checkoutdate", "untildate", "todate"]`) and `findEndDateField` (lines 648, 664-666) and confirmed this is exactly the list the live app's own calendar view and ICS export already use to recognize a genuine end-of-range field -- grepped both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts` and confirmed `findEndDateField` is wired into both (duplicated, same pattern as always). So an entity with a `checkoutDate` field already gets real multi-day-range rendering on the calendar and in exported `.ics` files, but its seeded demo data never actually spans more than one day -- undermining the exact "see your ranged bookings on a calendar" feature the demo data exists to showcase. Confirmed via `grep` that `packages/db/src/seed.test.ts`'s only existing regression test (line 292) covers exclusively the literal `startDate`/`endDate` pair, with no coverage for any of the other four hint-list conventions. Confirmed via `grep` that `codegen.ts` has no duplicate of `seedValueFor`/`generateSeedRecords` at all -- seeding happens once, server-side, during `/build`, so this is a single-file fix with no codegen.ts port needed.

**The fix**: added a local `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` const to `seed.ts` (duplicated from `entityFormatting.ts`, matching this codebase's established "small duplicated hint array per surface" convention rather than a cross-package import), and replaced the literal-substring regex with `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS.includes(field.name.toLowerCase())`.

**Tests**: a new test in `seed.test.ts`, placed right after the existing `startDate`/`endDate` test, using a `Booking` entity with `checkInDate`/`checkoutDate` fields, confirming the two dates are now distinct and `checkoutDate` lands after `checkInDate` -- the same assertions the pre-existing test already makes for the literal `endDate` name, now covering one of the four previously-unmatched conventions.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `seed.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure in isolation: the new test failed with `checkInDate` and `checkoutDate` both equal to the same date (`"checkInDate and checkoutDate must not collapse to the same day"`), while all 17 pre-existing tests in the file still passed. Restored `seed.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build: `@forge/db` 137 (+1), `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 441, `@forge/web` 855, `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. Entities with any of the five recognized end-of-range field-name conventions now get correctly-ordered seed dates, matching what the calendar view and ICS export already assume about them. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-487 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 489: the exported app's table keyboard shortcuts leaked through its own GlobalSearch overlay

**The candidate**: a fifteenth consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported `EntityView`'s j/k/x/d/Delete/Enter/n keyboard-shortcut handlers only ever guarded against `isTypingTarget`, never against the exported app's one overlay dialog, `GlobalSearch`, being open on top of the table -- a direct port gap of a bug the live preview fixed back in round 365.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` lines 1479-1547 and confirmed `isAnyDialogOpen()` (from `useDialogFocusTrap.ts`) already guards both of its own table-shortcut handlers there, exactly as round 365's own comment describes: "pressing j/k/x/d while reading the shortcuts cheat-sheet silently mutated or deleted a background row the person wasn't even looking at." Grepped `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` for `isAnyDialogOpen`/`useDialogFocusTrap`: zero matches anywhere in the file. Read both of `EntityView`'s own handlers (lines 3029-3055, 3080-3087 at the time) and confirmed each only checked `isTypingTarget(e.target)`. Read `GlobalSearch`'s own render output and confirmed it has several focusable, non-input controls (its own Close button, recent-search chips, "Show all") that `isTypingTarget` can't catch, plus confirmed `activeEntity.View` stays fully mounted underneath the `{showSearch && <GlobalSearch .../>}` overlay (so its window-level keydown listeners keep firing regardless of focus).

**The fix**: `GlobalSearch` is generated as a *separate* ES module (`web/src/components/GlobalSearch.jsx`) from `EntityView` (`web/src/components/EntityView.jsx`), so the live preview's own single-file `isAnyDialogOpen()` mount-counter pattern couldn't be ported as-is -- a bare module-scoped `let` in one file can't be mutated directly from another module. Added a module-scoped `searchDialogOpenCount`/`isSearchDialogOpen()` pair to `EntityView.jsx`, plus two exported mutator functions (`markSearchDialogOpen`/`markSearchDialogClosed`) for `GlobalSearch.jsx` to call from its own mount/unmount effect. Both of `EntityView`'s keydown handlers now check `isTypingTarget(e.target) || isSearchDialogOpen()`, mirroring the live preview's own guard exactly. Caught and fixed a real bug in my own first draft before it ever reached a test: the initial version had `GlobalSearch`'s effect mutate `searchDialogOpenCount` directly without importing it, which would have silently no-op'd (a plain top-level `let` is module-private; only an explicitly exported accessor can be read or written from outside) -- found by tracing the generated file boundaries directly rather than assuming shared module scope.

**Tests**: a new full-DOM test in `codegen.test.ts` renders both the real generated `EntityView` and `GlobalSearch` components together (as they'd be mounted as siblings in the real app), focuses a row with "j", confirms "d" does *not* duplicate it while `GlobalSearch` is mounted, then unmounts `GlobalSearch` and confirms "d" works normally again -- proving the guard is real, not just always-on. A pre-existing source-text test asserting `GlobalSearch.jsx`'s exact import line from `EntityView.jsx` was updated to include the two new mutator names.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `codegen.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping both test changes in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failures in isolation: the new test failed with the duplicate firing anyway (`postCount` 1 instead of 0), and the updated import-line test failed against the old (shorter) import line, with the other 161 pre-existing tests in the file still passing (163 total, 161 pass + 2 fail). Restored `codegen.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. A first full web-suite run surfaced the known `BuildProgress.test.ts` parallel-run flake again (isolated run: 31/31 clean; full suite re-run: 855/855 clean) before concluding -- no web file was touched this round, consistent with it being unrelated. Full suite + root build: `@forge/db` 137, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 442 (+1), `@forge/web` 855 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this port gap is closed. The live preview was never affected (it already had the guard since round 365) -- this was purely a one-directional codegen.ts port gap. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-488 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 490: viewMode never fell back to "table" when a live refine removed the entity's own board/date field

**The candidate**: a sixteenth consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that `EntityPanel.tsx`'s viewMode-revalidation effect's own doc comment claims it falls back to "table" when the persisted view needs a board/date field the entity no longer has, but its dependency array was only `[projectId, entity.name]` -- missing `boardFieldName`/`dateFieldName`, unlike the sibling `collapsedBoardColumns` effect written right above it in the same file, which already handles the identical "a field the view depends on can silently change identity" concern (round 435) by including `boardFieldName` in its own deps.

**Independent verification**: read the effect directly (lines 1087-1093 at the time) and confirmed the dependency array omission. Confirmed `boardField`/`dateField` are `useMemo`s keyed on `entity.fields` (lines 880-882), so they recompute live on every render when `entity.fields` changes shape -- but this effect never re-ran to react to that, only on an actual entity-tab switch. Confirmed via `App.tsx` that `EntityPanel` is rendered with `key={entity.name}` only (not keyed by `entity.fields`), so a refine that mutates the currently-active entity's own field list does NOT remount `EntityPanel` -- it re-renders in place with a new `entity` prop. Confirmed the two visible consequences by reading the render gates: the group-by `<select>`'s gate is `viewMode === "table" && groupableFields.length > 0` (so it stays hidden while `viewMode` is stuck on the stale `"board"` string, even though the table is what's actually rendering), and the view-toggle buttons' active-class checks (`viewMode === "table"`/`"board"`/`"calendar"`) all fail to match the stale value, leaving no button showing as active. Confirmed via `grep` that `codegen.ts` has no equivalent revalidation effect at all -- the exported app has no Refine feature, so `entity.fields` never mutates at runtime there, making this bug's precondition architecturally unreachable in the exported app.

**The fix**: added `const dateFieldName = dateField?.name ?? "";` alongside the already-existing `boardFieldName`, changed the effect's `stillValid` check to read `boardFieldName`/`dateFieldName` (string truthiness) instead of the `boardField`/`dateField` objects directly (avoiding an ESLint `exhaustive-deps` mismatch between what the body reads and what the dependency array lists), and added `boardFieldName, dateFieldName` to the effect's own dependency array -- removing the `eslint-disable-next-line` that previously suppressed the warning this fix now resolves correctly instead.

**Tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, placed right after round 435's own `collapsedBoardColumns` regression test (the closest existing precedent for "a schema edit changes which field a view depends on, without remounting"). Renders an entity with a `status` (board-eligible enum), an `isPriority` (groupable boolean), and a `dueDate` (date) field; switches to Board view; then uses the same `view.rerender(buildEntityPanelElement({...}))` pattern (no remount, mirroring `App.tsx`'s real `key={entity.name}` behavior) to simulate a refine removing `status` while keeping `dueDate`. Confirms the board stops rendering, the group-by select reappears (proving `viewMode` genuinely reached `"table"`, not just that the board's own render gate separately caught the missing field), exactly the Table and Calendar toggle buttons remain (Board's own button disappears since there's no longer a board field), and the Table button -- not neither button -- shows as active.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `EntityPanel.tsx`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure in isolation: the new test failed on the group-by-select assertion (stale `viewMode` still `"board"`), while all 109 pre-existing tests in the file still passed. Restored `EntityPanel.tsx` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. A full api-suite sanity check (no api file touched this round) surfaced one unrelated timing flake (`"concurrent hashPassword calls run in parallel, not serialized one after another"`); isolated run confirmed clean (7/7), and a full re-run confirmed 442/442 clean, consistent with this session's documented single-flake-in-parallel-run pattern -- a new instance of it, this time in a different file (`password.test.ts`) than the previously-seen `BuildProgress.test.ts` flake, reinforcing that the pattern is about concurrent-run timing pressure in general, not one specific test. Full suite + root build: `@forge/db` 137, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 442, `@forge/web` 856 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. It's a live-preview-only bug (no codegen.ts port needed, since the exported app's spec is baked in at export time and the Refine feature that triggers this bug's precondition doesn't exist there). ### Round 491: the table's grand-total tfoot kept counting a collapsed group's records

**The candidate**: a seventeenth consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that `numericFieldTotals` (the grand total shown in the table's `<tfoot>`) was computed via `sumNumericFields(visibleRecords, visibleFields)` -- the flat, collapse-unaware record set -- rather than `effectivelyVisibleRecords`, the collapse-aware value rounds 486-487 already migrated every other on-screen aggregate/action to (select-all, bulk actions, CSV export/copy, print, j/k navigation). This is a genuinely new consumer the earlier visible-staleness migration never touched, not a reopening of that already-closed pattern: the totals footer is a distinct feature (round 297) from everything the 485-487 fixes covered.

**Independent verification**: read `EntityPanel.tsx` directly and confirmed `numericFieldTotals` (originally lines 1392-1395) was declared and computed *before* `effectivelyVisibleRecords` even existed in scope (originally lines 1425-1428), reading `visibleRecords` instead. Confirmed `effectivelyVisibleRecords`'s own doc comment explicitly states its purpose is excluding "a collapsed group's records," and confirmed by reading the `<tfoot>` render block (lines 2846-2862) that it renders unconditionally whenever `hasNumericVisibleField` is true, with no collapse-awareness of its own -- unlike the per-group subtotal rows right above it in the `<tbody>` (lines 2824-2840), which correctly use `groupNumericTotals` keyed off each group's own `group.records` and are properly hidden when `collapsed` is true. Grepped `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` and confirmed the identical gap, duplicated verbatim (`numericFieldTotals` at the time computed from `visibleRecords` at lines 2957-2960, before `effectivelyVisibleRecords`'s own definition at lines 2978-2981, with the `<tfoot>` render at lines 4171-4183 having the same gap).

**The fix**: in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, moved the `numericFieldTotals` `useMemo` to after `effectivelyVisibleRecords`'s own definition (required, since `effectivelyVisibleRecords` itself depends on `recordGroups`/`collapsedGroups`, which weren't in scope yet at the old declaration site), and changed its computation from `sumNumericFields(visibleRecords, visibleFields)` to `sumNumericFields(effectivelyVisibleRecords, visibleFields)`, with the dependency array updated to match. `hasNumericVisibleField` stayed in its original location (it only depends on `visibleFields`, and the sibling `groupNumericTotals` block already needs it defined before that point).

**Tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, reusing the exact `Order`/Paid-Pending/`amount` fixture from round 302's own per-group-subtotal test (the closest existing precedent with a numeric field present). Groups by status, collapses "Paid" (1,500 across its 2 records), and confirms the one surviving subtotal row (Pending's 300) matches the grand total in the `<tfoot>` -- instead of the full 1,800 the bug would show. A mirroring full-DOM test in `codegen.test.ts` renders the real generated `EntityView.jsx` end to end (not just a source-text regex check) with an added `amount` field on the existing `Customer` fixture, groups by status, collapses "Won" (its 2 records totalling 80), and confirms the grand total matches the one surviving "New" subtotal (100) instead of the full 180. Caught and fixed an early mistake in both tests before they ever ran against the real implementation: `table tbody tr` counts after collapsing a group are not just header-row-plus-record-row counts once a numeric field is present, since each non-collapsed group's own subtotal row is also a `tr` inside `<tbody>` -- switched both assertions to check for the collapsed group's record text being absent, rather than an exact row count, after the first isolated run surfaced the miscount.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping all four test changes in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failures in isolation: the `EntityPanel.test.ts` test failed with the footer showing "Total: 1,800" instead of matching 300, and the `codegen.test.ts` test failed with "Total: 180" instead of matching 100 -- both the precise mismatch predicted, not a crash or an unrelated failure. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/db` 137, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 109, `@forge/api` 443 (+1), `@forge/web` 857 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed in both the live preview and the exported codegen.ts output. A fresh re-grep of every remaining `visibleRecords`/`numericFieldTotals` consumer in both files (captured above, in "Independent verification") found no further instances -- this was the one actual gap, now closed. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-490 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 492: Templates Gallery projects stayed Hebrew-labeled even when `lang: "en"` was explicitly requested

**The candidate**: an eighteenth consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that `POST /projects/from-template`'s own doc comment states `lang` was designed to pick "which of the template's two display-text pairs" becomes the new project's text -- but the implementation only ever applied this to `name`/`description`; `spec: template.spec` (the actual entities, fields, and enum values a project is built from) was inserted completely unchanged regardless of `lang`, since no English variant of any entity/field label existed anywhere in `templates.ts`.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` lines 438-463 directly and confirmed `useEnglish` (line 449) gated only the `name`/`description` fields passed to `insertProject` (lines 455-456), while `spec: template.spec` (line 457) ignored it entirely. Read `packages/spec-engine/src/templates.ts`'s six entity arrays and confirmed every entity/field `label` and `enumLabels` value was Hebrew-only, with no English counterpart anywhere -- only the top-level `TEMPLATES` array carried a bilingual `name`/`nameHe` and `description`/`descriptionHe` pair. Confirmed via the existing `app.test.ts` test (`POST /projects/from-template with lang: "en" uses the template's English display text instead`) that only `project.name` was ever asserted for the English-lang path -- nothing checked `spec.entities[*].label`, so this gap was never actually exercised by a test, just assumed covered by the top-level bilingual fields. Confirmed this is distinct from the already-open, deliberately-deferred round-380 candidate ("AI/heuristic-generated entity/field labels follow the project description's language"): that item is about labels that follow *free-text input* in AI-generated specs (an inherent heuristic quirk with no explicit language control), whereas this is a fixed, hand-authored template catalog whose route explicitly accepts and documents a `lang` parameter specifically to control language -- proving bilingual intent was designed in for this feature, just never finished.

**The fix**: added a `specEn` field to `AppTemplate` (alongside the existing Hebrew-only `spec`), and a parallel English entity array for each of the 6 templates (`RESTAURANT_ENTITIES_EN`, `CRM_ENTITIES_EN`, `PROJECT_TRACKER_ENTITIES_EN`, `VOLUNTEER_ENTITIES_EN`, `APPOINTMENTS_ENTITIES_EN`, `INVENTORY_ENTITIES_EN`) -- byte-identical in entity names, field names, types, `relationTo`, and `enumValues` to their Hebrew counterparts, with only `label`/`description`/`enumLabels` translated to English. Wired `/projects/from-template` to pick `useEnglish ? template.specEn : template.spec`, matching its existing `name`/`description` selection exactly.

**Tests**: in `templates.test.ts`, extended the existing schema-validity test to also validate every `specEn`, and added a new test asserting `spec` and `specEn` describe the *exact same shape* per template -- same entity order/names, same field name/type/relationTo/enumValues per field, non-empty and actually-different labels in each language, and matching enum-label key sets -- so an English pick can never silently diverge in structure from its Hebrew counterpart. In `app.test.ts`, added two new tests: one confirming `lang: "en"` produces an English `Deal` entity label, English `stage` field label, and English `enumLabels.won` on a real created project (not just the project's own name), and one confirming the no-`lang` default path still returns the original Hebrew labels unchanged.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `templates.ts` and `projects.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping all four test changes in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failures: the two new `templates.test.ts` tests failed with `specEn` reported as `undefined` (schema-invalid / `Cannot read properties of undefined`), and the new `app.test.ts` English-label test failed with the precise predicted mismatch (`'עסקה' !== 'Deal'`) -- while the new Hebrew-default test correctly still passed unchanged, confirming the fix is additive and doesn't disturb the existing default path. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/db` 137, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 110 (+1), `@forge/api` 445 (+2), `@forge/web` 857 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean (root build's `tsc -b` step also confirmed the new `AppTemplate.specEn` interface field type-checks cleanly across all its usages).

**Topic status**: this gap is closed for all 6 built-in templates. No codegen.ts duplicate applies -- this is a spec-authoring/API gap, not a client-rendering duplication; `codegen.ts` just serializes whatever `label` strings the inserted spec already has, so the fix at the source (the inserted spec itself) covers both the live preview and any later export of a template-created project automatically. The round-380 AI-generated-label-language candidate remains open, distinct, and unaffected by this fix. ### Round 493: a per-field filter outlived the field it filtered on, silently hiding every record after a live refine

**The candidate**: a nineteenth consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `fieldFilters` re-validation effect -- the immediate sibling of `viewMode`'s own effect, specifically fixed in round 490 for exactly this precondition -- was never given the equivalent fix. It still dropped a filter referencing a field the entity no longer has only on an actual entity-tab switch (`[projectId, entity.name]` in its dependency array), never while the same tab stayed mounted through a live Refine that mutates `entity.fields` in place.

**Independent verification**: read the effect directly (originally lines 1125-1134) and confirmed the dependency array omission, with an `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` suppressing the warning this round's fix now resolves correctly instead -- the same shape round 490's own fix took for `viewMode`. Read `visibleRecords`'s own filter check (`Object.entries(fieldFilters).every(([fieldName, value]) => !value || String(r[fieldName] ?? "") === value)`) and confirmed that once a filtered field is removed, every record's `r[fieldName]` becomes `undefined` while the stale filter's stored value stays non-empty, so `String(undefined ?? "") === value` is false for every record -- `.every()` fails universally, rendering zero rows with no search text, no error, and (per `filterableFields`'s own gate) no visible filter `<select>` left in the toolbar to explain why, though the "Clear filters" button does still appear and recovers the view once clicked. Grepped `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` and confirmed the identical `fieldFilters`/`visibleRecords` logic exists there too -- but confirmed it is NOT reachable in the exported app: `fieldFilters` is only ever initialized once via `useState(() => getPersistedFieldFilters(entity.name))`, with no re-validation effect at all, and the exported app's schema is frozen at export time (no live Refine ever runs against it post-export), so the "field removed while this tab stays mounted" precondition can never occur there -- no port needed, consistent with how round 490's own fix needed no codegen.ts counterpart for the same reason.

**The fix**: derived a `fieldNamesKey` via `useMemo(() => entity.fields.map((f) => f.name).join(","), [entity.fields])`, mirroring `viewMode`'s own `boardFieldName`/`dateFieldName` pattern of depending on a reactive primitive rather than the raw field array, and added it to the effect's dependency array (removing the `eslint-disable` it now correctly satisfies without one).

**Tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, placed right after round 490's own `viewMode` regression test (the closest existing precedent for "a schema edit changes a field this view depends on, without remounting"). Uses a `Deal` entity with `name`/`status` fields and 2 records with different `status` values; filters the table down to 1 visible record via the `status` filter `<select>`; then uses `view.rerender(buildEntityPanelElement({...}))` (no remount, mirroring `App.tsx`'s real `key={entity.name}` behavior) to simulate a refine that drops `status` entirely; confirms both records become visible again, instead of the table staying stuck on the one record the stale filter happened to match (or, in the real bug's case, on zero).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `EntityPanel.tsx`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: the new test's `waitForCondition` for both records reappearing timed out, since the stale filter was never dropped. ### Round 494: the exported app's Global Search discarded an in-progress query on Escape, instead of clearing it first

**The candidate**: a twentieth consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that the exported app's `GlobalSearch` never received the live preview's own round-290 "Escape clears the query first" UX behavior. `App.jsx`'s window-level Escape listener closed the whole search overlay unconditionally on every Escape press, so the ordinary, muscle-memory expectation for a search input -- press Escape to clear what you typed -- instead discarded the entire search and its results in one keystroke.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` lines 289-294 directly and confirmed its `handleInputKeyDown` explicitly handles `Escape` first (`if (e.key === "Escape" && query.length > 0) { ...; setQuery(""); return; }`), and that its search `<input>` (line 343) carries `data-escape-handled-locally` whenever `query.length > 0`. Read `useDialogFocusTrap.ts` lines 94-115 and confirmed the shared dialog-close-on-Escape listener explicitly checks `target?.closest("[data-escape-handled-locally]")` before closing -- a deliberate round-290 design (per the hook's own doc comment) specifically so an inner control can opt out of the dialog's own close-on-Escape for exactly one keypress. Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported `GlobalSearch`'s `handleInputKeyDown` (originally lines 4486-4498) and confirmed it has no `Escape` case at all, and its input carries no `data-escape-handled-locally` equivalent. Read the exported `App`'s own window-level Escape listener (originally lines 4813-4829) and confirmed it unconditionally calls `setShowSearch(false)` on any Escape, with no check for an in-progress query. Confirmed via the file's own existing test at line 4822 ("the exported app includes a real cross-entity global search") that this file already tracks round-290-adjacent features (it imports `markSearchDialogOpen`/`markSearchDialogClosed` from round 489's own fix) but never picked up this specific Escape-clears-query behavior -- a genuinely new, narrowly-scoped port gap, not a reopening of round 489's closed dialog-guard finding (that one was about *keyboard shortcuts leaking through* the overlay; this one is about *the overlay's own Escape key* discarding more than intended).

"" : undefined}` to its `<input>`, and updated `App`'s window-level Escape handler to check `e.target.closest("[data-escape-handled-locally]")` before calling `setShowSearch(false)`.
