### Round 495: an idempotency key could be replayed or blocked against a completely different user's or route's request

**The candidate**: a twenty-first consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that `withIdempotency`'s lookup (`apps/api/src/idempotency.ts`) only ever filtered by the bare client-supplied `key`, never by the `userId`/`route` stored on every row specifically to scope a key to the one request it was chosen for (per the table's own doc comment in `packages/db/src/idempotency.ts`). A key reused across a different user or a different route -- a client bug, or a guessed/forged header value, since this header is entirely client-supplied with no other validation -- would silently replay another request's cached "done" response, or get rejected as a duplicate of another request's unrelated "in_progress" one, with no relation to its own route or project at all.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/api/src/idempotency.ts` lines 32-69 directly and confirmed `getIdempotencyRecord(db, key)` is the sole lookup before both the `in_progress` 409 and the `done` replay, with `userId`/`route` never read back for comparison. Read `packages/db/src/idempotency.ts` lines 15-47 and confirmed `userId`/`route` are columns on every row, written on insert, and documented ("A row only ever covers one client-chosen key for one route") but never queried against. Traced a concrete scenario: `POST /projects/A/roles` with key `K` succeeds and caches project A's response; a later `POST /projects/B/roles` reusing the same key `K` within the 24h TTL would get project A's cached response replayed verbatim, with project B's own mutation never running and (if A and B have different owners) project A's response body disclosed to a request never authorized against it. Confirmed via `apps/web/src/api.ts` that every real call site generates a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` per call, so this isn't reachable through the app's own designed client flow today -- but the gap is a genuine server-side authorization hole with no defense in depth, since nothing else validates the header. Confirmed this is not a codegen.ts porting question: the exported standalone app has no idempotency mechanism or auth routes of this kind at all (a static single-tenant demo), so there is nothing to compare against on that side.

**The fix**: added a mismatch check in `withIdempotency`, right after the lookup and before either existing-status branch: `if (existing && (existing.userId !== userId || existing.route !== route)) throw new HttpError(409, ..., "IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH")`. A key collision across a different user or route is now rejected outright rather than replayed or blocked against. Added the new error code's localized strings (Hebrew and English) to `apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts`, matching the existing `error.<CODE>` convention every other server error code already follows.

**Tests**: a new test in `idempotency.test.ts`, placed right before the existing TTL-aging test. Covers both mismatch axes separately: the same key first used for `POST /projects/A/roles` as `user1`, then reused for `POST /projects/B/roles` as the same `user1` (route mismatch, rejected, underlying work never runs), then reused for `POST /projects/A/roles` again but as `user2` (userId mismatch on the identical route, also rejected).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `idempotency.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: "Missing expected rejection" on the route-mismatch assertion. Restored `idempotency.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/db` 137, `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 110, `@forge/api` 447 (+1), `@forge/web` 858 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. Not a live-preview/codegen.ts porting question (confined to `apps/api`'s own backend, no exported-app counterpart exists). The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred -- distinct from this round's finding, which is a scoping bug in the idempotency mechanism already shipped for other routes, not the still-unimplemented `/refine` SSE-stream design itself. Everything else still open from rounds 378-494 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 496: a new entity could silently inherit a removed entity's stale table and data when their sanitized names collided across a refine

**The candidate**: a twenty-second consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that `diffAndMigrate` (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`) has no defense against a sanitized-table-name collision between a brand-new entity and a *different* entity that existed in `previousSpec` and has since been removed. `tableNameFor` sanitizes an entity name by replacing every non-ASCII-alphanumeric character with `_` (`packages/db/src/identifiers.ts:16-20`), so two differently-named entities -- most plausibly two same-length non-ASCII names, e.g. Hebrew -- can collapse to the identical physical table name. `ProductSpecSchema`'s own `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` refine (round 283) already rejects that collision *within one spec*, but it only ever validates one spec at a time; it has no way to see that today's new entity collides with a name that existed in an *earlier* spec and is now gone from the current one.

**Independent verification**: read `identifiers.ts` and confirmed `tableNameFor("p", "לקוח")` and `tableNameFor("p", "מוצר")` both sanitize to `"entity_p_____"` (already demonstrated in `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions`'s own doc comment, round 283's fix). Read `diffAndMigrate` (`migrate.ts:196-230`) and traced the exact failure path: an entity "לקוח" (fields: `phone`) is removed from the spec on one refine -- additive-only migrations never drop its table -- and a later refine introduces an unrelated-looking entity "מוצר" (fields: `price`). For "מוצר", `prevEntity` is `undefined` (its name never existed in `previousSpec`), but `tableNameFor(projectId, "מוצר")` already has physical columns from "לקוח"'s stale table, so the `!prevEntity && currentColumns.size === 0` branch is false and the code falls through to the "entity absent from previousSpec but table already exists" reuse path -- built and commented for *same-name* reuse after removal, with zero check that the reused table's prior owner actually had the same name. "לקוח"'s real `phone` row would keep sitting in the table and surface as a "מוצר" record with no warning; any field whose name/SQL-type coincidentally matched would be silently reused rather than reported, exactly the real-data-corruption failure mode round 283's own case-insensitive/sanitized-collision checks exist to prevent -- just reached a hop later than those checks can see. Confirmed `ProductSpecSchema`'s existing refine genuinely cannot catch this (it only ever receives one spec's `entities` array, never a cross-spec diff). Confirmed no codegen.ts porting question: the exported standalone app (`renderServerJs`) always does a single fresh `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` from the current spec only, with no incremental per-refine migration state to collide against.

**The fix**: in `diffAndMigrate`, when `!prevEntity` (today's entity's name never existed in `previousSpec`), search `previousSpec.entities` for a *different*-named entity whose `tableNameFor` matches the same table. If found, throw a `ValidationError` (already defined in `packages/db/src/repository.ts`, already wired into `apps/api/src/app.ts`'s global error handler as a 400 with the existing, already-localized `VALIDATION_ERROR` code -- no new error class or i18n string needed) naming both colliding entities, instead of silently falling through to the reuse path. `pipeline.ts`'s existing `/build`/`/refine` catch block already surfaces any `diffAndMigrate` throw as a "Database" agent failure and retries once through the Debug Agent's automatic spec-fix path -- this plugs into that same, already-battle-tested recovery mechanism with no new plumbing.

**Tests**: a new test in `migrate.test.ts`, placed right after the existing case-insensitive-collision documentation test (its direct cross-refine counterpart). Builds a project with entity "לקוח" (phone), inserts a real record, then diffs against a next spec that drops "לקוח" and adds "מוצר" (price) -- asserts `diffAndMigrate` throws a `ValidationError` naming both entities, and that "לקוח"'s real row is still sitting untouched in the table afterward (not merged, not overwritten).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: "Missing expected exception" on the new test's `assert.throws`. Restored `migrate.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/db` 138 (+1), `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 110, `@forge/api` 447 (unchanged), `@forge/web` 858 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. Live-preview-only (`packages/db`'s own migration engine); no codegen.ts port needed for the reason given above. Distinct from round 283's within-one-spec collision guard (still in place, still doing its own job) and from the explicitly-rejected "require all-ASCII entity names" wider fix (round 283's own doc comment: a one-way schema door that would break existing non-colliding non-ASCII projects) -- this round's fix only blocks the specific cross-refine collision case, leaving a lone non-ASCII name exactly as workable as before. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-495 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 497: round 496's table-collision guard only looked back one refine hop, missing an entity removed two or more refines ago

**The candidate**: a twenty-third consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found that round 496's own sanitized-table-name collision guard in `diffAndMigrate` (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`) only ever searched `previousSpec.entities` -- the one immediately preceding spec -- for a colliding entity name. A real refine loop calls `diffAndMigrate` once per refine, each time with only that one hop of history (`pipeline.ts`'s only call site never passes anything older). An entity removed on an *earlier* refine is already absent from `previousSpec` by the time a later, differently-named colliding entity shows up, so round 496's own fix -- which closes the one-hop case -- still lets the two-or-more-hop case through silently.

**Independent verification**: confirmed via direct code reading that `pipeline.ts`'s only call site always passes the project's immediately-preceding spec, never anything older, and that `previousSpec.entities.find(...)` (round 496's own guard) genuinely has no way to see further back. Found `packages/db/src/checkpoints.ts`'s `listHistoricalEntityNames` (and its backing `checkpoint_entity_history` table) already exists, built specifically to answer "did this project ever have an entity named X" -- written at every `insertCheckpoint` call, never pruned by deleting an individual checkpoint, currently consumed only by `deleteProject` for the same "don't orphan a table" concern. Traced the exact two-hop scenario: build with `Customer`+`לקוח` (phone), then refine 1 drops `לקוח` (no collision yet -- nothing new is added), then refine 2's `previousSpec` is refine 1's own spec, which no longer mentions `לקוח` at all, and introduces an unrelated `מוצר` (price) whose sanitized table name still collides with `לקוח`'s stale one. Confirmed round 496's own guard finds nothing (searching only refine 1's spec) and the code falls through to the "benign reuse" path exactly as it did before round 496's fix, silently surfacing `לקוח`'s real row as a `מוצר` record.

**The fix**: added `allKnownEntityNames` in `migrate.ts`, which unions `previousSpec.entities`' names with `listHistoricalEntityNames(db, projectId)` when the `checkpoint_entity_history` table exists (checked via `sqlite_master` first, so a caller exercising `diffAndMigrate` without the checkpoint infrastructure -- e.g. this file's own pre-existing unit tests -- degrades gracefully to the original one-hop behavior rather than throwing "no such table"). Round 496's collision check now searches this fuller set instead of `previousSpec.entities` alone.

**Tests**: a new test in `migrate.test.ts`, placed right after round 496's own one-hop test. Calls `ensureCheckpointsTable` + `insertCheckpoint` (exactly what the real pipeline does after every successful `diffAndMigrate`) to populate the ledger, builds with `Customer`+`לקוח`, refines once to drop `לקוח` (checkpointed), then refines again adding `מוצר` against that second spec as `previousSpec` -- asserts `diffAndMigrate` still throws a `ValidationError` naming both entities, and that `לקוח`'s real row survives untouched.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: "Missing expected exception" on the new test's `assert.throws`, with round 496's own one-hop test still passing unaffected. Restored `migrate.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/db` 139 (+1), `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 110, `@forge/api` 447 (unchanged), `@forge/web` 858 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. Live-preview-only (same migration engine as round 496; no codegen.ts counterpart exists). Not a reopening of round 496 -- it closed the one-hop case correctly; this round closes the deeper, multi-hop variant of the same bug class using infrastructure (`checkpoint_entity_history`) that already existed but wasn't yet wired into this check. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-496 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 498: the table-collision guard compared names case-sensitively, missing a collision that differs only by letter case

**The candidate**: a twenty-fourth consecutive fresh Explore survey (general, no specific instruction) found a third, genuinely distinct angle on the same `diffAndMigrate` collision guard rounds 496 and 497 already hardened: the comparison itself (`tableNameFor(projectId, name) === table`) used plain, case-sensitive JS string equality. SQLite compares ASCII table identifiers case-insensitively even when double-quoted -- the exact fact `ProductSpecSchema`'s own `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames` refine exists to guard against within one spec (documented in that function's own doc comment and tested directly against this project's SQLite binding). An entity reused with only a case change after an earlier removal -- e.g. `Order` removed, `order` added later -- sanitizes to a table name SQLite treats as identical to the old one, but the guard's `===` comparison says they differ, so it finds nothing even though the colliding name is sitting right there in `allKnownEntityNames`.

**Independent verification**: read the guard directly (`migrate.ts` lines 249-258 before this round) and confirmed the comparison was a bare `===` on two `tableNameFor` results, with no case-folding anywhere in the collision-check path. Confirmed `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames`/`findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` both `.toLowerCase()` before comparing, and that this exact SQLite case-insensitivity is independently documented and tested elsewhere in this codebase (the "two entities whose names collide when compared case-insensitively" test in `migrate.test.ts`, which documents the *within-one-spec* version of the same fact). Traced the concrete scenario: build with entity `Order2` (field `note`, a real row inserted); refine removes `Order2` and adds an unrelated-looking `order2` (field `price`) in the same call. `tableNameFor(projectId, "Order2")` and `tableNameFor(projectId, "order2")` differ only by the leading letter's case, so the pre-this-round guard's `===` check found no collision, and the code fell through to the same silent-reuse path rounds 496/497 exist to close -- `Order2`'s real row would surface as an `order2` record with no warning.

**The fix**: lowercased both sides of the comparison in the collision check (`tableNameFor(projectId, name).toLowerCase() === table.toLowerCase()`), mirroring the exact pattern `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames`/`findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` already use. No other part of the guard (the `name !== entity.name` filter, `allKnownEntityNames`'s own union of `previousSpec` and `checkpoint_entity_history`) needed to change -- the fix is confined to the one comparison.

**Tests**: a new test in `migrate.test.ts`, placed right after round 497's own multi-hop test. Builds with `Order2` (note), inserts a real record, then diffs against a next spec that drops `Order2` and adds `order2` (price) in the same call -- asserts `diffAndMigrate` throws a `ValidationError` naming both entities, and that `Order2`'s real row survives untouched.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: "Missing expected exception" on the new test's `assert.throws`, with rounds 496's and 497's own tests still passing unaffected. Restored `migrate.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/db` 140 (+1), `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/spec-engine` 110, `@forge/api` 447 (unchanged), `@forge/web` 858 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. Live-preview-only (same migration engine as rounds 496/497; no codegen.ts counterpart exists). Not a reopening of either prior round -- 496 closed the within-one-spec-vs-cross-refine gap, 497 closed the one-hop-vs-full-history gap, and this round closes a third, independent gap in the comparison's own string semantics. This migrate.ts collision-guard area has now had three consecutive rounds of iteration; the next general survey's default instruction explicitly steers away from a fourth pass on this exact mechanism unless a genuinely new angle turns up. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-497 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 499: Export CSV/Copy/Print buttons stayed enabled with nothing actually visible once every group was collapsed

**First candidate, rejected after independent verification**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against the just-closed migrate.ts collision guard, first proposed `apps/api/src/backup.ts`'s `generateBackupZipEntries`: its `sanitizeZipEntryName` sanitizes but never rejects filesystem-unsafe characters, and maps every entity to a zip path with no collision check between entities, unlike the file's own `uniqueWhatsAppLogPath`, which already dedupes its one hardcoded entry against entity-name collisions. Independent verification disproved this as reachable: `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` refine on `ProductSpecSchema` sanitizes via `.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, "_").toLowerCase()` -- a strictly broader character replacement (every non-alphanumeric character, not just the narrower zip-unsafe set) plus case-folding than `sanitizeZipEntryName`'s own narrower, non-case-folding rule. Proved by case analysis that any two entity names colliding under the narrower zip rule must also collide under the broader, case-folded schema rule (the schema rule's replacement set is a superset, and lowercasing two already-identical strings keeps them identical), so any entity-vs-entity zip collision is mathematically guaranteed to already be rejected by the existing schema refine (wired into every spec-creation path since round 283) before the spec could ever reach `backup.ts`. Separately confirmed the manual single-entity-add route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `deriveEntityName`) can only ever produce pure ASCII letter/digit names, so it can't introduce an unsafe name through that path either. Correctly rejected as a false positive rather than implemented.

**The real candidate**: a second fresh Explore survey (denylisted against both the migrate.ts guard and the disproven backup.ts angle) found that round 487's own fix (commit `425a5d2`) updated `handleExportCsv`, `handleCopy`, and the print-list sheet's `records` prop to use the grouping/collapse-aware `effectivelyVisibleRecords` instead of the flat `visibleRecords`, but never touched the three buttons' own `disabled` props (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` and the duplicated copy in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`), which still read `selectedIds.size === 0 && visibleRecords.length === 0`. With every group collapsed -- a state the UI fully allows, with no "at least one open" constraint on `collapsedGroups` -- `visibleRecords.length` (the flat, pre-collapse count) stays > 0 while `effectivelyVisibleRecords.length` (what the table body and the export/copy/print actions actually use) is 0, so the buttons stayed enabled and clicking them silently produced a header-only CSV, an empty clipboard copy, or a blank print sheet.

**Independent verification**: read both files directly and confirmed the exact three `disabled={selectedIds.size === 0 && visibleRecords.length === 0}` occurrences in each (EntityPanel.tsx's copy/export/print buttons and codegen.ts's identical trio), with `effectivelyVisibleRecords` already in scope at each render site (defined earlier in the same component via the same `recordGroups.flatMap(...collapsedGroups.has(group.key) ? [] : group.records)` expression in both files). Confirmed `selectedOrAllRecords`'s call sites (`handleExportCsv`, `handleCopy`, and the print-list sheet's `records` prop) already pass `effectivelyVisibleRecords`, confirming the mismatch is exactly between what the buttons gate on and what the actions they trigger actually use.

**The fix**: changed all three `disabled` props in both files from `visibleRecords.length === 0` to `effectivelyVisibleRecords.length === 0`, matching the variable the buttons' own actions already use.

**Tests**: one new test in each of `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts`, placed right after the existing round-487 collapsed-group print-list test. Renders a 2-record entity, groups by status (one record per group), collapses both groups, and asserts all three buttons are `disabled` even though `visibleRecords` itself still has 2 records -- then re-expands one group and asserts they re-enable. Also updated two pre-existing round-487 tests in `codegen.test.ts` that asserted the old `visibleRecords.length === 0` text as the expected generated source for the export/copy buttons, now asserting the corrected `effectivelyVisibleRecords.length === 0` text instead.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure in both new tests: "Export CSV must disable once every group is collapsed and nothing is visible -- false !== true". ### Round 500: sortKeys' own re-validation effect never re-ran against fields a live refine removed, misnumbering a surviving sort key's priority badge

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against the just-closed migrate.ts guard, the disproven backup.ts angle, and the visible-staleness pattern (closed after 5 confirmed instances through round 499), revisited a previously-known-but-deprioritized small candidate: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `sortKeys` revalidation effect (lines 1110-1115 before this round) only dropped a persisted sort key referencing a removed field on `[projectId, entity.name]` -- an actual tab switch -- never while the tab stays mounted through a live Refine that mutates the currently-active entity's own `fields` array in place (App.tsx keys `EntityPanel` by `entity.name` alone, so it never remounts for this). Round 493's own roadmap entry had already spotted this exact gap and explicitly declined to fix it, reasoning that an invalid sort key simply becomes a no-op in `compareValues`/`resolveSortValue` (every record resolves the dead field to `undefined`, so the key never actually reorders anything) -- low severity, judgment call. This round's survey found a materially different consequence that round 493 didn't consider: a dead key left sitting at an *earlier* array index than a surviving one doesn't just no-op silently -- it corrupts the surviving key's own on-screen reporting. The "Clear sort" button, the per-column priority badge (`{keyIndex + 1}`, shown whenever `sortKeys.length > 1`), and the `aria-sort` attribute (set to the real direction only when `keyIndex === 0`) are all computed straight from `sortKeys.findIndex(...)`, so a surviving key stuck at index 1 behind a dead index-0 entry renders a `"2"` badge with no `"1"` anywhere to explain it, and reports `aria-sort="none"` to assistive tech even though it is visually the only key still sorting anything.

**Independent verification**: read the effect directly and confirmed it used `entity.fields` in its body but `[projectId, entity.name]` as its deps (missing the `fieldNamesKey` dependency its sibling `viewMode` effect, round 490, and `fieldFilters` effect, round 493, both already have -- the file's own comments literally say "Same reasoning as viewMode's own effect just above" / "Same reasoning as sortKeys' own effect just above" for the two siblings that already got the fix). Confirmed the Clear-sort button, priority-badge, and `aria-sort` rendering all key off the same `sortKeys.findIndex` pattern described above by reading the render code directly (`EntityPanel.tsx` lines 2541-2549 and 2745-2809). Confirmed the exported codegen app needs no port: `codegen.ts`'s `sortKeys` is a one-time `useState` initializer with no revalidating effect at all, since the standalone exported app has no live-refine mechanism -- its schema never changes while mounted, consistent with how rounds 490 and 493 also stayed live-preview-only.

**The fix**: hoisted the existing `fieldNamesKey` memo (previously declared just above the `fieldFilters` effect) up above the `sortKeys` effect and added it as a dependency there too, computing `validFieldNames` from `fieldNamesKey` instead of `entity.fields` directly -- exactly mirroring the `fieldFilters` effect's own shape. Both effects now share the one memo.

**Tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, placed right after the existing round-493 `fieldFilters` live-refine test. Sorts by `status` (primary) then shift-clicks `name` (secondary, picking up priority badge `"2"`), then simulates a refine that drops `status` while staying on the same `entity.name` (`view.rerender`, the same technique the round-490/493 tests use) -- asserts the priority badge disappears entirely (since only one real key remains) and `name`'s own `<th>` now reports `aria-sort="ascending"` instead of staying stuck at `"none"`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `EntityPanel.tsx`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). ### Round 501: Appointment's bare "reservation" keyword spuriously matched the ordinary, unrelated word "preservation"

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against migrate.ts's collision guard, the disproven backup.ts angle, and the now 6-instance-closed visible-staleness/stale-deps pattern family (explicitly steered away from EntityPanel.tsx's per-field revalidation effects this round), found a new instance of a different, well-established bug class in this codebase: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s Appointment entity rule listed a bare string keyword, `"reservation"` (line 119), matched via `matchesKeyword`'s plain `lower.includes(kw)` substring check (`heuristic.ts` line 67). `"reservation"` is a literal substring of the ordinary, unrelated English word `"preservation"` (p-**reservation**) -- so any business description mentioning historic preservation, data preservation, or wildlife preservation spuriously picked up an irrelevant Appointment entity (with its customerName/date/service/status/notes fields) alongside whatever the description was actually about.

**Independent verification**: reproduced directly by calling `matchEntities` against `"A historic preservation nonprofit that tracks buildings, donors, and fundraising campaigns."` -- confirmed it returns `['Appointment', 'Donation']`, with `Donation` the correct match and `Appointment` the spurious one. Read `domainEntities.ts` line 119 directly and confirmed the bare string. Read `matchesKeyword` (`heuristic.ts` line 66-68) and confirmed it already supports `string | RegExp`, with a plain string doing unbounded substring matching -- exactly the same mechanism this file's own doc comment (lines 17-28) and more than ten prior rounds (449-460: Service/"disservice", Vehicle/"mechanical" and "garage sale", Shipment/"worshipping", Project/"projector", Property/"enlisting", Product/"production", etc.) have already fixed one at a time for other entities' keywords, via either a collision-free string or a `\b`-bounded RegExp. Grepped `heuristic.test.ts`/`domainEntities.ts` for "preservation" and confirmed nothing already covered this exact collision.

**The fix**: replaced the bare string `"reservation"` with `/\breservations?\b/`, matching this file's own established convention (e.g. `/\border(s)?\b/`, `/\bpatient(s)?\b/`, `/\blisting(s)?\b/`) -- a leading `\b` to reject "preservation" (no word boundary between "p" and "r"), and a `(s)?` before the trailing `\b` so the plural "reservations" still matches (a trailing `\b` alone, without the optional "s", would have broken the plural case, since "n" and "s" are both word characters with no boundary between them).

**Tests**: a new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, placed right after the existing round-457 Property/"enlisting" test (the closest precedent in shape). Confirms a historic-preservation description no longer matches Appointment, and that real "reservation"/"reservations" usage (a restaurant table reservation) still does, both singular and plural.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: `AssertionError` on `'preservation' alone must not spuriously match Appointment via a bare 'reservation' substring` (the spurious match still fired). Restored `domainEntities.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 140, `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (+1), `@forge/api` 448 (unchanged), `@forge/web` 860 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. Single-file fix (`domainEntities.ts`'s own keyword list, consumed identically by both the live preview and the exported app's build-time spec generation -- there's no codegen.ts duplication question here, since heuristic matching only ever runs once, at build time, not in either rendered app). The keyword-collision bug class itself remains open in the sense that it has recurred many times across many different entities' keywords (a pattern, not a single bug) -- a future round finding yet another instance in a different entity's keyword list would still be a genuinely new, narrow finding, not a reopening. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-500 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 502: subscribeAuthExpired's own "mirrors handleAccountDeleted" doc comment was false -- a stale WhatsApp "To" value could survive a forced sign-out into the next login

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against migrate.ts's collision guard, the disproven backup.ts angle, the now 6-instance-closed visible-staleness/stale-deps effect family, and the now-11-instance keyword-collision bug class (round 501), found a genuinely different bug: `App.tsx`'s `subscribeAuthExpired` effect (lines 754-761 before this round) forces the app back to the login screen the moment any request reports the session is gone (a 401 from token expiry, "sign out everywhere," or a password change on another device), by calling `clearToken()`/`setUser(null)`/`setProject(null)`/`setView("home")`. Its own doc comment explicitly claimed this "mirrors `handleAccountDeleted`'s own clearToken+reset-to-home sequence" -- but `handleAccountDeleted` (and `handleLogout`) also reset `buildWarning`, `description`/`clearIdeaDraft()`, `error`, `activeEntity`, `selectedAnswers`, `additionalRequest`, `refineText`, `refineHistory`, and `refineHistorySearch`, none of which this effect touched. Since `AppContent` never unmounts across this transition (the `if (!user) return <AuthScreen />` is a conditional return inside the same component instance, not a remount -- `handleLogout`'s own comment states this explicitly as the reason its own long reset list exists), every one of those pieces of state survived an auth-expiry event into the next login in the same tab. The most concretely damaging instance: `whatsappPrefillTo`, set only by a per-record "Send WhatsApp" row action (a specific contact's phone number) and cleared only by `WhatsAppPanel`'s own three in-dialog callbacks (`onClose`/`onJumpToEntity`/`onJumpToRecord`).

**Independent verification**: read the effect directly and confirmed its 4-line reset list against the doc comment's claim. Read `handleLogout` and `handleAccountDeleted` directly and confirmed their actual ~10-item reset lists. Read `openPanel()` and confirmed it never touches `whatsappPrefillTo`. Read the generic topbar "💬 WhatsApp" button (no prefill) and the per-record `onSendWhatsApp` callback (sets the prefill) and `WhatsAppPanel`'s three JSX props (the only three places `whatsappPrefillTo` is ever reset to `null`). Confirmed the key architectural fact that makes this reachable specifically via this effect and not via `handleLogout`/`handleAccountDeleted`: read `domInert.ts`'s `hideBackgroundFromAssistiveTech` directly and confirmed it sets the real DOM `inert` attribute (not just `aria-hidden`) on every sibling of an open dialog's ancestors, up to `document.body` -- meaning the topbar (including the Logout button) is genuinely unclickable, not just screen-reader-hidden, while `WhatsAppPanel` is open. `handleLogout`/`handleAccountDeleted` can therefore only ever run once the panel is already closed (its own `onClose`/`onJumpTo*` callbacks already having cleared the prefill) -- but `subscribeAuthExpired` fires from an async promise rejection, not a DOM click, so it's the one path that bypasses this guard entirely and can fire while the panel sits open and polling. Confirmed the user-visible symptom is real, not just inert state: `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s `const [testTo, setTestTo] = useState(() => prefillTo ?? "")` (line 147) is a lazy initializer that reads `prefillTo` fresh on each new mount, and since the panel is conditionally rendered (`{showWhatsApp && <WhatsAppPanel ... />}`), every reopen is a fresh mount that would read whatever stale value `whatsappPrefillTo` was left holding.

**The fix**: added the missing resets to the effect -- `setDescription("")`, `clearIdeaDraft()`, `setError(null)`, `setActiveEntity(null)`, `setSelectedAnswers({})`, `setAdditionalRequest("")`, `setRefineText("")`, `setRefineHistory([])`, `setRefineHistorySearch("")`, matching `handleAccountDeleted`'s own list (the comment names that function specifically, not `handleLogout`, so `buildWarning` -- which `handleLogout` resets but `handleAccountDeleted` doesn't -- was left out), plus `setWhatsappPrefillTo(null)`, the one reset genuinely specific to this effect: neither `handleLogout` nor `handleAccountDeleted` need it, since their own trigger buttons are already `inert`-blocked while `WhatsAppPanel` is open. Updated the effect's own doc comment to explain this distinction explicitly, so the "mirrors handleAccountDeleted" claim is accurate rather than aspirational.

**Tests**: extended the existing regression test in `App.test.ts` (the same regex-extraction + `new Function` technique it already used, just with every additional setter mocked and asserted) rather than adding a new one, since it already existed specifically to check this effect's reset list and had simply never been kept in sync with the doc comment's own claim.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `App.tsx`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the extended test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: `AssertionError` on the new `descriptionSet` assertion (`'untouched' !== ''`), the first of the newly-added checks, since the old code never touched any of these setters. Restored `App.tsx` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 140, `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 448 (unchanged), `@forge/web` 860 (unchanged, since the existing test was extended in place rather than a new one added), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed, live-preview-only -- confirmed via grep that `codegen.ts` has no `subscribeAuthExpired`/`clearToken`/`AuthScreen` at all, since the exported standalone app has no auth/login system whatsoever (single-tenant, no multi-user session concept), so there's no codegen.ts counterpart to port this to. This is a distinct bug class from the "visible-staleness"/EntityPanel-revalidation-effect family closed after rounds 485-491/499/500 (this is cross-session UI-state leakage via a doc-comment-claimed-but-never-implemented reset list, not a live-refine/grouping staleness issue) and from the keyword-collision class closed after round 501 -- a third, independent pattern worth watching for: a doc comment asserting parity with another function's reset/cleanup list, where the actual code has quietly drifted out of sync. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-501 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 503: ICS calendar export duplicated a multi-day record once per day it spanned

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against migrate.ts's collision guard, the disproven backup.ts angle, the now 6-instance-closed visible-staleness/stale-deps effect family, the keyword-collision bug class, and round 502's subscribeAuthExpired fix, and actively steered toward rarely-touched areas, found a genuine integration bug in the calendar's "Export to Calendar (ICS)" feature (round 430): `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `icsMonthRecords` memo (and its byte-identical `codegen.ts` mirror) built the flat list handed to `buildCalendarIcs` by calling `buildCalendarMonth(...).filter((d) => d.inCurrentMonth).flatMap((d) => d.records)` -- but `buildCalendarMonth` (round 430's own ranged-date-support addition, commit `d4244cf`) *deliberately* places the exact same record object into every day cell a ranged record (start/end date pair, e.g. a Rental's `startDate`/`endDate`) spans, so the on-screen calendar grid correctly shows a multi-night stay's chip on each night it occupies. Reusing that per-day grouping for the *export* list meant the same record appeared once per day in the flattened array, and `buildCalendarIcs` emits one `VEVENT` per entry -- so a single N-day ranged record was exported as N byte-identical `VEVENT` blocks (same `UID`, same `DTSTART`/`DTEND`, same `SUMMARY`) instead of the one event the feature's own doc comment (`calendarIcs.ts` line 75, "one all-day VEVENT per record") promises.

**Independent verification**: read `buildCalendarMonth` (`entityFormatting.ts` lines 759-791) directly and confirmed `dayRecords` places the identical record into every day whose date falls within `[startDate, endDate]`. Read `icsMonthRecords` in `EntityPanel.tsx` (lines 1401-1406 before this round) and confirmed it flattens that per-day grouping with no deduplication. Read `buildCalendarIcs` (`calendarIcs.ts` lines 93-157) directly and confirmed its `for (const record of records)` loop emits one `VEVENT` per array entry, keyed by a `UID` built purely from `entity.name`/`record.id` (so duplicates share the identical UID, but still appear as separate blocks in the raw file). Confirmed via direct read that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (lines 3004-3011) has the byte-identical `icsMonthRecords` computation feeding the same `buildCalendarIcs` call, so the exported standalone app has the same bug. Grepped `EntityPanel.test.ts` and confirmed no existing test exercised `icsMonthRecords`/the ICS export button with a ranged (start/end) entity at all -- every prior ICS test used the single-date `Appointment` fixture, so this gap was never caught. Confirmed this is not a deliberate choice: nothing in the code, comments, or prior roadmap entries (round 430's own entry) indicates duplicate `VEVENT`s were ever intended.

**The fix**: changed `icsMonthRecords` in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts` to deduplicate the flattened per-day list by `record.id` (via `Array.from(new Map(flat.map((r) => [r.id, r])).values())`) before returning it, keeping the first occurrence's position and leaving `buildCalendarMonth`'s own per-day duplication (used elsewhere for the on-screen grid) untouched. Added a doc comment to both explaining why the dedup is needed, so a future reader doesn't reintroduce the same bug by "simplifying" it back to a bare `flatMap`.

**Tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, placed right after the existing round-430 ICS-export-button-disabled-state test, using a new `Rental`-shaped entity fixture (`title`/`startDate`/`endDate`) not previously used in this file. Renders a single 3-day-stay record fully inside the current month, clicks the ICS export button, captures the downloaded `Blob` via the same `URL.createObjectURL` stub pattern the existing CSV-export test uses, and asserts the resulting `.ics` text contains exactly one `BEGIN:VEVENT` block and exactly one occurrence of the record's `UID`, not three.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: `AssertionError: a single 3-day stay must export as exactly one VEVENT, not one per night it spans` with `3 !== 1`. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 140, `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 448 (unchanged, `codegen.ts` has no dedicated test for this exact line), `@forge/web` 861 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed, ported to both the live preview and the exported codegen app. This is a genuinely new finding in a previously-untested combination (ranged-date entities + ICS export), distinct from every denylisted pattern this round avoided. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-502 remains open and unchanged.

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent, denylisted against migrate.ts's collision guard, backup.ts's zip-collision, the visible-staleness/revalidation-effect family, keyword collisions, round 502's subscribeAuthExpired fix, and round 503's icsMonthRecords/buildCalendarMonth fix, searched broadly across column reorder/resize, CSV import/export, Business Twin, Time Machine/checkpoints UI, the WhatsApp Web (Baileys) connection manager and its pagination/race guards, the relation-field picker, Templates Gallery, i18n completeness, accessibility of less-common dialogs, the Anthropic provider's security-scan heuristics, codegen.ts/live-preview parity, project-preference cleanup completeness, and the "quick" spec-edit routes' concurrency model. It methodically ruled out five separate promising-looking leads with direct proof rather than taking any at face value: (1) `checkpointDiff.ts` ignoring a field's `required` flag -- an existing test (`checkpointDiff.test.ts`) already asserts this is intentional; (2) the bulk-edit toolbar's enum field allowing an unreachable `""` placeholder if submitted before picking an option -- consistent with every other optional field type's existing "leave unset → stored as null" semantic, not an inconsistency; (3) a hypothesized lost-update race between the "quick" spec-edit routes (`addRole`/`addEntity`/etc. in `projects.ts`) -- traced the actual execution and confirmed every one uses `node:sqlite`'s fully synchronous `DatabaseSync` with zero real `await` points between read and write, so two such requests cannot interleave on Node's single-threaded event loop (unlike `/build`/`/refine`, which genuinely yield during a real AI network call -- exactly why `activePipelines` exists only for those); (4) re-confirmed round 499's backup.ts zip-collision false-positive via the same algebraic argument; (5) mechanically diffed all 538 Hebrew/English translation keys and every `{placeholder}` across both languages -- zero mismatches.

**Independent verification**: confirmed this directly by running the actual regex: `/(?:(?<![a-zA-Z])ssn|SSN)(?![a-z])/.test("userSsn")` returns `false`, while `.test("userSSN")` returns `true` and `.test("businessName")` (the case these regexes exist to reject) correctly stays `false`. Also independently confirmed `apiSecretKey` still matches the sibling "secret" regex. Separately re-read `checkpointDiff.test.ts` directly and confirmed the exact test name and assertion the agent cited actually exists and covers this.

**Topic status**: no fix this round. The `userSsn`-style gap is real but genuinely low-severity (a cosmetic advisory message from `runSecurityScan`, not a validation or data-integrity control; the heuristic domain library never generates such a field name) and sits in an area (`SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS`'s word-boundary heuristics) already refined twice before for this exact kind of false-positive/false-negative tradeoff -- fixing it now would be a third round on the same narrow mechanism without a genuinely new angle, the same standard that already applies to migrate.ts's collision guard. ### Round 505: the exported standalone app's generated server.js broke every single write to a table when one of its relation fields had a dangling relationTo

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against migrate.ts's collision guard, backup.ts, the visible-staleness/keyword-collision/subscribeAuthExpired/icsMonthRecords families, and round 504's own just-rejected SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS candidate, and steered toward round 504's own suggested leftover areas, found a real, high-severity bug: `codegen.ts`'s `renderServerJs` table-creation loop (the `references` computation, line 339 before this round) emitted a `REFERENCES "<relationTo>"(id)` clause for any relation field whose `relationTo` was a non-empty string, with no check that it actually names one of the spec's own entities. `FieldSchema` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) only requires `relationTo` to be non-empty -- nothing anywhere enforces it must match a real entity name. `pipeline.ts`'s own documented characteristic of `/refine` (it regenerates the whole spec from prose with no access to the previous structure) makes it entirely plausible for an entity to be renamed or dropped by a later refine while another entity's relation field keeps its old `relationTo` string, unnoticed -- the spec stays 100% schema-valid and exportable. SQLite only checks a `REFERENCES` target at write time, not at `CREATE TABLE` time, so the generated table silently builds successfully and the break surfaces only when someone actually tries to write a row -- at which point *every* insert into that table fails, including ones that never touch the dangling relation field at all, with a cryptic `"no such table: main.Driver"` and no indication of the real cause. Once exported, the standalone app has zero runtime dependency on Forge AI (no Debug Agent, no recovery path) -- the affected entity becomes permanently unusable for creates/updates in the user's downloaded app.

**Independent verification**: read `migrate.ts`'s own equivalent guard directly (`entityNames.has(field.relationTo)`, used consistently across its table-creation, migration-diff, and FK-reference logic) and confirmed `codegen.ts`'s table-creation loop had no matching check, despite `codegen.ts`'s own *generated frontend* code (line 2623, `ALL_ENTITIES.some((e) => e.name === name)`) already filtering on exactly this condition -- an internal inconsistency within codegen.ts itself, not just a codegen-vs-migrate.ts divergence. Reproduced directly with `node:sqlite` (not just the agent's own repro): created a table with a column `REFERENCES "Driver"(id)` where no `Driver` table exists, with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, and confirmed inserting a row with that column set to `NULL` still fails with `"no such table: main.Driver"` -- the missing parent table itself breaks the write, not the FK constraint evaluating false. Confirmed the live preview is unaffected: `migrate.ts` already omits the clause correctly for a dangling `relationTo`, verified by reading its guard directly.

**The fix**: added `const ENTITY_NAMES = new Set(ENTITIES.map((e) => e.name));` once, before the table-creation loop, and added `&& ENTITY_NAMES.has(field.relationTo)` to the `references` computation's condition -- mirroring `migrate.ts`'s own `entityNames.has(field.relationTo)` guard and the generated frontend's own `ALL_ENTITIES.some(...)` filter.

**Tests**: added a new regression test to `codegen.test.ts`, placed right after the existing round-311/313 FK-enforcement test (the closest precedent in shape) -- a spec with one entity (`Order`) whose only relation field (`driverId`) points at a nonexistent `"Driver"` entity. Asserts the generated `server.js` source contains no `REFERENCES "Driver"` clause, then spawns the real generated server (the same `spawn(process.execPath, ["--experimental-sqlite", "server.js"], ...)` pattern every other FK/relation test in this file already uses) and confirms `POST /api/Order` with the dangling field entirely unset succeeds with a real `201`, not the `400` it returned before the fix. Also updated the pre-existing round-311/313 FK test's own pinned-regex assertion (it matched the exact literal source text of the `references` line, which this fix necessarily changed) to match the corrected line.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `codegen.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping both the new test and the updated pinned-regex assertion in place). Confirmed two distinct, exactly-predicted failures: the new test failed with `400 !== 201` on the `POST /api/Order` assertion (the exact "no such table" break reproduced through the real HTTP route), and the pre-existing FK test's pinned-regex assertion failed to match the old, unfixed source line. Restored `codegen.ts` from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 140, `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 449 (+1), `@forge/web` 861 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed, exported-app-only (confirmed the live preview was never affected, since `migrate.ts` already had the correct guard). This is a genuinely new finding, distinct from every denylisted pattern this round avoided -- a dangling `relationTo` reaching codegen.ts's table-creation code specifically, a combination no prior round had tested. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-504 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 506: WhatsApp's "Send" silently addressed a wrong, non-existent JID for a local-format phone number missing its country code

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against migrate.ts's collision guard, backup.ts, the visible-staleness/revalidation-effect/keyword-collision/subscribeAuthExpired/icsMonthRecords/renderServerJs-relationTo families, and round 504's rejected SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS candidate, found a real, high-impact bug: `WhatsAppWebManager.sendMessage` (`apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.ts`) built the outgoing WhatsApp JID as `` `${normalizePhone(to)}@s.whatsapp.net` `` with no country-code handling at all. `normalizePhone` (`apps/api/src/whatsapp.ts`) only strips non-digits and leading zeros -- for a bare local-format number like `"050-123-4567"` (this app's own seed data and every Hebrew template's own convention for phone fields) it produces `"501234567"`, missing the country code (`"972"`) entirely. The existing unit test for this exact scenario (`whatsappWeb.test.ts`, pre-round) asserted the resulting wrong JID (`"501234567@s.whatsapp.net"`) as if it were the correct, intended behavior. Crucially this isn't a rare input: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s "Send WhatsApp" row action feeds a record's raw, unmodified stored phone field straight through `App.tsx`'s `whatsappPrefillTo` into `WhatsAppPanel`'s send form, which submits it as-is -- so the one convenience feature built to avoid retyping a number systematically hits this gap using the app's own conventional local-format data, and `sendMessage` still returned `{ok: true}` with no indication the message never reached anyone.

**Independent verification**: read `normalizePhone` and `findMatchingRecord` (`apps/api/src/whatsapp.ts`) directly and confirmed `findMatchingRecord`'s own suffix-based local/international reconciliation exists specifically for comparing *the same number* against itself in two formats (incoming vs. stored) -- not a general country-code-inference mechanism applicable to an arbitrary different contact, ruling out reusing it directly for outbound JID construction. Ran `normalizePhone("050-123-4567")` directly and confirmed it returns `"501234567"`. Checked `git log -S "already-accepted gap"` to see where the test's own "known, separate, already-accepted gap" comment came from: it was added by the earlier round that fixed a narrower, separate bug (stripping a full leading "00" international access code, not this one) -- scoping language for that round's own fix, not a reasoned, documented product decision like the genuinely-closed candidates (CollaboratorsPanel email enumeration, round 374; ProductSpecSchema relationTo rejection, round 415), so this was legitimate to revisit. Confirmed `session.phoneNumber` (set from the connected account's own Baileys JID on `connection: "open"`) is available at send time as a reliable reference for what a real, fully-qualified number for this account's country looks like.

**The fix**: rejected the temptation to *guess* a country code (there's no reliable way to infer one for an arbitrary different contact's number, unlike `findMatchingRecord`'s narrower same-number-two-formats case) in favor of refusing honestly, mirroring this exact function's own existing "abc" → `invalid_phone_number` precedent one line above: if the connected account has a known own number and the normalized `to` is shorter than it, return `{ok: false, error: "missing_country_code"}` instead of building a JID that addresses nothing. Checked the `/send` route and `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`: this error code surfaces to the user exactly like the pre-existing `"invalid_phone_number"` already does (passed through as a raw string, no i18n translation layer in that specific path) -- consistent with an already-established pattern for this result shape, not a new inconsistency to fix.

**Tests**: renamed/updated the pre-existing unit test that had pinned the wrong JID as correct into a new test asserting the honest rejection (`"missing_country_code"`, no `sendCalls`), and changed the adjacent "succeeds once connected" test to use an already-fully-qualified target number so it still demonstrates a real successful send. ### Round 507: round 506's own fix wrongly refused every WhatsApp send to a legitimately shorter-numbered country

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against migrate.ts's collision guard, backup.ts, the visible-staleness/revalidation-effect/keyword-collision/subscribeAuthExpired/icsMonthRecords/renderServerJs-relationTo/missing-country-code families (round 506's fix itself was listed as closed), found a real false positive introduced by round 506's own fix in the same round it was deployed: the `missing_country_code` check compared the target number's digit count (`phone.length`) against the connected WhatsApp account's own number's digit count (`ownNumber.length`), rejecting anything shorter. But full E.164 digit counts vary by country -- an Israeli number normalizes to 12 digits, a US number to only 11 -- so a business connected with an Israeli WhatsApp account sending to any legitimately-shorter-numbered country's contact (the US, for instance) would be wrongly refused as "missing its country code" on *every single send*, not as a rare edge case. This wasn't a hypothetical: the fix's own justifying comment already said "for a plausible same-country contact," acknowledging the scoping the code never actually enforced.

**Independent verification**: read the current `sendMessage` code directly (lines 391-413) and confirmed the comparison is a bare `phone.length < ownNumber.length` with no country-awareness at all. Ran the exact `normalizePhone` logic by hand: `normalizePhone("972501234567")` (a connected Israeli account) → `"972501234567"`, 12 digits; `normalizePhone("+1 202-555-0123")` (a fully legitimate, fully-qualified US number) → `"12025550123"`, 11 digits -- confirmed `11 < 12` is `true`, so the old code would incorrectly return `{ok: false, error: "missing_country_code"}` for this completely valid send. Read all of `whatsappWeb.test.ts`'s `sendMessage` tests and confirmed none covered a cross-country pair -- every existing test either used same-length numbers or a target *longer* than the connected account's own number (the direction that doesn't trigger the bug), so this gap was real and untested, not something round 506 had already considered and accepted.

**The fix**: replaced the cross-number digit-count comparison with the actual signal `normalizePhone`'s own doc comment already establishes and that round 506 should have used instead: counting leading zeros in the *raw* (pre-normalization) input. Exactly one leading zero is the local trunk prefix convention (e.g. Israeli `"050-..."`) -- the country code is genuinely missing. Two leading zeros is the "00" international access code convention (already fully qualified once the normalization strips them, the same case round 506's own earlier fix separately handled). Zero leading zeros is either already-international or untaggable either way -- never flagged. This needs no other number to compare against at all, so it structurally cannot produce a cross-country false positive, and it no longer depends on `session.phoneNumber` for this specific check (still used elsewhere in the file for status/display, unaffected).

**Tests**: added a new regression test -- connects with an Israeli own number (`"972501234567"`, 12 digits) and sends to `"+1 202-555-0123"` (a fully-qualified US number, 11 digits), asserting the send succeeds and builds the correct JID (`"12025550123@s.whatsapp.net"`), not a rejection. Re-ran all 3 pre-existing `sendMessage` tests (the local-format rejection, the "00" access code success, and the already-qualified success) by hand-tracing the new leading-zero logic against each one's exact input and confirmed every one still produces its documented expected result -- none needed changes.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `whatsappWeb.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: only the new cross-country test failed (`result.error === "missing_country_code"` instead of `ok: true`), all 20 other tests in the file passed unchanged. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 140, `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 451 (+1), `@forge/web` 861 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. This is a legitimate, necessary follow-up to round 506's own fix within the very next round, not a reopening of a settled pattern without new information -- round 506 closed the original "silently builds a wrong JID" bug, and this round closed a distinct, newly-introduced regression in that same fix's own guard logic (an unsound cross-number comparison), found via genuinely fresh verification (a concrete repro with real digit counts for two different countries), exactly the standard this loop already applies to any claim before accepting it. WhatsApp remains live-app-only; no `codegen.ts` duplicate exists. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. ### Round 508: the Kanban board's own "move" select (and the add/edit form's enum select) silently blanked out a record's real, legacy enum value

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 507 (including both WhatsApp missing-country-code rounds), found a real inconsistency *within* an earlier fix: round `04a0c70` ("Fix Kanban board silently dropping records with unrecognized enum values") correctly stopped a record with a legacy enum value (e.g. a stale `"archived"` status left behind after an AI refine renamed the field's options -- `migrate.ts` only ever adds columns, never rewrites existing row data) from vanishing off the board, by collecting it into a synthetic `"(other)"` column. What that fix never touched: `BoardCard`'s own per-card "move" `<select>` (`EntityPanel.tsx`) only ever renders an `<option>` for each of the field's *current* `enumValues` -- never for the stale value itself. A controlled `<select>` whose `value` matches no `<option>` is silently blanked by the browser (`selectedIndex -1`), so the one control meant to show/change a card's current stage showed nothing at all for exactly the records this feature exists to stop hiding, even though the same stale value renders correctly everywhere else (the badge, CSV export, the column label). The identical pattern exists in `FieldInput`'s generic enum `<select>` (used by the regular add/edit form and the inline table-cell editor), and both are duplicated in `codegen.ts`'s generated standalone app.

**Independent verification**: read `BoardCard` (`EntityPanel.tsx` lines 416-426) and confirmed its `<select>`'s options come purely from `uniqueEnumValues(boardField.enumValues).map(...)`, with the controlled `value` set to the raw (possibly stale) `record[boardField.name]`. Read `FieldInput`'s enum branch (lines 712-732) and confirmed the identical shape. Confirmed the generated `codegen.ts` output has byte-for-byte the same gap in its own `BoardCard` and `FieldInput` functions. Confirmed via `git show 04a0c70` that the earlier fix's own scope was exactly the board-column grouping (`groupByField`'s "(other)" bucket) and never mentioned the per-card select at all -- this is a gap inside that fix's own blind spot, not a design choice (nothing claims the select should be blank for an out-of-range value; every sibling rendering path for the same value deliberately shows the raw string rather than hiding it).

**The fix**: in both `BoardCard` and `FieldInput`'s enum branch (`EntityPanel.tsx` and the matching functions in `codegen.ts`), compute the field's known (deduped) enum values as before, then render one extra leading `<option>` for the current value whenever it's non-empty and not already among the known values -- so the select actually reflects the stored data instead of silently discarding it. `onChange` and the rest of the component are untouched; a user explicitly re-picking a real stage still works exactly as before.

**Tests**: added a new test to `EntityPanel.test.ts`, right after the existing "(other)" column test, asserting the board card's `.board-card-move` select's `value` equals the record's real stale status (`"archived"`), not an empty string. For `codegen.ts`, updated the existing pinned-regex test ("every enum `<select>` branch routes through [uniqueEnumValues]") to match the new intermediate variable names (`knownBoardValues`/`boardOptionValues`, `knownEnumValues`/`enumOptionValues`) instead of the old direct inline call, and added a new test that extracts the real generated option-list computation via this file's own established "real generated code via `new Function`" standard and calls it directly with a stale value, an already-known value, and an empty value, confirming the extra option is added only when genuinely needed and never duplicated.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping all four test files' new/updated tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failures: the new `EntityPanel.test.ts` test failed with `moveSelect.value === ""` instead of `"archived"`; both the updated pinned-regex test and the new generated-code test in `codegen.test.ts` failed to match/compute against the old source. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 140, `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 452 (+1), `@forge/web` 862 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed, fixed in both the live preview and the exported codegen app. This is a genuinely new finding, distinct from every denylisted pattern this round avoided -- a gap left behind inside an earlier fix's own blind spot (the board-column grouping fix never touched the per-card select), not a reopening of the already-closed "(other)" column mechanism itself. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-507 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 509: `handleToggleColumn`'s own "keep at least one column visible" guard miscounted once `hiddenFields` held a name for a field that no longer exists

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 508, found that `hiddenFields`' own persisted-load effect (`EntityPanel.tsx`) is one of four structurally-identical siblings (alongside `recentSearches`, `columnOrderState`, `columnWidths`, `groupFieldName`) that never received the `fieldNamesKey` re-validation fix given to `viewMode`/`fieldFilters`/`sortKeys` in rounds 490/493/500 -- all five load from storage on `[projectId, entity.name]` only, never re-checking against `entity.fields` while the same entity tab stays mounted through a live refine. The subagent's own report already ruled out two of the four as not real bugs: `groupFieldName` and `columnOrderState` gracefully degrade in their consuming code. `hiddenFields` does not: `handleToggleColumn`'s "keep at least one column visible" guard computed `visibleCount` as `entity.fields.length - hiddenFields.size` -- a stale name in `hiddenFields` that no longer matches any of `entity.fields` is still counted toward `.size`, undercounting how many columns are genuinely visible and wrongly refusing to let the user hide a column that was never actually blanked out.

**Independent verification**: read `EntityPanel.tsx` lines 1005-1049 and confirmed `hiddenFields`' loading effect has no `fieldNamesKey` dependency, unlike the three already-fixed siblings (read in full at lines 1110-1178) which do. Read `handleToggleColumn` (lines 1366-1370) and confirmed the exact `entity.fields.length - hiddenFields.size` arithmetic. Confirmed the identical duplicated pattern exists in `codegen.ts` (lines 2906-2910), with the minor, expected difference that the exported app's `getHiddenColumns`/`toggleColumnVisibility` take no `projectId` (the exported app is single-project). Considered whether this bug's actual trigger -- a live refine mutating `entity.fields` without a remount -- is even reachable in the exported standalone app, since its `ENTITIES` constant is baked in as static JSON at export time with no runtime refine capability at all. Concluded it is still reachable there by a different, simpler path: a user re-running a newer export of the same project in a browser that still holds an older export's `localStorage` for that origin (keyed only by entity name, with no export-version dimension) would see the newer export's `entity.fields` against the old export's stale `hiddenFields` entries -- the same phantom-name scenario, reached without any live refine at all.

**The fix**: in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, count only the hidden names that still name a real field (`entity.fields.filter((f) => hiddenFields.has(f.name)).length`) before subtracting from `entity.fields.length`, instead of trusting `hiddenFields.size` directly. The guard's own behavior for a genuinely-hidden real field is unchanged.

**Tests**: added a new test to `EntityPanel.test.ts` that seeds `localStorage`'s `forge.hiddenColumns` with a stale entry naming a field ("stage") absent from the test entity's two real fields, confirms both real columns still render as visible and checked (the phantom entry hides nothing), then confirms the Status checkbox can still be unchecked -- hiding it -- instead of being silently refused. For `codegen.ts`, added a new test to `codegen.test.ts` using this file's own established "real generated code via `new Function`" standard, extracting the real generated `hiddenCount`/`visibleCount` computation and asserting a phantom hidden name is never counted toward `visibleCount`, while a real hidden field still counts normally.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping both test files' new tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failures: the new `EntityPanel.test.ts` test's `waitForCondition` on the post-hide header count never became true (the guard still refused the hide); the new `codegen.test.ts` test failed with "expected to find handleToggleColumn's real generated visibleCount computation" (the old source has no `hiddenCount` variable for the regex to match). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 140, `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 453 (+1), `@forge/web` 863 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed, fixed in both the live preview and the exported codegen app. `groupFieldName` and `columnOrderState` (the other two unfixed siblings besides `hiddenFields`) remain confirmed as not needing the `fieldNamesKey` fix, since their own consuming code already degrades gracefully against a stale name. ### Round 510: deleting your account could leave a stale-spec project's localStorage preferences orphaned forever

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 509, found a client/server asymmetry: `DELETE /auth/account`'s own server-side cleanup deliberately uses `listOwnedProjectIds` (a raw `SELECT id` query, round 411) instead of the tolerant `listProjectsForUser`, specifically because the latter silently drops any project whose stored `spec_json` no longer parses against today's (stricter) `ProductSpecSchema` -- a real, expected case for a project written by an older app version, per `tryRowToProject`'s own doc comment. `DeleteAccountPanel.tsx`, which needs the same complete set of project ids for a conceptually identical task -- sweeping this browser's own `localStorage` preference stores (`projectPreferenceCleanup.ts`) for every project this account is about to lose -- was never given an equivalent robust source. It derived its ids from `listProjects()` (`GET /projects`, the same tolerant `listProjectsForUser`), inheriting exactly the gap the server-side route was written to avoid.

**Independent verification**: read `DeleteAccountPanel.tsx` lines 56-66, confirming `ownedProjectIds`/`sharedProjectIds` (both the warning's project count and `onDeleted`'s arguments) are derived by filtering `listProjects()`'s response on `ownerId`. Read `packages/db/src/projects.ts`'s `tryRowToProject` (lines 53-61) and `listProjectsForUser` (lines 112-122), confirming any row whose `spec_json` fails `ProductSpecSchema.parse` is silently excluded. Read `apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts`'s `DELETE /auth/account` handler (lines 190-221) and its own doc comment (lines 176-188), confirming it deliberately uses `listOwnedProjectIds` instead for exactly this reason, and that `removeAllCollaborationsForUser` (used for shared-project cleanup) operates by `userId` alone with no project-id dependency at all -- so the server-side deletion itself is unaffected by this gap; only the client's own `localStorage` sweep is. Confirmed `project_collaborators` stores `projectId` directly (no join to `projects.spec_json` needed), so a robust `listCollaboratedProjectIds` was possible with the identical no-parsing guarantee as `listOwnedProjectIds`.

**The fix**: added `listCollaboratedProjectIds(db, userId)` to `packages/db/src/collaborators.ts` (a bare `SELECT projectId FROM project_collaborators WHERE userId = ?`, never touching `projects.spec_json`). Added a new route, `GET /projects/mine-ids` (registered before `GET /projects/:id` so the literal path is never captured as an `:id`), returning `{ ownedProjectIds, sharedProjectIds }` from `listOwnedProjectIds` + `listCollaboratedProjectIds` -- the robust complement to `GET /projects`, mirroring the reasoning `DELETE /auth/account` already established. Added a client function `listMyProjectIds()` and switched `DeleteAccountPanel.tsx`'s mount effect to use it instead of `listProjects()`, deriving both the summary counts and the actual ids passed to `onDeleted` from the same robust source.

**Tests**: added `listCollaboratedProjectIds returns every project id this user collaborates on...` to `collaborators.test.ts`. Added `GET /projects/mine-ids still returns an owned or shared project whose stored spec no longer parses...` to `app.test.ts`, writing a stale-spec project row directly via raw SQL (the same round-411 technique) for both an owned and a shared project, confirming `GET /projects` excludes both while `GET /projects/mine-ids` includes both, correctly split by ownership. Rewrote `DeleteAccountPanel.test.ts`'s `withListProjectsStub` helper to stub the new `/api/projects/mine-ids` endpoint instead, and added a new test asserting the panel still counts and passes along an id for which no parseable `Project` object exists at all (standing in for the stale-spec case), while `GET /api/projects` itself is stubbed to throw if called, proving the panel no longer depends on it.

**Regression-proof**: backed up all 5 changed implementation files (`collaborators.ts`, `index.ts`, `routes/projects.ts`, `api.ts`, `DeleteAccountPanel.tsx`), reverted all five via `git checkout --` (keeping all three test files' new/updated tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failures: the db-level test failed on module load (no such export); the new API route test got a 404 instead of 200; both web-layer tests touching the new summary/`onDeleted` flow failed with `waitForCondition: condition never became true` (the reverted component never calls the new endpoint), while the unaffected zero-projects test still passed on both versions. Restored all five files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16, `@forge/db` 141 (+1), `@forge/spec-engine` 111 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 454 (+1), `@forge/web` 864 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed. WhatsApp's own `deleteWhatsAppData` and checkpoint cleanup inside `deleteProject` are untouched by this gap (they're reached via the already-robust `listOwnedProjectIds` loop in `DELETE /auth/account`, never via the client's own id collection).
