### Round 511: clean survey — no new candidate cleared the bar

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, denylisted against every closed family through round 510, ran a broad sweep across `packages/db`, `packages/spec-engine`, `apps/api` routes/services, and `apps/web` components outside the already-mined `EntityPanel.tsx` mechanisms. Its top candidate: `migrate.ts`'s "reused column" branch (lines 375-393, reached when a field is removed from an entity and later re-added under the same name with no `prevField`) compares the column's physical SQL type against the new field's `sqlTypeFor`, but `text`/`longtext`/`enum`/`date` all collapse onto the same `TEXT` bucket -- so a field removed as `date` and re-added as `enum` (or any other same-bucket pair) reports no `type_changed` at all, leaving stale, now-invalid data with zero warning. The agent reproduced this directly against the real code (build → remove `startDate:date` → re-add `startDate:enum` → `diffAndMigrate` reports only `new_column`, no `type_changed`).

**Independent verification**: read `migrate.ts` in full, including round 444's own roadmap entry (`docs/roadmap.md`, "Round 444"), which fixed an *oscillation false positive* in the *different*, `prevField`-based branch (a field continuously present across refines, `relationTo` or type going A→B→A) and explicitly left `type_changed`'s identical oscillation problem unfixed there, naming the exact same root cause this round's candidate runs into: "`text`/`longtext`/`enum`/`date` collapse onto one indistinguishable SQL storage bucket... requires persisting a field's full type lineage beyond one hop, which does not currently exist" -- characterizing it as "a design/judgment-call item for a dedicated round... not a quick mechanical fix." Confirmed this round's candidate is a different branch (field fully removed-then-re-added, not continuously present) with the opposite symptom (false negative, not false positive) -- but a fix for it faces the identical blocker: the reused-column branch has no `prevField` at all to compare against (that's the entire premise of the branch), so distinguishing a genuine date→enum reuse from a benign one requires exactly the same not-yet-built type-lineage history round 444 already named and deferred. There is no narrower, safe fix available here the way round 444 found one for `relation_target_changed` (every `relationTo` maps to one distinct physical table, with no bucket collision to worry about) -- `sqlTypeFor`'s bucket collapse is unconditional for this data type family. Also independently checked the runner-up (`whatsapp.ts`'s `findMatchingRecord`, a phone-to-record matcher with no cross-entity disambiguation) and confirmed its own doc comment explicitly labels it "best-effort match" with the fuzzy-suffix tradeoff spelled out -- a deliberate, documented design choice, not an accidental gap.

**Topic status**: no new candidate implemented this round. The top candidate is architecturally the same deliberately-deferred limitation round 444 already named (no persisted field-type lineage beyond one hop) manifesting through a different call path, not a genuinely distinct, independently-fixable bug -- fixing it properly would mean building the same type-lineage infrastructure round 444 scoped out as a dedicated-round undertaking, not a mechanical patch. This is a legitimate clean-survey round, in the same spirit as rounds 463, 466, 482, and 504: a thorough sweep that correctly declined to force a fix onto a already-catalogued, deliberately-scoped-out limitation. ### Round 513: the "Appointments & Clients" template's own Appointment.date field promised a time it could never hold

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 512, found that the curated "Appointments & Clients" Templates Gallery entry (`packages/spec-engine/src/templates.ts`) labels its `Appointment.date` field "תאריך ושעה"/"Date & Time" in both `spec` and `specEn`, while its `type` is plain `"date"` -- a field type that, everywhere in this system, is strictly date-only with no time-of-day component at all: `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`'s `sqlTypeFor` stores every `"date"` field as a plain `TEXT` column, `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` renders it as a native `<input type="date">` (a browser calendar-day picker with no time selector), and `@forge/shared`'s own `FieldType` union has no `"datetime"` variant anywhere.

**Independent verification**: confirmed both label occurrences directly (`templates.ts` lines 530 and 579), confirmed `EntityPanel.tsx` line 787-798 renders `type: "date"` as `<input type="date">`, and confirmed via grep across every other `"date"`-typed field in `templates.ts` (14 total across all 6 templates) that this was the *only* one whose label claimed a time component -- every other date field in this exact file (`closeDate`, `dueDate`, `orderDate`, and two other plain `date`-named fields) uses a plain "תאריך"/"Date" label, confirming this was a one-off content defect in this one template, not a systemic labeling convention being violated. Confirmed via `packages/db/src/seed.ts` and `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s `DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS`/`END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` that all date-field heuristics key off `field.name` (already exactly `"date"`, already matching), never `field.label`, so relabeling has zero effect on any other behavior (seeding, calendar grouping, sorting). This is reachable by any real user: the Templates Gallery is a one-click, product-curated path (`GET /projects/templates`, `POST /projects/from-template` in `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`, both live routes) -- not an AI-generated spec that could plausibly contain an occasional mistake -- so every person who picks "Appointments & Clients" got an app whose one scheduling field's label permanently over-promised a capability (telling two same-day appointments apart by time, preventing/noticing a same-day double-booking) the field could never deliver.

**The fix**: relabeled `Appointment.date` to plain "תאריך" (Hebrew `spec`) and "Date" (English `specEn`), matching every other date field's label convention in this same file. Did not add a new `"datetime"` field type -- that would require new SQL storage handling, new `EntityPanel`/`codegen.ts` input rendering, new CSV/ICS/seed/search formatting, and a new `@forge/shared` `FieldType` variant threaded through the entire system, which is a genuinely large, cross-cutting design candidate, not a single-round content fix; the honest, minimally-scoped fix is to stop promising a capability the system doesn't have.

**Tests**: added a new general regression test to `templates.test.ts` -- `no "date"-type field's label claims a time-of-day capability the field can't actually hold` -- which scans every template's `spec` and `specEn` for any `"date"`-typed field whose label contains a Hebrew or English time-claiming substring ("ושעה"/"שעה ", "time"/"& time"), generalized so any future template content with this same mismatch is caught immediately rather than only this one instance.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `templates.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `templates.test.ts` in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: `template "appointments" entity "Appointment" field "date": Hebrew label "תאריך ושעה" claims a time component...`. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. One parallel background run (full suite + build run simultaneously) produced a single flaky failure in an unrelated `apps/api` WhatsApp async test -- isolating `apps/api`'s suite alone confirmed 455/455 clean, and one final fully sequential run (no concurrent build) confirmed the whole monorepo clean with no flakes: `@forge/shared` 16 (unchanged), `@forge/db` 141 (unchanged), `@forge/spec-engine` 112 (+1), `@forge/api` 455 (unchanged), `@forge/web` 864 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

### Round 514: CSV import's boolean coercion was the one field type with no rejection path for an unrecognized value

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 513, found that `buildImportRecords`'s boolean-field branch -- in both `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts` (live preview) and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s identical duplicate (exported standalone app) -- had no rejection path at all: `record[field.name] = ["true", "1", "yes"].includes(raw.toLowerCase())`. Every other coerced type in the exact same function (`number`, `enum`, `date`) explicitly validates the cell and pushes a row-numbered `rowError` when it doesn't parse; boolean alone silently resolved anything outside that three-value allowlist to `false`, with the row still accepted into `result.records` and nothing added to `result.errors`.

**Independent verification**: read both copies of `buildImportRecords` in full (`entityFormatting.ts` lines ~1109-1198, `codegen.ts`'s identically-structured duplicate) and confirmed the boolean branch (then at `entityFormatting.ts` line 1161-1162) was the only one of the four coerced types with no `if (!valid) { rowError = ...; break; }` guard -- `number` rejects a `NaN`, `enum` rejects an unmatched value/label, `date` rejects a malformed string, but boolean just defaulted. Confirmed the existing test (`buildImportRecords coerces booleans, numbers, and enum labels...`) only ever exercises `"true"`/`"yes"`/empty, never asserting anything about an unrecognized value -- so this was genuinely untested-for-the-failure-case behavior, not a gap already caught elsewhere. Confirmed the real-world reachability for this specifically Hebrew-first product: a shop owner re-importing a spreadsheet with a boolean column hand-written as "כן"/"לא" (the natural Hebrew yes/no, not an English string) would have every true-valued row silently flipped to `false`, with the UI reporting a clean, zero-error import -- the single most dangerous failure mode (quietly wrong data reported as success) in an otherwise consistently-validated import path.

**The fix**: added explicit `BOOLEAN_TRUE_VALUES`/`BOOLEAN_FALSE_VALUES` allowlists (`["true", "1", "yes", "כן"]` / `["false", "0", "no", "לא"]`) to both files' `buildImportRecords`. A raw cell matching neither list now produces a row-numbered error ("isn't a recognized yes/no value") instead of silently defaulting to `false`, matching the number/enum/date branches' own established validation convention. In `codegen.ts`, the two new arrays are declared *inside* `buildImportRecords` itself (not at module scope) specifically so `codegen.test.ts`'s existing convention of extracting and running the function in isolation via regex (as it already does for `isValidDate`/`matchesImportHeader`) continues to work without needing to also extract a separate constants block.

**Tests**: added `buildImportRecords rejects an unrecognized boolean value instead of silently defaulting it to false` to `entityFormatting.test.ts`, and the equivalent `the exported EntityView's CSV import rejects an unrecognized boolean value...` to `codegen.test.ts` (executing the real generated function extracted from actual codegen output, not a reimplementation). Both assert a Hebrew "כן" resolves to `true`, a Hebrew "לא" resolves to `false`, and an unrecognized value ("maybe") produces exactly one row-numbered error rather than a silent `false`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed implementation files, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure in both: `active: false` where `active: true` was expected for the "כן" row, and the "maybe" row missing from `result.errors`. Restored both from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16 (unchanged), `@forge/db` 141 (unchanged), `@forge/spec-engine` 112 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 456 (+1), `@forge/web` 865 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed, fixed identically in both the live-preview and exported-app copies -- no port-gap remains. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-513 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 515: FieldInput's relation picker had no fallback for a stored value its own fetch failure wiped out

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 514, found that `FieldInput`'s relation branch -- in both `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` (live preview) and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s identical duplicate (exported app) -- has no fallback for a stored id missing from `relatedEntityRecords`, unlike the `enum` branch a few lines below it (round 508's own fix), which explicitly re-injects a synthetic `<option>` for a stale value no longer in `field.enumValues`. The `loadRelated` effect just above it deliberately swallows ANY related-entity fetch failure into an empty array (`catch { return [name, []] }`), not `undefined` -- so a single transient fetch error (network blip, auth race) wipes out every real option, and any record whose relation field already holds a real, valid value renders that field as blank/unselected the moment it's opened for editing: the exact "stored value doesn't match any `<option>`" bug class round 508 already fixed for `enum`, just reached via a fetch failure instead of a stale AI-refine value.

**Independent verification**: read both copies of `FieldInput`'s relation branch in full (`EntityPanel.tsx` lines 675-707, `codegen.ts`'s identically-structured duplicate) and confirmed neither re-injects a synthetic option for the current value the way the enum branch does. Read `loadRelated` (`EntityPanel.tsx` lines 911-934, and its `codegen.ts` duplicate) and confirmed the `catch` genuinely resolves to `[name, []]`, not a rejected promise or `undefined` -- so the "still loading" guard (`!relatedEntityRecords`) stops applying the moment the fetch settles, success or failure alike, and the real, enabled `<select>` renders with whatever (possibly empty) array it got. Confirmed foreign-key constraints are enforced (`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, with an existing 409-on-violation test), so this can't be triggered by a deleted related row -- it's reachable purely via an ordinary transient failure of the related-entity fetch, the same category of failure the `catch` block itself exists to tolerate. If the relation field is `required`, the browser's native validation then blocks saving that record at all (no `<option>` matches the real value, so nothing satisfies `required`) until a later successful refetch -- a genuine "can't save this record anymore" regression triggered purely by an unrelated fetch hiccup, not by anything the user did.

**The fix**: in both `FieldInput` relation branches, when the field's current `value` is a non-empty id not present among `relatedEntityRecords`, render one extra synthetic leading `<option>` for it (labeled `#<id>`, the same fallback convention already used elsewhere in this codebase for an unresolvable relation id -- `entityFormatting.ts`, `backup.ts`, `displayField.ts`), exactly mirroring the enum branch's own `enumOptionValues` pattern.

**Tests**: added `EntityPanel's relation field keeps the record's real stored value selectable even when the related-entity fetch fails` to `EntityPanel.test.ts`, and the equivalent `the exported EntityView's relation field keeps the record's real stored value selectable...` to `codegen.test.ts` (executing the real generated `EntityView.jsx` via `render`, not a reimplementation). Both mock the related entity's fetch to return a real HTTP error response (`500`) rather than a rejected `fetch()` call -- the latter would instead trip `fetchWithWakeRetry`'s cold-start retry loop (wakeRetry.ts), which treats any thrown/rejected `fetch()` as a transient connection failure and retries for up to ~101s+ before giving up, entirely beside the point of this test. A real 4xx/5xx response is returned immediately per that file's own documented contract ("Only fetch() throwing... triggers a retry; an actual HTTP error response... is returned immediately"), and `loadRelated`'s `catch` swallows the resulting thrown `Error` into `[]` just as fast either way.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed implementation files, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure in both: `'' !== '9'` where the select's value should have reflected the record's real stored courier id. Restored both from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full suite + root build, no flakes this run: `@forge/shared` 16 (unchanged), `@forge/db` 141 (unchanged), `@forge/spec-engine` 112 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 457 (+1), `@forge/web` 866 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this bug is closed, fixed identically in both the live-preview and exported-app copies -- no port-gap remains. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-514 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 516: the "Appointments & Clients" template's Hebrew status enum mistranslated "scheduled" as "recurring/standing"

Confirmed the template's own English sibling (`APPOINTMENTS_ENTITIES_EN`, line 586) correctly maps `scheduled: "Scheduled"`, confirming the Hebrew side alone had drifted, not a dual-language design choice. ### Round 517: every Templates Gallery template's `roles` array was plain English, never translated for the Hebrew spec

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 516, found that all 6 templates' `roles` arrays (`packages/spec-engine/src/templates.ts`, e.g. restaurant's `["Manager", "Staff"]`) were reused byte-for-byte between the Hebrew `spec` and the English `specEn` passed to the `spec({...})` helper -- unlike every other display field in the same spec (entity `label`, field `label`, `enumLabels`, `description`, `summary`), each of which already has a real, separately-authored Hebrew/English split.

**Independent verification**: grepped every `roles:` occurrence in `templates.ts` and confirmed all 6 pairs (restaurant, crm, project-tracker, volunteers, appointments, inventory) were identical strings between the Hebrew `spec({...})` call and the English `specEn({...})` call immediately below it -- no `rolesHe` field or equivalent exists anywhere in the file. Confirmed this codebase has an established convention for translating roles to Hebrew: `packages/spec-engine/src/heuristic.ts`'s `matchRoles(text, isHebrew)` (lines ~101-110) explicitly returns `rule.labelHe` from `domainEntities.ts`'s `ROLE_RULES` when `isHebrew` is true, for every AI/heuristic-generated spec -- templates were the one spec-generation path that skipped this entirely, because the `roles` array is hardcoded shared literal data rather than derived from a language flag. Traced the real user-facing reachability: `POST /projects/from-template` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` line ~462) picks `template.spec` for any non-`"en"` `lang`, and `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s spec review screen (line ~1658-1670, under the Hebrew heading `t("spec.roles.heading")`) renders `project.spec.roles` directly as chips with no translation layer -- so a Hebrew-UI user picking any of the 6 templates saw English words like "Manager"/"Staff" mixed into an otherwise fully-Hebrew screen (Hebrew entity names, Hebrew summary, Hebrew field labels all around them). Confirmed `ProductSpecSchema.roles` is unconstrained (`z.array(z.string()).min(1)`, `packages/shared/src/index.ts` line 203), so Hebrew role strings parse without any schema change, and confirmed `templates.test.ts` had no existing assertion comparing `spec.roles` against `specEn.roles`, so this gap passed every existing test. Distinct from round 492's `specEn`-lang-selection fix and rounds 513/516's Appointments-specific `date`/`status` field fixes: this is a different field (`roles`, affecting ALL 6 templates) with a different root cause (no Hebrew/English split exists at all, rather than an existing split containing a wrong translation).

**The fix**: wrote natural Hebrew role names for each template's Hebrew `spec({...})` call, reusing this codebase's own established gender-neutral slash convention (`"מנהל/ת"` already used by `domainEntities.ts`'s `ROLE_RULES.Manager`, `"חבר/ת צוות"` already used by `heuristic.ts`'s `memberLabel` for "Member") and coining consistent new translations for the rest (`"נציג/ת מכירות"` for Sales Rep, `"מנהל/ת פרויקט"` for Project Manager, `"רכז/ת"`/`"מתנדב/ת"` for Coordinator/Volunteer, `"מנהל/ת מחסן"`/`"קניין/ית"` for Warehouse Manager/Buyer, `"צוות"`/`"לקוח/ה"` for Staff/Customer). Each template's `specEn({...})` call keeps its original English roles unchanged.

**Tests**: added `every template's Hebrew spec.roles are genuinely Hebrew, not reused English strings from specEn` to `templates.test.ts`, iterating every template and asserting (a) `spec.roles` and `specEn.roles` have the same length, (b) every string in `spec.roles` passes `domainEntities.ts`'s own `isHebrewText`, and (c) `spec.roles` is not deep-equal to `specEn.roles` -- generalized across all 6 templates so any future template added without a Hebrew `roles` translation is caught immediately.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `templates.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `templates.test.ts` in place). ### Round 518: Product's bare "מלאי" keyword spuriously matched "חשמלאי" (electrician) and "מלאים" (full)

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 517, found that `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s `Product` entity rule includes the bare Hebrew keyword `"מלאי"` ("inventory/stock"), matched via plain substring `.includes()` (not a `\b`-bounded RegExp, since JS's `\b` only recognizes ASCII word characters and can't bound Hebrew letters). `"מלאי"` is a literal substring of two unrelated, ordinary Hebrew words: `WorkOrder`'s own keyword `"חשמלאי"`/`"חשמלאים"` ("electrician(s)", line ~1041) and the common adjective `"מלאים"` ("full", plural) -- the exact same pitfall-1 substring-collision class this file's header documents and which past rounds already fixed for "order"/"disorder", "stock"/"livestock", "product"/"production", "reservation"/"preservation" (round 501), and "מנה"/"מנהלים" (round 488), but this specific pair had never been caught.

**Independent verification**: reproduced the collision directly by calling the real `matchEntities` function (not just static inspection): `matchEntities("אפליקציה לניהול קריאות שירות לחשמלאים עם לקוחות וטכנאים", true)` returned `['Customer', 'Service', 'Product', 'WorkOrder']` -- removing just "לחשמלאים" from the same description dropped `Product` entirely, isolating the cause to the "מלאי" substring. Went a layer further than the initial finding and discovered the bug was broader than one collision: `matchEntities("אפליקציה למעקב אחרי ארונות מלאים במחסן", true)` (an app for tracking "full cabinets in a warehouse") also spuriously matched `Product`, since "מלאים" (full, plural) likewise contains "מלאי" as its first four letters -- a far more common, everyday Hebrew word than "חשמלאי" alone would have suggested. Confirmed via `grep -rn "חשמלאי\|מלאי" packages/spec-engine/src/*.test.ts` that no existing test covered either collision. Confirmed this file's own established fix for an analogous unfixable-by-removal Hebrew collision ("מנה" vs "מנהלים", round 488) was to drop the bare keyword entirely because a non-colliding plural ("מנות") still covered the real term -- but verified via direct repro that dropping "מלאי" here would break real detection too: `matchEntities("אפליקציה לניהול מלאי בחנות", true)` (a plain "inventory management" app, with none of the other Product keywords "מוצר"/"מוצרים"/"inventory"/"stock" present) returned `['Product']` using "מלאי" alone, so simple removal was not a safe option this time.

**The fix**: replaced the bare `"מלאי"` string keyword with the RegExp `/(?<!חש)מלאי(?!ם)/` -- a lookbehind excluding the `"חש"` prefix (ruling out `"חשמלאי"`/`"חשמלאים"`) and a lookahead excluding the `"ם"` plural suffix (ruling out `"מלאים"`), while `"מלאי"` still matches as its own word in every other context, including with a leading definite article/preposition (`"המלאי"`, `"במלאי"`) or no affix at all (`"ניהול מלאי"`). Verified the regex against seven cases (the two collisions, the plain term, and four legitimate variants) before wiring it in.

**Tests**: added `Product's 'מלאי' keyword doesn't spuriously match 'חשמלאי' (electrician) or 'מלאים' (full)` to `heuristic.test.ts`, following this file's own established convention (round 501's `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()`-based test) -- asserting both an electrician-service description and a "full cabinets" description produce no `Product` entity, while a plain inventory-management description (with none of Product's other keywords) still does.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts` in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure: `'חשמלאים' (electricians) alone must not spuriously match Product via a bare 'מלאי' substring`. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Confirmed no `codegen.ts` duplicate exists to check (`matchEntities`/`DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` belong purely to server-side spec generation in `spec-engine`, never duplicated into the exported-app codegen templates). Full suite + root build clean: `@forge/shared` 16 (unchanged), `@forge/db` 141 (unchanged), `@forge/spec-engine` 115 (+1), `@forge/api` 457 (unchanged), `@forge/web` 866 (unchanged), `npm run build` clean.

**Topic status**: this gap is closed. The `domainEntities.ts` keyword-collision bug class (rounds 449-460, 501, now also 518) remains legitimately open for future genuinely-new entity/keyword pairs -- this specific pair ("מלאי"/"חשמלאי"/"מלאים") is closed. ### Round 519: GlobalSearch's Retry button kept a stale "Show all" expansion instead of the retry's own fresh data

**The candidate**: a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every closed family through round 518, found that `apps/web/src/GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s error-banner Retry button called `runSearch(highlightQuery)` directly, while `handleSubmit` and `handleRecentSearchClick` -- the component's only other two paths that re-run a search -- both call `setExpandedSamples({})` immediately beforehand. The render logic (`const displayed = expandedSamples[result.entityName] ?? result.sample`) unconditionally prefers a cached `expandedSamples` entry over the freshly-fetched `result.sample`, so Retry alone left any prior "Show all" expansion in place even after fetching genuinely new data.

**Independent verification**: read all three call sites directly in `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` (lines 169, 176, 367) and confirmed the asymmetry exactly as reported -- the two reset calls and the one that skips it. Confirmed the concrete failure sequence: a partial-failure search (one entity fails, triggering the error+Retry row while the other entity's results still show) -> the user clicks "Show all" on the successful entity's group, populating `expandedSamples` with its full match list as of that moment -> real data changes (a record edited/deleted by a collaborator, a WhatsApp-matched write, etc., entirely plausible while the panel stays open) -> the user clicks Retry, hoping the previously-failing entity now succeeds -> `runSearch` re-fetches everyone and computes a correct, fresh `result.sample`, but the render still shows the untouched, stale `expandedSamples` entry instead -- including, potentially, a "jump to record" button pointing at a now-deleted record id. Confirmed via `grep` that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own duplicate `GlobalSearch` component has the identical pattern at its own Retry button (`onClick={() => runSearch(query)}`, with the same two reset call sites earlier in the file) -- a second, independent instance of the same port-gap, not just a live-preview-only bug. Confirmed this is a distinct mechanism from every closed staleness item (all of which live in `EntityPanel.tsx`/`codegen.ts`'s own visible-staleness family or per-field revalidation-effect-deps family) and from the two other closed `GlobalSearchPanel`-specific bugs (489's dialog-guard, 494's Escape-clears-query) -- this one is the Retry button's own reset omission, never covered by either.

**The fix**: added `setExpandedSamples({})` to the Retry button's `onClick` handler in both files, matching the convention `handleSubmit`/`handleRecentSearchClick` (live preview) and their own identically-named equivalents (exported app) already use.

**Tests**: added `GlobalSearchPanel's Retry button clears a stale 'Show all' expansion instead of keeping outdated samples` to `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts`, and the equivalent `the exported GlobalSearch's Retry button clears a stale 'Show all' expansion...` to `codegen.test.ts` (via the real generated `GlobalSearch.jsx`, not a reimplementation). Both drive the full real sequence through real DOM events: a partial-failure search (one entity returns 7 matches, the other fails), click "Show all" to expand to all 7, click Retry (now both entities succeed, with the first entity's data changed to 2 different records), and assert the displayed results show the fresh 2-record data, not the stale 7-record expansion.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed implementation files, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping both new tests in place). Confirmed the exact predicted failure in both: the live-preview test timed out waiting for the hit-button count to reach 2 (stuck at the stale 7), and the exported-app test failed with `7 !== 2` directly. Restored both from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. One parallel background run (web's suite + api's suite running simultaneously) hung web's run entirely rather than producing a single flake -- an earlier fully sequential `npm test` run had already passed cleanly end-to-end, and an isolated re-run of web's suite alone confirmed no regression, consistent with this session's established "parallel background runs can cause contention" pattern (rounds 478, 485, 486, 490, 509, 513), just manifesting as a hang here instead of one failing test. Full suite + root build clean: `@forge/shared` 16 (unchanged), `@forge/db` 141 (unchanged), `@forge/spec-engine` 115 (unchanged), `@forge/api` 458 (+1), `@forge/web` 867 (+1), `npm run build` clean.

(2) the agent proposed that `backup.ts`'s `sanitizeZipEntryName` (line 46, replacing only `` /[\\/:*?"<>|\u0000-\u001f]/g `` with `"_"`) could let two differently-named entities collide into the same ZIP path unguarded. Independently re-derived the proof: `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` (line 78) replaces `` /[^A-Za-z0-9]/g `` -- every non-alphanumeric character, not just the narrow path-unsafe set -- then lowercases, before `ProductSpecSchema`'s own `.refine()` (line 212) rejects the spec outright on any collision. Since the narrow ZIP-sanitizer's replaced-character set is a strict subset of the broad schema-validator's replaced-character set, any two names that collide under the narrow sanitizer differ only at character positions where both characters already fall in the narrow set -- and since that set is contained in the broad set, those exact positions collapse to `"_"` under the broad sanitizer too, while every other (matching) position stays trivially equal regardless of case-folding. So a narrow-sanitizer collision necessarily implies a broad-sanitizer collision, which means `ProductSpecSchema` already rejects the project at creation/refine time before any export/backup code can run. This is the identical conclusion round 499 already reached and logged as a proven false positive -- confirming the guard is still airtight, not a new finding. (3) `matchesSearch`'s lack of special-case boolean handling was considered and correctly dismissed: a boolean cell renders as a bare icon (checkmark/dash), never as localized searchable text, so there's no "visible text that can't be matched" gap the way there was for number/date fields.

### Out-of-band (during round 522): login autofill fix + optional email-code 2FA step, requested directly by שלומי

שלומי messaged directly in chat (not through the hourly Routine): "בכניסה הוא לא זוכר את שם המשתמש והסיסמה תעשה סיסמה עם קוד למייל או לנייד" ("on login it doesn't remember the username/password; make a password with a code to email or phone"). Dropped the in-progress round 522 autonomous survey immediately per the standing absolute-priority rule.

**Investigated the first half directly**: `AuthScreen.tsx`'s email `<input>` had neither a `name` nor an `autoComplete` attribute at all, and `PasswordInput.tsx`'s own `<input>` toggles its `type` between `"password"` and `"text"` for the show/hide eye icon -- both are exactly the signals a browser's password manager uses to decide whether to offer to remember a login form. Fixed by adding `name="email"`/`autoComplete="username"` to the email field and a `name` prop (plumbed through to the underlying `<input>`) to `PasswordInput`, with `autoComplete="new-password"`/`"current-password"` set per mode as before.

**Clarified the second half with her directly** (AskUserQuestion, since it genuinely needed her decision, not a guess): she wants a code emailed on every login, added on top of the password (not replacing it) -- two follow-up questions settled "email, not SMS" and "2FA, not passwordless."

**Built**: `apps/api/src/email.ts`, a minimal `ResendEmailSender` (resend.com) built on plain `fetch`, matching this codebase's own `anthropicFetch.ts` precedent rather than adding a dependency. `.configured` is `false` whenever `RESEND_API_KEY` isn't set in the environment -- `routes/auth.ts`'s login route checks this and returns a token immediately exactly as it always has when it's false, so **this step is fully opt-in and cannot lock anyone out of a deployment that hasn't set up an email provider.** Once configured, a correct password instead deletes any other pending code for that account (`packages/db/src/loginCodes.ts`'s `deleteLoginCodesForUser` -- at most one pending code per account at a time), generates a secure random 6-digit code (`crypto.randomInt`), stores only its SHA-256 hash (never the plaintext) with a 10-minute TTL and an attempt counter, emails it, and returns `{ requiresCode: true, loginCodeId }` instead of a token. A new `POST /auth/login/verify-code` route checks the code (`timingSafeEqual`, locking out after 5 wrong attempts or on expiry) and only then issues the real session. `AuthScreen.tsx` gained a code-entry step shown whenever `requiresCode` comes back, with a "back" button to abandon and retry, and `api.ts`'s `login()` now threads the client's own current UI language through so the email itself is in Hebrew or English to match.

**Tests**: `loginCodes.test.ts` (7, DB-layer CRUD/TTL/per-user scoping), `email.test.ts` (5, `ResendEmailSender` against a fake `fetchImpl`), 5 new end-to-end tests in `app.test.ts` via a fake, inspectable `EmailSender` double injected through `createApp`'s new optional 5th parameter (full code flow including reuse-after-verify rejection, wrong-code lockout after 5 attempts, a fresh code invalidating the previous one, and `EMAIL_SEND_FAILED` when the sender itself throws), and 3 new tests in `AuthScreen.test.ts` (the autocomplete/name attributes in both modes, the full requiresCode-to-authenticated flow through real DOM events, and the back button). New error codes (`INVALID_LOGIN_CODE`, `LOGIN_CODE_EXPIRED`, `EMAIL_SEND_FAILED`) got Hebrew/English translations in the same pass -- `language.test.ts`'s own completeness scanners (round 425) caught nothing missing.

### Round 523: a new methodology finds a real bug after three clean code-reading rounds

Round 522 itself flagged, before being interrupted by the out-of-band work above, that three consecutive clean rounds (520, 521, 522) from pure code-reading surveys suggested a genuinely different methodology was likely to be more productive: actually running the app, or fuzzing an input-parsing boundary with real malformed data. Round 523 took that recommendation and dispatched a survey agent instructed specifically to do one of those two things instead of another static read.

**The survey**: the agent chose to fuzz the real CSV-import parsing path end-to-end -- not reasoning about the code, but actually running `buildImportRecords`/`parseCsv` from `entityFormatting.ts`, tracing each parsed record through the real wire-serialization code (`api.ts`'s `createRecord`, which does `JSON.stringify`), into the real server-side `coerceValue`/`insertRecord` in `repository.ts`, against a real in-memory SQLite DB. Several edge-case CSV cells were tried (hex numbers, a leading `+`, whitespace-only cells, the literal string `"NaN"`, a thousands-separator value that shifts columns); only one produced a genuine bug.

**The bug**: a CSV cell containing `"Infinity"` or `"-Infinity"` in a number field. `Number("Infinity")` evaluates to `Infinity`, not `NaN`, so the number-coercion branch's `Number.isNaN(n)` check let it straight through as a "valid" parsed number. But `Infinity`/`-Infinity` aren't valid JSON values -- `JSON.stringify({ amount: Infinity })` silently produces `{"amount":null}` -- so by the time the import's HTTP request body is built, the value has already silently become `null`, with the import UI reporting "imported successfully, 0 errors" the entire time. For a `required` number field the story is worse in a different way: the client-side required-check only tests `raw === ""`, so `"Infinity"` passes it too, and the request only fails once the server's own `coerceValue` sees the post-JSON `null` and throws a confusing "field is required" error for a cell the user visibly did fill in.

**Independent verification**: re-read `entityFormatting.ts`'s `buildImportRecords` number branch directly (line 1182-1188 before the fix) and confirmed the exact reported code: `const n = Number(raw); if (Number.isNaN(n)) { ...error...; } record[field.name] = n;` -- no finiteness check anywhere. Independently re-ran `Number("Infinity")` (`Infinity`, `Number.isNaN` false) and `JSON.stringify({a: Infinity, b: -Infinity})` (`{"a":null,"b":null}`) to confirm the claimed JS semantics directly, rather than trusting the agent's description. Also independently checked whether a raw `"Infinity"` string could reach `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` through some path other than CSV import (e.g. a direct API call bypassing the browser's `JSON.stringify`-before-send step) -- confirmed `coerceValue`'s own number branch (line 47-54) has the identical gap, and that Node's built-in `node:sqlite` driver actually accepts and stores a literal `Infinity` without error (verified directly), making this a real, separate path worth closing too, not just a redundant belt-and-suspenders check.

**codegen.ts duplicate check**: grepped `codegen.ts` for the same logic and confirmed it has an exact templated duplicate of both affected functions -- `buildImportRecords` (the CSV-import branch, line ~1853-1859) and the server-side `coerce()` function (line ~379-383) -- so every exported/standalone app generated by this platform carries the identical bug in both its client bundle and its generated server.

**The fix**: changed `Number.isNaN(n)` to `!Number.isFinite(n)` in all four locations -- `entityFormatting.ts`'s `buildImportRecords`, `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue`, and codegen.ts's templated duplicates of both. `Number.isFinite` rejects `NaN`, `Infinity`, and `-Infinity` in one check, so no behavior changed for any value that was already being correctly accepted or rejected.

**The tests**: a new `buildImportRecords` test in `entityFormatting.test.ts` (CSV rows with `"Infinity"`/`"-Infinity"` cells, confirmed rejected with row-numbered errors, the valid row still imported); a new `insertRecord` test in `repository.test.ts` (both literal strings rejected with `ValidationError`); and two new tests in `codegen.test.ts` following this file's own established regex-extraction convention for catching codegen.ts drift -- one extracts and executes the real generated `buildImportRecords` function from `generateExportFiles` output (not a reimplementation), and one spawns a real generated `server.js` and POSTs both bad values to a live HTTP endpoint, confirming a 400 response.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the three implementation files, reverted them via `git checkout --` (keeping the four new tests in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failures -- the `entityFormatting.test.ts` and extracted-function `codegen.test.ts` tests both failed with the literal `Infinity`/`-Infinity` values present in the "imported" records instead of being rejected; the `repository.test.ts` test failed with "Missing expected exception"; the spawned-server `codegen.test.ts` test is covered by the same code path as the extraction test and was confirmed failing alongside it. Restored all three files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran all four new tests against the restored code -- all passed. Full monorepo `npm test` (871 tests in `@forge/web`, up from 870; db and api counts up by 1 and 2 respectively) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `30c9765`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This is the first round since 519 to produce a real fix, and it came from the methodology change round 522 recommended, not from another code read -- worth keeping in mind for future rounds once code-reading surveys run dry again.

Two leads were investigated and ruled out; no new qualifying bug was found.

**Independent verification**: (1) the agent proposed that Appointment's bare `"booking"` keyword (a plain substring match via `matchesKeyword`'s `lower.includes(kw)`, confirmed by reading `heuristic.ts` lines 66-68 directly) could spuriously match "overbooking" the same way round 501's bare `"reservation"` spuriously matched "preservation" -- but ruled it out as not actually wrong, since every real phrase containing "...booking" (overbooking, double booking) is genuinely *about* bookings/reservations, unlike "preservation" which has zero semantic connection to "reservation". Independently confirmed this distinction holds: re-read `domainEntities.ts`'s own doc comment for this entity (line 120, "Bare 'reservation' ... is a substring of the **unrelated**, common word 'preservation'") and the existing `heuristic.test.ts` test (line 341-345) that deliberately includes "double bookings" in a sentence and asserts only that it doesn't spuriously match a *different* entity (Event) -- the author clearly already considered "booking" matching fine, and the semantic-relatedness argument (overbooking is literally about too many bookings, not an unrelated homograph) holds up under the same test the already-fixed cases (coworker/livestock/preservation/enlisting/disorder/projector/worshipping) all fail. (2) the agent proposed a lost-update race between two concurrent "add entity"/"add role" requests both reading a stale `project.spec` -- ruled out because node:sqlite's `DatabaseSync` is fully synchronous and neither route's handler contains a genuine async I/O boundary (no `fetch`, no `scrypt`) between reading and writing the spec, so Node's single-threaded event loop can't interleave another request's code mid-handler. This is a legitimate clean-survey round from the default code-reading methodology, in the same spirit as rounds 463, 466, 482, 504, 511, 520, and 521 -- a thorough sweep that correctly declined to force a fix onto leads that, on closer inspection, were either semantically sound matches or provably race-free. The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-523 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 525: REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS was sized for one Anthropic call per request, but /refine makes two

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, denylisted against every closed family through round 524, swept areas not recently covered: `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s fetch wrapper, `App.tsx`'s non-EntityPanel logic, `i18n`/`theme` contexts, `useDialogFocusTrap.ts`, `wakeRetry.ts`'s retry-wrapper logic itself, `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s checkpoint endpoints, `pipeline.ts`'s QA/security-scan logic, and `packages/db/src/checkpoints.ts`'s ledger. It found one genuine bug: `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (then 220s) and its own dedicated regression test both hard-code the real worst-case legitimate request as "101s of cold-start retry budget + one 60s Anthropic call" -- true for `/build`, but not for `/refine`, whose handler can make *two* sequential 60s Anthropic calls under the exact same client-side timeout.

**Independent verification, traced hop by hop rather than trusted**: (1) confirmed `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s own comment (lines 76-109, before this fix) explicitly states "101 + 60 = 161s is the real worst-case legitimate total" -- a one-call formula. (2) Read `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `/refine` handler (lines 797-826) directly: `await generateSpec(combinedDescription, provider)` (line 815) runs and is awaited *before* `streamPipeline()` is even called (line 816), and `streamPipeline` (lines 307-322) is the only place that calls `res.writeHead()` (line 313) -- so the entire `generateSpec` call, including its own internal 429/529 retry sleeps, elapses with zero response bytes sent, indistinguishable from a stalled connection from the client's point of view. (3) Confirmed `generateSpec` has no `timeoutMs` override anywhere in this call chain, so it inherits `packages/spec-engine/src/anthropicFetch.ts`'s `ANTHROPIC_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` default (line 12, confirmed as a default *parameter*, which JS/TS applies even when a caller explicitly passes `undefined`, not just when the argument is omitted). (4) Read `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts` (lines 306-352, the Debug-agent recovery flow): if `diffAndMigrate` throws on the regenerated spec, `requestSpecFix(nextSpec, dbError, { apiKey, model: ... })` (line 327) runs *mid-stream* (after headers are already sent) -- and this call also has no `timeoutMs` override, so it inherits the same 60s default via the same `fetchAnthropic` code path (confirmed in `packages/spec-engine/src/debug.ts` lines 55-79). (5) Confirmed both calls are gated by the *same* single `AbortController` created once in `api.ts`'s `fetchApi()` (lines 122-135): since `/refine` is one continuous SSE response from the client's perspective, the same 220s deadline covers the pre-stream `generateSpec` call, the in-stream `requestSpecFix` call, cold-start retrying, and everything else, with no reset in between. (6) Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicate of any of this logic (grepped for `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`/`wakeRetry`/`DEFAULT_DELAYS_MS`: no matches) -- the exported standalone app has no AI-powered refine feature at all, so no second fix site was needed.

**The real-world effect**: `101s (cold start) + 60s (generateSpec) + 60s (requestSpecFix) = 221s` already exceeded the 220s ceiling with zero margin left for the rest of the pipeline (migration, seeding, QA, security scan, DB writes) that the same budget was also meant to cover. A user hitting this exact combination -- a cold start plus a refine whose regenerated spec collides with the existing schema in a way the Debug agent is specifically built to auto-fix -- would see the translated "this is taking unusually long" (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT`) error even though the server was never stalled, likely still completing the refine (consuming a second real, billed Anthropic call) with no success feedback, risking a confused retry and a duplicate refine/checkpoint. This sits in the same code family round 163's incident and the wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency design (round 482) already flag as sensitive, so every hop above was traced and confirmed directly in the source rather than accepted from the survey agent's report.

**The fix**: bumped `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` from `220_000` to `280_000` (101s cold-start + 2×60s Anthropic calls = 221s, plus the same ~59s margin the constant's own history already establishes), and rewrote its doc comment to document both calls explicitly instead of re-deriving a one-call formula a third time.

**The tests**: updated the existing `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` regression test in `apps/web/src/api.test.ts` to multiply `anthropicCallBudgetMs` by 2 instead of hard-coding a single-call formula. While verifying the fix, also caught and fixed a second, closely related latent bug the change exposed: a *different* existing test ("fetchApi aborts a request that hangs past its timeout...") hard-coded `t.mock.timers.tick(220_000)` instead of referencing `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` -- bumping the constant alone would have made that tick no longer reach the new, larger timer, leaving the test's own pending promise hanging forever (surfacing as `cancelledByParent` test-runner failures, not a clean assertion failure) instead of the test continuing to actually verify anything. Fixed by ticking `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` itself.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `api.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the updated tests in place), confirmed the exact predicted failure (`220000ms` not exceeding the real `221000ms` worst case). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Hit one self-inflicted snag along the way: the first comment draft used the literal sequence `**/refine` inside a `/** ... */` JSDoc block, which TypeScript/esbuild parses as the comment's own closing `*/` followed by stray tokens -- caught immediately via a `TransformError`, not silently; fixed by rewording to avoid `**/` appearing inside a block comment. Full monorepo `npm test` (871/871, unchanged count since this only edited existing tests) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `70e418b`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this widens an internal timeout budget only; legitimate requests that previously could have been falsely aborted will now complete, and nothing that previously succeeded can now behave differently.

### Round 526: csvEscape's formula-injection guard and its own inverse only agreed on bytes, not on content

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, denylisted against every closed family through round 525, targeted the CSV import/export guard pair (`csvEscape`/`unescapeCsvGuard` in `entityFormatting.ts`) specifically because round 523's fuzzing methodology had already proven that boundary code family (CSV cell parsing) productive once, and the existing test coverage for this guard pair (round 376's fix, re-verified round 523) only exercised one direction of the ambiguity it was designed to resolve.

**The bug**: `csvEscape` prepends a guard `'` to a value starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab, or a CR, so spreadsheet apps don't execute it as a formula on open (CWE-1236); `unescapeCsvGuard` strips that `'` back off on import by checking whether the character right after a leading `'` is one of those same six. But a value that genuinely starts with a literal `'` immediately followed by one of those six characters -- e.g. `"'-interesting"` -- was left completely untouched by `csvEscape` (its own first character, `'`, isn't in the guarded set) and exports to the exact same bytes, `"'-interesting"`, as the guard applied to the unguarded value `"-interesting"`. `unescapeCsvGuard` cannot distinguish "csvEscape added this apostrophe" from "this apostrophe was always real data" from content alone, so it silently stripped the real leading apostrophe on every export-then-reimport round trip, or whenever such a value was typed directly into an importable CSV.

**Independent verification**: read `csvEscape` (lines 892-898, before the fix) and `unescapeCsvGuard` (lines 1089-1091) directly and confirmed they matched the agent's report exactly. Independently reproduced the corruption by running both functions live in Node outside the test suite: `csvEscape("'-interesting")` → `"'-interesting"` (byte-identical, confirming the guard never fires), then `unescapeCsvGuard("'-interesting")` → `"-interesting"` (the real apostrophe gone). Also independently grepped the whole repo for every other `csvEscape`/`unescapeCsvGuard`-shaped function rather than trusting the agent's line numbers for the codegen.ts duplicate: found a second, string-templated copy of this exact csvEscape/unescape pair inside `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the general entity CSV export/import feature baked into every standalone exported app, lines 1626 and 1830) -- read both directly and confirmed byte-for-byte the same vulnerable regex. Also found a *third*, unrelated `csvEscape` in `codegen.ts` (line 593, the one-way "Backup All Data" ZIP export) and a fourth in `apps/api/src/backup.ts` (the live-preview backup feature it mirrors) -- read both and confirmed neither has any unescape/import counterpart at all (backups are never re-imported through this guard), so neither one carries this bug and neither needed a fix.

**Why the fix isn't a narrow patch to just the one reported case**: the same ambiguity recurs one level up for a value with *two* genuine leading apostrophes followed by a guarded character (e.g. `"''-double"`), and so on for any number of real leading apostrophes -- any fix that only special-cases "exactly one real leading apostrophe" just pushes the same collision to "exactly two," unbounded. The only way to make the encoding fully invertible without an unbounded recursive rule is to make `csvEscape` add exactly one `'` whenever the value *already* starts with one, regardless of what follows it, and have `unescapeCsvGuard` mirror that by treating a leading `'` itself as "guarded" for the purposes of deciding whether to strip. That keeps the leading-apostrophe *count* unambiguous (always originalCount, or originalCount+1 if guarded) no matter how many real apostrophes a value starts with -- confirmed by hand-deriving and then live-testing the round trip for 0, 1, 2, and 3 genuine leading apostrophes, each both with and without a guarded character immediately after, all 8 combinations round-tripping exactly.

**The trade-off accepted**: a value that already starts with a literal `'` followed by an *ordinary* character (e.g. `"'Ohana"`, already covered by an existing round-376 test) now also gets doubled to `"''Ohana"` on export, where it previously was left untouched. This still round-trips correctly through this app's own import (confirmed: the existing `'Ohana` test needed no changes and still passes), but a CSV containing it would show one extra, visible apostrophe (`'Ohana` instead of `Ohana`) if opened directly in a third-party spreadsheet app without ever being reimported here -- a narrow, cosmetic cost for a case (data that is itself apostrophe-prefixed) already rare enough that it isn't covered by any existing bug report, traded for eliminating a genuine, previously-silent data-loss bug.

**The fix**: added `'` itself to the guarded-character regex in both `csvEscape` and `unescapeCsvGuard`, in both `entityFormatting.ts` and codegen.ts's templated duplicate (NOT in the two unrelated one-way `csvEscape` functions, which don't need it).

**The tests**: two new round-trip tests in `entityFormatting.test.ts` (a record with three fields each starting with `'` + a different guarded character, and a separate record with two genuine leading apostrophes) and a matching new test in `codegen.test.ts` following this file's own established "extract and execute the real generated functions" convention (not a reimplementation) for the same three-field case. Also had to update one pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` assertion that checked for the guard regex's literal source text appearing in the generated output -- intentionally updated to the new, wider regex rather than left stale.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both implementation files (`entityFormatting.ts`, `codegen.ts`), reverted them via `git checkout --` (keeping every new/updated test in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failures: both new round-trip tests failed with the leading apostrophes missing from the re-imported records (confirmed via the exact diff: `"'-interesting"` → `"-interesting"`, etc.), and the updated codegen.ts regex-literal assertion failed to match the old, narrower regex text. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran all four new/updated tests against the restored code -- all passed, including the pre-existing `'Ohana` test (unchanged, still green under the wider guard). Full monorepo `npm test` (873/873, up from round 525's 871) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `9fbb214`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects data containing a literal leading apostrophe going through CSV export/import, which now round-trips correctly instead of silently losing that apostrophe.

### Round 527: Hebrew "חיוב" (charge) silently collided with "חיובי" (positive)

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, denylisted against every closed family through round 526 (including round 526's own csvEscape/unescapeCsvGuard fix), was steered toward areas not recently surveyed (migrate.ts beyond the collision guard, seed.ts, twin.ts, idempotency.ts, BusinessTwinPanel/HistoryPanel/ChangePasswordPanel, auth.ts, users.ts, FieldLabelEditor, whatsapp.ts/whatsappWeb.ts non-race angles, i18n completeness, Templates Gallery content). It found one genuine bug: the bare Hebrew string `"חיוב"` ("charge"), used both in `heuristic.ts`'s `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` and in `domainEntities.ts`'s Invoice entity keyword list, is a substring of the ordinary, unrelated adjective/noun `"חיובי"`/`"חיובית"`/`"חיוביות"` ("positive"/"positivity") -- natural phrasing for any feedback/review/survey app ("משוב חיובי", "ביקורת חיובית"), with nothing to do with billing.

**Independent verification**: read `heuristic.ts` lines 15-26 (`PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`) and `domainEntities.ts` line 179 (the Invoice entry) directly and confirmed the exact reported bare-string entries. Read `matchesKeyword` (heuristic.ts line 66-68): a plain `string` entry matches via `.includes()`, with no word-boundary check at all. Independently reproduced the collision outside the test suite by inlining the real `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` array and `matchesKeyword` logic and running it against a plain Hebrew sentence describing a customer-satisfaction-survey app ("...איסוף משוב חיובי מלקוחות...") -- `mentionsPayments` came back `true` purely from the "חיוב" substring inside "חיובי", with no mention of money anywhere in the text. Grepped `docs/roadmap.md` and every `*.test.ts` file for "חיוב" -- zero hits in either, confirming this exact pair was never found or fixed by any of the many previous keyword-collision rounds (449-460, 501, 518), which are all about *other* entity/keyword pairs.

**Why this is the same bug class, not a reopening**: `heuristic.ts`'s own code comment (lines 17-23) already documents the identical collision class for `"stripe"`/`"striped"`/`"pinstripe"` (round 460, fixed with `/\bstripe\b/`), and round 518 independently hit the same problem for `"מלאי"`/`"חשמלאי"`/`"מלאים"`, fixed with a lookbehind/lookahead regex (`/(?<!חש)מלאי(?!ם)/`) since JS's `\b` doesn't bound Hebrew letters (they aren't `\w`). The Hebrew payment keywords were simply never audited the same way the English ones and the `מלאי` case were -- this is a legitimately new entity/keyword instance of an already-recognized pattern, not a reopening of a closed mechanism.

**The fix**: replaced the bare `"חיוב"` string with `/חיוב(?!י(?!ם))/` in both `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` and the Invoice entity's keyword list. This excludes "חיוב" whenever immediately followed by "י" *unless* that "י" is itself followed by "ם" -- which correctly keeps matching the real plural "חיובים" ("charges", e.g. "חיוב חודשי", "חיובים פתוחים") while rejecting all three "positive" derivations ("חיובי", "חיובית", "חיוביות"). Hand-verified all 8 relevant combinations (0 vs. real suffix, "positive" vs. "charges" plural) live in Node before applying. No `codegen.ts` duplicate exists for this logic -- `matchEntities`/`PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`/`DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` only run at spec-generation time inside `packages/spec-engine`, before `codegen.ts`'s template ever runs; confirmed via grep (no matches for "חיוב"/`PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`/`matchEntities`/`DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` in `codegen.ts`).

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, mirroring the existing `stripe`/`מלאי` regression tests' structure exactly -- confirms a positive-feedback description and a positive-reviews description no longer get a spurious Invoice entity or the "which payment provider" question, while the bare word and its real plural "חיובים" still correctly match Invoice and still correctly surface the payment-provider question.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both implementation files (`heuristic.ts`, `domainEntities.ts`), reverted them via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failure (49/50 pass, the new test failing on "'חיובי' (positive) alone must not spuriously match Invoice"). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran the new test against the restored code -- all 50 passed. Full monorepo `npm test` (spec-engine 116/116, up from 115 by exactly the one new test; every other workspace unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `ba38db8`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects which entities a Hebrew app description heuristically matches when describing a feedback/review/survey app; a description that genuinely needs billing still gets Invoice and the payment-provider question exactly as before.

### Round 528: withIdempotency scoped a key by endpoint *template*, never by the actual resource it mutated

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, denylisted against every closed family through round 527, was steered toward areas not recently surveyed (migrate.ts beyond the collision guard, seed.ts, twin.ts, idempotency.ts, BusinessTwinPanel/HistoryPanel/ChangePasswordPanel, auth.ts, users.ts, FieldLabelEditor, whatsapp.ts/whatsappWeb.ts non-race angles, i18n completeness, Templates Gallery content, collaborators.ts). It found one genuine bug, independent of round 495's own closed finding: `withIdempotency`'s mismatch guard (`apps/api/src/idempotency.ts`) compares `existing.userId`/`existing.route` against the current request, but every real per-resource call site in `routes/projects.ts` (clone, answers, roles, assumptions, entities, fields) passed the bare Express route *template* as `route` (e.g. `"POST /projects/:id/roles"`), never the actual project or entity id. Two requests for the same endpoint type against *two different projects*, by the *same user*, with a reused idempotency key, were therefore indistinguishable to the guard: `userId` and `route` both matched, so no `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH` fired. If the first request had already completed, the second project's own mutation never ran at all, and its caller silently got back the first project's cached response instead of an error.

**Independent verification**: read `idempotency.ts` lines 48-60 directly and confirmed the mismatch guard's exact logic. Grepped every `withIdempotency(` call site in `routes/projects.ts` (lines 387, 456, 575, 751, 1289, 1312, 1516, 1567) and read each one directly -- confirmed none of the six per-resource call sites (clone/answers/roles/assumptions/entities/fields) interpolates `req.params.id` or `req.params.entityName` into its route string; the two resource-*creation* call sites (`POST /projects`, `POST /projects/from-template`) correctly have nothing to scope by, since the resource doesn't exist until the call succeeds. Read `packages/db/src/idempotency.ts`'s table schema directly -- confirmed it has no resource/project-id column at all, so the mismatch check could never discriminate by resource even in principle, only by (`userId`, route-*template*). Read round 495's own regression test (`idempotency.test.ts` lines 116-148) directly and confirmed it calls `withIdempotency` with fabricated, non-literal route strings (`"POST /projects/A/roles"`, `"POST /projects/B/roles"`) that no real call site ever produces -- the test exercises the mismatch guard's logic correctly in isolation, but gives false confidence that cross-project reuse specifically is covered, when every real caller always passes the identical bare template regardless of which project is being mutated. Confirmed the bug live by calling the real `withIdempotency` against a real `:memory:` SQLite DB with the exact literal route string the real route handler passes -- a second call "for project B" with project A's key returned project A's cached response verbatim, and project B's own mutation never ran. Grepped `codegen.ts` for "Idempotency" -- no duplicate exists; the exported standalone app has no idempotency mechanism at all (already established by round 495).

**Reachability**: not reachable through today's real client -- `apps/web/src/api.ts` generates a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` inline on every single call site (`addRole`, `addAssumption`, `addEntity`, `addField`, `cloneProject`, `answerQuestions`, etc., all verified directly), so no designed client flow ever reuses a key across two projects. This is the same reachability caveat round 495's own finding already accepted for itself: the `X-Idempotency-Key` header is entirely client-supplied with no other validation, so this remains a genuine server-side defense-in-depth gap in a mechanism whose own doc comment already names "route or project" as what it's supposed to scope by, rather than something actively exploitable by today's UI.

**The fix**: interpolated the real project id (and entity name, for the fields route) into the `route` string template literal at each of the six per-resource call sites in `routes/projects.ts`, so `existing.route` and the current request's `route` can only match when they're genuinely the same resource. No change to `withIdempotency`'s own mismatch-guard logic was needed -- it already compared `route` correctly; the bug was entirely in what every caller handed it. Updated `idempotency.ts`'s own doc comment to state explicitly that `route` must be the resource instance, not just the template.

**The tests**: one new end-to-end test in `app.test.ts`, following this file's own established `withServer`/real-`fetch` integration-test convention for every other `withIdempotency` round (471-474) -- creates two real projects for the same user, reuses one idempotency key across a "add role" call to each, and confirms the second call is now rejected with `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH` (not a silent `200` replaying project A's data), that project B's spec is completely untouched afterward, and that a *fresh* key for project B still appends its own role normally.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both implementation files (`idempotency.ts`, `routes/projects.ts`), reverted them via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failure: the new test failed with `200 !== 409` (project B's reused-key request silently succeeded with project A's stale response, exactly the bug under investigation). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran the new test and the full `app.test.ts`/`idempotency.test.ts` suites against the restored code -- all passed (161/161 and 7/7 respectively). Full monorepo `npm test` (api 472/472, up from 471 by exactly the one new test; every other workspace unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `8f8ea20`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only hardens a server-side defense-in-depth mechanism that today's own client never actually triggers; no currently reachable behavior changes.

### Round 529: clean survey — two leads investigated and explicitly ruled out

A fresh Explore agent dispatch, denylisted against every closed family through round 528, swept areas not recently surveyed in depth: `pipeline.ts`'s `runQaChecks`/`runSecurityScan`/`computeImpact`, `migrate.ts` outside the collision guard, `seed.ts`, `repository.ts`, `users.ts`, `collaborators.ts`, `routes/auth.ts` in full, `zip.ts`, `displayField.ts`, `whatsapp.ts`/`whatsappWeb.ts`, `twin.ts`, `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx`, `CollaboratorsPanel.tsx`, `ChangePasswordPanel.tsx`, `ShortcutsPanel.tsx`, `useDialogFocusTrap.ts`, `checkpointDiff.ts`, `deleteAccountSummary.ts`, all 5 copy-pasted label/description editors, `templates.ts`'s spec/specEn parity, and a full i18n completeness scan (all 546 Hebrew/English key pairs cross-checked for presence parity and `{placeholder}` parity, including every real `t(key, {...})` call site in `apps/web/src`). It found two leads and ruled out both.

**Lead 1 (disproved by live repro)**: a hypothesis that `runQaChecks`'s per-required-field smoke test could spuriously throw a raw `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` instead of the expected `ValidationError`, if a required relation field's seeded guess (`seedValueFor`'s row-id-1 guess) were stale against a target entity whose first row was since deleted -- round 416 had explicitly flagged this exact seeded-guess staleness as a byproduct of its own analysis, but only fixed the Seed Data step, never `runQaChecks` itself. Built a live repro against a real `:memory:` SQLite DB with a stale relation guess and ran `runQaChecks` directly: no false failure. Independently confirmed the mechanism: `insertRecord` (`repository.ts` line 102) runs `coerceValue` across every field via `.map()` before the SQL `INSERT` (line 109) ever executes, so the required-field-missing check for whichever field the test loop actually deletes always throws first, regardless of field order -- the stale relation guess, present but merely stale (not missing), is never the thing that fails, and the real `INSERT`/FK check is never reached at all in this per-field-deletion methodology. Confirmed dead end, not a bug.

**Lead 2 (real but too weak to report)**: `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `fieldSignature()` builds an enum field's signature from `enumValues.slice().sort().join(",")`, so two different enum value sets whose members contain literal commas can collide (e.g. `["a,b","c"]` and `["a","b,c"]` both join to `"a,b,c"`) -- confirmed live, and confirmed `packages/shared`'s `FieldSchema` places no comma restriction on `enumValues` (`z.array(z.string())`), so this isn't strictly impossible via a real AI-generated spec. Independently verified both facts directly. Judged too contrived to warrant a fix this round: it needs an enum value containing a literal comma (none of the ~18 built-in domain entities or templates ever produce one), it additionally needs two *different* value sets whose sorted-and-joined strings coincide exactly (not just "any comma present"), and the impact is purely cosmetic -- a missed/wrong note in the Time Machine diff panel, no data loss, no security impact. Consistent with this process's own standard for declining a technically-real-but-contrived lead rather than straining for a weak candidate.

**Topic status**: no new candidate implemented this round. This is a legitimate clean-survey round from the default code-reading methodology, in the same spirit as rounds 463, 466, 504, 511, 520, 521, 522, and 524 -- a thorough sweep that correctly declined to force a fix onto a lead that, on closer inspection, cannot actually be reached (lead 1) or is real but too narrow and purely cosmetic to justify (lead 2). The wakeRetry `/refine` idempotency candidate (design-complete since round 482) remains open and deliberately deferred. Everything else still open from rounds 378-528 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 530: WhatsAppPanel's startPolling applied a stale message fetch after a concurrent disconnect

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, denylisted against every closed family through round 529, was steered toward areas not recently surveyed in depth. It found one genuine bug in `apps/web/src/WhatsAppPanel.tsx`: `startPolling`'s own polling tick, on the branch where `getWhatsAppStatus` reports the connection just became `"connected"`, calls `stopPolling()`, then `await`s `listWhatsAppMessages(projectId)`, then unconditionally calls `setMessages`/`setHasMoreMessages`/`startConnectedPolling()` with that result -- with no protection at all against a concurrent `handleDisconnect()` running while that fetch was still in flight.

**Independent verification**: read `startPolling` (lines 298-332 before the fix) and `handleDisconnect` (lines 391-402) directly and confirmed the exact reported shape. Traced why a naive `if (cancelled) return;` guard -- the pattern `startPolling`'s own *stale-status* case already uses just above it, and the obvious first instinct for this bug -- would be wrong, not just insufficient: `stopPolling()` (called by this *same* tick, two lines above the `await`, as part of every normal "connecting"/"qr" → "connected" transition) sets `cancelInFlightPollRef.current = null`, which is the very closure holding this tick's own `cancelled` variable -- but `cancelInFlightPollRef.current` is never actually *invoked* there, so `cancelled` itself isn't set true by a normal transition. Re-checked this by hand-tracing both call paths (normal transition vs. `handleDisconnect`'s own `stopPolling()` call) before concluding a *different* mechanism was needed anyway: `cancelled` has no way to distinguish "this fetch is stale because the connection was torn down" from "this fetch is perfectly current," since nothing before the `await` records *why* `stopPolling` might run again. Confirmed via `grep -ic whatsapp apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (0 matches) that no `codegen.ts` duplicate of this component/logic exists -- the exported standalone app has no WhatsApp integration at all, consistent with every prior WhatsApp-related round.

**Why this is the same bug class as rounds 431/432, not a new mechanism**: this codebase already has an established, proven idiom for exactly this shape of problem -- a `messagesVersionRef` counter (`useRef(0)`), bumped only when something that genuinely mutates `messages` server-side is confirmed to have succeeded (`handleDeleteMessage`, `handleClearHistory`, and `startConnectedPolling`'s own message-refresh tick, which captures `versionBeforeFetch` before its `await` and only applies the result if the version is unchanged after). `startPolling`'s "becoming connected" branch was the one place in this file with the same shape of race that had never been given this guard, and `handleDisconnect` -- the thing that actually tears down a connection -- never bumped the version at all, because nothing before this round needed it to.

**The fix**: in `startPolling`'s tick, capture `versionBeforeFetch = messagesVersionRef.current` before the `listWhatsAppMessages` call, and only run `setMessages`/`setHasMoreMessages`/`startConnectedPolling()` if `messagesVersionRef.current === versionBeforeFetch` afterward. In `handleDisconnect`, bump `messagesVersionRef.current += 1` immediately after `disconnectWhatsApp` resolves successfully (before `setStatus`/`setMessages`/`setHasMoreMessages`), mirroring the exact point `handleDeleteMessage`/`handleClearHistory` bump it.

**The tests**: two new tests in `WhatsAppPanel.test.ts`, using this file's own established regex-extraction + fake-`setInterval` technique (the same one the existing `startPolling`-discards-a-stale-status test already uses). One confirms the normal, non-racing path still applies the fetched page and starts connected-polling (a sanity counterpart, since the whole point of a version-based guard is that it must never fire on the ordinary path). The other holds `listWhatsAppMessages` open with a controlled promise, waits for the tick to actually reach it, bumps `messagesVersionRef.current` to simulate a concurrent `handleDisconnect`, then releases the fetch -- and confirms `setMessages`/`setHasMoreMessages`/`startConnectedPolling` are never called. Writing these surfaced a real, independent gap in two *pre-existing* tests: both of the file's existing `handleDisconnect` regex-extraction tests call it via `new Function(...)` without `messagesVersionRef` in the parameter list, so the new `messagesVersionRef.current += 1` line threw a `ReferenceError` inside the extracted function -- silently swallowed by `handleDisconnect`'s own `catch` block, which made the successful-disconnect test fail with `setStatus` never having been called (not a crash, just a wrong, hard-to-read assertion failure). Fixed by adding `messagesVersionRef` to both tests' parameter/argument lists, and added an explicit assertion to the successful-disconnect test confirming the version is actually bumped.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping every new/updated test in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failures: the successful-disconnect test failed with `7 !== 8` (the version never bumped), and the new race test failed with `1 !== 0` (`setMessages` was called despite the concurrent disconnect) -- 32/34 passing, exactly the two bug-detecting assertions failing, nothing else. Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran the full `WhatsAppPanel.test.ts` file against the restored code -- all 34 passed. Full monorepo `npm test` (web 875/875, up from round 529's 873 by exactly the two new tests; every other workspace unchanged: shared 16, spec-engine 116, db 149, api 472) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `2c856e8`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the rare timing window where a user clicks "disconnect" at almost the exact moment the panel's own background poll detects a successful QR-code connection; the panel now never resurrects a stale, already-superseded message page in that window.
