### Round 545: committing an inline cell edit with Enter sent a silent second PATCH for the same value

**The methodology**: after four consecutive rounds (542-544) closing every known instance of the "async action handler missing busy-guard" bug class, a fresh general-purpose survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist of every closed topic, to find a genuinely new bug shape rather than a fifth instance of the same family.

**The finding**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s inline cell editor (round 206) has three small handlers around its `editingCell`/`cellDraft` state: `commitInlineEdit` (Enter), `cancelInlineEdit` (Escape), and `handleCellBlur` (clicking away). `cancelInlineEdit` already sets a `suppressCellBlurCommitRef` flag *before* clearing `editingCell`, specifically because round 206 itself documented a real, Playwright-verified browser quirk: removing the focused input from the DOM (which happens the instant `editingCell` becomes `null`) still fires a genuine native `blur` event afterward, dispatched against whatever `handleCellBlur` closure was attached just before removal -- a closure that still sees the *old*, non-null `editingCell`/`cellDraft` from before the clear. `commitInlineEdit` clears `editingCell` through the exact same mechanism but never set that same flag first, so the identical stale-closure blur fires after every successful Enter-commit too, invoking `handleCellBlur` → `commitInlineEdit()` a second time with the pre-commit snapshot, sending a second, redundant PATCH for the same field/value. The exported app's generated `codegen.ts` carries a byte-for-byte copy of the same three handlers with the identical gap. Real consequence: a second PATCH fires on every single Enter-commit, and if a concurrent edit to that same field (another collaborator, or a board/calendar drag) lands in the gap between the two requests, the phantom second PATCH silently reverts it back to the stale pre-commit value -- a lost-update clobber the user never asked for.

**Independent verification**: read `commitInlineEdit`, `cancelInlineEdit`, and `handleCellBlur` directly in `EntityPanel.tsx` (lines ~2198-2229) and confirmed `commitInlineEdit` has no `suppressCellBlurCommitRef` reference anywhere, while its sibling `cancelInlineEdit` sets it unconditionally before its own `setEditingCell(null)`. Confirmed the generated-JS duplicate in `codegen.ts` has the identical structure and gap. Confirmed via `git log -S` that the `suppressCellBlurCommitRef` mechanism and its underlying browser-quirk rationale are an established, previously-verified fact from round 206's own commit (not something to re-derive from scratch), ruling this out as a duplicate of any closed topic -- it is a new instance of an *existing, already-guarded-against* mechanism simply missing from one of its three call sites, not a new race-condition class and not the denylisted bulk-action busy-guard family (no user double-click is involved; the second fire is triggered by React's own unmount-driven native blur).

**The fix**: added `suppressCellBlurCommitRef.current = true;` as the first statement in `commitInlineEdit`, immediately before `setEditingCell(null)` -- mirroring `cancelInlineEdit`'s existing order exactly, so the stale post-commit blur finds the flag already set and skips re-committing. Ported the identical one-line fix into `codegen.ts`'s generated copy.

**The test**: one new regression test per file, modeled on this project's own busy-guard-era extraction idiom rather than relying on jsdom to simulate the real browser's blur-on-unmount quirk (which it does not reliably reproduce): extracts `commitInlineEdit`/`cancelInlineEdit`/`handleCellBlur` as a single source block, builds a `makeHandlers()` factory bound to a shared `state`/`suppressCellBlurCommitRef`, starts a real commit via the render's own `commitInlineEdit()` (as Enter's `onKeyDown` does), then invokes that *same* render's own `handleCellBlur()` -- the exact stale closure a real native blur would call -- and confirms it does not trigger a second `updateRecord` call.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `EntityPanel.tsx`/`codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping both new tests in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failure in both: the stale blur triggered a second `updateRecord` call with the identical value in each file, while every other pre-existing test in both files (including the adjacent Enter/Escape inline-edit tests) stayed green. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran both full test files clean (`EntityPanel.test.ts` 121/121, `codegen.test.ts` 177/177). Full monorepo `npm test` (web 881/881, up from round 544's 880 by exactly the one new test; api 480/480, up from 479 by exactly the one new test; shared 16, spec-engine 116, db 149 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `5bc17ce`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the narrow case of pressing Enter to commit an inline table-cell edit; it now always sends exactly one PATCH, in both the live preview and any app exported via "Export code."

### Round 546: an unrecognized boolean field value silently stored as `false` and reported success, instead of being rejected

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every recently-mined mechanism (busy-guard, suppressCellBlurCommitRef, visible-staleness, migrate.ts collision-guard, server-side write-after-await), to find a genuinely new bug shape in previously-unexamined territory.

**The finding**: `coerceValue` (`packages/db/src/repository.ts`) -- the actual persistence-layer validator every record write funnels through, since `routes/projects.ts` passes `req.body` straight into `insertRecord`/`updateRecord` with no schema validation above it -- had no rejection path at all for its `boolean` branch, unlike every other branch in the same function: `number`/`relation`, `enum`, and `date` each explicitly throw a `ValidationError` for input they can't parse. A boolean field value outside the exact `true`/`"true"`/`1`/`"1"` allowlist -- a typo, `"yes"`, wrong-case `"TRUE"`, a stray number like `2` -- silently coerced to `0` (false) and was written to the DB, with the HTTP response still reporting a clean 200/201 success. The generated-JS duplicate `coerce()` in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (baked into every exported standalone app's own independently-callable REST API) carries the identical gap. Round 514 fixed this exact failure mode -- "quietly wrong data reported as success" -- but only in `buildImportRecords`, the client-side CSV-import parser that runs *before* a value is ever serialized into an HTTP request; it never touched `coerceValue`/`coerce()` itself, so a malformed boolean reaching either function by any other path (a direct API call, not just the CSV-import UI) was still silently corrupted rather than rejected.

**Independent verification**: read `coerceValue` in full and confirmed its `boolean` case is the only one with no `throw`, while `number`/`enum`/`date` right next to it all throw `ValidationError`. Read the generated `coerce()` in `codegen.ts` and confirmed byte-for-byte identical logic. Traced `routes/projects.ts`'s two record-write call sites (`insertRecord`/`updateRecord`, lines ~1199/~1692) to confirm `req.body` reaches `coerceValue` with zero validation above it -- unlike every other route in the file, which runs a Zod `safeParse` first. Grepped `repository.test.ts`/`codegen.test.ts` to confirm no existing test exercises an unrecognized boolean value against either function. Confirmed via `docs/roadmap.md` that round 514 is scoped explicitly to the CSV-import layer and round 523's `Number.isFinite` fix touched only the `number` branch -- neither round addressed `coerceValue`'s/`coerce()`'s own `boolean` branch.

**The fix**: added an explicit false-ish allowlist (`false`/`"false"`/`0`/`"0"`) alongside the existing true-ish one in both `coerceValue` and `coerce()`, throwing `ValidationError`/`Error` for anything outside both -- mirroring the throw convention every other branch in the same function already uses, without widening what counts as true/false beyond what was already recognized.

**The test**: `repository.test.ts` gained two tests -- one confirming every previously-recognized true/false form (`true`, `"true"`, `1`, `"1"`, `false`, `"false"`, `0`, `"0"`) still round-trips correctly, one confirming `"yes"`/`"no"`/`"TRUE"`/`"כן"`/`"לא"`/`2`/`"banana"` all now throw `ValidationError`. `codegen.test.ts` gained one test spawning a real generated server (the same standard this file's round-514/523 tests already use for `coerce()`) and confirming a direct POST with an unrecognized boolean value gets a real 400, not a silent 201.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `repository.ts`/`codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping all new tests in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failures: the "accepts every recognized form" test still passed against the old code, but the new rejection test failed in both files (`insertRecord` never threw; the spawned server returned 201 instead of 400 for `"yes"`). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran both full test files clean (`repository.test.ts` 20/20, `codegen.test.ts` 178/178). Full monorepo `npm test` (db 151/151, up from round 545's 149 by exactly the two new tests; api 481/481, up from 480 by exactly the one new test; shared 16, spec-engine 116, web 881 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `41f9869`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the narrow case of a boolean field value outside the recognized true/false forms reaching the server directly (not through the normal UI, which only ever sends a real checkbox's `true`/`false`); such a value is now rejected with a clear error instead of being silently stored as false, in both the live preview's backend and any app exported via "Export code."

### Round 547: the History panel's "N screens" count was wrong for every checkpoint, since it reads the entity count

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 542-546, to find a genuinely new bug class rather than a further instance of busy-guards, missing-call-sites, or validation-layer gaps.

**The finding**: `HistoryPanel.tsx` and `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `formatCheckpointHistory` (the "Download timeline" .txt export) both pass `checkpoint.spec.entities.length` as the `count` for the `history.screenCount` i18n key, whose text is literally "{count} screens" / "{count} מסכים". But a `ProductSpec`'s real `screens` array is a different, larger collection than `entities`: `heuristic.ts`'s `buildScreens` emits one Dashboard screen plus a List+Form pair per entity (`screens.length === 2*entities.length + 1`), and `templates.ts`'s `screensFor` emits one Dashboard plus one List screen per entity (`screens.length === entities.length + 1`). Neither formula equals `entities.length`, so every checkpoint shown in the History panel -- and every line of the exported timeline file -- has displayed a plausible-looking but factually wrong screen count since the feature shipped in round 165.

**Independent verification**: read both call sites directly and confirmed neither ever reads `checkpoint.spec.screens` at all. Read `buildScreens` in `heuristic.ts` and `screensFor` in `templates.ts` and confirmed both produce a `screens` array strictly longer than `entities`. Confirmed via `git log -S "spec.screens.length" -- apps/web/src/HistoryPanel.tsx` that the correct field has never been used here -- `entities.length` was used from the feature's introduction onward. Confirmed the gap went untested because the shared `makeSpec` test helpers in both `checkpointDiff.test.ts` and `HistoryPanel.test.ts` hardcode `screens: []`, so no existing assertion ever exercised a real, differently-sized `screens` array. Confirmed no `codegen.ts` duplicate exists -- Time Machine/History is a Forge AI platform-only feature, never ported to the exported standalone app.

**The fix**: both call sites now read `checkpoint.spec.screens.length` instead of `checkpoint.spec.entities.length` -- a one-line change in each of `HistoryPanel.tsx` and `checkpointDiff.ts`, with a comment at each site pointing at the other.

**The test**: updated the one pre-existing `checkpointDiff.test.ts` test that asserted on the screen-count text (it previously encoded the bug as "correct" by relying on `makeSpec`'s empty `screens: []` plus `entities.length` happening to match the assertion) to give each checkpoint a real `screens` array with a length deliberately different from its `entities` count, and tightened the assertions to the new, correct numbers. Added a new regression test in `HistoryPanel.test.ts` rendering a real checkpoint with 1 entity but 3 real screens and confirming the panel shows "3 screens", never "1 screens".

**Regression-proof**: backed up `HistoryPanel.tsx`/`checkpointDiff.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping all test changes in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failures against the old code in both files (each showed the old, wrong `entities.length`-based count). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran both full test files clean (`checkpointDiff.test.ts` 33/33, `HistoryPanel.test.ts` 21/21). Full monorepo `npm test` (web 882/882, up from round 546's 881 by exactly the one new test; db 151, api 481, shared 16, spec-engine 116 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `4b229f1`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the displayed/exported "screens" figure in the Time Machine history list and its downloadable timeline report; it now always matches the real number of screens in that checkpoint's spec.

### Round 548: the "Donation" domain entity spuriously matched the ordinary word "condonation"

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 542-547 (busy-guards, missing-call-sites, validation-layer gaps, the entities-vs-screens display bug, and every domain-entity/keyword pair already fixed), to find a genuinely new keyword-collision instance rather than a repeat of an already-closed mechanism.

**The finding**: `domainEntities.ts`'s Donation rule kept its "donation"/"donations" keywords as plain, unbounded strings (`lower.includes(kw)` in `matchesKeyword`, `heuristic.ts`), unlike the dozen-plus other keyword-collision fixes already in this same file. "donation" is a literal substring of the ordinary, unrelated legal/compliance phrase "condonation" (as in "condonation of delay", a standard term for excusing a missed filing deadline), so any law-firm or compliance-tracking description using that word spuriously produced a full charitable-Donation entity (`donorName`/`amount`/`campaign`/`status` fields) alongside the entities the description actually asked for.

**Independent verification**: read the Donation rule directly in `domainEntities.ts` (line ~843) and confirmed `"donation"`/`"donations"` were bare strings with no `\b`-bounding, unlike the neighboring "shipping" fix (round 455) at line ~880 which already uses `/\bshipping\b/`. Read `matchesKeyword`/`matchEntities` in `heuristic.ts` and confirmed string keywords match via plain `lower.includes(kw)`. Confirmed programmatically that `"condonation".includes("donation")` and `"condonations".includes("donations")` are both `true`. Ran a real repro through `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` with a law-firm/condonation-of-delay description and confirmed the generated spec included a spurious `Donation` entity alongside the correct `Customer`/`Case` entities. Confirmed via `git log -S'"donation"'` that this keyword has been unbounded since the entity was first added (round 64) and was never previously flagged or fixed. Confirmed no `codegen.ts` duplicate exists -- domain-entity keyword matching is a spec-engine-only concern, never ported to the exported standalone app.

**The fix**: replaced the bare `"donation"`, `"donations"` strings with a single `\b`-bounded `/\bdonations?\b/` RegExp -- the same pattern (plus the "(s)?" plural handling) this file's other collision fixes (reservation, shipping, stripe, מלאי, חיוב) already use.

**The test**: added a new regression test in `heuristic.test.ts` mirroring the existing reservation/preservation test's exact idiom -- confirms a condonation-of-delay law-firm description no longer matches `Donation`, while a real charity/donation description (singular and plural) still does.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failure against the old code (the condonation description still spuriously matched `Donation`). Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran the full test file clean (`heuristic.test.ts` 51/51). Full monorepo `npm test` (spec-engine 117/117, up from round 547's 116 by exactly the one new test; shared 16, db 151, api 481, web 882 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `36ab94d`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the narrow case of an app description that happens to use the word "condonation" (a legal/compliance term unrelated to charity); such a description no longer gets a spurious, irrelevant Donation entity, while every real donation/charity description still works exactly as before.

### Round 549: "Add field" accepted a numeral-led label that silently crashed the build

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 542-548 (busy-guards, missing-call-sites, validation-layer gaps, the entities-vs-screens display bug, and the Donation/condonation keyword collision), to find a genuinely new bug shape rather than a repeat.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `deriveFieldName` (the manual "Add field" UI's name-generation helper) splits a label on non-alphanumeric runs and joins the pieces with no check on the result's first character. A label like `"2024 Sales"` (or bare `"2024"`) joins to `"2024Sales"` -- a name that passes `AddFieldSchema` (just a non-empty string) and `FieldSchema` in `@forge/shared` (only guards reserved names and enum/relation shape, no identifier-shape check at all), so `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/fields` returns a clean 200 and the field is saved into the spec. The crash only surfaces later, at real build time: `packages/db/src/identifiers.ts`'s `SAFE_IDENTIFIER` (`/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`) requires a leading letter, and `migrate.ts` calls `assertSafeIdentifier(field.name, "column")` bare (no prefix) at four call sites, throwing a raw `Unsafe column identifier: "2024Sales"` `Error` the moment the Database step actually tries to create the column -- surfaced to the end user directly when no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is configured, or burning a real paid Debug-agent LLM call attempting to "fix" something that should never have been accepted in the first place, per `pipeline.ts`'s existing error-handling path (round 410's own trace of the identical catch/Debug-agent mechanism, just a different upstream cause).

**Independent verification**: read `deriveFieldName` (lines 182-193) directly and confirmed the only fallback is for a label with *zero* ASCII letters/digits at all (`words.join("") || "field"`) -- a numeral-led label never hits it, since it does have ASCII characters. Read `AddFieldSchema` (lines 121-123) and `FieldSchema`/`EntitySchema` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` and confirmed neither has any identifier-shape guard, only the reserved-name (`id`/`createdat`) and case-insensitive-duplicate-name checks round 410 already added. Read `packages/db/src/identifiers.ts` and confirmed `SAFE_IDENTIFIER` requires a leading letter, and that `tableNameFor` (used for *entity* names) always prefixes with `"entity_"`, so no entity name can ever violate it regardless of its own first character -- fields have no equivalent prefix, since column names are used bare. Grepped `migrate.ts` and confirmed `assertSafeIdentifier(field.name, "column")` is called at 4 call sites, all bare. Traced a real repro end to end: `POST .../fields` with label `"2024 Sales"` returns 200 (confirmed `updateProjectSpec`'s re-read via `ProductSpecSchema.parse` has nothing to reject it on), and the subsequent build fails with the raw error. Checked this isn't a duplicate of the round 410/411 "non-ASCII field name" candidate (evaluated and explicitly rejected as "too speculative" in round 411's own survey note) by reading that note directly: that candidate required the AI provider to violate its own prompt's explicit "MUST stay a plain ASCII identifier" instruction, and was about non-ASCII characters (e.g. Hebrew) reaching an AI-generated spec -- a completely different pathway and character class from this one, which is pure ASCII, deterministically reachable with zero AI involvement, through the manual "Add field" UI a human types into directly. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no `deriveFieldName` duplicate to port -- it's a live-preview-only UI helper, never duplicated for the exported app.

**The fix**: `deriveFieldName` now checks whether the joined result starts with a digit and, if so, prefixes it with `"field"` (reusing the exact fallback word the "no ASCII letters at all" case already uses) before the existing collision-dedup logic runs -- `"2024 Sales"` → `"field2024Sales"`, `"2024"` → `"field2024"`. This mirrors the protection entity names already get for free from `tableNameFor`'s permanent `"entity_"` prefix, just applied explicitly since fields have no such prefix.

**The test**: `apps/api/src/routes/projects.test.ts` gained a new test placed directly after the existing "falls back to 'field' when the label has no ASCII letters/digits at all" test, confirming three numeral-led labels (`"2024 Sales"`, bare `"2024"`, and `"3rd Quarter"`) all now derive a name with a leading letter.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `projects.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failure against the old code (`"2024Sales"` actual vs `"field2024Sales"` expected) -- exactly 1 failure, the other 12 pre-existing tests in the file stayed green. Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran the full test file clean (`projects.test.ts` 13/13). Full monorepo `npm test` (api 482/482, up from round 548's 481 by exactly the one new test; shared 16, spec-engine 117, db 151, web 882 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `5370deb`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the narrow case of adding a field whose label happens to start with a digit (e.g. a year or an ordinal); such a label now derives a valid column name instead of silently passing validation and then crashing the next build.

### Round 550: a library's "book checkout" spuriously produced an Order entity and recommended Stripe

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 542-549 (busy-guards, missing-call-sites, validation-layer gaps, the entities-vs-screens display bug, the Donation/condonation keyword collision, and the deriveFieldName identifier-shape gap), to find a genuinely new bug rather than a repeat.

**The finding**: the Order entity's keyword list in `domainEntities.ts` and the separate `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` list in `heuristic.ts` both carried the bare word `"checkout"`. Unlike every substring-collision this file has fixed before (e.g. "shipping"/"worshipping"), "checkout" is a whole word with no substring issue -- it's genuinely ambiguous English: an e-commerce purchase in most descriptions, but equally the ordinary word for a library's book checkout/return process or a hotel's checkout time, with nothing to do with orders or payments. A plain-language description for a library app ("manage book checkout, returns, and member records") produced a spec consisting of exactly one entity -- `Order`, with `customerName`/`total`/`status`/`items`/`courierId` fields -- nothing resembling a library, and recommended Stripe as the payment provider, via the deterministic no-API-key heuristic provider (the fallback path for any self-hosted deployment without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).

**Independent verification**: read the Order rule's keyword array directly and confirmed bare `"checkout"` sits alongside `/\border(s)?\b/`, `"purchase"`, `"delivery"` with no disambiguation. Read `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` and confirmed the identical bare `"checkout"` there too, feeding `buildOpenQuestions`'s `mentionsPayments` check. Ran a real repro directly against `matchEntities` with a library/book-checkout description and confirmed it returns exactly `["Order"]`. Grepped `git log -S'"checkout"'` on both files and confirmed the keyword has existed unbounded since the project's very first commit, never touched since. Checked no existing test anywhere in the repo relies on bare `"checkout"` matching anything (only a comment in `heuristic.test.ts` mentioning it as one of several PAYMENT_KEYWORDS entries a donation description should avoid -- unaffected by this fix). Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicate of this keyword-matching logic to port (the one `"checkout"` hit there, `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS`'s `"checkoutdate"`, is an unrelated date-field-pairing hint list).

**The fix**: both lists' bare `"checkout"` entries were replaced with three specific e-commerce phrases (`"checkout page"`, `"checkout flow"`, `"online checkout"`) -- the same disambiguation style this file's own "garage"/"garage sale" fix (round 454) already established for a genuinely ambiguous whole word, rather than a `\b`-bounded regex (which can't help here, since the collision isn't a substring issue).

**The test**: a new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, placed directly after the condonation/Donation regression test, confirms a library/book-checkout description no longer matches `Order` and no longer flips the payment open-question's recommendation to "Stripe" (every spec gets exactly one payment question; `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` only controls its wording/recommendation, not its presence -- the test's first draft wrongly asserted no payment question existed at all and had to be corrected to check the recommendation instead, after the initially-restored fix still failed it). A second assertion confirms a real `"checkout page"` phrase still matches `Order`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts` and `heuristic.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the test in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failure against the old code (the library description still matched `Order`) -- exactly 1 failure, the other 51 tests in the file stayed green. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran the full test file clean (`heuristic.test.ts` 52/52). Full monorepo `npm test` (spec-engine 118/118, up from round 549's 117 by exactly the one new test; shared 16, db 151, api 482, web 882 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `52910cb`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the narrow case of a description using the bare word "checkout" without any other order/purchase language (e.g. a library or hotel app); such a description no longer gets a spurious, irrelevant Order entity or a wrongly-recommended payment provider, while a real e-commerce description using an actual checkout phrase still works exactly as before.

### Round 551: a long entity label produced an unfolded PRODID line in exported .ics calendar files

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 542-550 (busy-guards, missing-call-sites, validation-layer gaps, the entities-vs-screens display bug, the Donation/condonation and Order/checkout keyword collisions, and the deriveFieldName identifier-shape gap), to find a genuinely new bug rather than a repeat.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/calendarIcs.ts`'s `buildCalendarIcs` builds its `PRODID` line (`` `PRODID:-//Forge AI//${icsEscapeText(entity.label ?? entity.name)}//EN` ``) and pushes it raw into the output, unlike every other variable-length line in the same function (`UID`, `SUMMARY`, `DESCRIPTION`), which all go through `foldIcsLine` -- the function this file's own doc comments say exists specifically because RFC 5545 §3.1 caps a content line at 75 UTF-8 octets, and because "a strict parser could reject or truncate" an over-length line (the exact failure round 430 already fixed for byte-counting inside `foldIcsLine` itself, on a different line). `entity.label` is exactly as unbounded and user-controlled as the other three fields -- `EntitySchema.label` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` is a bare `z.string().optional()` with no length cap, editable via the entity tab's inline rename -- yet PRODID was the one line that skipped the fold, apparently missed when PRODID's content was still just a short, developer-chosen entity name and never came close to the limit. The identical gap was duplicated in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s ported copy of the same function (used by every app exported via "Export code").

**Independent verification**: read both `calendarIcs.ts` and `codegen.ts`'s PRODID lines directly and confirmed neither calls `foldIcsLine`, while both files' UID/SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION lines do. Confirmed `EntitySchema.label`'s lack of a length cap by reading `packages/shared/src/index.ts` directly. Confirmed the gap is real and live-reachable (not test-only) by tracing the rename path (`EntityLabelEditor.tsx` → `PATCH .../entities/:entityName/label`, no server-side length validation anywhere in that route). Grepped `calendarIcs.test.ts` and confirmed no existing test exercises PRODID folding -- the one existing PRODID assertion (a regex matching `PRODID:-//Forge AI//.*//EN` on one line) only works because the test fixture's own entity label is short ("תור"), so this fix doesn't disturb it. Confirmed the same asymmetry is duplicated byte-for-byte in `codegen.ts`'s ported version via a direct grep.

**The fix**: both `calendarIcs.ts` and `codegen.ts` now wrap the PRODID line in `foldIcsLine(...)`, exactly like the other three lines in the same function.

**The tests**: `calendarIcs.test.ts` gained a new test, placed directly after the existing round-430 Hebrew-DESCRIPTION-folding test, confirming a ~150-character Hebrew entity label (well over the 75-UTF-8-byte budget) produces a correctly folded, multi-physical-line PRODID, with every physical line ≤75 UTF-8 octets. `codegen.test.ts` gained the analogous test using the file's own established real-generated-code extraction harness (regex-extracting `pickDisplayField`/`calendarLabelField`/`icsPad2`/`formatIcsDate`/`formatIcsTimestamp`/`icsEscapeText`/`utf8ByteLength`/`foldIcsLine`/`buildCalendarIcs` from the actual `generateExportFiles` output and assembling them via `new Function`, the same pattern the file's existing DTEND/escaping test already uses), confirming the exported app's own generated PRODID folds identically.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `calendarIcs.ts` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping both new tests in place), and confirmed the exact predicted failure in each (the raw PRODID line stayed on one physical line, over budget) -- exactly 1 failure in each file, every other pre-existing test in both stayed green (15/16 and 178/179 respectively). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran both full test files clean (`calendarIcs.test.ts` 16/16, `codegen.test.ts` 179/179). Full monorepo `npm test` (web 883/883, up from round 550's 882 by exactly the one new test; api 483/483, up from 482 by exactly the one new test; shared 16, spec-engine 118, db 151 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `f0a6183`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects the narrow case of an entity whose label is unusually long (well beyond any entity name this app's heuristic/AI engine or templates would ever generate on its own); the exported .ics calendar's PRODID line is now correctly folded like every other line in the file, so it can no longer make a strict calendar-app parser reject or mis-parse the whole file.

### Round 552: a "/" (or similar path-breaking character) in an entity/field name would permanently 404 every REST request for it, because `apps/web/src/api.ts` interpolates names into URL paths with no encoding

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-551 (keyword-collisions, the visible-staleness family, migrate.ts's collision guard, every race-condition class already fixed, the deriveFieldName identifier-shape fix, the entities-vs-screens display bug, and round 551's just-closed PRODID fold gap), to find a genuinely new bug.

**The finding**: every entity/field-scoped REST call in `apps/web/src/api.ts` (`renameEntityLabel`, `renameFieldLabel`, `addField`, `removeField`, `removeEntity`, `listRecords`, `createRecord`, `updateRecord`, `deleteRecord`) builds its URL by raw template-literal interpolation of `entityName`/`fieldName`, e.g. `` `/projects/${projectId}/entities/${entityName}` `` -- `encodeURIComponent` is never called anywhere in `apps/web/src` or `apps/api/src` (confirmed by grep: zero occurrences). `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` registers these as single-segment Express params (`/projects/:id/entities/:entityName`, `.../fields/:fieldName`, etc.). A name containing "/" -- a legal URL character browsers never percent-encode on their own -- splits the path into extra segments the single-segment param can't match, 404ing every request that names that entity/field, permanently, including its own rename/remove routes (renaming only ever changes the display `label`, never the underlying `name`).

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a re-opening of round 410's rejected non-ASCII-field-name candidate or round 283's rejected schema-level ASCII-identifier requirement**: confirmed `EntitySchema`/`FieldSchema` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` validate `name: z.string().min(1)` with no character-shape guard at all (only case-insensitive and sanitized-identifier *collision* checks exist, round 283). Confirmed `packages/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `deriveEntityName`/`deriveFieldName` (the manual "Add Entity"/"Add Field" UI's own name-generation helpers) split on `/[^A-Za-z0-9]+/`, stripping every non-alphanumeric character including "/" before a name is ever stored -- so this bug is entirely unreachable through the UI. The only other path a name is ever set is the real Anthropic provider, whose system prompt (`packages/spec-engine/src/anthropic.ts` line 39) says a name "MUST stay a plain ASCII identifier... no matter what" -- the same precondition round 410 called "too speculative to treat as a real bug" when evaluating a *different* downstream symptom (a raw non-ASCII SQL identifier). That round 410 decision was about not spending a dedicated round chasing an unconfirmed AI-violates-its-own-prompt scenario as the *headline* finding; it was never a blanket rule against ever hardening against it. The precedent for exactly this situation already exists: `apps/api/src/backup.ts`'s `sanitizeZipEntryName` (added specifically because "a project with an entity name containing '/' ... builds and runs live in this app perfectly normally" by the time it reaches that one unguarded code path) was implemented under the identical reachability assumption, as cheap, safe defense-in-depth -- not because anyone ever observed the AI actually violating its prompt. This fix follows that same established precedent for the one client-side code path (`api.ts`'s own URL construction) that precedent was never extended to. Confirmed via grep that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` needs no equivalent fix: `generateExportFiles` calls `assertSafe(entity.name)`/`assertSafe(field.name)` on every entity/field (lines 265-267, 331-334, 5309-5311) *before* any file -- including the exported app's own client code -- is ever generated, so an unsafe name can never reach the exported standalone app at all (the same conclusion rounds 283/284/379 already reached for this file).

**The fix**: wrapped `entityName`/`fieldName` in `encodeURIComponent(...)` at all 9 URL-interpolation sites in `apps/web/src/api.ts`. `encodeURIComponent` is a no-op change on the wire for every name already in use today (ASCII or Hebrew alike -- the browser already percent-encodes non-ASCII bytes during the real fetch either way), so no currently-working project is affected.

**The tests**: `apps/web/src/api.test.ts` gained a new test calling `listRecords`, `removeEntity`, and `removeField` with an entity/field name containing "/" (`"Profit/Loss"`, `"unit/price"`), asserting the captured `fetch` URL has the "/" percent-encoded (`%2F`) rather than splitting the path.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `api.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `api.test.ts`), confirmed the exact predicted failure (the raw, unencoded URL) -- exactly 1 failure, the other 25 pre-existing tests in the file stayed green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran `api.test.ts` clean (26/26). Full monorepo `npm test` (web 884/884, up from round 551's 883 by exactly the one new test; api 483, shared 16, spec-engine 118, db 151 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `45efd01`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this is a defensive hardening fix for a narrow, not-yet-observed scenario (an AI-generated spec whose entity/field name violates the AI's own explicit prompt instruction to stay ASCII); every project working today is completely unaffected.

### Round 553: manually adding or removing an entity pre-build left `spec.screens` permanently out of sync with `spec.entities`

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-552 (keyword-collisions, the visible-staleness family, migrate.ts's collision guard, every race-condition class already fixed, the client-side URL-encoding gap just closed in round 552, and the foldIcsLine coverage gap closed in round 551), to find a genuinely new bug.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `POST /projects/:id/entities` (add entity) and `DELETE /projects/:id/entities/:entityName` (remove entity) routes -- both pre-build-only, reachable from the real "Add Entity"/"Remove Entity" UI on the spec-review screen (`AddEntityForm` in `App.tsx`, `SpecListItemRemover.tsx`) -- built their `nextSpec` by copying `project.spec` and only ever touching `entities`; `screens` was carried through completely unchanged in both directions. `POST /projects/:id/build` then passes `project.spec` straight into the pipeline with no regeneration of `screens` from `entities`, and the resulting checkpoint is an immutable snapshot -- so any drift introduced before the first build is permanent. A manually-added entity therefore got zero screens of its own (silently undercounting the "N screens" HistoryPanel.tsx/checkpointDiff.ts display -- the spec's only two consumers of this field, confirmed by grep across both `apps/` and `packages/`), and a manually-removed entity left its own screen entries behind, dangling and naming an entity that no longer exists in the spec at all.

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of round 547 (closed)**: round 547 fixed HistoryPanel.tsx/checkpointDiff.ts *reading* `entities.length` instead of the already-correct `screens.length` -- it assumed the underlying `spec.screens` data was trustworthy and just needed to be read. This finding is that the assumption is sometimes false: `spec.screens` itself can be stale at the data layer, produced by a completely different code path (the two routes above, never touched by round 547's fix) that this round's own fix now also needs to patch. Confirmed by reading `packages/spec-engine/src/heuristic.ts`'s `buildScreens` (Dashboard + List + Form per entity) and `packages/spec-engine/src/templates.ts`'s `screensFor` (Dashboard + List only) directly -- neither is ever reapplied once a project exists, and a third producer (`AnthropicSpecProvider`) can emit an even more arbitrary shape per its own system prompt. Confirmed `packages/db/src/projects.ts`'s `updateProjectSpec` is a pure JSON passthrough with no normalization step anywhere in the write path. Confirmed zero existing test coverage of `screens` in combination with either route (`grep screens apps/api/src/routes/projects.test.ts` → no matches), consistent with round 547's own observation that test helpers always hardcoded `screens: []`.

**The fix**: added `deriveScreensForNewEntity` (`routes/projects.ts`), which -- since there's no single universal screens shape across this app's three spec producers -- mirrors whichever existing entity's own screens come last in the `entities` array (the most likely to reflect the project's current real convention, including after a refine), falling back to a single plain List screen when no entity has any tagged screens at all. Every screen either producer emits already carries its owning entity's name in `screen.entity`, so the add route appends the mirrored set and the remove route simply filters out every screen whose `entity` matches the removed name -- fully convention-agnostic in both directions.

**The tests**: 3 new unit tests for `deriveScreensForNewEntity` in `projects.test.ts` (mirroring a List+Form shape, a List-only shape, and the no-tagged-screens fallback), plus 2 new end-to-end tests in `app.test.ts` using the real heuristic-matched "A CRM with customers and deals" fixture (confirmed elsewhere in the file to produce exactly `[Customer, Deal]` with no relation between them) -- one confirming a newly-added entity's screens mirror the existing `Deal List`/`Deal Form` shape instead of being empty, one confirming removing `Deal` also removes its own screens instead of leaving them dangling.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `projects.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping all 5 new/updated tests in place). `projects.test.ts` failed immediately at module load (`SyntaxError: ... does not provide an export named 'deriveScreensForNewEntity'`) -- an accepted strong confirmation signal per this project's own established methodology. The two new `app.test.ts` tests failed with exactly the predicted pre-fix shapes (an empty screens array for the added entity; the stale "Deal" entries still present after removal), and all 167 other tests in that file stayed green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran clean: `projects.test.ts` 16/16, `app.test.ts` 169/169, full `@forge/api` 488/488 (+5). Full monorepo `npm test` (web 884 unchanged, api 488 [+5], db 151/spec-engine 118/shared 16 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `1d9d12d`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- every project that already exists and has never used the manual Add/Remove Entity buttons pre-build is completely unaffected; this only corrects the screen count/entries for entities added or removed through that specific pre-build flow going forward.

### Round 554: a WhatsApp send failure (missing country code, invalid phone number, or disconnected) showed the raw internal error code on screen instead of a translated message

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-553 (keyword-collisions, the visible-staleness family, migrate.ts's collision guard, every race-condition class already fixed, the client-side URL-encoding gap closed in round 552, and the spec.screens producer-side drift gap closed in round 553), to find a genuinely new bug.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.ts`'s `sendMessage()` returns one of three stable, machine-readable snake_case codes on a known, anticipated failure before ever reaching Baileys: `"not_connected"`, `"invalid_phone_number"`, `"missing_country_code"` (lines 384, 393, 420). `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `POST /projects/:id/integrations/whatsapp/send` forwards that string verbatim in a 502 body (`{ok: false, error: result.error}`) -- a different response shape than the `{error, code}` shape every other route's generic error middleware uses. `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `sendWhatsAppMessage` explicitly distinguishes the two shapes (a comment right there says so) and runs the `{error, code}` shape through `resolveErrorMessage` for translation -- but for the `{ok, error}` shape, it returned `body` completely as-is, with no translation lookup at all. `apps/web/src/WhatsAppPanel.tsx` then displayed `result.error` directly in both its "send test message" and "Retry" failure paths, so the literal text `missing_country_code` (or the other two codes) appeared on screen, in both Hebrew and English UI modes, for this Hebrew-first app.

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of rounds 506/507's country-code fix**: those rounds fixed the *detection logic* -- correctly building the JID and correctly recognizing when a country code is genuinely missing (round 506 proposed it, round 507 fixed an unsound digit-count comparison in that same detection). This finding is strictly downstream of correct detection: the failure reason is already identified correctly by the time it reaches this bug; the bug is that the correctly-identified reason is never translated or formatted before reaching the screen. Confirmed via grep that none of the three literal strings appear anywhere in `apps/web/src` except inside `apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.test.ts`'s own assertions -- no existing translation key, no existing client-side mapping. Read the full chain end-to-end (`whatsappWeb.ts` → `routes/projects.ts` → `api.ts` → `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`) directly to confirm the exact point translation was skipped (the `typeof body.ok === "boolean"` branch in `api.ts`, which returns early before the `resolveErrorMessage` call just below it). Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no equivalent client-side WhatsApp-send helper to port to -- this integration is live-preview-only, never part of the exported standalone app.

**The fix**: `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `sendWhatsAppMessage` now checks whether the `{ok, error}` shape's `error` string is one of the three known codes; if so, it translates via `resolveErrorMessage({code: "WHATSAPP_SEND_<CODE>", error: body.error})`, the exact same `error.<CODE>` convention every other server error in this app already uses (falling back to the raw string if no translation exists for an unrecognized code, same as `resolveErrorMessage` already does elsewhere). Any other string -- a genuine Baileys-internal failure caught in `sendMessage`'s own `catch` block, which has no fixed shape and genuinely can't be translated -- still passes through completely unchanged. Three new translation keys (`error.WHATSAPP_SEND_NOT_CONNECTED`, `error.WHATSAPP_SEND_INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER`, `error.WHATSAPP_SEND_MISSING_COUNTRY_CODE`) were added in both Hebrew and English in `apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts`, right next to the existing `error.WHATSAPP_NOT_CONNECTED` key.

**The tests**: `apps/web/src/api.test.ts` gained a new test confirming all three known codes are translated (asserting the raw code string never appears in the result), placed directly after the existing test that confirms an arbitrary/unrecognized failure string (e.g. "socket write failed") still passes through raw -- the two tests together pin both halves of the fix's behavior. `apps/web/src/i18n/language.test.ts`'s own existing translation-completeness scanner (he/en key parity, used-vs-defined keys) ran clean against the three new keys with no changes needed.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `api.ts` and `language.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new/updated tests in place), confirmed the exact predicted failure -- exactly 1 failure (the new test), with the other 26 pre-existing tests in `api.test.ts` staying green, including the "passes through unchanged" test for an unrecognized string. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran `api.test.ts` clean (27/27) and `language.test.ts` clean (20/20, confirming no translation-key gaps). Full monorepo `npm test` (web 885/885, up from round 553's 884 by exactly the one new test; api 488, db 151, spec-engine 118, shared 16 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `513440f`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- a WhatsApp send failure for one of these three reasons now shows a clear, translated message instead of a raw internal code; any other failure reason (a genuine connectivity/Baileys error) is unaffected and continues to show its own real message as before.

### Round 555: a numeral-led entity label (e.g. "2024 Sales") built and ran fine, but always failed on Export

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-554 (keyword-collisions, the visible-staleness family, migrate.ts's collision guard, every race-condition class already fixed, the client-side URL-encoding gap closed in round 552, the spec.screens producer-side drift gap closed in round 553, and the WhatsApp send-failure dual-shape translation gap closed in round 554), to find a genuinely new bug.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s `deriveEntityName` (used by `POST /projects/:id/entities`, the real "Add Entity" UI flow) title-cases and joins a free-text label's words with no separator, but never checked whether the joined result starts with a digit. A plain, everyday English label like `"2024 Sales"` joins to `"2024Sales"`; a bare `"2026"` joins to `"2026"` unchanged. `EntitySchema`/`ProductSpecSchema` in `@forge/shared` only check for an empty string and case-insensitive collisions -- never identifier shape -- so this passes spec validation and the project builds and runs completely normally in the live preview, because `packages/db/src/identifiers.ts`'s `tableNameFor` always prepends a permanent `entity_` prefix to every entity's real SQL table name, which guarantees a leading letter regardless of what `deriveEntityName` itself produced. But `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported-app generator (`renderServerJs`, invoked from `generateExportFiles`) uses `entity.name` directly as the SQL table/route name with no such prefix, so its own `assertSafe` (`SAFE_IDENTIFIER = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`) throws the moment the user clicks "Export App" on an otherwise-healthy, already-built project -- surfaced as a 422 `EXPORT_UNSAFE_IDENTIFIER` whose own message ("rename it to use only English letters, digits, and underscores") is actively misleading here, since `"2024Sales"` already satisfies that literal description.

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of round 549 (closed)**: round 549 fixed this exact mechanism for `deriveFieldName` (column names) only -- its own doc comment explicitly claims entity names "get this same protection for free from tableNameFor's permanent entity_ prefix," which is true for the live-preview path but was never checked against codegen.ts's export path, where fields and entities are *not* symmetric: fields have no prefix of their own either way, while entities' prefix is a live-preview-only artifact that doesn't exist in the exported app's own generated SQL. Confirmed via direct `node -e` repro: `deriveEntityName("2024 Sales", [])` → `"2024Sales"`, and `/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/.test("2024Sales")` → `false`. Confirmed via grep that `codegen.ts` calls `assertSafe(entity.name, "entity")` directly (lines 265, 5309) with no prefixing step anywhere before it. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no independent copy of `deriveEntityName`/`deriveFieldName` to also patch -- both are route-level, pre-build-only helpers.

**The fix**: `deriveEntityName` now prefixes the joined base with `"Entity"` whenever it starts with a digit (mirroring round 549's own `deriveFieldName` fix, which prefixes with `"field"`), before the de-dup suffix logic runs -- so `"2024 Sales"` now derives to `"Entity2024Sales"`. The misleading doc comment on `deriveFieldName` claiming entities get this protection "for free" was also corrected to note the export-path exception this round found.

**The tests**: a new unit test in `projects.test.ts` (`"2024 Sales"` → `"Entity2024Sales"`, bare `"2024"` → `"Entity2024"`, `"3rd Party Vendors"` → `"Entity3rdPartyVendors"`), placed directly after the existing `deriveEntityName` collision-suffix test, mirroring round 549's own `deriveFieldName` numeral-led test. Plus a new end-to-end test in `app.test.ts`: add an entity via the real route with label `"2024 Sales"`, build, then export -- confirming the export now returns 200 instead of the `EXPORT_UNSAFE_IDENTIFIER` 422, the same shape as the existing non-ASCII-entity-name export test just above it in the file.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `projects.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping both new/updated tests in place). `projects.test.ts` failed with exactly the predicted pre-fix value (`'2024Sales'` instead of `'Entity2024Sales'`) -- exactly 1 failure, with `deriveFieldName`'s own analogous test and the other 15 tests in the file staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran `projects.test.ts` clean (17/17). Full monorepo `npm test` (web 885 unchanged, api 490 [+2], db 151/spec-engine 118/shared 16 all unchanged) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `e7502d0`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- every project that already exists and has never added an entity with a numeral-led label is completely unaffected; this only fixes a project that does so going forward from being unexportable.

### Round 556: GlobalSearch's "Show all" button kept promising matches that no longer existed, once real data drifted after the original search

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-555 (keyword-collisions, the visible-staleness family, migrate.ts's collision guard, every race-condition class already fixed, and the two now-closed identifier-shape gaps in `deriveFieldName`/`deriveEntityName` from rounds 549/555), to find a genuinely new bug.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s `handleShowAll` re-fetches one entity's records with no sample cap and recomputes the full match list via `searchEntityRecords`, correctly populating `expandedSamples[entityName]` with every real current match. But it never patches that entity's own `totalMatches` field inside the `results` array -- the header's `t("search.resultCount", { count: result.totalMatches })` text and the `remaining = result.totalMatches - displayed.length` calculation that decides whether the "Show all" button itself should still render both keep reading the *original* search's now-stale count. If a record matching the query is deleted (by a collaborator, a WhatsApp-triggered write, or the same user in another tab) between the original search and the "Show all" click -- entirely plausible, since the search panel can stay open for any length of time -- `displayed` already reflects every real current match (via the fresh fetch), but `remaining` stays positive forever, since `totalMatches` never shrinks to match. The "Show all" button never disappears, continuing to promise matches that don't exist; clicking it again just re-fetches and re-displays the exact same, already-complete list, with no way out short of closing and reopening the whole panel. The same gap exists verbatim in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s duplicated `GlobalSearch` component, so every exported standalone app has the identical bug.

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of round 519 (closed)**: round 519 fixed the Retry button skipping `setExpandedSamples({})` before its own re-search, so a *different* query's fresh data got mixed with a *stale* expansion from before the retry -- a cross-request contamination bug, guarded in part by the pre-existing `searchRequestId` race guard the surrounding code comment documents. This finding has no race at all: it's a single, successful, in-order `handleShowAll` call whose own fetch is already fully up to date, but whose one piece of carried-over state (`totalMatches`, computed once by the *original* search and never touched again) silently drifts out of sync with the very data `handleShowAll` itself just fetched. Confirmed via direct reading of `handleShowAll` (lines 198-223) that `setExpandedSamples` is the *only* state update it performs, with `results` never touched. Confirmed `searchEntityRecords`'s own `limit = records.length` call site inside `handleShowAll` means `full.sample.length` always equals the entity's real, current total match count -- the exact value `totalMatches` needed but never got. Confirmed via grep that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own `handleShowAll` has the identical one-sided `setExpandedSamples`-only update, with no `setResults` call either.

**The fix**: `handleShowAll` now also calls `setResults` to patch the matching entity's `totalMatches` to the fresh fetch's own real count, in both `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`'s duplicate -- the same pattern each file already uses for `setExpandedSamples`, just extended to the one piece of state that was never kept in sync.

**The tests**: a new test in `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` and its mirror in `codegen.test.ts` (driven through the real generated `GlobalSearch.jsx`, not a reimplementation) both: run an initial search returning 7 matches (capped to a 5-row sample with a "Show all" button for the other 2), mock the "Show all" click's own re-fetch to return only 5 records (simulating 2 having been deleted in between), and assert the "Show all" button disappears once every real match is shown -- instead of staying visible forever, offering 2 more matches that no longer exist.

**A sub-finding surfaced while writing these tests**: the first draft asserted `assert.equal(document.querySelector(".global-search-show-all"), null, ...)` directly -- the same literal pattern round 519's own closed test already uses successfully. Against the old, unpatched code, this hung the test process for the node:test default timeout instead of failing cleanly within milliseconds: a failing `assert.equal` on a live React-rendered DOM node forces Node's assertion module to serialize that node (and its still-attached Fiber tree) into the failure message, which is prohibitively slow for a node carrying React internals. Round 519's own version of this assertion never hit this path because it only runs when the assertion *passes*. Fixed by comparing a boolean (`querySelector(...) === null`) instead of the raw node, in both new tests -- the assertion's intent is unchanged, but a genuine failure now reports in milliseconds instead of hanging.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping both new tests in place). Both new tests failed with the exact predicted shape -- the "Show all" button stayed present after the fresh 5-match fetch -- confirmed in well under a second each (after fixing the boolean-comparison issue above), with every other test in both files staying green (`GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` 19 others, `codegen.test.ts`'s full suite). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran clean: `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` 20/20, full `@forge/api` 491/491 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, spec-engine 118, db 151 all unchanged; api 491 [+1]; web 886 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `9e32fb0`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects a search panel left open while matching data changes elsewhere; every other search flow is unaffected.

### Round 557: two new keyword collisions -- "booking"/"overbooking" (Appointment) and "task"/"multitasking" (Task)

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-556 (keyword-collisions already fixed, the visible-staleness family, migrate.ts's collision guard, every race-condition class already fixed, and round 556's just-closed stale-derived-count gap in GlobalSearchPanel), to find a genuinely new bug. The survey returned to the keyword-collision class -- still open-ended, since a new entity/keyword pair not yet checked is always a valid finding regardless of how many prior rounds mined this file.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s Appointment rule kept a bare `"booking"` string keyword, and its Task rule kept a bare `"task"` string keyword. `matchesKeyword` (`heuristic.ts`) does a plain `lower.includes(kw)` substring test for string keywords -- no word boundary. `"booking"` is a substring of the ordinary, unrelated word **"overbooking"** (airline/hotel capacity management), and `"task"` is a substring of **"multitasking"** (a personal-productivity/time-management skill). This is the `HeuristicSpecProvider`, used whenever `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset AND as the automatic fallback whenever the Anthropic provider throws (`packages/spec-engine/src/index.ts`), so it's reachable by any real user -- a description like "An airline tool to track overbooking rates and flight seat capacity" silently got a bogus `Appointment` entity injected, and "A coaching app to help employees improve multitasking and focus skills" silently got a bogus `Task` entity injected, alongside whatever the description actually asked for.

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of the dozen+ prior keyword-collision fixes**: confirmed directly via `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` calls against the real source tree (not just static inspection): the overbooking description returned `entities: ['Appointment']`, and the multitasking description returned `entities: ['Employee', 'Task']`. Confirmed `matchesKeyword`'s plain-substring behavior for string keywords by reading `heuristic.ts` directly. Confirmed this is a genuinely new keyword/entity pair, distinct from every prior fix in this file (order/disorder, stock/livestock, driver/screwdriver, patient/impatient, garage/garage-sale, donation/condonation, reservation/preservation, shipping/worshipping, mechanic/mechanical, "checkout" polysemy) -- same mechanism (pitfall-1: bare keyword as a substring of an unrelated longer word), never-checked word pair. Confirmed via grep that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicate of `matchEntities`/`domainEntities.ts` to also patch -- this heuristic only runs at spec-generation time, before any export exists.

**The fix**: both bare keywords were replaced with `\b`-bounded RegExps plus the established `"(s)?"` plural handling this file's other collision fixes already use -- `/\bbookings?\b/` for Appointment (so "booking"/"bookings" still match, but not "overbooking"), and `/\btasks?\b/` for Task (so "task"/"tasks" still match, but not "multitasking"/"tasking").

**The tests**: two new tests in `heuristic.test.ts`, mirroring the exact idiom of the existing reservation/preservation and donation/condonation collision tests: each confirms the collision description does NOT produce the wrong entity, then confirms the real keyword still matches both singular and plural forms on its own (using a description that avoids the rule's other keywords, so a match can only come from the keyword under test).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping both new tests in place). Both new tests failed with the exact predicted shape -- 2 failures (one per collision), with every other test in the file staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran clean: `heuristic.test.ts` 54/54 (+2), full `@forge/spec-engine` 120/120 (+2). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, db 151, api 491, web 886 all unchanged; spec-engine 120 [+2]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `9157d9c`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects a project description containing "overbooking" or "multitasking" without otherwise describing appointments or tasks, and only when the heuristic provider is in use (no API key, or the Anthropic provider failed).

### Round 558: Property's bare "property" keyword collided with "intellectual property", "lost property", and "property damage"

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-557 (every closed keyword-collision pair, including round 557's just-closed booking/overbooking and task/multitasking), to find a genuinely new bug. The survey returned once more to the keyword-collision class -- still open-ended, since a new entity/keyword pair not yet checked is always a valid finding regardless of how many prior rounds mined this file.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s Property rule kept a bare `"property"` string keyword. Unlike the substring-in-a-longer-word pitfall already fixed a dozen-plus times (order/stock/driver/..., most recently booking/overbooking and task/multitasking in round 557), this one is the *other* established collision shape in this file: a whole, correctly-spelled word that's genuinely ambiguous in ordinary English, the same shape as the already-fixed "garage"/"garage sale" (round 454) and "checkout" (round 550). "Intellectual property" (patents/trademarks), "lost property" (a lost-and-found service), and "property damage" (an insurance/incident-tracking app) are all ordinary idioms that word-boundary-match "property" correctly, with nothing to do with real estate. Confirmed via direct `matchEntities()` calls against the real source tree: an IP-law-firm description returned `['Customer', 'Property', 'Case']` (spurious Property), a lost-and-found description returned `['Property']` alone (nothing but the bogus entity), and an incident/damage-claims description returned `['Employee', 'Property']` (spurious Property) -- while a genuine real-estate description correctly kept matching.

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of round 457 (closed)**: round 457 fixed this same rule's bare `"listing"` keyword colliding with the substring "enlisting" -- a different keyword in the same rule, and the substring-pitfall shape, not the whole-word-polysemy shape. Round 457's own roadmap entry explicitly noted "no further domainEntities.ts candidates are currently known" after that fix, meaning the bare `"property"` keyword itself was never flagged or checked at the time. Confirmed via grep that this is the only Property-related fix in the closed list. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicate of `domainEntities.ts`/`matchEntities` to also patch -- this heuristic only runs at spec-generation time, before any export exists.

**The fix**: the bare `"property"` keyword was replaced with `/\b(?<!intellectual\s)(?<!lost[\s-])propert(?:y|ies)\b(?!\s+damage\b)/` -- a lookbehind/lookahead pattern that excludes only the three known false-positive idioms, verified against seven cases (the three collisions, both positive and negative variants of "lost property"/"lost-property", and two genuine real-estate phrasings) via a standalone Node regex test before writing it into the file, mirroring the disambiguation style `"garage"`'s `(?!\s+sales?\b)` lookahead already established in this file.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, mirroring the exact idiom of the existing "garage"/"garage sale" and "listing"/"enlisting" collision tests: confirms all three collision descriptions do NOT produce a spurious Property entity, then confirms the real keyword still matches both singular and plural forms on its own (using a description that avoids the rule's other keywords, so a match can only come from "property"/"properties" itself).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place). The new test failed with the exact predicted shape -- 1 failure (the first of the three collision assertions, since `assert.ok` throws immediately), with every other test in the file staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Re-ran clean: `heuristic.test.ts` 55/55 (+1), full `@forge/spec-engine` 121/121 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, db 151, api 491, web 886 all unchanged; spec-engine 121 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `8c0480f`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects a project description containing "intellectual property", "lost property", or "property damage" without otherwise describing a real-estate business, and only when the heuristic provider is in use (no API key, or the Anthropic provider failed).

### Round 559: the "Manager" role was spuriously fabricated for any description mentioning "mismanagement"

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-558 (including round 558's just-closed Property/"intellectual property" whole-word-polysemy finding), to find a genuinely new bug.

Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicate of `domainEntities.ts`/`matchRoles` -- same as rounds 557-558, this heuristic only runs at spec-generation time, before any export exists.

### Round 560: the topbar's WhatsApp unread badge could flash a stale nonzero count while the panel was already open

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-559 (including round 559's just-closed ROLE_RULES/"mismanagement" finding), to find a genuinely new bug. The survey moved away from the keyword-collision class entirely and into a fresh area: the cross-component interaction between two independent WhatsApp pollers.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s global unread-badge poll (`checkUnread`, every `WHATSAPP_UNREAD_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` = 20s) and `apps/web/src/WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s own poll (`startConnectedPolling`, every `CONNECTED_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` = 10s, which is also what keeps the panel's own "last seen" marker in `localStorage` up to date via its `useEffect(() => { if (messages.length > 0) setWhatsAppLastSeenId(...) }, [projectId, messages])`) run on two completely independent, unsynchronized schedules. `openPanel("whatsapp")` zeroes `whatsappUnreadCount` exactly once, at the moment the panel opens -- confirmed by reading `openPanel`'s own body and the `{showWhatsApp && <WhatsAppPanel .../>}` render block, which passes no `onUnreadChange`-style callback back into `App.tsx`. So if a new inbound message arrives while the panel is open, and `checkUnread`'s own tick lands before `WhatsAppPanel`'s own poll has caught up and updated the last-seen marker, `checkUnread` reads the still-stale marker, counts the new message as unread, and flashes a nonzero badge on the topbar's WhatsApp button -- right next to the very message the user is already looking at live in the open log.

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of the closed WhatsApp list**: the denylist's WhatsApp entries are round 530's `startPolling` stale-fetch race (a race *inside* `WhatsAppPanel`'s own polling logic, between it and `handleDisconnect`), round 554's dual-shape error-translation gap, and rounds 506-507's `sendMessage` country-code handling -- none of which concern this specific cross-component interaction between `App.tsx`'s own independent poll and `WhatsAppPanel`'s poll/last-seen-marker pipeline. Confirmed via direct reading of both files' effects and intervals (not trusting any "already handled" claim) that `checkUnread`'s dependency array (`[project?.id, project?.status]`) and body never reference `showWhatsApp` at all, and that the toolbar's WhatsApp button (with the badge) renders unconditionally regardless of whether the panel itself is open. A runner-up candidate (`ROLE_RULES.Admin`'s bare `"owner"` colliding with "homeowner"/"property owner") was investigated and found behaviorally inert -- `matchRoles` unconditionally adds Admin regardless of any keyword match, so the collision has no observable effect. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no WhatsApp-unread-badge logic to also patch -- this feature was never ported to the exported app.

**The fix**: added a `showWhatsAppRef` mirroring the `showWhatsApp` state via its own small `useEffect`, read inside `checkUnread`'s closure (without adding `showWhatsApp` to the poll effect's own dependency array, which would otherwise restart the whole 20s interval every time the panel opened or closed). `checkUnread` now forces the badge to 0 whenever `showWhatsAppRef.current` is true, instead of trusting the possibly-still-stale last-seen marker.

### Round 562: Event's bare Hebrew keyword "כנס" collided with כ.נ.ס login/enter verb conjugations

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-561 (including round 561's just-closed Student/"pupil" finding), to find a genuinely new bug. This is a substring of several extremely common conjugations of the כ.נ.ס root ("to enter"/"to log in"): `להיכנס` ("to log in" -- arguably the single most common phrase in Hebrew app descriptions for describing any login/access flow), `נכנס` ("enters/logs in"), `תיכנס`, `מתכנס`, `התכנסות`. Strikingly, this very entity's own Review-entity keyword comment a few hundred lines up in the same file already warns about the identical "event" ⊂ "prevents" substring shape in English (explaining why Event's own English keywords use "event planning"/"conference" instead of bare "event") -- but the parallel Hebrew collision on `כנס` itself had never been caught. Confirmed via a direct `matchEntities()` call against the real source tree: a plain employee/task-management app description mentioning "כל עובד יכול להיכנס למערכת" ("each employee can log into the system") returned `['Employee', 'Task', 'Event']`, fabricating a spurious Event entity (with its own Dashboard/List/Form screens, `date`/`venue`/`capacity`/`status` fields) for a description with no conference concept at all.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, mirroring the exact idiom of the existing Hebrew collision tests: confirms three distinct כ.נ.ס-conjugation descriptions (`להיכנס`, `נכנס`, `מתכנס`) do NOT produce a spurious Event entity, then confirms the real keyword still matches both singular (`כנס`) and plural (`כנסים`) conference usage on its own.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, mirroring the exact idiom of the existing Hebrew collision tests (and round 550's "checkout" test, since this keyword also lives in `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`): confirms the martial-arts-club description does NOT produce a spurious Subscription entity and that its payment-question recommendation stays `"בלי תשלומים"` (not Stripe) rather than only checking the question's bare presence, confirms a second description (`אמנויות`, a visual-arts school) also doesn't collide, then confirms the real keyword still matches both singular (`מנוי`) and plural (`מנויים`) subscription usage on its own. (While writing this test, the first draft's lookup for the payment question used the literal substring `"תשלום"`, which does not match `"תשלומים"` -- Hebrew's word-final `ם` vs. mid-word `מ` are different characters, so a naive substring check across that boundary silently fails; fixed by searching for the shorter common prefix `"תשלו"` instead, catching this before it could become a vacuous assertion.)
