### Round 566: Rental was never added to BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES, so rental-business descriptions got "No payments" recommended

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-565 (including round 565's just-closed Employee/"עובד" finding). Given the keyword-collision class in `domainEntities.ts` had now been mined 5 consecutive rounds (562-565), the agent was explicitly steered toward a different bug class this round rather than re-scanning that file again.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/heuristic.ts`'s `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES` set (`new Set(["Invoice", "Order", "Donation", "Subscription"])`, introduced in an earlier round specifically to stop `buildOpenQuestions`'s payment recommendation from drifting out of sync with `domainEntities.ts`'s own growing keyword list -- see that fix's own comment warning "new payment-flavored keyword phrasing for these entities will keep getting added over time... checking the entity itself is the one place this can't silently drift out of sync") never included `"Rental"`. `domainEntities.ts`'s Rental entity (added in round 57, after `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES` was already established) has keywords like `"equipment rental"`/`"rent out"`/`"rental business"` that share no substring with any of `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` (`payment`/`invoice`/`billing`/`subscription`/`checkout page`/`stripe`/Hebrew equivalents), so a rental-business description matching only Rental never set `mentionsPayments`, and since Rental was missing from `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES`, `hasBillingEntity` was also false -- `needsPayments` ended up `false`. Confirmed via a direct `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` call against the real source tree: `"A tool rental business for a hardware store. Customers rent tools for a few days at a time."` matched only `Rental`/`Customer` and got `recommendation: "No payments"` -- plainly wrong, since renting items out for a fee is definitionally a paid transaction. Reproduced identically in Hebrew (`"אפליקציה לניהול השכרת ציוד לחנות כלי עבודה..."` → `"בלי תשלומים"`).

**Independent verification, including why this is NOT a duplicate of the closed list**: this is the exact same producer/consumer drift class the `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES` set's own original fix (for Donation/Subscription, documented earlier in this file) explicitly predicted could recur for a future entity -- confirmed via `grep -n "BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES" docs/roadmap.md`, which shows only that one prior fix, never Rental. Not a `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`/`ROLE_RULES` keyword-substring collision (the 5-straight-round class) -- Rental's own keywords match correctly and unambiguously; the bug is a stale, separate list that was never updated when a later entity was added. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no reference to `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES`/`needsPayments`/`mentionsPayments` to also patch -- same as every other heuristic-provider fix in this file, this logic only runs at spec-generation time. Other domain entities added after the set's introduction (`WorkOrder`, `Course`, `Property`, `Deal`) were checked and found not to be as clear-cut a "this entity's whole purpose is a paid transaction" case as Rental, so the fix was scoped to Rental only rather than broadly re-deriving the list.

**The fix**: added `"Rental"` to `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES`, plus a doc-comment addendum explaining the drift and pointing future rounds at the same risk for any entity added later.

### Round 567: Vehicle's bare "רכב" keyword collided with "רכבת"/"רכבות" (train/trains)

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined in rounds 449-566 (including round 566's just-closed BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES/Rental drift fix, and noting WorkOrder/Course/Property/Deal had already been checked and ruled out for that specific gap). The keyword-collision class in `domainEntities.ts` was explicitly deprioritized (but not disallowed) given 5 straight prior rounds in that shape, with the agent steered toward other classes (stale-derived-value gaps, other producer/consumer drift, identifier-shape/validation gaps, URL/path-encoding gaps, client-side races) as a first pass.

**The finding**: the agent spent most of its effort checking those other classes (localStorage preference cleanup, idempotency.ts, migrate.ts, twin.ts, seed.ts, displayField.ts, backup.ts CSV formatting, various projects.ts/auth.ts routes for TOCTOU races) and found nothing that cleared the bar, then fell back to the keyword-collision class. `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s Vehicle rule's keyword list includes the bare string `"רכב"` ("car"/"vehicle"). This is a literal prefix-substring of `"רכבת"` ("train") and its plural `"רכבות"` ("trains") -- extremely common everyday Hebrew words (Israel Railways is "רכבת ישראל") -- and since `matchesKeyword`/`matchEntities` in `heuristic.ts` matches via plain `lower.includes(kw)` with no word-boundary support for Hebrew (JS's `\b` does not bound Hebrew characters), any Hebrew description about a train/railway business spuriously matched the Vehicle entity.

**Independent verification**: reproduced directly against `matchEntities()` on the real source tree, with no mocking: `"אפליקציה לניהול תחנות רכבת, לוחות זמנים ומעקב אחרי כרטיסי נוסעים."` (an app to manage train stations, schedules, and passenger ticket tracking) returned `["Vehicle"]` -- completely wrong, no car/fleet concept in the description at all. A second description using the plural `"רכבות"` matched the same way. Removing just the train word from the first description dropped the match to the generic default `"Item"` entity, confirming `"רכב"`'s substring match inside `"רכבת"`/`"רכבות"` was the sole cause. Confirmed via `grep` of `docs/roadmap.md` that no prior round (including the two earlier Vehicle-specific fixes, round 450's English "mechanic"/"mechanical" and round 454's English "garage"/"garage sale") ever touched the Hebrew keyword `"רכב"` itself. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no reference to `matchEntities`/`domainEntities.ts` to also patch -- same as every other heuristic-provider fix in this file.

**The fix**: replaced the bare `"רכב"` string with `/רכב(?!ו?ת)/` -- a negative lookahead excluding "רכב" immediately followed by an optional "ו" then "ת" (covering both "רכבת" and "רכבות"), while still matching real usage like "רכב", "רכבים" (vehicles, plural), "ברכב", and "כלי רכב". The redundant separate `"רכבים"` list entry was folded into this one regex (it already matches as a substring, since "רכבים"'s suffix doesn't trigger the lookahead).

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, mirroring this file's established Hebrew-collision test idiom: confirms a train-station description and a trains-plural description do NOT produce a spurious Vehicle entity, then confirms real usage ("רכב אחד", "צי רכבים") still matches Vehicle.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts` in place). The new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (the train description's Vehicle false-positive returned, exactly as the un-fixed repro had shown). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: `heuristic.test.ts` 63/63 (+1), full `@forge/spec-engine` 129/129 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, db 151, api 491, web 887 all unchanged; spec-engine 129 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `6160c88`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects a Hebrew project description about trains/railways/stations, and only when the heuristic provider is in use (no API key, or the Anthropic provider failed).

### Round 568: `extractJson()` mis-extracted well-formed JSON whose own content contained a markdown fence or a leading prose brace -- duplicated and unfixed in both `anthropic.ts` and `debug.ts`

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist covering every mechanism mined through round 567 (including the just-closed Vehicle/"רכב" keyword-collision fix), with the keyword-collision class in `domainEntities.ts`/`heuristic.ts` flagged as a last resort given 20+ prior rounds in that shape. The agent spent most of its effort on other classes (stale-derived-value drift, identifier-shape gaps, URL/path-encoding, client-side races, doc-comment-claims-parity checks) before landing on a different angle: re-examining a candidate a *previous* round had found but talked itself out of filing.

**The finding**: round 533's own survey had fuzzed `extractJson()` in `packages/spec-engine/src/anthropic.ts` (the function that strips markdown fences/surrounding prose from an Anthropic response before `JSON.parse`) and found genuine, reproducible failures -- but declined to file it, reasoning that `debug.ts`'s byte-identical copy of the same function was already "closed" per rounds 531-532's "ALL VERIFIED CORRECT" static-reading sweep, so filing it would just be re-filing an already-closed finding under a different filename. That reasoning doesn't hold: rounds 531/532's verdict came from a human-style *read* of the code, never from running it against adversarial input -- a fundamentally different and stronger methodology, the same distinction round 523 itself established when it first justified fuzzing over reading. Nobody had ever actually run either copy of `extractJson()` against adversarial input, so "closed" was a false negative, and the bug was never fixed in either file.

The bug itself has two independent failure modes, both from the same root cause -- the function never checks whether the whole response is already valid JSON before applying its fence-stripping/brace-slicing heuristics: (1) a well-formed spec whose own entity `description` field legitimately contains a markdown code fence (e.g. a documentation/code-snippet business idea) has that fence matched by the un-anchored fence regex *inside the JSON string value*, extracting pure garbage instead of the real JSON; (2) if the model's response is preceded by so much as one sentence of prose containing a `{`/`}` (e.g. "Note: the schema uses {} for objects. {...real json...}"), the naive `indexOf("{")`/`lastIndexOf("}")` fallback grabs the prose's own brace instead of the real JSON's.

**Independent verification**: read both `anthropic.ts` (lines 136-155) and `debug.ts` (lines 24-43) directly in the current source tree and confirmed the function bodies are still byte-identical to each other and to round 533's description. Copied the exact current function body (not a paraphrase) into a standalone Node script and ran it against both adversarial inputs -- both failures reproduced exactly as predicted, with real `JSON.parse` error messages (`Unexpected token 'j', "js\ncode\n" is not valid JSON` for case 1, `Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 3` for case 2). Confirmed `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is a real, configured Render env var for this deployment (round 522's entry), so `anthropic.ts`'s copy is the real production path, not a theoretical one. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no reference to `extractJson` -- this logic only runs at spec-generation time, same as every other spec-engine fix.

**The fix**: both copies of `extractJson()` now try `JSON.parse(trimmed)` on the whole response first, returning it immediately on success and skipping every heuristic below -- this alone fixes failure mode 1, since the response genuinely is valid JSON as-is and the fence inside the string value is never examined in isolation. For the brace-slicing fallback (only reached when the response isn't already valid JSON and has no markdown fence), replaced the naive first-`{`/last-`}` slice with a loop that tries each `{` occurrence in turn (not just the first) paired with the final `}`, returning the first candidate slice that itself parses as valid JSON -- this fixes failure mode 2, since the prose's own brace fails to parse and the loop advances to the real JSON's opening brace.

**The tests**: two new tests added to each of `anthropic.test.ts` and `debug.test.ts` (four total), mirroring each file's own existing fenced/prose test idioms: one confirms a clean response whose entity `description` contains a markdown code fence still parses correctly (entity name comes through intact), the other confirms a response preceded by brace-containing prose still parses correctly. Both existing fenced-block and prose-around-fence tests in both files continue to pass unchanged, confirming the fix doesn't regress the prior round's own fix for a different shape of the same function.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `anthropic.ts` and `debug.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the four new tests in place). All four new tests failed with the exact predicted mismatches (the same `JSON.parse` errors reproduced above), every other test in both files staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` on both files, then re-ran green: `anthropic.test.ts` + `debug.test.ts` 24/24 combined (+4), full `@forge/spec-engine` 133/133 (+4). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, db 151, api 491, web 887 all unchanged; spec-engine 133 [+4]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `9afb32e`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this affects the real Anthropic-backed spec generator and the Debug Agent's self-healing path whenever a response happens to contain a markdown fence inside its own content or is preceded by brace-containing prose; previously this silently degraded to the heuristic fallback (or, for the Debug Agent, surfaced a confusing raw build failure) with no visible signal about why.

### Round 569: the exported app's `EntityView.jsx` never got round 540's self-referencing relation picker race fix -- it was ported to `EntityPanel.tsx` only

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent was dispatched with an explicit denylist through round 568, with the keyword-collision class once again flagged as a last resort. The brief also noted round 568's own methodology lesson -- a prior round's "ruled out" or "already closed" reasoning is worth re-checking against the real current code rather than skipped past at face value -- as a legitimate way to find a new candidate. The agent checked several other leads (an inert `"admin"`/`"badminton"` keyword collision, `templates.ts`'s spec/specEn parity, `projectPreferenceCleanup.ts`'s purge coverage, `pipeline.ts`'s security-scan hint lists, `codegen.ts`'s URL-encoding posture) and ruled all of them out with direct verification before landing on this port-gap.

**The finding**: round 540 (two rounds before this one) fixed a genuine race in `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`: for a self-referencing relation field (e.g. `Category.parentCategoryId -> Category`), the mount-time `loadRelated` effect and `refresh()` (round 438's own earlier fix) were two independent writers of `relatedRecords[entity.name]`. `refresh()` merges a newly-created record in immediately, but if `loadRelated`'s own fetch for that same entity resolved *after* a fast subsequent create, its stale, pre-creation snapshot wholesale-replaced `relatedRecords`, silently undoing round 438's fix. Round 540's commit (`d2b1dca`) fixed this only in `EntityPanel.tsx` -- unlike virtually every other EntityPanel-family fix in this codebase (rounds 543→544, 545, 546, 551, 552, 553, 556 all explicitly check `codegen.ts`'s duplicate component and port or explicitly rule it out), round 540's own roadmap entry never mentions `codegen.ts` at all. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s `renderEntityViewJsx()` -- the template for every exported standalone app's `EntityView.jsx` -- still had the pre-540 shape: `loadRelated` fetched every `relationTargets` entry including `entity.name` itself, with an unconditional full `setRelatedRecords(Object.fromEntries(entries))` replace, identical to the exact mechanism round 540 found and fixed in the live preview.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s post-540 `loadRelated` effect (lines 932-975) directly to confirm the real fix shape (`isSelfReferencing`/`otherTargets` filtering, merging `prev[entity.name]` back in rather than replacing). Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s `loadRelated` effect (lines 2706-2729, pre-fix) directly and confirmed it had none of that filtering (`grep -n "otherTargets\|isSelfReferencing" apps/api/src/codegen.ts` → zero matches before the fix). Confirmed via `git show --stat d2b1dca` that round 540's commit touched only `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` and `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.test.ts`, never `codegen.ts`. Confirmed the existing adjacent regression test (`codegen.test.ts`, "the exported EntityView's self-referencing relation field picker includes a record created after the panel first loaded") only exercises round 438's mechanism -- it waits for the initial GET to resolve *before* creating the new record, so it never held the initial fetch open long enough to exercise the race, and would not have caught this gap. Confirmed self-referencing relation fields are an established, previously-exercised spec shape in this exact file family (rounds 438, 440, 515, 540 all use the same `Category.parentCategoryId -> Category` shape), so this is reachable by any real exported app with such a field, not a contrived scenario.

**The fix**: ported round 540's exact approach into `codegen.ts`'s `loadRelated` effect -- excludes `entity.name` from the network-fetched targets when self-referencing (`otherTargets`), and when applying results, merges `prev[entity.name]` back in instead of a full replace, making `refresh()` the sole writer of that one slot (as the live preview already does).

**The tests**: one new regression test in `codegen.test.ts`, mirroring `EntityPanel.test.ts`'s own round-540 test technique (holding the initial GET open via a controlled promise, releasing it only after a fast subsequent create has already landed), adapted to the exported app's `/api/Category` fetch URL and `writeGeneratedWebComponent`/`withRealLocalStorage` test harness.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `codegen.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `codegen.test.ts` in place). The new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch ("Office Supplies" vanished from the parent picker's options after the delayed fetch resolved, exactly as the un-fixed mechanism predicted). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: `codegen.test.ts` 181/181 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, spec-engine 133, db 151, web 887 all unchanged; api 492 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `fdc0bf1`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects an exported standalone app with a self-referencing relation field, in the narrow timing window where the entity's own initial page-load fetch resolves after a fast subsequent same-entity create; the newly-created record now stays correctly selectable in every exported app regardless of that timing, matching the live preview's own round-540 fix.

### Round 570: codegen.ts's `fieldFilters` hid every record once its filtered field no longer existed -- a prior round's own "no port needed" reasoning was superseded without revisiting it

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent, denylisted through round 569 (including round 569's own closed port-gap mechanism, with instructions not to re-propose it), spent most of its effort re-checking hypotheses that turned out to already be closed -- including one it nearly re-proposed that round 529 had already live-repro'd and disproven -- before landing on a genuinely new angle: systematically re-examining whether an *earlier* round's own "no codegen.ts port needed" verdict still held up against a *later* round's own established precedent.

**The finding**: rounds 490, 493, and 500 each fixed a sibling bug in `EntityPanel.tsx` -- `viewMode`, `fieldFilters`, and `sortKeys` respectively all failed to re-validate against `entity.fields` after a live refine removed a field they depended on, with `fieldFilters`' own failure mode being the most severe: `visibleRecords`' `Object.entries(fieldFilters).every(...)` check hides **every** record once the filtered field no longer exists on any of them (`r[fieldName]` becomes `undefined` while the stale filter value stays truthy). All three rounds explicitly checked `codegen.ts` and concluded "no port needed," reasoning that the exported app's schema is frozen at export time with no live refine, so the "field removed while mounted" precondition could never occur there. Round 509 (later) found a different, real reachability path for the *same* persisted-state shape (fixing the sibling `hiddenFields` bug): a user loading a newer export of the same project in a browser that still holds an older export's `localStorage` for that origin, keyed only by entity name with no export-version dimension, sees the new export's `entity.fields` against the old export's stale preference entries -- no live refine needed at all. Round 509 applied this reasoning only to `hiddenFields`; rounds 490/493/500's own "no port needed" verdicts were never revisited against it.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s `fieldFilters` state (`useState(() => getPersistedFieldFilters(entity.name))`, no validation against `entity.fields`) and its storage (`FIELD_FILTERS_STORAGE_KEY`, keyed by entity name alone, no export-version dimension) directly, confirming the identical shape round 509 already accepted as a real reachability vector. Confirmed the identical `.every()` filter-hiding logic exists in `visibleRecords`' `useMemo`, byte-for-byte matching the live-preview bug round 493 fixed. Checked the recovery path: `filterableFields` is derived from the *current* `entity.fields`, so the removed field's own filter `<select>` disappears, and the "Clear filters" button's gate (`filterableFields.length > 0 && Object.values(fieldFilters).some(Boolean)`) requires `filterableFields.length > 0` -- if the removed field was the entity's only filterable one, that gate is false too, and there is no in-app recovery at all short of clearing browser storage. Checked `viewMode` and `sortKeys` for the same gap and confirmed both already degrade gracefully at render time (`viewMode==="board"&&boardField` / `==="calendar"&&dateField` fall through to the table view; `sortKeys`' damage is limited to a mis-numbered priority badge) -- real but far less severe, so this round's fix was scoped to `fieldFilters` alone, the one genuinely data-hiding sibling.

**The fix**: added `sanitizeFieldFilters(filters, fields)`, dropping any persisted filter entry whose field name isn't in the entity's current `fields`, applied at both the lazy `useState` initializer and the entity-switch effect that re-reads the persisted value.

**The tests**: one new full-DOM test in `codegen.test.ts`, seeding `localStorage`'s `forge_field_filters` with a filter naming a field ("priority") the test entity doesn't have, then confirming both real records still render instead of the table going empty with no visible cause. Updated one existing source-text regex assertion to match the new wrapped initializer.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `codegen.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping both test changes in place). Both affected tests failed with the exact predicted mismatches (0 rendered rows instead of 2; the regex no longer matching the old unwrapped initializer), every other test staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: `codegen.test.ts` 182/182 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, spec-engine 133, db 151, web 887 all unchanged; api 493 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `3434d6e`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- this only affects an exported standalone app whose browser still holds a stale per-field filter from an older export of the same project after a newer export removed that field, and only once that filter targeted the entity's own only filterable field would it have had no visible in-app recovery; `viewMode`/`sortKeys` remain correctly unfixed in `codegen.ts`, since their own render-time guards already degrade gracefully against the identical stale-value shape.

### Round 571: Vendor's bare `"ספק"` keyword spuriously matched the unrelated "doubt" homograph, not just an unbounded substring like the file's other 25+ Hebrew keyword-collision fixes

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent, denylisted against every entity/keyword already fixed (רכב, מלאי, חיוב, מנוי, מוצר, עובד, כנס, pupil, property, booking, management, checkout, reservation, stripe, donation, garage) and every closed mechanism family (visible-staleness, migrate.ts's collision guard, backup.ts zip-entry-collision), was pointed at several promising new directions -- stale "no port needed" verdicts, old EntityPanel.tsx-only port gaps, producer/consumer drift in other lookup tables, URL-encoding gaps, new client-side races -- and converged independently on a genuinely new angle inside the already-mined keyword-collision class: not a new entity/keyword pair, but a different *shape* of collision within one already-examined entity.

**The finding**: Vendor's bare Hebrew keyword `"ספק"` ("supplier"/"vendor") is a true homograph, not merely an unbounded prefix/suffix substring like every one of the file's prior ~25 Hebrew collision fixes. The identical spelling "ספק" is also the ordinary word for "doubt," used in extremely common filler idioms that have nothing to do with purchasing: "ללא ספק"/"אין ספק"/"בלי ספק" ("undoubtedly"/"no doubt"/"without doubt") and "מוטל בספק" ("in doubt"). Since `matchesKeyword` (`heuristic.ts`) does a plain `.includes()` substring check for string keywords with no Hebrew word-boundary support, any description containing one of these ordinary idioms as filler text spuriously fabricated a whole Vendor entity (name/contactPerson/phone/email/category fields) with nothing to do with suppliers.

**Independent verification**: read the current `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` entry for Vendor directly (`domainEntities.ts`), confirming the bare string `"ספק"` alongside `"vendor"`/`"supplier"`/`"procurement"`/`"ספקים"`/`"רכש"`. Grepped `docs/roadmap.md` for "ספק", "ללא ספק", "אין ספק", "מוטל בספק", and "Vendor" -- confirmed no prior round examined this entity's own keyword list for this collision shape. Wrote a standalone script calling the real `matchEntities` directly (not just reasoning about the code) against `"אפליקציה לניהול משימות לעסק קטן. ללא ספק הצוות שלנו צריך את זה."` (a small-business task-management app description using "ללא ספק" purely as filler) and confirmed it returned `['Employee', 'Task', 'Vendor']` -- Employee and Task correctly matched via "צוות"/"משימות", Vendor spuriously matched via the bare "ספק" substring inside "ללא ספק." Repeated with "אין ספק" and "בלי ספק"/"מוטל בספק" variants, confirming the same spurious match in each case, before designing or writing any fix.

**The fix**: replaced the bare string `"ספק"` in `domainEntities.ts`'s Vendor rule with `/(?<!ללא )(?<!אין )(?<!בלי )(?<!מוטל ב)ספק(?!ות)/` -- negative lookbehinds excluding "ספק" immediately preceded by each of the four known doubt-idiom words (the `"ב"` prefix fuses directly onto "ספק" in "מוטל בספק" with no space, hence `"מוטל ב"` as the excluded prefix), plus a negative lookahead excluding the `"ות"` plural suffix that marks "ספקות" (doubts, plural) -- the same lookahead/lookbehind disambiguation style every one of the file's prior Hebrew substring fixes already uses (rounds 518, 562, 563, 564, 565, 567), just keyed on preceding words rather than suffix/prefix letters since this is a genuine homograph with identical spelling, not a substring-inside-a-longer-word case. `"ספקים"` (suppliers, plural) stays its own unambiguous keyword entry, since that plural never collides with "doubts" (which is "ספקות," a different plural).

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, mirroring the file's established per-collision test shape -- confirms `"ללא ספק"`, `"אין ספק"`, and `"בלי ספק"`/`"מוטל בספק"` (combined in one description) each fail to spuriously match Vendor, while `"ספק"` and `"ספקים"` in genuine supplier-management descriptions still match it correctly.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts`). The new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (Vendor spuriously present where absent was expected) on its first assertion, every other test (63 of 64) staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: `heuristic.test.ts`/spec-engine suite 134/134 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, db 151, api 493, web 887 all unchanged; spec-engine 134 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `09dc627`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- a plain Hebrew description using "ללא ספק"/"אין ספק"/"בלי ספק"/"מוטל בספק" as ordinary filler text no longer fabricates a spurious Vendor entity; real supplier/vendor/procurement descriptions are unaffected. The keyword-collision class remains open in general (per the standing accumulated lesson) -- this round shows it also recurs as a true homograph, not only as a substring-inside-a-longer-word, so future audits of this file's keyword lists should check both shapes.

### Round 572: InsuranceClaim's bare Hebrew keyword `"תביעה"` spuriously matched the generic legal sense of "claim"/"lawsuit" -- a false-start subagent claim was independently caught and corrected first

**The methodology, including a correction mid-round**: the first survey agent dispatched this round proposed MenuItem's bare `"cafe"` keyword colliding with "cafeteria," explicitly claiming it had grepped `docs/roadmap.md` for "cafe"/"cafeteria" and found no hits. Before touching any code, that claim was independently re-run: `grep -ic cafe docs/roadmap.md` returned 4 hits, not 0. Reading them showed this exact pair had already been evaluated and declined twice -- round 454 flagged it as a weaker, lower-confidence runner-up, and round 564's own survey explicitly re-investigated and declined it again with real reasoning ("a cafeteria is itself a real food-service venue that plausibly wants menu/price tracking, unlike the other closed pairs where the colliding word has zero semantic relationship to the entity"). The candidate was discarded without implementation, and a second survey agent was dispatched with this correction plus pointers to round 454's own two still-unverified standing candidates (Project/"projector", Property/"enlisting"). That agent instead surfaced a different, genuinely new finding in the same general keyword-collision class.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s InsuranceClaim rule carried a bare Hebrew keyword `"תביעה"` alongside the correctly-scoped `"תביעת ביטוח"`/`"תביעות ביטוח"` ("insurance claim(s)"). `"תביעה"` alone is simply the ordinary, everyday Hebrew word for "claim" or "lawsuit" in general legal usage ("הגשת תביעה" -- filing a lawsuit, "תביעה אזרחית" -- civil claim), with zero connection to insurance specifically. Unlike this file's many substring-inside-a-longer-word fixes (רכב/מלאי/מוצר/עובד/כנס/מנוי/ספק), this is whole-word genuine polysemy -- the same shape as the already-fixed "property"/"garage"/"pupil" pairs -- so any law-firm or legal-case description that mentioned a client's claim spuriously fabricated an InsuranceClaim entity.

**Independent verification**: read the current keyword array directly, confirming `"תביעה"` sat as a bare string alongside the two correctly-scoped phrases. Ran `grep -n "תביעה\|InsuranceClaim\|insurance claim" docs/roadmap.md` directly (5 hits, none about this collision -- one was the InsuranceClaim status-enum-icon fix from early on, others were unrelated "insurance claim" phrasing in examples) and `grep -n "legal case\|legal matter\|law firm" docs/roadmap.md` (only the line introducing the Case entity originally), confirming no prior round raised or rejected this pair. **The fix**: removed the redundant bare `"תביעה"` keyword entirely, rather than regex-guarding it -- unlike the substring-inside-a-word fixes, there's no narrower pattern to carve out here, and `"תביעת ביטוח"`/`"תביעות ביטוח"` already fully cover every genuine insurance phrasing on their own with no loss of real matches.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, confirming a law-firm/legal-case description using bare `"תביעה"` no longer matches InsuranceClaim, while both `"תביעת ביטוח"` and `"תביעות ביטוח"` in genuine insurance descriptions still do. Checked the existing test suite's own Hebrew insurance test (`"אפליקציה לטיפול בתביעות ביטוח מבעלי פוליסה"`) uses the plural phrase, unaffected by removing the bare singular word.

### Round 573: `findDateField` picked the wrong field in a startDate/endDate pair whenever endDate was declared first, silently losing the whole date range

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent, denylisted against every closed topic through round 572 (including the standing methodology lesson from last round's near-miss on an unverified grep claim), converged on round 454's own two still-unverified standing candidates (Project/"projector", Property/"listing"/"enlisting") as the first lead to chase. Both turned out already fixed (rounds 456-457), so the agent pivoted to a fresh general survey and found a genuinely new gap in a file family -- `entityFormatting.ts`'s date-field heuristics -- that had already been the site of several prior fixes (rounds 101, 383, round 26348's `seedValueFor` fix) but not this particular angle.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s `DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` (`["date", "appointmentdate", "scheduleddate", "eventdate", "duedate"]`) had no `"startdate"` entry, even though its sibling `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` does have `"enddate"`. `findDateField` falls back to `dateFields[0]` -- the first date-typed field in declaration order -- whenever no field name matches a hint. The built-in `Rental` entity (`domainEntities.ts`, fields `startDate` then `endDate`) only ever worked correctly because it happens to declare `startDate` first, purely by luck of field order, not because any hint actually recognized the name. An entity whose JSON declares `endDate` before `startDate` -- equally valid, and with no ordering guarantee for an AI-generated spec -- had `findDateField` silently pick `endDate` as the "start" field, and `findEndDateField` then had nothing left among the remaining date fields to pair it with (returning `null`), since `startDate` isn't in `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` either. The calendar view and `.ics` export would render every record as a single-day event on the booking's end date instead of a real range -- the opposite of the entire feature `findEndDateField` (round 383) was built to provide.

**Independent verification**: read `entityFormatting.ts` lines 631-667 directly, confirming the exact hint arrays and both functions. Ran a direct repro against the real `findDateField`/`findEndDateField` via `npx tsx`: a fields array `[guestName, endDate, startDate]` (text, then date, then date, in that declaration order) returned `findDateField` → `"endDate"` and `findEndDateField` → `null`, while the identical fields reordered to declare `startDate` first correctly returned `"startDate"`. Confirmed the Rental entity's own field order (`domainEntities.ts` line 805 area) declares `startDate` before `endDate`, explaining why this has never surfaced through the built-in domain library. Grepped `docs/roadmap.md` for `"startdate"` (0 hits) and for `"DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS"` (ten hits, none concerning a missing start-date hint or declaration-order dependence -- round 101 fixed an unrelated misspelled `"scheduledat"` hint, and the later hits concern `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS`'s own separate seed-data gap, already closed). Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` carries an identical duplicated copy of both hint arrays and functions (lines 2018-2034, the established live/exported-app duplication convention), with the identical gap, so the exported standalone app has the same bug.

**The fix**: added `"startdate"` to `DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` in both `entityFormatting.ts` and `codegen.ts`, mirroring the existing convention that pairs `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS`'s `"enddate"` entry.

**The tests**: one new test in `entityFormatting.test.ts`, confirming `findDateField` picks `startDate` over `endDate` even when `endDate` is declared first in the fields array, and that `findEndDateField` still correctly pairs the two. A matching new test in `codegen.test.ts`, extracting and evaluating the real generated `findDateField`/`findEndDateField` source from the exported `EntityView.jsx` (not a reimplementation), confirming the identical fix in the exported app.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both `entityFormatting.ts` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping both new tests in place). Both new tests failed with the exact predicted mismatch (`"endDate"` where `"startDate"` was expected) on their first assertion, every other test in both files staying green (144/145 in `entityFormatting.test.ts`, 182/183 in `codegen.test.ts`). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` for both files, then re-ran green: `entityFormatting.test.ts` 145/145 (+1), `codegen.test.ts` 183/183 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, spec-engine 135, db 151 all unchanged; api 494 [+1]; web 888 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `d291122`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- any entity with a `startDate`/`endDate`-style field pair now renders its real date range on the calendar and in `.ics` exports regardless of the order the two fields happen to be declared in, in both the live preview and the exported standalone app.

### Round 574: Employee's bare "staff" keyword spuriously matched "Staffordshire" (the dog breed)

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent, denylisted against every closed topic through round 573 (including the new "asymmetric sibling hint-list" bug class round 573 itself discovered, and an explicit instruction not to re-propose round 454's two standing candidates without re-verifying they're genuinely still broken), was pointed at that new hint-list-asymmetry angle as the first lead. It instead converged on a different, more familiar bug class -- a new instance of the bare-keyword-substring-collision shape this file has now fixed over two dozen times -- this time in a keyword (`"staff"`) that had never been checked before.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s Employee entry (both in `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` and the sibling `ROLE_RULES.Employee`) kept a bare string keyword `"staff"` with no `\b` boundary, right next to the file's own already-`\b`-bounded `"worker"` fix from round 446 (which exists for the identical reason -- "coworker" contains "worker" as a substring). `"staff"` is itself a literal substring of `"Staffordshire"`, the dog breed, so any dog-breeding app description mentioning a Staffordshire Terrier spuriously fabricated both an Employee entity (its own name/role/email/active table) and an Employee role, despite the description having zero HR/staff-management concept.

**Independent verification**: read the exact keyword arrays at both sites directly (`domainEntities.ts` line 170 for the entity rule, line 1310-area for `ROLE_RULES.Employee`), confirming `"staff"` sat as a bare string immediately next to the already-`\b`-bounded `/\bworkers?\b/`. Reproduced directly against the real `HeuristicSpecProvider`: `"An app to track Staffordshire Terrier puppies I breed and sell, including their vaccination records and buyer info."` returned `entities: ['Employee']` and `roles: ['Employee', 'Admin']`; the identical sentence with "Staffordshire" replaced by "dog" returned `entities: ['Item']` and `roles: ['Admin', 'Member']` -- isolating the "staff" substring inside "Staffordshire" as the sole cause. Grepped `docs/roadmap.md` for `"staff"` (case-insensitive) directly, finding only mentions of the already-fixed, different `"worker"`/`"coworker"` collision (round 446) and the unrelated `roles` Hebrew-translation gap (round 517) -- no prior round examined this specific keyword.

**The fix**: replaced the bare `"staff"` string with `/\bstaff\b/` at both sites, mirroring the identical `\bworkers?\b` precedent already sitting next to it in the same two keyword arrays.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, following this file's own established pattern for the `"worker"`/`"coworker"` fix -- confirms a Staffordshire-Terrier-breeding description matches neither the Employee entity nor the Employee role, while a genuine staff-management description ("manage our retail staff and their shift schedules") still matches both.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts`). The new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (Employee spuriously present) on its first assertion, every other test (65 of 66) staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: spec-engine suite 136/136 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, db 151, api 494, web 888 all unchanged; spec-engine 136 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `7860e55`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- a dog-breeding (or any other "Staffordshire"-mentioning) app description no longer fabricates a spurious Employee entity or role; real staff-management descriptions are unaffected.

### Round 575: Event's bare "חתונה"/"חתונות" (wedding/weddings) keywords spuriously matched "תחתונה"/"תחתונות" (lower clothing/underwear)

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent, denylisted against every closed topic through round 574 (including both of round 454's standing candidates already confirmed fixed, and explicitly pointed at the still-open "asymmetric sibling hint-list" class round 573 discovered as a first lead). It audited every paired HINTS array in `entityFormatting.ts`/`codegen.ts`/`displayField.ts`/`whatsapp.ts` and found them all mutually consistent (that class appears fully closed for now), then converged on a new instance of the file's dominant bug class -- a bare Hebrew keyword substring collision -- this time on the Event entity's own `"חתונות"` (weddings, plural) keyword colliding with `"תחתונות"` ("underwear"/"lower clothing," plural), an unrelated clothing term that is literally the same letters with a `"ת"` prefix.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s Event entity kept bare Hebrew keywords `"חתונה"` (wedding) and `"חתונות"` (weddings) with no `\b` boundary (Hebrew has none anyway). Both are literal substrings of `"תחתונה"`/`"תחתונות"` ("lower [clothing]"/"underwear," e.g. the ordinary retail phrase "הלבשה תחתונה" -- lingerie), since each is exactly `"ת"` + the Event keyword, letter-for-letter. The survey agent's own repro caught only the plural collision; independently extending the same check found the singular collides too -- a plain underwear/lingerie-store description, with zero mention of weddings or events, spuriously fabricated an Event entity (its own date/venue/capacity/status fields) purely from this substring, whether the description used the singular or plural clothing term.

**Independent verification**: re-ran the survey agent's own grep claims myself before touching anything -- `grep -n "חתונ\|תחתונ" docs/roadmap.md` (2 hits, both unrelated: an example idea description and an existing test's `SUMMARY`/`DESCRIPTION` content, neither about this collision) and `grep -c "תחתונות\|תחתונים\|panties\|underwear\|lingerie" docs/roadmap.md` (0 hits) -- confirming no prior round examined this pair. Read the exact keyword array directly (`domainEntities.ts` lines 742-753), confirming both bare strings sat right after the file's own already-lookbehind-guarded `"כנס"` fix (round 562) in the same array. Reproduced directly against the real `matchEntities()`/`HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` via `npx tsx`: `"ניהול מלאי של תחתונות"` (manage underwear inventory) returned `['Product', 'Event']`; a fuller realistic description ("חנות הלבשה תחתונה לנשים, עם מעקב מלאי ומחירים" -- a lower-clothing store) returned `['Event']` alone, isolating the singular collision the survey agent hadn't checked; `"תחתונה".includes("חתונה")` and `"תחתונות".includes("חתונות")` both confirmed `true` at the raw-string level. Confirmed genuine wedding/event descriptions using either form still match correctly once the fix was designed.

**The fix**: replaced both bare strings with `/(?<!ת)חתונה/` and `/(?<!ת)חתונות/` -- negative lookbehinds excluding the specific `"ת"` prefix, the same disambiguation approach the file's own adjacent `"כנס"` fix (round 562) already uses in this exact keyword array.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, confirming both a singular ("הלבשה תחתונה") and a plural ("תחתונות וחזיות") underwear/lingerie description no longer spuriously match Event, while genuine singular ("חתונה") and plural ("חתונות") wedding/event descriptions still do.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts`). The new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (Event spuriously present for the singular underwear case) on its first assertion, every other test (66 of 67) staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: spec-engine suite 67/67 in `heuristic.test.ts` (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared, db, api, web all unchanged; spec-engine package total 888/888 [+1] across the whole suite) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `4abb32a`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- a plain underwear/lingerie-store description, singular or plural, no longer fabricates a spurious Event entity; real wedding/event descriptions are unaffected. The keyword-collision class remains open in general -- this round again shows it keeps surfacing in keywords nobody had individually audited yet, on an entity (Event) that had already been the site of one prior collision fix (round 562's "כנס").

### Round 576: Donation's Hebrew keyword "עמותה" (nonprofit) had no plural entry -- a fresh bug shape within the Hebrew-keyword class (missing match, not a false-positive collision), caught alongside a vacuous-test near-miss

**The methodology**: a fresh survey agent, denylisted against every closed topic through round 575 and specifically pointed at round 575's own lesson (check other keywords within entities that already had one collision fix, and check both singular and plural forms), surfaced a genuinely different bug shape within the same general "Hebrew lacks `\b`" family this file has mined for 25+ rounds: not a false-positive substring collision, but a false-negative -- a keyword whose standard Hebrew plural is not textually derivable from its singular at all, so the plural form matched nothing.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s Donation entity carried the bare singular `"עמותה"` (nonprofit) but no plural entry. Every other Hebrew noun pair in this file's keyword arrays (e.g. `"תרומה"`/`"תרומות"` right next to it) forms its plural by appending a suffix, so the singular is always a substring of the plural and a single entry would almost cover both -- but Hebrew's ה→ות plural pattern for this specific noun class replaces the final letter rather than appending to it, so `"עמותה"` is not a substring of `"עמותות"` the way `"תרומה"` is of `"תרומות"`. A description that only used the plural (e.g. describing nonprofit-management software in the plural, a entirely ordinary phrasing) matched no domain entity at all and fell back to the generic `Item` entity.

**Independent verification**: grepped `docs/roadmap.md` directly for `"עמותה\|עמותות\|מוסך\|מוסכים"` myself (2 hits, both unrelated: one about WorkOrder deliberately not sharing Vehicle's keywords, one an unrelated idea string), confirming no prior round addressed this gap. Read the exact keyword array directly (`domainEntities.ts` lines 946-960), confirming the bare singular with no plural sibling. Reproduced directly against the real `matchEntities()` via `npx tsx`: `"מערכת לניהול עמותות"` (plural only) returned `['Item']`; `"אפליקציה לניהול עמותה אחת"` (singular) returned `['Donation']` -- confirming the plural-only description was the one that failed.

**A regression-proof near-miss, caught by the protocol itself**: the first version of the new test used a plural-only sentence that also happened to contain the word `"תרומות"` ("donations"), which already matches Donation independently via an existing keyword -- making the assertion vacuous (it would pass whether or not the fix was applied, exactly the round-477 pitfall the roadmap has warned about ever since). This was caught during the regression-proof revert step itself: reverting `domainEntities.ts` to the pre-fix code and re-running the suite showed the new test passing anyway, which should have been an exact predicted failure. Rewriting the test sentence to drop `"תרומות"` and isolate the `"עמותות"` keyword alone, then re-reverting, produced the correct predicted failure (67 of 68 passing, only the fixed assertion failing) before the fix was restored.

**The fix**: added `"עמותות"` as its own keyword entry alongside the existing `"עמותה"`.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, confirming a plural-only nonprofit description (with no other Donation keyword present) matches Donation, and a singular-only description still matches too.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the corrected test in `heuristic.test.ts`). The corrected test failed with the exact predicted mismatch on its first assertion, every other test (67 of 68) staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: spec-engine suite 68/68 (+1). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, db 151, api 494, web 888 all unchanged; spec-engine 138 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean. Commit `931c045`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- a nonprofit-management description phrased only in the Hebrew plural now correctly fabricates a Donation entity instead of falling back to the generic Item entity; singular descriptions are unaffected.

**Standing backup candidate for a future round (not fixed this round, same bug class, different root cause)**: Vehicle's keyword `"מוסך"` (garage, `domainEntities.ts` line 717) has the identical missing-plural shape for a different Hebrew-morphology reason -- its plural `"מוסכים"` swaps the word-final sofit-kaf (ך) for a regular kaf (כ), a different Unicode character, so `"מוסך"` is not a substring of `"מוסכים"` either. Confirmed via the same grep (0 hits for `"מוסכים"`) and a real repro (`"אפליקציה לניהול רשת מוסכים ברחבי הארץ"` → `['Item']`, plural-only failing the same way). Left open for a future round since this round's scope covered one finding; a one-line fix (adding `"מוסכים"` to Vehicle's keyword array) would close it the same way.

### Round 577: Vehicle's Hebrew keyword "מוסך" (garage) had no plural entry -- the exact standing backup candidate round 576 flagged, fixed with a deliberately non-vacuous test from the start

Its plural `"מוסכים"` replaces the word-final sofit-kaf (ך, used only at the end of a word) with a regular kaf (כ) -- two distinct Unicode characters -- so `"מוסך"` is not a substring of `"מוסכים"` the way most of this file's Hebrew nouns are of their own plurals. A description phrased only in the plural (e.g. describing a network of garages) matched no domain entity and fell back to the generic `Item` entity.

**Independent verification**: re-ran the exact grep round 576 had already run (`grep -n "מוסך\|מוסכים" docs/roadmap.md`) myself before touching any code -- 2 hits, one the round-576 standing-candidate note itself, one an unrelated WorkOrder/Vehicle-keyword-sharing comment, confirming the gap was still genuinely unaddressed. **The fix**: added `"מוסכים"` as its own keyword entry alongside the existing `"מוסך"`.

**The tests**: one new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, written deliberately to avoid round 576's own vacuous-test near-miss from the start -- both test sentences were checked against every other Vehicle keyword ("רכב", "מכונאי", "כלי רכב", "garage", "mechanic", "car dealership") before being finalized, confirming the plural-only sentence isolates "מוסכים" alone with no other keyword present. The new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch on its first assertion -- correctly, not vacuously this time -- every other test (68 of 69) staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: spec-engine suite 69/69 (+1).
