### Round 586: brand-new "Automation Rules" feature's own field_equals trigger could be made to fire on every unrelated edit to an already-matching record, sending duplicate WhatsApp messages

**Context**: between round 585 and this round, שלומי sent a genuine chat request ("upgrade, serious upgrades, use all related skills") that was handled out-of-band -- not as a numbered round -- adding a whole new Automation Rules feature (`packages/db/src/automations.ts`, `apps/api/src/automations.ts`, new routes in `routes/projects.ts`, `apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.tsx`): an if-this-then-that system that can trigger an outbound WhatsApp send when a record is created or when one of its fields transitions to a specific value. That code had unit tests but had never been through an adversarial bug-hunting round. Per round 585's own guidance (missing-plural class too expensive to keep mining without a fresh angle), this round's survey deliberately targeted that brand-new, unaudited surface first instead of opening a new domain blind.

**The methodology**: a fresh Explore survey agent was dispatched specifically at the new Automations feature (matchesTrigger's field_equals semantics, interpolateTemplate's field-type handling, fireRule's destination resolution, the fire-and-forget `void runAutomationsForRecordChange(...)` pattern, and packages/db's cascade-delete coverage), with a documented fallback to a different domain if nothing concrete turned up there.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/automations.ts`'s `matchesTrigger` doc comment promises that a `field_equals` rule only fires on an update when the matching field was genuinely part of that update's own diff -- not merely whenever the record's current value happens to match -- specifically so a rule like "when status becomes Delivered, text the customer" fires once on the real transition, not again on every later unrelated edit. But the route that feeds it the "changed fields" set, `PATCH /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/:recordId` in `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`, computed it as `new Set(Object.keys(req.body ?? {}))` -- trusting that the request body only contains touched fields. `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s main record-edit modal (`startEdit`/`handleSubmit`, the primary edit path used throughout the live app) always submits the entire record object on every save, not a diff. So in practice `changedFields` was "every field on the entity" on every edit through the main form, making the field_equals guard a no-op for the app's most common edit path: a customer whose order already carries `status: "Delivered"` would get a duplicate "your order is delivered" WhatsApp message every time an unrelated field (e.g. a typo in notes) was corrected and saved, for as long as the record stayed in that status. The inline-cell-edit, bulk-edit, and Kanban-drag update paths were unaffected since they already send true per-field diffs (`{ [field]: value }`).

**Independent verification**: read `matchesTrigger`, the PATCH route, `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `startEdit`/`handleSubmit`, and `automations.test.ts`'s own unit tests directly. The unit tests pass because they hand-construct a narrow `changedFields` Set directly, never going through the route -- they verify `matchesTrigger`'s own logic correctly, but never exercised the route's (wrong) diff computation, which is why this had never been caught.

**The fix**: added `computeChangedFields(entity, before, after)` to `routes/projects.ts` -- a pure, independently-testable helper that compares the actual pre- and post-update field values (fetched via the already-exported `getRecord`) rather than trusting which keys the request body happened to include. The PATCH route now calls `getRecord` before `updateRecord` and passes `computeChangedFields(entity, before, record)` to `runAutomationsForRecordChange` instead of the old `Object.keys(req.body)`. This fixes the contract at the one real server-side call site, protecting every current and future caller (not just EntityPanel's form) regardless of whether it submits a diff or a full object.

**The tests**: four new tests for `computeChangedFields` in `apps/api/src/routes/projects.test.ts`, following this file's existing pure-function-testing convention (it has no HTTP-level/supertest tests, only direct unit tests of exported functions) -- covering the exact repro (a full-form resubmit where only one field actually changed), a genuine transition, the no-prior-record case (treats everything as changed, matching "created" semantics), and the fully-unchanged case (empty set).

**Regression-proof**: ran the new tests plus the full `@forge/api` suite (511/511, +4), then the full monorepo suite (db 162, shared 16, spec-engine 147 all unchanged; api 511 [+4]; web 896 unchanged -- note the baseline here already reflects the out-of-band Automations-feature commit between rounds 585 and 586, not round 585's own 494/888 baseline) and `npm run build` (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 538.9kb, web tsc+vite built in 1.02s) -- all clean before commit. Commit `2dceff1`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- WhatsApp automations tied to a `field_equals` trigger now only fire on the real transition, through every edit path, not just the ones that already sent true diffs. The brand-new Automations feature has now had one adversarial round; its other surfaces surveyed and found clean this round include `interpolateTemplate`'s field-type handling and the fire-and-forget error-swallowing pattern in `runAutomationsForRecordChange`/`fireRule` -- a backup candidate was also identified (inconsistent validation between `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`/`UpdateAutomationRuleSchema`: a PATCH can produce an internally-inconsistent rule, e.g. `toMode:"field"` with a still-null `toField`, since the update schema lacks the create schema's cross-field `.refine()`s and `findField` existence checks) but was deliberately left unfixed this round -- it degrades gracefully to a recorded "no destination configured" failure, is unreachable through the current `AutomationsPanel.tsx` UI (which only ever PATCHes `{enabled}`), and is lower-severity than the duplicate-send bug just fixed. A future round can pick it up directly without a fresh survey.

### Round 587: `PATCH /projects/:id/automations/:ruleId` could silently save an internally-inconsistent automation rule -- round 586's own ready backup candidate

**Context**: round 586 closed having already identified and documented this exact gap as a ready backup candidate, so round 587 implemented it directly per the trigger's own stated default -- no fresh Explore survey needed.

**The finding**: `CreateAutomationRuleSchema` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) enforces three cross-field invariants via `.refine()` (field_equals requires fieldName+fieldValue; toMode:"static" requires toNumber; toMode:"field" requires toField), plus the POST handler calls `findField` to confirm `fieldName`/`toField` actually name real fields on the entity. `UpdateAutomationRuleSchema` had none of this -- every one of its fields is `.optional()` (a PATCH only sends what it's changing), so there was no single static shape to run the same `.refine()`s against, and the route passed the raw patch straight to `updateAutomationRule` with no further check. A PATCH of `{"toMode":"field"}` against a rule created with `toMode:"static"` (so `toField` was still `null`) saved successfully, producing a rule that can never resolve a destination -- every future fire would record a "no destination configured" failure instead of ever having been rejected up front.

**The fix**: added `findAutomationRuleInvariantViolation(rule)`, a pure function checking the same three invariants `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`'s `.refine()`s enforce, written to take `string | null` fields (unlike reusing the create schema directly, which expects `string | undefined` and would reject a legitimately-null field on an unrelated rule shape). The PATCH route now fetches the existing rule via the already-exported `getAutomationRule`, computes `next = { ...existing, ...parsed.data }` (the same merge `updateAutomationRule` itself performs internally), runs `findAutomationRuleInvariantViolation(next)` and -- when the trigger/toMode call for it -- the same `findField` existence checks the create route already runs, all before the actual write. The route's pre-existing `NotFoundError` catch around `updateAutomationRule` stays in place as defense-in-depth against a delete racing between the new existence check and the write, the same pattern this file already uses elsewhere for similar races.

**The tests**: five new tests for `findAutomationRuleInvariantViolation` in `apps/api/src/routes/projects.test.ts`, following the file's pure-function-testing convention -- two valid shapes (record_created+static, field_equals+field-destination) returning no error, and three rejections (field_equals missing fieldName/fieldValue, toMode:static missing toNumber, and the exact repro: a record built by applying only `{toMode:"field"}` on top of an otherwise-valid static rule, missing toField).

**Regression-proof**: ran the new tests plus the full `@forge/api` suite (516/516, +5), then the full monorepo suite (db 162, shared 16, spec-engine 147, web 896 all unchanged; api 516 [+5]) and `npm run build` (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 540.1kb, web tsc+vite built in 1.37s) -- all clean before commit. (The first `npm test --workspaces` attempt this round was run with a stray trailing `&` under `run_in_background: true` -- the exact double-backgrounding anti-pattern this process's own notes warn against -- producing a suspiciously short, incomplete log despite reporting exit code 0; caught by comparing line counts against a typical run, and the suite was re-run correctly without the shell `&` to get a trustworthy result.) Commit `56a0ba8`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- an automation rule's `toMode`/`trigger`-dependent fields can no longer be left in a self-contradictory state via PATCH, through the API directly or (once the UI grows past its current `{enabled}`-only PATCH) through `AutomationsPanel.tsx`. The Automations feature has now had two adversarial rounds (586, 587); no further backup candidate specific to it is currently known -- a future round touching this feature again should run a fresh, targeted look rather than assume more low-hanging fruit remains.

### Round 588: entity/field removal never cleaned up automation_rules, letting a stale rule silently resurrect against an unrelated later entity/field that reuses the same name

**Context**: round 587 closed the Automations feature with no further ready backup candidate, so this round opened with a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against missing-plural, domainEntities.ts keyword-collisions as a mined-out class, the visible-staleness family, migrate.ts's collision-guard mechanism, wakeRetry, and the Automations feature's own first two rounds' specific findings (changedFields diff, PATCH cross-field validation) -- while still leaving room to look at Automations again from a genuinely different angle.

**The finding**: the survey's initial repro used `DELETE /projects/:id/entities/:entityName` and `DELETE /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/fields/:fieldName` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`), but independent verification found both routes are gated to `project.status !== "built"` (pre-build spec review only) -- and automation rules can only be created on a *built* project (the automation routes require `project.status === "built"`), so those two specific routes can never actually have a rule to orphan. The real reachable path is `POST /projects/:id/refine` on an already-built project: it regenerates the entire spec via a fresh `generateSpec` call and feeds the result through `diffAndMigrate(db, projectId, previousSpec, nextSpec)` (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`), which is deliberately additive-only -- it already leaves a removed entity's table and a removed field's column in place, by design, for exactly this "a later refine might reuse the name" reason (its own `allKnownEntityNames`/sanitized-collision-guard comments describe this explicitly). But nothing in that same function (or in the checkpoint-restore route, `routes/projects.ts:1075`, the third `diffAndMigrate` call site) ever cross-referenced `automation_rules`. `listAutomationRules`/`listEnabledAutomationRulesForEntity` (`packages/db/src/automations.ts`) have no entity-existence filtering at all, so a dangling rule stayed `enabled` and visible in `AutomationsPanel.tsx` forever, and -- because `deriveEntityName`/`deriveFieldName` (`routes/projects.ts`) only dedupe against names that currently exist in the live spec -- a later refine that reconverges on the same obvious name (quite plausible: an AI regenerating a spec for the same business tends to re-derive the same entity/field names, e.g. "Order"/"status") silently reactivates the old rule against a field/entity it was never actually written for, potentially firing an unrelated WhatsApp send built from a stale template.

**Independent verification**: read every `deleteAutomationRule*` call site (`grep -rn "deleteAutomationRule" apps/api/src packages/db/src`) and confirmed none covers entity/field removal; read all three `diffAndMigrate` call sites (`pipeline.ts` x2, `routes/projects.ts`'s checkpoint-restore route) to confirm the gap is caller-independent; read `matchesTrigger` (`apps/api/src/automations.ts`) to confirm it has zero schema/entity awareness and just blindly reads `record[rule.fieldName]`, so nothing downstream would catch this either.

**The fix**: added `deleteAutomationRulesForEntity(db, projectId, entityName)` and `deleteAutomationRulesForField(db, projectId, entityName, fieldName)` to `packages/db/src/automations.ts` (the latter checked against both `fieldName` and `toField`, since a rule can reference a field either as its field_equals trigger or as a toMode:"field" destination). Both are called from inside `diffAndMigrate` itself (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`), not from the API routes, right after the existing per-entity migration loop: for each `previousSpec` entity no longer in `nextSpec`, every rule on it is deleted; for each surviving entity, every field no longer present has its referencing rules deleted. Fixing it inside `diffAndMigrate` -- the same place the screens-array cleanup for entity removal already lives (round 553's precedent, which this feature's own addition simply never got extended to) -- covers all three call sites (refine, the Debug Agent's retry, checkpoint restore) uniformly, with no route-level duplication. `ensureAutomationRulesTable(db)` is called defensively right before the new cleanup code, since `diffAndMigrate` is also exercised directly in `migrate.test.ts` against a bare `openDatabase(":memory:")` that never goes through `store.ts`'s own centralized table setup -- the idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` costs nothing when the table already exists.

**The tests**: two new tests in `packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts` -- one confirming a whole entity's rules are deleted when the entity is removed, and one confirming a rule is deleted whether it referenced the removed field as its trigger *or* as its destination, while an explicit third rule on a field that survives the same refine is asserted to remain untouched (guarding against a vacuous "every rule on the entity died" false pass).

**Regression-proof**: reverted `migrate.ts` via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests) -- both new tests failed with exactly the predicted assertion (`getAutomationRule` still returning the stale rule), every other test (162 of 164) staying green; restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: `@forge/db` 164/164 (+2). Full monorepo `npm test` (shared 16, spec-engine 147, api 516, web 896 all unchanged; db 164 [+2]) and `npm run build` both clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 541.1kb, web tsc+vite built in 1.09s). Commit `971af4e`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- deleting or renaming an entity/field via Refine (or restoring an older Time Machine checkpoint) now also retires any automation rule that referenced it, instead of leaving it dormant and resurrectable. This is now the Automations feature's third adversarial round (586 changedFields, 587 PATCH validation, 588 this cascade-delete gap) -- each found something genuinely different (trigger-matching, single-rule-consistency, cross-feature schema-drift respectively), so the feature is not yet being treated as mined-out, but a fourth round should bring a clearly new angle rather than re-scanning the same three mechanisms.

### Round 589: calendar .ics export's UID content line left entity.name unescaped, unlike PRODID/SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION in the same file

**Context**: with Automations now past three rounds and no further backup candidate, this round opened with a fresh Explore survey denylisted against every previously-mined pattern. The survey's methodological note from round 588 (verify route/status-guard reachability independently before committing to a repro) proved directly relevant again this round, just in the opposite direction -- a candidate fix this time turned out to be unreachable in exactly one of its two intended locations, caught before it was committed.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/calendarIcs.ts`'s `buildCalendarIcs` builds the `UID:` content line as `` `UID:${entity.name}-${record.id}@forge-ai` `` with no `icsEscapeText` call, unlike every other unbounded TEXT value this same function emits -- `PRODID` already wraps `entity.label` in `icsEscapeText` (round 551, whose own fix comment states label is "exactly as unbounded and user-controlled as UID/SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION"), and `SUMMARY`/`DESCRIPTION` both escape their content. `EntitySchema.name` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) is a bare `z.string().min(1)` with no character restriction actually enforced, and `backup.ts`'s own `sanitizeZipEntryName` comment already documents, for a different downstream construction, that "a project with an entity name containing '/' or similar builds and runs live in this app perfectly normally." An AI-generated spec with a semicolon, comma, backslash, or embedded newline in an entity name (plausible hallucination the system prompt only advises against, never enforces) therefore reaches the UID line unescaped; an embedded newline in particular splits RFC 5545's content-line structure outright, since a bare newline inside a logical line has no continuation-marker leading space.

**Independent verification, including a candidate that turned out wrong**: confirmed via `calendarIcs.test.ts`'s existing tests that nothing exercises an entity name containing these characters feeding into UID, and confirmed no doc comment anywhere marks UID as deliberately exempt from escaping. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app's own generated calendar code) has a byte-for-byte duplicate of the same unescaped `UID:` line, so the fix was initially ported there too and a matching regression test written against the real generated+extracted `buildCalendarIcs` function (the file's own established "extract real generated source via regex, execute via `new Function`" convention). That test failed immediately with `Refusing to export: unsafe entity identifier` -- `codegen.ts`'s own `assertSafe` (`SAFE_IDENTIFIER = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`) rejects any entity name outside plain ASCII identifiers before `generateExportFiles` produces any output at all, making this specific escaping gap categorically unreachable in the exported app: no character `icsEscapeText` would ever need to escape (`;`, `,`, `\`, newline) can pass `assertSafe` in the first place. The codegen.ts fix and its test were reverted rather than kept as "harmless but inert" code, consistent with this process's standing preference for fixes tied to a real, verified reachable path over speculative parity changes.

**The fix**: wrapped `entity.name` in the existing `icsEscapeText(...)` call in `calendarIcs.ts`'s UID line only -- the one place this is actually reachable (the live preview, which has no `assertSafe`-equivalent guard on entity names at calendar-export time).

**The tests**: one new test in `apps/web/src/calendarIcs.test.ts`, right after the existing comma/semicolon/backslash/newline escaping test for SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION -- an entity named `Weird;Name,With\Chars` asserts the UID line shows the fully-escaped form and never the raw unescaped name.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against the full `@forge/web` suite fresh (897/897, +1), then reverted `calendarIcs.ts` via `git checkout --` (keeping the test) -- it failed exactly as predicted, every other test staying green; restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test` (db 164, shared 16, spec-engine 147 all unchanged; api 516 unchanged, confirming the reverted codegen.ts change left no trace; web 897 [+1]) and `npm run build` both clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 541.1kb byte-identical to round 588's, web tsc+vite built in 1.09s). Commit `51d7053`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- an AI-generated entity name containing RFC-5545-significant characters can no longer corrupt a calendar export's UID line. `codegen.ts`'s duplicate line was deliberately left unchanged (confirmed unreachable, not merely untested) -- do not re-propose porting this specific fix there without a new argument for how an unsafe entity name could survive `assertSafe` in that path.

### Round 590: Security scan's `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS` plain-substring "token" hint spuriously flagged "tokenizer"/"detokenize" fields

**Context**: this round implemented the backup candidate already documented at the end of round 589 rather than opening a fresh survey -- `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS` array mixes word-boundary-aware regex hints (`secret`/`Secret` fixed in an earlier round, `ssn`/`SSN` fixed round 459) with five hints still checked via plain `.includes()` substring matching (`password`, `apikey`, `api_key`, `token`, `creditcard`) -- the exact same collision class fixed for `secret` and `ssn` in this same array, left open on these siblings.

**The finding**: of the five remaining plain-substring hints, only `"token"` has a genuine, demonstrable collision: `"token"` is an ordinary English word (like `"secret"`), and `lowerName.includes("token")` also matches `"tokenizer"`, `"detokenize"`, and `"retokenize"` -- real, plausible field names (e.g. a Document/File entity tracking a text-tokenizer setting) that have nothing to do with storing a sensitive token. Confirmed directly: `["password","apikey","api_key","token","creditcard"].some(h => "tokenizer".toLowerCase().includes(h))` returns `true` against the pre-fix array. The other four hints (`password`, `apikey`, `api_key`, `creditcard`) are long, uncommon compound strings with no realistic natural-language or domain-field-name collision -- a search of this app's own built-in domain-entity field-name library (`packages/spec-engine/src/*.ts`) for any field name containing any of these four as a substring returned no matches, and converting them to regexes with no real input able to distinguish old from new behavior would be an unverifiable, speculative parity change rather than a genuine bug fix. Scope was deliberately kept to `"token"` alone for this reason, consistent with this process's standing preference for fixes tied to a demonstrated collision over speculative completeness.

**The fix**: replaced the plain `"token"` string in `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS` with a regex mirroring `secret`'s own shape exactly (both are ordinary words, not acronyms like `ssn`): `/(?:(?<![a-zA-Z])token|Token)(?![a-z])/` -- a lowercase `"token"` only counts at a word start or right after a non-letter separator (`"token"`, `"token_value"`, `"api_token"`), an uppercase `"Token"` is always a valid word start wherever it appears (`"authToken"`, `"apiToken"`), and either form is rejected when immediately followed by a lowercase letter, ruling out `"tokenizer"`/`"detokenize"`/`"retokenize"`.

**The tests**: one new test in `apps/api/src/pipeline.test.ts`, mirroring the existing `secret`/`ssn` tests exactly -- a `Document` entity with `tokenizer`/`detokenize` (must not be flagged) alongside `token`/`authToken`/`token_value` (must still be flagged), asserting exactly 3 warnings.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against the full `pipeline.test.ts` suite fresh (24/24, +1), then reverted `pipeline.ts` via `git checkout --` (keeping the test) -- it failed exactly as predicted (`"an ordinary 'tokenizer' field must not be flagged as looking sensitive"`), every other test staying green; restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` and `npm run build --workspaces` both run clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always).

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- an AI-generated field named "tokenizer" or "detokenize" no longer trips a false "looks sensitive" security warning. `password`/`apikey`/`api_key`/`creditcard` were deliberately left as plain-substring hints (no demonstrated collision risk) -- do not re-propose converting them without a concrete real-word collision example, the same bar `token`/`secret`/`ssn` each met before being fixed.

### Round 591: seed data collapsed two unrelated date fields on the same entity to the identical value

**Context**: with no backup candidate documented from round 590, this round opened with a fresh Explore survey explicitly denylisted against every exhausted pattern (keyword-collision, visible-staleness, migrate.ts collision-guard, SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS, Automations, calendarIcs escaping, etc.). The survey's own framing noted that round 488 had already hardened `packages/db/src/seed.ts`'s date-seeding logic once, for a different gap in the same function.

**The finding**: `seedValueFor`'s `"date"` case (`packages/db/src/seed.ts`) computes its offset from the record index and a single `isEndLike` boolean (whether the field's name matches `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` -- `enddate`/`returndate`/`checkoutdate`/`untildate`/`todate`, round 488's own fix). That boolean only ever distinguishes a *recognized* end-of-range field from everything else -- it says nothing about two date fields that are both unrecognized, i.e. not a start/end pair at all. An AI-generated entity with two ordinary, unrelated date fields (e.g. an Employee's `hireDate` and `birthDate`, or an Order's `orderDate` and `paymentDueDate`) got `isEndLike = false` for both, so both resolved to the exact same `dayOffset` for every seeded record -- every demo Employee was seeded with an identical hire date and birth date. This is a different root cause from round 488 (which widened the *recognized-name* list for genuine start/end pairs) -- here neither field is a start/end pair at all, so no hint-list addition could fix it.

**Independent verification**: read `seedValueFor` directly and traced the arithmetic by hand -- `dayOffset` depends only on `index` and `isEndLike`, never on the field's own identity beyond that one boolean, so any two non-end-like date fields on one entity were mathematically guaranteed to collide at every index. Confirmed the built-in `domainEntities.ts` library doesn't happen to produce this shape today (only Rental's start/end pair exists there), but a freeform `/build` from natural language produces exactly this shape routinely -- two unrelated dates on one entity is an entirely ordinary real-world spec. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicate of `seedValueFor` (same as round 488 found) -- seeding happens once, server-side, so no port is needed.

**The fix**: added `dateFieldOrdinal` -- the field's position among the entity's own `date`-type fields -- and added it to the offset for every non-end-like field: `const dayOffset = isEndLike ? baseOffset - 3 : baseOffset + dateFieldOrdinal;`. A start/end pair's start field always has ordinal 0, so this adds nothing and leaves round 488's existing behavior for recognized pairs completely unchanged; any other non-end-like date field now gets a distinct day based on its position.

**The tests**: one new test in `packages/db/src/seed.test.ts`, right after the existing Rental/Booking end-of-range tests -- an Employee entity with `hireDate`/`birthDate` (neither an end-of-range name) asserts the two dates are no longer equal.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against the full `seed.test.ts` suite fresh (19/19, +1), then reverted `seed.ts` via `git checkout --` (keeping the test) -- it failed exactly as predicted (`"hireDate and birthDate must not collapse to the same day"`, both sides `"2026-10-10"`), with exactly 18/19 passing (only the new test failing, nothing else regressed). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` (db 165 [+1], shared 16, spec-engine 147, api 517, web 897 -- all others unchanged) and `npm run build --workspaces` both run clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 542.0kb, web tsc+vite built in 1.06s). Commit `e29150c`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- an AI-generated entity with two unrelated date fields now gets two genuinely distinct seeded dates instead of an identical one. Round 488's own end-of-range-pair fix is unaffected and still covers its original case correctly.

### Round 592: WhatsApp desktop notification used whatever language was active when the poll effect last (re)started, not the language active when the notification actually fired

**Context**: with seed.ts's date-offset mechanism now having had two genuinely different fixes (488, 591) and no backup candidate documented, this round opened with a fresh Explore survey, denylisted against every exhausted pattern. The survey re-examined a second candidate an earlier round-591 survey had surfaced but not pursued -- a stale-closure gap unrelated to any previously-mined pattern (not the EntityPanel/codegen.ts "visible-staleness" family, which is about field-shape re-validation, not translation state).

**The finding**: `App.tsx`'s WhatsApp unread-poll `useEffect` (the one that drives the topbar badge and desktop notifications) has dependency array `[project?.id, project?.status]`. Its `checkUnread` closure, created once per effect run, calls `maybeNotifyNewWhatsAppMessages(messages, lastNotifiedWhatsAppIdRef, document.hidden, t)` on every interval tick, where `t` is destructured from `useTranslation()` at the top of the component. `LanguageContext.tsx`'s `LanguageProvider` builds `t: (key, params) => translate(lang, key, params)` as a brand-new closure on every render -- bound to whatever `lang` is current at that render -- but the poll effect only re-runs when `project?.id`/`project?.status` changes, not when the user switches the app's language. So a language toggle mid-session (same project, same status) left `checkUnread` calling `maybeNotifyNewWhatsAppMessages` with the *old* `t` for the rest of that session: a desktop `Notification` for a new inbound WhatsApp message, fired while the tab was backgrounded, rendered its title in whichever language was active when the project was opened/reconnected, not the language the user was actually using when the message arrived.

**Independent verification**: read `useTranslation()`/`LanguageProvider` directly and confirmed `t` is reconstructed fresh on every render with `lang` baked into the closure (not read live from a ref). Read the poll effect and `checkUnread` directly and confirmed `t` is referenced only inside that once-per-effect-run closure, never re-captured on a tick. This file already has the identical "read a live value without restarting the poll" problem solved once before, two lines above: `showWhatsAppRef` (round 560) exists so `checkUnread` can read the current `showWhatsApp` state without putting it in the effect's own dependency array (which would otherwise restart the whole `WHATSAPP_UNREAD_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` timer every time the panel opens or closes) -- the same idiom applies directly here.

**The fix**: added `tRef` (mirroring `showWhatsAppRef` exactly): `const tRef = useRef(t); useEffect(() => { tRef.current = t; }, [t]);`, then changed the notify call to pass `tRef.current` instead of the bare `t`. The poll effect's own dependency array is untouched, so a language change still doesn't restart the timer -- it just updates what the next tick reads.

**The tests**: one new test in `apps/web/src/App.test.ts`, right after the existing `checkUnread` suppression test -- using the same established "regex-extract the real `checkUnread` body out of `App.tsx`, execute it via `new Function`" convention this file already uses. ### Round 593: deleting the exact message a WhatsApp notification baseline tracked made a real desktop notification re-announce already-read messages

**Context**: with round 592's stale-`t`-closure fix just applied to a different effect in the same file, this round opened with a fresh Explore survey explicitly told that App.tsx's other effects, migrate.ts, seed.ts's date logic, and Automations had all already been mined for their own distinct angles, and to look for either a genuinely new instance of the "stale closure / missing resync" class elsewhere, or something else entirely. The survey ruled out a long list of other candidates (HistoryPanel/GlobalSearchPanel's own effects, backup.ts's zip-entry sanitization, CSV import/export round-tripping, repository.ts's coerceValue, the account-deletion cascade, CollaboratorsPanel/auth flows, migrate.ts's type/relation-change handling, Business Twin, projectPreferenceCleanup.ts's localStorage sweep) before landing on this one.

**The finding**: `App.tsx`'s independent WhatsApp unread-poll tracks a desktop-notification baseline, `lastNotifiedWhatsAppIdRef`, purely in memory -- advanced every tick to `messages[0]?.id` (the newest message in the page, either direction), with no resync path of its own. `findNewInboundMessages` (`apps/web/src/whatsappNotify.ts`) walks the freshly fetched page looking for that baseline id; if the baseline isn't found at all, it deliberately treats *every* inbound message currently on the page as "new" -- an intentional, tested fallback, but one whose own doc comment and test only ever reason about the page-overflow case (more messages arrived between checks than one page holds). Neither considers the much more ordinary way a tracked id can vanish from the next fetch: the user deleting it. `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s `handleDeleteMessage` (single message) and `handleClearHistory` (whole log) both remove rows immediately and permanently server-side, with no equivalent resync of `lastNotifiedWhatsAppIdRef` at all -- unlike the sibling topbar-badge "last seen" marker (`whatsappUnread.ts`, localStorage), which already self-heals on every `messages` state change via its own effect in `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`. Deleting the single newest message in the log (any direction, even one the user just sent) while the tab is later backgrounded makes the next poll tick's `findNewInboundMessages` call miss the baseline entirely and fire a real OS notification re-announcing older, already-read inbound messages with a misleading count/snippet.

**Independent verification**: read `handleDeleteMessage`/`handleClearHistory` directly and confirmed both delete server-side immediately and update local `messages` state, with no signal of any kind reaching App.tsx's own ref. Read `findNewInboundMessages`'s doc comment and its own existing test (`whatsappNotify.test.ts`, "caps the count... when lastNotifiedId isn't found in it at all") and confirmed both reason exclusively about pagination overflow, never about deletion. Confirmed the badge's own `whatsappLastSeenId` marker is written by a `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` effect keyed on `messages` (so it resyncs after every delete/clear automatically) with no equivalent for the notification baseline.

**The fix**: added two new optional callback props to `WhatsAppPanel`, `onMessageDeleted(id)` and `onHistoryCleared()`, called right after a successful delete/clear. `App.tsx` wires them to null out `lastNotifiedWhatsAppIdRef.current` -- for a single delete, only when the deleted id matches the tracked baseline; for clear-history, unconditionally. Setting the ref to `null` reuses `findNewInboundMessages`'s own existing, already-tested "null baseline = no notification, just silently re-seed" path (the same one a fresh project reconnect already relies on), rather than inventing new semantics.

**The tests**: two new tests in `apps/web/src/WhatsAppPanel.test.ts`, right after the existing per-message-delete tests, following that file's established full-render (`@testing-library/react` + mocked `fetch`) convention -- one clicks the delete button and asserts `onMessageDeleted` fires with exactly the deleted message's own id, the other clicks "Clear history" and asserts `onHistoryCleared` fires exactly once.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against the full `WhatsAppPanel.test.ts` suite fresh (37/37, +2), then reverted `App.tsx` and `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` via `git checkout --` (keeping the tests) -- both failed exactly as predicted (`onMessageDeleted` never called; `onHistoryCleared` count stayed `0`), with exactly 35/37 other tests staying green. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` (db 165, shared 16, spec-engine 147, api 517 -- all unchanged; web 900 [+2]) and `npm run build --workspaces` both run clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 542.0kb byte-identical to round 592's, web tsc+vite built in 2.32s). Commit `b469463`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- deleting a message, or clearing a WhatsApp conversation's whole history, can no longer trigger a misleading desktop notification re-announcing already-read messages.

### Round 594: record creation (`POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName`) was never wrapped in the idempotency guard every sibling mutating route already got

**Context**: with rounds 592-593 both having mined App.tsx's WhatsApp mechanism for distinct staleness angles and no backup candidate ready, this round opened with a fresh Explore survey covering a different area entirely. The survey landed on `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md` (round 470's design doc) and its own "Full inventory of mutating routes" section as a place worth re-checking against the routes that inventory actually led to being fixed (rounds 471-474, 528).

**The finding**: the design doc's inventory lists `POST /projects`, `/from-template`, `/clone`, `/roles`, `/assumptions`, `/entities` (add spec-entity), and `/entities/:name/fields` (add field) as the unguarded-insert routes needing `withIdempotency()` -- all seven converted across rounds 471-474. It never mentions `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName`, the actual end-user record-creation route (e.g. adding a new Customer/Order/Courier row), even though that route calls `insertRecord()` directly with no guard at all, the exact same unguarded-insert shape every one of the seven listed routes was flagged and fixed for. `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `createRecord()` -- the client function this route serves -- also never sent an `X-Idempotency-Key` header, unlike its 8 sibling functions (`createProject`, `cloneProject`, etc.) that already do. A connection dropped after the server fully inserts a real record but before the response reaches the browser makes `fetchWithWakeRetry` (`apps/web/src/wakeRetry.ts`) resend the identical POST, and with no guard on either end, that created a genuine duplicate record the user never asked for.

**Independent verification**: re-verified the subagent's report myself before touching any code, by directly reading: `createRecord`'s exact header list in `api.ts` against its 8 siblings; every `withIdempotency` call site in `routes/projects.ts` via grep; the original `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName` handler in full; `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`'s inventory section in full (confirming the route is genuinely absent, not just unlisted by omission); `idempotency.ts`'s complete `withIdempotency` implementation (the `{status, body}` contract, the cached-replay short-circuit, the throw-cleans-up-and-rethrows error path); and the sibling `POST /projects/:id/entities` (add spec-entity) route as the exact pattern to mirror.

**The fix**: wrapped the route's `insertRecord()` call (plus its `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` → `INVALID_RELATION_TARGET` translation) in `withIdempotency(db, idempotencyKey, req.userId!, \`POST /projects/${project.id}/entities/${entity.name}\`, async () => { ... })`, mirroring the add-spec-entity route exactly, including interpolating the real project id and entity name into the route string per round 528's own lesson (a bare route template would wrongly collide across different projects/entities). The fire-and-forget `runAutomationsForRecordChange` call was deliberately moved to fire *inside* the `run` callback, before the `return`, so a replayed/cached retry doesn't re-trigger the automation (e.g. a WhatsApp send) a second time -- the same "guard the side effect, not just the response" principle `insertRecord` itself benefits from in the same callback. Added `headers: { "x-idempotency-key": crypto.randomUUID() }` to `createRecord` in `apps/web/src/api.ts`, matching the file's own established pattern.

**The tests**: one new test in `apps/api/src/app.test.ts`, mirroring the existing `/entities` (add spec-entity) idempotency test's structure combined with the existing relation-target test's build+record-creation setup: builds a courier-delivery project, creates a Courier record with a fixed `X-Idempotency-Key`, retries the identical POST with the same key, and asserts the retry returns the exact same record id and an identical response body -- then confirms via the entity's own GET-records list that exactly one new row was inserted (accounting for the build pipeline's own seeded sample records, which the test captures as a baseline count first rather than assuming zero).

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current code fresh (171/171 api tests green). Backed up `routes/projects.ts` and `api.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted: the retry returned a genuinely new record id (`4 !== 3`) instead of replaying the first (170/171, only the new test failing, nothing else regressed). Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (171/171).

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. No action needed from שלומי -- adding a new record to any entity (Customer, Order, Courier, or any other) is now protected the same way every other mutating action already was against a flaky connection causing a duplicate.

### Round 595: an automation rule's `field_equals` trigger accepted any free-text value with no validation against the field's real type, silently creating a permanently-dead rule

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 595, this round opened with a fresh Explore survey instructed to avoid every already-exhausted bug class (keyword-collision, visible-staleness, migrate.ts's collision-guard, the withIdempotency inventory, codegen.ts port-gaps, Automations rounds 586-588) and to look at mechanisms with little or no prior attention.

**The finding**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s "Value" input for a `field_equals` rule is a plain `<input type="text">` regardless of the selected field's type -- no checkbox for boolean, no `<select>` of `enumValues` for enum. Neither `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`/`UpdateAutomationRuleSchema` nor `findAutomationRuleInvariantViolation` (round 587) check `fieldValue`'s *content* against the field's type -- only that it's non-empty and that `fieldName` names a real field. `matchesTrigger` (`automations.ts`) then compares with a byte-exact `String(actual) === rule.fieldValue`, with no normalization. For a boolean field, `rowToRecord` always yields a real JS boolean, so `String(actual)` is always exactly `"true"` or `"false"` -- typing "yes", "1", or "כן" (all natural things to type) creates a rule that can mathematically never fire, for any input a user would plausibly type other than those two exact strings. Same gap for an enum field whose typed value doesn't exactly match one of `field.enumValues`. `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s own "Last run: never" is indistinguishable from "hasn't happened yet," so the user has no way to discover the rule is dead.

**Independent verification**: confirmed directly by reading `matchesTrigger`'s exact comparison (`automations.ts` line 50), `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`/`UpdateAutomationRuleSchema`/`findAutomationRuleInvariantViolation` in full (confirming presence-only checks, no content validation), the "Value" input's JSX in `AutomationsPanel.tsx` (confirming it's unconditionally `type="text"`), and repository.ts's own `coerceValue` boolean/enum checks (the established convention to mirror). Checked `docs/roadmap.md`'s rounds 586-588 to confirm this is a 4th, distinct root cause: 586 fixed re-firing timing, 587 fixed cross-field *presence* invariants, 588 fixed cascade-delete on removal -- none validate `fieldValue`'s content against the field's type.

**The fix**: added `validateAutomationFieldValue(field, fieldValue)` in `routes/projects.ts`, right next to `findField`, mirroring `coerceValue`'s own boolean (`must be "true" or "false"`) and enum (`must be one of: ...`) checks exactly, including the same error message style. Called it from both the `POST .../automations` create route and the `PATCH .../automations/:ruleId` update route, right after each already-existing `findField(entity, fieldName)` call (previously its return value was discarded) -- the PATCH route validates the same merged `next` state `findAutomationRuleInvariantViolation` already validates, so a PATCH that only changes `fieldValue` (keeping an existing `fieldName`) is checked too.

**The tests**: one new test in `apps/api/src/app.test.ts`, building an appointment-management project (Employee's boolean `active` field, Appointment's enum `status` field) and asserting: a boolean rule with `fieldValue:"yes"` is rejected 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`; the literal `"true"` is accepted 201 (not a blanket rejection of booleans); an enum rule with a lowercase/mistyped value is rejected 400; and a PATCH re-pointing an existing rule's `fieldValue` to `"yes"` is rejected the same way.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current code fresh (172/172 api tests green). Backed up `routes/projects.ts`, reverted via `git checkout --` (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (the bad-boolean rule creation returned `201` instead of `400`), 171/172 nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (172/172). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` (db 165, shared 16, spec-engine 147 -- all unchanged; api 519 [+1]; web 900 unchanged) and `npm run build --workspaces` both run clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 543.1kb, web tsc+vite built in 2.40s). Commit `83d2ee7`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A `field_equals` automation rule whose value can never match the field's real stored type (a boolean typo, an enum mismatch) is now rejected with a clear error at creation/update time, instead of saving successfully and silently never firing.

### Round 596: checkpoint restore ("Time Machine") permanently lost an automation rule that round 588's own cascade-delete had hard-deleted, contradicting `diffAndMigrate`'s own documented "always safe to restore" guarantee

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 596, a fresh Explore survey was instructed to avoid every already-exhausted bug class, including a fourth angle on Automations (586 timing, 587 presence-invariants, 588 cascade-delete, 595 value-type validation) unless clearly distinct from all four. The survey found a cross-feature interaction between round 588's own fix and Time Machine that neither feature's own prior rounds had examined.

**The finding**: `diffAndMigrate` (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`)'s own doc comment describes it as additive-only: "creates tables... ADD COLUMN... Never drops or renames anything, even if a field or entity was removed... consistent with... Time Machine checkpoints always being safe to restore." Round 588 added the one real exception: when an entity/field present in `previousSpec` is absent from `nextSpec`, it called `deleteAutomationRulesForEntity`/`deleteAutomationRulesForField` (`automations.ts`), a genuine `DELETE FROM automation_rules`. The checkpoint-restore route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` line 1096) calls the same `diffAndMigrate(db, project.id, project.spec, checkpoint.spec)` -- the project's *current* spec as `previousSpec`, the checkpoint being *restored* as `nextSpec`. Nothing in that direction recreates a deleted row: refine away an entity (its rule is hard-deleted), then restore an earlier checkpoint that still has the entity, and the entity comes back but its automation rule does not -- silently, with no warning anywhere (`describeMigrationHazards` has no variant for it) -- directly contradicting the function's own stated contract.

**Independent verification**: confirmed directly by reading `deleteAutomationRulesForEntity`/`deleteAutomationRulesForField`'s own `DELETE` SQL, `diffAndMigrate`'s loop (only walks `previousSpec.entities`, so nothing fires when an entity reappears in `nextSpec`), the checkpoint-restore route's exact `diffAndMigrate` call and argument order, and `diffAndMigrate`'s own doc comment stating the additive-only/safe-to-restore contract. Confirmed via grep that these two functions have exactly one call site each (inside `diffAndMigrate`), so the fix has no other callers to consider. Checked `docs/roadmap.md`'s own Automations/Time Machine entries to confirm this cross-feature interaction was never examined by either feature's own prior rounds.

**The fix**: renamed `deleteAutomationRulesForEntity`/`deleteAutomationRulesForField` to `disableAutomationRulesForEntity`/`disableAutomationRulesForField` and changed their SQL from `DELETE` to `UPDATE automation_rules SET enabled = 0, updatedAt = ? WHERE ...`. The row (and its own history -- `lastTriggeredAt`/`lastStatus`/`lastError`) survives; `listEnabledAutomationRulesForEntity` already filters `enabled = 1` so a disabled rule still can't fire, matching current behavior exactly, but `listAutomationRules` (used by `GET /projects/:id/automations`) returns all rows regardless of `enabled`, so the rule stays visible and re-enable-able through the existing PATCH route and `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s own enable/disable toggle once the entity/field it references comes back.

**The tests**: updated round 588's own two tests in `migrate.test.ts` to assert `enabled === false` instead of `getAutomationRule(...) === undefined` (the row no longer disappears). Added one new test reproducing the full two-step sequence through `diffAndMigrate` itself (not just the disable in isolation): refine away an entity with a rule on it (rule disabled, confirmed), then call `diffAndMigrate` again in the restore route's own argument order to bring the entity back, and assert the rule still exists with its original `entityName`/`fieldName` intact.

**Regression-proof**: ran all three against current code fresh (166/166 db tests green, +1). Backed up `automations.ts`/`migrate.ts`/`index.ts`, reverted via `git checkout --` (keeping the updated/new tests) -- failed exactly as predicted: both updated tests threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'enabled')` (the hard-deleted row no longer exists) and the new restore test failed the same way before even reaching its own restore step, 26/29 nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (166/166). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` (shared 16, spec-engine 147, api 519 -- all unchanged; web 900 unchanged) and `npm run build --workspaces` both run clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 543.2kb, web tsc+vite built in 2.97s). Commit `07d876b`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. An automation rule whose entity/field is removed by a refine is disabled, not destroyed -- a later Time Machine restore that brings the entity/field back now also brings the rule back, interactable and re-enable-able, matching the guarantee `diffAndMigrate`'s own doc comment already made for every other kind of spec-adjacent state.

### Round 597: an automation rule's WhatsApp destination field (`toField`) had no type restriction, letting a date/enum value flow into a real WhatsApp send attempt instead of being rejected at rule-save time

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 597, a fresh Explore survey was instructed to avoid a 5th angle on Automations unless clearly distinct from all four prior rounds (586 timing, 587 presence-invariants, 588 cascade-delete, 595 trigger-fieldValue-type-validation, 596 restore-interaction). The survey found a genuinely new mechanism: the destination field's *type*, not the trigger's typed-in value.

**The finding**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s `toField` `<select>` (for a `toMode:"field"` rule) lists every field of the chosen entity with zero type filtering -- date/enum/number/boolean/relation fields alongside the intended text/longtext phone field, and even auto-defaults to `selectedEntity.fields[0]` on entity change. The create/update routes (`routes/projects.ts`) only ever called `findField(entity, toField)` -- existence only, never type, unlike `fieldValue`, which round 595 added real type validation for. `fireRule`'s (`automations.ts`) own `typeof to !== "string"` guard catches `number`/`relation`/`boolean` destination fields (each becomes a real non-string JS value via `rowToRecord`), but `date` and `enum` fields are stored as plain strings (`repository.ts`'s `coerceValue`) and sail straight through: a date value like `"2024-01-15"` strips to `"20240115"` via `normalizePhone`, and -- critically -- has zero leading zeros, so round 506/507's own `missing_country_code` heuristic (which only catches exactly one leading zero) doesn't catch it either. The stripped digits reach `WhatsAppWebManager.sendMessage`'s real `sock.sendMessage` call with a nonsensical JID, attempting a genuine outbound send instead of being rejected when the rule was saved.

**Independent verification**: confirmed directly by reading `fireRule`'s exact `to = record[rule.toField]` line and its `typeof` guard, `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s `toField` JSX (confirming no type filtering), both automation routes' `findField`-only check on `toField`, `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` (confirming date/enum are both stored as plain strings), and `WhatsAppWebManager.sendMessage`'s full `missing_country_code` leading-zero heuristic (confirming `"20240115"`'s zero leading zeros slips past it). Grepped `docs/roadmap.md` for every `toField` mention -- only round 587's unrelated presence-invariant note (`toMode:"field"` requiring a non-null `toField`, never its type) -- confirming this angle was never examined.

**The fix**: added `validateAutomationToField(field)` in `routes/projects.ts`, right after `validateAutomationFieldValue`, rejecting with a clear `VALIDATION_ERROR` unless `field.type` is `"text"` or `"longtext"` -- the only types that can plausibly hold free-text phone-number data. Called from both the create and update automation routes, wrapping the existing `findField(entity, toField)` call.

**The tests**: one new test in `apps/api/src/app.test.ts`, building an appointment-management project (Appointment's `date` field, Customer's enum `status` field, Customer's text `phone` field) and asserting: a `toField:"date"` rule is rejected 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`; a `toField:"status"` (enum) rule is rejected 400; a `toField:"phone"` (text) rule is accepted 201 (not a blanket rejection of `toMode:"field"`); and a PATCH re-pointing an existing rule's `toField` to the enum field is rejected the same way.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current code fresh (api green). Backed up `routes/projects.ts`, reverted via `git checkout --` (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (the bad-date `toField` rule creation returned `201` instead of `400`), 172/173 nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (api 520, +1). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` (db 166, shared 16, spec-engine 147 -- all unchanged; web 900 unchanged) and `npm run build --workspaces` both run clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 543.6kb, web tsc+vite built in 1.48s). Commit `2d71bff`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A `toMode:"field"` automation rule whose destination can never genuinely hold a phone number (a date, an enum, any non-text field) is now rejected with a clear error at rule-save time, instead of saving successfully and later attempting a real WhatsApp send to a nonsensical number.

### Round 598: "Print list" silently dropped a hidden column's data, unlike Export CSV and per-record Print on the exact same hidden field

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 598 (Automations had already had 5 rounds, 586-588 and 595-597), a fresh Explore survey was instructed to look at areas outside every exhausted pattern (visible-staleness, migrate.ts's collision guard, domainEntities.ts keyword-collisions without a concrete new instance, the deliberately-deferred wakeRetry /refine implementation). It found a genuinely new finding in the print feature, distinct from the visible-staleness *record*-set bugs (rounds 485-487, 499) already mined there -- this one is about the *field* set, not the record set.

**The finding**: `EntityPanel.tsx` computes `orderedFields` (all of `entity.fields`, reordered by the user's column drag order) and `visibleFields` (`orderedFields` further filtered by `hiddenFields`, the Columns-menu's hide list). The file's own doc comment, right above `visibleFields`, states CSV export and the print sheet "intentionally ignore this and always include every field, since those are whole-record actions, not 'what's currently on screen'" -- and `handleExportCsv`/`handleCopy` (`recordsToCsv(entity.fields, ...)`) and the per-row `RecordPrintSheet` (`entity.fields.map(...)`) both honor this correctly. But the toolbar's "Print list" action (`RecordListPrintSheet`) was passed `fields={visibleFields}` instead -- the one hidden-filtered list the comment says must never reach a whole-record action. Since `RecordListPrintSheet`'s `fields` prop drives both the `<thead>` header and every row's `<td>` cell, a hidden field's data doesn't just render blank -- it's never read into the print sheet at all. The identical bug was duplicated in `codegen.ts` (the exported app's own copy of the feature), which read `entity.fields` correctly for its own CSV export and per-row print, but also passed `visibleFields` to its `RecordListPrintSheet`.

**Independent verification**: confirmed via direct line-by-line reading of both files -- `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `orderedFields`/`visibleFields` definitions and doc comment, its `RecordListPrintSheet` call site (passing `visibleFields`), its CSV export and per-row print call sites (both using `entity.fields`), and `RecordListPrintSheet`'s own body (`fields.map` drives both header and cells, no fallback). Same confirmed in `codegen.ts`. `git log -S"intentionally ignore this" -- apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` traced the rule to commit `533f3d4` (round 138, the Columns menu's own introduction) -- predating `RecordListPrintSheet` entirely, which round 229 added later without noticing the rule applied to it too. Grepped both test files for any existing "hidden column + Print list" coverage -- none; the only Columns-menu test never touches print/CSV, and the only Print-list tests never touch the Columns menu.

**The fix**: changed both `RecordListPrintSheet` call sites from `fields={visibleFields}` to `fields={orderedFields}` (keeping the user's column *order*, which is harmless for print layout, while restoring every field's *data*) -- in `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`. Updated both files' doc comments above `visibleFields` to explicitly name `RecordListPrintSheet` alongside the per-record sheet and CSV export as a whole-record action, so a future reader doesn't reintroduce the same drift.

**The tests**: one new test in each of `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts`, both following the same shape -- hide the Status column via the Columns menu, confirm it's genuinely gone from the on-screen table (mirroring the existing Columns-menu test's own assertion), then open Print list and confirm the same hidden column's header and data (the enum's translated label, e.g. "Won"/"הצליח") are still present in `.print-list-sheet`, proving Print list matches CSV export and per-record Print's behavior on the identical hidden field rather than the on-screen table's.

Backed up `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests) -- both failed exactly as predicted (Status column genuinely absent from the printed sheet's text), nothing else regressed (121/122 and 183/184). Commit `85b8b73`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. "Print list" now includes every field of the record, matching the "whole-record action" rule its own neighboring CSV export and per-record Print already follow -- hiding a column from the on-screen table no longer silently removes that column's data from a printed handout.

### Round 599: dragging a ranged calendar record's chip from any day OTHER than its own start day silently relocated the booking's start to the drop target, ignoring the day actually dragged

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 599 (Automations exhausted at 5 rounds, Print feature just closed at round 598), a fresh Explore survey was instructed to avoid every exhausted pattern (visible-staleness, migrate.ts's collision guard, Automations, Print, domainEntities.ts without a concrete new instance) and look at areas not recently covered. It found a genuinely new mechanism in the calendar's drag-to-reschedule feature -- a different bug class from any of the "set"-asymmetry or validation-gap patterns mined so far.

**The finding**: `buildCalendarMonth` deliberately renders a ranged record (one with both a start and end date field, e.g. Rental's `startDate`/`endDate`) into every day cell it spans -- a 5-night stay's chip shows up on all 5 nights, intentional and already covered by existing ICS-export tests (round 503). Every one of those chip instances is identically `draggable`, and the chip's own `onDragStart` only ever stored the record's `id` in `dataTransfer` -- nothing distinguishing which day of the span a particular chip instance represented. The day cell's `onDrop` looked the record up by id and always called `handleCalendarDrop(record, dateFieldName, droppedDay)`, which unconditionally set the record's start field to the dropped-on day and shifted the end field by `droppedDay - record's actual stored start` to "preserve duration" -- correct only when the dragged chip happened to be the start day's own instance. Dragging the chip shown on any other day (e.g. the stay's last night, the natural thing to grab to nudge a booking) produced a result with no relationship to the day actually under the cursor: the start silently jumped to wherever the chip was dropped, and the end shifted by a delta measured from the record's unrelated original start -- not from the day that was dragged.

**Independent verification**: confirmed via direct reading of `handleCalendarDrop` (its `deltaDays = date - oldStart`, never referencing which day's chip triggered the drop), the chip's `onDragStart` (`dataTransfer.setData("text/plain", String(record.id))`, no day information at all), and the day cell's `onDrop` (looks up the record by id, calls `onReschedule(record, day.date)` regardless of origin). Confirmed the chip is rendered identically for every day in `day.records` with no per-day distinction in `draggable` or `onDragStart`. Traced the design assumption to round 383's own doc comment ("dragging only the start day while leaving endDate untouched could push start past end") -- an assumption the UI itself doesn't enforce, since the identical chip is draggable from every day of the span. Grepped `docs/roadmap.md` for `handleCalendarDrop`/"ranged record" -- only round 383 (introduced the duration-preserving shift, assumed start-day-only dragging) and round 522 (a clean survey round that looked at this function but reported no finding) ever touch it; neither examined dragging from a non-start day. Confirmed via `EntityPanel.test.ts`/`codegen.test.ts` that the only calendar-drag tests use a single-date `Appointment` entity (no end field, so the bug can't manifest) and the only ranged-record calendar test (round 503's ICS dedup) never drags anything.

**The fix**: the dragged chip's own origin day is now carried through `dataTransfer` alongside the record id (`${record.id}|${dayKey}`), threaded through `onDrop` → `onReschedule` → `handleCalendarDrop` as a new `originDay` parameter. `handleCalendarDrop` now computes the shift delta from `droppedDay - originDay` (falling back to the record's own stored start when no origin is available, e.g. a non-ranged entity, where this is always already the start day by construction), and applies that same delta to **both** start and end fields -- shifting the whole range by exactly the days dragged, whichever day of the span was grabbed, instead of always re-anchoring start to the drop target. The no-op guard (dropping a chip back where it came from) now compares against the actual origin day rather than the record's stored start, so it correctly no-ops for a non-start-day chip dropped back on its own day too. Fixed in both `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` (live preview) and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (exported app) -- the latter needed its new `` `${record.id}|${dayKey}` `` dataTransfer line escaped (`` \`\${record.id}|\${dayKey}\` ``) since that whole component is itself embedded inside codegen.ts's own outer template literal, the same convention its sibling ICS-generation code already uses.

**The tests**: one new test in each of `EntityPanel.test.ts` (a real DOM drag-and-drop simulation: a 3-night Rental stay, dragging the specific chip instance rendered on the last night forward by one day, confirming the real PATCH shifts both start and end by exactly one day) and `codegen.test.ts` (a direct extraction-and-execution test calling the generated `handleCalendarDrop` with an explicit `originDay` not equal to the record's stored start, confirming the same shift, plus a same-origin-day no-op check). Three pre-existing codegen.test.ts assertions (the chip's `onDragStart` regex, the `onReschedule`/`handleCalendarDrop` signature regexes, and the no-op-check regex) were updated to match the new 4-parameter signature and dataTransfer format -- the underlying call/assertion semantics otherwise unchanged.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code fresh -- EntityPanel.test.ts 123/123, codegen.test.ts 185/185, both green. Backed up `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new/updated tests) -- EntityPanel.test.ts failed exactly as predicted (the real PATCH body showed `startDate`/`endDate` both jumping to match the old anchor-to-drop-target bug, not shifting by the dragged delta), 122/123 nothing else regressed; codegen.test.ts failed its 3 updated regex/extraction assertions exactly as predicted (old 3-param signature and dataTransfer format), 182/185 nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green: db 166, shared 16, spec-engine 147 (all unchanged), api 522 (unchanged from round 598), web 902 (+1). `npm run build --workspaces` clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 544.7kb, web tsc+vite built in 1.42s). Commit `244db14`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Dragging any day's chip of a multi-day calendar record now shifts the whole booking by the exact number of days dragged, matching how a real calendar app's multi-day event drag behaves, instead of silently relocating the booking's start to wherever the chip happened to be dropped.

### Round 600: POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/automations (create automation rule) was the one insert route left with no idempotency guard, letting a lost-response retry create a duplicate rule that then double-sends on every subsequent real trigger

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 600 (Automations exhausted at 6 rounds across 586-588/595-597, Print closed at 598, calendar drag closed at 599), a fresh Explore survey was instructed to avoid every exhausted pattern and look at areas not recently covered. It found that Automation Rules -- added out-of-band between rounds 585 and 586, after `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`'s own inventory of mutating routes (round 470) was written -- was never cross-referenced against that inventory, and its create route was the one insert left completely unguarded.

**The finding**: every other real-effect POST in `routes/projects.ts` (`/projects`, `/from-template`, `/clone`, `/answers`, `/roles`, `/assumptions`, `/entities` add-entity, `/entities/:name/fields` add-field, and `/entities/:entityName` record creation added in round 594) reads an `X-Idempotency-Key` header and wraps its insert in `withIdempotency(...)`. `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/automations` called `insertAutomationRule(db, ...)` bare, with no guard at all -- and `packages/db/src/automations.ts`'s `insertAutomationRule` does a plain `INSERT` with a random UUID primary key, no content-based uniqueness constraint. Worse, `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `createAutomationRule` sent no `X-Idempotency-Key` header at all, unlike all 8 of its sibling creation functions -- so even a server-only guard wouldn't have helped the real client. A response lost in transit after the rule was already inserted (the exact `fetchWithWakeRetry` retry-on-any-thrown-fetch-error scenario rounds 471-474/594 exist for) would resend the identical POST and insert a second, fully duplicate rule. Since `runAutomationsForRecordChange` fires every enabled rule on an entity independently with no dedup across rules of identical content, the next real trigger (e.g. an Order's `status` becoming `Delivered`) would send the same WhatsApp message twice, permanently, until the user noticed and manually deleted the duplicate -- arguably worse than round 586's re-firing bug, since this duplicates the rule object itself rather than re-firing a single rule on unrelated edits.

**Independent verification**: confirmed directly by reading the route handler (`routes/projects.ts`, the automation-rule-create route -- bare `insertAutomationRule` call, no `withIdempotency`), `api.ts`'s `createAutomationRule` (no `x-idempotency-key` header, confirmed against all 8 siblings which do set it), `packages/db/src/automations.ts`'s `insertAutomationRule` (plain INSERT, no uniqueness beyond the random id), and `automations.ts`'s `runAutomationsForRecordChange` (fires each enabled rule independently, no cross-rule dedup). Confirmed `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md` predates the feature entirely (`grep -i automation` on the design doc: no matches). Confirmed round 594 (the prior idempotency-focused round) scoped its own check to record creation specifically and never cross-referenced the automations route. Confirmed the feature's 6 prior adversarial rounds (586-588, 595-597) covered timing, cross-field invariants, cascade-delete, trigger `fieldValue` type, and `toField` type -- none of them about request-retry safety.

**The fix**: mirrors round 594's own fix for record creation exactly. `routes/projects.ts`'s automation-rule-create route now reads `const idempotencyKey = req.header("X-Idempotency-Key") || undefined;` and wraps the existing validation + `insertAutomationRule(...)` call in `withIdempotency(db, idempotencyKey, req.userId!, \`POST /projects/${project.id}/entities/${entity.name}/automations\`, ...)` -- the route string interpolates the real project id and entity name (round 528's own lesson: a bare template string would wrongly collide across different projects/entities reusing the same key). `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `createAutomationRule` now sends `headers: { "x-idempotency-key": crypto.randomUUID() }`, matching all 8 sibling creation functions.

**The tests**: one new test in `app.test.ts`, mirroring the existing record-creation idempotency test exactly -- builds the beauty-clinic project, creates a `toMode:"field"` automation rule on Customer's `phone` field with a fixed `X-Idempotency-Key`, retries the identical POST with the same key, asserts the retry returns the exact same rule id/body, and confirms via `GET /projects/:id/automations` that exactly one rule exists (not two).

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- app.test.ts 174/174, green. Backed up `routes/projects.ts` and `api.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted (the retry returned a genuinely different rule id, a newly inserted row), 173/174 nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green: db 166, shared 16, spec-engine 147 (all unchanged), api 523 (+1), web 902 (unchanged from round 599). `npm run build --workspaces` clean (db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always; api esbuild 545.1kb, web tsc+vite built in 1.43s). Commit `3809c41`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Creating an automation rule is now protected from a retried request producing a duplicate rule, like every other insert route in the app -- a connection dropped after a successful create no longer risks a WhatsApp message being sent twice per real trigger forever after.

### Round 601: the exported app's own generated ICS calendar export left the UID line's entity.name unescaped, unlike the live-preview version already fixed in round 589

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 601 (Automations closed at 6 rounds, Print closed at 598, calendar drag closed at 599), a fresh Explore survey was instructed to avoid every exhausted pattern and specifically look for drift between `apps/web`'s hand-written implementations and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated equivalents -- exactly the kind of bug round 599's calendar-drag fix turned out to be. It found that `calendarIcs.ts`'s `buildCalendarIcs` (the live in-product preview) had its UID line's `entity.name` escaped via `icsEscapeText` back in round 589, but the near-identical copy of the same function embedded in `codegen.ts` -- emitted verbatim into every exported, downloaded standalone app -- was never updated to match.

**The finding**: `codegen.ts`'s generated `buildCalendarIcs` pushes `foldIcsLine(\`UID:${entity.name}-${record.id}@forge-ai\`)` with `entity.name` interpolated raw, while the same function's PRODID, SUMMARY, and DESCRIPTION lines all correctly wrap their unbounded text in `icsEscapeText(...)`. `EntitySchema.name` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) is a bare `z.string().min(1)` with no character restriction enforced, so an entity can legitimately be named something containing a semicolon, comma, or backslash. Fed through the generated code, the exported app's downloaded `.ics` file would contain a UID content line like `UID:Weird;Name,With\Chars-3@forge-ai` -- an unescaped `;`, which RFC 5545 reserves as the parameter delimiter inside a content line. A standards-strict calendar client parsing that file can misread everything after the `;` as a bogus parameter or reject the VEVENT outright, in the one output (a real end user's downloaded, standalone exported app) that people actually import into real calendar apps. `codegen.test.ts`'s own comment on the adjacent PRODID-folding test claimed UID was "already handled" alongside SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION -- true only for folding; `foldIcsLine` alone performs no character escaping, and the `icsEscapeText` call specifically for UID's `entity.name` was the one spot round 589's web-side fix was never ported to.

**Independent verification**: read both implementations side by side -- `apps/web/src/calendarIcs.ts`'s UID line calls `icsEscapeText(entity.name)` (with its own code comment describing the round-589 fix and round-551's PRODID fix that should have covered UID too), while `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated copy does not. Confirmed `calendarIcs.test.ts` already exercises exactly this scenario (an entity named `"Weird;Name,With\Chars"`) and asserts the escaped UID, with no equivalent test existing for the generated copy in `codegen.test.ts`.

**The fix**: `codegen.ts`'s generated `buildCalendarIcs` now pushes `foldIcsLine(\`UID:${icsEscapeText(entity.name)}-${record.id}@forge-ai\`)`, matching `calendarIcs.ts` exactly (with the outer-template-literal escaping codegen.ts requires for genuine backticks inside its embedded source).

**The tests**: one new test in `codegen.test.ts`, reusing the same real-generated-code extraction harness as the adjacent PRODID-folding test (extracting `buildCalendarIcs` and its helpers from the actual generated `EntityView.jsx` source and invoking it directly) -- mirrors `calendarIcs.test.ts`'s own UID-escaping test, invoking the extracted function with an entity named `"Weird;Name,With\Chars"` and asserting the UID line is properly escaped, not raw.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- codegen.test.ts 186/186, green. Backed up `codegen.ts`, reverted via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted (raw `UID:Weird;Name,With\Chars-3@forge-ai` in the output), 185/186, nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (902/902 in the last-run workspace shown, exit code 0 overall; db/shared/spec-engine/api all unchanged in count from round 600 except api's +1). `npm run build --workspaces` clean (api esbuild 545.1kb; web tsc+vite built in 1.44s). Commit `7f76133`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The exported, standalone app's calendar export now escapes entity names the same way the live-preview version has since round 589, so an unusually-named entity's downloaded .ics file no longer risks a malformed UID content line in real calendar clients.

### Round 602: POST .../integrations/whatsapp/send was the one real-effect mutating route never wrapped in withIdempotency, letting a lost-response retry send the same WhatsApp message to a customer twice
