**Context**: with no backup candidate ready for round 602, a fresh Explore survey's first candidate -- a claimed false-FK-failure bug in `pipeline.ts`'s `runQaChecks` (its synthetic smoke-test record's dangling required-relation guess allegedly reaching the database layer and tripping a `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` on an unrelated required-field test) -- was independently empirically refuted before any code was touched: a real repro test showed `runQaChecks` returning `allPassed: true` in the exact scenario described, because `insertRecord`'s `coerceValue` processes `entity.fields` in order and throws `ValidationError` for whichever single field the test loop deliberately emptied *before* the SQL `INSERT` (and thus before any FK check) ever executes -- the dangling relation id never actually reaches the database layer in that code path. A second survey, explicitly required to empirically confirm any candidate with a real test before reporting it (not just reason about it), found and confirmed this round's actual bug instead.

**The finding**: every other real-effect mutating route in `routes/projects.ts` (`/projects`, `/from-template`, `/clone`, `/answers`, `/roles`, `/assumptions`, `/entities` add-entity, `/entities/:name/fields` add-field, record creation [594], automation-rule creation [600]) reads an `X-Idempotency-Key` header and wraps its insert in `withIdempotency(...)`. `POST /projects/:id/integrations/whatsapp/send` called `whatsapp.sendMessage(...)` (a genuine network round-trip to the WhatsApp Web socket) and `insertWhatsAppMessage(...)` bare, with no guard at all -- and `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `sendWhatsAppMessage()` sent no `X-Idempotency-Key` header either, unlike every one of its sibling creation functions. `docs/wakeRetry-idempotency-design.md`'s own "full inventory of mutating routes" (the design doc that drove rounds 471+) never mentions this route at all -- it was simply missed, even though it fits the doc's own "real, unguarded risk" category more severely than any route already covered, since this one duplicates a real outbound message to an external WhatsApp contact rather than app-internal data. A response lost in transit after `whatsapp.sendMessage()` already succeeded (the exact `fetchWithWakeRetry` retry-on-any-thrown-fetch-error scenario rounds 471-474/594/600 exist for) would resend the identical POST and send the same real WhatsApp message to the customer a second time, with no way for them to tell the duplicate was a glitch rather than a second genuine message.

**Independent verification**: confirmed directly by reading the route handler (`routes/projects.ts`'s WhatsApp-send route -- bare `whatsapp.sendMessage`/`insertWhatsAppMessage` calls, no `withIdempotency`), `api.ts`'s `sendWhatsAppMessage()` (no `x-idempotency-key` header, confirmed against sibling creation functions like `createAutomationRule`/`createProject`), and `fetchApi`'s own implementation (built directly on `fetchWithWakeRetry`, confirming this route genuinely goes through the same retry-on-dropped-response window every other converted route does). Confirmed an existing test ("a failed send stays logged as failed, and retrying with the same recipient/body... succeeds and adds a new sent entry," modeling the panel's own Retry button) sends no idempotency-key header at all, so it continues to exercise a genuinely new, deliberate user-initiated resend -- confirming the fix doesn't collide with that already-established, intentionally-unguarded product behavior.

**The fix**: mirrors round 594/600's own pattern exactly. The route now reads `const idempotencyKey = req.header("X-Idempotency-Key") || undefined;` and wraps the send + match + `insertWhatsAppMessage` effect in `withIdempotency(db, idempotencyKey, req.userId!, \`POST /projects/${project.id}/integrations/whatsapp/send\`, ...)` (route string with the real project id, round 528's own lesson), returning `{status, body}` for both the success and the existing 502-failure response shapes. `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `sendWhatsAppMessage()` now sends `"x-idempotency-key": crypto.randomUUID()` alongside its existing headers.

**The tests**: one new test in `app.test.ts`, mirroring round 600's own idempotency-retry test shape -- connects a fake WhatsApp socket, sends with a fixed `X-Idempotency-Key`, retries the identical POST, asserts the exact same response is replayed, confirms via the fake socket's own `sendCalls` array that the real send only ran once, and confirms via `GET .../messages` that exactly one message was logged (not two).

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- app.test.ts 175/175, green. Backed up `routes/projects.ts`/`api.ts`/`app.test.ts`, reverted the first two via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted (174/175, the retry performed a second real send), nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (902/902 in the last-run workspace shown, exit code 0 overall, ~297s -- an earlier run that appeared to hang past 30 minutes turned out to be resource contention from running several diagnostic test commands concurrently during the false-positive investigation, not a real issue; isolating each workspace individually confirmed every one green). `npm run build --workspaces` clean (api esbuild 545.6kb; web tsc+vite built in 1.44s; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always). Commit `8c49bdf`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Sending a WhatsApp message is now protected from a retried request sending a duplicate real message to a customer, like every other mutating route in the app. Lesson for future rounds: a plausible-sounding bug must be empirically confirmed with a real repro before it's trusted, not just reasoned about -- the refuted `runQaChecks` candidate would have wasted a full implementation cycle on a non-bug had it not been tested first.

### Round 603: entityFormatting.ts's sortRecords broke stable-sort tie ordering on "desc" by reversing the whole sorted array, unlike its sibling sortRecordsMulti

**Context**: with the idempotency-coverage sweep now closed after 8 rounds (471-474, 594, 600, 602) and every other adversarial-tested domain (Automations, Print, calendar drag, ICS UID escaping, runQaChecks) exhausted or refuted, round 602's own lesson ("a plausible-sounding bug must be empirically confirmed with a real repro before it's trusted") was made a hard requirement for this round's Explore survey. The survey spent most of its effort ruling out several already-closed or already-refuted candidates (csvEscape divergence, Content-Disposition dead code, several codegen.ts-vs-entityFormatting.ts functions verified byte-for-byte equivalent) before finding and empirically confirming this round's actual bug via a real script run against the live code, not just reasoning.

**The finding**: `sortRecords` (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`) computes a stable ascending sort, then calls `.reverse()` on the whole array for `"desc"`. Reversing the full array also flips the relative order of any tied pair (two records with an equal sort value), breaking the sort's stability -- a real stable "desc" sort must keep ties in their original relative order. Its sibling `sortRecordsMulti` (added later, round 177) already avoids this exact mistake by negating the comparator's own result per element (`direction === "desc" ? -cmp : cmp`) instead of reversing the whole result -- and its own doc comment already explains why reversing is wrong, yet `sortRecords` itself was never fixed to match. `entityFormatting.test.ts`'s own existing test for `sortRecords`' direction handling only ever exercised unique values, never a genuine tie in `"desc"`, so the divergence from its sibling was never caught. Confirmed via repo-wide grep that `sortRecords` currently has no live caller in production code -- `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`'s exported-app generator both call `sortRecordsMulti` exclusively, even for a single sort column -- so this is a real, verified defect in an exported, tested utility with zero current user-facing impact, not a live regression.

**Independent verification**: re-ran the grep across `apps/web/src` and `apps/api/src` myself (confirmed `sortRecords(` appears only in `entityFormatting.ts`'s own definition and `entityFormatting.test.ts`'s own test file; `codegen.ts` has no `sortRecords` function at all, only `sortRecordsMulti`). Read `sortRecordsMulti`'s own doc comment directly, which already states in plain English exactly why `sortRecords`' reverse-the-whole-array approach is wrong for any case with ties -- confirming this was a known, documented gap in a sibling function that was simply never ported back.

**The fix**: `sortRecords` now negates the comparator's own result per `direction === "desc" ? -cmp : cmp`, exactly matching `sortRecordsMulti`'s approach, instead of sorting ascending and reversing.

**The tests**: one new test in `entityFormatting.test.ts`, mirroring the existing direction tests' style -- two tied records (`v: 5`) and one distinct one (`v: 2`), sorts `"desc"`, asserts the two tied records keep their original relative order (id 1 then id 2), not reversed.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- entityFormatting.test.ts 146/146, green. Backed up `entityFormatting.ts`, reverted via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted (the tied pair came back reversed), 145/146 nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (903/903 in web, exit code 0, ~297s). `npm run build --workspaces` clean (api esbuild 545.6kb; web tsc+vite built in 1.70s; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always). Commit `5d1761b`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. `sortRecords` now sorts "desc" the same stable way its sibling `sortRecordsMulti` already does, kept correct for the exported utility surface even though no current call site exercises it -- fixed rather than deleted, since it's still a tested, public function a future call site could reasonably reach for.

### Round 604: an array value for a required number/relation field silently bypassed both the required-field check and the number-shape check, in both `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` and `codegen.ts`'s duplicated `coerce()`

**Context**: with no backup candidate ready, a fresh Explore survey was again required to empirically confirm its candidate with a real repro before reporting, per round 602's lesson. It found a new, concrete instance of the exact bug family rounds 408 (whitespace-string) and 523 ("Infinity"-string) already fixed in `coerceValue` -- the same function, a different input shape (an array) exploiting the same underlying gap.

**The finding**: `coerceValue`'s `isEmpty` check only recognizes `undefined`/`null`/`""`/whitespace-only strings as "no real value" -- a JS array is none of those, so it falls through to the `number`/`relation` branch's `Number(raw)` call. `Number([])` is `0` and `Number([42])` is `42` (a well-known JS quirk, not `NaN`), so `Number.isFinite` passed and the array was silently stored as a real number/foreign-key id. For a *required* field this was worse than a type-coercion quirk: since `isEmpty` never flagged the array as empty, the required-field check never fired either, so a client sending `{"amount": []}` for a required field got a `201` with a fabricated `0` instead of the `400 ValidationError` every other not-really-a-value input already gets. Reachable from the real HTTP API: `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName` (`routes/projects.ts` ~line 1456) passes `req.body` straight into `insertRecord` with no prior schema/shape validation. The exact same copy-pasted logic, down to the same `isEmpty` definition, is duplicated in `codegen.ts`'s own `coerce()` function (the exported, standalone app's server-side validation) -- the same gap, the same fix needed, confirmed by direct `grep` that no `coerceValue`/`coerce` name match existed for this check in either copy before the fix.

**Independent verification**: re-read `coerceValue` directly (`packages/db/src/repository.ts` lines 31-59) and confirmed the exact mechanism. Ran `node -e "console.log(Number([]), Number([42]))"` directly to confirm the JS quirk itself (`0`, `42`, both `Number.isFinite`-true). Confirmed the route handler passes `req.body` with zero prior validation. Found and read `codegen.ts`'s duplicated `coerce()` function (lines 373-401) and confirmed it has the identical `isEmpty` definition and the identical unguarded `Number(value)` call for `number`/`relation` fields -- following this file's own established "always check codegen.ts for a duplicate" convention (confirmed again in rounds 599, 601, 603).

**The fix**: both `coerceValue` (`repository.ts`) and `coerce()` (`codegen.ts`) now throw the same `ValidationError`/`Error` ("must be a number") immediately via an `Array.isArray(raw)` check at the top of the `number`/`relation` branch, before `Number()` is ever called -- a narrow, targeted guard matching the existing style of the whitespace-string and "Infinity"-string fixes right next to it, rather than broadening `isEmpty`'s own definition (which would also affect `text`/`enum`/`boolean`/`date` fields whose own coercion paths already reject an array value correctly via their own existing checks, confirmed by reading each branch).

**The tests**: one new test in `packages/db/src/repository.test.ts`, mirroring the existing whitespace/Infinity tests' exact style -- `insertRecord` with `amount: []` and `amount: [42]` for a required number field, both asserted to throw `ValidationError`, plus a sanity check that a real `500` still succeeds. One new test in `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts`, mirroring the existing "Infinity" test's real-spawned-server harness exactly -- generates and spawns the real `server.js`, POSTs `amount: []` and `amount: [42]` to a required number field, asserts both get a real `400`.

**Regression-proof**: ran each new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- `repository.test.ts` 21/21, `codegen.test.ts` 187/187, both green. Backed up both pairs of files, reverted `repository.ts` alone (keeping its test) -- failed exactly as predicted (20/21, the array silently coerced), nothing else regressed; restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran green. Repeated the same cycle for `codegen.ts` alone (keeping its test) -- failed exactly as predicted (186/187), restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green after each fix was restored (db 167/167 [+1], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 526/526 [+1], web 903/903, exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces` clean both times (api esbuild 545.7kb/545.8kb; web tsc+vite built in 1.43s/1.60s; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always). Commits `2c8188a` (repository.ts) and `bb4e0b3` (codegen.ts).

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A required number/relation field can no longer be silently satisfied with an array value in either the live-preview API or the exported standalone app, in both cases now rejected with the same clean validation error every other malformed input already gets. Lesson for future rounds: the `coerceValue`/`coerce()` input-validation-gap family (round 408 whitespace, round 514/round-boolean, round 523 Infinity-string, round 604 arrays) keeps finding genuinely new JS-coercion-quirk instances on different input shapes -- a future round finding yet another one (e.g. a plain object `{}`, which also quirks through `Number({})` as `NaN` already correctly, so is not itself a gap, or some other shape) is still a legitimately new finding, not a rehash, as long as it's empirically confirmed first.

### Round 605: `isValidDateString`/`isValidDate` wrongly rejected any real calendar date whose year falls in the 0-99 range, across all four duplicated copies of the function

**Context**: a fresh Explore survey found a new, independent bug unrelated to the `coerceValue` family that round 604 closed -- a quirk of the `Date` constructor itself, not of JS's `Number()` coercion.

**The finding**: `isValidDateString`/`isValidDate` validates a `YYYY-MM-DD` string by round-tripping it through `new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day))` and checking `getUTCFullYear()`/`getUTCMonth()`/`getUTCDate()` all match what was parsed -- the same technique that correctly catches a calendrically-impossible date like `"2024-13-45"`. But `Date.UTC` (and the `Date` constructor generally) has a legacy ECMA-262 special case: a `year` argument in the 0-99 range silently gets `1900` added to it (`Date.UTC(99, 0, 1)` parses as year `1999`, not `99`). So the round-trip check for a syntactically valid, real date like `"0099-01-01"` compared `1999 !== 99` and wrongly rejected it as invalid -- the exact same false-positive failure mode the function exists to avoid for actually-bad input. The bug is duplicated identically four times: `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `isValidDateString` (the live API's own validation), `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s `isValidDateString` (the live UI's CSV-import validation), and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s two `isValidDate` copies (the exported standalone app's server-side `coerce()` and its client-side CSV import) -- all four copy-pasted from the same original.

**Independent verification**: confirmed the exact `Date.UTC` quirk directly via `node -e "console.log(Date.UTC(99,0,1), new Date(Date.UTC(99,0,1)).getUTCFullYear())"` (returns year `1999`, not `99`) and `node -e` reproductions of the actual extracted function logic confirming `isValidDateString("0099-01-01")` returns `false` (the bug) while `"0100-01-01"`/`"2024-01-01"` correctly return `true` (unaffected, since 100+ has no special-casing) and `"0000-01-01"` also incorrectly returns `false`. Read all four source locations directly to confirm each is byte-for-byte the same buggy logic. Verified the fix (`new Date(0)` followed by `setUTCFullYear(year, month - 1, day)` instead of passing the year through `Date.UTC`) via another `node -e` reproduction, confirmed it fixes every 0-99-year case while leaving all existing validation behavior (malformed strings, impossible calendar dates, leap-year logic) unchanged, since `setUTCFullYear`'s year argument has no such special-casing.

**The fix**: all four copies now build the `Date` via `new Date(0); parsed.setUTCFullYear(year, month - 1, day);` instead of `new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day))` -- a narrow, targeted change to only how the date is constructed, leaving the round-trip comparison itself untouched.

**The tests**: one new test in each of the four surrounding test files, each asserting a `"0099-01-01"` date is now accepted instead of rejected, mirroring each file's own existing date-validation test style exactly: `packages/db/src/repository.test.ts` (`insertRecord` succeeds), `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.test.ts` (`buildImportRecords` returns zero errors and the parsed record), and two tests in `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts` -- one extending the existing real-spawned-`server.js` test with an extra `201` assertion, one new standalone test executing the real generated `isValidDate`/`buildImportRecords` extracted from `generateExportFiles`'s actual output (mirroring the existing "impossible date" CSV-import test).

**Regression-proof**: ran each new/extended test against current (fixed) code fresh -- `repository.test.ts` 168/168, `entityFormatting.test.ts` 147/147, `codegen.test.ts` 188/188, all green. Backed up all three file pairs, then reverted and re-verified each independently: `repository.ts` alone reverted -- failed exactly as predicted (the new test threw the expected `ValidationError`), nothing else regressed; `entityFormatting.ts` alone reverted -- failed exactly as predicted (1 error instead of 0), nothing else regressed; `codegen.ts` alone reverted -- failed exactly the 2 predicted tests (186/188), nothing else regressed. Each restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green after all three fixes restored (db 168/168 [+1], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 527/527 [+1], web 904/904 [+1], exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web tsc+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commits `56ff39d` (repository.ts), `0d3bec5` (entityFormatting.ts), `502982a` (codegen.ts).

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A date field's year can now be anywhere in the full valid calendar range, including 0-99, in the live API, the live UI's CSV import, and both copies in the exported standalone app -- previously a date like `"0099-01-01"` was wrongly rejected as invalid everywhere a date field exists. This closes out the distinct `isValidDateString`/`isValidDate` duplication family (separate from the `coerceValue`/`coerce()` family round 604 closed) with its own fresh, independent bug, not a rehash of a previously-fixed input shape.

### Round 606: a refine that kept an automation rule's WhatsApp-destination field NAME but changed its TYPE left the rule silently enabled, pointed at a now-unsafe destination

**Context**: a fresh Explore survey found an eighth angle on the Automations feature (previously audited across rounds 586-588, 595-597, 600) -- this time a gap in `diffAndMigrate`'s own automation-rule safety sweep (added rounds 587/588) itself, rather than in the feature's trigger/action-type validation.

**The finding**: `diffAndMigrate` (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`) already computes a `type_changed` entry whenever a field keeps its name but its declared type differs from the previous spec -- the same list surfaced to the user as a migration-hazard warning. Separately, in the same function, an automation-rule safety sweep (round 587/588) disables any rule referencing an entity/field a refine has *removed*, checking only field-NAME presence. It never consulted the `type_changed` list it had already computed moments earlier. So a `toMode:"field"` automation rule's WhatsApp destination (e.g. a `text` field named "phone") stayed fully `enabled: true`, with its `toField` still "phone", even after a later refine redefined that same-named field as `date` or `enum`. This matters because `routes/projects.ts`'s `validateAutomationToField` (round 597's own fix, which rejects a `toField` unless it's `text`/`longtext`) only runs at rule create/update time, never re-checked afterward -- and `fireRule`'s only runtime guard (`typeof to !== "string"`) is powerless here, since `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` stores date/enum values as plain strings too. The result: a rule valid when saved could be silently invalidated by a later refine and keep firing, reproducing the exact dangerous scenario round 597 set out to prevent, just reached via a different, unguarded path.

**Independent verification**: re-read `diffAndMigrate`'s `type_changed` computation and the automation-rule safety sweep directly (`migrate.ts` lines ~299-310, ~483-495), and `validateAutomationToField`/`fireRule` (`routes/projects.ts` ~415-423, `apps/api/src/automations.ts` ~91-105), confirming the mechanism. Wrote and ran a real repro script (`npx tsx`, not mocked) against the actual production functions: created a real `text` "phone" field with a real automation rule pointed at it as `toField`, ran a real `diffAndMigrate` call redefining "phone" as `date` (same name), confirmed the migration genuinely reports a `type_changed` entry, confirmed the rule was still `enabled: true` afterward, inserted a real record under the new schema (`phone` stored as plain string `"2024-01-15"`), and confirmed `matchesTrigger` says the rule fires for it -- reproducing the full chain to `fireRule` attempting a real outbound send to a date string. Also confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicate of this logic (the exported standalone app has no refine/migration feature at all, so there's only one location to fix).

**The fix**: `diffAndMigrate` now tracks, alongside each `type_changed` entry, whether the field's new type is NOT `text`/`longtext` (the same invariant `validateAutomationToField` enforces), in a small per-entity map built during the type-change computation. The automation-rule safety sweep now also calls the existing `disableAutomationRulesForField` for any field in that map, not just fields removed by name. A sanity check confirmed a `text` <-> `longtext` retype (both valid WhatsApp destinations) correctly leaves the rule enabled, so this doesn't over-disable.

**The tests**: two new tests in `migrate.test.ts`, mirroring the existing "removed field" automation-sweep tests' exact style -- one creates a `toMode:"field"` rule pointed at the fixture's real `name` field (`text`), refines it to `date`, and asserts both the `type_changed` entry and the rule's `enabled: false`; the other does the same retype to `longtext` and asserts the rule stays `enabled: true`.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code fresh -- `migrate.test.ts` 31/31, green. Backed up both files, reverted `migrate.ts` alone (keeping the tests) -- failed exactly as predicted (the type-change test's rule stayed `enabled: true` instead of `false`, 30/31), nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 170/170 [+2], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 527/527, web 904/904) -- one transient failure in `apps/api/src/auth/password.test.ts`'s concurrency-timing test on the first full run, confirmed a resource-contention flake (passed in isolation, unrelated to this change), and a clean re-run of the full suite came back all-green. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web tsc+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `dff48ba`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. An automation rule's WhatsApp destination field can no longer be silently invalidated by a same-named-but-retyped field surviving a refine -- the safety sweep that already handled a field's outright removal now also handles it keeping its name but losing the shape the rule depends on.

### Round 607: a `field_equals` automation rule on a `date` field accepted a locale-formatted value with no validation, creating a permanently, silently dead rule -- the same gap round 595 closed for boolean/enum fields, left open for dates

**Context**: a fresh Explore survey found a ninth angle on the Automations feature (audited across 8 prior rounds: 586-588, 595-597, 600, 606) -- this time in `validateAutomationFieldValue` itself, the exact function round 595 added, which simply never got a `date` branch.

**The finding**: `validateAutomationFieldValue` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) rejects a `field_equals` rule's `fieldValue` that can never match a real stored value -- for `boolean` fields it requires exactly `"true"`/`"false"`, for `enum` fields it requires membership in `enumValues` (both added round 595). It had no check at all for `field.type === "date"`. `matchesTrigger` (`apps/api/src/automations.ts`) compares with a byte-exact `String(actual) === rule.fieldValue`, and a date field's only real stored shape is `"YYYY-MM-DD"` (`repository.ts`'s own `coerceValue` enforces this at insert time). But the live app's UI never shows a user that raw ISO form -- `EntityPanel.tsx`'s table cells render every date field through `toLocaleDateString` (e.g. `"3/15/2026"` for en-US). So the only date text a real user has ever seen for that field is the locale-formatted one, and `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s field dropdown lists date fields with no restriction while its `fieldValue` box is unguided free text -- there is nothing stopping, and every visual cue encouraging, a user to type the date exactly as they see it everywhere else. That value is silently accepted at rule creation, then can never match the real stored value, leaving the rule permanently, silently dead with no error anywhere -- exactly the failure class round 595 explicitly set out to close, just missed for this one field type.

**Independent verification**: read `validateAutomationFieldValue` directly, confirmed no `date` branch exists (only `boolean`/`enum`). Read `matchesTrigger` directly, confirmed the byte-exact `String(actual) === rule.fieldValue` comparison. Wrote and ran a real repro script (`npx tsx`, spinning up the real `createApp`/`createStore` against a real HTTP server, not mocked) against the actual production code: signed up, built a real "beauty clinic" project (produces the built-in `Appointment` entity with a required `date` field), created a `field_equals` automation rule with `fieldValue: "3/15/2026"` (`new Date(2026,2,15).toLocaleDateString("en-US")`, i.e. exactly what the live table shows) -- got a real `201 Created`, no validation error. Inserted a real record with the same date stored the only way this app ever stores one (`"2026-03-15"`). Confirmed via `GET .../automations` that the rule's `lastTriggeredAt` stayed `null` -- the rule never fired despite a genuinely matching record. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has zero mentions of "automation" (grepped directly) -- Automations is a live-preview-only feature with no exported-app duplicate, so there's nothing to port a fix to.

**The fix**: exported `isValidDateString` from `packages/db/src/repository.ts` (previously module-private) and re-exported it from the package's `index.ts`, then imported it in `routes/projects.ts` and added a `field.type === "date"` branch to `validateAutomationFieldValue` that rejects any `fieldValue` failing that same real-calendar-date check -- mirroring the existing boolean/enum branches' "reject at creation, don't rely on a runtime guard" discipline. Unlike every other duplicated copy of `isValidDateString`/`isValidDate` this project has accumulated (round 605 found and fixed four), this one is a genuine *export*, not a fifth duplicate: `apps/api` already depends on `@forge/db` directly in the same Node process, unlike `apps/web` or the physically separate exported standalone app (`codegen.ts`'s generated output), which can't import it and must keep their own copies.

**The tests**: one new test in `apps/api/src/app.test.ts`, mirroring round 595's own test's exact structure and style -- builds the beauty-clinic project, asserts a `field_equals` rule on `Appointment`'s `date` field with `fieldValue: "3/15/2026"` is rejected with `400`/`VALIDATION_ERROR`, then asserts the real stored ISO shape (`"2026-03-15"`) is still accepted with `201` (not a blanket rejection of all date values).

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- `app.test.ts` 176/176, green. Backed up all four changed files (`repository.ts`, `index.ts`, `routes/projects.ts`, `app.test.ts`), reverted the three source files (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`201 !== 400`), 175/176, nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 170/170, shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 528/528 [+1], web 904/904, exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web tsc+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `3f42e84`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A `field_equals` automation rule's `fieldValue` is now validated against every field type that has a narrower real-world shape than "any string" -- boolean, enum, and now date -- closing the one field type round 595's own fix left open.

### Round 608: `groupByField`/`groupRecordsByField`'s hardcoded `"__other__"` sentinel for the synthetic "(other)" overflow bucket collided with a real, declared enum value of the same literal name

**Context**: the Automations feature had accumulated 9 rounds of findings (586-588, 595-597, 600, 606, 607) and was explicitly steered away from this round in favor of fresh territory. A first Explore survey ran a wide, honest sweep and found no new bug, correctly reporting a clean negative result rather than padding with a weak claim (ruling out, among others, `checkpointDiff.ts`'s deliberate `required`-change-ignoring contract, already covered by an explicit existing test). It flagged one concrete unexplored lead: whether board-view grouping (`groupByField`/`groupRecordsByField`) and the persisted `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` state could interact in a genuinely new way. A second, narrowly-scoped follow-up survey on exactly that lead found this bug.

**The finding**: `groupByField` (board/Kanban columns) and `groupRecordsByField` (table "group by") both build one bucket per declared enum value, then append a trailing synthetic overflow bucket -- for any record whose stored value isn't one of the field's current `enumValues` (e.g. a legacy value left behind by a refine) -- keyed by the hardcoded literal string `"__other__"`. `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s `FieldSchema` places no restriction at all on what strings `enumValues` may contain (only `field.name` is checked against reserved names), so nothing stops an AI-generated or hand-edited spec from declaring an enum field whose `enumValues` genuinely includes `"__other__"` as one of its real options. When that entity also has at least one record with an actual legacy/unrecognized value (triggering the overflow bucket), the two functions produce two separate buckets that both key as `"__other__"` -- one the real declared column, one the unrelated synthetic one. `EntityPanel.tsx` renders board columns with `key={column.value}` and reads/writes collapsed state via `collapsedBoardColumns.has(column.value)` / `toggleBoardColumnCollapsed(column.value)`, where `collapsedBoardColumns` is a plain `Set<string>` persisted by `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` as a flat string array -- neither has any way to tell the two same-valued buckets apart. Net effect: collapsing the real, declared `"__other__"` column silently collapses the unrelated overflow column too (and vice versa), with the wrong choice then persisted across reloads. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has a verbatim-ported duplicate of both functions with the identical hardcoded sentinel, so the exported standalone app carries the same defect.

**Independent verification**: read `groupByField`/`groupRecordsByField` directly (`entityFormatting.ts` lines ~618-640, ~1382-1405), confirmed the hardcoded `"__other__"` literal in both. Read `FieldSchema` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts`, confirmed `enumValues: z.array(z.string()).optional()` has no content restriction. Wrote and ran a real repro (`npx tsx`, not mocked) against the actual production functions: declared a field with `enumValues: ["New", "__other__"]`, three records (one matching "New", one matching the real "__other__" value, one with a genuinely unrecognized value) -- confirmed both functions produce two entries keyed `"__other__"`, an exact duplicate-key collision. Read `EntityPanel.tsx`'s board-column render and `toggleBoardColumnCollapsed`/`collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts`, confirming the Set/persisted-array keying is purely by the raw `column.value` string with no disambiguation. Confirmed `codegen.ts` carries an identical duplicate (lines ~1976-2023).

**The fix**: added `otherGroupKey(enumValues)` next to `uniqueEnumValues` in both `entityFormatting.ts` and `codegen.ts` -- starts from `"__other__"` and appends underscores until the result no longer matches anything in the field's own `enumValues`, guaranteeing no collision for any finite declared set. Both `groupByField` and `groupRecordsByField` now call it instead of using the literal string. `codegen.test.ts`'s existing regex-extraction test for the generated `groupByField` was updated to also extract and scope in the new `otherGroupKey` function (its generated source calls it now too).

**The tests**: two new tests in `entityFormatting.test.ts` (one for `groupByField`, one for `groupRecordsByField`) -- a field with `enumValues: ["New", "__other__"]` and a genuinely-unrecognized-value record, asserting no two columns/groups share a key, the real `"__other__"` column is never marked `isOther`, and the real overflow bucket gets a distinct key. One new assertion block added to `codegen.test.ts`'s existing `groupByField` regression test, extending the same scenario against the real generated code via `new Function(...)`.

**Regression-proof**: ran each new/extended test against current (fixed) code fresh -- `entityFormatting.test.ts` 149/149, `codegen.test.ts` 188/188, both green. Backed up all four files, reverted `entityFormatting.ts` alone (keeping its tests) -- failed exactly as predicted (both new tests failed on `2 !== 3`, the duplicate-key collision), 147/149, nothing else regressed; restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran green. Reverted `codegen.ts` alone (keeping its test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`"expected to find otherGroupKey in generated output"`), 187/188, nothing else regressed; restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green after both fixes restored (db 170/170, shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 528/528, web 906/906 [+2], exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean (no type errors from the new code); db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `385df92`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A real declared enum value named `"__other__"` can no longer silently alias the synthetic overflow bucket's own collapsed/expanded state, in either the live-preview board/table views or the exported standalone app.

### Round 609: `seed.ts`'s end-of-range date-collision fix never distinguished two RECOGNIZED end-of-range fields from each other, only an end-like field from a non-end-like one

**Context**: a fresh Explore survey, correctly steered away from the now-heavily-mined Automations feature, found a genuinely new gap in a previously-fixed mechanism -- `seed.ts`'s own end-of-range date-collision handling, last touched by round 591's `dateFieldOrdinal` fix for two *unrecognized* date fields colliding.

**The finding**: `seedValueFor`'s `case "date":` branch computes `dayOffset = isEndLike ? baseOffset - 3 : baseOffset + dateFieldOrdinal`, where `isEndLike` is whether the field's name matches `END_DATE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` (`["enddate", "returndate", "checkoutdate", "untildate", "todate"]`). The `else` branch's `dateFieldOrdinal` -- this field's position among the entity's own date fields -- already exists specifically to stop two date fields from colliding, per the function's own doc comment. But the `isEndLike` branch gives *every* matching field the identical `baseOffset - 3`, with no further distinction at all. So an entity with two different fields that both match the end-of-range hint list -- e.g. a rental/booking-style entity with both `checkoutDate` and `returnDate`, or `endDate` and `untilDate` -- seeds both fields to the exact same day, in every single seeded record. `ProductSpecSchema` has no rule against two such field names coexisting on one entity, so an AI-generated or refined spec can reach this shape freely.

**Independent verification**: read `seedValueFor`'s date branch directly (`seed.ts` lines 93-120), confirmed the `isEndLike` branch's offset formula has no per-field distinction at all, unlike the `else` branch right next to it. Wrote and ran a real repro (`npx tsx`) against the actual `generateSeedRecords` export with a `Booking` entity declaring `startDate`/`checkoutDate`/`returnDate` -- confirmed `checkoutDate === returnDate` in every one of 3 generated records (e.g. both `"2026-10-13"` in record 0). Confirmed `generateSeedRecords` is called directly from the real build pipeline (`apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s Seed Data Agent step, run on every real `/build` and `/refine`), so this reaches real generated demo data, not just an internal code path. Confirmed `seed.test.ts`'s existing end-of-range tests only cover an (end-like, non-end-like) pair (`checkInDate`/`checkoutDate`) and an (unrecognized, unrecognized) pair (`hireDate`/`birthDate`) -- no existing test covers two fields that both match the hint list, so this exact gap was genuinely untested.

**The fix**: added `endLikeOrdinal` -- this field's position among only the entity's end-of-range-matching date fields -- mirroring `dateFieldOrdinal`'s own fix but scoped to just the end-like fields. `dayOffset` for an end-like field is now `baseOffset - 3 + endLikeOrdinal`: a single end-like field keeps ordinal `0`, so its offset is unchanged from before (no regression for the already-covered single-end-like-field case); two or more end-like fields each get a distinct day, while all of them still land after the entity's non-end-like (start-like) date field's own offset.

**The tests**: one new test in `seed.test.ts`, mirroring the existing Rental/Booking tests' exact style -- a `Booking` entity with `startDate`/`checkoutDate`/`returnDate`, asserting `checkoutDate !== returnDate` and that both still land after `startDate`.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- `seed.test.ts` 20/20, green. Backed up `seed.ts`+`seed.test.ts`, reverted `seed.ts` alone (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`checkoutDate and returnDate must not collapse to the same day`, both `"2026-10-13"`), 19/20, nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Confirmed `seed.ts`/`generateSeedRecords` has no duplicate in `codegen.ts` (seeding only happens server-side at build time, never in the exported standalone app), so there was only one location to fix. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 171/171 [+1], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 528/528, web 906/906, exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `dd994f3`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Two recognized end-of-range date fields on the same entity (e.g. `checkoutDate`/`returnDate`) now seed to genuinely distinct days, closing the one case the round 591 fix's own doc comment didn't account for.

### Round 610: a QA failure during build/refine left the new entity's real table permanently orphaned, surviving even full project deletion

**Context**: a fresh Explore survey, steered explicitly away from every heavily-mined pattern (keyword-collision, missing-plural, visible-staleness, Automations, coerceValue, seed.ts, ICS escaping, migrate.ts's collision guard), found a genuinely new gap in the build/refine pipeline's own bookkeeping.

**The finding**: `runBuildPipeline` (`apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`) applies a real migration (`diffAndMigrate`) and real seed inserts, both committed immediately -- no transaction wraps either (confirmed via `grep` for `transaction`/`BEGIN`/`COMMIT` across `migrate.ts`/`pipeline.ts`/`connection.ts`: none). It then runs `runQaChecks` and, on a real, designed-for QA failure (the function's own top comment: "can genuinely fail with a real error"), `return`s immediately -- before `updateProjectSpec`, `markProjectBuilt`, or `insertCheckpoint` ever run. `insertCheckpoint` was the *only* writer of the durable `checkpoint_entity_history` ledger (besides a one-time startup backfill), so a QA-failed refine's new entity never gets recorded there. `deleteProject` (`packages/db/src/projects.ts`) computes which real tables to drop as the union of exactly three sources -- the project's current `spec_json`, `listAllCheckpointedEntityNames`, and `listHistoricalEntityNames` -- none of which can ever learn about an entity that was only ever touched by a QA-failed attempt. Its real table (and whatever got seeded into it) survives forever, even across full project deletion, unreachable under a project id that no longer exists anywhere.

**Independent verification**: read `pipeline.ts` lines 317-514 directly, confirming the QA-failure `return` at line 475 sits before every one of `updateProjectSpec`/`markProjectBuilt`/`insertCheckpoint` (lines 493-506). Read `checkpoints.ts` to confirm `insertCheckpoint` is the sole writer of `checkpoint_entity_history` outside the startup backfill, and `projects.ts`'s `deleteProject` to confirm its three-source union. Wrote and ran a real repro (`npx tsx`) using the exact production functions (`openDatabase`, `diffAndMigrate`, `insertRecord`, `insertCheckpoint`, `listHistoricalEntityNames`, `deleteProject`): built a project with `Customer`, then simulated a refine adding `Invoice` via a direct `diffAndMigrate` + `insertRecord` call *without* ever calling `insertCheckpoint` for it (standing in for a QA failure) -- confirmed `listHistoricalEntityNames` never learned about `Invoice`, and after `deleteProject`, `Invoice`'s real table (with its real row) was still queryable, with the project row itself gone. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicate of any of this (the build/refine pipeline and checkpoint system aren't part of the exported standalone app).

**The fix**: extracted `insertCheckpoint`'s own history-writing loop into a new exported `recordEntityHistory(db, projectId, spec)` in `checkpoints.ts`; `insertCheckpoint` now calls it instead of duplicating the loop. `pipeline.ts` calls `recordEntityHistory(db, project.id, nextSpec)` directly, right after a successful migration (covering both the direct-success path and the Debug Agent's recovery-success path), independent of whatever QA/Security/checkpoint-insert does next.

**The tests**: a new test in `checkpoints.test.ts` asserting `recordEntityHistory` writes every entity name without creating a checkpoint row. A new test in `projects.test.ts`, mirroring the file's own existing "entity added then later removed from the spec" orphan test's exact raw-call methodology ("reproduces the exact real sequence ... rather than asserting against a contrived fixture") -- builds a project, then simulates a refine adding `Invoice` via `diffAndMigrate`+`insertRecord`+`recordEntityHistory` but *never* `insertCheckpoint` (standing in for a QA failure), then asserts `deleteProject` still drops `Invoice`'s real table.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code fresh -- `checkpoints.test.ts` and `projects.test.ts` both green, db 173/173 (+2). Backed up `checkpoints.ts`/`index.ts`/`pipeline.ts`, reverted `checkpoints.ts` (removing `recordEntityHistory`) and its `index.ts` export (keeping both new tests) -- failed exactly as predicted: both files failed to even load (`recordEntityHistory` no longer exported), 142/144 db tests still passing, nothing else regressed. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (173/173). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 173/173 [+2], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 528/528, web 906/906, exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `1c842f2`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A build/refine's new entity table is now tracked in the durable history ledger the moment its migration succeeds, so a later QA failure can no longer leave it as a permanent, unreachable orphan. Note: the narrower edge case of a *Database-step* failure whose Debug Agent recovery also fails (returns before ever reaching this new call site) is not covered by this fix and remains open for a future round if pursued.

### Round 611: round 610's own flagged edge case -- a Database-step failure (not QA) could still orphan an earlier entity in the same diffAndMigrate call

**Context**: round 610's own trigger note named this exact narrower gap as an open backup candidate, so this round implemented it directly rather than running a fresh Explore survey.

**The finding**: round 610 moved the `checkpoint_entity_history` ledger write to right after the pipeline's migration call succeeds, closing the QA-failure trigger. But `diffAndMigrate` (`migrate.ts`) processes `nextSpec.entities` one at a time inside a `forEach`, each with its own real, immediately-committed `db.exec` (no transaction wraps the whole call -- confirmed, same as round 610). If an EARLIER entity's own migration genuinely commits (e.g. a brand-new table) and a LATER entity in that same call then throws -- the clearest, already-tested real trigger being `migrate.ts`'s own sanitized-name collision guard (rounds 496-498) rejecting a new entity that collides with a long-removed one from project history -- the whole `diffAndMigrate` call throws, propagating to `pipeline.ts`'s catch block. If the Debug Agent's recovery then also fails (or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset), the pipeline returns before ever reaching round 610's `recordEntityHistory(db, project.id, nextSpec)` call, since that call only runs once the whole try/catch block around the migration succeeds. The earlier entity's real, already-committed table is orphaned exactly the same way a QA failure used to orphan one.

**Independent verification**: read `migrate.ts`'s `generateCreateTableStatements` (called once upfront for `applyMigrations`, the initial-`/build` path) and confirmed it throws during statement *generation* (before any `db.exec`), so the initial-build path can't partially commit on a bad field name. But the refine path's `nextSpec.entities.forEach(...)` loop (used whenever `previousSpec` is defined) calls `db.exec` per-entity *inside* the loop, with the sanitized-name collision check (lines 266-276) running before that entity's own `db.exec`. Wrote and ran a real repro (`npx tsx`) using the exact production functions: built a project with `Customer`+`לקוח`, refined `לקוח` away, then attempted a second refine adding `Invoice` (first in the array) and `מוצר` (second, colliding with the now-removed `לקוח` from history) in the same `diffAndMigrate` call -- confirmed the call threw `ValidationError` on `מוצר`, `Invoice`'s real table already existed, `checkpoint_entity_history` never learned about it, and after `deleteProject`, `Invoice`'s table was still orphaned -- reproducing round 610's exact symptom through this genuinely different trigger.

**The fix**: moved the ledger write into `diffAndMigrate` itself, at per-entity granularity -- `checkpoints.ts` now exports `recordEntityNameInHistory(db, projectId, entityName)` (the single-entity primitive `recordEntityHistory` delegates to), and `migrate.ts` calls it immediately after each entity's own migration step actually commits (both the brand-new-table branch and the ordinary existing-entity field-diff branch), guarded by a `hasCheckpointHistoryTable` check (mirroring `allKnownEntityNames`'s own existing tolerance for a bare test database that never called `ensureCheckpointsTable`). This is a strict superset of round 610's whole-call write, so the now-redundant `recordEntityHistory(db, project.id, nextSpec)` call in `pipeline.ts` was removed rather than kept as a duplicate.

**The tests**: a new test in `migrate.test.ts`, structured as the direct single-call twin of the existing "removed two refines ago" collision test -- adds `Invoice` then `מוצר` in the same `diffAndMigrate` call, asserts the call throws `ValidationError` but `Invoice`'s name is in `listHistoricalEntityNames` and its real table exists. A new test in `projects.test.ts` mirroring round 610's own `deleteProject` orphan-test style, confirming `deleteProject` still drops `Invoice`'s table after this exact failed-call sequence.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code fresh -- green, db 175/175 (+2). Backed up `checkpoints.ts`/`index.ts`/`migrate.ts`/`pipeline.ts`. Reverted just the two `migrate.ts` call sites (keeping both new tests) -- failed exactly as predicted (only the 2 new tests failed, "Invoice's own migration already committed... its name must be tracked"), 173/175 nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran green. Also reverted `checkpoints.ts`'s new `recordEntityNameInHistory` export alone (keeping `migrate.ts`'s now-dangling import) -- confirmed a module-load failure cascading to every test file importing `migrate.ts` (`migrate.test.ts`, `projects.test.ts`, `repository.test.ts`, `seed.test.ts`, 84/88 passing in that reduced run), the established strong module-load-crash confirmation pattern. Restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran green (175/175). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 175/175 [+2], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 528/528, web 906/906, exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `054a915`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Every entity a build/refine's migration actually commits a real table for is now tracked in the durable history ledger the instant that happens, regardless of what any later entity in the same call -- or any later pipeline step -- does afterward. Together with round 610, both known triggers for this orphan class (a later pipeline step failing, and a later entity in the same migration call failing) are now closed.

### Round 612: a 5th convergent "project is gone, purge its client-side preferences" path missed -- being removed as a collaborator by someone else

**Context**: round 611's own trigger note flagged one backup candidate (a WhatsApp inbound-message-vs-delete-project race) for this round. Independent code tracing before any implementation found that candidate to be a false lead: `handleIncomingMessages` (`apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.ts`) has no internal `await` in its message-processing loop, so it is atomic relative to `deleteProject`; it also early-returns via a `!project` check once the project is gone, and `deleteWhatsAppData` (`packages/db/src/whatsapp.ts`) unconditionally deletes every `whatsapp_messages` row for that `projectId` regardless of insertion timing. Whichever side of the race wins, the outcome is self-consistent -- no orphan possible. A fresh Explore survey was launched instead, steered away from this now-cleared lead and every other heavily-mined pattern.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/projectPreferenceCleanup.ts`'s `purgeProjectPreferences(projectId)` sweeps ~18 separate localStorage stores for one project id, and is called from exactly four places in `App.tsx` -- `handleDeleteProject`, `handleBulkDeleteProjects`, `handleAccountDeleted` (both owned and shared ids), and `CollaboratorsPanel`'s `onLeft` ("leave project") callback (rounds 390/392/403/404). All four are actions the *same browser* explicitly just performed, so it can purge synchronously right after. The gap: when the project **owner** removes a *different* collaborator (`CollaboratorsPanel.tsx`'s `handleRemove`, a `DELETE /projects/:id/collaborators/:userId` the owner's own browser sends), that happens entirely in the owner's session. The removed collaborator's own browser has no websocket/push to learn about it -- the only place it ever finds out is the home screen's own `listProjects()` effect (`App.tsx` lines 844-849) simply omitting that project id on its next fetch. That effect only ever overwrote `myProjects` with whatever came back; it never diffed the previous list against the new one to notice an id vanished, so `purgeProjectPreferences` was never called for it -- the identical unbounded-growth leak the four prior fixes already exist to prevent, reached through a path none of them covers (the server-side state change originates in someone *else's* session). The same gap applies if the owner deletes the whole project while a non-deleting collaborator has local preferences for it.

**Independent verification**: read `App.tsx`'s `listProjects()` effect and confirmed its own doc comment already (half-)acknowledges the scenario ("keeps this list correct after ... being removed as a collaborator") without ever mentioning preference cleanup. Read all four existing `purgeProjectPreferences` call sites to confirm each is a same-browser-initiated action. Read `CollaboratorsPanel.tsx`'s `handleRemove` and the server route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` lines 943-954) to confirm the removal is a plain DELETE with no push channel back to the removed user's own session. Read `projectPreferenceCleanup.ts` to confirm `purgeProjectPreferences`'s signature and that repeated/idempotent calls are harmless (removing an already-absent localStorage key is a no-op).

**The fix**: added a `myProjectIdsRef` (`useRef<Set<string>>`) tracking the ids this effect has already seen. On every successful `listProjects()` fetch, it now computes the fresh id set, calls `purgeProjectPreferences` for any previously-seen id missing from it, then updates the ref before calling `setMyProjects`. The very first fetch (empty ref) never purges anything, since there's no prior list to diff against yet.

**The tests**: a new test in `App.test.ts`, extracting the real effect callback out of `App.tsx` (the same "slice a JSX/hook body out of the source via regex, transform with esbuild, run in a sandboxed `new Function`" technique the file's other handler-extraction tests already use) -- asserts the first-ever fetch purges nothing, a second fetch with one id missing purges exactly that id, and an id present in both fetches is never purged.

**Regression-proof**: the extraction regex initially produced a syntax error (`new Function`'s body ended in `return (${code})` with esbuild's own trailing `;` inside the parens) -- fixed by dropping the extra parens to match the file's own existing `onLeft`-test pattern (`return ${code}`, no wrapping parens). Ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green, web `App.test.ts` 72/72 (+1). Backed up `App.tsx`, reverted just the effect's own fix (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted ("a project id present in the previous fetch but missing from this one must be purged", `[]` vs `['revoked-project']`), 71/72 nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green. Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 175/175, shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 528/528, web 907/907 [+1], exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `dc252ee`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A project that silently disappears from a user's own home-screen list -- for any reason, including being removed as a collaborator by someone else -- now has its client-side preferences purged on the very next home-screen fetch that notices the disappearance, closing the last of the five convergent "this browser can never reach this project again" paths.

### Round 613: a field_equals automation rule's fieldValue on a `number` field was the one type `validateAutomationFieldValue` never covered

**Context**: round 612's own trigger note left no backup candidate, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, steered away from the now-heavily-mined Automations fieldValue-type-validation family (rounds 595, 607) among everything else already closed.

**The finding**: `matchesTrigger` (`apps/api/src/automations.ts`) compares `String(actual) === rule.fieldValue` byte-exact. For a `number` field, `rowToRecord` (`packages/db/src/repository.ts`) returns a real JS number, so `String(1000)` is `"1000"`. But the only form of that value a real user has ever seen on screen is `EntityPanel.tsx`'s locale-formatted one (`entityFormatting.ts`'s `formatNumberValue`: `(1000).toLocaleString()` is `"1,000"`) -- the natural thing to type into the rule's free-text `fieldValue` box, which can never byte-match `"1000"` and leaves the rule permanently, silently dead with no error anywhere. `validateAutomationFieldValue` (`routes/projects.ts`) already closed this exact gap for `boolean` (round 595), `enum` (round 595), and `date` (round 607) fields; `number` was simply never added, even though it has the identical failure mode.

**Independent verification**: read `validateAutomationFieldValue` directly, confirming it has branches for `boolean`/`enum`/`date` but none for `number`. Read `matchesTrigger`'s byte-exact comparison and `rowToRecord`'s real-number return, and `formatNumberValue`'s `toLocaleString` call. Ran real JS directly (`node -e`) confirming `String(1000) === "1,000"` is `false`. Wrote and ran a real repro (`npx tsx`) calling the actual exported `matchesTrigger` with a real `AutomationRule`/`EntityRecord` pair -- confirmed a rule with `fieldValue: "1,000"` against `record.amount = 1000` never matches, while `fieldValue: "1000"` does. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicate (Automations isn't part of the exported standalone app).

**The fix**: added a `number` branch to `validateAutomationFieldValue`, rejecting unless `Number.isFinite(Number(fieldValue)) && String(Number(fieldValue)) === fieldValue` -- the one canonical string shape that can ever match (rejects grouping separators like `"1,000"`, trailing-zero/leading-zero variants, scientific notation; accepts `"1000"`, `"10.5"`, `"-5"`).

**The tests**: a new test in `app.test.ts` mirroring round 607's date-field test exactly -- builds the beauty-clinic project (whose heuristic spec includes a `Service` entity with a `price` number field), asserts a rule with `fieldValue: "1,000"` on `Service.price` is rejected 400/VALIDATION_ERROR, and `fieldValue: "1000"` is still accepted 201.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green. Backed up `routes/projects.ts`, reverted just the new `number` branch (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (201 instead of 400), 528/529 nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (529/529). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 175/175, shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 529/529 [+1], web 907/907, exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `a031b6d`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A `field_equals` automation rule's `fieldValue` is now rejected at creation/update time for every field type (`boolean`, `enum`, `date`, `number`) whose free-text-typed value could never byte-match the real stored shape -- closing the last type in this validation family.

### Round 614: an enum field narrowing its `enumValues` (same name, same type) was invisible to `diffAndMigrate`'s automation-rule safety sweep

**Context**: round 613 left no backup candidate, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly steered away from the dozen-plus already-exhausted bug classes (visible-staleness, purgeProjectPreferences, checkpoint_entity_history orphaning, validateAutomationFieldValue type-completeness, migrate.ts's collision guard, domainEntities.ts keyword-collisions, the Automations feature's prior 7 rounds of fixes, withIdempotency coverage, ICS UID escaping, unproven "race condition" claims, and the coerceValue input-validation family).

**The finding**: `diffAndMigrate`'s per-field loop (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`) only tracks a field as automation-unsafe when `prevField.type !== field.type` (producing a `type_changed` entry). A refine that keeps an enum field's name and type but narrows its `enumValues` -- e.g. renaming or removing the option `"pending"` from a `status` field -- never triggers that branch at all: no `type_changed` entry, nothing added to the set the automation-disable sweep below consumes. Any `field_equals` automation rule whose stored `fieldValue` named the now-removed option (valid when the rule was created -- `validateAutomationFieldValue`, rounds 595/607/613, only checks shape at creation/update time) stays `enabled` forever, pointed at a value `coerceValue` (`repository.ts`) can never store again once the field's `enumValues` no longer include it. This is a 4th distinct trigger for the existing field-automation-disable mechanism (entity removal, field removal, and toField-unsafe-retype were the other three, rounds 586-600) -- not a 5th instance of the already-closed `validateAutomationFieldValue` type-completeness family, since that family is about creation-time validation and this is about the spec evolving *after* a rule already validly exists.

**Independent verification**: read `migrate.ts`'s per-field loop directly, confirming the `prevField.type === field.type === "enum"` case was a complete no-op. Found the identical narrowing condition already implemented for a different purpose in `pipeline.ts`'s `computeImpact` (`(prevField.enumValues ?? []).some((v) => !nextValues.has(v))`, used to warn the user about a tightened field). Ran the real `diffAndMigrate` via `npx tsx --experimental-sqlite` against two in-memory databases with no mocking: inserted a real `field_equals` rule on a `status` enum field with `fieldValue: "pending"`, then refined the spec to narrow `enumValues` to drop `"pending"` -- `diffAndMigrate` returned an empty change list and the rule was read back still `enabled: true`. Confirmed `migrate.test.ts` had no existing coverage for this path. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicate (Automations isn't part of the exported standalone app).

**The fix**: added an `else if (field.type === "enum" && prevField.type === "enum")` branch alongside the existing `type_changed` branch, running the same narrowing check `computeImpact` already uses, and on a hit adding the field to the same tracking map the `type_changed` branch already feeds into the automation-disable sweep. Renamed that map from `toFieldUnsafeAfterTypeChange` to the more general `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable` (and updated its doc comment) since it now has two independent triggers, not one.

**The tests**: two new tests in `migrate.test.ts` right after the existing toField/type-change tests: (1) a rule with `fieldValue: "New"` on the fixture's `status` enum field (`["New", "Won"]`) is disabled when a refine narrows `enumValues` to `["Won"]`, with an explicit assertion that no `type_changed` entry is produced for that narrowing (proving this is genuinely a separate code path, not accidentally piggybacking on the existing branch); (2) the same rule stays enabled when `enumValues` only grows (`["New", "Won", "Lost"]`), proving the check is really about losing the rule's own value, not any enumValues edit at all.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (34/34 in `migrate.test.ts`). Backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted just the new enum-narrowing branch (keeping both tests and the rename) -- failed exactly as predicted (test 1 only: `true !== false`), 33/34, nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (34/34). Full `@forge/db` suite clean (177/177). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 177/177 [+2], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 529/529, web 907/907, exit code 0). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `215d8bb`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The field-automation-disable mechanism (`disableAutomationRulesForField`/`disableAutomationRulesForEntity`) now covers all four known triggers: entity removal, field removal, toField-unsafe retype, and enum-value narrowing.

### Round 615: Export CSV, Copy, and per-record Print ignored the user's drag-reordered column order -- only Print list respected it

**Context**: round 614 left no backup candidate, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, steered away from the exhausted bug classes (visible-staleness, purgeProjectPreferences, checkpoint_entity_history orphaning, validateAutomationFieldValue completeness, migrate.ts's collision guard, domainEntities.ts keyword-collisions, the Automations feature's 8 prior rounds, withIdempotency coverage, ICS UID escaping, unproven race claims, coerceValue's input-validation family, and wakeRetry's design-only /refine idempotency).

**The finding**: `EntityPanel.tsx` computes `orderedFields = applyColumnOrder(entity.fields, columnOrder)` -- the entity's fields reordered to match whatever order the user has actually dragged columns into (round 203's column-reorder feature, persisted via `columnOrder.ts`). Round 597 (commit `85b8b73`) deliberately switched `RecordListPrintSheet`'s ("Print list") call site from `visibleFields` to `orderedFields`, so it both includes hidden columns AND preserves the user's drag order. But the other two whole-record-action siblings never got that same treatment: `handleExportCsv`/`handleCopy` both called `recordsToCsv(entity.fields, ...)`, and `RecordPrintSheet` (per-record Print) hardcoded `entity.fields.map(...)` -- both still used the entity's raw, undragged declared order. Concretely: drag "Phone" before "Name" in the table, and the on-screen table + Print list both show Phone first, but Export CSV, Copy, and per-record Print still emit Name first -- silently ignoring the reorder, inconsistent with their own sibling action.

**Why this isn't already-exhausted pattern #1 (visible-staleness, collapsed-group dimension)**: nothing here involves collapsed groups or a missing effect dependency -- it's a straightforward "round 597's fix was applied to one of three sibling call sites of the same whole-record-action convention, never ported to the other two," freshly exposed by round 597's own fix having established what the correct behavior for all three should be.

**Independent verification**: read the literal current source in both duplicated locations. `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`: `orderedFields`'s own doc comment (line ~1409) already documents the INTENDED behavior ("CSV export and both print sheets... always include every field") but never says they should also follow `orderedFields` specifically -- confirmed `handleExportCsv`/`handleCopy` passed `entity.fields` (not `orderedFields`) to `recordsToCsv`, and `RecordPrintSheet` had no `fields` prop at all, hardcoding `entity.fields.map`. Confirmed the identical split in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own `RecordPrintSheet`/`handleExportCsv`/`handleCopy`. Confirmed via `git show 85b8b73` that round 597 intentionally chose `orderedFields` (not `entity.fields`) for `RecordListPrintSheet` alone, proving the two other actions simply never picked up the same change.

**The fix**: in both files, `RecordPrintSheet` now takes a `fields` prop (mirroring `RecordListPrintSheet`'s own existing convention) and maps over it instead of `entity.fields`; its call site passes `fields={orderedFields}`. Both `recordsToCsv(...)` calls (`handleExportCsv`, `handleCopy`) now pass `orderedFields` instead of `entity.fields`.

**The tests**: one new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, right after round 598's "Print list includes a hidden column" test -- persists a real reordered `columnOrder` via `localStorage.setItem("forge.columnOrder", ...)` (the same round-trip the drag-and-drop reorder test already exercises), confirms the on-screen table already reflects it, then exercises Export CSV (reading back the real downloaded Blob), Copy (reading back the real `navigator.clipboard.writeText` call), and per-record Print (reading the real `.print-record-sheet dt` order) -- all three now list Status before Name, matching the reordered table.

**The wrinkle this round surfaced**: fixing the literal `entity.fields` -> `orderedFields` change broke two pre-existing regex-extraction tests in `codegen.test.ts` ("the exported EntityView's Export CSV routes through selectedOrAllRecords..." and "...renders a real Copy button...") -- both hardcoded the old `recordsToCsv(entity.fields, ...)` literal in their own match regex, unrelated to the actual selection-routing behavior they verify. A fresh round of the long-standing "changing a shared literal/signature requires grepping every regex-extraction test" lesson (previously hit for different helpers in rounds 432, 494, 545, 611) -- updated both regexes to expect `orderedFields` instead, with no change to what they actually assert.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new `EntityPanel.test.ts` test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (124/124). ### Round 616: `validateAutomationFieldValue` had no branch for `relation` fields -- round 613's own "closed" claim was premature

**Context**: round 615 left no backup candidate, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly steered away from the exhausted bug classes (visible-staleness, purgeProjectPreferences, checkpoint_entity_history orphaning, validateAutomationFieldValue "completeness" [boolean/enum/date/number], migrate.ts's collision guard AND its automation-disable sweep, domainEntities.ts keyword-collisions, the Automations feature's 9 prior rounds, withIdempotency coverage, ICS UID escaping, unproven race claims, coerceValue's input-validation family, wakeRetry's design-only /refine idempotency, and round 615's own just-closed orderedFields convention).

**The finding**: round 613 declared `validateAutomationFieldValue` "closed... for every field type whose free-text-typed value could never byte-match the real stored shape" after adding its 4th branch (`number`), on top of `boolean`/`enum`/`date` (rounds 595/607). But `FIELD_TYPES` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) has 7 field types, not 4 -- `text`/`longtext` genuinely need no validation (the raw stored string IS the value a user sees and types, so there's no display-vs-stored gap to close), but `relation` does have the identical gap and was simply never added. `repository.ts`'s `rowToRecord` stores a relation field's value as the related record's raw internal id (no special-casing, same code path as `number`), and `automations.ts`'s `matchesTrigger` compares `String(actual) === rule.fieldValue` byte-exact against that id. But no UI surface anywhere -- not `EntityPanel.tsx`, not `codegen.ts` -- ever shows that raw id; every rendering of a relation field (table cells, print sheets, CSV, the record form's own picker) uses `relationDisplayLabel`, the related record's own label. `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s rule-creation form lets a user pick a relation field as the `field_equals` trigger with no warning and a plain free-text `fieldValue` box, so the one thing a real user has ever seen for that field (its display label) is also the one thing that can never match.

**Independent verification**: read `validateAutomationFieldValue` (`routes/projects.ts`) directly, confirming branches only for `boolean`/`enum`/`date`/`number`, nothing for `relation`. Read `rowToRecord` confirming no relation-specific handling (same `string | number | null` cast as every other non-boolean type). Read `matchesTrigger`'s byte-exact comparison. Ran the real exported `matchesTrigger` directly (`npx tsx`, no mocking) with a rule `fieldValue: "Dana Levi"` (a plausible display label) against a record whose raw relation value is `42` -- returned `false`; the same rule with `fieldValue: "42"` returned `true`, confirming only the never-shown internal id can ever match. Confirmed `codegen.ts` needs no duplicate fix (Automations isn't part of the exported standalone app, per round 613's own prior confirmation).

**The fix**: added a 5th branch to `validateAutomationFieldValue`, rejecting unless `fieldValue` is a plain non-negative integer string matching `String(Number(fieldValue)) === fieldValue` -- the one shape the stored id can ever take, mirroring the `number` branch's own rejection shape exactly (the two field types share the same underlying storage representation).

**The tests**: a new test in `app.test.ts`, right after round 613's own number-field test -- builds the existing "A small courier delivery business." fixture (`Order` with a `courierId` relation to `Courier`, already used by several other relation-focused tests in this file), creates a real `Courier` record and a real `Order` referencing it, asserts a rule with `fieldValue` set to the courier's own display label (`"Dave"`) is rejected 400/VALIDATION_ERROR, and `fieldValue` set to the real stored id (`String(courier.id)`) is still accepted 201.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green. Backed up `routes/projects.ts`, reverted just the new `relation` branch (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (201 instead of 400), nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (`app.test.ts` 178/178). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces`: db 177/177, shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, web 908/908 all green; `@forge/api` first showed 529/530 with 1 failure -- `password.test.ts`'s "concurrent hashPassword calls run in parallel" wall-clock timing assertion, the exact same CPU-contention flake round 615 already hit once (several heavy test suites running in parallel in the same round) -- confirmed by re-running `password.test.ts` alone, clean (7/7), a 3rd instance of the isolate-and-rerun-clean protocol first established for `BuildProgress.test.ts` (round 478) and reconfirmed for this same timing test in round 615. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always.
