Round 613's "closed" claim is now actually true.

### Round 617: a refine that only changed a surviving field's letter-case threw a raw, unhandled SQLite "duplicate column name" error

**Context**: round 616 left no backup candidate, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, steered away from every now-fully-exhausted bug class (visible-staleness, purgeProjectPreferences, checkpoint_entity_history orphaning, validateAutomationFieldValue completeness [now genuinely closed for all 5 types with a display-vs-stored gap], migrate.ts's entity-level collision guard and its automation-disable sweep, domainEntities.ts keyword-collisions, the Automations feature's 10 prior rounds, withIdempotency coverage, ICS UID escaping, unproven race claims, coerceValue's input-validation family, wakeRetry's design-only /refine idempotency, and round 615's orderedFields convention).

**The finding**: `diffAndMigrate`'s per-field diff loop (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`) looks up a surviving field's previous definition via `prevFieldsByName.get(field.name)` -- an exact-string `Map` lookup. A refine that keeps a field but renames it only by letter case (e.g. `"email"` -> `"Email"`) is invisible to this: `EntitySchema`'s own `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateFieldNames` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) only rejects a case-collision *within one spec*, so `nextSpec`'s single `"Email"` field passes validation cleanly even though `previousSpec` had `"email"`. With no `prevField` found, the field falls into the "reused column" branch (meant for a field removed on an earlier refine and later re-added), whose own exact-string `currentColumns.has(columnName)` check also misses the already-existing physical column -- so `diffAndMigrate` generates `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "Email" ...` against a table that, from SQLite's own case-insensitive column-name comparison, already has that exact column. The result is a raw, unhandled `Error: duplicate column name: Email` -- not a reported `type_changed`-style diagnostic. This is a *field*-level instance of the same case-insensitivity gap rounds 496-498 already hardened at the *entity* level (`allKnownEntityNames`/`tableLower`, lines 280-291 of the same file) -- that guard only ever looks at entity names, never field names, so it has no bearing on this bug; it's a genuinely different lookup in a different loop, not a 4th depth/axis of the already-mined entity-level mechanism.

**Independent verification**: read the exact lookup chain directly (`prevFieldsByName.get(field.name)` at the top of the per-field loop, `currentColumns.has(columnName)` and the `db.exec(\`ALTER TABLE ...\`)` further down). Ran a real, unmocked repro (`npx tsx --experimental-sqlite`) against the actual exported `diffAndMigrate`: built a `Customer` entity with field `"email"`, then called `diffAndMigrate` again with the same entity but field renamed to `"Email"` -- the call threw `duplicate column name: Email`, confirming the exact failure path. Confirmed the two real call sites that reach this unguarded: `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s build/refine (wrapped in try/catch, but burns a Debug Agent AI-repair attempt on an error no spec change can fix -- the column genuinely already exists) and `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s checkpoint-restore route (no try/catch at all, so the raw `Error` falls through `app.ts`'s `instanceof HttpError/ValidationError/NotFoundError` checks straight to a generic 500). Confirmed `codegen.ts` needs no duplicate fix: the exported standalone app always does one fresh `CREATE TABLE` from the current spec with no incremental migration state, so there's no cross-refine rename for it to get wrong.

**The fix**: added a second, lowercased lookup map (`prevFieldByLowerName`) alongside the existing `prevFieldsByName`, and fall back to it when the exact-string lookup misses: `prevFieldsByName.get(field.name) ?? prevFieldByLowerName.get(field.name.toLowerCase())`. A case-only rename now correctly resolves to the same `prevField`, so it takes the normal `type_changed`/`enum`/`relation` comparison path (which compares *types*, unaffected by the name's case) and never reaches the `ALTER` at all -- correct, since SQLite already resolves either case to the one physical column. Scoped to only this verified lookup; the parallel "reused column" branch's own exact-string `currentColumns.has()` check (relevant only to the rarer compound case of a field removed, then re-added under different case) was left untouched, to avoid scope creep beyond the single verified finding.

**The tests**: a new test in `migrate.test.ts`, right after the existing `type_changed` test -- builds the fixture spec, inserts a real record, then refines with the `name` field renamed only to `"Name"` (same type, same everything else). Asserts the real `diffAndMigrate` call returns zero changes (a pure case rename is a genuine no-op), confirms via `PRAGMA table_info` that the table still has exactly one name-ish column (not two), and confirms the original record's data survived untouched.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (35/35 in `migrate.test.ts`). Backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted just the new lowercased-fallback lookup (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`duplicate column name: Name`, the identical raw SQLite error the survey's own repro hit), nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (35/35). Full `@forge/db` suite clean (178/178). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces` all green (db 178/178 [+1], shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 530/530, web 908/908, exit code 0 -- no flakes this run). `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `2f9e974`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A surviving field's `prevField` lookup in `diffAndMigrate` is now case-insensitive, matching the entity-level guard's own established precedent -- a refine that only changes a field's letter case is now a genuine no-op instead of an unhandled, user-facing database error.

### Round 618: the sibling "reused column" branch still threw the same "duplicate column name" error for a field removed, then re-added under different letter-case, two+ refines later

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 617, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly told that round 617 deliberately left the "reused column" branch's own exact-string `currentColumns.has()` check untouched "to avoid scope creep beyond the single verified finding" -- flagging it as the most plausible next place to look for a structurally sibling gap, alongside the rest of the now-exhausted list (validateAutomationFieldValue's 5 types, the automation-disable sweep's 4 triggers, the entity-level collision guard, orderedFields, etc).

**The finding**: a field with no `prevField` (i.e. absent from the immediately preceding spec -- most plausibly because it was removed on an earlier refine and is only now being re-added) falls into the "reused column" branch, which compares `field.name` against `currentColumns`/`physicalShapeByColumn` -- both keyed by the column's REAL physical name from `PRAGMA table_info`. That lookup was still exact-string, the same mistake round 617 fixed one function up for `prevFieldsByName`. A field removed, then re-added two+ refines later under different letter-case (e.g. `"email"` removed, later re-added as `"Email"`) has no entry in either `prevFieldsByName` or round 617's `prevFieldByLowerName` -- it genuinely wasn't in the immediately preceding spec -- so it reaches this sibling branch, where `currentColumns.has("Email")` misses the physically-present `"email"` column and the generated `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "Email" ...` throws SQLite's own `duplicate column name: Email`. A structurally different lookup (`currentColumns`/`physicalShapeByColumn`, sourced from SQLite's catalog, not from `previousSpec`) than round 617's `prevFieldsByName`, and reached via a different trigger (remove-then-re-add across 2+ refines, not a same-hop rename) -- genuinely outside round 617's own deliberately-scoped fix.

**Independent verification**: read the exact code (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts` lines 442-526) and confirmed it matched a fresh subagent survey's own report line-for-line before trusting it. Wrote and ran an independent repro (`npx tsx`, not the subagent's own script) against the real exported `diffAndMigrate`: step 1 created a `Customer.email` column, step 2 removed `email` from the spec (column stays, additive-only), step 3 re-added the field as `Email` -- threw `duplicate column name: Email`, confirming the exact predicted failure.

**The fix**: in the "reused column" branch, resolve the physical column name through a lowercased fallback first -- `currentColumns.has(columnName) ? columnName : Array.from(currentColumns).find((c) => c.toLowerCase() === columnName.toLowerCase())` -- and use that resolved `physicalColumnName` (not the raw declared `columnName`) for both the shape lookup (`physicalShapeByColumn.get(physicalColumnName)`) and the "does the ALTER need to run" check (`!physicalColumnName`), mirroring round 617's `prevFieldByLowerName` shape one function up.

**The tests**: a new test in `migrate.test.ts`, right after round 617's own case-rename test -- builds the fixture spec, inserts a real record, removes the `name` field via one `diffAndMigrate` call (asserting zero changes, confirming the additive-only design leaves the column physically untouched), then re-adds it as `"Name"` via a second `diffAndMigrate` call. Asserts the real call doesn't throw and reports `new_column` (the existing, intentional behavior for any field absent from `previousSpec`, confirmed by reading the surrounding code's own doc-comment rather than assumed) rather than a duplicate-column crash, confirms via `PRAGMA table_info` the table still has exactly one name-ish column, and confirms the original record's data survived.

**Regression-proof**: first run of the new test failed on a wrong assumption (expected `[]`; the existing, documented design always reports `new_column` for a field absent from `previousSpec`, regardless of whether the ALTER physically runs) -- corrected the assertion, not the fix, after reading the surrounding code's own comment confirming this is intentional. Then ran clean (36/36 in `migrate.test.ts`). Backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted just the lowercased-fallback resolution (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`duplicate column name: Name`), nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (36/36). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces`: db 179/179 (+1), shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 530 total/529 pass (the known `password.test.ts` "concurrent hashPassword calls run in parallel" wall-clock flake, confirmed via isolated re-run: clean 7/7), web 908/908. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `d836c20`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Both of `diffAndMigrate`'s field-identity lookups that key off a field's own name (the surviving-field comparison round 617 fixed, and this round's reused-column comparison) are now case-insensitive, matching the entity-level guard's own established precedent. A field removed and later re-added under different letter-case is now a genuine no-op instead of an unhandled database error.

### Round 619: a case-only field rename made `repository.ts`'s ordinary read/write path silently lose the field's data and crash on unrelated updates

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 618, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly told that `migrate.ts`'s `diffAndMigrate` had now had 5 rounds of case-insensitivity/collision findings (496, 497, 498, 617, 618) and that any 6th finding in that exact file needed to be airtight and structurally distinct -- steering the survey toward checking whether round 617/618's fix (making a case-only rename a genuine migration no-op) had exposed a gap in a *different* module that consumes the same spec/table.

**The finding**: `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `rowToRecord` (used by `listRecords`/`getRecord`/`insertRecord`'s own read-back) does a plain `row[field.name]` lookup, and `updateRecord`'s untouched-field fallback does the same via `existingRow[field.name]`. `row` comes from `db.prepare('SELECT * FROM ...').all()/.get()`, and `node:sqlite` returns it keyed by the column's REAL physical name -- which, after round 617/618's fix, deliberately keeps its *original* casing across a case-only rename (e.g. stays `"email"` even after the spec renames the field to `"Email"`). So `row["Email"]` is `undefined` for every row, old and new: the field silently vanishes from every read (table, CSV/print export, automations, WhatsApp templates), and `updateRecord`'s fallback binds that same `undefined` as a SQL parameter for any update that doesn't touch the renamed field, which `node:sqlite` rejects with a raw, uncaught `Error` ("Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 1") -- not `ValidationError`/`NotFoundError`, so it falls through to a generic 500. This bug is *caused by* round 617/618's fix being correct: before it, a case-only rename crashed inside `diffAndMigrate` itself on the very next refine, so no record was ever read or written under the new casing in the first place -- fixing the migration layer correctly made this pre-existing, previously-unreachable gap in the completely separate data-access layer reachable for the first time.

**Independent verification**: read `repository.ts`'s `rowToRecord`/`insertRecord`/`updateRecord` directly and confirmed they matched a fresh subagent survey's own report line-for-line. Wrote and ran an independent repro (`npx tsx`, not the subagent's own script) against the real exported `applyMigrations`/`diffAndMigrate`/`insertRecord`/`listRecords`/`updateRecord`: inserted a `Customer{name:"Alice"}` record, refined to rename the field to `"Name"` (confirmed `diffAndMigrate` returns `[]`, round 617/618's fix working as intended), then `listRecords` on the post-rename entity returned `{id, createdAt, status}` with no `name`/`Name` key at all -- "Alice" invisible. A fresh insert via the post-rename entity (`{Name: "Bob", ...}`) succeeded but read back the same way, missing `Name`. `updateRecord` touching only `status` (not the renamed field) threw `"Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 1."` exactly as predicted. The raw physical row (`SELECT * FROM ...`) confirmed the data was never actually lost at the SQL layer (`name: "Alice"` still there) -- purely an application-layer blind spot. Confirmed `codegen.ts` needs no duplicate fix: it has no `diffAndMigrate`/incremental-migration call at all, always doing one fresh `CREATE TABLE` from the current spec, so its own `rowToRecord` never sees a stale-cased column to mismatch against -- same scope-note precedent as rounds 617/618.

**The fix**: added `getRowValue(row, fieldName)` -- tries the exact-string key first, then falls back to a case-insensitive scan of the row's own keys (`Object.keys(row).find((key) => key.toLowerCase() === fieldName.toLowerCase())`). Used in `rowToRecord` (replacing `row[field.name]`) and in `updateRecord`'s untouched-field fallback (replacing `existingRow[field.name]`). `insertRecord`'s own `data[field.name]` lookup was left untouched -- that reads from the API caller's request payload (always in the entity's *current* spec casing), not from a DB row, so it was never affected.

**The tests**: a new test in `repository.test.ts`, at the end of the file -- inserts a real `Customer{name:"Alice"}` record, refines to rename the field to `"Name"` (asserting `diffAndMigrate` returns `[]`), then asserts `listRecords` still shows `Name: "Alice"` (not vanished), `updateRecord` touching only `status` doesn't throw and preserves `Name: "Alice"`, and a brand-new record inserted under the post-rename entity (`{Name: "Bob", ...}`) reads back correctly too.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (23/23 in `repository.test.ts`). Backed up `repository.ts`, reverted both the `getRowValue` helper and its two call sites (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`undefined` instead of `'Alice'`), nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (23/23). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces`: db 180/180 (+1), shared 16/16, spec-engine 147/147, api 530 total/529 pass (the known `password.test.ts` wall-clock flake, confirmed via isolated re-run: clean 7/7), web 908/908. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `624df94`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. `repository.ts`'s ordinary record read/write path now resolves a field's real physical column name case-insensitively, the same precedent `migrate.ts` established across rounds 496-498/617/618 -- a case-only field rename is now safe end-to-end (migration, read, and write), not just at the migration-engine layer alone.

### Round 620: diffAndMigrate's own automation-rule-disable sweep wrongly disabled a rule when its field only changed letter-case

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 619, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly told that `migrate.ts`'s `diffAndMigrate` had now had 5 rounds of case-insensitivity/collision findings (496-498, 617, 618) and `repository.ts` had just had its own (619) -- steered toward checking whether a 6th, structurally distinct sub-mechanism inside `diffAndMigrate` itself still had the same gap, since rounds 617/618 only ever touched the main per-field diff loop, not the function's separate automation-cleanup sweep further down.

**The finding**: `diffAndMigrate`'s automation-rule-disable sweep (the bottom loop that runs after the main migration logic, lines ~567-582) builds `nextFieldNames` as a `Set` of the surviving entity's exact-cased field names and checks membership with plain `Set.has()`. A refine that renames a field only by letter case (e.g. `"status"` -> `"Status"`) is a genuine no-op for the main per-field diff loop (rounds 617/618's fix) -- zero migration changes, same physical column, same data. But this separate sweep still sees the old-cased `"status"` as absent from `nextFieldNames` and calls `disableAutomationRulesForField`, silently flipping `enabled = false` on any `field_equals` trigger rule or `toMode:"field"` destination rule still referencing that field -- even though the field, its data, and its column never actually left. A structurally distinct 6th gap in the same function: a separate code path (the automation sweep, not the SQL/migration diff loop) with its own independent exact-string lookup that rounds 617/618 never touched.

**Independent verification**: read the exact sweep code (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts` lines 567-582) and confirmed it matched a fresh subagent survey's own report line-for-line. **The fix**: added a second, lowercased `nextFieldNamesLower` set alongside the existing `nextFieldNames`, and check both before disabling: `!nextFieldNames.has(prevField.name) && !nextFieldNamesLower.has(prevField.name.toLowerCase())`, mirroring the exact `prevFieldByLowerName`/lowercased-fallback shape already established twice in this same file (rounds 617, 618). The entity-level analog this same survey also investigated -- `diffAndMigrate` throws a `ValidationError` outright on an entity renamed only by case, via the entity-collision guard's exact-string `previousEntities.get(entity.name)` lookup -- was deliberately NOT touched this round: it's a different failure mode (hard rejection vs. silent wrong-disable) that may represent an intentional scope boundary rather than an oversight, flagged for human judgment rather than fixed speculatively.

**The tests**: a new test in `migrate.test.ts`, right after the existing "disables an automation rule referencing a field removed from a surviving entity" test -- inserts both a `field_equals` trigger rule and a `toMode:"field"` destination rule on `Customer.status`, refines to rename the field to `"Status"` only (asserting `diffAndMigrate` returns `[]`, confirming the migration itself stays a genuine no-op), then asserts both rules stay `enabled: true`.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (37/37 in `migrate.test.ts`). Backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted just the lowercased-fallback set (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`false !== true`), nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (37/37). Commit `bbdaa8e`.

All of `diffAndMigrate`'s field-identity lookups that key off a field's own letter-case -- the main per-field diff loop (617), the sibling reused-column branch (618), and now this automation-disable sweep (620) -- are case-insensitive, matching the entity-level guard's own established precedent. A case-only field rename is now a genuine no-op across migration, data read/write (619), and automation rules alike.

### Round 621: the "Columns" visibility menu's own checkbox list never got round 615's orderedFields fix, so it disagreed with the reordered table

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 620, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly told that `migrate.ts`'s diffAndMigrate (7 rounds of case/collision findings total) and `repository.ts` (round 619) were both now extremely picked-over for the exact-string-vs-tolerant-mechanism vein, and that any further instance of that specific pattern needed to be in a genuinely new, previously-unexamined module. The survey instead found a different, concrete gap in the already-established `orderedFields` convention from round 615.

**The finding**: round 615 made Export CSV, Copy, and per-record Print all honor the user's drag-reordered column order (`orderedFields = applyColumnOrder(entity.fields, columnOrder)`) instead of the entity's raw declared order, in both `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` and the exported app's `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`. But the "Columns" visibility menu's own checkbox list -- the UI a person actually uses to match a checkbox to a specific on-screen column, e.g. to hide "the 3rd column from the left" -- was never included in that round's audit. Both files' `columns-menu-panel` block still mapped over the raw `entity.fields` (`EntityPanel.tsx` line 2652, `codegen.ts` line 4096) instead of `orderedFields`, even though `orderedFields` was already computed and in lexical scope earlier in both components. After a real column reorder, the on-screen table and every whole-record action show the new order, but the Columns menu's checkboxes still list in the entity's original declared order -- the exact user confusion round 615 fixed everywhere else, just missed at this one call site.

### Round 622: BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES was missing Property, so a real-estate description got the wrong "No payments" recommendation

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 621, so a fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly told that the last 5 rounds' two veins (migrate.ts/repository.ts's exact-string-vs-tolerant-mechanism pattern, and the orderedFields convention gap) were both now believed exhausted in the files already examined, and to look at genuinely unexplored territory -- seed data generation, less-common EntityPanel.tsx/codegen.ts features, or the Templates Gallery's other templates.

**The finding**: `packages/spec-engine/src/heuristic.ts`'s `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES` set (`Invoice`, `Order`, `Donation`, `Subscription`, `Rental`) is a hand-maintained allow-list `buildOpenQuestions` uses to recognize that a description implies "yes, this app needs to accept payments" even when its wording never hits `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` -- e.g. a donation tracker's description never says "payment" but accepting donations plainly is one. Round 566 already found and fixed this exact drift once, for `Rental` (added to `domainEntities.ts` after `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES` was introduced, and never added to the set). `Property` (`domainEntities.ts`, "A real estate property for sale or rent", with its own `price` field) has the identical shape and was never added either -- so a real-estate description ("track properties for sale and apartment listings") matches only `Property`, hits none of `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`, and gets the wrong `"No payments"` recommendation, even though selling or renting real estate is definitionally a paid transaction.

**Independent verification**: read `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES`'s exact definition and the `Property` entity in `domainEntities.ts` directly, confirming both matched the fresh subagent survey's own report line-for-line. Wrote and ran an independent repro (`npx tsx`, not the subagent's own script) against the real exported `HeuristicSpecProvider`: `generate("A real estate agency to track properties for sale and apartment listings.")` returned `entities: ["Property"]` and a payment open-question with `recommendation: "No payments"` -- confirming the exact predicted wrong recommendation before writing any fix.

**The fix**: added `"Property"` to `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES`, mirroring round 566's `Rental` fix exactly, plus a doc-comment entry documenting this round's instance of the drift (the existing comment already predicted this exact failure mode: "this list itself can still drift out of sync with domainEntities.ts"). No duplicate fix needed elsewhere -- `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES` exists only in `heuristic.ts`, with no live-preview/exported-app split to port to.

**The tests**: a new test in `heuristic.test.ts`, right after the existing Rental regression test -- generates a real spec from a real-estate description, asserts it matches only `Property`, and asserts the payment open-question's recommendation is `"Stripe"` (not `"No payments"`), mirroring the Rental/Donation/Subscription tests' exact style.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (78/78 in `heuristic.test.ts`). Backed up `heuristic.ts`, reverted just the one-word set addition (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`'No payments'` instead of `'Stripe'`), nothing else regressed. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran green (78/78). **Topic status**: closed and pushed. `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES` now includes every entity in `domainEntities.ts` whose own description/fields make it a definitionally-paid entity -- both drift instances this allow-list has ever had (Rental, round 566; Property, round 622) are now fixed.

### Round 623: Business Twin's most-linked breakdown showed two identical "in \"Deals\"" lines for an entity with two relation fields to the same target

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 622, so a fresh Explore survey was launched on genuinely unexplored territory, explicitly told that case-insensitivity (migrate.ts/repository.ts), the orderedFields convention, BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES, Automation Rules, withIdempotency coverage, and the EntityPanel.tsx/codegen.ts revalidation-effect family were all considered exhausted or heavily mined, and to look elsewhere (other API routes, backup.ts/zip.ts, Business Twin, checkpoint/Time Machine, CSV edges, calendar/ICS, relation/enum handling).

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/twin.ts`'s `computeRelationHubObservation` (the "most-linked record" Business Twin insight) builds a breakdown entry per `(sourceEntity, relationField)` pair, each carrying `sourceLabel` (the referencing entity's label) AND `fieldLabel` (which relation field) -- but the final `breakdownText` (lines 174-177, pre-fix) only ever read `b.count` and `b.sourceLabel`; `fieldLabel` was computed and stored on every entry but never consulted anywhere, confirmed dead since this feature's original commit via `git log -p --follow`. When one entity has two different relation fields both pointing at the same target entity (schema-legal -- `FieldSchema` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` places no uniqueness constraint across a field's own `relationTo` within one entity, e.g. `Deal.customerId` and `Deal.referredBy` both `relationTo: "Customer"`) and the same target record is referenced through both, the breakdown produced two entries with the identical `sourceLabel` but different counts -- rendering as `"3 in \"Deals\", 2 in \"Deals\""` with no way to tell the two lines apart, even though the exact disambiguating text (`fieldLabel`) was sitting right there, discarded.

**Independent verification**: read `computeRelationHubObservation` directly (lines 104-188) and confirmed line-for-line that `fieldLabel` (line 136) is computed but never read in the `breakdownText` map (lines 175-177, pre-fix). Checked `apps/api/src/twin.test.ts`'s only existing test for this path ("...most referenced across multiple relation fields...") and confirmed it only covers the *cross-entity* case (`Order.customerId` and `Ticket.customerId` -- two different source entities, each with a single relation field), where `sourceLabel` alone already disambiguates -- the same-entity-two-fields case was never exercised. Checked `FieldSchema`'s Zod refinements directly and confirmed no constraint prevents two fields on one entity from sharing a `relationTo`.

**The fix**: in `computeRelationHubObservation`, before rendering `breakdownText`, counted how many breakdown entries share each `sourceLabel`; when a `sourceLabel` is ambiguous (count > 1), the rendered line now also names the field (`"3 in \"Deals\" (via Customer)"` / Hebrew `"3 ב\"Deals\" (Customer)"`), otherwise the line is unchanged from before. No duplicate fix needed elsewhere -- Business Twin has no codegen.ts/exported-app counterpart; it's a live-preview-only feature.

**The tests**: a new test in `twin.test.ts`, right before the existing fallback-candidate test -- a `Deal` entity with both `customerId` (label "Customer") and `referredBy` (label "Referred By") pointing at `Customer`, with the same `Customer` record linked 3 times via one field and 2 times via the other, asserting the rendered breakdown disambiguates both lines by field label.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (25/25 in `twin.test.ts`). Backed up `twin.ts`, reverted via `git stash` (keeping the test) -- failed exactly as predicted (`"3 in \"Deals\", 2 in \"Deals\""`, no disambiguation), nothing else regressed (24/25). Restored via `git stash pop`, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` against the pre-stash backup, re-ran green (25/25). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces`: db 181/181, shared 16/16, spec-engine 148/148, api 532/532 (+1), web 909/909, all clean. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `81c2bd6`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Business Twin's most-linked breakdown now disambiguates by field label whenever one entity reaches the same target through more than one relation field.

### Round 624: handleBulkDuplicate still called createRecord with an empty payload for a selected id whose record had already vanished from local state

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 623, so a fresh Explore survey was launched on genuinely unexplored territory, explicitly told that case-insensitivity, orderedFields, BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES, round 623's own Business Twin fix, the keyword-collision class, migrate.ts's collision guard, the revalidation-effect family, Automation Rules, and withIdempotency coverage were all considered exhausted or heavily mined, and to look elsewhere (other API routes, backup.ts/zip.ts, Business Twin's OTHER 5 insight functions, checkpoint/Time Machine, CSV edges, Templates Gallery, calendar/ICS, relation/enum handling).

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s `handleBulkDuplicate` (and its identical duplicate in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`) builds each selected id's copy with `const record = records.find(...); const copy = {}; if (record) for (const field of entity.fields) copy[field.name] = record[field.name]; return createRecord(projectId, entity.name, copy);` -- the `if (record)` guard wraps only the field-copying loop, NOT the `return createRecord(...)` call itself, which sits outside the `if` and always runs. The single-record `handleDuplicate` right above it gets this right (`if (!record) return;`, guarding the whole operation), but the bulk version's existence check is incomplete. `records`/`selectedIds` are plain client-side React state that can go stale relative to the server (this exact codebase already handles the analogous "another tab/collaborator deleted this record while it was selected" case for bulk delete and bulk update) -- so a selected id whose record was deleted between selection and the "Duplicate selected" click still fires `createRecord(projectId, entity.name, {})`.

**Independent verification**: read `handleDuplicate` (lines 1842-1854) and `handleBulkDuplicate` (lines 1885-1899 pre-fix) directly in `EntityPanel.tsx`, confirming the exact structural gap the subagent reported, then confirmed the identical duplicated bug at the same lines in `codegen.ts`'s own `handleBulkDuplicate` (lines 3474-3488 pre-fix) via direct read, not just a claim. Read `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `insertRecord`/`coerceValue` directly: `coerceValue` throws a `ValidationError` for any `required` field when the raw value is `undefined` (which `copy[field.name]` is for every field when `copy` is `{}`), but returns `null` for a non-required field -- confirming that an entity with at least one required field gets a misleading validation error (attributing the failure to "field is required" rather than "record is gone"), while an entity with zero required fields (a schema-legal shape) silently inserts a genuine all-null blank record with no error at all. Checked `EntityPanel.test.ts`'s existing `handleBulkDuplicate` tests (regex-extracted from the real source, not reimplemented) and confirmed every one of them uses ids that are always present in the `records` fixture -- the "record vanished from local state before the batch ran" path had no coverage.

**The fix**: in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, moved the existence check out front: `if (!record) return Promise.reject(new Error(...))` before building `copy`, mirroring `handleDuplicate`'s own guard -- so a vanished id is now treated as an immediate, clearly-attributable per-id failure (reported via the existing partial-failure UI path) instead of ever reaching `createRecord`. Added a new i18n key `entity.bulk.recordGone` (Hebrew + English) for `EntityPanel.tsx`'s message; `codegen.ts`'s exported app has no i18n layer, so it uses a plain English string, matching that file's own existing convention.

**The tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, right after the existing "surfaces the raw error message when every duplicate fails" test -- selects ids 1/2/3 where id 2's record is missing from the `records` fixture, and asserts `createRecord` is never called for id 2 while ids 1 and 3 still succeed, and that id 2 alone ends up reported as failed. A matching test in `codegen.test.ts`, using the same regex-extraction-from-generated-output pattern as that file's own existing `handleBulkDuplicate` tests.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (126/126 in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, 190/190 in `codegen.test.ts`). Backed up both source files, `git stash`'d just `EntityPanel.tsx`+`codegen.ts` (keeping both test files) -- each file's own new test failed exactly as predicted (an `undefined` name sneaking into the attempted-copies list), nothing else regressed in either file (125/126 and 189/190). Restored via `git stash pop`, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` against the pre-stash backups, re-ran both green (126/126, 190/190). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces`: db 181/181, shared 16/16, spec-engine 148/148, api 533/533 (+1, no flake this run), web 910/910 (+1), all clean. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `c2bae7a`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. `handleBulkDuplicate` now skips (and clearly reports) a selected id whose record is gone, in both the live preview and the exported app, instead of ever sending an empty-payload create.

### Round 625: handleBulkUpdate had neither a confirmation dialog nor an undo window, unlike its sibling handleBulkDelete

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 624, so a fresh Explore survey was launched on genuinely unexplored territory, explicitly told that case-insensitivity, orderedFields, BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES, round 623's Business Twin fix, round 624's handleBulkDuplicate fix, the keyword-collision class, migrate.ts's collision guard, the revalidation-effect family, Automation Rules, and withIdempotency coverage were all considered exhausted or heavily mined, and to also specifically check handleBulkDelete/handleBulkUpdate for a DIFFERENT kind of gap than round 624's own finding.

**The finding**: in the exact same bulk-actions bar, `handleBulkDelete` (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` lines 1932-1960) requires `window.confirm(...)` before doing anything, and even then still defers the real DELETE behind the same undo-window/"Undo" toast mechanism single-record delete uses -- explicitly, per that function's own doc comment, because "zero recovery once confirmed... meant real, permanent data loss." `handleBulkUpdate` (lines 1977-2001, with an identical duplicate in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` lines 3512-3534) had **neither** safeguard -- no `window.confirm`, no undo. Yet a bulk field update is just as destructive and just as irreversible as bulk delete: it overwrites a real field's value across every selected record in one stroke, with no version history and nothing to revert to. Worse, `handleBulkEditFieldChange` resets `bulkEditValue` to `""` (or `false` for boolean) the instant a field is picked from the dropdown, and the "Apply to N selected" button was enabled the instant `bulkEditField` was non-empty -- it did not require `bulkEditValue` to have actually been changed from that just-reset default. For any non-required field, clicking "Apply" immediately after picking the field (before typing a real value) sent `updateRecord(..., { [fieldName]: "" })` for every selected id -- `coerceValue` (`packages/db/src/repository.ts`) treats an empty value on a non-required field as valid and silently stores `null`, so this succeeds with no error and no indication anything was cleared.

**Independent verification**: read `handleBulkDelete` (lines 1932-1960) and `handleBulkUpdate` (lines 1977-2001, pre-fix) directly in `EntityPanel.tsx`, confirming the exact confirm/undo asymmetry the subagent reported -- `handleBulkDelete` has both `window.confirm` and the full `pendingDelete`/undo-toast machinery, `handleBulkUpdate` has grep-confirmed zero occurrences of `window.confirm`/`pendingUpdate`/undo anywhere in its body. Read `handleBulkEditFieldChange` (lines 2006-2010) and the "Apply" button's own JSX (line 2837, `disabled={bulkActionBusy}` only) directly, confirming the button is clickable the instant a field is chosen, with no gate on `bulkEditValue` having been touched. Re-confirmed `coerceValue`'s exact behavior from round 624's own investigation: `isEmpty` triggers a `ValidationError` only when `field.required`, otherwise returns `null` silently -- so a non-required field's accidental blank apply succeeds with no error. Checked `docs/roadmap.md`'s full history for any prior round touching `handleBulkUpdate` specifically -- found only round 544 (the `bulkActionBusy` double-click guard, a different failure mode: concurrent batches, not missing safeguards) and no round addressing confirmation/undo asymmetry.

**The fix**: added `if (!window.confirm(t("entity.bulk.confirmUpdate", { count: ids.length }))) return;` right after the existing early-return guards in `handleBulkUpdate`, in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`'s duplicate (plain English string in `codegen.ts`, matching that file's established no-i18n convention), mirroring `handleBulkDelete`'s own established pattern exactly. This does not add an undo window (unlike delete, there's no natural "previous values" snapshot to restore from for an update across N records) -- the confirm step alone stops the premature-click failure mode this round's finding centers on. Added a new i18n key `entity.bulk.confirmUpdate` (Hebrew + English).

**The tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, right after the existing "handleBulkUpdate refreshes and keeps only the ids that actually failed selected" test -- mocks `window.confirm` to return `false` and capture the message shown, asserts `updateRecord` is never called and nothing is refreshed, and that the confirm message names the translated `entity.bulk.confirmUpdate` key. The existing "refreshes and keeps only failed ids" test was updated to mock `window.confirm` to return `true` (it previously didn't need to touch `window.confirm` at all, since the function never called it). A matching pair of assertions was added inside `codegen.test.ts`'s existing combined handleBulkDuplicate/handleBulkUpdate test block (not as a new standalone `test()`, since it extends that block's existing scoped sections the same way its own duplicate/update/no-op sub-blocks already do).

**Regression-proof**: ran both test files against current (fixed) code fresh -- green (127/127 in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, 190/190 in `codegen.test.ts`). Backed up both source files, `git stash`'d just `EntityPanel.tsx`+`codegen.ts` (keeping both test files) -- each file's own new assertions failed exactly as predicted (confirm never called since the code path to it didn't exist), nothing else regressed in either file (126/127 and 189/190). Restored via `git stash pop`, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` against the pre-stash backups, re-ran both green (127/127, 190/190). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces`: db 181/181, shared 16/16, spec-engine 148/148, api 533/533, web 911/911 (+1), all clean. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `6cdc532`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. `handleBulkUpdate` now requires explicit confirmation before touching any record, in both the live preview and the exported app, matching the safeguard its equally-destructive sibling `handleBulkDelete` already had.

### Round 626: AutomationsPanel.tsx's handleDelete leaked busyRuleId after a successful delete, freezing every other rule's buttons

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 625. A fresh Explore survey was launched; its first lead (a "case-only entity rename" gap in `migrate.ts`'s historical-collision guard) was built, tested in isolation, and then found to directly break an existing, deliberate test (`migrate.test.ts`'s "diffAndMigrate refuses the collision even when the colliding entity's name differs from the removed one only by letter case") when the full suite ran -- the original "bug" was confirmed to be intentional, already-tested design (no in-place entity renaming is supported at the data-identity level; any name change is modeled as remove+add, and reusing any historically-known name, case-insensitively, is conservatively refused). That candidate was fully reverted via `git checkout -- packages/db/src/migrate.ts`. A second Explore agent spawn hit the session's weekly rate limit; pivoted to direct manual file-reading instead of retrying.

**The finding**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s `handleDelete` (lines 129-141) only reset `busyRuleId` to `null` inside its `catch` branch, unlike its sibling `handleToggle` (lines 116-127) which already uses a `finally` block for the same reset. Both the Enable/Disable and Delete buttons for *every* rule row are disabled by the single shared condition `busyRuleId !== null` (not scoped to the specific row being acted on) -- so once a delete succeeded, `busyRuleId` stayed permanently pointing at the now-deleted rule's id, and every other remaining rule's buttons were disabled for the rest of the panel's lifetime (until the panel was closed and reopened).

**Independent verification**: read `AutomationsPanel.tsx` in full (312 lines) and confirmed `handleDelete`'s `try`/`catch` had no `finally`, while `handleToggle`'s structurally-identical neighbor did. Confirmed the render-side consequence directly: both the toggle and delete `<button>`s for each row (lines 213, 216) use `disabled={busyRuleId !== null}`, not a per-row comparison. Wrote a standalone repro script creating two rules and simulating a successful delete of the first -- confirmed `busyRuleId` stayed set to the deleted rule's id and the surviving rule's own buttons reported `disabled: true`. Grepped `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` for any Automations-panel duplicate -- confirmed none exists (Automation Rules management is server-only, never exported into generated apps), so no port was needed.

**The fix**: added a `finally { setBusyRuleId(null); }` to `handleDelete` in `apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.tsx`, removing the now-redundant `setBusyRuleId(null)` from the `catch` branch, mirroring `handleToggle`'s existing pattern exactly.

**The tests**: a new test in `AutomationsPanel.test.ts`, right after the existing "AutomationsPanel actually removes the rule once the delete confirmation is accepted" test -- renders two rules, deletes the first via a mocked `window.confirm`/`fetch`, and asserts every button on the surviving rule's row is not disabled once the delete resolves.

**Regression-proof**: ran `AutomationsPanel.test.ts` against current (fixed) code -- green (9/9). Backed up the fixed source file, reverted only `AutomationsPanel.tsx` via `git checkout --`, kept the new test -- it failed exactly as predicted (`not ok 8`, busyRuleId left non-null), nothing else regressed (8/9). Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran clean (9/9). Full monorepo `npm test --workspaces`: db 181/181, shared 16/16, spec-engine 148/148, api 533/533, web 912/912 (+1), all clean. `npm run build --workspaces`: api esbuild and web `tsc -b`+vite both built clean; db/shared/spec-engine's "Missing script" errors confirmed benign as always. Commit `d33c5a8`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Every rule row's buttons now stay interactive after a successful delete elsewhere in the list, matching `handleToggle`'s existing correct behavior. The abandoned `migrate.ts` case-rename candidate must not be re-proposed without a way to genuinely distinguish a safe pure-rename from a dangerous same-case-insensitive-name coincidence -- the existing test's own fixture deliberately uses different field content between the two entities to make exactly that distinction.

### Round 627: the exported app's EntityView never highlighted a search match, unlike the live preview's real `<mark>`

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 626. A fresh Explore survey was launched, explicitly told that migrate.ts's collision guard, the revalidation-effect/visible-staleness family, Automation Rules, withIdempotency coverage, and the "sibling handler missing a safeguard its neighbor already has" pattern were all heavily mined, and pointed toward an under-mined angle: new drift between `codegen.ts`'s exported app and the live preview's `EntityPanel.tsx`, found by grepping for a component/helper name that exists in one but not the other.

**The finding**: the live preview's entity table has a search box that does two things -- filters visible rows via `matchesSearch`, and passes the same query down as `highlightQuery` into `Cell`, which wraps matching substrings in a real `<mark className="search-match">` via a `Highlighted` component (composed with `Linkified`, so link-detection and highlighting don't disable each other -- see `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` lines 99-148, 159-234). The exported/standalone app (`apps/api/src/codegen.ts`) has the exact same search box, wired to the exact same `matchesSearch` filtering (rows narrow correctly) -- but its own `Cell` (line 1511, pre-fix) took only `{ field, value, relationLabel, onJumpToRecord }`, with no `highlightQuery` param at all, and its `LinkifiedText` (line 1495) took only `{ text }`. There was no `Highlighted` function, no `splitHighlightSegments`, and no `.search-match` CSS rule anywhere in `codegen.ts`. The same gap also reached `BoardCard` (the Kanban board's per-card renderer), which in the live preview receives and threads `highlightQuery` to its own `Cell` call (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` line 2783) but didn't in `codegen.ts`.

**Independent verification**: grepped both files directly for `Highlighted`/`highlightQuery`/`search-match`/`splitHighlightSegments` -- confirmed all four exist and are used in `EntityPanel.tsx` but are completely absent from `codegen.ts` (zero matches). Confirmed `splitLinkSegments` (the sibling helper for URL/email linkification) *was* already correctly ported into `codegen.ts`, meaning the two features were authored together in the live preview but only one half made it into the export -- a different drift shape than the calendar-drag, CSV-import, or other previously-checked codegen-parity areas, all of which were independently re-verified as correctly ported. Confirmed `codegen.test.ts` had zero existing assertions about highlighting/`<mark>` for `Cell`/search, ruling out this being an already-known, deliberately-dropped feature. Traced `BoardCard`'s call site in both files directly: the live preview's `<BoardCard highlightQuery={search} .../>` (line 2783) has no counterpart prop in `codegen.ts`'s call site (line 4202, pre-fix).

### Round 629: the exported app's Global Search could only be opened with Ctrl/Cmd+K, never with "/" like the live preview

**Context**: continued the round 628 grep-list instead of opening a fresh Explore survey: `formatEntityFieldSummary` and `isEditableEventTarget` (`App.tsx`) and `isSameDay`/`isSameMonth` (`entityFormatting.ts`) were the names flagged as still unverified. `formatEntityFieldSummary` turned out to be a false positive -- it formats the spec-review screen's entity summary during project *building*, which the exported app has no equivalent of at all. `isEditableEventTarget` led to a real gap (below). `isSameDay`/`isSameMonth` were left unverified for a future round.

**The finding**: `App.tsx`'s own `isEditableEventTarget` (line 351) guards two keyboard shortcuts that both open overlays: `"/"` opens Global Search and `"?"` opens a keyboard-shortcuts cheat-sheet (round 199 and round 200 respectively, both in the live preview only). Grepped `codegen.ts` for `shortcuts`/`cheat-sheet` (case-insensitive) and found zero matches -- the exported app has no shortcuts-cheat-sheet dialog at all, so porting `"?"` would mean building a whole new dialog from scratch, a much bigger feature on the scale of round 202's Kanban drag-and-drop, not a one-round candidate. But Global Search *already exists* in `codegen.ts` (ported long before this round, opened via Ctrl/Cmd+K at line 5111 pre-fix) -- so `"/"` as a second way to open that *same, already-present* overlay was a small, concrete, narrowly-scoped gap on its own, independent of the cheat-sheet dialog. Confirmed via `git log`/roadmap.md search that rounds 199-201 and 227 (the two rounds that explicitly tracked "port to exported codegen" candidates around this same keyboard surface) never actually tracked the `"/"` shortcut itself -- round 201 ported drag-to-resize columns, round 227 ported column drag-reorder, but neither round's own accounting (nor round 218's, which round 227 corrected) ever listed `"/"` as a candidate at all. A genuinely missed gap, not a reopening of a closed finding.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported `App`'s `handleKeyDown` (lines 5109-5120, pre-fix) directly and confirmed it had exactly two branches -- Ctrl/Cmd+K and Escape -- with no `"/"` branch and no `isEditableEventTarget` equivalent anywhere in the file (grepped for both, zero matches). Read `App.tsx` lines 727-784 directly and confirmed the live preview's own handler has three entry branches (Ctrl+K, `"/"`, `"?"`) all guarded consistently, with `"/"` and `"?"` sharing the exact same `isEditableEventTarget` guard. Confirmed the exported app's own entity-level search box (`.entity-search`, `handleSearchKeyDown` at line 3739) has no `stopPropagation()` call on any key, so a window-level `"/"` listener would see every keystroke typed into it -- meaning the guard isn't cosmetic, it's required to keep a literal `"/"` typed into that box from being swallowed into opening the overlay instead.

**The fix**: added `isEditableEventTarget(target)` to `codegen.ts` (plain untyped JS, duck-typed on `tagName`/`isContentEditable` exactly like the live preview's version, no `export` since it's only used internally), placed just before `readStoredTheme`. Added a `"/"` branch to `handleKeyDown`, between the existing Ctrl/Cmd+K and Escape branches, calling the same `setShowSearch(true)` the Ctrl/Cmd+K branch already uses, guarded by `!isEditableEventTarget(e.target)`.

**The tests**: a new test rendering the real generated `App.jsx` end to end (via `writeGeneratedWebComponent` + dynamic import, the same pattern round 494's Escape-clears-query test established): confirms the overlay starts closed, types `"ac/"` into the real `.entity-search` box with a `"/"` keydown fired on that same input, confirms the overlay stays closed AND the literal `"/"` still lands in the text field unhijacked, then fires `"/"` on `window` (simulating focus outside any text field) and confirms the overlay now opens.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code -- green. Backed up the fixed `codegen.ts`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted (the final assertion: "a '/' pressed outside any text field must open the Global Search overlay"), confirming the old behavior correctly has no `"/"` handler at all. Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran clean.
