### Round 630: WhatsAppPanel's Retry button for a failed message stayed clickable on a DIFFERENT row while the first row's retry was still in flight, letting a real duplicate WhatsApp send reach a customer

**Context**: closed out round 628's grep-list first: `isSameDay`/`isSameMonth` (`entityFormatting.ts`) were confirmed false positives -- already ported under renamed counterparts `isSameCalendarDay`/`isSameCalendarMonth` (`codegen.ts` lines 2121-2125), with identical semantics including the "Today" button's disable-when-current-month behavior (line 2310, 2326). With the round-628 name list now fully exhausted, opened a fresh Explore survey (the standing instruction for when that happens), explicitly pointed at everything already heavily mined and told to look for a different angle. It returned one well-verified candidate: a sibling-handler-missing-a-safeguard bug in `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`, the same bug *class* round 626 found in `AutomationsPanel.tsx` (a shared busy-id slot mishandled relative to its siblings), but a structurally different bug (wrong disable scope, not a missing `finally`) with a materially worse consequence: a real duplicate message sent to a real customer, not just a frozen UI.

**The finding**: `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s `retryingId` (line 193, `useState<string | null>(null)`) is a single panel-wide slot remembering at most one in-flight retry, but the Retry button's own disabled check was scoped per-row (`disabled={retryingId === m.id}`, pre-fix) rather than "is any retry in flight" (`!== null`). Repro: the WhatsApp log has two failed messages, A and B, each with its own Retry button. Click Retry on A -- `handleRetry` (lines 561-581) calls `setRetryingId(A.id)` synchronously, then `await sendWhatsAppMessage(...)`, a real network round-trip (confirmed below). While A's send is still pending, click Retry on B -- `handleRetry(B)` immediately calls `setRetryingId(B.id)`, **overwriting** the shared slot. React re-renders: A's own disabled check (`retryingId === A.id`) is now `false`, since `retryingId` now holds B's id -- A's button visibly re-enables even though A's original request hasn't resolved. A second click on A fires `handleRetry(A)` again, concurrently with the first, sending the identical message body to the same real customer a second time. The sibling `deletingId`/delete-one-message button (line 196, same per-row check pre-fix) has the identical root-cause shape, though lower severity in practice since `handleDeleteMessage` is gated behind a blocking `window.confirm` and a redundant delete just 404s harmlessly.

**Independent verification**: read `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` lines 561-581 (`handleRetry`) and 965-972 (the button) directly and confirmed the exact pre-fix shape the survey described. Read `apps/web/src/api.ts:767-777` (`sendWhatsAppMessage`) and confirmed it generates a fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` idempotency key *per call* -- the two sends are never correlated server-side, so nothing dedupes them. Read `apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.ts:424` and confirmed `await session.sock.sendMessage(jid, { text: body })` is a genuine network await to the real WhatsApp socket (not a synchronous server call the "no await = no race" rule would exempt -- round 423/424/431-433's standing lesson to check this explicitly before trusting a race claim). Grepped the same `string | null`-busy-slot shape across the codebase and confirmed three other panels already solve this correctly with the global `!== null` form: `AutomationsPanel.tsx:213,216` (`busyRuleId !== null`), `CollaboratorsPanel.tsx:216,222` (`removingUserId !== null`), and `HistoryPanel.tsx:406,415` (`busyId !== null || deletingId !== null`) -- the last with an explicit doc comment (lines 396-401) spelling out this exact hazard almost verbatim ("clicking a second checkpoint's button while the first restore is still pending fires a second concurrent...request, and whichever response lands last silently overwrites the other's result"). Confirmed `handleDeleteMessage` (line 654) really does call `window.confirm` before `setDeletingId`, supporting the lower-severity read for that sibling button.

**The fix**: in `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`, changed both `disabled={retryingId === m.id}` (Retry button) and `disabled={deletingId === m.id}` (delete-one-message button) to the global `!== null` form, matching the three sibling panels' established convention. The busy-label text (`retryingId === m.id ? "Sending..." : "Retry"`, `deletingId === m.id ? "…" : "🗑️"`) stays scoped by id -- only `disabled` needed the global check. Added a comment above the Retry button spelling out the hazard, mirroring `HistoryPanel`'s own.

**The tests**: a new test renders the real `WhatsAppPanel` with two failed messages and a controllable `sendGate` promise (same pattern `CollaboratorsPanel.test.ts`'s own gated-fetch test uses -- the promise and its `resolve` are constructed once at the top level, not inside the mock's conditional branch, to avoid a TS narrowing pitfall hit on the first attempt: declaring `resolveSend` as `(() => void) | null` and assigning it only inside the mock's POST branch made `tsc` infer `never` at the later call site). Clicks Retry on the first row, confirms via the real send-mock that a request actually started, then asserts the SECOND row's Retry button is also disabled while the first is still pending -- the one new assertion that fails pre-fix -- resolves the gate, and confirms both buttons re-enable and only one send occurred in total.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code -- green. Backed up the fixed `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted, on exactly the one assertion built to catch this ("a DIFFERENT row's Retry button must also be disabled..."), nothing else. Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran clean. Hit one real, unrelated snag along the way: the first draft's `resolveSend` variable shape made `npm run build --workspace=@forge/web` fail `tsc -b` with "Type 'never' has no call signatures" -- fixed by restructuring to the gate-promise-at-top-level pattern above; re-ran the single test clean afterward and confirmed the build was the only thing that had been red. Final full run: `npm run build --workspace=@forge/web` clean (`tsc -b` + vite), full `@forge/web` suite 913/913 (+1), `@forge/api`/`@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `6db2947`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. WhatsAppPanel's Retry and delete-one-message buttons now both disable panel-wide while any one of their own kind is in flight, matching AutomationsPanel/CollaboratorsPanel/HistoryPanel's established convention, closing a real customer-facing duplicate-send hazard. The round-628 grep-list technique is now fully exhausted across all three live-preview files; round 630 instead reused the "sibling handler missing a safeguard its neighbor already has" pattern (last closed for AutomationsPanel in round 626) against a different file (WhatsAppPanel), via a fresh Explore survey rather than a targeted grep -- confirming that pattern-class still has reach once pointed at a not-yet-audited file, even with the specific codegen-parity name list dried up.

### Round 631: the exported app's dark/light theme never followed a live OS switch, and silently baked in the OS's theme as a fake explicit choice on first visit

**Context**: first re-ran round 630's own suggested next step directly (no fresh Explore survey yet): grepped every `useState<string | null>(null)` busy-id slot across `apps/web/src` and checked each one's disabled-scoping against the global-`!== null` vs. per-row-`=== id` bug class rounds 626/630 both found. Every remaining instance (`App.tsx`'s `templateBusy`/`cloningId`/`deletingId` on the home screen, `HistoryPanel`'s `busyId`/`deletingId`, `CollaboratorsPanel`'s `removingUserId`, `AutomationsPanel`'s `busyRuleId`, `AuthScreen`'s `pendingLoginCodeId`) was already correctly scoped -- this exact technique is now exhausted across the whole live-preview codebase. Opened a fresh Explore survey instead, explicitly told everything already mined (including the exhausted busy-slot technique) and pointed toward checking the same pattern *class* in files not yet looked at that way, or a genuinely different angle on codegen.ts-vs-live-preview parity (not the already-exhausted function-name-diff). It returned one very well-evidenced candidate: a dark-mode regression in the exported app's theme logic, with a real prior fix commit for the identical bug in the live preview that was simply never ported over.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported `App.jsx` (pre-fix, lines ~5144-5154) persisted the current theme to `localStorage` unconditionally inside a `useEffect` keyed on `[theme]` -- including on the very first mount, where `theme` was only ever *derived* from `prefersDarkFromSystem()` (no stored value existed yet), never actually chosen by anyone. This silently turned "no explicit choice yet" into a fake explicit choice on a person's very first visit to their downloaded app. There was also no `window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")` `"change"` listener anywhere in the file (confirmed via `grep -n "addEventListener(\"change\""` returning nothing) -- so even before that first write, a live OS light/dark switch was never followed at all. The result: open a freshly exported app for the first time with the OS in dark mode -- it loads dark (correct), but immediately persists `"dark"` as if chosen; switch the OS to light afterward -- nothing happens live, and even a reload stays stuck in dark, because the bogus stored value now always wins over `detectInitialTheme`'s own "explicit beats system" contract. The only way out is manually clicking the theme toggle once.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/theme/ThemeContext.tsx` directly and confirmed it already has the fix for this exact bug: a `hasExplicitChoiceRef` (line 36) that's `true` only when a real stored choice exists at mount or `toggleTheme` is actually called, gating both persistence and a `matchMedia` `"change"` listener (lines 42-55) that otherwise keeps following the OS live. Read `codegen.ts`'s pre-fix theme block directly (lines 5061-5154) and confirmed it has neither mechanism -- just `readStoredTheme`/`prefersDarkFromSystem`/`detectInitialTheme` (the same pure helpers, correctly ported) wired to an unconditional persist-on-every-change effect and a plain toggle button, with the effect's own comment explicitly (and incorrectly) claiming it "Mirrors the live Forge AI preview's own ThemeProvider." Confirmed via `git log` that dark mode was added to the exported app in an earlier commit than the live preview's own `hasExplicitChoiceRef` fix commit, and that fix's diff touches only `apps/web/src/theme/ThemeContext.tsx` and its test -- never `codegen.ts` -- confirming this is a genuinely missed port, not a reopening of a closed finding. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts`'s own pre-existing theme-toggle test asserted the buggy unconditional-persist shape as if it were the intended behavior, with no test anywhere for "follows a live OS switch" or "doesn't persist a derived-only theme" -- matching the live preview's own 3 dedicated regression tests for this exact bug in `ThemeContext.test.ts`.

**The fix**: in `codegen.ts`'s generated `App.jsx`, added `useRef` to the React import line. Captured `storedTheme` once per render (mirroring the live preview) and added a `hasExplicitChoiceRef` initialized from whether that stored value is `"light"`/`"dark"`. Split the old combined effect into two: one that only sets the `data-theme` attribute (no persistence), and a new one that attaches a `matchMedia` `"change"` listener which calls `setTheme` only while `hasExplicitChoiceRef.current` is still `false` (checked on every event, not just at listener-setup time, so a toggle made mid-session still blocks a later system switch). Moved persistence into the theme-switch button's own `onClick`, where it now also sets `hasExplicitChoiceRef.current = true` before writing to `localStorage` -- the exact split the live preview's fix already established.

**The tests**: updated the one pre-existing regex-extraction assertion that matched the old `onClick` body shape and the old unconditional-persist line. Added 3 new tests mirroring `ThemeContext.test.ts`'s own 3 regression tests exactly, against the real generated `App.jsx` (via `writeGeneratedWebComponent` + dynamic import, not a regex proxy): a `withFakeMatchMedia` helper (same event-dispatching stand-in shape as the live preview's test file's `createFakeMatchMedia`, since jsdom itself implements no `matchMedia` at all) confirms (1) the app follows a live OS switch in both directions when nothing has been explicitly chosen and never persists the derived-only theme, (2) an already-stored explicit choice wins at mount and is never overridden by a later system switch, and (3) a mid-session toggle-button click sets and persists an explicit choice that a subsequent system switch then also can't override.

**Regression-proof**: ran all 4 tests (3 new + 1 updated) against current (fixed) code -- green. Backed up the fixed `codegen.ts`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the test changes) -- 2 of 4 failed exactly as predicted: the updated regex assertion (old `onClick` shape gone) and the "follows a live OS switch... never persists a derived-only theme" test, failing on exactly the assertion built to catch it ("must not silently persist a system-derived (non-explicit) theme on mount", `'light' !== null`). The other 2 "ignores a system switch" tests passed even against the unfixed code, as expected -- the pre-fix code has no `matchMedia` listener at all, so it trivially "ignores" every system event regardless of explicit-choice state; those two tests still serve as real regression protection against a *different* future bug (e.g. a listener added later that forgets the guard), just not this one. Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran all 4 clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (esbuild + `tsc -b` + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite 539/539 (+3); `@forge/web`/`@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `d1cc5bf`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The exported app's theme now follows a live OS light/dark switch exactly like the live preview, and no longer bakes in a derived-only theme as a fake explicit choice on first visit. The round-630 busy-id-slot grep technique is now confirmed exhausted across the whole live-preview codebase (not just the files already checked) -- future rounds should look for the same "sibling missing a safeguard" pattern *class* in apps/api/src/routes/* or codegen.ts's own generated code instead, or open a fresh Explore survey directly.

### Round 632: the exported app's per-entity recent-searches store didn't filter non-string entries, unlike its own two sibling implementations in the same file

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 631. Opened a fresh Explore survey, explicitly told everything already mined including both exhausted codegen-parity techniques (the 78-name function-diff from rounds 627-629, and the busy-id-slot disabled-scoping grep from rounds 626/630), and pointed toward either a different file for the "sibling missing a safeguard" pattern class or another documented-fix-commit-never-ported instance like round 631's. It returned a third kind of sibling-inconsistency: not a disabled-scoping bug and not an unported live-preview fix, but one of *three* parallel implementations of the identical "don't trust a stored array's element types" defensive pattern, where two were correct and one -- in the same generated file as one of the correct ones -- was missing it.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` generates two separate localStorage-backed "recent searches" stores for the exported app. `getGlobalSearchRecentSearches` (lines 4569-4578) reads its stored array and immediately runs `parsed.filter((v) => typeof v === "string")` before returning it. But `readEntityRecentSearchesStore` (lines 898-908, pre-fix) -- the per-entity-table search box's own store, a few hundred lines earlier in the *same file* -- returned its parsed object as-is, with no equivalent per-element filter. Its only validation was the outer `typeof parsed !== "object" || Array.isArray(parsed)` shape check; nothing validated what a given entity's own array actually contained. The live preview's own counterpart this store is modeled on, `apps/web/src/entityRecentSearches.ts`'s `readStore()` (lines 8-22), does exactly what `getGlobalSearchRecentSearches` does: `value.filter((v): v is string => typeof v === "string")` per entity key. So two of the three implementations defend against a corrupted/foreign localStorage value containing a non-string array entry; only the exported app's entity-level store didn't.

**What a user would observe**: if `forge_entity_recent_searches` ever ends up holding a non-string entry in one of its per-entity arrays (a browser extension touching storage, a manual devtools edit, or any future code elsewhere writing something other than a trimmed string), `getEntityRecentSearches` would return the corrupted array unchanged -- a stray `42`/`null`/object could render as a recent-search chip -- and worse, the very next keystroke committing a new search (`handleSearchKeyDown` → `addEntityRecentSearch`, `codegen.ts:3739-3741`) runs `existing.filter((q) => q.toLowerCase() !== trimmed.toLowerCase())` unconditionally over that same array. A non-string entry there throws `TypeError: q.toLowerCase is not a function`, uncaught, from inside the search box's own `onKeyDown` handler -- there's no error boundary around `EntityView` to catch it. `removeEntityRecentSearch` has the identical crash path on clicking a stale chip's own remove button.

**Independent verification**: read `codegen.ts` lines 898-938 (the full pre-fix store) and 4569-4578 (`getGlobalSearchRecentSearches`) directly, confirming the exact asymmetry the survey described. Read `apps/web/src/entityRecentSearches.ts` lines 8-22 directly and confirmed its `readStore()` does the identical per-key, per-element filter the exported app's sibling store was missing. Read `codegen.ts:3739-3741` (`handleSearchKeyDown`) and confirmed `addEntityRecentSearch` really is called unconditionally on every Enter keypress with a non-empty query, with no try/catch anywhere between the keypress and the `.toLowerCase()` call. Checked `codegen.test.ts`'s existing coverage (the cap/dedupe/scoping test, lines 9970-9956 region) and confirmed it has no corrupted-data case at all, mirroring the gap the live preview's own round-401 `sharedProjectSeen.ts` fix was specifically introduced to close for a different store -- this project already treats "corrupted/foreign localStorage must not throw" as a standing convention, just hadn't applied it here.

**The fix**: rewrote `readEntityRecentSearchesStore` to build a fresh object via `Object.entries(parsed)`, keeping only array values and filtering each to `typeof v === "string"` -- an exact copy of the live preview's `readStore()` logic, adapted to this file's untyped-JS convention. `getEntityRecentSearches`/`addEntityRecentSearch`/`removeEntityRecentSearch` needed no changes themselves, since they already call `readEntityRecentSearchesStore()` and already guard with `Array.isArray(store[entityName])` -- once the store itself only ever contains string arrays, their existing logic is correct.

**The tests**: a new test extracts the real generated store functions (same `new Function(...)` execution pattern the existing cap/dedupe test already uses, not a reimplementation), seeds a fake `localStorage` with a corrupted array (`["acme", 42, null, "globex"]`) for one entity, and confirms: a plain `getEntityRecentSearches` call already returns only the two real strings (not just "doesn't crash on write"), `addEntityRecentSearch` does not throw and the result reflects the new entry prepended to the cleaned list, and `removeEntityRecentSearch` against a freshly-reseeded corrupted array also doesn't throw.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code -- green, along with both pre-existing recent-searches tests (entity-level cap/dedupe, Global-Search cap/dedupe) staying green. Backed up the fixed `codegen.ts`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test) -- failed exactly as predicted, on the first assertion ("the non-string entries must already be filtered out of a plain read"), confirming the corrupted entries really did survive a plain read pre-fix (the test never even reached the `addEntityRecentSearch`/`removeEntityRecentSearch` crash assertions, since the read-level assertion already caught it first). Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran all 3 recent-searches tests clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (esbuild + `tsc -b` + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite 540/540 (+1); `@forge/web`/`@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `82bd742`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The exported app's per-entity recent-searches store now defends against a corrupted/foreign localStorage value exactly like its own Global-Search sibling already does and the live preview's counterpart it's modeled on, closing a crash-on-next-keystroke hazard. Confirms a third distinct flavor of "sibling implementations disagree, one is right" is still findable via a fresh Explore survey once the two already-exhausted targeted-grep techniques (function-name-diff, busy-id-slot scoping) are explicitly ruled out up front.

### Round 633: the exported app's sort-keys store had no per-element shape validation, unlike every sibling preference store in the same file -- a malformed entry crashed the whole entity view's render

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 632. Opened a fresh Explore survey, explicitly pointed at the same "sibling implementations within codegen.ts itself" technique round 632 introduced (not yet exhausted, since codegen.ts has many small duplicated preference-store patterns) alongside the other still-open angles. It returned a sibling of round 632's own finding family -- same root pattern (a localStorage-backed preference store skipping shape validation its neighbors have) but in a different store, with a materially worse failure mode: not a crash on the *next* keystroke, but an unconditional crash on *every render* of the affected entity's table.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own comment (lines 1040-1044) says its group-by/view-mode/sort-keys/field-filters stores "mirror the live preview's own groupByPreference.ts, viewModePreference.ts, and sortKeysPreference.ts." Three of those four stores validate per-value *shape*, not just outer container type: `getPersistedGroupField` checks `typeof === "string"`, `getPersistedViewMode` checks the value is one of exactly `"table"`/`"board"`/`"calendar"`, and the collapsed-groups/collapsed-board-columns stores filter each array entry to `typeof === "string"`. But `readSortKeysStore` (pre-fix, lines 1112-1123) only checked that the *outer* container wasn't an array/null/non-object -- `getPersistedSortKeys` then returned `store[entityName]` as-is once it passed `Array.isArray(...)`, with no check that each array element was actually a well-formed `{field, direction}` object. That unvalidated array flows directly into `sortRecordsMulti`'s `for (const { field, direction } of sortKeys)` (line 1713), invoked synchronously inside a render-time `useMemo` (the table's own `visibleRecords`). Destructuring a non-object entry (`null`, a string, a number) throws a `TypeError`, uncaught -- the exported app registers no error boundary anywhere in the whole file -- blanking that entity's entire table on every single render until the `forge_sort_keys` key (deliberately unscoped by project id, per the same comment, since this single-tenant app has no project id) is manually cleared from localStorage.

**Independent verification**: read `codegen.ts` lines 1049-1103 (group-field/view-mode stores) and 1226-1289 (collapsed-groups/collapsed-board-columns stores) directly and confirmed each really does validate per-value shape, not just container type. Read the pre-fix `readSortKeysStore`/`getPersistedSortKeys` (lines 1112-1134) directly and confirmed the only check was the outer `typeof parsed !== "object" || Array.isArray(parsed)` -- nothing inspecting `store[entityName]`'s own elements. Read `sortRecordsMulti` (lines 1710-1722) directly and confirmed `for (const { field, direction } of sortKeys)` really does destructure every element unconditionally, with the `sortKeys.length === 0` early-return the only guard (which a malformed-but-non-empty array doesn't trip). Grepped the whole file for `ErrorBoundary`/`componentDidCatch`/`getDerivedStateFromError` -- zero matches, confirming there is genuinely no error boundary anywhere to catch this. Read the live preview's `apps/web/src/sortKeysPreference.ts` lines 9-33 directly and confirmed its `isSortKey`/`isSortKeyArray` helpers reject the *entire* per-entity array unless every element passes `isSortKey` (a stricter whole-array-rejection, not per-element filtering like the collapsed-groups stores use) -- and confirmed `sortKeysPreference.test.ts` has a dedicated, named regression test for exactly this scenario ("ignores an entry that isn't a real sort-key array (foreign data written by something else)").

**The fix**: added `isSortKey(value)` (checks `value` is a non-null object with `typeof value.field === "string"` and `value.direction` equal to `"asc"` or `"desc"`) and `isSortKeyArray(value)` (`Array.isArray(value) && value.every(isSortKey)`) to `codegen.ts`, exact copies of the live preview's own helpers adapted to this file's untyped-JS convention. Rewrote `readSortKeysStore` to build a fresh object via `Object.entries(parsed)`, keeping only values that pass `isSortKeyArray` -- mirroring `sortKeysPreference.ts`'s own whole-array rejection exactly, not the per-element filtering round 632's fix used for a different store (the two live-preview stores genuinely use different strategies, and this fix matches each one's own actual counterpart). First attempt introduced a real syntax error: the new doc comment used literal backtick characters to quote a code snippet (`` `for (const { field, direction } of sortKeys)` ``), which -- since this whole block is itself text inside an *outer* template literal in codegen.ts's own TypeScript source -- prematurely closed that outer template literal, spilling the quoted comment text out as bare, unparseable JavaScript (`esbuild` reported "Expected ';' but found 'for'" at the exact line). Fixed by rewording the comment to avoid backticks entirely, a variant of this file's own standing backslash/`${`-escaping discipline applied to a comment instead of code.

**The tests**: a new test extracts the real generated `readSortKeysStore`/`getPersistedSortKeys` (via the same broad regex-extraction span the existing round-trip test already uses) plus the real `compareValues`/`resolveSortValue`/`sortRecordsMulti` (same extraction regex as the existing multi-column-sort test), confirms a stored entry with an invalid `direction` value is rejected entirely (not partially kept), confirms a literal `null` entry alongside a valid one also rejects the whole array (matching the live preview's whole-array-rejection semantics, not a per-element filter), and confirms feeding the store's own cleaned return value into the real `sortRecordsMulti` never throws even though the raw stored value had a `null` entry.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code -- green, along with the pre-existing round-trip test for all four stores. Backed up the fixed `codegen.ts`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the test changes) -- failed exactly as predicted, on the first assertion ("an entry with an invalid direction must be rejected entirely"), returning the raw unvalidated `{field: "status", direction: "sideways"}` entry unchanged. Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran both sort-keys tests clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (esbuild + `tsc -b` + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite: one transient flake on the first run (540/541, in a test unrelated to this round's diff per the output), confirmed as non-reproducing by re-running the full suite twice more, both fully green (541/541 each time) -- `@forge/web`/`@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `a053e2f`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The exported app's sort-keys store now validates each entry's shape before trusting it, matching every sibling preference store in the same file and the live preview's own counterpart, closing a render-crashing hazard more severe than round 632's (every render, not just the next keystroke). The "sibling implementations within codegen.ts itself" technique has now found two real bugs in two rounds (632, 633) across the same family of ~8 localStorage-backed per-entity preference stores -- `getPersistedFieldFilters` was checked and ruled a non-issue (its one consumer coerces values safely via `String(...)`, so a non-string value there can't throw), and `getColumnOrder`/`applyColumnOrder` was also checked and ruled harmless (a non-string `Map` key simply fails to match, no throw) -- so this specific family of stores is now believed fully audited; a future round reusing this technique should look at other duplicated-helper families in codegen.ts, not revisit this one without a new angle.

### Round 634: the exported app's GlobalSearch overlay never trapped focus, moved focus in, or hid the background from assistive tech, unlike the live preview's identical dialog

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 633. Opened a fresh Explore survey, explicitly told every exhausted technique (function-name-diff, busy-id-slot scoping, and the now-fully-audited preference-store family within codegen.ts) and pointed toward either a genuinely new duplicated-helper family or a different kind of codegen.ts-vs-live-preview parity gap entirely. It returned a dialog-accessibility gap: the live preview's own `useDialogFocusTrap.ts` + `domInert.ts` pair -- added to the live preview's `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` in commit `577ee2c` -- was never ported to `codegen.ts`'s own `GlobalSearch` renderer, the exported app's only overlay dialog.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/useDialogFocusTrap.ts` gives the live preview's search dialog three behaviors once open: it moves focus into the dialog on mount (unless `autoFocus` already placed it), traps Tab/Shift+Tab so the user can't tab out to the page behind it, and restores focus to whatever had it before the dialog opened once it closes (captured via `useRef(document.activeElement)` at render time, not inside the effect, since effects run after `autoFocus` has already moved focus). `apps/web/src/domInert.ts`'s `hideBackgroundFromAssistiveTech` additionally marks every sibling of every ancestor up to (not including) `document.body` as `inert` + `aria-hidden="true"` while the dialog is open, so a screen reader's virtual cursor can't wander into the page behind it, and restores exactly what it changed on cleanup. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported `GlobalSearch` component (the exported app's own equivalent overlay) had none of this: opening it left focus wherever it already was, Tab could walk straight out of the panel into the entity table sitting (only visually) behind it, that table remained fully reachable by a screen reader the whole time the panel was "open," and closing the panel never returned focus anywhere.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/useDialogFocusTrap.ts` in full (143 lines) and confirmed the focus-trap/move-in/restore-on-unmount mechanics directly, including the render-time (not effect-time) capture of the previously-focused element. Read `apps/web/src/domInert.ts` in full (51 lines) and confirmed the sibling-of-ancestor walk, the `inert`+`aria-hidden` marking, and the exact-restore cleanup. Read `apps/web/src/useDialogFocusTrap.test.ts` (lines 1-160) and mirrored its test patterns. Read `codegen.ts`'s pre-fix `GlobalSearch` component directly and confirmed it had no `ref`, no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, no focus-trap keydown handler, and no inert/aria-hidden marking of anything outside the panel -- just a plain `<div className="search-panel">`. Confirmed via `git log` on `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` that commit `577ee2c` added this exact mechanism to the live preview and never touched `codegen.ts`. Separately confirmed `codegen.ts` already has correct, working Escape-key handling for this same dialog (an App-level Escape listener plus a `data-escape-handled-locally` convention, present at both the App-listener site and inside `GlobalSearch` itself) -- so Escape was deliberately left untouched rather than re-added, avoiding redundant/conflicting logic.

**The fix**: added `hideGlobalSearchBackgroundFromAssistiveTech(dialogElement)` to `codegen.ts`, a direct port of `domInert.ts`'s sibling-of-ancestor walk (marking each with a `data-forge-dialog-inert` marker plus `inert`/`aria-hidden`, and returning a cleanup that restores each sibling's prior `inert`/`aria-hidden` state exactly). Inside `GlobalSearch`, added a `dialogRef` and a `previouslyFocusedRef` (captured via `useRef(document.activeElement)` at render time, matching the live preview's own rationale for not capturing it inside the effect). Added a new effect that calls the inert-hider, moves focus into the first focusable element (or the container itself if none exists) unless focus is already inside it, attaches a keydown handler that traps Tab/Shift+Tab between the first and last focusable elements, and on cleanup removes the listener, restores the background, and refocuses whatever had focus before the dialog opened. Added `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` (pointing at a newly-id'd heading) to the panel's markup.

**The tests**: added two new tests to `codegen.test.ts` rendering the real generated `GlobalSearch` via `writeGeneratedWebComponent` + dynamic import (not a regex proxy). The first creates a real trigger button in `document.body`, focuses it, opens the dialog, confirms `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="true"`/`aria-labelledby` resolve to a real element and focus landed on `.global-search-input`, confirms Tab from the last focusable element wraps to the first and Shift+Tab from the first wraps to the last (via real `fireEvent.keyDown`), then unmounts and confirms focus returns to the original trigger. The second creates a `<main>` sibling standing in for the rest of the app, opens the dialog, confirms that sibling gets `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert`, then unmounts and confirms both are lifted.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the pre-existing 16-test GlobalSearch suite and the 5 App-level nested-render tests (Escape-clears-query, "/" shortcut, EntityView Escape, relation-cell-jump, jump-to-record) -- all passed, confirming no regression and no conflict with the untouched Escape handling. Backed up the fixed `codegen.ts`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the test changes) -- both new tests failed exactly as predicted (missing `role="dialog"`, `aria-hidden` never applied). Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran the full 20-test GlobalSearch-related suite clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (esbuild + `tsc -b` + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite 543/543 (+2); `@forge/web`/`@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `1d08710`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The exported app's GlobalSearch overlay now traps focus, moves focus in on open, hides the background entity table from assistive tech while open, and restores focus to the trigger on close -- matching the live preview's own dialog exactly, closing a real keyboard- and screen-reader-accessibility gap in the exported app's only modal dialog. This is a new technique variant ("a documented behavioral hook/utility in the live preview never ported to codegen.ts's own use of the same UI pattern," distinct from round 631's "a specific bugfix commit never ported") -- future rounds could look for other live-preview hooks/utilities (e.g. any other `useXxx` hook in `apps/web/src`) whose equivalent behavior might be missing from codegen.ts's generated components.

### Round 635: two of Business Twin's four observation builders could produce identical-looking lines when two fields on the same entity shared a display label -- the exact gap round 623 already closed for a fifth

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 634. Opened a fresh Explore survey, explicitly told every exhausted technique (function-name-diff, busy-id-slot scoping, the preference-store family within codegen.ts, and round 634's "live-preview hook never ported to codegen.ts's matching UI pattern"), and pointed at either another `useXxx` hook, a different duplicated-helper family within codegen.ts, or any other genuinely new, independently-verifiable bug. It returned a bug entirely outside codegen.ts: a label-collision gap in `apps/api/src/twin.ts`'s Business Twin observation builders, already fixed once for a sibling function in round 623 but never ported to three others in the same file -- and backed its finding with an actual `tsx --test` run against the real `computeBusinessTwin`, not just a read of the code.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/twin.ts`'s `computeRelationCoverageObservations` (lines 68-94), `computeNumericAggregateObservations` (lines 347-382), and `computeEnumDistributionObservations` (lines 396-433) each built their observation text from `fieldLabel` (`field.label ?? field.name`) alone, with nothing disambiguating two fields on the same entity that happen to share a label. `FieldSchema`/`EntitySchema` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) only ever enforce uniqueness on a field's internal `name` (case-insensitively), never on its display `label` -- and the field-label route (`PATCH /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/fields/:fieldName/label` in `routes/projects.ts`) lets a user rename any field to any label with no collision check at all, reachable with two clicks through `FieldLabelEditor`. A real example: an `Order` entity with `subtotal` and `shipping`, both renamed to "Amount", produces two Business Twin lines reading `Total "Amount" in "Orders": 800 (average 400 across 2 records).` and `Total "Amount" in "Orders": 30 (average 15 across 2 records).` -- a business owner reading the Twin panel (whose whole stated purpose, per its own doc comment, is "genuine facts... a real person can decide to act on") has no way to tell which of their two money fields either line is actually about. The identical shape hits relation-coverage ("... have no "Customer" set.") and enum-distribution ("Status" breakdown) text the same way. This exact reachable-collision state was already established once before, in round 287's CSV-import fix for a different symptom (columns silently misassigned).

**Independent verification**: read `twin.ts` in full for all five observation builders. Confirmed `computeRelationHubObservation` (lines 104-204, esp. 174-193) already disambiguates its own breakdown text with `(via <fieldLabel>)` whenever two relation fields on the same entity happen to share a *source* label, added in round 623 specifically because (its own comment) "those lines would read as identical-looking duplicates" -- confirmed via `twin.test.ts` lines 254-302's dedicated regression test for exactly that. Confirmed the other three builders had no equivalent check by reading their full bodies directly (reproduced above). Read `FieldSchema`/`EntitySchema` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` directly (lines 92-162) and confirmed only `name` uniqueness is enforced -- `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateFieldNames` runs against `.name`, never `.label`. Read the field-label PATCH route in `routes/projects.ts` (lines 1564-1600) directly and confirmed it writes any label straight through `RenameFieldLabelSchema` with no collision check against sibling fields. Checked `twin.test.ts`'s existing coverage for the three affected functions (numeric-aggregate, enum-distribution, relation-coverage tests) and confirmed none covered a same-label case, unlike `computeRelationHubObservation`'s own dedicated test.

**The fix**: in each of the three functions, added a `labelOccurrences` map built once per entity (counting how many fields of that function's relevant type share each label), then -- for the field actually being reported -- checked whether its own label's count exceeds 1 and, if so, appended `` (${field.name})`` right after the closing quote, mirroring `computeRelationHubObservation`'s own established "quote the label, then a parenthetical qualifier" text shape (adapted here to use the field's own name as the disambiguator, since the label itself is what collided -- unlike the hub observation's case, where the labels genuinely differ and the field label itself is the disambiguator).

**The tests**: three new tests (one per fixed function), each constructing an entity with two same-typed fields sharing an identical label (two relation fields both labeled "Customer"; two number fields both labeled "Amount"; two enum fields both labeled "Status"), confirming exactly one observation is produced per field (not collapsed into one, and not silently dropping one), that each observation's text includes its own field's real `(fieldName)` disambiguator, and that each field's own real values (sums/breakdowns) land in the correct, correctly-attributed observation rather than being confusable with its sibling's.

**Regression-proof**: ran all three new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing `twin.test.ts` suite (28/28, including the untouched `computeRelationHubObservation` disambiguation test). Backed up the fixed `twin.ts`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the test changes) -- all three new tests failed exactly as predicted, each assertion showing the real duplicate-looking output (`'In "Tickets", 1 of 1 records have no "Customer" set.'` appearing twice; `'Total "Amount" in "Orders": 800...'` / `'...: 30...'` with no disambiguator; `'"Status" breakdown...'` twice). Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran the full 28-test suite clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (`tsc -b` + esbuild + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite 546/546 (+3); `@forge/web`/`@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `5f508f4`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Business Twin's numeric-aggregate, enum-distribution, and relation-coverage observations now disambiguate same-entity, same-label fields exactly like `computeRelationHubObservation` already did, closing a real user-facing ambiguity in the one panel whose entire purpose is reporting trustworthy, actionable facts. This confirms round 631/634's "a fix already applied to one sibling function/component but never ported to its close relatives" technique generalizes beyond codegen.ts-vs-live-preview parity -- it also applies *within* a single file, across genuinely different functions that happen to share an underlying data-shape risk (here: label non-uniqueness). A future round could check whether any other per-field or per-entity text-building code elsewhere in the codebase (outside twin.ts and codegen.ts's already-audited CSV import) has the same unguarded-label-collision shape.

### Round 636: the "take it with you" calendar export (.ics) showed two indistinguishable description lines when two fields on the same entity shared a label -- the same gap round 635 just fixed in a different file

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 635. The first Explore survey this round re-proposed `migrate.ts`'s case-only-entity-rename candidate (round 626's own abandoned finding) as if it were new -- its suggested fix was to treat a historical table-name collision as safe whenever the colliding name is case-insensitively identical to the entity's own new name. Independent verification caught this before any code was touched: that condition is tautological, since the guard's own `collidingName` lookup (`tableNameFor(name).toLowerCase() === tableLower`) can only ever find names that are case-insensitively identical to the entity's new name in the first place -- it does not, and cannot, distinguish the proposed safe-rename scenario from the existing `migrate.test.ts` regression test's deliberately-dangerous scenario (two genuinely different entities, "Order2"/text-field vs. "order2"/number-field, colliding by case alone), which must keep being rejected. Implementing it as proposed would have broken that test, reproducing round 626's own documented failure exactly. Declined without writing any code, and a second Explore survey was launched with that reasoning included so the candidate stays closed. It returned a genuinely new instance of round 635's own technique, applied to a different file: the live preview's `calendarIcs.ts` and its byte-for-byte port in `codegen.ts` had the identical unguarded-label-collision gap round 635 fixed in `twin.ts`, confirmed via a real `tsx --test` repro, not just a code read.

**The finding**: `buildCalendarIcs`'s DESCRIPTION-line builder (`apps/web/src/calendarIcs.ts` lines 142-159, identically duplicated in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` lines 2280-2312) builds each line as `` `${f.label ?? f.name}: ${value}` `` for every field on the entity other than the date/label/end fields, with nothing checking whether two of those fields happen to share a label. `FieldSchema`/`EntitySchema` only ever enforce uniqueness on a field's `name`, never its `label` (same fact round 635 already confirmed), and the field-label PATCH route lets a user rename any two fields on an entity to the identical label with zero collision check, reachable via `FieldLabelEditor` in two clicks. A concrete example: an `Order` entity with `subtotal` and `shipping` number fields, both renamed to "Amount", exported via the real "download calendar (.ics)" button and opened in any real calendar app (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook) shows a VEVENT whose DESCRIPTION reads `Amount: 800` then `Amount: 30` -- two identical-looking lines with no way to tell which was the subtotal and which was the shipping cost, in the one feature whose entire purpose (per the live preview's own comment) is "take your records with you."

**Independent verification**: read `calendarIcs.ts`'s full `buildCalendarIcs` (lines 93-170) directly and confirmed the unguarded `` `${f.label ?? f.name}: ${value}` `` line. Read `codegen.ts`'s generated copy (lines 2280-2325) directly and confirmed the identical gap in the exported app (`` \`\${f.label || f.name}: \${value}\` ``). Confirmed via `calendarIcs.test.ts`/`codegen.test.ts` grep that no existing test covers a same-label scenario for this function, unlike the dedicated tests that already exist for relation-resolution, enum-translation, and RFC-5545 escaping in the same function. ### Round 637: CSV export (both the per-entity "Export CSV" button and the full-project backup ZIP) showed two indistinguishable header columns when two fields shared a label -- the third instance of round 635/636's unguarded-label-collision gap

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 636. Opened a fresh Explore survey, explicitly pointed at round 636's own suggested follow-up ("check CSV export headers, print-sheet rendering, or Kanban board cards for the same unguarded-label-collision shape") alongside other still-open directions, and told to say plainly if a checked area was already safe rather than force a weak finding. It found a real, verified instance in CSV export -- the strongest of the candidates it checked, since a corrupted header silently breaks *structured* data (and any later re-import), not just a one-off printed page.

**The finding**: `recordsToCsv`'s header-row builder had the identical gap already fixed for Business Twin (635) and the calendar export (636), in three separate places: `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s `recordsToCsv` (line 1024, pre-fix: `fields.map((f) => csvEscape(f.label ?? f.name)).join(",")`), the exported app's own copy of the same function inside `codegen.ts`'s generated `EntityView.jsx` (lines 1813-1816, same shape with `||`), and a third, independent copy inside `codegen.ts`'s generated `server.js` -- `entityToCsv`, the project-wide "Backup All Data" ZIP's per-entity CSV builder (lines 645-651). All three built their header purely from `f.label ?? f.name`/`f.label || f.name` with no check for a repeated label. A concrete example: an `Order` entity with `subtotal` and `shipping` number fields both renamed to "Amount" (reachable via the Field Label editor, as established in rounds 623/635/636 -- only `name` is enforced unique, never `label`) produces a CSV whose header row reads `Amount,Amount`. Opened in Excel/Sheets, or fed back through the app's own CSV *import* feature (which matches columns by header text), there is no way to tell which column is which, and a re-import would silently misassign one field's data onto the other -- the same root hazard round 287 already fixed for a *different* symptom in the import path itself, now found on the export side too.

**Independent verification**: read `recordsToCsv` in full in `entityFormatting.ts` and confirmed the exact unguarded line. Read `codegen.ts`'s two separate generated copies (`recordsToCsv` inside `EntityView.jsx`'s template, and `entityToCsv` inside `server.js`'s template) directly and confirmed both have the identical shape -- genuinely two separate code paths, not one function reused, since the per-entity CSV export and the backup endpoint are unrelated features that happen to duplicate the same formatting logic (the same "third, separate copy" pattern rounds 117/118 already documented for this exact file trio). Grepped `entityFormatting.test.ts`/`codegen.test.ts` for any existing same-label test on either function -- none exists. The agent also checked `RecordPrintSheet`/`RecordListPrintSheet`/`BoardCard` (`EntityPanel.tsx` lines 276/332/413) and found the identical unguarded shape there too, but that was left out of this round's fix to keep the diff focused on the strongest, most-verified instance (silently corrupted structured/re-importable data) -- a future round could port the same fix to the print/board rendering paths.

**The fix**: in `entityFormatting.ts`'s `recordsToCsv`, added a `labelOccurrences` map (mirroring rounds 635/636's established pattern exactly) and appended `` (${f.name})`` to a column's header whenever its label repeats among the entity's fields. Ported the identical logic into `codegen.ts`'s `recordsToCsv` (adapted to that file's untyped-JS convention) and into the separate `entityToCsv` backup-CSV builder in the same file.

**The tests**: a new test in `entityFormatting.test.ts` builds an `Order` entity with `subtotal`/`shipping` number fields both labeled "Amount", confirms the real header reads `Amount (subtotal),Amount (shipping)`. Two matching tests in `codegen.test.ts` extract and execute the real generated `recordsToCsv` (from `EntityView.jsx`) and the real generated `entityToCsv` (from `server.js`) via the same `new Function(...)` extraction harness the pre-existing CSV-formatting tests in this file already use, confirming the identical disambiguation in both of the exported app's own independent copies.

**Regression-proof**: ran all three new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing suites in both files (`entityFormatting.test.ts` 150/150, `codegen.test.ts` 203/203). Backed up both fixed source files, reverted only them via `git checkout --` (keeping all three test files) -- all three new tests failed exactly as predicted, each showing the real unguarded `Amount,Amount` header. ### Round 638: print sheets and board cards (both the live preview and the exported app) showed two indistinguishable field labels when fields shared a label -- finishing the sweep round 637 left open

**Context**: no backup candidate was ready after round 637, but round 637 itself had already confirmed the exact bug (`RecordPrintSheet`/`RecordListPrintSheet`/`BoardCard` in `EntityPanel.tsx` lines 276/332/413, deliberately left unfixed) -- so this round implemented that ready candidate directly rather than opening a fresh Explore survey. Independently re-verified by reading all three render sites directly before touching any code, plus their equivalents in `codegen.ts`, confirming the generated app has the identical gap in all three (and that `BoardCard`'s own copy didn't even have the `|| f.name` fallback the other two had).

**The finding**: `RecordPrintSheet`'s `<dt>{f.label ?? f.name}</dt>` (print-one-record sheet), `RecordListPrintSheet`'s `<th key={f.name}>{f.label ?? f.name}</th>` (print-the-visible-list sheet), and `BoardCard`'s `<span className="muted small">{f.label ?? f.name}</span>` (Kanban board cards) all rendered a field's label with no check for a repeated label among sibling fields -- the same gap already fixed in Business Twin (635), the calendar export (636), and CSV export (637). An entity with two number fields (e.g. `subtotal`/`shipping`) both renamed to "Amount" via the Field Label editor would show two identical "Amount" entries on a printed record sheet, two identical "Amount" columns on a printed list, and two identical "Amount" labels stacked on a board card -- in all three cases with no way to tell which field either one actually was. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `RecordPrintSheet`/`RecordListPrintSheet`/`BoardCard` (the exported app's own copies) had the identical shape, and `BoardCard`'s copy there was even one step worse: `{f.label}` with no `|| f.name` fallback at all, so a field with no label set would have rendered as literally nothing.

**Independent verification**: read all three live-preview render sites directly (lines 276, 332, 413 as flagged) and confirmed each builds its label text with no disambiguation. Read `codegen.ts`'s `RecordPrintSheet`/`RecordListPrintSheet`/`BoardCard` directly and confirmed the identical gap, plus the extra `BoardCard` fallback gap. Grepped both `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts` for any existing same-label coverage on these three components -- none exists, matching the established pattern that this specific failure mode had never been tested anywhere.

**The fix**: rather than reimplementing the label-occurrences logic a fourth time, extracted `recordsToCsv`'s existing inline computation (added in round 637) into two shared helpers in `entityFormatting.ts` -- `fieldLabelOccurrences(fields)` (builds the label→count map) and `fieldDisplayLabel(field, occurrences)` (returns the label, with `` (${field.name})`` appended when ambiguous) -- and refactored `recordsToCsv` itself to call them (behavior unchanged, confirmed by the pre-existing CSV tests still passing unmodified). Wired the same two helpers into `RecordPrintSheet`, `RecordListPrintSheet`, and `BoardCard` in `EntityPanel.tsx`, computing the occurrences map once per render (per `fields`/`otherFields` list) rather than per field. Applied the identical refactor to `codegen.ts`: extracted its own `recordsToCsv`'s inline computation into generated-code equivalents `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` (plain-JS style, object literal instead of `Map`), and wired them into the generated `RecordPrintSheet`/`RecordListPrintSheet`/`BoardCard` -- `BoardCard`'s label line now also gains the `|| f.name` fallback as a direct consequence of routing through the shared helper.

**The tests**: a new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` renders the real `EntityPanel` with an `Order` entity whose `subtotal`/`shipping` fields both carry the label "Amount", clicks the row's Print button and confirms the print-record-sheet's `<dt>` elements read `"Amount (subtotal)"`/`"Amount (shipping)"`, clicks "Print list" and confirms the same disambiguation in the `<th>` elements, then switches to board view and confirms the same disambiguation on the board card's field labels -- one test exercising all three fixed surfaces through real DOM interaction, mirroring the file's existing Print/Print-list/board-view test patterns. A matching test in `codegen.test.ts` renders the real generated `EntityView` (via `writeGeneratedWebComponent` + dynamic import, not a reimplementation) against the same fixture and exercises the identical three interactions. The four pre-existing `recordsToCsv` regex-extraction tests in `codegen.test.ts` (added/updated in round 637) were updated to also extract the new `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` generated functions into their `new Function(...)` harness, since `recordsToCsv` now calls them.

The new `EntityPanel.test.ts` test first failed for an unrelated reason (its custom `Order` entity didn't match the shared `mockRecordsFetch` helper's hardcoded `/entities/Deal` route) -- fixed by writing a small inline fetch mock for `/entities/Order` instead, matching the established per-test convention other custom-entity tests in this file already use. ### Round 639: a relation field retargeted to a different entity (or reusing a column that lost its FK) never disabled a `field_equals` automation rule built on it, letting the rule fire against a coincidentally-id-matching record of the wrong entity

**Context**: the unguarded-label-collision family (635-638) is closed, with no new ready candidate after it. A fresh Explore survey was launched with that family and `migrate.ts`'s case-only-entity-rename (round 626/636, tautological "fix" already rejected twice) explicitly marked off-limits, to steer toward genuinely new territory. It returned a new, well-evidenced candidate: `diffAndMigrate`'s relation-retarget detection (`relation_target_changed`/`relation_missing_fk`) never fed `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable`, unlike its `type_changed`/enum-narrowing siblings in the exact same per-field loop.

**The finding**: `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`'s `diffAndMigrate` already disables any `field_equals` automation rule referencing a field whose `type_changed` (lines ~356-361) or whose enum `enumValues` narrowed away the rule's own stored value (lines ~370-375), by adding the field to a `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable` map that a later sweep (lines ~590-591) feeds into `disableAutomationRulesForField`. The reasoning is that a `field_equals` rule's stored `fieldValue` stops being a trustworthy thing to compare against once the field's own meaning has shifted underneath it. A relation field's FK target shifting underneath it is the exact same hazard, arguably worse: the rule's stored `fieldValue` on a relation column is a raw row id, meaningful only against whatever table the FK actually watches. Two relation branches detect exactly this (`relation_target_changed`, when a surviving field's `relationTo` is repointed to a different existing entity but the physical FK -- which SQLite can't retroactively repoint -- still watches the old table; `relation_missing_fk`, when a column reused after an earlier removal never had a FK at all) in two separate code paths (the `prevField` branch, lines ~376-438, and the "reused column" branch, lines ~478-509, for a field whose name was removed and then reused) -- four call sites in total (two change types × two paths) -- and none of the four ever added the field to `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable`. A `field_equals` rule on such a field survives every refine fully enabled, and since the id it's comparing against is just an integer, it can coincidentally match a real record of the *new*, unrelated target entity and fire for a reason that has nothing to do with what the rule was actually written for -- not merely stale (the removed-field/removed-entity sweep already handles "gone"), but silently wrong while the field is still very much present and in active use.

**Independent verification**: read `migrate.ts` lines 335-444 directly and confirmed the `type_changed`/enum-narrowing branches both call `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable.get(entity.name)!.add(field.name)`, while the `relation`-to-`relation` branch immediately below them (pushing `relation_target_changed`/`relation_missing_fk`) genuinely never did. Read lines 460-509 directly and confirmed the sibling "reused column" branch has the identical gap for both change types. Read `automations.ts`'s `matchesTrigger` (lines 37-51) directly and confirmed a `field_equals` rule's check is a plain `String(record[rule.fieldName]) === rule.fieldValue` -- no awareness of what table a relation field's id is supposed to belong to, confirming the id-coincidence hazard is real and not caught anywhere else. Read `disableAutomationRulesForField`/`disableAutomationRulesForEntity` in `packages/db/src/automations.ts` (lines 251-278) and the consumer sweep in `migrate.ts` (lines 567-591) directly, confirming `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable` is exactly the existing, already-wired mechanism this fix needed to feed -- no new plumbing required. Grepped `migrate.test.ts` for every existing automation+relation test and confirmed none covers a `field_equals` rule surviving a relation retarget or a reused-column FK loss -- only separate tests exist for the migration-report side of `relation_target_changed`/`relation_missing_fk` (reporting the change, not touching automations) and separate automation-disable tests for `type_changed`/enum-narrowing/letter-case.

**The fix**: added the same four-line `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable.get(entity.name)!.add(field.name)` pattern (mirroring the `type_changed`/enum-narrowing branches exactly) at all four call sites: the `prevField` branch's `relation_target_changed` and `relation_missing_fk` pushes, and the "reused column" branch's `relation_target_changed` and `relation_missing_fk` pushes. No change needed in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` -- confirmed directly via grep that the exported app's generated code has no `diffAndMigrate`/incremental-migration concept at all, so this bug and its fix are specific to the live app's own database layer.

**The tests**: two new tests in `migrate.test.ts`. The first builds an `Order` entity with a `customerId` relation field pointing at `Customer`, inserts a `field_equals` rule on it plus an unrelated `field_equals` rule on `total`, then refines `relationTo` to a different existing entity (`Vendor`) -- confirms the diff reports `relation_target_changed` and that the `customerId` rule is disabled while the unrelated `total` rule stays enabled. The second mirrors the existing `relation_missing_fk` repro (a `boolean` field removed, then re-added under the same name as a `relation`, reusing the same FK-less INTEGER column) but deliberately inserts the `field_equals` rule only *after* the field has already been removed from the spec -- so the pre-existing field-removal sweep (which already, correctly, disables a rule that existed *before* its field was dropped) can't be what's credited for the disable, isolating the new `relation_missing_fk` branch's own fix as the only mechanism that can still catch it.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing `migrate.test.ts` suite (39/39, +2). Backed up the fixed `migrate.ts`, reverted only that file via `git checkout --` (keeping the test changes) -- both new tests failed exactly as predicted (`true !== false`: the retargeted/reused-column rule stayed enabled), with no other test affected. Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran the single-file suite clean (39/39). Full `@forge/db` suite 183/183. Full `@forge/api` build (esbuild) clean; full `@forge/api` suite 550/550, unaffected since `codegen.ts` needed no change. `@forge/web`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `84b6c38`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A relation field's retarget or FK-loss now correctly disables any `field_equals` automation rule built on it, closing a gap in the exact safety sweep `type_changed`/enum-narrowing already covered for two of three ways a field's *meaning* can shift underneath a rule without the field itself disappearing. This is a new instance of round 631/634/635's own "a fix already applied to sibling code but never ported to a structurally parallel branch" technique, found this time inside a single function's own per-field loop rather than across files -- a future round could check whether `routes/projects.ts`'s `validateAutomationFieldValue` (which validates a rule's `fieldValue` at *creation* time) has any related gap for relation fields, though that is a distinct question from this round's migration-time fix and was not investigated here.
