### Round 641: migration-impact and checkpoint-diff warnings named a removed/added field by a shared label alone -- actively claiming a label was "no longer reachable" even while a same-labeled sibling field was still live, a sixth and seventh instance of the unguarded-label-collision shape

**Context**: round 640's own closing note explicitly warned that "closed" doesn't rule out another copy, and suggested a repo-wide grep sweep for remaining `f.label ?? f.name`/`f.label || f.name` patterns as a low-priority future check. This round's Explore survey ran exactly that sweep first (per round 640's own suggestion) and it did NOT come back clean -- it found a new cluster in two files neither of which had ever been touched by rounds 635-640: `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts` (the live build-pipeline's Architect-step impact summary) and `apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts` (the Time Machine panel's checkpoint-restore preview).

**The finding**: `computeImpact`'s `changedEntities` (`pipeline.ts` lines 136-144, pre-fix) built `newFieldNames`/`removedFieldNames`/`tightenedFieldNames` from `f.label ?? f.name` with no check for a repeated label, and `architectEvent` (lines 160-197) fed `removedFieldNames` straight into the build-stream's user-facing warning text (`` `${e.label} lost field(s): ${e.removedFieldNames.join(", ")}` ``, " -- their data is kept but is no longer reachable through the app"). Unlike every previously-fixed instance (635-640), which only made two distinct things *look* identical in a list, this one is actively **wrong**: removing only one of two sibling fields sharing a label (e.g. `subtotal`/`shipping` both labeled "Amount") made the warning claim that shared label is "no longer reachable through the app" -- false, since the other field with the identical label is still a live, visible field on the same entity -- and gave the user no way to tell which field was genuinely removed at all. `apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts`'s `computeCheckpointDiff` (lines 67-74, pre-fix) had the structurally identical gap for `removedFieldNames`/`addedFieldNames`/`changedFieldNames`, feeding the Time Machine panel's own restore-preview warning (`HistoryPanel.tsx`'s `entityLostFields` display) with the same false-implication risk when restoring an older or newer checkpoint.

**Independent verification**: read `pipeline.ts`'s `computeImpact`/`architectEvent` in full (lines 95-197) directly and confirmed the exact unguarded lines and their direct feed into the warning message. Read `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `computeCheckpointDiff` in full (lines 46-87) and confirmed the identical shape at three call sites. Re-confirmed (as every prior round in this family has) that `EntitySchema`'s field-uniqueness check in `packages/shared/src/index.ts` only enforces `name`, never `label`. Grepped both `pipeline.test.ts` (every `label:` occurrence, line by line) and `checkpointDiff.test.ts` and confirmed neither ever gives two sibling fields a custom, colliding label -- zero existing coverage for this exact gap in either file. Grepped `codegen.ts` for any equivalent of `computeImpact`/`architectEvent`/`computeCheckpointDiff` and confirmed none exists -- the exported app has no build-pipeline or checkpoint-diff concept at all, so no corresponding change was needed there.

**The fix**: ported the established `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` helper pair (as local copies, matching this codebase's own duplicate-rather-than-import convention already used in `backup.ts`) into both `pipeline.ts` and `checkpointDiff.ts`. Unlike every previous instance -- where occurrences were counted over one single list of currently-displayed fields -- the right domain here is the **union** of fields on both sides of the comparison (previous spec's fields ∪ next spec's fields, deduped by name so an unchanged field isn't double-counted): this is what correctly catches a removed field's label still colliding with a *surviving* sibling field's label, not just two fields colliding within the same new/removed/tightened list.

**The tests**: a new test in `pipeline.test.ts` builds an `Order` entity with `subtotal`/`shipping` number fields both labeled "Amount", refines to drop only `shipping`, and confirms the real Architect warning reads `"...Amount (shipping)..."` (not the bare, misleading "Amount") and that `detail.changedEntities[0].removedFieldNames` is `["Amount (shipping)"]`. A matching test in `checkpointDiff.test.ts` builds a current spec with only `subtotal` ("Amount") and a checkpoint that still has both `subtotal`/`shipping` ("Amount"), confirming `addedFieldNames` reads `["Amount (shipping)"]` rather than the bare shared label.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing suites in both files (`pipeline.test.ts` 25/25, `checkpointDiff.test.ts` 34/34). Backed up both fixed source files, reverted only them via `git checkout --` (keeping both test files) -- both new tests failed exactly as predicted (`pipeline.test.ts`: the real message still read the bare, misleading `"...Amount -- their data is kept..."`; `checkpointDiff.test.ts`: `addedFieldNames` was `["Amount"]` instead of `["Amount (shipping)"]`), with no other test affected. Restored both fixes from the backups, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran both single-file suites clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (esbuild + `tsc -b` + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite 552/552 (+1); full `@forge/web` suite 917/917 (+1) -- the first full-suite run was cut short by an overly tight `timeout 180` wrapped around the backgrounded command rather than any real failure (exit 143/SIGTERM), confirmed by re-running without that artificial cap and getting a clean, complete 917/917 in under 5 minutes; `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `febb1b5`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The live build pipeline's own migration-impact warnings and the Time Machine panel's checkpoint-diff warnings now both disambiguate same-entity, same-label fields, closing a sixth and seventh confirmed instance of the unguarded-label-collision shape (twin.ts/635, calendarIcs.ts+codegen.ts/636, entityFormatting.ts+codegen.ts×2/637, EntityPanel.tsx+codegen.ts×2/638, backup.ts/640, pipeline.ts+checkpointDiff.ts/641) -- and the worst one found so far, since it didn't just render two things identically but actively asserted something false about data reachability. This reconfirms round 640's own lesson in the strongest possible way: a repo-wide grep sweep, even after a family is declared "closed" twice already, is still worth running before accepting that closure. A future round's sweep should specifically also check any OTHER place that builds a user-facing sentence from a list of field names/labels derived from a spec diff (not just a currently-rendered table/header), since that's exactly the shape this round and round 640 both found outside the originally-audited UI-rendering surfaces.

### Round 642: the same migration-impact and checkpoint-diff warnings round 641 just fixed for same-labeled FIELDS had the identical gap one level up, for same-labeled ENTITIES

**Context**: round 641's own closing note suggested checking any other place that builds a sentence from a spec diff. This round's Explore survey, explicitly told the field-label grep sweep was already thoroughly covered, looked one level up instead and found that `pipeline.ts`'s `computeImpact`/`architectEvent` and `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `computeCheckpointDiff` -- the exact two functions round 641 just fixed -- never addressed the structurally identical gap for an entity's own `label`, only for a field's.

**The finding**: `entity.label` is exactly as unenforced-unique as `field.label` -- `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s `findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames`/`findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` only ever check `entity.name`, and the Entity Label editor's `PATCH /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/label` route (`routes/projects.ts` line ~1539) accepts any non-empty trimmed string with zero collision check against sibling entities' labels. `computeImpact`'s `changedEntities`/`newEntities`/`removedEntities` (`pipeline.ts`, pre-fix) all built their `label` field from `entity.label ?? entity.name` with no disambiguation, and `architectEvent`'s own warning text (lines 230, 233 pre-fix) read that bare label straight into the build-stream message: `` `${e.label} lost field(s): ...}` ``. Two entities sharing a label (e.g. a `Product` and a `Service` entity both labeled "Items") that each lose a *different* field in the same refine produced a warning like `"Items lost field(s): price; Items lost field(s): duration"` -- indistinguishable, with no way to tell which "Items" lost which field, or even that two different entities are involved at all. The identical `detail` object is also read directly by `apps/web/src/App.tsx` (lines 305-319, chat-history rendering) with the same bare `e.label`, so the live chat transcript inherited the identical ambiguity with no separate bug of its own to fix. `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `computeCheckpointDiff` had the structurally identical gap (`entity.label ?? entity.name` at three call sites), feeding `HistoryPanel.tsx`'s Time Machine restore-preview warnings (lines 366-390) the same way.

**Independent verification**: read `pipeline.ts`'s `computeImpact`/`architectEvent` in full and confirmed the unguarded `e.label` at every one of the three `label:` construction sites and both warning-message template lines, immediately below the already-fixed `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` pair in the very same function -- confirming this is a sibling gap in the identical function round 641 touched, not a new file. Read `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s entity-uniqueness refines directly and confirmed only `name` is checked. Read the `PATCH .../label` route directly and confirmed `RenameEntityLabelSchema` requires only a non-empty trimmed string, with `updateProjectSpec` writing it straight through -- a real, reachable path for a user to create two same-labeled entities. Read `App.tsx`'s chat-history renderer and `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `computeCheckpointDiff` directly and confirmed both have the identical unguarded `label` construction. Grepped `pipeline.test.ts` and `checkpointDiff.test.ts` for any existing entity-label-collision coverage -- none exists (only the round-641 field-level tests do).

**The fix**: added `entityLabelOccurrences`/`entityDisplayLabel` -- the entity-level twin of the existing field-level helper pair -- to both `pipeline.ts` and `checkpointDiff.ts`, following the exact same domain-choice pattern round 641 established: occurrences counted over every entity that exists on *either* side of the comparison (previous ∪ next, or current ∪ checkpoint), deduped by name, so a changed/removed entity's label is checked against a surviving same-labeled entity too. Wired into all three `label:` construction sites in `computeImpact` (`newEntities`, `changedEntities`, `removedEntities`) and all three in `computeCheckpointDiff` (`removedEntities`, `changedEntities`, `addedEntities`). No change needed in `App.tsx` or `HistoryPanel.tsx` -- both simply render whichever `label` string the fixed functions now already return disambiguated, and no change needed in `codegen.ts`, confirmed via grep to have no equivalent of either function at all (same as round 641's finding).

**The tests**: a new test in `pipeline.test.ts` builds `Product`/`Service` entities both labeled "Items", drops a field only from `Product`, and confirms the real Architect warning reads `"Items (Product) lost field(s): price"` with no bare, un-disambiguated `"Items lost field(s)"` anywhere in the message. A matching test in `checkpointDiff.test.ts` builds the same two-entity fixture and confirms `changedEntities` reports `"Items (Product)"` rather than the bare shared label. The first draft of the `pipeline.test.ts` test used a copy-pasted negative-assertion regex from round 641's field-level test (`/lost field\(s\): price(?! \()/`) that doesn't apply here, since this round's disambiguator appends `(Product)` to the *entity* label, not after the field name -- caught immediately when the real (correctly-fixed) output failed it; corrected to check for the literal bare phrase `"Warning: Items lost field(s)"` instead.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing suites in both files (`pipeline.test.ts` 26/26, `checkpointDiff.test.ts` 35/35). Backed up both fixed source files, reverted only them via `git checkout --` (which, since both files already carried round 641's committed fix, cleanly isolated just this round's new entity-level diff) -- both new tests failed exactly as predicted (`pipeline.test.ts`: the real message read the bare `"Items lost field(s): price"`; `checkpointDiff.test.ts`: `changedEntities[0].label` was `"Items"` instead of `"Items (Product)"`), with no other test affected. Restored both fixes from the backups, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran both single-file suites clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (esbuild + `tsc -b` + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite 553/553 (+1); full `@forge/web` suite 918/918 (+1), both run as raw backgrounded commands with no external `timeout` wrapper per round 641's own lesson; `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `7d1017d`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The live build pipeline's migration-impact warnings, the chat-history transcript, and the Time Machine panel's checkpoint-diff warnings now all disambiguate same-labeled entities exactly as they already did for same-labeled fields, closing the entity-level half of a gap round 641 only fixed at the field level in these same two functions. This is a fresh variant of the unguarded-label-collision family -- not a sixth file-level copy of the field-label fix, but the realization that `entity.label` and `field.label` are two independently-unenforced, independently-vulnerable pieces of display metadata, and a fix for one doesn't imply the other was covered even within the *same function*. A future round should check whether any other consumer of `ProductSpec`'s entities built human-facing text from `entity.label` directly (outside the handful of files already audited across this whole family) before treating this as fully closed.

### Round 643: importing a CSV of pre-existing customers fired a real WhatsApp "welcome" message to every row in the file, all at once -- CSV import had no way to tell the server it wasn't a genuine new-record creation event

**Context**: the unguarded-label-collision family (635-642) is now considered low-priority/mostly-exhausted after a thorough repo-wide sweep. This round's Explore survey was steered at genuinely fresh territory (roles enforcement, multi-tenant isolation, pagination, file uploads, validation asymmetries, automations/WhatsApp edge cases) rather than another label-collision instance. It ruled out several directions as already safe (roles are disclosed-cosmetic, not a real gap; multi-project isolation is consistently enforced via `requireProjectAccess`/`tableNameFor`; no file-upload feature exists; the one `req.body` path without a zod schema -- record create/update -- is intentional, since entity shape is dynamic per-project) and landed on a real, high-impact finding in the automations/bulk-action intersection nobody had looked at across 8 prior rounds of Automation Rules hardening.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s `handleImportFile` (CSV import, lines 2082-2118 pre-fix) parses every row of an uploaded CSV and POSTs each one *concurrently* via `Promise.allSettled(parsedRecords.map((record) => createRecord(...)))`. `createRecord` (`apps/web/src/api.ts`) is the exact same client call a single "Add" form uses, hitting the same `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName` route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`), which unconditionally called `void runAutomationsForRecordChange(db, whatsapp, project, entity, "created", record, ...)` for every created record, with no concept anywhere of "this record was imported, not freshly created by a user." `runAutomationsForRecordChange`/`fireRule` (`apps/api/src/automations.ts`) has no rate limiting, queueing, or batching -- each call independently evaluates every enabled `record_created` rule and, if WhatsApp is connected, immediately calls the real `whatsapp.sendMessage()`. The result: a completely ordinary workflow -- "set up a 'welcome new customer' WhatsApp automation, then import your existing 500-customer spreadsheet to migrate off another system" -- sent an unsolicited WhatsApp message to all 500 real people, fired in a concurrent burst, with zero warning or way to opt out. `apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.ts`'s own module comment already worries about a number "showing automated behavior" getting flagged or blocked by WhatsApp; this concurrent-burst-of-sends pattern from CSV import is exactly that risk, at the worst possible scale.

**Independent verification**: read `handleImportFile` directly and confirmed the exact `Promise.allSettled`/`createRecord` concurrency pattern. Read `createRecord` (`api.ts`) and confirmed no "imported"/"bulk" flag existed anywhere in the request. Read the `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName` route in full and confirmed the unconditional, fire-and-forget `runAutomationsForRecordChange` call, with no suppression mechanism of any kind. Read `runAutomationsForRecordChange`/`fireRule` in full and confirmed no rate limiting or bulk-awareness exists in either function. Grepped `apps/api/src/automations.test.ts` and `apps/api/src/app.test.ts` for any test combining CSV import (or any bulk-creation path) with an enabled automation rule -- none exists; `docs/roadmap.md`'s own extensive automation-hardening history (field_equals diff-only firing, relation-retarget disable, enum-value-removed disable, busy-id-slot races) never once mentions bulk-import/bulk-update interacting with automations, confirming this is genuinely unaudited territory. Confirmed the identical `handleImportFile`/`createRecord` pattern exists in `codegen.ts`'s generated exported app (lines 3890-3911) -- but confirmed via grep that the exported app has no automations/WhatsApp feature at all (zero matches for "automation"/"whatsapp" anywhere in `codegen.ts`), so no corresponding change was needed there.

**The fix**: added an `X-Suppress-Automations` header, set only by `handleImportFile`'s `createRecord` calls (via a new `options?: { suppressAutomations?: boolean }` parameter on the client function), checked by the create-record route before calling `runAutomationsForRecordChange` -- when present, the call is skipped entirely. A single "Add" form submission, `handleBulkDuplicate`, and `handleBulkUpdate` all still hit the same route without this header, so they're unaffected and still fire automations normally -- this is deliberately scoped to CSV import alone, the one case where the created records are unambiguously pre-existing data being backfilled rather than new creation events, not a blanket bulk-action/automation redesign.

**The tests**: a new HTTP-level test in `app.test.ts` builds a real project with a `record_created` → WhatsApp automation rule, connects the fake WhatsApp socket, POSTs one record with `X-Suppress-Automations: true` (confirms zero sends after a short wait) and one ordinary record with no header on the same rule (confirms exactly one real send, with the correct recipient and message) -- proving the fix is scoped to the header, not a blanket disable. A matching real-DOM test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` uploads a real two-row CSV `File` through the actual `handleImportFile` wiring and captures the real `fetch` request headers for both resulting POSTs, confirming every one carries `x-suppress-automations: true`.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing suites in both files (`app.test.ts` 179/179, `EntityPanel.test.ts` 129/129). Backed up all three fixed source files (`routes/projects.ts`, `api.ts`, `EntityPanel.tsx`), reverted only them via `git checkout --` (keeping all test changes) -- both new tests failed exactly as predicted (`app.test.ts`: the imported record's automation fired anyway, `1 !== 0`; `EntityPanel.test.ts`: the captured request header was `null` instead of `"true"`), with no other test affected. Restored all three fixes from the backups, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran both single-file suites clean. Full `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api --workspace=@forge/web` clean (esbuild + `tsc -b` + vite). Full `@forge/api` suite 554/554 (+1); full `@forge/web` suite 919/919 (+1), both run as raw backgrounded commands with no external `timeout` wrapper and without piping to `grep`/`tail` on the authoritative run (an intermediate piped background run earlier in this same round silently discarded the final summary line, caught and corrected by re-running plainly); `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `654cb57`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. CSV import no longer triggers live WhatsApp automation rules for backfilled, pre-existing data, closing a real-world-harm-causing gap that had survived 8 prior rounds of Automation Rules hardening because every one of those rounds focused on correctness of rule *matching* and *disabling*, never on whether a bulk-creation UI path should be treated as "created" at all. A future round could reconsider whether `handleBulkDuplicate` deserves the same treatment -- duplicating an existing record is a genuinely new record from the app's point of view (arguably correct to fire automations), but is worth a second look with fresh eyes rather than assumed safe by extension of this round's reasoning.

### Round 644: the main record Edit form sent a stale full-record snapshot on every save, silently reverting any field the user never touched if it had genuinely changed elsewhere while the dialog was open

**Context**: round 643's survey lens -- "a bulk/batch path can inherit a single-item path's side effect inappropriately when nothing distinguishes a backfill from a genuine new event" -- was explicitly reused to steer this round's Explore survey. It found a related but inverted shape: not a bulk path missing a single-item path's safeguard, but the single, most-used Edit form itself being the one path inconsistent with all of its own sibling single-field-update paths in the exact same file.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s `startEdit` snapshots every field of a record into `form` state when the Edit dialog opens, and `handleSubmit` (pre-fix) sent that whole `form` object back via `updateRecord(projectId, entity.name, editingId, form)` on save -- including every field the user never touched in the dialog. Every sibling mutation path in the same file already avoids this: `commitInlineEdit` sends `{ [field]: value }`, `handleBulkUpdate` sends `{ [bulkEditField]: bulkEditValue }`, and the Kanban/calendar drag handlers each send only the one field being dragged. If a different field on the same record legitimately changed elsewhere (another tab, a Kanban drag, an automation) while the Edit dialog was still open, saving silently reverted that field back to whatever stale value was on screen when the dialog opened -- and because the stored value genuinely transitions (e.g. back from "Shipped" to "Pending"), `computeChangedFields` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) correctly treats it as a real change and can re-fire a `field_equals` automation for a value nobody in this dialog actually set. `computeChangedFields`'s own pre-existing doc comment confirms a prior round already fixed a related-but-distinct false positive (resubmitting an unchanged value) by comparing real before/after DB values -- which is exactly why a genuine, if unintended, revert-transition like this one is indistinguishable from a real one from that function's point of view, making this a genuinely new, deeper lost-update bug rather than a rediscovery.

**Independent verification**: read `startEdit`/`handleSubmit` directly and confirmed the whole-`form`-object PATCH. Read `commitInlineEdit`, `handleBulkUpdate`, and the drag handlers directly and confirmed each already sends a partial payload. Read `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `updateRecord` and confirmed its own doc comment explicitly documents partial-payload support: an untouched field keeps its already-stored raw value exactly as-is. Read `computeChangedFields`'s doc comment in `routes/projects.ts` and confirmed it documents the prior, different fix, establishing this round's finding as new. Read the form-rendering JSX and confirmed `form[field.name]` is read/written with no type coercion, so a diff-based fix carries no false-positive risk from stale type mismatches. Confirmed via grep that `codegen.ts`'s generated `EntityView.jsx` has the structurally identical `startEdit`/`handleSubmit` pattern (and the same already-partial `commitInlineEdit`/`handleBulkUpdate` siblings), so the same fix was ported there too.

**The fix**: added `editingOriginalRef` (a `useRef` holding the exact record `startEdit` snapshotted `form` from, kept separate from the mutable `form` state) to `EntityPanel.tsx`. `handleSubmit` now diffs `form` against `editingOriginalRef.current` field-by-field and PATCHes only the fields that actually differ, bringing the main Edit form in line with every sibling mutation path in the file. Ported the identical fix into `codegen.ts`'s generated `EntityView.jsx` (`editingOriginalRef`, the same diff in `handleSubmit`, `startEdit` populating the ref), adapted to the file's own untyped-JS convention.

**The tests**: a new real-DOM test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` opens the Edit dialog on a record, mutates the mock record store's `status` field directly (standing in for a concurrent external change bypassing the dialog), edits only the `name` input, submits, and asserts the real captured PATCH body contains only `{ name: ... }` and that the concurrently-set `status` survives in the store rather than being reverted. A matching test in `codegen.test.ts` extracts the real generated `startEdit`/`handleSubmit` source via `new Function` (the same technique the file's existing `commitPendingDelete` test uses, chosen over a full jsdom render since both functions close over several state variables each) and asserts the same: only the genuinely-edited field is sent.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing suites in both files (`EntityPanel.test.ts` 130/130, `codegen.test.ts` 205/205). Backed up both fixed source files (`EntityPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`), reverted only them via `git checkout --` (keeping both test changes) -- both new tests failed exactly as predicted (`EntityPanel.test.ts`: the captured PATCH body included the stale `status: "new"`; `codegen.test.ts`: the update payload included the stale `status: "New"`), with no other test affected. Restored both fixes from the backups, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran both single-file suites clean. Full `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` + vite for `@forge/web`, esbuild for `@forge/api`). Full `@forge/api` suite 555/555 (+1); full `@forge/web` suite 920/920 (+1), both run as raw backgrounded commands with no pipe to `grep`/`tail`/`head` and no external `timeout` wrapper; `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `e320e83`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The live preview's main Edit form, and the exported app's identical copy, now both save only the field the user actually touched -- removing a silent, hard-to-notice lost-update/concurrent-overwrite path that had existed since this form was first written, surfaced only by deliberately reusing round 643's "bulk path vs. single-item path" lens one level differently (here, finding the one path inconsistent with its own siblings, rather than a bulk path missing a safeguard its single-item sibling had). A future round could check whether `handleBulkDuplicate`'s own write path (not CSV import, already closed in round 643) has any similar staleness risk, though it was not investigated this round.

### Round 645: the table column resize handle was mouse-drag-only, invisible to assistive tech, while its own sibling (column reorder) already had a keyboard fallback

**Context**: with the label-collision family exhausted and the prior two rounds' bulk-vs-single-item and sibling-consistency lenses already applied, this round's Explore survey was steered at fresh angles (validation asymmetries, relation/FK edge cases, automation edge cases, checkpoint/Time-Machine edge cases, search/sort type coercion, codegen.ts feature-parity gaps) rather than re-treading any closed family. It surveyed broadly, confirmed several candidates were already correctly handled or explicitly closed, independently re-checked `handleBulkDuplicate` per round 644's own suggested follow-up (confirmed it sends a fresh `createRecord` of current values -- correct create semantics, not the stale-PATCH-diff shape round 644 fixed, so no bug there), and landed on a genuine WCAG 2.1.1 ("Keyboard") failure in the table's column resize handle.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s column resize handle (the `<span className="column-resize-handle">` inside each sortable `<th>`, pre-fix) had only an `onMouseDown` handler and `aria-hidden="true"` -- no `tabIndex`, no `onKeyDown`, no `role`. A keyboard-only user had no way to resize a column at all: the only other width-related control, "Reset column widths," undoes every manual resize at once rather than letting someone widen or narrow one specific column, so it's not a substitute. A screen-reader user wasn't even told the control existed, since `aria-hidden="true"` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. This is a real, reachable accessibility gap, not a cosmetic nit -- and it's a sibling inconsistency within the exact same `<th>`: the column **reorder** feature sitting right next to the resize handle (the `‹`/`›` move-earlier/move-later buttons, fixed for the identical mouse-drag-only gap in round 185) already has a full keyboard-operable fallback with real `<button>` elements and `aria-label`s. Resize was simply never given the equivalent treatment. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `EntityView.jsx` has a byte-for-byte parallel copy of both the handle and its `startResize`, with the identical gap.

**Independent verification**: read the resize handle JSX, `startResize`, and the window-level mousemove/mouseup drag effect directly in `EntityPanel.tsx` and confirmed the mouse-only wiring and `aria-hidden="true"`. Read the column-move buttons in the same `<th>` and confirmed their existing `aria-label`/`disabled`-boundary keyboard fallback, establishing the sibling-inconsistency shape. Read `columnWidths.ts`'s `computeResizedWidth`/`MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH`/`MAX_COLUMN_WIDTH` to confirm the exact clamping and RTL-direction-flip math a keyboard step would need to reuse. Read `codegen.ts`'s parallel resize handle, `startResize`, and its own (RTL-less, single-language) `computeResizedWidth` and confirmed the identical gap exists there too. Grepped `EntityPanel.test.ts`'s and `codegen.test.ts`'s existing resize-handle tests and confirmed both only ever simulate mouse drag events -- nothing exercises a keyboard interaction, `aria-hidden`, or focusability, so neither would catch this gap.

**The fix**: made the handle a real `role="slider"` control with `tabIndex={0}`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax`/`aria-valuenow`, and an `aria-label` naming the actual field (mirroring the move-buttons' own `aria-label` pattern); removed `aria-hidden="true"`. Added `handleResizeKeyDown`, wired to the handle's new `onKeyDown`: ArrowRight/ArrowLeft nudge the width by a fixed step (`RESIZE_KEYBOARD_STEP = 20`px) through the same `computeResizedWidth`/`setColumnWidth` the mouse drag already uses, so the same clamping and (in the live preview) RTL-aware direction flip apply either way. Added a matching `:focus-visible` outline in `styles.css` (and codegen.ts's generated stylesheet), mirroring the existing global `button:focus-visible` style, since a bare `<span>` has no default focus ring. Added the `entity.columns.resizeHandle` i18n key (Hebrew + English) for the live preview's `aria-label`; `codegen.ts`'s exported app hardcodes English strings directly (no i18n system), matching its existing move-button labels' own convention. Ported the identical fix into `codegen.ts`.

A real bug surfaced while writing the keyboard-handler logic itself (not by the Explore survey): the first draft read `columnWidths[fieldName]` from the handler's outer closure to compute `startWidth`, exactly mirroring `startResize`'s own mouse-handler shape. Two ArrowLeft/ArrowRight presses handled within the same React batch would both read that same pre-update closure value, so the second press's effect was silently lost (confirmed by a test asserting two ArrowLeft presses after one ArrowRight landed at the wrong width). Fixed by computing `startWidth` from the `setColumnWidths` updater's own `prev` parameter instead -- mirroring the existing mouse-drag `handleUp` function's own established pattern of calling `setColumnWidth` (the persistence side effect) from inside the `setColumnWidths` updater -- so each press, however they batch, sees the other's update.

**The tests**: a new real-DOM test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` confirms the handle now carries `role="slider"`, `tabIndex="0"`, a field-naming `aria-label`, and no `aria-hidden`; fires a real ArrowRight then two ArrowLefts via `fireEvent.keyDown` and confirms the header's live width and `getColumnWidths`-persisted width land exactly where the fixed step arithmetic predicts (200 → 220 → 180), not reverted or double-applied. A matching test in `codegen.test.ts`, using the file's own real-generated-component render technique (not `new Function` extraction, since the handler closes over several pieces of component state), asserts the identical behavior against the actual generated `EntityView.jsx`, confirming the real i18n-free English `aria-label` names the field's own label.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing suites in both files (`EntityPanel.test.ts` 131/131, `codegen.test.ts` 206/206). Backed up all four touched source files (`EntityPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`, `i18n/language.ts`, `styles.css`), reverted all four via `git checkout --` (keeping both test files) -- both new tests failed exactly as predicted (`role` read `null` instead of `"slider"`), with no other test affected. Restored all four from the backups, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran both single-file suites clean. Full `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` + vite for `@forge/web`, esbuild for `@forge/api`). Full `@forge/web` suite 921/921 (+1). Full `@forge/api` suite showed one failure (`password.test.ts`'s "concurrent hashPassword calls run in parallel" timing assertion) on its first *and* second full run -- both runs happened to overlap with the `@forge/web` full suite still running concurrently in the background, confirmed via `ps aux` to be genuine CPU contention from two full suites running at once, unrelated to this round's diff (not a file this round touched, and a timing-tolerance assertion, not a logic one). Re-ran `@forge/api`'s full suite a third time in true isolation (confirmed via `ps aux` that no other test process was running) and got a clean 556/556 (+1), closing out the question. `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `aea5805`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The table's resize handle is now keyboard-operable and exposed to assistive tech exactly like its own sibling reorder buttons already were, in both the live preview and the exported app. This round also reconfirms two standing lessons in a single pass: a "handler X already matches its protected siblings" check must look at the *exact* mechanism each sibling uses (the move buttons' keyboard fallback didn't imply the resize handle had one, even sitting in the same `<th>`), and a closure-over-outer-state bug in a brand-new handler is just as real as one found in existing code -- writing the fix is not exempt from the same batching pitfalls documented elsewhere in this project's history. A future round could look for other mouse/drag-only controls across the app (column reorder and resize are now both fixed; any others never audited) before treating this general shape as closed.

### Round 646: the inline table-cell editor's Enter handler broke multi-line entry for longtext fields -- a fix the full add/edit form already carried, never ported to its own faster sibling path

**Context**: with resize/reorder keyboard-accessibility now closed (645) and Kanban/calendar drag confirmed to already have keyboard fallbacks, this round's Explore survey was steered at the remaining fresh angles (validation asymmetries, other drag interactions, relation/FK edge cases, automation ordering, checkpoint restore, search/sort type coercion, codegen.ts feature-parity gaps). It ruled out several candidates as already correctly handled (Kanban/calendar drag both have real keyboard fallbacks via the status `<select>` and the full edit form; relation/FK deletion-blocking and checkpoint/entity-restore interactions are extremely thoroughly hardened; automation rule firing/ordering is already carefully defensive; `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` is consistent with the client form, no asymmetry) before landing on a genuine, concrete UX-breaking bug in the inline cell editor's own keydown handling.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s inline table-cell editor (opened by double-clicking any `isInlineEditableField` cell -- every field type except `relation`) wires one generic `onKeyDown` handler into `FieldInput` (pre-fix, lines ~2398-2406): `if (e.key === "Enter") { e.preventDefault(); void commitInlineEdit(); }`, with no exception for field type. For a `longtext` field, `FieldInput` renders a real `<textarea>` (lines 788-799) and wires that exact same handler straight onto it. The result: a bare Enter inside an inline-edited Notes/Description cell immediately commits and closes the cell instead of inserting a line break -- there is no way to type a second line through the fast inline-edit path at all. This is not a theoretical edge case; `isInlineEditableField` (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts:1398-1400`) explicitly includes `longtext`, so any entity with a Notes-type field hits this the moment someone double-clicks that cell. The full add/edit form's own identical `<textarea>` already carries a dedicated, deliberate fix for this exact problem (lines ~2469-2478, with its own doc comment: "a bare Enter there only inserts a newline... unlike every single-line input where Enter already submits natively" -- only Ctrl/Cmd+Enter calls `requestSubmit()`). That fix was simply never carried over to the separate inline-cell-edit code path, which was evidently written generically on the single-line-input model (where Enter-to-commit is correct and already well-tested) without re-deriving the same reasoning for `longtext`. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `EntityView.jsx` has the byte-for-byte identical pair: the same unconditional inline-editor handler (lines ~4009-4017) alongside the same already-correct full-form guard (lines ~4051-4055).

**Independent verification**: read the inline editor's `onKeyDown` prop and `FieldInput`'s `longtext` branch directly in `EntityPanel.tsx` and confirmed the same handler reaches the textarea unconditionally. Read `isInlineEditableField` directly and confirmed `longtext` is included, not excluded. Read the full form's own `onKeyDown` (attached to the `<form>` element, not the textarea directly) and confirmed its Ctrl/Cmd+Enter-only-submits logic and accompanying doc comment, establishing the project's own prior, deliberate design principle for this exact textarea-vs-Enter conflict. Read `codegen.ts`'s parallel inline-editor handler and full-form guard and confirmed the identical gap exists there too, byte-for-byte. Grepped `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts` for every `longtext`/Enter-related test and confirmed both existing Ctrl/Cmd+Enter tests are scoped only to `.record-form textarea` (the full form) -- neither file had any coverage for Enter behavior inside the inline cell editor's own textarea.

**The fix**: in the inline editor's `onKeyDown` (both files), special-cased `field.type === "longtext"`: when the field is `longtext` and neither Ctrl nor Cmd is held, the handler returns without calling `preventDefault()`/`commitInlineEdit()`, letting the browser's native Enter-inserts-newline behavior proceed; Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter still commits exactly as before. Every other inline-editable field type (text/number/boolean/enum/date) keeps its existing, already-tested Enter-commits behavior unchanged. Ported the identical fix into `codegen.ts`.

**The tests**: a new real-DOM test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` double-clicks a Notes cell, types a two-line value into the inline textarea, fires a bare Enter and confirms no PATCH fires and the cell stays in edit mode, then fires Ctrl+Enter and confirms the real multi-line value commits through the real API and the cell exits edit mode. A matching test in `codegen.test.ts`, using the file's own real-generated-component render technique, asserts the identical behavior against the actual generated `EntityView.jsx`. An existing codegen.ts test ("the exported EntityView supports double-click inline cell editing...") asserted the inline handler's exact pre-fix source text via a literal regex; updated that regex to match the new `longtext`-guarded shape, since the old literal text no longer exists in correctly-fixed code -- this is an expected, correct consequence of the fix, not a new gap.

**Regression-proof**: ran both new tests against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing suites in both files (`EntityPanel.test.ts` 132/132, `codegen.test.ts` 207/207, including the updated literal-regex test). Backed up both fixed source files (`EntityPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`), reverted only them via `git checkout --` (keeping both test files) -- three tests failed exactly as predicted: both new behavioral tests (a bare Enter still committed, `1 !== 0`) and the updated literal-regex test (the old unconditional source no longer matched the new regex, as expected since the source was reverted to its old, un-fixed shape), with no other test affected. Restored both fixes from the backups, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran both single-file suites clean. Full `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` + vite for `@forge/web`, esbuild for `@forge/api`). Learning from round 645's CPU-contention flake, ran the two full workspace suites sequentially rather than concurrently this time: full `@forge/web` suite 922/922 (+1), then full `@forge/api` suite 557/557 (+1), both clean on the first run with no contention. `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine` untouched by this round's diff. Commit `03cc262`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Both the live preview and the exported app now let a bare Enter insert a newline inside an inline-edited longtext cell, exactly like their own full add/edit forms already did -- closing a real, easily-reproduced UX gap (any Notes/Description field, the moment someone tries to add a second line via the fast inline-edit path) that had existed since inline cell editing was first shipped (round 206) because the full form's own Ctrl/Cmd+Enter fix was never re-derived for this separate code path. This is a fresh instance of a now-familiar shape across this project's history: a fix applied to one of two structurally-parallel paths (here, the full form vs. the inline editor, both rendering the identical `<textarea>`) doesn't imply the other path inherited it. Running the two full workspace suites sequentially, rather than backgrounding them concurrently, avoided repeating round 645's CPU-contention false alarm entirely.

### Round 647: a WhatsApp automation message template sent a relation field's raw numeric id to real recipients instead of the related record's own name

**Context**: with the "same UI element, multiple render paths" family closed for the inline-edit textarea (646), this round's Explore survey was steered toward fresh angles the trigger explicitly listed as unexplored: validation asymmetries, WhatsApp/automation edge cases beyond firing/ordering, checkpoint restore, and search/sort type coercion. It ruled out several candidates as already thoroughly hardened (`matchesSearch`/`sortRecords`/`groupByField`; `FieldInput` is genuinely shared between the full form and inline editor, unlike the round-646 longtext case, so no drift there; relation FK retargeting in `migrate.ts`; `coerceValue`'s insert/update symmetry; WhatsApp phone normalization and webhook handling) before landing on a real, severe bug in automation message-template interpolation.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/automations.ts`'s `interpolateTemplate` (pre-fix) substituted `{{fieldName}}` placeholders with `record[fieldName]` verbatim, with zero field-type awareness. For a relation field, the record's stored value is the target record's raw numeric foreign key (see `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `rowToRecord`/`coerceValue`), not anything a human could read -- a template like `"Hi {{customer}}, your order is ready"` sent the literal text `"Hi 7, your order is ready"` over real WhatsApp instead of `"Hi Dana Levi, your order is ready"`. This is directly reachable: the create-rule UI (`apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.tsx`) exposes `messageTemplate` as free text with its own hint explicitly inviting any field name (`"Use {{fieldName}} to insert a value from the record, e.g. {{customerName}}."`), and server-side, `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`/`UpdateAutomationRuleSchema` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) validate `messageTemplate` only as `z.string().min(1)` -- no check on which field types a template references. This sits in sharp contrast to the same file's own deliberate type-checking for a rule's *trigger* `fieldValue` and destination `toField` (`validateAutomationFieldValue`/`validateAutomationToField`), which reject exactly this kind of relation/date/enum mismatch -- that same discipline was simply never extended to the message body itself, a fresh instance of this project's now-familiar "fix on one structurally-parallel path doesn't imply the others inherited it" shape. Any entity with a relation field (the domain library's own Order→Customer, Invoice→Customer, Appointment→Client shapes) and a rule referencing that field by name trips this on a real send -- not a hypothetical, but the single most common "personalize the message" use case a business owner would reach for.

**Independent verification**: read `interpolateTemplate` and `fireRule` directly in `automations.ts` and confirmed the unconditional, type-blind `String(record[fieldName])` substitution and that `fireRule` is called with the raw DB record, no entity/field-type context at all. Read `rowToRecord`/`coerceValue` in `repository.ts` and confirmed a relation field's stored/returned value is genuinely the raw integer id. Read `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s own hint text and `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`/`UpdateAutomationRuleSchema` and confirmed no field-type restriction exists on `messageTemplate` contents, contrasted against the same file's `validateAutomationFieldValue`/`validateAutomationToField`, which do exactly this type-checking for the rule's other two field references. Grepped `automations.test.ts` and confirmed its three existing `interpolateTemplate` tests only ever used plain string fields -- never a relation, enum, or boolean field -- so none would catch this. Confirmed via grep that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no automations/WhatsApp feature at all (its only "automation" hit is an unrelated drag-and-drop comment), so no codegen.ts port is needed -- this is a live-app-only fix.

**The fix**: added `resolveRelationFieldsForTemplate` to `automations.ts`, which resolves every relation field on the record to the same human display label the UI itself would show -- using the already-existing server-side `displayField.ts` helpers (`recordDisplayLabel`/`pickDisplayField`, already used by `twin.ts`/`whatsapp.ts`/`backup.ts` for the identical purpose) plus `getRecord` (a synchronous single-row fetch from `@forge/db`, so no async plumbing was needed), falling back to `"#<id>"` exactly like the client's own `relationDisplayLabel` does when the target entity or record can't be found. `fireRule` now calls this before `interpolateTemplate`, which itself gained an `entity` parameter so it can also render a boolean field as `TRUE`/`FALSE` and an enum field via its translated label -- mirroring `entityFormatting.ts`'s/`backup.ts`'s own `fieldDisplayValue`, which already applies the identical relation/enum/boolean convention for CSV export. `runAutomationsForRecordChange` was updated to thread `entity` through to `fireRule`.

**The tests**: a new test in `automations.test.ts` builds a real two-entity project (`Customer`/`Deal`, with `Deal.customer` as a relation field), inserts a real `Customer` record, fires a real automation rule referencing `{{customer}}` in its template, and confirms the real sent WhatsApp message body carries the customer's own name rather than the bare numeric id. A second new test confirms `interpolateTemplate` itself renders a boolean field as `TRUE`/`FALSE` and an enum field via its translated label rather than the raw stored code. The three pre-existing `interpolateTemplate` tests were updated to pass the now-required `entity` argument (a signature change, not new coverage).

**Regression-proof**: ran all three new/updated test groups against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing `automations.test.ts` suite (15/15, +2). Backed up the fixed `automations.ts`, reverted only it via `git checkout --` (keeping the test file) -- exactly the three tests touching the new/changed behavior failed as predicted (the three-argument calls fed `entity` into the old function's `record` parameter, producing unresolved placeholders and a bare `"Congrats 1, ..."` id instead of the customer's name), with every other test unaffected. Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran the single-file suite clean (15/15). Full `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` + vite for `@forge/web`, esbuild for `@forge/api`). Full `@forge/api` suite 559/559 (+2); `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine`/`@forge/web` untouched by this round's diff, so only `@forge/api`'s full suite was run (plus the full build, which covers both workspaces). Commit `90cb2d1`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Every automation message template now renders a relation field as the real related record's display label, and an enum/boolean field in the same human-readable form the on-screen table already uses, closing a gap that could have been sending meaningless or unlocalized data to real WhatsApp recipients since automation rules first shipped. This round also reconfirms that `getRecord` (unlike a hypothetical async relation-resolution path) is a plain synchronous SQLite read, which kept the fix simple -- no new async plumbing through `fireRule` was needed beyond what already existed for the WhatsApp send itself.

### Round 648: the exported app's own create/update routes passed a raw SQLite foreign-key error straight to the user, unlike its own delete route and the live backend's create/update routes it otherwise mirrors

**Context**: with round 647's "N parallel paths handling the same failure, some protected, some not" angle explicitly carried forward, this round's Explore survey looked for other clusters of sibling validations/paths with an unprotected member. It ruled out several fresh angles (matchesSearch/sortRecords/groupByField's boolean exclusion is intentional, since the table never renders a boolean as text; automation rules' create/update symmetry re-confirmed; checkpoint restore's field-type-change-then-restore already surfaces a migration-hazard warning; WhatsApp's manual-send route and message pagination already fully covered; no array-typed fields exist in this schema at all) before landing on exactly the pattern it was steered toward -- this time inside `codegen.ts` itself rather than `automations.ts`.

**The finding**: the exported app's generated `server.js` enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` and emits a real `REFERENCES` clause for every relation column (already covered by an existing test, `codegen.test.ts` line 652), so its three record-mutation routes -- `app.post`, `app.patch .../:id`, and `app.delete .../:id` (pre-fix, `codegen.ts` lines 443-490) -- can all hit the identical SQLite error, `"FOREIGN KEY constraint failed"`. Only `app.delete` translated it, into a real `409` with an actionable message, explicitly commented as mirroring "the same route-level pattern the live Forge AI backend uses." `app.post` and `app.patch` both just did `catch (err) { res.status(400).json({ error: err.message }); }` -- the raw SQLite string went straight to the client, and the generated frontend's own record form (`codegen.ts`'s `handleSubmit`/error-rendering) then displayed it verbatim to the end user. This is directly reachable: a relation field's picker in the exported app's own `EntityView.jsx` is built from `relatedRecords` fetched once into React state, so submitting a create or edit referencing a record someone else deleted in the meantime hits this exact constraint -- precisely the scenario the live backend's own already-existing guards document for its create and update routes. The live backend (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` lines 1488-1500 and 2024-2036) already protects exactly these two routes, each explicitly calling out the other as getting "the same translation" -- i.e. the live app treats create and update as full siblings requiring identical protection, and both already have it. `codegen.ts` ported that protection to its DELETE route only, never to the POST/PATCH routes it's supposed to mirror the same live-backend behavior for.

**Independent verification**: read all three mutation routes directly in `codegen.ts` and confirmed the exact asymmetry -- DELETE's dedicated FK-message check vs. POST/PATCH's bare `err.message` passthrough. Read the live backend's own create-route guard (`routes/projects.ts` lines 1488-1500) and confirmed its exact wording, status code (`400`), and doc comment describing the same reachability scenario (a relation picker built from data fetched earlier, referencing a record deleted by another collaborator in the meantime). Confirmed `packages/db/src/repository.test.ts` lines 404-422 that this exact SQLite message is thrown on insert, not just delete, establishing the create/update routes are genuinely exposed to it. Grepped `codegen.test.ts` for "FOREIGN KEY"/"INVALID_RELATION_TARGET"/"references another record" and confirmed only the one DELETE-focused test (line 652) exists -- nothing exercises the exported app's create or update FK path.

**The fix**: added the identical FK-constraint catch to `codegen.ts`'s generated `app.post` and `app.patch` route templates, translating `"FOREIGN KEY constraint failed"` into a `400` with the message `"This record references another record that no longer exists"` -- matching the live backend's own create/update wording exactly (DELETE keeps its own distinct `409` wording, since the live backend also gives delete a different status/message than create/update).

**The tests**: a new real-spawned-server test in `codegen.test.ts`, using the same standard as the existing DELETE-FK test (spawns the real generated `server.js`, not just a regex check), creates a Courier, deletes it (unreferenced, so the delete itself succeeds), then confirms both a `POST .../Order` with `courierId` set to the now-deleted Courier's id and a `PATCH .../Order/:id` setting the same dangling `courierId` each return `400` with the exact friendly message, rather than the raw SQLite string.

**Regression-proof**: ran the new test against current (fixed) code -- green, alongside the full pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` suite (208/208, +1). Backed up the fixed `codegen.ts`, reverted only it via `git checkout --` (keeping the test file) -- the new test failed exactly as predicted (`actual: 'FOREIGN KEY constraint failed'` instead of the friendly message), with no other test affected (207/208). Restored the fix from the backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran the single-file suite clean (208/208). Full `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` + vite for `@forge/web`, esbuild for `@forge/api`). Full `@forge/api` suite 560/560 (+1); `@forge/db`/`@forge/shared`/`@forge/spec-engine`/`@forge/web` untouched by this round's diff, so only `@forge/api`'s full suite was run (plus the full build, which covers both workspaces). Commit `8eccbc0`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The exported standalone app's create and update routes now give a real, actionable error for a dangling relation reference, exactly like its own delete route and the live backend's equivalent routes already did -- closing a gap where codegen.ts had only partially caught up to the live-backend behavior it exists to mirror. This is the same "N parallel paths, not all protected" shape round 647 found, but inverted in an interesting way: there, a live-app file had two protected siblings and one unprotected; here, codegen.ts had successfully mirrored the live backend for one of three routes (delete) but not the other two (create/update) it was equally supposed to mirror -- a reminder that when auditing "did codegen.ts mirror this live-app fix," checking just one route of several sharing the same underlying failure mode isn't enough.

### Round 649: the app's own default table view, bulk-edit field picker, columns menu, filter/group-by dropdowns, and add/edit form never disambiguated two fields sharing a label, unlike print sheets and board cards

**Context**: this round's Explore survey was explicitly steered toward the dominant "N parallel sites, fixed in SOME not ALL" lens from rounds 643-648, plus the fresh angle the round-648 trigger suggested: "does codegen.ts mirror a live-app feature on ALL the relevant routes/surfaces, or only some?" It was given the full closed/off-limits list through round 648 (CSV-bulk-automation-suppression, EntityPanel's main Edit form diffing, the resize-handle keyboard fallback, the inline-textarea Enter key, automation message interpolation, codegen.ts's FK-error translation on POST/PATCH).

**The finding**: the field-label-collision gap rounds 635-642 fixed one render path at a time -- Business Twin, the calendar export, CSV export, and (round 638) `RecordPrintSheet`, `RecordListPrintSheet`, and `BoardCard` -- was fixed via a shared helper, `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts` lines 1025-1036, mirrored in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` lines 1849-1858), but that helper was only ever wired into those three call sites in each file. The app's own default, every-day table view -- the single highest-traffic surface in the whole app -- never got it, nor did several sibling dropdowns that render every field's label together, the same "render every field's label simultaneously" situation a print sheet is in:

1. The main table's column header (`sort-header` button) and its move-earlier/move-later/resize-handle `aria-label`s -- `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` (pre-fix) lines 2984, 2994, 3003, 3016; `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` line 4521 (which did not even have the `?? f.name` fallback the live code had).
2. The bulk-edit "set field" dropdown (`handleBulkUpdate`'s field picker) -- `EntityPanel.tsx` line 2912; `codegen.ts` line 4459.
3. The columns show/hide checklist -- `EntityPanel.tsx` line 2748; `codegen.ts` line 4313.
4. The per-field filter dropdowns' `aria-label` and "All …" option text -- `EntityPanel.tsx` lines 2605/2615 (filterable fields are enum/boolean only, so this and the next two surfaces only manifest with two enum/boolean fields sharing a label, not two number fields).
5. The group-by dropdown -- `EntityPanel.tsx` line 2654.
6. The exported app's add/edit form field label -- `codegen.ts` line 4084, printed with no fallback and no disambiguation at all (the live app has a separate `FieldLabelEditor.tsx` component here, covered below).

Concrete repro: rename two different number fields on the same entity (e.g. "subtotal" and "shipping") to the identical label "Amount" via the Field Label editor -- `PATCH .../fields/:fieldName/label` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` lines 1591-1617) applies a new label with zero uniqueness check, so this is fully legal. Both table columns now read "Amount" with no way to tell them apart, not even via the move/resize controls' `aria-label`s, and a person mass-editing 50 selected records via the bulk-edit field picker has a 50/50 chance of silently writing to the wrong underlying field -- while the exact same entity's **Print list** view (fixed in round 638) correctly shows "Amount (subtotal)"/"Amount (shipping)".

A closely related eighth site, not flagged by the survey (codegen.ts has no equivalent component, since it has no field-rename feature) but found during independent verification: the live app's own `FieldLabelEditor.tsx` -- the add/edit form's per-field rename control, which also renders every field's label simultaneously -- had the identical gap (`currentLabel = field.label ?? field.name`, used directly in the read-only `<span>`, line 43/84).

**Independent verification**: grepped every call site of `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` in both `entityFormatting.ts`/`EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, confirming exactly three each (print-record, print-list, board-card), and confirmed via `git log -S fieldLabelOccurrences` that round 78bc50a introduced the helper and wired it into exactly those three places. Read all seven survey-flagged lines directly in both files and confirmed each renders a bare `f.label ?? f.name` (or `f.label`/`f.label || f.name` in codegen.ts) with no disambiguation. Separately read `FieldLabelEditor.tsx` in full and found the eighth site myself: its `currentLabel` is used both for the read-only display AND as the rename draft's initial value/no-op-comparison target, so disambiguating naively (reusing the disambiguated text as the draft) would have introduced a NEW bug -- saving an unchanged rename would literally rename the field to "Amount (subtotal)". Checked `EntityPanel.test.ts`/`codegen.test.ts`/`FieldLabelEditor.test.ts` for existing coverage of this scenario on these eight surfaces -- none existed; every prior "same label" test targeted print sheets, board cards, CSV, calendar .ics, or CSV-import column mapping only.

In `FieldLabelEditor.tsx`, added a required `labelOccurrences: Map<string, number>` prop, kept `currentLabel` (the real, raw label) for the draft/no-op logic, and added a separate `displayLabel = fieldDisplayLabel(field, labelOccurrences)` used only in the read-only `<span>`; `EntityPanel.tsx` now computes `entityFieldLabelOccurrences` and passes it down to the component's one call site. Ported the identical pattern into `codegen.ts`'s generated `EntityView` template (same six `useMemo`s, same seven-plus-one call-site replacements, including the add/edit form's plain-span label, which has no rename-draft complication since the exported app has no rename feature).

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one real-DOM test exercising all five live-app surfaces at once (table header, resize-handle `aria-label`, filter/group-by dropdowns via two boolean fields sharing the label "Flag", the columns menu, and the bulk-edit picker after selecting a row), reusing the same `orderEntity`/"Amount" fixture round 638's precedent test established. `FieldLabelEditor.test.ts` gained a test confirming the read-only span shows "Original Field Label (phone)" when another field shares the label, while the rename input's draft still starts from the real, undisambiguated "Original Field Label" -- and updated the two existing render call sites to pass a `labelOccurrences` map now that the prop is required. `codegen.test.ts` gained the equivalent real-generated-app test (via `writeGeneratedWebComponent` + dynamic import, same technique as the round-638 precedent) covering all six exported-app surfaces including the add/edit form, and one pre-existing test (an exact literal-source regex asserting `entity.fields.filter(isInlineEditableField).map((f) => (`) needed updating to match the new `bulkEditableFields.map((f) => (` shape -- an expected, correct consequence of the fix, not a new bug.

Re-ran all three test files against the reverted source: `EntityPanel.test.ts`'s new test failed exactly as predicted (`got: ["Name","Amount","Amount","Flag","Flag","Created"]`, no disambiguation); `FieldLabelEditor.test.ts`'s new test failed exactly as predicted (`actual: 'Original Field Label *✏️'`, the raw undisambiguated text); `codegen.test.ts` failed exactly two tests as predicted -- the new disambiguation test (identical header-array mismatch) and the literal-regex test (since `bulkEditableFields` doesn't exist on reverted source), 207/209.
