### Round 650: the exported standalone app ported every keyboard-shortcut mechanic the live preview has, but never the "?" cheat-sheet that's the only place any of them are actually documented to a real end user

**Context**: round 629 first flagged porting the live preview's own `ShortcutsPanel.tsx` ("?"-triggered keyboard-shortcuts cheat-sheet) into `codegen.ts` as a known, deliberately-deferred gap -- `docs/roadmap.md`'s own round-629 entry says verbatim: *"porting '?' 's shortcuts cheat-sheet remains open as a separate, larger candidate (a whole new dialog, not yet built in the exported app at all) -- not undertaken this round since it's a different scale of work."* Every trigger prompt since then (through round 649) carried this forward as "מועמד גדול חדש... round נפרד, גדול יותר" (a bigger candidate deserving its own round) without anyone picking it up. Round 650's Explore survey, steered toward the "does codegen.ts mirror live-backend/live-preview feature X on ALL the relevant UI-surfaces, or just some" lens that had just closed the field-label-disambiguation family (round 649), re-surfaced this exact long-deferred gap as still open and well-scoped for a dedicated round.

**The finding**: `codegen.ts`'s generated app faithfully ports every one of the live preview's keyboard-shortcut *mechanics* -- j/k row navigation, Enter→edit, x→toggle select, n→new record, Delete/Backspace→delete, d→duplicate, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter→submit, and Ctrl/Cmd+K plus "/"→open Global Search -- but has zero "?" handler anywhere (confirmed via grep: no `e.key === "?"` match in the whole file) and no `ShortcutsPanel`-equivalent component or any help/cheat-sheet dialog at all. The only discoverability affordance in the entire exported app is one static `<span className="shortcut-hint">Ctrl+K</span>` badge next to the search button, which only ever advertises that one shortcut -- the other seven are completely undocumented. A real end user who exports a Forge AI project and runs it as their own production app, with no way back to the Forge AI platform or its docs, has no way to discover (or even guess, since pressing "?" itself does nothing) any of that shortcut set.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/ShortcutsPanel.tsx` in full (its 13-row `SHORTCUTS` array, its `useDialogFocusTrap` usage, its exact markup/CSS classes) and `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s own wiring (the `showShortcuts` state, the `"?"` keydown handler at the time guarded by `isEditableEventTarget`, the topbar button with its `shortcut-hint` span, and the conditional render). Read `codegen.ts`'s existing `GlobalSearch` dialog in full (`renderGlobalSearchJsx`, ~470 lines) and confirmed its focus-trap/background-inert logic (`GLOBAL_SEARCH_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, `hideGlobalSearchBackgroundFromAssistiveTech`) was fully generic despite its GlobalSearch-specific naming -- an artifact of being written back when, per the file's own comment, "the exported app's only overlay dialog is GlobalSearch." Confirmed the shared dialog-open counter (`searchDialogOpenCount`/`isSearchDialogOpen`/`markSearchDialogOpen`/`markSearchDialogClosed`, used by `EntityView`'s own j/k/x/d/n keydown handlers to suppress themselves while any dialog sits on top of the table) lived in `EntityView.jsx` and was likewise generic in behavior, just search-specific in name. Confirmed via `grep -c "^test("` that `codegen.test.ts` had 209 tests before this round's changes, giving a clean baseline to diff against.

**The fix**: added a new generated file, `web/src/components/ShortcutsPanel.jsx` (`renderShortcutsPanelJsx` in `codegen.ts`), porting the live preview's exact 13-row shortcut list (hardcoded English text, matching every other string in this i18n-free exported app) and reusing the same focus-trap/background-inert/dialog-count pattern `GlobalSearch.jsx` already has. Rather than duplicate that ~70-line trap a second time, generalized the shared pieces now that a second dialog needs them: `searchDialogOpenCount`→`openDialogCount`, `isSearchDialogOpen`→`isAnyDialogOpen`, `markSearchDialogOpen`→`markDialogOpen`, `markSearchDialogClosed`→`markDialogClosed` (all still in `EntityView.jsx`), and moved+exported `GLOBAL_SEARCH_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`→`DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` and `hideGlobalSearchBackgroundFromAssistiveTech`→`hideDialogBackgroundFromAssistiveTech` from being local to `GlobalSearch.jsx` into the same shared `EntityView.jsx` module, which both `GlobalSearch.jsx` and the new `ShortcutsPanel.jsx` now import. Wired `"?"` (guarded by the existing `isEditableEventTarget`, same convention as `"/"`) into `App.jsx`'s own keydown handler to open the panel, added `setShowShortcuts(false)` alongside the existing Escape-closes-search branch, added a topbar `⌨️ Keyboard shortcuts` button (same `.search-trigger` styling as the Search button, with its own `?` hint span) next to the Search button, and added the conditional render next to `GlobalSearch`'s. Added the missing `.shortcuts-list`/`.shortcuts-row`/`.shortcuts-keys`/`.shortcuts-keys kbd` CSS rules (ported from `apps/web/src/styles.css`), reusing the exported app's existing generic `.search-overlay`/`.search-panel`/`.search-header` classes for the dialog shell rather than introducing a parallel `.history-overlay`/`.history-panel` naming the exported app has no other use for (unlike the live app, codegen.ts has no History feature at all).

**The tests**: `codegen.test.ts` gained four new tests against the real generated app (via `writeGeneratedWebComponent` + dynamic import, not source-text regexes): (1) `ShortcutsPanel` renders its heading and all 13 shortcut rows with the exact descriptions the live preview's own array declares; (2) `ShortcutsPanel` gets real dialog accessibility (`role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, focus lands on its own Close button since it has no autoFocus input, Tab/Shift+Tab wraps within the panel, closing restores focus to the trigger) -- proving the generalized `DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`/`hideDialogBackgroundFromAssistiveTech` work against a second real consumer, not just `GlobalSearch`; (3) `EntityView`'s "d" shortcut does not fire while `ShortcutsPanel` is open on top of the table (mirroring the existing GlobalSearch-suppression test, now proving `isAnyDialogOpen` genuinely shares state across both dialogs); (4) `App.jsx`'s own end-to-end wiring -- "?" opens the panel, the topbar button opens it via a real click, Escape closes it. Two pre-existing tests needed updating as an expected, correct consequence of the fix (not a new bug): the literal file-list assertion in `generateExportFiles produces a real multi-file React (Vite) + Express project` now includes `web/src/components/ShortcutsPanel.jsx`, and the literal import-line regex in `the exported app includes a real cross-entity global search...` now matches the renamed, multi-line `markDialogOpen, markDialogClosed, DIALOG_FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR, hideDialogBackgroundFromAssistiveTech` import. One of the four new tests itself had a bug caught on first run: asserting `/Keyboard shortcuts/` against the whole `App` container's text matched the always-present topbar button's own label regardless of whether the panel was actually open, so it couldn't distinguish "panel open" from "button exists" -- fixed by asserting on `.shortcuts-list`'s presence/absence instead.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `codegen.ts` to scratchpad, reverted only it via `git checkout --` (keeping the test file). Re-ran `codegen.test.ts` against the reverted source: exactly 6 failures as predicted -- the 2 updated pre-existing tests (file-list/import-regex, since the reverted source lacks `ShortcutsPanel.jsx` and still has the old names) plus all 4 new tests (3 failing with `Cannot find module '.../ShortcutsPanel.jsx'`, since that generated file no longer exists on reverted source; the 4th, the App-level "?" test, failing with `'?' must open the shortcuts panel`) -- 207/213. Restored the fix from the scratchpad backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q` (no output). Re-ran `codegen.test.ts` clean: 213/213. Since only `apps/api` files changed this round (no `apps/web` diff at all), ran only the full `@forge/api` suite -- 565/565 pass, except one unrelated pre-existing flake (`auth/password.test.ts`'s "concurrent hashPassword calls run in parallel", a timing-tolerance test in a file this round never touches), re-confirmed clean (7/7) in isolation immediately after. Full `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` + vite for `@forge/web`, esbuild for `@forge/api`). Commit `bfa83ad`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Round 629's long-deferred "?" shortcuts cheat-sheet candidate is done: the exported standalone app's own power-user feature set (j/k/x/n/Delete/d/Ctrl+Enter/Ctrl+K/"/") is now actually discoverable by a real end user who has no access back to the Forge AI platform, through the same "?" convention, topbar button, and Escape-close behavior the live preview already has. As a side effect of generalizing the dialog-open guard and focus-trap helpers for a second dialog, codegen.ts's own architecture now slightly more closely mirrors the live preview's real shared-hook design (one counter/one set of helpers serving every dialog) rather than the GlobalSearch-only one-off it had when it only needed to serve one.

### Round 651: automation rule messages sent a raw, unformatted date/number to real WhatsApp recipients, unlike the same field's own on-screen rendering

**Context**: this round's Explore survey was explicitly steered toward the dominant "N parallel paths/UI-surfaces/helpers, fixed for some but not all" lens that has found a genuine bug in every one of the last seven rounds (643-650), with both of the two most recently closed families (field-label disambiguation, keyboard-shortcuts discoverability) ruled off-limits. It spent most of its budget re-verifying several other strong-looking leads (`checkpointDiff.ts`'s `fieldSignature`, `handleBulkUpdate`'s blank-value warning, `fireRule`'s `toField` relation-id exposure, `backup.ts`'s zip-path collisions, i18n key symmetry, route-level authorization, bulk-operation symmetry between the live app and codegen.ts) and found every one of them already correctly handled or intentional, before landing on a genuinely new instance of the same shape inside `automations.ts` itself -- not a codegen.ts-parity gap this time (codegen.ts has no automations/WhatsApp feature at all), but a gap between two field-type branches within the *same function*.

**The finding**: `interpolateTemplate` (`apps/api/src/automations.ts`, pre-fix lines 29-37) special-cased `boolean` (`"TRUE"`/`"FALSE"`) and `enum` (translated label) -- added by round 647 -- but fell through to a bare `String(value)` for every other field type, including `date` and `number`. A business owner building an automation rule's message template with `"Hi {{customerName}}, your appointment on {{date}} is confirmed"` or `"Your total is {{total}}"` (both directly reachable through the existing `AutomationsPanel.tsx` UI, using any of the built-in domain-library entities that already have `date`/`number` fields, e.g. `Appointment`'s `date` or `Invoice`'s `total` in `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`) would have the real WhatsApp message sent to the customer read the field's raw stored form -- `"2026-03-15"` instead of the locale-formatted date the business owner herself sees on screen (`"15.3.2026"` in Hebrew, `"3/15/2026"` in English), and `"1500"` instead of `"1,500"`. The function's own pre-fix doc comment explicitly says it models boolean/enum "the same way entityFormatting.ts's/backup.ts's own `fieldDisplayValue` does for CSV export" -- but `fieldDisplayValue`'s own doc comment (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts` lines 950-968) explains *why* it deliberately leaves date/number raw: a CSV export must round-trip through `buildImportRecords`, and a locale-formatted `"1,500"`/`"1/2/2024"` would fail that re-parse. That rationale is specific to CSV and does not apply to an outbound WhatsApp message, which is never re-imported -- it's pure one-way human reading, the exact situation the on-screen table cell (`formatDateValue`/`formatNumberValue`, same file, lines 118/183) is already in. Round 647 modeled this function on the wrong sibling convention.

**Independent verification**: read `interpolateTemplate` and its doc comment directly, confirmed the `boolean`/`enum` branches exist and `date`/`number` genuinely fall through to the bare `String(value)` return. Read `fieldDisplayValue` in full (`entityFormatting.ts` lines 950-983) and confirmed its own doc comment states the CSV-round-trip rationale verbatim. Read `formatDateValue`/`formatNumberValue`/`parseFieldDate`/the `LOCALE` map (`entityFormatting.ts` lines 4, 53, 118-121, 183-184, 773-780) to confirm the exact locale-formatting convention the table cell already uses, and empirically checked the real `toLocaleDateString`/`toLocaleString` output for both `he-IL`/`en-US` in this Node runtime (`"15.3.2026"`/`"3/15/2026"`, `"1,500"`/`"1,500"`) rather than assuming it. Confirmed `apps/api/src/twin.ts` line 475 already solves the identical "no stored per-project language preference" problem via `isHebrewText(project.description)` (exported from `@forge/spec-engine`, already a dependency of `apps/api`), giving a precedent for picking a locale in this same package without new plumbing. Grepped every call site of `interpolateTemplate` (exactly one, in `fireRule`) and of the existing `automations.test.ts` coverage, confirming zero existing tests exercised a `date` or `number` field through this function.

**The fix**: added a local `Lang`/`LOCALE` (mirroring `entityFormatting.ts`'s own) and a local `parseFieldDate` helper to `automations.ts` (duplicated rather than cross-imported, since `apps/api` cannot import from `apps/web/src` -- the same duplication convention `codegen.ts` already uses for its own copies of live-app logic). `interpolateTemplate`'s signature gained a required fourth `lang: Lang` parameter; its `date` branch now parses via `parseFieldDate` and renders via `date.toLocaleDateString(LOCALE[lang])` (falling back to the raw stored value if unparseable, matching `formatDateValue`'s own fallback), and its `number` branch renders via `Number(value).toLocaleString(LOCALE[lang])`. `fireRule` now computes `const lang: Lang = isHebrewText(project.description) ? "he" : "en";` and threads it into the `interpolateTemplate` call.

**The tests**: updated all 4 existing `interpolateTemplate` call sites in `automations.test.ts` to pass `"en"` as the new required argument. Added two new tests: one confirming a `date` field renders as `"3/15/2026"`/`"15.3.2026"` and a `number` field as `"1,500"` in English/Hebrew respectively (not the raw `"2026-03-15"`/`"1500"`), and one confirming a genuinely invalid date string still falls back to its raw stored value rather than producing `"Invalid Date"`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `automations.ts` to scratchpad, reverted only it via `git checkout --` (keeping the test file). Re-ran `automations.test.ts` against the reverted source: exactly 1 failure as predicted -- the new locale-formatting test, with the exact predicted mismatch (`actual: 'Due 2026-03-15, total 1500'` vs `expected: 'Due 3/15/2026, total 1,500'`); the new invalid-date-fallback test coincidentally still passed against the reverted source too, since a bare raw-value passthrough (the old behavior for every date, valid or not) happens to match that test's own expected fallback behavior -- 16/17. Restored the fix from the scratchpad backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q` (no output). Re-ran the single-file suite clean (17/17, +2). The full `@forge/api` suite had already been run clean with this exact fix in place *before* the revert/restore cycle -- 567/567, with no flake this time (unlike round 650's unrelated `password.test.ts` flake) -- and since only `apps/api` files changed this round (no `apps/web` diff at all, and codegen.ts has no automations feature to mirror), that result stands; re-running it again post-restore was not needed. Full `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` + vite for `@forge/web`, esbuild for `@forge/api`). Commit `58b1469`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Automation messages now render a date/number field the same way a business owner already sees it on screen, in both supported languages, closing the last field-type gap in `interpolateTemplate`'s own type-aware formatting (boolean and enum were already covered by round 647; relation was already resolved to a display label by `resolveRelationFieldsForTemplate`). Unlike rounds 648-650, this was not a codegen.ts-parity gap -- codegen.ts has no automations/WhatsApp feature at all -- so there was no second file to port the fix into. This round's own Explore survey ruled out several other strong-looking candidates as already solid (see its own report, summarized in Independent verification above); a future round applying this same lens would need genuinely fresh territory, since this survey's negative findings (checkpointDiff required-ness, handleBulkUpdate's blank-value design, fireRule's toField safety, backup.ts's zip-path collision impossibility, i18n symmetry, route authorization, bulk-operation symmetry) are now also effectively closed.

### Round 652: a message deleted by another collaborator between two "Load older messages" clicks made WhatsAppPanel silently and permanently skip the next real message, with no error and no duplicate to reveal it

**Context**: this round's Explore survey continued the "N parallel paths, fixed for some but not all" lens that has found a genuine bug in every one of the last nine rounds (643-651), but landed on a NEW variant of the shape: not a fix missing from a sibling path, but a fix (round 476's own insertion-shift dedup guard) that reasoned through only one of two symmetric failure modes of the exact same race, inside its own doc comment, and never considered the other.

**The finding**: `listWhatsAppMessages` (`packages/db/src/whatsapp.ts`, pre-fix) paginated with a plain SQL `OFFSET` over a `DESC`-ordered log. An offset recomputes a page's position from the top of that ordering on every call -- it says "skip N rows," not "start after this specific row." `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s `handleLoadMore` read `messages.length` as that offset at click time, and its own doc comment already reasoned through what happens when a *new* message is **inserted** above the boundary between two clicks (the "older" page shifts down and re-includes a row already shown, which round 476 fixed by deduping the fetched page against `prev`). It never considered the symmetric case: a message **deleted** above the boundary (via `DELETE /projects/:id/integrations/whatsapp/messages/:messageId`, gated by `requireProjectAccess` -- reachable by any collaborator, not just whoever is paginating) shifts the log the other way, so the next offset-based "load more" call silently skips exactly one message. Unlike the insertion case, there's no duplicate id for the existing dedup filter to catch -- the skipped message simply never appears, in that session or any later reload of that same stale page, with `hasMore` still reporting `true` as if nothing were missing.

**Independent verification**: read `listWhatsAppMessages`'s real SQL directly and confirmed it used `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` over `ORDER BY createdAt DESC, rowid DESC`. Read `handleLoadMore`'s own doc comment in full and confirmed it explicitly reasons through the insertion-shift case (citing round 476) but never mentions deletion. Manually worked through the row arithmetic for a 5-row log with a page size of 2: fetching page 1 (rows 4,3), deleting row 4, then fetching "page 2" at offset 2 returns rows 1,0 instead of 2,1 -- row 2 is skipped, never duplicated. Confirmed `messagesVersionRef` (the existing same-session race guard) is bumped only by the LOCAL session's own `handleDisconnect`/`handleDeleteMessage`/`handleClearHistory`, never by a remote collaborator's edit, so it cannot and was never meant to catch this. Confirmed the delete-one-message route uses `requireProjectAccess` (any collaborator), not an owner-only check, so the race is practically reachable by anyone with access to the project, not just its owner. Confirmed `WhatsAppMessage.id` is a non-sortable `randomUUID()` `TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, so a real fix needs SQLite's own hidden per-row `rowid` (not a declared column) as the sortable cursor component, mirroring the tie-break role it already plays in the existing `ORDER BY createdAt DESC, rowid DESC`.

**The fix**: rewrote `listWhatsAppMessages` (`packages/db/src/whatsapp.ts`) from offset-based to keyset (cursor) pagination. It now accepts an optional opaque `cursor?: string | null` (`"<createdAt>|<rowid>"`, taken from a previous page's own `nextCursor`) instead of a numeric offset, explicitly selects `rowid AS _rowid`, and filters with `WHERE projectId = ? AND (createdAt < ? OR (createdAt = ? AND rowid < ?))` when a cursor is given -- pinning "everything strictly after this specific row" rather than a row count, so it is unaffected by any number of inserts or deletes elsewhere in the log. A new `parseWhatsAppMessagesCursor` helper tolerantly falls back to "start from the newest message" for a missing, malformed, or hand-edited cursor, the same tolerance the old numeric `offset` param already had for a non-numeric value. The public `WhatsAppMessage` type is untouched -- the cursor is a separate pagination token built and consumed only by this function's own return value/parameter. Threaded the new signature through every call site: `collectAllWhatsAppMessages` (`apps/api/src/backup.ts`, the full-history export loop), the `GET .../whatsapp/messages` route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`, now reading `?cursor=` instead of `?offset=`), the web API client (`apps/web/src/api.ts`), and `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`, which gained a `nextCursorRef` (a ref, not state, since setting it never needs to trigger a re-render on its own) updated alongside every one of the 5 existing `setHasMoreMessages` call sites: the two initial-load paths (`startPolling`'s reconnect transition, `loadInitialStatus`) store the fetched page's own `nextCursor`; `handleDisconnect` and `handleClearHistory` null it out; and `handleLoadMore` -- the actual core of the fix -- now reads `nextCursorRef.current` instead of `messages.length` as its request's cursor, and stores the fresh page's own `nextCursor` afterward. The existing id-based dedup filter in `handleLoadMore` stays as defense-in-depth against the one race a cursor still doesn't cover (a message landing in the brief window between reading the cursor and the server running the query, which can repeat the cursor's own row but never cause a skip).

**The tests**: reworked `packages/db/src/whatsapp.test.ts`'s existing pagination test to pass cursors (each page's own returned `nextCursor`) instead of literal numeric offsets, and added a new test that inserts 5 messages, reads page 1's cursor, deletes the newest message (above the page-1/page-2 boundary) via `deleteWhatsAppMessage`, then fetches page 2 with the stored cursor and confirms every remaining message is still reached in the right order -- reproducing the exact round-652 bug scenario and confirming the fix prevents it. Updated the one pre-existing test in `packages/db/src/projects.test.ts` whose literal `deepEqual` against `listWhatsAppMessages`'s return shape broke on the new `nextCursor` field, an expected consequence of the correct shape change. In `apps/web/src/WhatsAppPanel.test.ts`, updated 4 real-render tests (`fetch` mocks keyed on `offset=`/`offset=2` query strings) to key on `cursor=`/a real `cursor-after-page1` token instead, and updated 2 `new Function`-based handler-extraction tests (`handleDisconnect`'s successful-disconnect case, `startPolling`'s "becoming connected, no race" case) to inject the new `nextCursorRef` free variable the extracted code now references -- without it, the extracted code's new `nextCursorRef.current = ...` line threw a `ReferenceError` that was silently swallowed by the surrounding `try`/`catch` already in `handleDisconnect`'s real source, producing a wrong-looking assertion failure (`startConnectedPollingCalls` off by one) rather than an obvious crash. Added an explicit assertion that a successful disconnect clears `nextCursorRef.current` to `null`, and that `startPolling`'s "becoming connected" path stores the fetched page's own `nextCursor`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up all 5 fixed source files (`whatsapp.ts`, `backup.ts`, `routes/projects.ts`, `api.ts`, `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`) to scratchpad. ### Round 653: table-view keyboard shortcuts (j/k/x/Delete/d/Enter/n) checked only `e.key`, so a browser/OS modifier shortcut like Ctrl/Cmd+D silently fired the real duplicate-record request instead

**Context**: continuing the "N parallel paths, inconsistently covered" lens for a tenth consecutive round (643-652 plus this one), this round's Explore survey was steered toward fresh territory -- codegen.ts/live-app parity for features codegen.ts actually implements, validation/authorization consistency, bulk-vs-single-record symmetry, and the round-652 "doc comment reasoning through only one symmetric direction" angle applied to other open/close, forward/backward, and create/delete pairs -- with every topic closed through round 652 ruled off-limits. It landed on a genuinely new instance: not a missing symmetric case this time, but a missing *guard* that every sibling keydown handler in the codebase already has.

**The finding**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s table-view row-shortcut effect (pre-fix lines 1651-1692: j/k/ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Enter/x/Delete/Backspace/d/Escape) and its separate "n"-shortcut effect (pre-fix lines 1707-1716) each tested only `e.key`, with no check of `e.ctrlKey`/`e.metaKey`/`e.altKey`. `e.key` is the same bare letter (`"d"`, `"k"`, `"n"`, ...) whether or not a modifier is held, and the guards that already run first in both effects (`isTypingTarget(e.target)`, `isAnyDialogOpen()`) look only at the event's target and whether a dialog is open, never at its modifier flags. Every other keydown handler in the file (and in `App.tsx`) already checks modifiers: `App.tsx:770`'s own Ctrl/Cmd+K search shortcut, the record-form's Ctrl/Cmd+Enter submit (`EntityPanel.tsx:2482`), and the inline longtext-cell-editor's Ctrl/Cmd+Enter carve-out (`EntityPanel.tsx:2412`) -- `grep ctrlKey|metaKey apps/web/src/*.tsx` returns exactly those three lines, and none of them are the two effects in question. With a row keyboard-focused (an entirely ordinary state for anyone using j/k navigation), pressing **Ctrl+D** or **Cmd+D** -- the browser's own "bookmark this page" shortcut -- matched the `e.key === "d" && isFocusedRowVisible` branch and called `handleDuplicate(focusedRowId)` (`EntityPanel.tsx:1920-1932`) exactly as a bare "d" would: a real `createRecord` POST, with **no confirmation dialog**, since duplicating is deliberately designed to skip one ("duplicating creates rather than destroys", per that function's own doc comment). The identical shape hijacks Ctrl/Cmd+K (moves row focus instead of letting `App.tsx`'s own search shortcut look clean -- both listeners fire for the same event since neither calls `stopPropagation`), Ctrl+J (Chrome's Downloads shortcut), Cmd+Backspace (opens the delete-confirm dialog), Ctrl/Cmd+Enter (opens the focused row for editing instead of reaching the form's own submit shortcut), and Ctrl/Alt+N in any environment that delivers it to the page. `codegen.ts`'s exported-app mirror of both effects (`codegen.ts:3439-3480`, `3490-3498`) has the byte-for-byte identical gap, confirmed by reading it directly.

**Independent verification**: read both EntityPanel.tsx effects directly and confirmed neither references `ctrlKey`/`metaKey`/`altKey` anywhere in their bodies. Grepped `apps/web/src/*.tsx` for every modifier check in the codebase and confirmed exactly 3 exist, none in the two effects in question. Read `handleDuplicate` directly and confirmed it has no confirmation step and performs a real `createRecord` POST. Read `App.tsx:770`'s Ctrl+K handler and confirmed it is a second, independent `window` `keydown` listener with no `stopPropagation`, so both fire on the same event. Read `codegen.ts`'s two mirrored effects directly and confirmed the identical missing check. Confirmed via the survey's own grep that no other component in the app (GlobalSearch, History, WhatsApp panel, ShortcutsPanel, etc.) has a bare single-letter shortcut with this same gap -- it's confined to these two effects and their two codegen.ts mirrors.

**The fix**: added `if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;` as the first line of both handlers in `EntityPanel.tsx` (before the existing `isTypingTarget`/`isAnyDialogOpen` check), and the identical line to both mirrored handlers in `codegen.ts`. A bare key press (no modifier) is completely unaffected; any modifier-held press now falls through to the browser/OS's own default handling instead.

**The tests**: added a new real-render test to `EntityPanel.test.ts` confirming Ctrl+D and Cmd+D never trigger the real duplicate POST (count stays 0) and never move row focus for Ctrl+K or open the row for Ctrl+Enter, then confirms a bare "d" with no modifier still works -- proving the guard doesn't over-suppress the ordinary shortcut. Added two assertions to the existing "n" shortcut test confirming Ctrl+N and Alt+N leave an in-progress edit untouched. Added a mirrored real-render test to `codegen.test.ts` (using the existing `generateExportFiles`/dynamic-`import()` harness the file's other EntityView shortcut tests already use) confirming the same Ctrl+D/Cmd+D-never-duplicates behavior in the exported app, with a bare "d" still working.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed source files (`EntityPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`) to scratchpad. Reverted `EntityPanel.tsx` alone via `git checkout --`: `EntityPanel.test.ts` failed exactly the 2 predicted tests (the new Ctrl/Cmd/Alt-modifier test, and the "n" test's new Ctrl+N assertion) with the exact predicted mismatches (`1 !== 0` on the duplicate-POST count; `'' !== 'Globex'` on the reset-despite-modifier check) -- 132/134. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (134/134, hit the known round-649 hang-on-exit in this same file after all tests reported `ok`, same as every prior round that touched it). Reverted `codegen.ts` alone: `codegen.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test (the new exported-app Ctrl/Cmd+D test) -- 213/214. Restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran clean (214/214). Ran the full `@forge/api` suite: one spurious failure on the first attempt (no `not ok` line in the captured output, consistent with the known CPU-contention flake, not a real regression), clean 568/568 on immediate re-run. Full `@forge/web` glob run reached the same known `EntityPanel.test.ts` hang-on-exit after 301/301 reported tests passed with zero failures (the isolated single-file run above already proved this file's own 134/134 cleanly, independent of the hang). ### Round 654: the table view's Enter shortcut had no idea where the keydown it just hijacked actually came from, so Enter on an unrelated focused Save/Delete/Duplicate button silently discarded whatever that button was about to do

**Context**: continuing the "N parallel/structurally-similar paths, inconsistently covered" lens for an eleventh consecutive round (643-653 plus this one), this round's Explore survey was steered toward fresh territory -- mouse/pointer handlers for a round-653-shaped missing-guard, codegen.ts parity for features it actually implements, accessibility gaps in unaudited components, and the round-652 "doc comment reasoning through only one symmetric case" angle applied to other open/close and expand/collapse pairs -- with every topic closed through round 653 ruled off-limits. It found something closer to round 653's own shape than any of those: not a missing modifier-key guard this time, but a missing *target* check on the one key (Enter) that, uniquely among this effect's own key set, already has a native meaning on the element the keydown might actually be coming from.

**The finding**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s table-view row-shortcut effect (the same `window`-level keydown listener round 653 fixed) opens the keyboard-"focused" row for editing on Enter (pre-fix lines 1680-1685) by checking only `e.key === "Enter" && isFocusedRowVisible` -- never `e.target`. `focusedRowId` (line 934) is purely a *visual* highlight set by j/k/ArrowUp/ArrowDown (`setFocusedRowId`, lines 1676/1679); nothing in that code path ever calls `.focus()` on a real DOM node. So once a user has pressed `j` even once, `focusedRowId` stays set indefinitely while real DOM focus can be anywhere else entirely -- on the record form's own `<button type="submit">` after Tab, on a *different* row's Delete/Duplicate button, on a cell's auto-linked `<a href>`, or on any other button on the page. `isTypingTarget` (the guard that already runs first) deliberately excludes `BUTTON` -- confirmed by its own existing test asserting `isTypingTarget({tagName: "BUTTON"})` is `false` -- because j/k/x/Delete/d have no native meaning on a focused button. Enter is the one key in this effect's own set that both *does* have one (native activation of a focused `<button>`/`<a href>`/`role="button"` element) and was never checked for it. Concretely: focus row 1 with `j`, open row 2 for editing and type an unsaved change, Tab to the form's own Save button, press Enter -- the window listener's `e.preventDefault()` suppresses the button's native activation (calling `preventDefault()` on a bubbling keydown does suppress a focused button's own Enter-triggered click), and `startEdit(record1)` fires instead, silently replacing the form with row 1's values and discarding row 2's edit with no confirmation. The identical byte-for-byte gap exists in `codegen.ts`'s mirrored effect (`codegen.ts:3464-3470` pre-fix).

**Independent verification**: read the Enter branch directly in both files and confirmed neither reads `e.target`. Read `isTypingTarget` (`entityFormatting.ts`) directly and confirmed it excludes `BUTTON`/`A` by design, and read its own existing test asserting exactly that. Grepped every `setFocusedRowId` call site (exactly 2, both inside the j/k branches) and confirmed none of them, nor anywhere else in the file, ever calls `.focus()` on a DOM node -- `focusedRowId` is state-only. Confirmed round 350's own precedent for this exact hazard class: the calendar day cell's `onKeyDown` (`EntityPanel.tsx:565-577`) already guards an analogous "a focused child's own Enter bubbles up and gets reinterpreted by a parent handler" case with `if (e.target !== e.currentTarget) return;` -- a per-element React handler can compare targets directly; this effect is a single `window`-level listener with no single "this element" to compare against, so the equivalent fix has to ask "is the target itself (or an ancestor) a native activation target" via `closest()` instead. Confirmed `codegen.ts`'s mirrored effect has the byte-for-byte identical gap by reading it directly.

**The fix**: added `enterTargetsInteractiveElement` to `entityFormatting.ts`, checking `target.closest('button, a[href], [role="button"], summary')`, and wired it into the Enter branch's condition alongside a new `!e.defaultPrevented` check (covering the one case the `closest()` walk can't: a React `onKeyDown` on a non-native `role="button"` element -- `EntityLabelEditor`'s own rename trigger -- that already handled this exact Enter and called its own `preventDefault()`). Ported the identical helper and condition into `codegen.ts`'s mirrored effect. The public type of nothing else changes -- this is purely an additional guard on when the Enter branch is allowed to fire.

**The tests**: added `enterTargetsInteractiveElement`'s own unit tests to `entityFormatting.test.ts` (duck-typed `closest()` stubs, mirroring `isTypingTarget`'s own plain-Node testing convention in that file, since it has no jsdom). Added a real-render regression test to `EntityPanel.test.ts` reproducing the exact scenario: focus row 1 with `j`, open row 2 for editing and change its name, move real DOM focus to the Save button, fire a real `Enter` keydown targeted at that button, and confirm the edit draft survives untouched (not reset to row 1's values) and no PATCH fires. Added the mirrored real-render test to `codegen.test.ts` using the file's existing `generateExportFiles`/dynamic-`import()` EntityView harness.

**Regression-proof**: backed up all 3 fixed source files (`entityFormatting.ts`, `EntityPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`) to scratchpad. Reverted `entityFormatting.ts` and `EntityPanel.tsx` together (they're coupled by the new export/import): `entityFormatting.test.ts` failed at module load exactly as predicted (`SyntaxError: ... does not provide an export named 'enterTargetsInteractiveElement'`, the standing "module-load crash = strong confirmation" signal), and `EntityPanel.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test with the exact predicted mismatch (`'Acme Corp' !== 'Globex Renamed'`, confirming Enter on the focused Save button really did hijack to row 1) -- 134/135. Restored both from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran both clean (152/152, 135/135). Reverted `codegen.ts` alone: `codegen.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test with the identical mismatch pattern, plus one unrelated flake (`EADDRINUSE` port collision on an unrelated real-server-spawn test, confirmed transient by its clean re-run) -- 213/215. Restored, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran clean (215/215). Ran the full suites: `@forge/api` 569/569, `@forge/web` 928/928 -- the full glob run completed cleanly end-to-end this time with no hang-on-exit (unlike every prior round that touched `EntityPanel.test.ts`), confirming that hang is a genuine intermittent environment artifact, not something tied to any particular source state. Full `npm run build` clean, including `tsc -b` for `@forge/web`. Commit `9f2656d`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The table view's Enter shortcut now defers to a focused button/link's own native activation instead of always reinterpreting the key as "open the visually-focused row," closing the one case in this effect's own key set (Enter alone, among j/k/x/Delete/d) where that reinterpretation could silently destroy real work. This is the eleventh consecutive round (643-653 plus this one) to find a genuine bug under the "N parallel/structurally-similar paths, inconsistently covered" lens, and the second in a row (after round 653) to find it specifically in this one `window`-level keydown effect -- a future round would need to establish this effect has a third such gap before returning to it, since this round's own verification covered its full guard chain (modifiers, typing targets, dialog state, and now interactive-element targets) against every key it currently handles.

### Round 655: the exported app's own GlobalSearch and ShortcutsPanel could stack on top of each other, each marking the other inert and aria-hidden, because its App.jsx never adopted the live preview's own dialog-exclusivity guard

**Context**: two consecutive rounds (653, 654) had found genuine bugs in the exact same `window`-level keydown effect in `EntityPanel.tsx`/`codegen.ts`, but that effect's own guard chain was verified complete after round 654, so this round's Explore survey was explicitly steered away from it -- toward other window/document-level event listeners anywhere else in the codebase, mouse/pointer handlers, and codegen.ts parity for features it implements but hadn't been audited yet. It found a different `window`-level keydown effect entirely -- codegen.ts's generated `App.jsx`, not `EntityPanel.tsx`/`EntityView.jsx` -- with a gap the live preview had already fixed for itself three rounds after the exported app's own search/shortcuts wiring was ported, in a way the parity-porting round never revisited.

**The finding**: codegen.ts's `renderAppJsx` (pre-fix, the `window` `keydown` effect around lines 5575-5600) tracks `showSearch` and `showShortcuts` as two completely independent `useState` booleans. Its three "open" branches (Ctrl/Cmd+K, "/", "?") each set one of those booleans directly, with no check of whether the other dialog is already open, and the two overlays render as unconditional sibling `{showX && <Component/>}` blocks. The live preview's own `App.tsx:766-788` handles the identical three shortcuts through `openPanel()` (already mutually exclusive among its six panels by construction) plus an explicit `if (isAnyDialogOpen()) return;` guard added in round 366 for the two dialogs `openPanel` doesn't cover. codegen.ts's exported app has no `openPanel`-equivalent at all -- `setShowSearch`/`setShowShortcuts` are called directly -- and never imported or checked `isAnyDialogOpen` (which `EntityView.jsx` already exports in the same generated bundle, and which the exported app's own `EntityPanel`-equivalent keydown effects already consume, per rounds 653/654). Concretely: press "?" to open ShortcutsPanel (its own focus trap puts focus on its Close button, not an editable target), then press "/" or Ctrl+K -- GlobalSearch mounts on top of the still-open ShortcutsPanel. Both overlays share the same `.search-overlay`/`.search-panel` CSS, and GlobalSearch's own `hideDialogBackgroundFromAssistiveTech` walks the DOM tree marking every unmarked sibling `inert`/`aria-hidden` as "background" -- which now includes the ShortcutsPanel overlay sitting underneath it, since nothing distinguishes "the real page" from "another dialog" in that walk. The dialog visually on top (whichever opened second) is the one the user can see, but the dialog actually reachable by keyboard/Tab/screen-reader is whichever opened first and is now marked inert underneath it -- and the exported app's own Escape branch (handled in this same function, unlike the live preview where Escape lives separately in `useDialogFocusTrap.ts`) closes both dialogs unconditionally on a single press either way, discarding whatever was in the search box.

**Independent verification**: read `renderAppJsx`'s generated keydown handler directly (codegen.ts lines ~5575-5600 pre-fix) and confirmed none of the three open branches checks dialog state, and confirmed the import list (lines ~5417-5420) never imports `isAnyDialogOpen`. Read the live preview's `App.tsx:766-788` directly and confirmed its `isAnyDialogOpen()` guard and its round-366 doc comment explaining the exact "two simultaneous focus traps fighting over the same Tab cycle and background inert state" hazard this round reproduces in the exported app. Confirmed via grep that `isAnyDialogOpen`/`markDialogOpen`/`markDialogClosed` are defined once in the generated `EntityView.jsx` (consistent with rounds 653/654's own citations) and already flipped by both `GlobalSearch.jsx`'s and `ShortcutsPanel.jsx`'s own mount/unmount effects -- so the counter this round's fix needs already exists and already tracks exactly these two dialogs correctly; only `App.jsx` itself never consulted it. Confirmed the exported app has no other dialogs beyond these two (unlike the live preview's `openPanel`'s six panels plus ChangePassword/DeleteAccount), so a single `isAnyDialogOpen()` check on the three open branches is sufficient parity, with no equivalent to `openPanel`'s own extra mutual-exclusivity needed. Confirmed directly that the exported app's Escape branch lives in the same handler as the three open branches (unlike the live preview's separate `useDialogFocusTrap.ts`), meaning a blanket top-of-function guard (mirroring the live app's `if (isAnyDialogOpen()) return;` verbatim) would have broken Escape's own ability to close an already-open dialog -- the fix has to gate only the three open branches, not Escape.

**The fix**: added `import { isAnyDialogOpen } from "./components/EntityView.jsx";` to the generated `App.jsx`'s imports, and `if (isAnyDialogOpen()) return;` as the first line inside each of the three open branches (Ctrl+K, "/", "?") -- never inside the Escape branch, which still unconditionally closes whichever dialog is actually open. Updated the doc comment above the effect to explain the round-655 rationale and why Escape is deliberately excluded from the new check.

**The tests**: added a new end-to-end test to `codegen.test.ts` using the file's existing full-`App.jsx` render harness (`generateExportFiles`/`writeGeneratedWebComponent`/dynamic `import()`). Reproduces both stacking directions: opens ShortcutsPanel via "?", then fires "/" and separately Ctrl+K, asserting exactly one `[role="dialog"]` remains mounted and it's still the shortcuts panel (GlobalSearch's own `.global-search-input` never appears) each time; then Escape closes it cleanly. Repeats in reverse -- opens GlobalSearch via "/", fires "?", asserts exactly one dialog remains (still GlobalSearch, `.shortcuts-list` never appears) -- then Escape closes that one too.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `codegen.ts` to scratchpad. Reverted it alone via `git checkout --`: `codegen.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test, with the exact predicted mismatch (`2 !== 1` dialogs mounted after pressing "/" while ShortcutsPanel was already open) -- 215/216. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (216/216). Since only `apps/api` files changed this round, ran that workspace's full suite (570/570) plus the full `npm run build` (clean, including `tsc -b` for `@forge/web`) rather than the `@forge/web` suite too, per the standing single-workspace-change shortcut. Commit `3183c2b`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The exported app's own global-search and keyboard-shortcuts overlays now respect the same mutual-exclusivity the live preview's `openPanel()` already gave its own panels, closing a parity gap that opened specifically when `ShortcutsPanel` was ported (round ~629) without revisiting an earlier round's correct-at-the-time note that "there was nothing to stack" in the exported app. This is the twelfth consecutive round (643-654 plus this one) to find a genuine bug under the "N parallel/structurally-similar paths, inconsistently covered" lens -- this instance's variant being a fix (round 366's `isAnyDialogOpen` guard) that reached one of two parallel implementations (live preview, exported app) but not the other, compounded by a doc comment whose "no parity fix needed" reasoning silently stopped being true once a second exported-app dialog was added. A future round checking `App.jsx`'s own dialog handling specifically would need fresh territory, since this round's own survey confirmed the exported app has no dialogs beyond these two, and both already flip the correct shared counter.

### Round 656: a board column's drop handler accepted any drag -- an entity tab or a file from the desktop -- and fell through to a real PATCH for a nonexistent record, unlike its own sibling calendar drop handler right below it

**Context**: this round's Explore survey was steered toward fresh territory beyond dialogs/overlays (rounds 655 and earlier having closed out the keydown-effect and dialog-exclusivity families), toward drag-and-drop, pointer handlers, and other per-view event wiring. It landed on `EntityPanel.tsx`'s board (Kanban) view drop handler, finding a gap against a guard its own documented sibling -- the calendar view's drop handler a few dozen lines below it -- already had.

**The finding**: `handleCardDrop` (pre-fix, `EntityPanel.tsx` lines ~2271-2281) reads `const id = Number(e.dataTransfer.getData("text/plain"));`, checks `if (Number.isNaN(id)) return;`, then looks up `const record = records.find((r) => (r.id as number) === id);` and proceeds to `if (record && String(record[fieldName] ?? "") === value) return;` before calling `void handleMove(id, fieldName, value);` unconditionally otherwise. A board column's native `onDrop` fires for *any* drag ending over it, not just its own `.board-card` elements: App.tsx's entity-tab drag (`App.tsx:2009`) never calls `e.dataTransfer.setData(...)` in its own `onDragStart`, and a file dragged in from the desktop carries `types: ["Files"]`, not `text/plain` -- both produce `getData("text/plain") === ""`. `Number("")` evaluates to `0`, not `NaN`, so `Number.isNaN(id)` lets `id = 0` straight through. `records.find(...)` then correctly returns `undefined` for a nonexistent id `0`, but `record && ...` short-circuits to `false` (not a throw, not a skip) when `record` is falsy -- so the intended "skip if this condition is true" reasoning silently does nothing, and execution falls through to `void handleMove(0, fieldName, value)`. `handleMoveFields`/`handleMove` (`EntityPanel.tsx:2245-2258`) issues a real `updateRecord(projectId, entity.name, 0, fields)` PATCH; the server's `parseRecordId` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:466-471`) accepts `"0"` as a valid id (matches `/^\d+$/`), so the request reaches `packages/db/src/repository.ts`, which throws `NotFoundError: "Record 0 not found in <Entity>"` (`repository.ts:197`) since no such record exists -- surfacing a real, visible `<p className="error">` banner over a board where the user never actually dragged a card. The calendar view's own drop handler, documented in an earlier round as this handler's direct structural sibling, already guards this exact case: `if (record) onReschedule(...)` -- it simply never fires when `record` is `undefined`, with no equivalent gap. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported `EntityView.jsx` template mirrors the live `handleCardDrop` line-for-line, including the same gap.

**Independent verification**: read `EntityPanel.tsx:2271-2281` (`handleCardDrop`) and `EntityPanel.tsx:595-599` (the calendar view's sibling drop handler) directly, confirming the calendar handler's `if (record) ...` guard and the board handler's missing equivalent. Read `App.tsx:2009` directly and confirmed the entity-tab drag's `onDragStart` never calls `setData`, so its `text/plain` payload is genuinely `""` on drop, not merely assumed. Read `EntityPanel.tsx:2245-2258` (`handleMoveFields`/`handleMove`) directly and confirmed it issues a real `await updateRecord(...)` PATCH inside try/catch, with `setError`/`setMoveErrorId` on failure producing a real error banner, not a silently-swallowed rejection. Read `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:466-471` (`parseRecordId`) and `packages/db/src/repository.ts:197` directly and confirmed `"0"` passes the id-format check and reaches a lookup that throws `NotFoundError` for a genuinely nonexistent record. Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `handleCardDrop` template directly and confirmed it reproduces the identical gap (same `Number.isNaN` check, same unguarded `record && ...` short-circuit, same fallthrough to `handleMove`) -- a live-app/exported-app parity match rather than a divergence, so both needed the same fix.

**The fix**: added `if (!record) return;` immediately after the `records.find(...)` lookup, before the "already in this column" no-op check, in both `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `handleCardDrop` and `codegen.ts`'s mirrored generated copy -- matching the calendar view's own sibling guard exactly. A column drop with no real record id now does nothing at all, rather than falling through to a PATCH for an id that was never a real card.

**The tests**: added `"EntityPanel's board column drop with no real record id (an entity tab or a dragged-in file) is a silent no-op, not a PATCH to a nonexistent record"` to `EntityPanel.test.ts`, firing a board column drop with a `dataTransfer.getData` that returns `""` and asserting zero PATCH requests, no error banner, and the one real record's field completely untouched. Updated the pre-existing literal-source regex assertion in `codegen.test.ts` (which asserted the old `if (record && ...) return;` text verbatim) to assert the new `if (!record) return;` line instead, and added a new end-to-end test using the file's full-render harness (`generateExportFiles`/`writeGeneratedWebComponent`/dynamic `import()` of the generated `EntityView.jsx`) reproducing the same empty-payload board drop against the real exported component and asserting zero PATCH calls and an untouched record.
