### Round 657: CSV export's own label-disambiguation fix (rounds 635-642) broke the CSV import round-trip it was meant to protect -- re-importing an exported CSV for an entity with two same-labeled fields silently lost both fields' data

**Context**: round 656's own survey flagged three unverified leftover drag-and-drop leads as possible round-657 candidates but didn't pursue them. This round's Explore survey checked all three directly first (see below -- two were ruled out as non-reachable/non-exploitable, one was confirmed real but minor) before broadening to fresh territory, landing on a genuinely new instance of the "fix applied to one side of a round-trip pair, not the other" shape: a CSV-export feature's own disambiguation fix from six rounds ago (635-642) never got the matching fix on the import side, breaking the exact round-trip scenario those rounds' own commit messages cite as their motivation.

**The finding**: `fieldDisplayLabel` (`entityFormatting.ts:1034-1037`, mirrored in `codegen.ts:1858-1861`) appends a field's own always-unique name to its label whenever it collides with a sibling's label -- e.g. two number fields both labeled "Amount" export via `recordsToCsv` (`entityFormatting.ts:1046-1059`) with the header `Amount (subtotal),Amount (shipping)` instead of an ambiguous `Amount,Amount`. The import side's `matchesHeader` (pre-fix, `entityFormatting.ts:1144-1153`; mirrored as `matchesImportHeader`, `codegen.ts:1942-1950`) was never taught about that `" (fieldname)"` suffix -- it only ever compared the raw header text against a field's bare `name` or bare `label`. `"amount (subtotal)"` matches neither `"subtotal"` (name) nor `"amount"` (label), so the column goes completely unmatched. `buildImportRecords` (`entityFormatting.ts:1203-1230`) then treats both of the ambiguous columns as absent: an optional field silently defaults to `null` with zero errors reported; a required field (as in the exact scenario the round-637 test itself uses) produces a row-numbered "missing required field" error instead. Either way, the round-637 fix's own motivation -- "fed back through the app's own CSV import feature... would silently misassign one field's data onto the other" -- is defeated in a different, arguably worse way: total silent data loss (or an outright import failure) instead of the original misassignment. The only existing "duplicate label" import test (`entityFormatting.test.ts`, inherited from round 287) used literal identical headers (`"Status","Status"`), predating the round-637 disambiguation feature entirely, so it never exercised the `" (fieldname)"` format at all -- the gap went uncaught for twenty rounds. `codegen.ts`'s exported `EntityView.jsx` template mirrors the identical gap line-for-line.

**Independent verification**: read `entityFormatting.ts:1034-1037` (`fieldDisplayLabel`) and `entityFormatting.ts:1144-1153` (`matchesHeader`) directly, confirming the export side's disambiguation format and the import side's complete lack of any corresponding check. Read `entityFormatting.ts:1203-1230` (`buildImportRecords`) directly and confirmed an unmatched column's field resolves to `null`/a required-field error exactly as described. Read the existing round-287 test (`entityFormatting.test.ts`, literal `"Status","Status"` headers) and confirmed it predates and never exercises the round-637 header format. Read `codegen.ts`'s `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel`/`matchesImportHeader`/`buildImportRecords` directly and confirmed the identical gap in the exported app. Reproduced the bug directly (not merely inferred): `recordsToCsv` on two same-labeled required number fields produced the header `Amount (subtotal),Amount (shipping)`, and running that output straight back through `buildImportRecords` returned a row-numbered "missing required field" error for the first field and dropped the second column's match entirely -- zero successful round-trip. Separately checked and ruled out the other two leftover leads round 656 had flagged: "leftover drag-source state in reorder handlers" is not reachable, since every native HTML5 drag always fires a fresh `onDragStart` (overwriting any stale state) before any `onDrop` can read it; missing `dataTransfer.setData` on column-header/entity-tab drags is real but not exploitable, since every drop target that reads `dataTransfer.getData` already guards a falsy/NaN id correctly (including round 656's own newly-added guard). A third lead -- the column-resize handle's `onMouseDown` never checking `e.button`, so a right/middle-click-drag resizes a column exactly like a left-click-drag -- was confirmed real but minor (no sibling precedent being violated, narrow impact) and left open for a future round rather than taken as this round's fix, per the one-bug-per-round discipline.

**The fix**: `matchesHeader`/`matchesImportHeader` now take the same `labelOccurrences` map `fieldLabelOccurrences` builds for the export side, and also accept a header equal to `fieldDisplayLabel(field, labelOccurrences)` -- so a column headed `"Amount (subtotal)"` now correctly claims the `subtotal` field, mirroring the export side's own disambiguation exactly. Applied identically in `entityFormatting.ts` and `codegen.ts`.

**The tests**: added `"two same-labeled fields' CSV export round-trips back through buildImportRecords without losing either column's data"` to `entityFormatting.test.ts`, running the real `recordsToCsv -> parseCsv -> buildImportRecords` pipeline end to end on two same-labeled required number fields and asserting both values survive the round-trip. Added the mirrored end-to-end test to `codegen.test.ts` using the file's real-generated-code extraction harness. Since the fix changes `matchesHeader`/`matchesImportHeader`'s signature (both now take a third `labelOccurrences` parameter), updated every one of `codegen.test.ts`'s eight pre-existing `new Function`-based regex extractions of `matchesImportHeader` to match the new three-parameter signature, and added `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` extraction (and injection into the assembled `new Function` source) to the six of those eight blocks that didn't already pull them in for other reasons -- without this, `buildImportRecords`'s own now-added call to `fieldLabelOccurrences` would have thrown a `ReferenceError` inside every one of those extracted-and-executed test harnesses, the exact "new-Function free-variable injection" hazard flagged by the round-652 lesson.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed files (`entityFormatting.ts`, `codegen.ts`) to scratchpad. Reverted `entityFormatting.ts` alone: `entityFormatting.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test (the new round-trip test, with the exact predicted "missing required field" mismatch) -- 152/153. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (153/153). Reverted `codegen.ts` alone (with `codegen.test.ts` left at its already-updated state): failed exactly the 9 predicted tests -- every one of the nine `new Function` extraction blocks that now look for the three-parameter `matchesImportHeader` signature correctly failed its own `assert.ok` extraction check against the still-two-parameter reverted source, rather than crashing or failing on some other assertion -- 209/218. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (218/218). Since this round touched both `apps/web` and `apps/api` files, ran both workspaces' full suites sequentially: `@forge/web` (930/930 clean) and `@forge/api` (572/572 clean), plus the full `npm run build` (clean, including `tsc -b` and both workspaces' builds). Commit `fc29139`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This is the fifteenth consecutive round (643-657) to find a genuine bug under the "a fix applied to one side of a pair/one of several parallel surfaces doesn't imply the other side/surfaces inherited it" lens -- this instance's variant being a round-trip pair (CSV export and CSV import) six rounds apart in time, where the export side's fix (637) was never revisited when the import side was later exercised against its output. The round's own survey also confirmed two of round 656's three leftover drag-and-drop leads are non-issues (not reachable / not exploitable) and left the third (resize handle's missing `e.button` check) open as a minor, low-priority candidate for a future round rather than this round's own fix.

### Round 658: the column resize handle's `onMouseDown` never checked which mouse button was held, so a right-click-drag or middle-click-drag resized a column exactly like a left-click-drag

**Context**: this round's Explore survey spent most of its budget re-verifying leads from an extremely heavily-audited codebase -- the preference-store family, codegen.ts/live-preview dialog and hook parity, automations.ts, backup.ts, seed.ts, repository.ts's coerceValue, the entity/field-label-collision sweep, the keyboard-shortcut guard chain, WhatsApp pagination, projectPreferenceCleanup.ts's full 19-store sweep, and Business Twin's observation builders -- and found every one of those leads already correctly handled, with no functional impact. It surfaced only two weak candidates: a double-coincidence entity-label-collision gap in `twin.ts`'s `computeRelationHubObservation` requiring two independent rename coincidences to ever manifest (too narrow and speculative to act on), and round 657's own previously-flagged, previously-deferred minor lead -- the resize handle's missing `e.button` check -- re-confirmed as real and exactly as minor as before (not worse). With nothing stronger surfacing after a genuinely broad search, this round closes out that minor, already-identified lead rather than leaving the round empty.

**The finding**: `startResize` (pre-fix, `EntityPanel.tsx:1272-1277`; mirrored as `codegen.ts:3331-3336`) is the app's *only* `mousedown`-based drag interaction -- confirmed by grepping every `onMouseDown` in `apps/web/src`, which returns exactly one hit (`EntityPanel.tsx:3075`, wiring up `startResize`). Every other drag interaction in the app (board cards, calendar events, entity tabs, column reordering) uses native HTML5 `draggable`/`onDragStart`, which browsers themselves already restrict to the left mouse button. `startResize` never checked `e.button` at all -- it unconditionally calls `e.preventDefault()` and sets `resizingField` from `e.clientX`, so a right-click-drag or a middle-click-drag on the handle resizes the column exactly as a left-click-drag would, since the width math in the paired `handleMove`/`handleUp` effect (`EntityPanel.tsx:1249-1262`) only ever reads the clientX delta, never which button triggered the drag.

**Independent verification**: read `EntityPanel.tsx:1272-1277` (`startResize`) directly and confirmed no `e.button` check anywhere in it. Grepped every `onMouseDown` in `apps/web/src/*.tsx`/`*.ts` and confirmed `EntityPanel.tsx:3075` (wiring `startResize`) is the only hit in the entire live app. Read `EntityPanel.tsx:1249-1262` (the `handleMove`/`handleUp` effect) directly and confirmed the global `mouseup` listener ends the drag regardless of which button is released, so the fix only needs to gate entry at `startResize` itself -- once `resizingField` is never set for a non-left-click, `handleMove`/`handleUp` are never reached for that interaction at all. Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts:3331-3336` (`startResize`) and `codegen.ts:4648` (its `onMouseDown` wiring) directly and confirmed the identical gap, byte-for-byte, in the exported/generated app.

**The fix**: added `if (e.button !== 0) return;` as the first line of `startResize`, in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, before `e.preventDefault()`. A mousedown from any button other than the left one is now a complete no-op -- `resizingField` is never set, so the drag never starts.

**The tests**: added `"EntityPanel's column resize handle ignores a mousedown from a non-left mouse button, instead of resizing on a right- or middle-click-drag"` to `EntityPanel.test.ts`, firing a `mouseDown`/`mouseMove`/`mouseUp` sequence with `button: 2` (right) and separately `button: 1` (middle) on the resize handle and asserting the column's width and persisted storage are both completely untouched after each. Added the mirrored end-to-end test to `codegen.test.ts` using the file's real-generated-component render harness, driving the real generated `startResize` through the same two button values inside `act()`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed files (`EntityPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`) to scratchpad. Reverted `EntityPanel.tsx` alone: `EntityPanel.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test (`'260px' !== '200px'`, a right-click-drag resizing the column exactly like a left-click-drag) -- 136/137. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output). The re-run after restoring hit the known intermittent hang-on-process-exit artifact (rounds 649-657) -- all 137 tests reported `ok` with zero `not ok` lines, confirmed twice across two separate re-runs, before the process was killed each time; combined with the already-clean 137/137-with-exit-0 run taken before the revert, this is accepted as sufficient confirmation per the standing lesson that this hang is a source-state-independent environmental artifact, not a regression. Reverted `codegen.ts` alone (with `codegen.test.ts` left at its already-updated state): failed exactly the 1 predicted test (`'60px' !== ''`, the same right-click-drag mismatch against the real generated component) -- 218/219. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (219/219). Since this round touched both `apps/web` and `apps/api` files, ran both workspaces' full suites sequentially: `@forge/web` (931/931 clean) and `@forge/api` (573/573 clean), plus the full `npm run build` (clean, including `tsc -b` and both workspaces' builds). Commit `2bfea74`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This closes out the one remaining item from round 657's three leftover drag-and-drop leads (the other two -- stale drag-source state and missing `setData` on tab/header drags -- were confirmed non-issues in round 657 itself). This is a narrower, lower-severity instance of the standing "N parallel paths, only some protected" lens than recent rounds: here there was no sibling handler to compare against at all (this is the app's only `mousedown`-based drag), so the gap was simply a missing standard-practice guard rather than an inconsistency between two implementations -- the comparison was instead against the implicit browser-level guarantee every other (native HTML5) drag interaction already gets for free. A fresh round-658 survey found the codebase largely exhausted of strong leads after 15 consecutive successful rounds (643-657); a future round sweeping `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s ~52 routes for access-control asymmetries in one systematic pass (suggested by this round's own survey, only spot-checked so far) is a reasonable next target.

### Round 659: Manager's bare Hebrew "מנהל" role-rule keyword is a plain substring of Admin's own "מנהל מערכת" phrase, so a description naming only a system admin fabricated a spurious Manager role and silently suppressed the generic Member fallback

**Context**: this round needed three successive Explore surveys to find a genuine candidate -- the codebase is now extremely heavily audited after 16 consecutive successful rounds (643-658). Survey 1 (assigned round 658's own suggested direction) did a full systematic route-by-route sweep of all 52 routes in `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` for access-control asymmetries and confirmed, with DB-layer scoping verification beyond round 651's original spot-check, that the topic is genuinely closed -- a valuable negative result, but no bug. Survey 2 swept `backup.ts`, `seed.ts`, `zip.ts`, and a long list of smaller files and components, confirming all of them clean (several already-closed topics reconfirmed from a fresh angle, several previously-unaudited small files newly confirmed correct). Survey 3, assigned the specifically still-promising `heuristic.ts`/`checkpoints.ts`/`routes/auth.ts` territory, found this round's actual fix on its first file.

**The finding**: `ROLE_RULES` (`packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts:1376-1395`) defines `Admin: { keywords: [..., "מנהל מערכת", ...] }` and, two lines below it, `Manager: { keywords: ["manager", /\bmanagement\b/, "מנהל", "מנהלת", "ניהול"] }`. `matchesKeyword` (`heuristic.ts:98-100`) does a plain, unbounded substring check for a string keyword (`lower.includes(kw)`), with no word-boundary guard at all for Hebrew string keywords. Manager's bare `"מנהל"` is itself a substring of Admin's own `"מנהל מערכת"` ("system administrator") phrase sitting right above it in the same table -- so any Hebrew description naming only a system admin, with no manager concept at all, matches both rules. `matchRoles` (`heuristic.ts:133-148`) always force-adds Admin regardless of the description, and only adds the generic Member fallback when the matched-role set's size is exactly 1 (i.e., nothing besides Admin matched) -- so this spurious Manager match doesn't just add a harmless extra role, it actively *suppresses* Member and leaves the spec with a fabricated Manager role/persona/screens the description never asked for. Reproduced directly: `"האפליקציה מיועדת למנהל מערכת אחד בלבד, בלי תפקידים אחרים"` ("the app is meant for one system admin only, with no other roles") produced roles `["מנהל/ת ראשי/ת", "מנהל/ת"]` (Admin+Manager) instead of the correct `["מנהל/ת ראשי/ת", "חבר/ת צוות"]` (Admin+Member) -- confirmed the English side is unaffected, since none of "admin"/"administrator"/"owner" contain "manager". This is the same "bare keyword is a substring of a longer, unrelated phrase" shape this exact file has already fixed dozens of times for other keyword pairs (e.g. "lead"⊂"leadership", "booking"⊂"overbooking", "property"⊂"intellectual property", "חיוב"⊂"חיובי") -- just never previously caught for this specific Admin/Manager pair, since those earlier audits were scoped to `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` (entity matching), not `ROLE_RULES` (role matching).

**Independent verification**: read `domainEntities.ts:1376-1395` (`ROLE_RULES`) directly and confirmed Admin's `"מנהל מערכת"` keyword and Manager's bare `"מנהל"` keyword sit two lines apart in the same literal table. Read `heuristic.ts:98-100` (`matchesKeyword`) and `heuristic.ts:133-148` (`matchRoles`) directly and confirmed the plain-substring match for string keywords and the exactly-one-match condition that gates the Member fallback. Confirmed via grep that this file's own established disambiguation idiom for this exact bug class is a regex with a negative lookahead/lookbehind excluding the specific colliding phrase (e.g. `/חיוב(?!י(?!ם))/` at line 203, `/מוצר(?!ט)/` at line 333, `/רכב(?!ו?ת)/` at line 749), confirming the fix direction matches the file's own convention rather than inventing a new one. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no mirror of `ROLE_RULES`/`matchRoles`/`domainEntities.ts` at all -- this is a spec-*generation*-time heuristic (used before a project exists), not a feature the already-generated exported app needs to reimplement, so no codegen.ts parity fix was needed.

**The fix**: changed Manager's bare `"מנהל"` keyword to `/מנהל(?!\s*מערכת)/` -- a negative lookahead excluding Admin's own phrase, matching this file's established idiom exactly. `"מנהלת"` and `"ניהול"` (Manager's other two Hebrew keywords) are untouched and still cover the ordinary standalone-word cases.

**The tests**: added `"Manager's bare 'מנהל' keyword doesn't spuriously match inside Admin's own 'מנהל מערכת' phrase"` to `heuristic.test.ts`, right after the structurally identical pre-existing round-559 "management"/"mismanagement" test. Runs the real `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate` end to end on the system-admin-only description above and asserts Manager (`"מנהל/ת"`) is absent and Member (`"חבר/ת צוות"`) is present instead, then confirms a genuine standalone `"מנהל חנות"` ("store manager") description still correctly adds the Manager role.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `domainEntities.ts` to scratchpad. Reverted it alone via `git checkout --`: `heuristic.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test, with the exact predicted mismatch (`expected: true, actual: false` on the Manager-absence assertion) -- 78/79. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (79/79). Since only `packages/spec-engine` files changed this round, ran that workspace's full suite (149/149 clean) plus the full `npm run build` (clean, including every workspace's build). Commit `171b323`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This is a fresh instance of a bug class this file has fixed many times before (bare-substring-of-a-longer-phrase), but on a table (`ROLE_RULES`) that hadn't been audited for this specific shape before -- all of this file's many prior substring-collision fixes were scoped to `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`. It took three Explore surveys this round to land on a genuine, previously-unfound bug, confirming the codebase is now very thoroughly mined; the third survey's own sweep of `heuristic.ts`, `checkpoints.ts`, and `routes/auth.ts` otherwise came back entirely clean (including a `getCheckpoint`'s non-tolerant-throw pattern that looks superficially like a candidate but is the same deliberately-accepted tradeoff already documented for `getProject`/`rowToProject`). A future round should expect to need a similarly broad, possibly multi-survey search before finding its next genuine candidate.

### Round 660: MenuItem's own plural Hebrew keyword "מנות", chosen specifically to dodge an earlier collision with "מנהל" (manager), is itself a bare substring of this same file's Order rule's "הזמנות" ("orders") keyword

**Context**: following round 659's own lesson directly ("a bug-fix class applied repeatedly to one table/area doesn't imply a structurally-parallel table/area got the same systematic audit"), this round's Explore survey first swept every other keyword-matching table in `heuristic.ts`/`domainEntities.ts` besides `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`/`ROLE_RULES` (confirming `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` already has its own three documented fixes and no other keyword table exists anywhere in the codebase), then found this round's actual bug via a different but closely related angle: a cross-entity collision *within* `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` itself that nobody had cross-checked when the keyword was originally chosen specifically to dodge a *different* collision.

**The finding**: MenuItem's rule (`packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`, keyword list around line 423-432) includes the plural `"מנות"` ("dishes/portions") in place of the singular `"מנה"`, with a doc comment (lines 409-416) explaining this was a deliberate choice to avoid "מנה" being a 3-letter prefix of "מנהל"/"מנהלת"/"מנהלים" (manager/manageress/managers) -- one of this file's own `ROLE_RULES` keywords for Admin, and an extremely common word in Hebrew business descriptions. That reasoning is correct as far as it goes, but it never cross-checked the *replacement* keyword against the rest of this same file's own keyword list: `"מנות"` (מ-נ-ו-ת) is itself a bare, contiguous substring of the Order rule's own Hebrew keyword `"הזמנות"` ("orders", ה-ז-מ-נ-ו-ת) a few entries earlier in the same file (line 259). So any Hebrew description naming only orders -- with zero restaurant/menu concept -- spuriously matches MenuItem too, fabricating a restaurant-menu entity (with `price`, a `category` enum of `Starter/Main/Dessert/Drink`, and `available`) plus its List/Form screens for, e.g., a clothing store's order tracker. Reproduced directly: `"אפליקציה לניהול הזמנות של חנות בגדים אונליין"` ("an app to manage orders for an online clothing store") returned entities `['Order', 'MenuItem']` instead of just `['Order']`.

**Independent verification**: read `domainEntities.ts`'s Order rule keyword list directly and confirmed `"הזמנות"` at line 259. Read the MenuItem rule's keyword list and its own doc comment directly and confirmed `"מנות"` at the position described, with the comment's reasoning scoped only to the "מנה"/"מנהל" collision, never mentioning Order's keyword at all. Confirmed programmatically that `"הזמנות".includes("מנות")` is `true` -- a direct substring check, not inference. Reproduced the spurious match live against the real `matchEntities`/`HeuristicSpecProvider.generate` pipeline with the clothing-store description above. Confirmed via grep that `matchesKeyword` (`heuristic.ts:98-100`) still does the same plain, unbounded `.includes()` for string keywords this entire bug class has always exploited. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no mirror of this spec-generation-time file at all (same as round 659), so no codegen.ts parity fix was needed.

**The fix**: changed `"מנות"` to `/(?<!ז)מנות/` -- a negative lookbehind excluding the specific preceding letter that makes it part of `"הזמנות"` (and its own prefixed variants like `"ההזמנות"`/`"שהזמנות"`), the same disambiguation idiom this file already uses for its many other substring-collision fixes (e.g. `/מנוי(?!ות)/`, `/מוצר(?!ט)/`). A standalone `"מנות"` (e.g. `"תפריט מנות"`) still matches normally, since the character immediately before it in that context is never `ז`.

**The tests**: added `"MenuItem's 'מנות' keyword doesn't spuriously match inside Order's own 'הזמנות' keyword"` to `heuristic.test.ts`, right after the pre-existing round-448-era "מנה"/"מנהלים" test. Runs the real `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate` end to end on the pure order-management description above, asserting MenuItem is absent and Order is still present, then confirms a genuine standalone "מנות" description (a small eatery, avoiding every other MenuItem keyword) still correctly matches MenuItem.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `domainEntities.ts` to scratchpad. Reverted it alone via `git checkout --`: `heuristic.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test, with the exact predicted mismatch (`expected: true, actual: false` on the MenuItem-absence assertion) -- 79/80. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (80/80). Since only `packages/spec-engine` files changed this round, ran that workspace's full suite (150/150 clean) plus the full `npm run build` (clean, including every workspace's build). Commit `0f23f32`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This round's own survey confirmed round 659's assigned angle (other keyword-matching tables) is now exhausted -- no other such table exists in the codebase -- but found a *different*, closely-related instance of the same underlying lesson one level down: a keyword chosen specifically to dodge one named collision was never cross-checked against the *rest* of the same table's own keywords. The pattern generalizes: whenever a doc comment explains "keyword X was chosen instead of Y to avoid colliding with Z," that reasoning covers only the one collision it names -- it is not evidence the replacement was checked against every other keyword in the same file. This is the tenth consecutive round (643, 644, ..., 659, 660) under some variant of the standing "a fix/check applied narrowly doesn't imply broader coverage" lens, continuing an unbroken streak of 18 successful rounds since 643.

### Round 661: `LanguageContext.tsx`'s own comment claims it mirrors `ThemeContext.tsx`'s fix for the identical bug, but only half the fix was actually ported -- language never followed a live browser/OS language change, unlike theme, which already does

**Context**: this round's Explore survey was steered toward sibling-implementation and doc-comment-accuracy angles, since round 660's own lesson ("a doc comment's stated reasoning covers only what it explicitly names") generalizes beyond keyword tables. It found a case of that exact shape one level up: a doc comment in `LanguageContext.tsx` that explicitly claims full parity with a named sibling fix, where the claim is true for one half of that fix and silently false for the other.

**The finding**: `ThemeContext.tsx` has two independent halves to its round-290 `hasExplicitChoiceRef` fix: (1) gate persistence -- only write to `localStorage` once a real explicit choice has been made (`toggleTheme`'s `hasExplicitChoiceRef.current = true`) or was already stored at mount, never for an auto-detected value; and (2) gate-and-follow -- a live `window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")` `"change"` listener that calls `setTheme` whenever the OS theme changes, but only while `hasExplicitChoiceRef.current` is still false. `LanguageContext.tsx`'s own doc comment (pre-fix, lines ~24-31) reads "Mirrors ThemeContext.tsx's own hasExplicitChoiceRef fix for the identical bug" and its code did carry half (1) correctly -- the persistence `useEffect` only calls `localStorage.setItem` when `hasExplicitChoiceRef.current` is true. But half (2) was never ported at all: there was no `window.addEventListener("languagechange", ...)` anywhere in the file, so a person relying on the auto-detected `navigator.language` (no explicit choice made) who then changed their OS/browser language mid-session saw no change at all until a full page reload -- unlike dark/light mode, which already follows a live system change instantly. The comment's claim of full parity was true for the bug it names (persistence) but silently omitted an entire second half of the sibling fix that the comment itself doesn't distinguish.

**Independent verification**: read `ThemeContext.tsx` in full directly and confirmed its two-part fix: the gated persistence effect and the separate `matchMedia`/`"change"`-listener effect, both guarded by the same `hasExplicitChoiceRef`. Read `LanguageContext.tsx` in full directly (pre-fix) and confirmed its persistence effect correctly mirrors half (1), and confirmed via direct inspection and a grep for `addEventListener`/`languagechange`/`matchMedia` in the file that no live-follow listener of any kind existed. Read `language.ts`'s `detectInitialLang(storedValue, browserLanguage?)` directly and confirmed its signature already supports being called with `null` for `storedValue` to force a fresh browser-locale detection, exactly what a live-follow handler needs. Confirmed via grep across `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` that it has zero hits for `setLang`/`LanguageContext`/`useTranslation`/`navigator.language` -- the exported app has no language-switching feature at all, unlike the theme-follow-OS feature codegen.ts already carries from round 631 -- so no codegen.ts parity fix was needed for this round's fix, correctly applying the standing "check codegen.ts actually has the feature first" lesson.

**The fix**: added a second `useEffect` to `LanguageContext.tsx`'s `LanguageProvider`, placed right after the existing persistence effect, registering a `window.addEventListener("languagechange", handleSystemChange)` whose handler checks `hasExplicitChoiceRef.current` (so an already-made explicit choice, including one made after the listener was attached, is never overridden) and otherwise calls `setLangState(detectInitialLang(null, navigator.language))` to pick up the live change. Cleans up via `removeEventListener` on unmount, mirroring `ThemeContext.tsx`'s own `matchMedia` effect structure exactly (jsdom's `window` is a real `EventTarget`, so unlike `matchMedia` -- which jsdom doesn't implement at all -- no fake-event-dispatching stand-in was needed for the test).

**The tests**: added two tests to `LanguageContext.test.ts`. `"LanguageProvider follows a live browser language change when the user has never made an explicit choice"` renders with no stored choice (starts "en" from an "en-US" browser locale), changes `navigator.language` to "he-IL" and fires a real `window` `"languagechange"` event via `fireEvent`, asserting the rendered language switches to "he", then switches the browser locale back to "en-US" and fires the event again, asserting it follows back to "en". `"LanguageProvider ignores a live browser language change once an explicit choice is already stored"` pre-seeds `localStorage` with an explicit "en" choice, fires the same live "he-IL" `languagechange` event, and asserts the language stays "en" -- confirming the fix's gate, not just its follow behavior.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `LanguageContext.tsx` to scratchpad. Reverted it alone via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests): `LanguageContext.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test, with the exact predicted mismatch (`expected: 'he', actual: 'en'` on the live-follow assertion) -- 4/5; the companion "ignores" test correctly but trivially still passed in the reverted state, since with no listener at all nothing changes regardless. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (5/5). Since only one `apps/web` file changed (no `apps/api` touch, confirmed no codegen.ts parity needed above), ran the full `@forge/web` suite. Two files (`EntityPanel.test.ts`, `WhatsAppPanel.test.ts`) hit the known intermittent hang-on-exit artifact (rounds 649-661) in a more aggressive form than before -- both hung even in true single-file isolation, not just inside a full-glob run. Worked around it: ran the other 59 files via an explicit file list (758/758 clean, exit 0), then ran each hang-prone file individually and confirmed via log content alone that `EntityPanel.test.ts` reports all 137 tests `ok` with zero `not ok` lines (killed on the background time limit right after its own final test, before it could print a summary) and `WhatsAppPanel.test.ts` reports all 38 tests (its file's own exact `test(` count) `ok` with zero `not ok` lines (killed by the same background time limit immediately after its 38th and last test). Total: 758 + 137 + 38 = 933/933 clean, matching the expected 931 (round 658's baseline) + 2 new tests. Full `npm run build` across every workspace: clean. Commit `df169e9`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This is the eleventh consecutive round (643-661) under some variant of the standing "a fix/guard/check applied to one of several parallel paths doesn't imply the others inherited it" lens, and the second in a row (after 660) to find the gap one level above the keyword-table family: a doc comment explicitly claiming a sibling fix was fully mirrored, when only one of that fix's two independent halves actually was. The lesson generalizes further than round 660's: a fix can have multiple independent parts (here, persistence-gating vs. live-follow), and a comment can be completely accurate about the part it names while staying silent about a part it doesn't -- so "the comment says it mirrors X" is not itself verification; only reading the actual sibling implementation in full, side by side, confirms whether every part made the trip. The intermittent hang-on-exit artifact also escalated this round (now defeating single-file isolation, not just full-glob runs) without blocking progress, via the established log-content-inspection tolerance.

### Round 662: the entity-tab bar's reorder was drag-and-drop only -- no keyboard fallback existed at all, unlike its own documented sibling (table-column reorder), which already had one since round 478

**Context**: round 645's own closing note had explicitly flagged "other mouse/drag-only controls across the app (column reorder and resize are now both fixed; any others never audited)" as open future work, but no round from 646 through 661 ever picked that lead up. This round's Explore survey revisited it directly, alongside a broader sweep of other `createContext` pairs (none besides Theme/Language exist), other `window.addEventListener` usages (all already audited), and other `apps/api/src/routes/*.ts` files (only `projects.ts`/`auth.ts` exist, both closed) -- all coming back clean -- before landing on the one genuinely unaudited mouse/drag-only control round 645 had named but never checked: the entity-tab bar itself.

**The finding**: `App.tsx`'s entity-tab bar (the `<nav className="entity-tabs">` block, pre-fix lines ~1997-2028) let a user reorder project entity tabs only via native HTML5 drag-and-drop -- `draggable`, `onDragStart`, `onDragOver`, `onDrop={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); handleReorderEntityTab(entity.name); }}` on each tab `<button>`. There was no `onKeyDown`, no move-earlier/move-later buttons, no ARIA drag affordance of any kind -- confirmed via a full grep of the file. Its own doc comment (`App.tsx:564-574`, pre-fix) explicitly claims `handleReorderEntityTab` "mirrors EntityPanel.tsx's own handleReorderColumn exactly, down to reusing the same reorderColumns helper" -- true for the underlying reorder *algorithm* (both literally call `reorderColumns` from `columnOrder.ts`), but silently false for the keyboard-accessible *entry point* into that algorithm: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own `handleMoveColumn` (added round 478) is reachable from two real `<button>`s with `aria-label`s and disabled boundaries (`EntityPanel.tsx:3053-3072`); `handleReorderEntityTab` was reachable only from `onDrop`, which a keyboard-only or screen-reader user can never fire. A keyboard-only user could Tab to each tab `<button>` and press Enter/Space to *switch* tabs, but had no way whatsoever to change their *order*, even though a mouse user could freely drag any tab anywhere. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `App.jsx` (its own entity-tabs `<nav>`, pre-fix lines ~5706-5728) mirrors the identical drag-only gap byte-for-byte, alongside its own already-fixed `handleMoveColumn`/`column-move-btn` keyboard fallback for table columns (round 478's own codegen.ts parity) -- confirming the gap in both the live preview and the exported standalone app.

**Independent verification**: read `App.tsx` lines 1985-2029 in full directly and confirmed the tab `<button>` has only `draggable`/`onDragStart`/`onDragOver`/`onDragLeave`/`onDrop`/`onClick` -- no `onKeyDown`, no move buttons. Read `App.tsx:564-581` (`handleReorderEntityTab`) directly, confirming its doc comment's explicit "mirrors... exactly" claim and its reuse of `reorderColumns`. Read `EntityPanel.tsx:3053-3072` directly, confirming the real keyboard-operable move-earlier/move-later `<button>`s with `aria-label`/`disabled` boundaries, and `EntityPanel.tsx:1512-1522` (`handleMoveColumn`) confirming it calls the same `reorderColumns` helper from `columnOrder.ts`. Grepped `App.tsx`/`styles.css` for any tab-reorder keyboard/ARIA affordance -- zero hits. Grepped `App.test.ts` and confirmed its only pre-existing entity-tab-reorder test drove `handleReorderEntityTab` directly via a `new Function` extraction simulating a drop, never a keyboard interaction, so no existing test caught this gap. Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `App.jsx` entity-tabs block and its own `handleMoveColumn`/`column-move-btn` table-column fix directly, confirming the identical drag-only gap for entity tabs sitting right alongside the already-fixed column keyboard fallback in the same generated file.

**The fix**: added `handleMoveEntityTab(entityName, direction)` to `App.tsx`, mirroring `handleMoveColumn`'s own swap-with-neighbor logic via the identical `reorderColumns` primitive. Restructured the entity-tabs `<nav>` so each tab is wrapped in a `<span className="tab-wrapper">` (since a `<button>` can't nest inside another `<button>`), with a new `<span className="tab-move-buttons">` holding two `<button>`s ("‹"/"›") calling `handleMoveEntityTab(entity.name, "earlier"|"later")`, each `aria-label`ed via two new i18n keys (`entity.tab.moveEarlier`/`moveLater`, he+en) and `disabled` at the ends of the order, mirroring `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own `column-move-buttons`/`column-move-btn` CSS and structure. Ported the identical fix to `codegen.ts`'s generated `App.jsx` (no i18n there -- hardcoded English `aria-label`s, matching that file's own convention for `column-move-btn`).

**The tests**: added `"App's handleMoveEntityTab moves an entity tab earlier/later and persists via entityTabOrder.ts, but is a no-op at the ends of the order or with no project open"` to `App.test.ts`, using the same `new Function`-extraction convention as the pre-existing `handleReorderEntityTab` test, passing in the real `reorderColumns`. Added the mirrored `"the exported App's entity tabs have keyboard-operable 'move earlier'/'move later' buttons..."` test to `codegen.test.ts`, asserting the generated `handleMoveEntityTab`/`tab-wrapper`/`tab-move-buttons` text via regex against the real generated `App.jsx`, then extracting and executing the real generated handler via `new Function` against plain data. Updated the pre-existing drag-and-drop entity-tabs test's own literal-signature regex assertion (`{orderedEntities.map((e) => (` → `{orderedEntities.map((e, entityTabIndex) => (`) to match the new per-tab index parameter the fix's `disabled` boundaries need.

**Regression-proof**: backed up all four fixed files (`App.tsx`, `styles.css`, `language.ts`, `codegen.ts`) to scratchpad. Reverted the three `apps/web` files alone via `git checkout --` (keeping test changes): `App.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test (`"expected to find handleMoveEntityTab in App.tsx"`) -- 72/73. Reverted `codegen.ts` alone (with `codegen.test.ts` left at its already-updated state): failed exactly the 2 predicted tests -- the pre-existing drag-and-drop test's updated signature-regex (correctly failing against the reverted two-parameter `(e) =>` source) and the new keyboard-fallback test's function-body regex -- 218/220. Restored all four from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output on any of the four). Re-ran both single-file suites clean (`App.test.ts` 73/73, `codegen.test.ts` 220/220). Since this round touched both `apps/web` and `apps/api` files, ran both workspaces' full suites sequentially: `@forge/web` (934/934 clean, no hang this round) and `@forge/api` (574/574 clean), plus the full `npm run build` across every workspace (clean). This closes out round 645's own three-round-old open lead ("other mouse/drag-only controls, never audited") with the one instance that was actually still open -- column reorder and resize were both already fixed, and this round's own survey confirmed no other drag-only control exists anywhere in the app besides the entity-tab bar itself. ### Round 663: Global Search's "Show all" button silently swallowed a failed fetch -- no catch clause at all, unlike its own sibling fetch (runSearch) in the exact same component

**Context**: round 662's own survey, having exhausted keyword tables, context pairs, event listeners, and drag-only controls as search angles, suggested fresh unexplored territory for round 663: ARIA/accessibility attribute coverage, focus management after actions, loading/error/empty-state symmetry, confirm-dialog coverage for destructive actions, debounce consistency, and any `apps/api/src`/`apps/web/src` files not yet named in any roadmap entry. This round's Explore survey worked through all of these systematically (see below -- most came back clean) and landed on a genuine async-error-handling asymmetry within `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` itself: one of its two sibling `listRecords` fetches surfaces a failure to the user, the other one doesn't.

**The finding**: `handleShowAll` (pre-fix, `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:210-238`) -- the handler behind the "Show all N more" button, which re-fetches an entity's full record set with no sample cap -- wraps its `await listRecords(projectId, entityName)` call in a bare `try { ... } finally { ... }` with no `catch` clause anywhere. If that fetch rejects (a timeout, a cold-starting Render backend, a 404 from an entity a collaborator removed since the original search ran), the exception propagates past the `try` as an unhandled promise rejection: the `finally` block still correctly clears `showAllLoading` (so the button visually reverts from "Loading…" back to "Show N more"), but `setError` is never called anywhere on this path -- there is no visible indication whatsoever that the fetch failed, indistinguishable on screen from the click having done nothing at all. Its own sibling, `runSearch` (`GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:113-165`), makes the exact same kind of `listRecords` call for every entity via `Promise.allSettled`, and explicitly calls `setError(...)` (lines 156-163) whenever any entity's fetch fails -- rendering this component's own `error-retry-row`/`<p className="error" role="status">` banner (lines 377-385), the same banner `handleShowAll`'s own failures never reach. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `GlobalSearch.jsx` mirrors the identical gap byte-for-byte: its own `handleShowAll` (lines 5046-5064) has the same bare `try/finally`, while its own `runSearch` (lines 4992-5016) already calls `setError(...)` on failure via `searchAllEntities`'s own `failures` array.

**Independent verification**: read `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:210-238` (`handleShowAll`) directly and confirmed the `try { ... } finally { ... }` has no `catch` anywhere in it. Read `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:113-165` (`runSearch`) directly and confirmed its `Promise.allSettled` + `setError(...)` failure-surfacing convention, and `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:377-393` directly, confirming the real `error-retry-row` banner `runSearch`'s own failures reach. Confirmed `listRecords` (`api.ts:659`, built on `fetchApi`) genuinely can and does reject -- on a timed-out request, a network failure, or any non-2xx response -- and that `wakeRetry.ts`'s own extensive cold-start-retry documentation confirms exactly this kind of transient backend failure is a real, expected occurrence for this app's Render free-tier hosting, not a hypothetical edge case. Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `handleShowAll` (lines 5046-5064) and `runSearch` (lines 4992-5016) directly and confirmed the identical asymmetry in the exported app. Grepped both `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts` for `handleShowAll` and confirmed neither file's existing tests ever make the fetch reject -- only the stale-request-guard and the fewer-real-matches-than-expected scenarios are covered -- so this gap had never been exercised by a test. The same round's survey separately swept debounce usage (none exists anywhere, not an inconsistency), every destructive action's confirm-dialog coverage (uniformly present), the loading/error/empty-state triad across six other data-fetching panels (all fully symmetric), the clipboard-copy family (7 call sites, byte-for-byte consistent), the count-formatter family, and the Blob/download family (8 call sites, byte-for-byte consistent) -- all coming back clean, narrowing the search down to this one genuine asymmetry.

**The fix**: added `catch (err) { setError((err as Error).message); }` to `handleShowAll`, between the existing `try` body and `finally` block, mirroring `runSearch`'s own error-surfacing convention one function above it in the same file. Applied the identical fix to `codegen.ts`'s generated `handleShowAll` (`setError(err.message)`, no TypeScript cast needed in the generated plain-JS output).

**The tests**: added `"GlobalSearchPanel's handleShowAll surfaces a failed fetch via setError, instead of silently swallowing it"` to `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts`, using the same `new Function`-extraction convention as this file's existing `handleShowAll`/`runSearch` tests -- passes a `listRecords` mock that throws, and asserts `setError` is called with the rejection's own message while `setShowAllLoading` is still called exactly twice (add then clear) despite the failure. Added the mirrored `"the exported GlobalSearch's handleShowAll surfaces a failed fetch via setError..."` test to `codegen.test.ts`, extracting and executing the real generated `handleShowAll` the same way.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed files (`GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`) to scratchpad. Reverted `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` alone: `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test, with the rejection surfacing as an unhandled exception instead of being captured by `setError` -- 20/21. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (21/21). Reverted `codegen.ts` alone (with `codegen.test.ts` left at its already-updated state): failed exactly the 1 predicted test -- 220/221. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (221/221). Since this round touched both `apps/web` and `apps/api` files, ran both workspaces' full suites sequentially: `@forge/web` (935/935 clean, no hang) and `@forge/api` (575/575 clean), plus the full `npm run build` across every workspace (clean). Commit `fc62dda`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This is the thirteenth consecutive round (643-663) under some variant of the standing "a fix/guard/pattern applied to one of several structurally-parallel paths doesn't imply the others inherited it" lens -- the narrowest-scope instance yet, since both siblings (`runSearch`, `handleShowAll`) live in the same function-adjacent block of the same single file, making the same kind of network call, yet only one of them was ever taught to surface a failure. This round's own survey exhausted several broad accessibility/consistency angles (ARIA coverage, focus management, confirm-dialog coverage, debounce, loading/error/empty-state symmetry) without finding further gaps, suggesting those particular angles are now closed; a future round may need to look at narrower within-file async-handling asymmetries like this one, rather than cross-component/cross-table patterns, to keep finding genuine bugs.

### Round 664: the keyboard-shortcuts cheat sheet never mentioned that Backspace deletes a row -- only "Delete" was ever listed, even though the real handler has treated them as equivalent since round 349, and this list's own sibling rows document every one of their working keys

**Context**: round 663's own survey, having exhausted several broad async-error-handling and accessibility-consistency angles, pointed toward auditing every async fetch in the app for sibling error-handling asymmetry as the next promising direction. This round's Explore survey did that systematically (every async handler across `EntityPanel.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`, `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx`, `AutomationsPanel.tsx`, `CollaboratorsPanel.tsx`, `HistoryPanel.tsx`, `BuildProgress.tsx`, `AuthScreen.tsx`, `ChangePasswordPanel.tsx`, `DeleteAccountPanel.tsx`, and codegen.ts's own generated copies) and came back clean -- that angle is now genuinely exhausted. It then found this round's actual bug via a documentation-completeness angle instead: a static cheat-sheet list whose own sibling rows establish a "document every working key" convention that one specific row has silently violated since the day it was created.

**The finding**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own table keydown handler (`EntityPanel.tsx:1719`) reads `} else if ((e.key === "Delete" || e.key === "Backspace") && isFocusedRowVisible) { ... void handleDelete(...); }` -- both keys genuinely delete the keyboard-focused row, with the real confirm dialog and undo toast. But `ShortcutsPanel.tsx`'s own static `SHORTCUTS` array (the "?"-triggered cheat sheet whose own doc comment states its purpose is to be "the simplest overlay panel," the one place a person can ever see the full shortcut list) lists that row as `{ keys: ["Delete"], descriptionKey: "shortcuts.rowDelete" }` -- "Backspace" appears nowhere in the array, nor in either language's translation text (`he`: "מחיקת הרשומה המסומנת בטבלה"; `en`: "Delete the focused table row" -- neither sentence names Backspace either). This list's own sibling rows for j/k row-navigation already establish the opposite convention: `{ keys: ["j", "↓"], ... }` and `{ keys: ["k", "↑"], ... }` both explicitly list every key that performs the action, not just one of two. A person reading the cheat sheet has no way to learn Backspace does the same thing as Delete, and might reasonably infer the opposite, since every other dual-key row here is documented with both keys. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `App.jsx` mirrors the identical gap byte-for-byte: its own keydown handler (`codegen.ts:3514`) treats the two keys as equivalent exactly like the live app, while its own generated `SHORTCUTS` array (`codegen.ts:5280`) lists only `["Delete"]`, alongside its own correctly-dual-keyed j/k rows (lines 5275-5276).

**Independent verification**: read `EntityPanel.tsx:1719` directly and confirmed the real `e.key === "Delete" || e.key === "Backspace"` dual-key check. Read `ShortcutsPanel.tsx` in full directly and confirmed the j/k rows list two keys each while the Delete row lists only one, and confirmed via grep that neither language's translation string for `shortcuts.rowDelete` names Backspace. Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own generated keydown handler (line 3514) and generated `SHORTCUTS` array (lines 5270-5284) directly and confirmed the identical asymmetry in the exported app. Read `docs/roadmap.md`'s own round-349 entry (the round that introduced the Delete/Backspace binding) and confirmed its own documentation update added only a singular "Delete" row to the list, never Backspace, even though that same round's code change bound both keys -- the gap is original to the row's creation, not a later regression, and has survived 300+ subsequent rounds undetected. Grepped `ShortcutsPanel.test.ts`/`codegen.test.ts` for "Backspace" and confirmed the only existing hits test the real key-binding handler itself, never the cheat-sheet's own documentation of it, so this gap had never been exercised by a test either. Confirmed this is distinct from two previously-closed topics that touch the same panel: the round-365 dialog-stacking fix (a different mechanism -- background shortcuts firing under an open dialog) and the round-629/650 "ShortcutsPanel missing from codegen.ts" gap (about the panel's *existence* in the exported app, whose fix faithfully copied the live app's own already-incomplete row, carrying this exact gap into codegen.ts rather than introducing a new one).

**The fix**: changed `{ keys: ["Delete"], descriptionKey: "shortcuts.rowDelete" }` to `{ keys: ["Delete", "Backspace"], descriptionKey: "shortcuts.rowDelete" }` in `ShortcutsPanel.tsx`, and the identical change to the generated `SHORTCUTS` array in `codegen.ts`. No translation-string change needed -- both languages' existing description text ("delete the focused row") already covers either key equally well, exactly like the j/k rows' own single shared description per pair.

**The tests**: added an assertion to `ShortcutsPanel.test.ts`'s existing "renders a real dialog listing every actual shortcut" test, confirming `kbds.includes("Backspace")` alongside the pre-existing `kbds.includes("Delete")` check. Added the mirrored assertion to `codegen.test.ts`'s existing "the exported ShortcutsPanel renders every one of the live preview's own 13 keyboard-shortcut rows" test, confirming a real `<kbd>Backspace</kbd>` renders in the generated component. Both are new assertions inside already-existing tests, not new test functions, since the row count (13) and overall panel structure are unchanged -- only one row's own key list grew by one entry.
