### Round 665: the exported standalone app's Search button hint badge only ever advertised "Ctrl+K" -- never "/", even though its own generated keydown handler has genuinely opened search via "/" since round 629

**Context**: round 664's survey suggested, as fresh unexplored territory, checking other static UI-text surfaces besides `ShortcutsPanel.tsx`'s cheat-sheet for the same "documentation doesn't match real behavior" shape -- tooltips, inline hint badges, placeholder text. This round's Explore survey took that angle and, after confirming no further dual-key-binding gaps exist anywhere in the live app itself (the j/k, Delete/Backspace families are now fully and correctly documented), found a second instance of the same shape on a different text surface entirely: an inline topbar badge in the *exported* app, rather than the live preview's own cheat-sheet.

**The finding**: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `App.jsx` renders its Search button as `🔍 Search <span className="shortcut-hint">Ctrl+K</span>` (line 5722) -- but the very same generated file's own `handleKeyDown` (lines 5645-5663) opens search on *both* `(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === "k"` *and*, in a separate branch just below it, `e.key === "/" && !isEditableEventTarget(e.target)`. The "/" branch is real and unconditional beyond the same `isAnyDialogOpen()` guard the Ctrl+K branch uses -- not a leftover or disabled code path. The live Forge AI preview's own identical badge, `App.tsx:1892`, already reads `Ctrl+K · /` -- and round 199's own commit message (cited in this file) explicitly established that this exact badge must be kept in sync with which keys actually work, "so the new shortcut is actually discoverable, not just functional." Round 629 ported the "/" shortcut's *functionality* into `codegen.ts`'s `handleKeyDown` but never touched this badge's text, so anyone running the exported standalone app -- with no way back to the live Forge AI app or its own docs -- saw a topbar hint that silently undersold what the app could already do. Notably, `codegen.ts`'s own generated `ShortcutsPanel.jsx` cheat-sheet (the fix round 664 touched) already correctly lists both `["Ctrl", "K"]` and `["/"]` as separate rows -- this is not a reopening of round 664's fix, but a second, narrower stale-text instance on the one surface that fix didn't cover.

**Independent verification**: read `codegen.ts:5721-5722` directly and confirmed the Search button's badge literally reads `"Ctrl+K"` with no mention of `/`. Read `codegen.ts:5645-5663` (the generated `handleKeyDown`) directly and confirmed both the Ctrl/Cmd+K branch and the separate, unconditional `/` branch genuinely call `setShowSearch(true)`. Read `apps/web/src/App.tsx:1890-1893` directly and confirmed the live preview's own sibling badge already reads `"Ctrl+K · /"`. Grepped `codegen.test.ts` for `shortcut-hint` and confirmed the only existing assertion (`assert.match(appJsx, /shortcut-hint/)`) matches regardless of the span's actual text content, so this gap was never caught by a test. Grepped the whole live app for every dual-key `e.key === X || e.key === Y` binding and confirmed only j/↓, k/↑, and Delete/Backspace exist, and all three are already fully documented in `ShortcutsPanel.tsx` (round 664 closed Delete/Backspace) -- no further undocumented dual-key gap exists in the live app itself, so this round's candidate is specifically the cross-boundary (live-app-correct, exported-app-stale) badge rather than a live-app gap.

**The fix**: changed `codegen.ts`'s generated badge from `<span className="shortcut-hint">Ctrl+K</span>` to `<span className="shortcut-hint">Ctrl+K · /</span>`, matching the live preview's own badge text exactly. No change needed to `apps/web/src/App.tsx` -- its own badge was already correct.

**The tests**: replaced `codegen.test.ts`'s existing bare `assert.match(appJsx, /shortcut-hint/)` (inside the pre-existing "the exported app includes a real cross-entity global search" test) with an exact-text assertion, `assert.match(appJsx, /<span className="shortcut-hint">Ctrl\+K · \/<\/span>/)`, so the test now actually pins the badge's content rather than merely confirming the span exists.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `codegen.ts` to scratchpad. Reverted it alone via `git checkout --` (keeping the updated test assertion): `codegen.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test, with the exact predicted mismatch (the new exact-text regex failing against the old `"Ctrl+K"`-only badge) -- 220/221. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran clean (221/221). Since this round touched only `apps/api` files, ran that workspace's full suite (575/575 clean, unchanged count since this round replaced an assertion inside an existing test rather than adding a new one) plus the full `npm run build` across every workspace (clean). Commit `4621cae`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This is the fifteenth consecutive round (643-665) under some variant of the standing "a fix/convention/doc-text applied to one of several structurally-parallel surfaces doesn't imply the others inherited it" lens -- round 664's variant (a static cheat-sheet list) recurs here on a different text surface (an inline hint badge) and across a different boundary (live app vs. its exported-app mirror) rather than within one file. The pattern generalizes further: any place the UI tells a person which keys do something is a candidate for this check, not just a dedicated help panel. This round's own survey confirmed the live app itself has no further undocumented dual-key gaps, so a future round checking this angle again would need to look at other hint/tooltip/badge text, not keybindings specifically.

### Round 666: AutomationsPanel.tsx's "send to a field" dropdown offered every field on the entity as a WhatsApp phone destination, including types the server unconditionally rejects

**Context**: round 665's closing survey confirmed the live app has no further undocumented dual-key-binding gaps, redirecting this round's search away from keybindings and toward other validation/UI-copy mismatches. This round's Explore survey found a candidate in a different family entirely: a form control whose own label makes a type promise ("Choose a phone field") that its options list doesn't honor.

**The finding**: `apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.tsx:277-284` (before this fix) rendered the `toField` `<select>` by mapping over `selectedEntity.fields` unfiltered by type -- boolean, number, date, enum, and relation fields all appeared as selectable "phone field" destinations, not just text fields. The `<select>`'s own `aria-label` is `t("automations.toField.placeholder")`, which reads "Choose a phone field" (en) / "בחרו שדה טלפון" (he) -- directly contradicted by listing non-text fields as valid choices. The auto-default effect (`AutomationsPanel.tsx:63-72`), which keeps `toField` pointed at a real field whenever the chosen entity changes (including on first render), picked `selectedEntity.fields[0]?.name` with zero type awareness -- for any entity whose first field isn't text/longtext, the form opened already pointed at an invalid destination. The server's own `validateAutomationToField` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:449-456`) has always rejected any `toField` that isn't `"text"` or `"longtext"`, called from both the create route (`projects.ts:2121-2123`) and the update route (`projects.ts:2191-2193`) -- so a non-text pick, or an untouched bad default, was guaranteed a predictable 400 that the UI never needed to risk. A clean in-file contrast exists: the sibling `fieldName` select for the `field_equals` trigger condition (`AutomationsPanel.tsx:251-257`) is correctly left unfiltered, because its own server-side counterpart `validateAutomationFieldValue` (`projects.ts:406-431`) genuinely accepts every field type with type-specific value parsing -- only `toField` carries a hard type restriction, and only `toField`'s UI failed to mirror it.

**Independent verification**: read `AutomationsPanel.tsx:277-284` and `:63-72` directly and confirmed the unfiltered `.fields.map`/`.fields[0]` logic. Read `projects.ts:449-456` and both call sites (`:2121-2123`, `:2191-2193`) directly and confirmed the server's strict text/longtext-only gate applies on both create and update. Read the sibling `fieldName` select (`AutomationsPanel.tsx:251-257`) and `validateAutomationFieldValue` (`projects.ts:406-431`) directly and confirmed that select is correctly left unfiltered by design, so the contrast is real, not an oversight on the sibling's side. Grepped `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` for "Automation"/"automation" and found a single unrelated comment match -- codegen.ts does not export this feature at all, so no parity port was needed, following the standing "check first whether codegen.ts even has the feature" discipline. Checked `AutomationsPanel.test.ts`'s fixture entity and confirmed every one of its fields is typed `"text"`, explaining why no existing test ever exercised the unfiltered-list/bad-default gap.

**The fix**: added a `phoneFields` derived list in `AutomationsPanel.tsx` (`selectedEntity?.fields.filter((f) => f.type === "text" || f.type === "longtext") ?? []`), mirroring `validateAutomationToField`'s own condition exactly. The auto-default effect now picks `phoneFields[0]?.name` instead of `selectedEntity.fields[0]?.name`, and the `<select>` now maps over `phoneFields` instead of `selectedEntity.fields`. Added a guard: when `phoneFields.length === 0` (the chosen entity has no text/longtext field at all), the form renders a real message (`automations.toField.none`, new i18n key in both `he`/`en`) instead of an empty or invalid dropdown. codegen.ts needed no change, since it doesn't generate this panel.

**The tests**: added two new tests to `AutomationsPanel.test.ts`, each with its own custom entity fixture (not the shared module-level `project`, per the "custom entity in a test needs its own fixture" convention) via a new `renderPanelWith` helper. The first, using a `Shipment` entity whose fields are `[number, text, longtext, boolean]` in that order, asserts the `toField` select's options are exactly `["contactPhone", "notes"]` (excluding `priority` and `isUrgent`) and that its default value is `"contactPhone"` -- the first *eligible* field, not the entity's literal first field. The second, using a `Metric` entity with no text/longtext field at all (`[number, boolean]`), asserts no `toField` select renders and that the new message text appears instead.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `AutomationsPanel.tsx` and `language.ts` to scratchpad. Reverted both alone via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests): the file-level suite failed exactly the 2 predicted tests (unfiltered options list; select rendered instead of the "none" message) -- 9/11 passing, 2 failing as predicted. Along the way, caught and fixed a self-inflicted bug in the new "no eligible field" test: it originally used `assert.equal(domElement, null)` on the `toField` select, which is the long-standing documented hang hazard (node's loose-equality comparison against a DOM node), confirmed via two reverted-code background runs that both silently truncated after 10/11 tests with ~150s of unaccounted time; switched it to `assert.equal(domElement === null, true)`, after which the revert run completed quickly and cleanly with the full, correctly-predicted 2-failure result. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output on either file), re-ran the single file clean (11/11). Ran the full `@forge/web` suite clean (937/937 -- 935 baseline + 2 new) and the full `npm run build` across every workspace (clean). Since this round's fix touched only `apps/web` files, `@forge/api`'s suite was not re-run (unchanged, per the single-workspace-change shortcut). Commit `f192d64`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A new instance of the broader standing lens, but in a different shape from rounds 643-665's run: here the mismatch is between a UI control's own promised constraint (a label/placeholder naming a specific field type) and its actual unfiltered options list, rather than between two sibling code paths or two text surfaces describing the same keybinding. The underlying discipline is the same -- a claim made in one place (UI copy, a doc comment, a sibling's behavior) is not evidence that another place (an options list, a default-picker, an exported mirror) actually honors it; each needs its own direct verification. This round also reconfirmed the standing `assert.equal(domElement, null)` hang hazard firsthand, including its disguised symptom: a background test run that silently drops the last-registered test and reports a plausible-looking summary with ~150s of unexplained duration, rather than an obvious timeout error.

### Round 667: AutomationsPanel.tsx's rule list showed a rule's raw internal entity/field names instead of their display labels, even though the same component's own create-form already shows labels for those same entities/fields

**Context**: round 666's closing survey confirmed the "type-promising selector" family (toField/phoneFields) is closed, and found no other dual-key or badge-text gap remaining. This round's Explore survey checked a different angle entirely within the same component round 666 had just touched: whether the rule-list display, not the create-form, honors the same entity/field label convention.

**The finding**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s `describeRule`/`describeDestination` (before this fix, at lines 149-161) interpolated a saved rule's raw `rule.entityName`/`rule.fieldName`/`rule.toField`/`rule.fieldValue` directly into the i18n description strings (`apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts:607-611` he, `:1219-1223` en -- e.g. the Hebrew `"כש-\"{field}\" בישות \"{entity}\" הופך ל-\"{value}\""`). `AutomationRuleView` (`apps/web/src/api.ts:834-848`) only ever carries these as raw internal identifier strings, never a label. But `Entity` and `Field` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts:96,101,155`) both carry an optional, independently-set `label` distinct from `name` -- `name` is the stable internal identifier, `label` is the human-facing (often Hebrew) display string this app is built around. The very same component's own create-form `<select>`s, just above in the same file (`AutomationsPanel.tsx:236-242`, `:257-263`, `:284-290`, all pre-existing), already render `e.label ?? e.name` / `f.label ?? f.name` when the rule is first built -- so a rule assembled from Hebrew-labeled fields rendered back, once saved and listed, under its raw English/camelCase internal names instead. The enum case compounded this: `fieldValue` for an enum field is stored as the raw `enumValues` entry (per `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:410-411`'s `validateAutomationFieldValue`), and the server's own `interpolateTemplate` (`apps/api/src/automations.ts:59-73`) already resolves that raw value through the field's `enumLabels` before sending the real WhatsApp message -- but the rule-list description never did the same resolution for its own on-screen summary.

**Independent verification**: read `AutomationsPanel.tsx:149-161` directly and confirmed both functions interpolate the raw `rule.*` fields with no lookup against `entities`/`project.spec.entities`, which this component already has in scope (used for `selectedEntity`/`phoneFields`, round 666's own addition). Read the create-form's three `<select>` blocks directly and confirmed each already renders `.label ?? .name`. Read `packages/shared/src/index.ts:92-115` (`FieldSchema`) and `:151-160` (`EntitySchema`) directly and confirmed `label` is optional, independent of `name`, with its own doc comment: "Falls back to `name` when absent." Read `apps/api/src/automations.ts:59-73` (`interpolateTemplate`) and `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:406-411` (`validateAutomationFieldValue`) directly and confirmed the server stores/resolves enum values the same raw-value-plus-`enumLabels` way, establishing the correct target behavior to mirror. Re-grepped for any other type-promising-selector gap (the round 666 family) and found none remaining -- `phoneFields` (round 666) is the only one, already closed.

**The fix**: added `ruleEntity`/`entityLabel`/`fieldLabel`/`fieldValueLabel` helper functions in `AutomationsPanel.tsx` that look up `rule.entityName`/`fieldName` against `entities` (falling back to the raw identifier when the entity/field can no longer be found, e.g. renamed or deleted since the rule was created -- matching `label`'s own documented fallback), and for enum fields resolve `fieldValue` through `field.enumLabels` exactly like `interpolateTemplate` does server-side. `describeRule`/`describeDestination` now call these instead of using the raw `rule.*` strings. codegen.ts doesn't export this panel at all (confirmed via `grep -c "Automation" apps/api/src/codegen.ts` -> 1, an unrelated comment, same as round 666), so no parity port was needed.

**The tests**: added a new test to `AutomationsPanel.test.ts` using a custom fixture entity (`labeledProject`, its own `Order` entity labeled `"הזמנה"`, with an enum `status` field labeled `"סטטוס"` with `enumLabels` and a `customerPhone` field labeled `"טלפון לקוח"`) via the existing `renderPanelWith` helper (round 666). It asserts the rendered rule row contains every label (`הזמנה`, `סטטוס`, `נמסר`, `טלפון לקוח`) and asserts, via negative-lookaround regexes, that none of the corresponding raw identifiers/raw enum value (`status`, `Delivered`, `customerPhone`) appear. Also had to update the pre-existing "lists existing rules" test's assertions: its own shared fixture entity's fields already carried labels distinct from their names (`"Status"`, `"Customer Phone"`) that the old, buggy code happened to never show -- its lowercase-exact `/status/`/`/customerPhone/` regexes were quietly passing only because the raw lowercase name and the capitalized label were different enough strings that nobody had noticed the display was wrong. Updated those two assertions to `/Status/`/`/Customer Phone/`, matching the now-correct label-based display -- an existing test broken by a correct fix, per the standing "update it, don't work around it" convention.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `AutomationsPanel.tsx` to scratchpad. Reverted it alone via `git checkout --` (keeping both test changes): the file-level suite failed exactly the 2 predicted tests (the updated "lists existing rules" assertions, back to seeing raw names; the new labels test) -- 10/12 passing, 2 failing as predicted, all 12 accounted for, no hang. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran the single file clean (12/12). Ran the full `@forge/web` suite clean (938/938 -- 937 baseline + 1 new) and the full `npm run build` across every workspace (clean). Since this round's fix touched only `apps/web` files, `@forge/api`'s suite was not re-run (unchanged, per the single-workspace-change shortcut). Commit `bd84d10`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A third shape in the ongoing "a claim made in one place doesn't imply another place honors it" family, but unlike round 666 (a UI label's promised type-constraint vs. an unfiltered options list) this round's mismatch is between two render paths inside the exact same React component: the create-form (correct, label-first) and the rule-list display (buggy, raw-identifier). The lesson generalizes further: label-first display is this app's own established convention wherever an entity or field name reaches the screen, and every new place a stored rule/record/reference renders an entity or field name back to the user is a candidate for this same check, not just form controls that collect new input.

### Round 668: a `field_equals` automation rule's "Value" input was a plain, type-blind text box for every field type, even though rounds 595/607/613 only ever closed this exact gap server-side, never on the client control itself

**Context**: round 667's own closing note redirected the search toward places that display or collect a stored entity/field reference, suggesting history/audit views, backup summaries, and similar read paths. This round's Explore survey checked that family first (and found it already exhaustively closed with no gaps), then found a different, write-side instance of the same underlying discipline inside a feature this routine has already touched eleven times.

**The finding**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s `field_equals` trigger "Value" input (before this fix, lines 303-309) was an unconditional `<input type="text">`, regardless of the selected field's `type` -- no checkbox for `boolean`, no `<select>` of `enumValues` for `enum`, exactly mirroring the shape of bug round 595 first described for this same input. The server's `validateAutomationFieldValue` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:406-432`) already rejects a `fieldValue` that can't byte-match the field's real stored shape -- added for `boolean`/`enum` in round 595, `date` in round 607, `number` in round 613 -- but every one of those rounds fixed the gap only by adding a server-side 400 rejection; none of them touched the client control itself. Meanwhile `FieldInput` (`EntityPanel.tsx:746-787`), the component every real record-editing form in this app already uses, renders a real `<input type="checkbox">` for `boolean` and a `<select>` of `field.enumValues` (showing `field.enumLabels?.[v] ?? v`) for `enum` -- the exact type-aware convention this app has established everywhere else a field's raw value is entered. `AutomationsPanel.tsx` itself already applies this same "match the control to the field's type" discipline for its sibling `toField` control (round 666's `phoneFields` filter) -- `fieldValue`, in the very same form, was the one structurally parallel input that never received it. The placeholder text itself (`apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts:595/1207`, "Value (e.g. Shipped)" / Hebrew "ערך (לדוגמה: נשלחה)") actively invites typing a human-facing label rather than the field's raw stored value, compounding the gap: a Hebrew-labeled enum field's own `enumLabels` display text is exactly what a user would type here, and it can never byte-match the raw `enumValues` entry the server actually compares against.

**Independent verification**: read `AutomationsPanel.tsx:303-309` directly, confirmed the input renders unconditionally as `type="text"` with no field-type branching. Read `FieldInput`'s boolean (`:746-757`) and enum (`:758-788`) branches directly, confirming the checkbox/select convention this fix mirrors. Read `validateAutomationFieldValue` directly and the roundmap entries for 595/607/613, confirming each one only ever added a server-side rejection branch, never a client-side control change -- so this is a genuinely new angle, not a reopening of that validation-completeness family. Confirmed `codegen.ts` doesn't export the Automations feature at all (`grep -c "Automation" apps/api/src/codegen.ts` -> 1, the same unrelated comment match as rounds 666/667), so no parity port was needed.

**The fix**: added a `selectedField` lookup (`selectedEntity?.fields.find((f) => f.name === fieldName)`) and a new `useEffect` keyed on `fieldName` that points `fieldValue` at one of the newly-selected field's real options whenever it changes (defaulting a `boolean` field to `"true"`, an `enum` field to its first `enumValues` entry) instead of carrying over unrelated free text left from a previously-selected field. The "Value" control now renders: a checkbox (wrapped in a new `.automations-field-value-checkbox` label, matching the app's own existing `<label className="...">` + checkbox pattern from `App.tsx`) for `boolean`, bound to the exact strings `"true"`/`"false"`; a `<select>` of `uniqueEnumValues(selectedField.enumValues)` showing `enumLabels` for `enum`; and the original plain text input, unchanged, for every other field type. Added one new i18n key, `automations.fieldValue.booleanLabel` ("True" / "אמת (true)"), for the checkbox's own label text, and a small CSS rule for the new wrapper class.

**The tests**: two new tests in `AutomationsPanel.test.ts`, using a new `Ticket` fixture entity (`triggerFieldProject`, with a `text` field for the phone-destination requirement, a `boolean` `resolved` field, and an `enum` `priority` field with Hebrew `enumLabels`) via the existing `renderPanelWith` helper. The first switches the trigger to `field_equals` and the field to `resolved`, asserts the checkbox renders checked by default (not an empty/unset value), asserts the plain text input does NOT render for this field type, unchecks it, submits, and asserts the request body's `fieldValue` is the literal string `"false"`. The second switches to the `priority` enum field, asserts the rendered `<select>`'s options are exactly `["Low","High"]` with their Hebrew `enumLabels` as visible text, asserts it defaults to the first value, changes it to `"High"`, submits, and asserts the request body's `fieldValue` is the raw `"High"`, not its display label.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `AutomationsPanel.tsx`, `language.ts`, and `styles.css` to scratchpad. Reverted all three alone via `git checkout --` (keeping the test changes): the file-level suite failed exactly the 2 predicted tests -- 12/14 passing, 2 failing as predicted, no hang. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` on all three files (no output), re-ran the single file clean (14/14). Ran the full `@forge/web` suite: first attempt showed 939/940 with the lone failure being `BuildProgress.test.ts`'s own already-documented recurring flake (not a new regression); re-ran `BuildProgress.test.ts` alone in isolation (31/31 clean), then re-ran the full suite again clean (940/940 -- 938 baseline + 2 new). Ran the full `npm run build` across every workspace (clean). Since this round's fix touched only `apps/web` files, `@forge/api`'s suite was not re-run (unchanged, per the single-workspace-change shortcut). Commit `a50227b`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. This closes the client-side half of a gap the Automations feature's own validation-completeness family (595, 607, 613) only ever addressed server-side -- the "Value" input can now only ever hold one of the selected field's real, matchable values for `boolean`/`enum` fields, the same two types `FieldInput` already treats specially everywhere else in this app. A twelfth round touching this feature, and the first to fix one of its *client controls* rather than adding another server-side rejection branch.

### Round 669: Business Twin's enum-distribution insight silently excluded boolean fields, even though two sibling features already treat a boolean's two values as the same "small, fixed value space" as an enum's

**Context**: round 668's own closing note explicitly asked to diversify away from the Automations feature (12 rounds already: 586-588, 595-597, 600, 606-608, 613-614, 666-668). This round's Explore survey was steered toward other features entirely and, after ruling out CSV import/export, Time Machine diffing, WhatsApp Web connection races, Global Search, and collaborator permission routing (all already well-hardened with explicit fix-history comments), found a genuinely new gap in the Business Twin panel.

**The finding**: `twin.ts`'s `computeEnumDistributionObservations` (the function that produces a per-value-count insight like `"Status" breakdown in "Order": 18 "pending", 4 "shipped"`) filtered its candidate fields with `f.type === "enum" && f.enumValues && f.enumValues.length > 0` (line 430, before this fix) -- the only place anywhere in `twin.ts` that produces this kind of distribution insight, and a `grep` for `boolean` in the whole file turned up zero `field.type === "boolean"` checks. Meanwhile `entityFormatting.ts` already establishes, in two other features, that a boolean's two values belong in the exact same category as an enum's for this kind of summarization: `isGroupableField` (line 1455-1456) is literally `field.type === "enum" || field.type === "boolean"`, and `findFilterableFields`'s own doc comment (line 534-546) explicitly narrates fixing this same gap for the per-field filter dropdown at round 286 ("a boolean field's two values (Yes/No) are exactly the kind of workable, human-scannable value space the filter was built for"). A business-meaningful boolean field -- `Paid`, `IsActive`, `IsBillable` (common in `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s own seeded specs) -- got no distribution insight at all in the one panel whose own `computeNumericAggregateObservations` doc comment states the Twin's explicit design principle: a "most-business-meaningful" value type should not be "silently invisible to the one panel meant to summarize the data."

**Independent verification**: read `computeEnumDistributionObservations` (`twin.ts:423-472`) directly, confirmed its field filter requires `type === "enum"` with no boolean branch. Grepped the whole file for `boolean` and confirmed every match is the `hebrew: boolean` parameter type annotation, never a `field.type` check. Read `isGroupableField` (`entityFormatting.ts:1455-1456`) and `findFilterableFields`/`findFilterableEnumFields` (`entityFormatting.ts:531-551`) directly, confirming both already fold boolean into the same category as enum for structurally similar purposes (table grouping, per-field filtering), with `findFilterableFields`'s own doc comment explicitly describing the same "never widened to match" shape this round's finding repeats. Read `repository.ts`'s `rowToRecord`, confirming a boolean field's value always comes back as a real JS boolean (`Boolean(value)`), so `String(raw)` on it always yields exactly `"true"`/`"false"` -- the same two-value space `countByValue`'s generic string-keyed counting already handles correctly once the field is let through the filter. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has zero mentions of `computeBusinessTwin`/`BusinessTwin`/`computeEnumDistribution` (`grep -c` -> 0) -- the Business Twin is a live-preview-only feature with no exported-app duplicate, so no parity port was needed.

**The fix**: widened `computeEnumDistributionObservations`'s field filter to `(f.type === "enum" && f.enumValues && f.enumValues.length > 0) || f.type === "boolean"`, renamed the local variable to `distributionFields`, and updated the doc comment to explain the boolean widening and cite the sibling convention it mirrors. In the per-value label lookup, a boolean field's raw `"true"`/`"false"` string now displays as `"TRUE"`/`"FALSE"` -- the same literal, unlocalized convention `interpolateTemplate` (`automations.ts`, WhatsApp message formatting) and `entityFormatting.ts` (CSV export) already use for a boolean's textual form, rather than inventing a third convention or incorrectly running it through `enumLabels` (which a boolean field never has).

**The tests**: two new tests in `twin.test.ts`, mirroring the existing enum-distribution test's exact style with a `paid: boolean` field on an `Order` entity. The first inserts two `true` records and one `false` record, asserts a distribution observation exists mentioning "Paid", and asserts its text matches `/2 "TRUE".*1 "FALSE"/` (sorted by count descending, same as the enum case). The second inserts two records that both have `paid: true`, asserting no distribution observation appears at all -- the same "a single shared value isn't a distribution" guard the enum case already has, now confirmed to also apply to booleans.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `twin.ts` to scratchpad. Reverted it alone via `git checkout --` (keeping both new tests): the file-level suite failed exactly 1 of the 2 new tests (`not ok 25`, the TRUE/FALSE-distribution test) -- the second new test (single-shared-value skip) passed even against the unfixed code, since a boolean field produced no observation at all either way before this fix, so that assertion doesn't distinguish fixed from unfixed behavior on its own; it still correctly documents the post-fix guard. 29/30 passing, 1 failing as predicted. Restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` (no output), re-ran the single file clean (30/30). Ran the full `@forge/api` suite clean (577/577 -- 575 baseline + 2 new) and the full `npm run build` across every workspace (clean). Since this round's fix touched only `apps/api` files, `@forge/web`'s suite was not re-run (unchanged, per the single-workspace-change shortcut). Commit `24779e3`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. A new instance of the standing "a convention established in one place doesn't imply a structurally-parallel place honors it" lens, in yet another shape: here the convention (boolean ≈ enum for small-fixed-value-space UI) was already fixed twice in `entityFormatting.ts` (table grouping, per-field filtering), but a third, independent place doing the same kind of per-value summarization -- the Business Twin's distribution insight -- never inherited it. Also the first round in 27 rounds (643-669) to leave the Automations feature entirely, confirming the broader lens generalizes across features, not just within one heavily-mined one.

### Round 670: Board view's BoardCard ignored the user's drag-reordered column order, the one whole-record render path round 615/621's own audits never reached

**Context**: round 669's own closing note asked to keep diversifying, steering away from Automations (12 rounds) but also noting Business Twin's other observation builders were fair game if a genuinely new gap turned up there. This round's Explore survey checked several angles (project-preference purge sweep, seed/checkpoint/calendar mechanics, Business Twin's remaining observation builders, a hypothesized backup.ts ZIP-path sanitization collision, checkpointDiff.ts's deliberate `required`-change-ignoring contract) and ruled all of them out as either already-sound or already-tested-as-intentional, before finding a genuinely new gap in a different feature: the drag-reorder-columns convention round 615 and round 621 established.

**The finding**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `BoardCard` (the component rendering each Kanban-style card in Board view) computed its non-board-field fields with `entity.fields.filter((f) => f.name !== boardField.name)` (line 409, before this fix) -- the entity's raw, undragged declared order. Every other whole-record render path in the exact same file already uses `orderedFields` (`applyColumnOrder(entity.fields, columnOrder)`, line 1463) instead: the on-screen table itself (`visibleFields`, derived from `orderedFields`), Export CSV and Copy (`recordsToCsv(orderedFields, ...)`), the per-record Print sheet and Print list sheet (`fields={orderedFields}`), and the Columns visibility menu (`orderedFields.map(...)`). Round 615 (commit `629802f`) explicitly ported the drag-order fix to Export CSV, Copy, and per-record Print (Print list already had it from round 597); round 621 separately ported it to the Columns menu. Neither round's own audit reached `BoardCard`, a fifth/sixth sibling doing the same "render every field of a record" job -- so after dragging columns into a custom order, a user sees that order on the table, in CSV/Copy, on both print sheets, and in the Columns menu, but switching to Board view still showed every card's fields in the spec's original declaration order. `codegen.ts` carries a verbatim duplicate of `BoardCard` with the identical bug, confirmed via direct comparison.

**Independent verification**: read `BoardCard`'s definition (`EntityPanel.tsx:378-467`) directly, confirmed line 409's `entity.fields.filter(...)` and that `entity`/`boardField.name` are the only fields used elsewhere in the function body (so dropping the `entity` prop in favor of `orderedFields` is safe). Read `orderedFields`'s definition (line 1463) and all five of its other usages (table `visibleFields` at 1472-1474, CSV/Copy at 2134/2158, print sheets at 3174/3183, Columns menu at 2806) directly, confirming each already receives it while `BoardCard`'s own call site (line 2926-2942, before this fix) passed `entity` instead. Read round 615's and round 621's roadmap entries and their own stated scope (four and one sibling respectively, neither naming `BoardCard`) to confirm this is a genuinely unaudited sibling, not a reopening. Confirmed `codegen.ts`'s `BoardCard` (lines 2621-2661) and its call site (line 4515-4529, before this fix) carry the identical `entity.fields.filter(...)` pattern. Confirmed the one existing board-card test (`EntityPanel.test.ts`, label-disambiguation coverage) only asserts label text via `.includes`, never field order, so this was never incidentally covered.

**The fix**: in both files, `BoardCard` now takes an `orderedFields` prop instead of `entity`, and computes `otherFields` from it (`orderedFields.filter((f) => f.name !== boardField.name)`) -- mirroring round 615's exact pattern. Both call sites now pass `orderedFields={orderedFields}` instead of `entity={entity}`.

**The tests**: one new test in `EntityPanel.test.ts`, mirroring round 615's own test structure -- a custom three-field `Deal` entity (name, phone, status), persists a reordered `columnOrder` (phone before name) via `localStorage`, confirms the on-screen table already reflects it, switches to Board view, and asserts the board card's field labels read "Phone" then "Name," not the entity's declared "Name" then "Phone." One new test in `codegen.test.ts`, mirroring the existing board-disambiguation test's real-DOM technique (`generateExportFiles` + `writeGeneratedWebComponent` + dynamic import, not a reimplementation) against a four-field `Order` entity (name, status, subtotal, shipping), persisting a reordered `forge_column_order` and asserting the same reordered sequence on both the table and the board card. Also had to update one pre-existing hardcoded signature regex in `codegen.test.ts` (`/function BoardCard\(\{ entity, boardField, ... \}\)/`) to expect `orderedFields` instead of `entity` -- the standard "changing a shared signature requires grepping every regex-extraction test" lesson (previously hit in rounds 432, 494, 545, 611, 615).

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed files to scratchpad. Reverted `EntityPanel.tsx` alone via `git checkout --` (keeping its new test): `EntityPanel.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test -- 137/138 passing, no hang. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran clean (138/138). Reverted `codegen.ts` alone via `git checkout --` (keeping both its new test and the updated regex): `codegen.test.ts` failed exactly the 2 predicted tests (the updated signature-regex assertion; the new board-order test) -- 220/222 passing. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran clean (222/222). Since this round touched both workspaces, ran both full suites in sequence: `@forge/web` 941/941 (940 baseline + 1 new), `@forge/api` 578/578 (577 baseline + 1 new). Full `npm run build` across every workspace clean. Commit `1f0da2e`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. The sixth consecutive-family instance (643-670) of "a fix/convention applied to several sibling render paths doesn't imply every structurally-parallel sibling inherited it" -- here the convention is the drag-reorder-columns family round 597/615/621 already established across five other whole-record actions, and `BoardCard` was the one remaining sibling neither of those rounds' own audits named. Closed in both the live preview and the exported standalone app in the same round, since `codegen.ts` carries a verbatim duplicate.

### Round 671: matchesSearch matched a boolean field's raw "true"/"false" value instead of the localized "Yes"/"No" shown everywhere else that field type appears

**Context**: round 670's closing note again asked to keep diversifying rather than resettle on one feature. This round's Explore survey, continuing the diversification steer, looked at `entityFormatting.ts`'s `matchesSearch` function -- the search box's own per-field display-matching logic, already fixed for relation (round ~415), number (round 415), and date (round 475) fields in earlier rounds -- and found the same category of gap still open for boolean fields.

**The finding**: `entityFormatting.ts`'s `isGroupableField` and `findFilterableFields` already treat `boolean` fields the same as `enum` for every other "small, fixed value space" UI surface: the table's group-by/Kanban column headers and the per-field filter dropdown both resolve a boolean value to its real localized "Yes"/"No" ("כן"/"לא" in Hebrew), the same way `language.ts`'s `entity.groupBy.yes`/`entity.groupBy.no` keys are used at `entityFormatting.ts:1484-1485` and `EntityPanel.tsx:2687-2688`. `matchesSearch`'s own ternary chain, however, had branches for `enum`, `relation`, `number`, and `date` display-matching, but no `boolean` branch -- it fell through to the final `String(value)` fallback, matching the raw stored JS boolean's literal "true"/"false" text. That text appears nowhere in the actual UI: the table cell itself renders a checkmark/dash for a boolean field, not even "true"/"false" as text. So typing "Yes"/"No" (or "כן"/"לא") -- the exact words shown in the adjacent filter dropdown and group-by header for that same field -- found nothing in the search box. `codegen.ts`'s own duplicate `matchesSearch` (the exported/standalone app's copy) had the identical gap, confirmed via direct comparison; its own `groupRecordsByField` already uses plain unlocalized "Yes"/"No" literals (no i18n in the exported app), so its fix follows that same unlocalized convention rather than a he/en split.

**Independent verification**: read `entityFormatting.ts`'s `matchesSearch` (lines ~200-261) directly, confirming the ternary chain's enum/relation/number/date branches and the absence of a boolean one. Read `isGroupableField`/`findFilterableFields`'s own `field.type === "boolean"` handling and their call sites (the group-by header, the filter dropdown) to confirm the sibling convention being extended. Confirmed the table cell's actual boolean rendering is a checkmark/dash, not text, at `EntityPanel.tsx:216-218`. Confirmed `entityFormatting.ts` has no live `t()` translator import (only the `Lang` type), matching the existing precedent for a hardcoded he/en literal map already used by the same file's `BOOLEAN_TRUE_VALUES`/`BOOLEAN_FALSE_VALUES` constants. Confirmed via `grep` that `codegen.ts` carries its own duplicate `matchesSearch` (read in full) with the identical gap, and that its own `groupRecordsByField` uses plain "Yes"/"No" literals rather than a translation lookup.

**The fix**: in `entityFormatting.ts`, added a `BOOLEAN_DISPLAY` constant (a `Record<Lang, { true: string; false: string }>` literal map for "Yes"/"No"/"כן"/"לא") and a new boolean branch in `matchesSearch`'s ternary chain, `field.type === "boolean" ? BOOLEAN_DISPLAY[lang][value ? "true" : "false"] : ...`, before the final `String(value)` fallback. In `codegen.ts`'s generated copy, added an unlocalized boolean branch (`value ? "Yes" : "No"`) in the same position, matching the exported app's own unlocalized `groupRecordsByField` convention.

**The tests**: three new tests in `entityFormatting.test.ts`, mirroring the existing date-field test block's structure -- one asserting "Yes"/"No" match a boolean field's `true`/`false` value in English while the raw "true" string does not match; one asserting "כן"/"לא" match in Hebrew; one asserting the English default applies when no `lang` argument is given. One new test in `codegen.test.ts`, mirroring the existing number/date-field `matchesSearch` tests' real-generated-code extraction technique (`generateExportFiles` + regex-extracting the real `matchesSearch` source + `new Function`, not a reimplementation), asserting "Yes"/"No" match and the raw "true" string does not.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both fixed files to scratchpad. Reverted `entityFormatting.ts` alone via `git checkout --` (keeping its three new tests): `entityFormatting.test.ts` failed exactly the 3 predicted tests -- 153/156 passing. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran clean (156/156). Reverted `codegen.ts` alone via `git checkout --` (keeping its one new test): `codegen.test.ts` failed exactly the 1 predicted test -- 222/223 passing. Restored, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, re-ran clean (223/223). Since this round touched both workspaces, ran both full suites in sequence: `@forge/web` 944/944 (941 baseline + 3 new), `@forge/api` 579/579 (578 baseline + 1 new). Full `npm run build` across every workspace clean. Commit `806e62b`.

**Topic status**: closed and pushed. Extends the "boolean ≈ enum for small-fixed-value-space UI" convention (established by `isGroupableField`/`findFilterableFields`, already ported to Business Twin's distribution insight in round 669) to `matchesSearch`'s text-search matching -- the fourth field type (after relation, number, date) found missing from this same function across the routine's history. Closed in both the live preview and the exported standalone app in the same round, since `codegen.ts` carries a verbatim duplicate.

### Direct request (between round 671 and 672): "file" as a new field type -- file/image upload

**Context**: שלומי sent a genuine message (not through the hourly Routine): the generated apps felt "built simply and unprofessionally," and she wanted the quality level of a professional AI app builder like base44. Clarifying questions narrowed the complaint to feature depth specifically. A research pass (base44's public product surface vs. Forge AI's current feature set) produced a prioritized gap list -- file/image uploads first (highest visible impact for the effort, and the single most obvious "demo app" tell: no field type exists for a resume, ID photo, or invoice scan at all) -- and she confirmed: build the app to a very high standard, starting with that list.

**The feature**: added `"file"` as a full seventh field type, spanning every layer a field type touches:
- `packages/shared/src/index.ts`: added to `FIELD_TYPES`. No extra schema constraints needed (unlike enum/relation) -- a file field just stores a JSON descriptor string.
- `packages/db`: no code change needed in `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` or `migrate.ts`'s `sqlTypeFor` -- both already fall through their `default` case to plain `TEXT`/`String(raw)` handling, which is exactly right for a JSON-string value. `seed.ts` gets an explicit `case "file": return null;` so demo data doesn't synthesize a fake, 404-ing file descriptor.
- `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`: a new `POST /projects/:id/entities/:entityName/fields/:fieldName/upload` route, multer-backed (disk storage, 10MB/1-file limit, filenames always a fresh `randomUUID()` + a sanitized extension, never the original filename). Returns `{ file: { url, name, size, mimeType } }`; never touches the record/database itself -- the client then writes that JSON-stringified descriptor as the field's own value through the ordinary record create/update routes, same as any other field. Project-access and field-type validation run in their own middleware *before* multer's disk-storage middleware, so an unauthorized or malformed request never gets a file written to disk first (verified by a dedicated test asserting the 404/400 happens with nothing on disk).
- `apps/api/src/app.ts`: `/api/uploads` is served via `express.static`, registered **before** `createAuthRouter`/`createProjectsRouter` -- a real bug caught by the round's own integration test: `createProjectsRouter`'s `router.use(requireAuth(db))` applies to *every* path sharing its `/api` mount, matched route or not, so mounting the static route after it (the first, wrong attempt) made every uploaded file require a Bearer token to fetch -- which a plain `<img src>` or download `<a href>` in the real UI can never send. Access control for uploads is therefore the "unguessable randomUUID filename" model instead, the same one most simple file-hosting setups use.
- `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`: `parseFileFieldValue`/`isImageMimeType` helpers; `fieldDisplayValue` (CSV export) shows the filename; `buildImportRecords` skips a file column per row exactly like relation, and a *required* file field refuses the whole CSV import up front exactly like a required relation field (the error message was generalized from "required relation field" to "required ${type} field" to cover both without duplicating the guard). `isInlineEditableField` now also excludes `"file"` (its real editing UI needs more room than one table cell), which automatically excludes it from the bulk-edit dropdown too, since that list is built from the same function.
- `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`: `Cell` renders a file value as a thumbnail (image MIME types) or a filename download link; `FieldInput` gets a `<input type="file">` branch that uploads immediately on choice (via the new `uploadRecordFile` in `api.ts`) and stores the returned descriptor, with its own local upload-error state. Needs `projectId`/`entityName` props threaded through, but only the one add/edit-form call site actually passes them -- the other two call sites (inline cell edit, bulk edit) can never reach the file branch at all now that `isInlineEditableField` excludes it.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts`: `entity.file.choose`/`entity.file.remove`, plus Hebrew/English translations for the four new `HttpError` codes the upload route can throw (`NOT_A_FILE_FIELD`, `NO_FILE_UPLOADED`, `FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `UPLOAD_ERROR`) -- caught by the existing `language.test.ts` scan that every thrown code has both translations, exactly as designed.
- `packages/spec-engine/src/anthropic.ts`: the AI spec-generation prompt's type enum and a short rule on when to actually propose a `file` field (a genuine upload the description implies, not just any text).
- **Scope decision, disclosed to שלומי**: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported/standalone app generator) does **not** get upload support this round -- every other field type's logic is duplicated there as a template-string copy, and giving the exported app real upload support means its own multer setup and disk storage, a comparably sized follow-up, not a quick port. A `file` field in an exported app currently degrades to codegen's generic text fallback (shows/edits the raw JSON descriptor as text) rather than crashing -- ugly, not broken.

**The tests**: `apps/api/src/app.test.ts` -- three new tests exercising the real route end to end: (1) upload → the file is actually reachable at the returned URL through the real static route → that descriptor round-trips through a real record create and a real record read; (2) uploading to a non-file field is rejected with nothing written to disk; (3) uploading to a project the authenticated user has no access to is rejected before multer ever runs. `withServer`'s test helper now gives every test a fresh `mkdtemp`-ed uploads directory, auto-cleaned in its `finally`. `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.test.ts` -- two new tests: the add form's real upload-on-choose flow through to a real create-record POST carrying the exact descriptor, and the table cell rendering a stored descriptor as a real link (not the raw JSON). `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.test.ts` -- updated the existing `isInlineEditableField` test to also assert `"file"` is excluded.

**Bugs the tests caught before anything shipped**: (1) the `/api/uploads` mount-order bug described above -- caught by the integration test actually fetching the returned URL rather than only checking the upload response's shape; (2) `language.test.ts`'s existing "every `HttpError` code has both translations" scan immediately failed on the four new codes, exactly the kind of regression that scan exists to catch, fixed by adding all four translations.

**Verification**: ran every touched workspace's full suite in sequence (this round touched five: `@forge/shared`, `@forge/db`, `@forge/spec-engine`, `@forge/api`, `@forge/web`) plus the full `npm run build`. `@forge/shared` 16/16, `@forge/db` 184/184, `@forge/spec-engine` 150/150 (all three unchanged, confirming the new field type's default-case fallthrough is genuinely a no-op for them), `@forge/api` 582/582 (579 baseline + 3 new), `@forge/web` 946/946 (944 baseline + 2 new, after fixing the missing translations above). Full build clean. Given this is new, additive, cross-cutting feature work rather than a single isolated bug fix, verification here is "every touched workspace's full suite plus build, all clean, with the new tests themselves each independently confirmed to catch a real regression during development" rather than the usual single-fix revert/restore/diff cycle, which doesn't map cleanly onto a feature spanning sixteen files across five workspaces. Commit `807333d`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed; reported to שלומי in Hebrew with the live link. Next up per her own prioritization and the research pass's ranking: scheduled/recurring automations, then a visual (chart-based) dashboard for Business Twin, then a generic outbound-webhook automation action, then real role enforcement (RBAC) -- she can redirect at any point.

### Direct request, continued: scheduled/recurring automations ("every day at 9am, send X")

**Context**: second item on the priority list from the base44 research pass, continuing straight after the file-upload field type with no further redirect from שלומי.

**The feature**: a third automation trigger, `"schedule"`, alongside the existing `record_created`/`field_equals`:
- `packages/db/src/automations.ts`: `AutomationTrigger` gains `"schedule"`; `AutomationRule` gains two nullable columns, `scheduleTimeUtc` ("HH:MM", 24-hour UTC) and `scheduleDaysOfWeek` (comma-separated `0`-`6`, `getUTCDay()` numbering; null/empty = every day). `ensureAutomationRulesTable` adds both via the same additive `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` + `PRAGMA table_info` idempotence check `checkpoints.ts`'s own `kind` column migration already established -- an existing database from before this round upgrades safely, no backfill needed (both columns are simply unused/null for every pre-existing `record_created`/`field_equals` row). New `listEnabledScheduledRules(db)` -- global across every project, unlike `listEnabledAutomationRulesForEntity`, since a schedule check has no single record-change event to scope it.
- `apps/api/src/automations.ts`: **no periodic/cron infrastructure existed anywhere in this codebase before this round** (confirmed by an Explore survey: `idempotency.ts` explicitly does opportunistic per-request cleanup "since this app has no cron/scheduler infrastructure"; `whatsappWeb.ts` deliberately has no auto-reconnect timer either). Added `isScheduledRuleDue(rule, now)` -- a pure, directly-unit-testable function: due when the scheduled time has already passed *today* (not an exact-minute match, which a jittered or missed tick could silently skip past) AND it hasn't already fired today, reusing the *existing* `lastTriggeredAt` column (already written by every `recordAutomationRun` call) rather than adding a third new column just to track that. `fireScheduledRule` is `fireRule`'s schedule-sibling -- deliberately separate rather than reused with nulled-out arguments, since a schedule rule has no triggering record at all: no `toMode:"field"` destination lookup is possible (enforced at the schema level, see below), and `messageTemplate` is sent verbatim with no `{{field}}` interpolation. `runScheduledAutomationsCheck(db, whatsapp, now)` is one tick: list every enabled schedule rule globally, fire whichever `isScheduledRuleDue` says are due, catching each rule's own failure so one bad rule can't stop the rest. `startScheduledAutomationsLoop` wraps that in a bare `setInterval` (60s) and returns a `stop()`.
- **Test-leak constraint, deliberately designed around**: `startScheduledAutomationsLoop` is called **only from `server.ts`'s top-level script, never from `createApp()`** (`app.ts`) -- `app.test.ts`'s `withServer` helper calls `createApp()` fresh per test with no corresponding place to stop a background interval, so starting the scheduler inside `createApp()` would leak a live, never-cleared `setInterval` on every single test in that file (hundreds of them), each keeping its own timer alive indefinitely. Confirmed via the architecture-mapping survey before writing any code, not discovered after the fact.
- `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`: `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`/`UpdateAutomationRuleSchema` gain `scheduleTimeUtc` (regex-validated `HH:MM`) and `scheduleDaysOfWeek` (regex-validated comma-separated `0`-`6`), plus two new `.refine()`s: `scheduleTimeUtc` is required when `trigger === "schedule"`, and `toMode` must be `"static"` for a schedule rule (there's no triggering record to read a `toMode:"field"` destination from). `findAutomationRuleInvariantViolation` (the PATCH route's own merged-result validator) gets the identical two checks, so a PATCH that would make an existing schedule rule internally inconsistent (e.g. flipping `toMode` to `"field"`) is rejected the same way creation is.
- `apps/web`: `api.ts`'s hand-duplicated `AutomationTrigger`/`AutomationRuleView`/create/update types and request builders updated to match. `AutomationsPanel.tsx` gets a `<option value="schedule">`, a time input + seven day-of-week checkboxes (default: every day selected; sent as `undefined`/"every day" rather than a redundant literal `"0,1,2,3,4,5,6"` when all seven stay checked) shown only for the schedule trigger, a `useEffect` that forces `toMode` to `"static"` the instant `"schedule"` is chosen (hiding the toMode selector entirely, not just disabling it, so it never dishonestly implies "field" is still a live option), and a `describeSchedule` rule-list description using the real `Intl.DateTimeFormat` weekday formatter (locale-aware day names) instead of seven more hand-maintained translation keys.

**The tests**: `packages/db/src/automations.test.ts` -- insert/update round-tripping the two new columns; the additive-migration test mirroring `checkpoints.test.ts`'s own pattern exactly (old-shape table, insert a row, run the migration, confirm it backfills nulls without disturbing the existing row, confirm idempotence on a second run); `listEnabledScheduledRules` returning exactly the enabled schedule rules across multiple projects, excluding a disabled one and a non-schedule one. `apps/api/src/automations.test.ts` -- `isScheduledRuleDue`'s four real behaviors (due once the time passes; not due again the same UTC day; day-of-week filtering, including the `null` = every-day case; always false for a non-schedule trigger or a missing `scheduleTimeUtc`); `fireScheduledRule`'s three outcomes (sent, with the template left un-interpolated even when it contains `{{field}}`-shaped text; failed with no destination; failed when disconnected); `runScheduledAutomationsCheck` firing exactly the due, enabled rules across two different projects in one call, leaving a not-yet-due rule and a disabled-but-due rule both untouched. `apps/api/src/app.test.ts` -- the real HTTP route rejecting a schedule rule with no `scheduleTimeUtc`, rejecting `toMode:"field"` for one, accepting a valid one and storing `scheduleDaysOfWeek` correctly, and rejecting a PATCH that would flip an existing schedule rule's `toMode` to `"field"`. `apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.test.ts` -- choosing "schedule" reveals the time input and seven day checkboxes (all checked by default), unchecking one and changing the time, confirms the toMode selector is gone from the DOM entirely, fills in the static phone number and message, and asserts the real submitted request carries the exact `scheduleTimeUtc`/`scheduleDaysOfWeek`/`toMode:"static"` chosen -- not just that *some* request fired.

**Verification**: `@forge/db` 189/189 (184 baseline + 5 new), `@forge/api` 591/591 (582 baseline + 9 new), `@forge/web` 947/947 (946 baseline + 1 new). Full `npm run build` clean. Same "every touched workspace's full suite plus build, all clean" verification bar as the file-upload round above, for the same reason (new cross-cutting feature work, not a single isolated fix). Commit `e1ba325`.

**Known limitation, disclosed**: the scheduled time is UTC only -- there's no stored per-project timezone anywhere in this app (the same gap `interpolateTemplate`'s own `lang` parameter already has, picked from `isHebrewText(project.description)` rather than a real stored preference). A business owner has to do their own UTC conversion when picking a time. Not fixed in this round; flagged as a natural fast-follow if it turns out to matter in practice.

**Status**: shipped and pushed; reported to שלומי in Hebrew with the live link. Next up per the priority list: a visual (chart-based) dashboard for Business Twin, then a generic outbound-webhook automation action, then real role enforcement (RBAC).

### Direct request, continued: a visual Dashboard view for Business Twin (bar charts + stat tiles)

**Context**: third item on the priority list, continuing straight after scheduled automations with no redirect from שלומי.

**The finding**: every Business Twin observation builder in `apps/api/src/twin.ts` already computes real structured data internally -- `computeEnumDistributionObservations`'s `countByValue` Map and sorted per-value breakdown, `computeNumericAggregateObservations`'s `sum`/`average` -- but immediately formats it into a prose sentence and discards the numbers; the `BusinessTwin` API response and `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx`'s own rendering were both prose/stat-tile-count only, with no chart-like visual anywhere (confirmed via an architecture-survey subagent before writing any code: no bar, no SVG/canvas, nothing under `.twin-*` in styles.css implying proportional width).

**The fix**:
- `apps/api/src/twin.ts`: `computeEnumDistributionObservations` and `computeNumericAggregateObservations` now ALSO return their already-computed structured data on each item (`breakdown: {value, label, count}[]` and `sum`/`average`/`recordCount` respectively), alongside the unchanged `text` prose -- purely additive, the existing `jumpableObservations` prose list and every existing test against it are untouched. `BusinessTwin` gains two new top-level arrays, `distributions` and `numericStats`, populated from these two builders' own results (captured separately before being spread into `jumpableObservations` as before).
- `apps/web`: `api.ts`'s client-side `BusinessTwin` type mirrors the two new arrays. `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx` gets a Report/Dashboard toggle (reusing the app's existing `.view-toggle`/`.view-toggle-btn` convention from `EntityPanel.tsx`'s table/board/calendar toggle) -- **defaults to Report**, specifically so every pre-existing jumpable-observation test and behavior (mostLinkedRecord/mostActiveObservation/jumpableObservations buttons) keeps rendering immediately exactly as before, with the Dashboard as something a person opts into rather than a replacement. The Dashboard view renders a new `TwinBarChart` component (one per distribution) and a stat tile (reusing `.twin-stat-tile`, with a new `.twin-stat-tile-static` to drop its hover-as-clickable affordance) per numeric aggregate.
- **Design decision on chart color**, following the dataviz skill's procedure (form → color → validate → marks → interaction → accessibility) loaded before writing any chart code: a single flat accent color (`var(--accent)`, the app's own existing brand color) for every bar in every chart, rather than a different hue per bar/value. An enum's value set (or the list of entities) is arbitrary, business-specific, AI-generated data with no fixed categorical order to assign stable hues to -- the skill's own non-negotiable ("a 9th series is never a generated hue") argues directly against inventing one here. Identity comes from each row's own text label; magnitude comes from real bar length (`width: %` of the row's own max), which reads correctly regardless of color vision, consistent with the skill's "never encode the only information in color" principle. No chart library was added -- plain HTML/CSS bars, matching this app's existing zero-dependency, hand-rolled stat-tile style (confirmed via survey: no Recharts/Chart.js/D3/etc. anywhere in `apps/web/package.json`).

**The tests**: `apps/api/src/twin.test.ts` -- two new tests confirming `twin.distributions`/`twin.numericStats` carry the exact real numbers (not just matching prose), including an enum field's translated `enumLabels` in the structured `breakdown` too. `apps/web/src/BusinessTwinPanel.test.ts` -- a full round-trip test: dashboard content absent until the toggle is clicked, then a bar per breakdown value with the correct label/value text, the larger bucket's bar genuinely wider than the smaller one (not just correct numbers -- real relative bar length), a stat tile showing the right sum, and switching back to Report hides the chart again; plus an empty-state test when there's nothing to chart. `apps/web/src/twinReport.test.ts`'s and `BusinessTwinPanel.test.ts`'s own pre-existing `BusinessTwin` object fixtures needed the two new required fields added (caught immediately by the existing tests crashing on `undefined.length` the first time the full suite ran -- fixed before this was ever a real regression).
