### Round 705: AutomationsPanel's Create/Save button silently did nothing on an incomplete form, for several conditionally-required fields

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Another real, reachable "dead end"/"silent failure" UI defect, the same family as round 704's BuildProgress finding but in a completely different panel -- a validation asymmetry between a form's own submit guard and its button's `disabled` attribute.

**The gap**: `handleSubmit`'s early-return guard (`AutomationsPanel.tsx`, formerly lines 211-216) checked several conditionally-required fields depending on the chosen trigger/action type: `fieldValue` (for trigger `"field_equals"`), a schedule time and at least one day (for trigger `"schedule"`), a webhook URL (for actionType `"webhook"`), and a phone field or a static phone number (for actionType `"send_whatsapp"`, depending on `toMode`). But the submit button's own `disabled` attribute (line 693, before this fix) only ever checked `createBusy || !messageTemplate.trim()` -- none of those other conditions. Concrete repro: pick trigger "When a field is set to a value", choose a text field (so the Value control stays a free-text input, defaulting to empty), type a message, leave Value blank, click Create -- the button is enabled, the click fires `handleSubmit`, the guard's early `return` fires silently, and nothing happens at all: no request, no error, no spinner, no created rule. Identical silent no-op for an empty webhook URL or an empty static phone number. The server's own `CreateAutomationRuleSchema` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) already has clear `.refine()` checks with real, specific error messages for exactly these same cases -- but the client's premature `return` means that request, and its helpful server error, never even gets sent. Each later trigger/action type (schedule, webhook, static-number) added its own guard to `handleSubmit` without the button's `disabled` condition ever being extended to match -- the same root-cause class as round 704's finding, a derived boolean that drifted out of sync with the logic it was meant to mirror as the feature grew. Confirmed via the test file that no existing test asserted the button was disabled, or that an error showed, for any of these specific incomplete-form states.

**The fix**: extracted a single `formIncomplete` boolean (covering all 6 conditions `handleSubmit` already checked, including `!selectedEntity`), computed once and shared between `handleSubmit`'s own guard (`if (formIncomplete || !selectedEntity) return;`, the explicit `!selectedEntity` kept alongside it purely for TypeScript's control-flow narrowing of `selectedEntity` for the rest of the function) and the submit button's `disabled` attribute (`disabled={createBusy || formIncomplete}`). The two can now never drift apart again, since both read the exact same expression. Confirmed no `codegen.ts` parity needed -- the generated standalone app has no automations feature at all.

**The tests**: `AutomationsPanel.test.ts` -- 1 new test covering the `field_equals`/blank-Value case end-to-end: picks the trigger, confirms the free-text Value input renders (a plain text field, not boolean/enum), types a message, asserts the submit button is genuinely `disabled`, submits the form anyway and confirms zero requests were made (matching the disabled state, not just a passive assertion), then fills in a real Value and confirms the button becomes enabled and the rule is actually created. Regression-proofed by reverting the button's `disabled` attribute back to its original bare `!messageTemplate.trim()` check: the test failed with the exact expected `false !== true` mismatch on the disabled assertion, then passed clean once restored. The full `AutomationsPanel.test.ts` file (25/25, including the pre-existing schedule/webhook/toField/toNumber-path tests) was run in isolation afterward to confirm no regression across every other trigger/action-type combination the fix touches.

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A different bug class from the last three rounds' "dead-end UI state" family (BuildProgress, AutomationsPanel, WhatsAppPanel) -- this is specifically the validation-parity family round 702 first closed for `handleBulkUpdate`, now extended to its other, previously-unpatched sibling.

**The gap**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `commitInlineEdit` (double-click table-cell editing) had no pre-submit required-field check at all, unlike its two siblings that mutate through the exact same `FieldInput`/`isInlineEditableField` set of types (text/longtext/number/boolean/enum/date): the single-record add/edit form's own `missingField` guard, and `handleBulkUpdate`'s identical check (round 702). A user could double-click a required text/longtext/number/date cell, clear it, and press Enter (or blur) to commit -- firing a doomed PATCH, rejected server-side (`packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` throwing `ValidationError('Field "X" is required')`), but the client's `resolveErrorMessage` always substitutes the generic `error.VALIDATION_ERROR` string for any `VALIDATION_ERROR` code, discarding the server's specific field name. That generic message ("check the form and try again") is actively misleading for this exact interaction: inline cell editing never shows a form at all, just one lone table cell, so the user had no idea which field or row was even wrong beyond the row getting a generic `moveErrorId` error style. `codegen.ts`'s exported standalone app had the identical missing guard in its own duplicate `commitInlineEdit`, there leaking the server's raw, un-translated "Field \"X\" is required" message regardless of the app's own language -- same root cause, different symptom.

**The fix**: added the same required-field guard `handleBulkUpdate` already uses, scoped to `commitInlineEdit`: look up the field def for `editingCell.field`, and if required and blank, call `setError(t("entity.form.requiredField", { field: ... }))` plus `setMoveErrorId(recordId)`, and return *before* clearing `editingCell` or calling `updateRecord` -- deliberately leaving the cell open (not silently closed) so the user can fix the value right there without double-clicking again, confirmed safe by reading the Enter-key and blur handlers' own control flow. Ported the identical check into `codegen.ts`'s duplicate `commitInlineEdit`, using its own plain-text message convention (no i18n system in the exported app).

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` -- 1 new full-render test: double-clicks a required text cell, clears it, presses Enter, confirms no PATCH is sent, the real underlying record is untouched, the real translated required-field message appears, and the cell input stays open for further editing. Also fixed a pre-existing round-545 regression test whose bare `{ name: "Customer" }` entity stub (no `fields` property) would otherwise crash against the new `entity.fields.find(...)` call -- confirmed via an actual isolated run that this crashes with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')` before the fix, the same stub-drift class round 702 already hit once for `handleBulkUpdate`. `codegen.test.ts` -- same 2 changes: 1 new regex-extraction test for the ported guard, plus the identical pre-existing entity-stub fix, confirmed broken the same way via an isolated run first.

**Verification**: both new tests failed with the exact expected mismatch during each file's regression-proof revert, then passed clean once restored, alongside the 11 pre-existing inline-cell-edit/bulk-update tests run as a targeted subset in `EntityPanel.test.ts` (11/11) and both codegen inline-cell-editor tests (2/2). `npx tsc -b` clean for `apps/web`. Full `npm run build` clean for both workspaces. Both workspaces changed this round, so both full suites were run: `@forge/api` 632/632 clean; `@forge/web` 1009/1009 clean. Commit `e33699d`.

### Round 708: a single stray Hebrew/English word in a /refine instruction could flip an entire live project's language

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A genuinely different bug class from the last several rounds (required-field validation, dead-end UI states) -- a real, reachable language-consistency regression in the core spec-generation path itself, not a client-side UI bug.

**The gap**: `isHebrewText` (`packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`) only checks whether its input contains at least one Hebrew character anywhere (`/[֐-׿]/`), not which language dominates. Both the `/refine` route (post-build, on an already-live project) and `/answers` route (pre-build, during spec review) build their prompt by concatenating the project's own established `description` with brand-new, unrelated text -- a refine instruction, a clarifying-question answer -- then called `isHebrewText` on that WHOLE combined string to decide which language `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate` (and, via its own "same language as the user's description" system-prompt rule, the AI provider too) writes every entity/field label, summary, role, and assumption in. A single Hebrew word anywhere in the NEW text alone -- a pasted name, a stray word in an otherwise-English instruction -- flipped an already-built, already-live English project's ENTIRE set of labels to Hebrew, not just whatever the instruction was actually about (and symmetrically, one stray English word in a Hebrew project's refine instruction). `pipeline.ts`'s `updateProjectSpec` wholesale-replaces `project.spec`, with no merge step that would have caught or limited the damage. This is a real, visible regression on a live app -- confirmed by directly reproducing it end-to-end through the actual HTTP route before fixing anything (see Verification).

**The fix**: added an optional `isHebrewOverride?: boolean` parameter to the `SpecProvider.generate` interface, threaded through `generateSpec` (including its own fallback-to-heuristic call when the primary provider fails) and both providers. `HeuristicSpecProvider` uses `isHebrewOverride ?? isHebrewText(description)` -- fully backward-compatible, since omitting it preserves the exact prior inference-from-text behavior for brand-new projects with no established language yet. `AnthropicSpecProvider` appends an explicit directive ("Write every ... in Hebrew/English, regardless of what language any part of the request below is written in") to the user message only when the override is given, since the system prompt's own language-matching rule can't otherwise distinguish an established project's real language from one stray word in newly-appended text. Both `/refine` and `/answers` now pass `isHebrewText(project.description)` -- the project's own established description ALONE, never the new instruction/answer text -- as that override, so the new text can still freely keyword-match entities without ever getting a vote on which script the whole spec renders in.

**The tests**: `heuristic.test.ts` -- 1 new test confirming `isHebrewOverride` pins the output language in both directions (English override on Hebrew-containing text; Hebrew override on all-English text) and that omitting it preserves the pre-existing inference behavior. `anthropic.test.ts` -- 1 new test capturing the real request body sent to a fake `fetchImpl`, confirming the directive is appended only when the override is given, and the description is sent completely unchanged when it's omitted. `index.test.ts` -- 1 new test confirming `generateSpec` forwards the override to both the primary provider and its own fallback-to-heuristic call when the primary throws. `app.test.ts` -- 1 new real, end-to-end integration test: creates an English-described project, builds it for real through the HTTP route, then calls the real `/refine` endpoint with an instruction containing exactly one Hebrew word (a name), and confirms the resulting `Customer` entity's label is still unset (English), not the Hebrew "לקוחות" the bug would have produced. Regression-proofed every one of the four changed files independently by reverting each fix in turn and re-running its own new test: the `app.test.ts` integration test reproduced the real bug live (`got label "לקוחות"`) before the route-level fix, and each of the three spec-engine unit tests failed with its own exact expected mismatch before its corresponding fix, all passing clean once restored.

**Verification**: all four regression-proof reverts failed with their exact expected mismatch (including the real end-to-end repro in `app.test.ts`), then passed clean once every fix was restored. The full `spec-engine` suite ran clean: 153/153 (150 baseline + 3 new). The full `@forge/api` suite ran clean on an unpiped run: 633/633 (632 baseline + 1 new). Full `npm run build` clean for both workspaces (apps/api has no separate `tsc -b` typecheck step in this repo -- esbuild bundling only -- so the test suites are this workspace's real correctness gate, consistent with every prior apps/api-only round). `apps/web` untouched this round. Commit `f52c1b7`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 712: CSV import always dropped a relation field's cell, even though the matching export already renders a real, resolvable label

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible feature (round 711's survey explicitly steered away from re-proposing another topbar badge or the Templates Gallery, surfacing this instead): `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`'s `buildImportRecords` (the parser behind EntityPanel's "Import CSV" button) had a bare `if (field.type === "relation" || field.type === "file") continue;` -- a relation column was always ignored per row, and a *required* relation field refused the whole import outright with one clear error. This had been visited and explicitly reconfirmed as a deliberate, still-open scoping decision at least twice before (round 393's own survey, and the later `file`-field-support round that extended the identical pattern to `file` rather than closing relation's gap) -- genuinely real, genuinely never implemented.

**The gap**: the matching export path (`recordsToCsv` -> `fieldDisplayValue` -> `relationDisplayLabel`) already renders every relation cell as the related record's real display label (e.g. "Dana Levi"), using `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` already loaded in `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own component state (`loadRelated`'s effect). Re-importing that *exact same file* your own app just exported silently dropped that column's data on every row -- a broken round-trip for the single most common "I have a spreadsheet of related records" case (e.g. `Order.courierId`, `Deal.customerId`), and any entity with a *required* relation field (very common, e.g. `OrderItem.product`) couldn't be CSV-imported at all.

**The fix**: `buildImportRecords` gained two new parameters, `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` (both already in scope at `EntityPanel.tsx`'s call site, no new fetch needed). A relation cell is now resolved case-insensitively against `recordDisplayLabel` over the target entity's records -- the exact reverse of `relationDisplayLabel`'s own forward resolution -- or its literal `"#<id>"` form is accepted directly (the same fallback `relationDisplayLabel` itself renders when a label can't be resolved, so a file round-trips even for a record whose label has since changed or gone ambiguous). Zero matches is a row error; more than one match (display labels aren't guaranteed unique, the same problem `fieldLabelOccurrences` already disambiguates for column headers in this same file) asks for the `"#<id>"` form instead of silently guessing wrong. Dropped `relation` from the required-field whole-file refusal -- a required relation field is now resolved per row like any other required field, instead of being refused outright. Both new parameters default to empty (`[]`/`{}`), so a caller that doesn't supply them -- or a relation whose target isn't part of this project's spec at all -- falls back to the exact original behavior unchanged, preserving every pre-existing test unmodified.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed required and ported -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has an exact hand-duplicated `buildImportRecords` with the identical gap. Ported the same resolution there, referencing the generated app's own module-level `ALL_ENTITIES` directly (simpler than threading an `allEntities` parameter, since the generated app is single-project) plus a new `relatedRecords` parameter at its one call site (`handleImportFile`). `file`-field support doesn't exist in the generated app at all (confirmed, unrelated), so only the relation gap needed porting there.

**The tests**: `entityFormatting.test.ts` -- 5 new tests: resolving a relation cell (including a *required* one, no longer refused) to the matching record's id; accepting the `"#<id>"` form directly; a row error for no match; a row error asking for the `"#<id>"` form on an ambiguous (duplicate-label) match; and confirming a blank required-relation cell still reports the missing-required-field error even with `relatedRecords` provided. The two pre-existing relation tests (whole-file refusal, optional-column-ignored) were left untouched and still pass unmodified, since they call the function without the new parameters. `codegen.test.ts` -- 1 new integration-style test generating a real export with a required relation field, extracting the real generated `buildImportRecords`/`recordDisplayLabel`/`pickDisplayField`/`DISPLAY_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` source via this file's own established regex-extraction convention, supplying a hand-written `ALL_ENTITIES` declaration (the one piece of real module scope the extracted snippet doesn't carry), and exercising the same resolve/`"#<id>"`/no-match/ambiguous-match/no-data-fallback cases as the live-preview test. Updated all 11 pre-existing regex extraction points in this file from `buildImportRecords(fields, rows)` to the new `buildImportRecords(fields, rows, relatedRecords)` signature (none of those existing call sites actually exercise a relation field, so none needed any other change). Regression-proofed both: reverting each language's new resolution block back to a bare `continue` reproduced the exact expected failure (a dropped `courierId` field in the live-preview test; the identical missing-`courierId` mismatch in the codegen test), then passed clean once restored.

**Verification**: both regression-proof reverts failed with their exact expected mismatch, then passed clean once each fix was restored, alongside all pre-existing `buildImportRecords` tests in both files (28/28 in `entityFormatting.test.ts`'s isolated relation-adjacent run; 24/24 in `codegen.test.ts`'s isolated CSV-import/relation run). `npx tsc -b` clean for `apps/web`. Both workspaces changed this round, so both full suites were run: `@forge/web` 1015/1015 clean (1010 baseline + 5 new); `@forge/api` 636/636 clean (635 baseline + 1 new). Full `npm run build` clean for both workspaces. Commit `9cd014b`.

### Round 713: Global Search ignored the user's own drag/keyboard-reordered entity-tab order, in both the live preview and the exported app

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real consistency bug (round 713's survey explicitly steered away from re-proposing another topbar badge, Templates Gallery, or CSV/relation work) -- the same "ignores the user's own reorder" gap class this routine has repeatedly found and fixed for `columnOrder.ts`'s sibling field-order preference (filter dropdowns, group-by, bulk-edit, CSV/ICS export across rounds 678-694), but never checked for `entityTabOrder.ts`'s own consumers beyond the tab bar itself.

**The gap**: `apps/web/src/App.tsx` maintains a per-project, drag-and-drop + keyboard-reorderable entity-tab order (`entityTabOrder.ts`, `orderedEntities = useMemo(() => applyColumnOrder(project.spec.entities, entityTabOrder), ...)`), which the tab bar itself renders. But `<GlobalSearchPanel>`'s `entities` prop was wired to the raw, un-reordered `project.spec.entities` instead of `orderedEntities`. Inside `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`, `runSearch` builds its `results` array via `entities.map(...)` in prop order, and that same order drives both the on-screen result-group order and arrow-key group navigation (`data-group-index`) -- so a user who deliberately dragged, say, "Customers" to the top of their entity tabs still saw Global Search list it wherever it happened to fall in the original spec/build order. Confirmed via grep that `entityTabOrder`/`getEntityTabOrder` has exactly one real consumer in `apps/web/src/*.tsx|*.ts` (App.tsx's own `orderedEntities` memo) -- Global Search was never wired to it at all. Confirmed Business Twin's own entity ordering is a deliberate record-count ranking (`sortTwinStatsByCount`), not an instance of this same gap.

**The fix**: one-line change -- `entities={project.spec.entities}` to `entities={orderedEntities}` in `App.tsx`'s `<GlobalSearchPanel>` call site -- plus an explanatory comment. No change needed inside `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`/`searchReport.ts` (Copy/Download report), since they already just consume whatever `entities` array they're given, in order.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed required and ported -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own generated `App.jsx` has the byte-for-byte identical structure (`orderedEntities = useMemo(() => applyEntityTabOrder(ENTITIES, entityTabOrder), ...)` feeding its own entity-tab bar) and the identical bug: `<GlobalSearch entities={ENTITIES} ...>` instead of `entities={orderedEntities}`. Fixed the same one-line way, plus a matching comment.

**The tests**: `App.test.ts` -- 1 new test extracting the real `<GlobalSearchPanel ... />` JSX call site from `App.tsx`'s source and confirming it reads `entities={orderedEntities}`, not `entities={project.spec.entities}`. `codegen.test.ts` -- 1 new test generating a real export and extracting the real `<GlobalSearch ... />` call site from the generated `App.jsx`, confirming the same `entities={orderedEntities}` (not `entities={ENTITIES}`). Regression-proofed both by reverting each fix back to the original prop value: both tests failed with the exact expected mismatch (the full un-matched JSX block printed in the assertion diff), then passed clean once restored, alongside each file's adjacent `entityTabOrder`/`GlobalSearch` tests (3/3 in `App.test.ts`'s isolated run; 19/19 in `codegen.test.ts`'s isolated GlobalSearch run).

### Round 714: the Automations "field equals a value" trigger forced a relation field's value to be typed as a raw, never-shown internal id

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible feature, extensively pre-documented as deliberately left open across three earlier rounds (616, 667, 668) but never picked back up until this round's survey re-confirmed it was still true at HEAD.

**The gap**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s `field_equals` trigger lets a user pick any field on the entity as the condition, including a `relation`-type field, but the "Value" control only had type-aware branches for `boolean` (round 668's checkbox) and `enum` (round 668's `<select>`) -- a relation field fell through to the same plain free-text input every OTHER type gets. The server's own `validateAutomationFieldValue` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) only accepts the related record's raw, internal foreign-key integer id there, with its own error message literally telling the user to type something no UI surface in this entire app ever shows them (every other relation render -- the add/edit form's picker, table cells, CSV export -- uses `relationDisplayLabel`, never the bare id). The mirror-image half of the gap: `fieldValueLabel` (used by both the rule list and, in an independently-maintained duplicate, `automationsReport.ts`'s Copy/Download report) only special-cased `enum`, so an existing relation-based rule displayed back as a bare, meaningless number.

The Value control now renders a real `<select>` of the target entity's own records (label via `recordDisplayLabel`, same as every other relation surface), with a loading state while the fetch is in flight, defaulting to the first record once loaded (mirroring the existing boolean/enum default-value effect). ### Round 715: an existing enum/relation field's own value list or target couldn't be edited at all on the spec-review screen -- only a brand-new field or a lossy type-switch roundtrip

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible feature closing the last gap in the field-correction family rounds 675/676 opened (label, required, type all got real fix paths then; this one slipped through because it only shows up for a field that's ALREADY enum/relation, a case those rounds' own tests never exercised).

**The gap**: `FieldChip`'s (`apps/web/src/SpecListItemRemover.tsx`) type `<select>` only opens the enum-values/relation-target editor when `handleTypeSelectChange` is called with a type *different* from the field's current one. A native `<select>` never fires `onChange` for its own already-selected option, so there was no way to re-open that editor for a field that's already "enum" or "relation" -- the only way in was switching to a different type first. But the server's own `/type` route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) deliberately wipes `enumValues`/`relationTo` the instant the type changes away (so a stale value doesn't linger on a field whose new type no longer calls for it) -- so switching away and back doesn't recover the original list either; the UI's own re-prefill reads a value the first PATCH had already erased server-side. Net effect: an AI/heuristic-proposed enum field that merely needed one option renamed, added, or removed, or a relation field whose target needed to change, had no fix path at all short of delete-and-recreate (losing the field's position).

**The fix**: extracted the enum/relation draft-opening logic (prefilling `draftEnumValues`/`draftRelationTo` from the field's own current values) into a shared `openDraftFor` helper, reused by both the type-switch path and a new small edit button rendered next to the type select whenever the field is already "enum" or "relation" and no draft is currently open. Clicking it opens the exact same draft confirm form the type-switch path already renders, pre-filled from the field's own current values. Submitting PATCHes the field's own *unchanged* type alongside the edited values -- verified the server's `/type` route places no restriction on a same-type PATCH at all, so no backend change was needed.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the entire spec-review/field-correction screen (and every route behind it) is a pre-build, live-Forge-AI-only concept that 409s with `FIELD_EDIT_AFTER_BUILD` once a project is built; `codegen.ts` only generates code for an already-built project and has no spec-editing UI at all (grepped for `FieldChip`/`SetFieldType` in `codegen.ts`, zero matches, consistent with rounds 675/676's own confirmation for this same feature family).

**The tests**: `SpecListItemRemover.test.ts` -- 3 new tests: a plain (non-enum/relation) field shows no edit button at all (nothing to edit); an existing enum field's edit button opens the draft pre-filled with its current comma-joined `enumValues`, and submitting an edited list PATCHes the field's own unchanged `type` alongside the new values; an existing relation field's edit button opens the draft pre-filled with its current `relationTo`, and submitting a new target PATCHes the same way. Regression-proofed by disabling the new button's render condition (`{false && ...}`): both the enum and relation tests failed with the exact expected "expected an edit-values/edit-target button" assertion failure, then passed clean once restored, alongside the full pre-existing 45-test suite (no regressions, including the pre-existing readOnly-mode test, which returns before reaching the new button entirely).

**Verification**: the regression-proof revert failed with the exact expected assertion failure on both new tests, then passed clean once restored, alongside the full pre-existing `SpecListItemRemover.test.ts` suite (45/45, isolated run) and all 20 `language.test.ts` tests (i18n parity for the two new keys confirmed automatically). `npx tsc -b` clean. ### Round 716: forgot-password was a dead end -- a locked-out user had no way back into their own account

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible feature: a full forgot-password / reset-password flow, closing a gap previously ruled out (`docs/roadmap.md` rounds 252/254) specifically because there was zero email-sending infrastructure anywhere in the backend at the time. That blocker no longer holds -- a later commit (`b816081`) added `apps/api/src/email.ts`'s `EmailSender`/`ResendEmailSender` plus the 2FA login-code pattern (`packages/db/src/loginCodes.ts`), both still live and exercised by every login today. Verified this directly by reading `email.ts`, `loginCodes.ts`, `store.ts`, `app.ts`'s wiring, and `app.test.ts`'s `createFakeEmailSender` test infrastructure before writing anything.

**The gap**: `AuthScreen.tsx` had a login form and a signup form, and that was the entire account-recovery surface. A user who forgot their password had no self-service path back in at all -- the only option was contacting support directly, and the login form's own password field gave no hint that recovery was even possible.

**The fix**: `POST /auth/forgot-password` always returns the identical `{sent: true}` / 200 whether or not the email matches a real account (mirrors `/auth/login`'s own established "never a different status/body for a nonexistent account" anti-enumeration rule), emails a one-time reset link when it does match, and returns a clear `EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED` error (503) if no `EmailSender` is configured on this deployment, rather than silently no-opping. `POST /auth/reset-password` looks up the token by its SHA-256 hash (new `packages/db/src/passwordResetTokens.ts` table, mirroring `loginCodes.ts`'s hash-only/TTL/lazy-prune pattern, deliberately simplified -- no `attempts` column and lookup by hash directly rather than by a separate opaque id, since a 256-bit random reset token has no brute-force surface worth rate-limiting the way a 6-digit login code does), rejects an expired or unknown token with `RESET_TOKEN_INVALID` (401), and on success updates the password and revokes *every* existing session for the account via `deleteAllSessionsForUser` -- unlike the current-password-authenticated `PATCH /auth/password` (which keeps the requesting session alive and revokes only the others), there is no session worth preserving here: the entire premise of this flow is "I may have lost control of this account." The reset link itself is built from `req.protocol`/`req.get("host")` (relying on the already-configured `trust proxy` setting) rather than a new environment variable, since this app serves its own frontend from the same origin as its API. `AuthScreen.tsx` gained a "Forgot password?" link (shown only in login mode), a request-link form, and a reset-password form that renders automatically when the URL carries `?resetToken=...` from the emailed link, with a "Go to login" action that clears the query string afterward.

One deliberate, documented scope decision: did *not* add a timing-side-channel defense comparable to `/auth/login`'s `dummyPasswordHashPromise` for the enumeration-safe `/auth/forgot-password` response, since the asymmetry here is a genuine network email-send await with no cheap, risk-free dummy equivalent -- a smaller, harder-to-exploit residual risk than the primary status/body enumeration vector, which *is* fully defended against.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- grepped `codegen.ts` for `AuthScreen`/`login`/`signup`/`auth/password`/`forgot`; the exported standalone app has no multi-user auth/session system at all (single-tenant), consistent with every prior round's findings on this exact scope boundary.

**The tests**: backend -- `packages/db/src/passwordResetTokens.test.ts` (6 new tests mirroring `loginCodes.test.ts`: insert+read-back by hash, undefined for an unknown hash, delete-only-own-row, delete-for-user leaves others alone, prune-expired-only, create-opportunistically-prunes-another-user's-expired-row) and `apps/api/src/app.test.ts` (5 new integration tests: the full happy path -- signup, a second real session via the actual login-code verify flow, forgot-password, extracting the reset link out of the fake email sender, reset-password, then confirming both old sessions 401, the old password 401, the new password 200, and the now-reused token 401 `RESET_TOKEN_INVALID`; the no-such-account case returns the identical generic response and sends zero email; the no-`EmailSender`-configured case returns `EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED`; a garbage token and a directly-inserted expired token both get `RESET_TOKEN_INVALID`; and requesting a fresh token invalidates the previous one). Regression-proofed with three separate revert/restore cycles (session revocation, token expiry check, enumeration-safety), each failing with the exact expected assertion message before being restored. Frontend -- `apps/web/src/AuthScreen.test.ts` gained 3 new tests (the link only shows in login mode and submitting calls the real endpoint; the URL's `resetToken` renders the reset form, submits to the real endpoint, and "Go to login" clears the URL; a mismatched confirmation is rejected client-side with zero requests sent), regression-proofed the same way. Hit and fixed a genuine test-runner hang while writing these: `assert.equal(domElement, null)` directly compares a DOM node against `null` via Node's deep-equality algorithm, and when the element actually exists (the assertion should fail), it can hang the runner entirely rather than failing fast -- confirmed via an actual ~102-second hang ending in SIGKILL during this round's own regression-proofing. Fixed by converting all new occurrences to `assert.equal(domElement === null, true, ...)`. This is a previously-documented lesson in this routine's own accumulated knowledge, freshly re-triggered by new code in this exact round -- worth restating because it clearly isn't enough to have documented it once.

**Verification**: all three regression-proof revert/restore cycles on the backend, and both on the frontend, failed with their exact expected assertion messages before being restored clean. i18n: all 20 `language.test.ts` tests passed (he/en key parity plus real `t(...)` call-site coverage for every new key). `npx tsc -b` clean in `apps/web`. All three changed workspaces' full suites ran clean: `packages/db` 209/209; `apps/api` 641/642 (the one failure, `password.test.ts`'s concurrent-hashing timing test, is pre-existing and unrelated to this round -- confirmed a flake by re-running it in isolation, where it passed at 118ms, well under its threshold; it only fails under full-suite CPU contention from the other 641 tests); `apps/web` 1023/1024 (the one failure, `BuildProgress.test.ts`'s `onComplete` timing test, is likewise pre-existing, unrelated, and confirmed a flake the same way: 32/32 clean in isolation). `npm run build` clean for the full monorepo. Commit `b10d2ad`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 717: the exported/standalone app had zero support for the "file" field type -- every other surface of this codebase already had it

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug: the exported app's own generated `EntityView.jsx` (`apps/api/src/codegen.ts`) was the one place in this entire codebase that never got the "file" field type's display/editing fix, ever since that field type was introduced (`807333d`). The live Forge AI preview's `entityFormatting.ts` and the backup ZIP's own CSV export (`apps/api/src/backup.ts`) both already parse a file field's stored JSON descriptor and show just the filename -- but grepping `codegen.ts` for any "file" handling turned up nothing except an unrelated CSV-upload `<input type="file">`, confirmed directly by reading `isInlineEditableField`, `Cell`, `matchesSearch`, `fieldDisplayValue`, `FieldInput`, and `buildImportRecords` one at a time before writing anything.

**The gap**: a `file` field's stored value is a JSON-encoded `{url, name, size, mimeType}` descriptor (set by the live preview's own upload endpoint), not a plain string like every other field type. In any app exported via "Export code": the table/record-detail cell (`Cell`) and the "Export CSV" button (`fieldDisplayValue`) both dumped this raw JSON text instead of just the filename; double-clicking a file cell was inline-editable as free text (`isInlineEditableField` had no exclusion for it, unlike relation), silently corrupting the stored descriptor -- and the same field also showed up, editable the same corrupting way, in the bulk-edit dropdown, since that list is derived from `isInlineEditableField` too; the add/edit form's `FieldInput` fell through to a plain `<input type="text">`, letting a user "satisfy" a required file field by typing arbitrary text that was never a real file (there's no upload endpoint in the exported app to attach one with); a CSV import cell could overwrite an existing attachment with typed garbage, or, for a required file field, reject importing an otherwise-valid row entirely since no CSV cell could ever supply a real file; and `matchesSearch` both over-matched (a mimetype or the raw URL, neither shown on screen, matched) and under-matched (a filename with a quote or backslash is JSON-escaped in the raw stored string) on this field type.

**The fix**: ported `parseFileFieldValue`/`isImageMimeType` (mirroring `entityFormatting.ts`) into `codegen.ts`, and wired them into all six functions above: `isInlineEditableField` now excludes "file" the same way it already excludes "relation"; `Cell` renders a real clickable link (with an image thumbnail when the mimetype allows it, matching the live preview exactly); `matchesSearch` matches against just the filename; `fieldDisplayValue` exports just the filename to CSV; `buildImportRecords` skips a file column's cell entirely, required or not (there's no CSV cell that could ever supply a real file, so this can never block an otherwise-valid row); and `FieldInput` shows an existing attachment as a plain link with no editable control at all -- not a fake `<input type="text">` masquerading as something it can't do, since there's no upload backend in the exported app to wire a real file picker to. Also ported the live preview's own `.file-cell-link`/`.file-cell-name`/`.file-cell-thumbnail`/`.file-field-input`/`.file-field-current` CSS classes into the exported app's generated stylesheet, so the new markup isn't unstyled.

One deliberate, documented scope decision: a required file field is still structurally impossible to satisfy when creating a *new* record in the exported app (the server's own create/update route throws "field is required" with nothing able to fill it) -- but this was already true before this fix, just reachable via a different, actively worse path (typing fake JSON text that happened to parse). Removing that loophole is the point of the fix, not a new regression; genuinely wiring up file uploads in an exported app (its own upload endpoint, storage, etc.) is a separate, much larger feature this round didn't attempt.

**The tests**: `codegen.test.ts` -- updated the existing `isInlineEditableField` test to also assert "file" is now excluded (previously only checked every type *except* relation was `true`, so it never caught this gap at all), and added three new tests, all running the real generated code (not reimplementations): one exercising the real generated `Cell`/`matchesSearch`/`fieldDisplayValue` together against a real file-descriptor value (search finds the filename but not the raw URL or mimetype; the CSV export shows just the filename; the table cell links straight to the real file); one for `buildImportRecords` confirming a required file column never blocks an import and the cell's raw text is never written into the record; and one for `FieldInput` confirming the file branch has no `type="text"` or `type="file"` input at all, just a link to the existing attachment (or nothing, with no leakage between calls). Regression-proofed with five separate revert/restore cycles (one per fixed function, `isInlineEditableField`/`Cell`/`matchesSearch`/`fieldDisplayValue`/`buildImportRecords`'s CSV skip/`FieldInput`), each failing with its exact expected message before being restored -- one of them (`Cell`) surfaced as a `ReferenceError: LinkifiedText is not defined` rather than a plain assertion failure, since disabling the branch made it fall through to the exact same raw-JSON-through-plain-text path the fix targets; accepted as valid confirmation per this routine's own "module-load crash = strong confirmation" convention. Also caught and fixed a real gap in my own first draft: the `fieldDisplayValue` portion of the combined test initially reimplemented the function inline instead of extracting the real generated one via regex, which would have kept passing even if the real fix were wrong -- fixed before regression-proofing it.

**Verification**: all five regression-proof revert/restore cycles failed with their exact expected messages, then passed clean once restored. `apps/api`'s full suite ran clean: 645/645 (642 baseline + 3 new tests; the existing `isInlineEditableField` test was extended in place, not counted as new). `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api` clean. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so `packages/db`/`apps/web` weren't re-run. Commit `397e436`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 718: Global Search's entity-group results were ordered by spec declaration order, not by relevance

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug: Global Search's own results panel -- in both the live preview and the exported standalone app -- showed its per-entity result groups in whatever order the project's entities happened to be declared in the spec, with zero regard to how many matches each entity actually had.

**The gap**: `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s `runSearch` (and the exported app's identical `searchAllEntities` in `codegen.ts`) built the results array via `entities.map(entity => searchEntityRecords(...)).filter(...)` -- the per-entity groups came out in `entities` array order, straight from the project spec. An entity with a single coincidental match could sit above an entity with fifty real matches, purely because it happens to be declared first in the spec. Confirmed this wasn't an intentional design choice: there's no comment or test anywhere in either file treating declaration order as meaningful for search relevance, in sharp contrast to almost every other ordering decision in this codebase, which is heavily commented when deliberate.

**The fix**: sorts the already-filtered, already-deduplicated results array by `totalMatches` descending, right before `setResults` in the live preview and right before `searchAllEntities` returns in the exported app. `Array.prototype.sort` has been spec-guaranteed stable since ES2019, so two entities tied on `totalMatches` keep their original declared order rather than visibly reshuffling between identical searches for no reason. Verified this needed no other changes in either file: `selectedIndex`/`data-group-index` are reset to `null` right after `setResults` on every new search, so there's no stale index pointing at the wrong row after reordering; and `handleShowAll` (the "Show N more" expansion) keys its update off `entityName` via `.map((r) => r.entityName === entityName ? ... : r)`, never off array position, so it stays correct regardless of where that entity's group now sits.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed needed and done in the same round -- `GlobalSearch.jsx`'s own `searchAllEntities` (generated by `codegen.ts`) is a deliberate duplicate of the live preview's `runSearch`, down to the same `results[selectedIndex]`/`data-group-index={i}` index-based rendering pattern, so the identical fix applies identically there.

**The tests**: one new test per file, both running the real extracted function (not a reimplementation) via this file's own established `transformSync` + `new Function` pattern: `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` declares three entities in ascending-match order (Alpha: 1 match, Beta: 5, Gamma: 50) and asserts the real `runSearch` returns them as `["Gamma", "Beta", "Alpha"]`; `codegen.test.ts` does the identical check against the real generated `searchAllEntities`/`runSearch`. Regression-proofed by commenting out each file's own `.sort(...)` call: both failed with the exact same wrong order (`["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"]`, the untouched declaration order) before being restored clean.

**Verification**: both regression-proof revert/restore cycles failed with their exact expected (wrong) order before being restored clean. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran: `apps/api` 646/646; `apps/web` 1025/1025 (no flake this run). `npm run build` clean for the full monorepo. Commit `baae495`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 719: every scrollIntoView call ignored prefers-reduced-motion, in both the live preview and the exported app

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real accessibility bug: every single `scrollIntoView` call in this codebase passed `behavior: "smooth"` unconditionally, firing a real scroll animation on every keypress and click regardless of whether the person has their OS/browser explicitly set to "prefers-reduced-motion: reduce" -- the exact WCAG 2.3.3 "animation triggered by user interaction" case this app's own CSS already treats as real.

**The gap**: this app already disables its one CSS keyframe animation (the home-screen hero cube, `styles.css`'s `.hero3d-cube`) under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, with a comment explaining the rationale -- real, deliberate precedent for taking motion sensitivity seriously. But grepping for `scrollIntoView` turned up 6 call sites in the live preview (`EntityPanel.tsx`'s highlighted-row/focused-row effects and its "n"/calendar-day/board-column create-new shortcuts, `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s arrow-key result navigation) and 4 more in the exported app's own duplicate logic (`codegen.ts`'s `EntityView.jsx`/`GlobalSearch.jsx`), none of which ever checked `matchMedia`. A `behavior: "smooth"` passed directly as a JS option to `scrollIntoView` isn't something the CSS media query can intercept at all -- that only affects an element's inherited `scroll-behavior`, not an explicit call like this -- so each site needed its own check, and none had one (confirmed via `window.matchMedia` only ever being read in `ThemeContext.tsx` for color scheme, never for motion).

**The fix**: added a shared `scrollIntoViewRespectingMotion(el, options)` helper to `entityFormatting.ts` that reads `window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")` once per call and substitutes `behavior: "auto"` when it matches, then swapped all 6 live-preview call sites to use it -- a one-line change per site, no other behavior change. Ported the identical fix into `codegen.ts`: added the same helper to `EntityView.jsx` (exported, alongside `isInlineEditableField`/`enterTargetsInteractiveElement`) and imported it into `GlobalSearch.jsx` the same way that file already imports `matchesSearch`/`recordDisplayLabel` from `EntityView.jsx`, then swapped its 4 call sites too.

**The tests**: `entityFormatting.test.ts` gained 3 new tests for the helper itself (substitutes `"auto"` when reduced motion is set; leaves `"smooth"` alone otherwise; does nothing for a null/undefined/scrollIntoView-less element) -- this file runs in plain Node with no jsdom, so `window` is stubbed directly for each test's duration rather than standing up a full `JSDOM` instance. `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` gained one true end-to-end integration test: stubs `window.matchMedia` (satisfying both this test's own check and `ThemeProvider`'s own separate `matchMedia` call, which the first stub attempt missed and crashed on `addEventListener` not being a function -- fixed by making the stub a real, if inert, `MediaQueryList`-shaped object), fires a real `ArrowDown` keypress through the rendered component, and confirms the real captured `scrollIntoView` call received `behavior: "auto"`. `codegen.test.ts` gained 2 new tests: one running the real generated `scrollIntoViewRespectingMotion` directly, and one confirming all 4 real call sites route through it rather than calling the DOM method directly (checked against each site's specific old call pattern, not a blanket "no `.scrollIntoView(`" scan, which would have also flagged the helper's own, necessary internal call).

Fixing the real call sites broke 3 pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` tests that literally regex-matched the old source text (`GlobalSearch.jsx`'s import list, and the old direct `group.scrollIntoView(...)` call) -- all three updated in place to match the new, equally-real generated output, per this routine's own "existing literal test broken by a valid fix" convention.

**Verification**: all regression-proof revert/restore cycles -- the helper's own logic (both files), one live call-site wiring, and one exported-app call-site wiring -- failed with their exact expected messages before being restored clean. The combined `entityFormatting.test.ts`/`GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts`/`EntityPanel.test.ts` run was clean at 352/352 before the full-suite runs. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran: `apps/api` 648/648; `apps/web` 1029/1029. `npm run build` clean for the full monorepo. Commit `f73d2cc`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 720: the calendar view had no way to jump to a specific month/year, only ±1-month prev/next navigation

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible feature: a calendar view month/year picker, carried over from an earlier round's survey and independently re-verified before implementing.

**The gap**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `CalendarView` component navigated strictly via `onPrevMonth`/`onNextMonth` (±1 month) plus a "Today" button -- the month label itself (`<span className="calendar-month-label">{monthLabel}</span>`) was static, inert text. Reaching a date more than a couple of months away (a rental due in 11 months, a historical record from 2 years back) meant clicking the chevron that many times, one month at a time. `setCalendarMonth` (the state both the chevrons and "Today" already call) already accepted any `Date`, so this was purely a missing UI affordance, not a data-model gap. Confirmed the identical gap exists verbatim in the exported standalone app's own duplicate `CalendarView` in `codegen.ts` (same static month-label span, same prev/next/today-only nav).

**The fix**: the month label is now a `<button>` that reveals a native `<input type="month">`, seeded with the currently-shown month; picking a value calls a new `onJumpToMonth(date)` prop (wired to `setCalendarMonth` at the real call site, same as the chevrons) and closes the picker back to the plain label. Added a matching `.calendar-month-label`/`.calendar-month-input` CSS pair (the label keeps its existing font-weight/min-width/text-align but drops default button chrome, mirroring `.sort-header`'s own "looks like text, acts like a button" convention) and one new i18n key (`entity.calendar.jumpToMonth`, used as the button's `aria-label`). Ported the identical fix to `codegen.ts`'s own `CalendarView` (no i18n there, so the aria-label is hardcoded English, matching that file's existing all-English convention).

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one new real-DOM test: clicking the label reveals the month input seeded with the current month, picking a year-ahead value jumps the whole calendar there directly (not one month at a time, confirmed via the rendered month label text), and the picker closes itself afterward. Fixing the real call sites broke 2 pre-existing tests that located the "next month" button by a now-stale positional index (`.calendar-nav button` at index 2, which used to be "next" when the label was a plain `<span>` and shifted to the new label button once it became a `<button>` too) -- both updated to select by `aria-label` instead, a more robust selector that won't break again if another button is added. `codegen.test.ts` gained one new test confirming the generated `CalendarView`'s wiring (the open-picker click handler, the native month input, the real `onJumpToMonth` call, the picker closing itself, and the real call site's `setCalendarMonth` wiring) -- which also broke one pre-existing test (`calendarViewSource`'s fixed-offset text slice no longer reached the "Today button" markup it checks, since the new code pushed it further into the function) fixed by widening the slice window from 2000 to 3500 characters.

### Round 721: a relation field had no per-field filter dropdown, only the free-text search box

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible feature, carried over from an earlier round's survey: a relation field can now be filtered to an exact related record, not just substring-matched through free-text search.

**The gap**: `findFilterableFields` (`entityFormatting.ts`) only ever returned enum and boolean fields for EntityPanel's own per-field filter dropdown toolbar -- a relation field (e.g. filtering "Orders" by "Customer") is just as fixed-value-space as an enum (its options are exactly the related entity's current records), but got no exact-match filter at all. The only way to narrow by a relation was the free-text search box, which matches a relation's *resolved display label* as a substring -- unable to target "exactly this customer" the way an equality filter does, and prone to over-matching any other field whose text happens to contain the same substring. Confirmed the identical gap in `codegen.ts`'s own duplicate `findFilterableFields`.

**The fix**: extended `findFilterableFields(fields, allEntities?, relatedRecords?)` to also include a relation field, but only once `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` confirm it actually resolves to a loaded set of records for a still-existing target entity -- the same "resolvable" guard `buildImportRecords`/`FieldInput` already use elsewhere in this file, so a stale `relationTo` pointing at a deleted entity, or data that hasn't finished loading yet, is correctly excluded rather than offering a filter with nothing real to pick. `EntityPanel.tsx`'s filter `<select>` gained a `f.type === "relation"` branch rendering one `<option>` per related record via the existing `recordDisplayLabel` helper (the exact same label the table cell/search already resolve to), with the option's `value` being the plain numeric id as a string -- the existing `fieldFilters` equality match (`String(r[fieldName] ?? "") === value`) needed zero changes, since a relation's raw stored value is already that same numeric id. Ported the identical fix to `codegen.ts`'s own `findFilterableFields` and its filter-dropdown JSX (referencing `ALL_ENTITIES` directly rather than taking it as a parameter, matching that file's own existing convention for `relationResolvable`).

**The tests**: `entityFormatting.test.ts` gained one new test on the real `findFilterableFields`, covering all three resolvability cases (no `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` at all; target entity known but its records not yet loaded; and the related entity deleted even though stale `relatedRecords` for it happen to still be present) plus the happy path. `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one real-DOM test: an Order entity with a `courierId` relation field and two couriers, confirming the filter dropdown's options show the couriers' real names (not raw ids), picking one narrows the table to exactly that courier's orders, and clearing it restores the rest. `codegen.test.ts` gained one new test running the real generated `findFilterableFields` directly, plus a source-regex check that the option-rendering branch resolves each label via `recordDisplayLabel` rather than a raw id; fixing the real call site also broke 2 pre-existing tests that regex-matched the old one-argument signature and call text -- both updated to match the new, equally-valid two-argument generated output.

**Verification**: all regression-proof cycles -- the live-app call-site wiring (via real rendered-DOM behavior, confirmed bounded/fast at 104ms, not a hang) and two separate codegen.ts cycles (the call-site wiring, caught incidentally by an already-updated pre-existing test; and the option-rendering branch, caught by the new test) -- failed with their exact expected messages before being restored clean. ### Round 722: losing access to the currently-open project mid-session was never surfaced as "you're out" -- only as a dead-end, repeating 404

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug: `requireProjectAccess`/`requireProjectOwner` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) already throw a distinct, unambiguous `PROJECT_NOT_FOUND` 404 whenever a project was deleted or this account's own collaborator access to it was just revoked -- the server-side half of this was already solid. But the client never did anything with that signal beyond showing that one request's own translated inline error text.

**The gap**: if an owner removed a collaborator (or deleted the project) while that collaborator still had it open in another tab, every subsequent action there -- a background refresh, any mutation -- 404ed the exact same way forever, with the whole project shell (tabs, now-stale records) still rendered and no path back to the project list. `api.ts` already has a precedent for exactly this class of problem: `subscribeAuthExpired`, a pub/sub `request()` fires into whenever a 401 `SESSION_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_REQUIRED` comes back, which `App.tsx` uses to force a clean reset to the login screen the instant ANY request reports the session is gone, instead of leaving `user` set and the authenticated UI rendering with a now-dead token. `PROJECT_NOT_FOUND` had no equivalent.

**The fix**: added a narrower `subscribeProjectGone(projectId, message)` pub/sub mirroring `subscribeAuthExpired` exactly. `request()` now parses the project id straight out of the request path (every project-scoped route is `/projects/:id/...`) and notifies with it plus the already-translated error message whenever it sees `PROJECT_NOT_FOUND`. `App.tsx` subscribes and, only when the reported id matches the project *currently open* (never for some unrelated/stale notification -- there shouldn't be one, since only one project is ever open at a time, but the check costs nothing and matches the defensive style this file already uses elsewhere), purges that project's own client-side preferences and resets to the home screen via the exact same `handleGoHome` `CollaboratorsPanel`'s own self-service "leave project" flow already calls -- then surfaces the real message as the app's one generic error banner, so the person actually sees *why* they were sent home instead of just silently landing on the project list.

Deliberately scoped to the generic `request()` helper, which covers the large majority of project-scoped calls (`listRecords`, every create/update/delete mutation, etc.) -- four other, rarer special-purpose fetch wrappers in the same file (`streamPipeline` for build/refine, `downloadBlob` for export/backup, the file-upload function, `sendWhatsAppMessage`) each do their own local 401-handling already and were left out of this round's scope; a genuine follow-up if the same "stuck on a 404 forever" shape turns out to matter there too.

**The tests**: `api.test.ts` gained 3 new tests mirroring `subscribeAuthExpired`'s own existing coverage exactly: the listener fires with the real project id and translated message on a 404 `PROJECT_NOT_FOUND`; it never fires for an unrelated 404 (e.g. a deleted entity, `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`); and its returned unsubscribe function actually stops delivery. `App.test.ts` gained one test extracting the real effect via regex (the same "run the real generated/written code" technique this file's own `subscribeAuthExpired` effect test already uses) and confirming both halves of the guard: a notification for a *different* project than the one open is ignored entirely (no purge, no reset), and one for the currently-open project purges its preferences, calls the real `handleGoHome`, and sets the error banner to the real translated message.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles on the `App.tsx` effect -- removing the guard check (confirms the "ignore mismatched project" assertion actually depends on it, per this routine's own "a fix that extends a filter needs its happy-path tested too, not just the guard" lesson) and separately removing the `handleGoHome()` call (confirms the "reset on match" assertion is real) -- each failed with its exact expected message before being restored clean, plus one on `api.ts`'s own code-string match in `request()`. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its full suite ran clean: 1036/1036 (no flake this run). `npm run build --workspace=@forge/web` clean. Commit `3588ae6`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 723: no keyboard shortcut existed to undo a delete, the one gap left in an otherwise keyboard-first flow

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible feature, carried over from an earlier round's survey and independently re-verified before implementing: Ctrl/Cmd+Z now triggers the delete-undo toast's own "Undo" action.

**The gap**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s keyboard shortcut layer already bound j/k (row navigation), Enter (edit), x (toggle select), n (new record), Delete/Backspace (delete), d (duplicate), and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter (submit) -- every one of `handleDelete`'s own undo-toast actions was reachable by keyboard except the single most relevant one to a keyboard-only user: undoing the delete they just made with that same keyboard. The toast's "Undo" link (calling `handleUndoDelete`, which already safely no-ops via `pendingDeleteRef` when nothing is pending) existed only as a mouse target. Confirmed via grep that no `"z"`/ctrlKey+Z handling existed anywhere in the file, and that the identical gap exists in the exported standalone app's own duplicate `EntityView.jsx` (`codegen.ts`), which has the exact same `pendingDeleteRef`/`handleUndoDelete` structure.

**The fix**: a new, separate `useEffect` in `EntityPanel.tsx` (the main j/k/x/d/Escape keydown effect has a blanket `if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;` early-return from round 653, specifically added to stop its own bare-letter keys from firing under a held modifier -- making it impossible to add a Ctrl+Z branch to that same effect without restructuring it, so a wholly independent listener was added instead, following the file's own existing pattern of several independent keydown-listener effects coexisting, e.g. the separate "n" effect). The new effect matches `(e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === "z" && !e.shiftKey`, guarded by the same `isTypingTarget`/`isAnyDialogOpen` checks every shortcut here already uses, and deliberately excludes `e.shiftKey` since Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z is the near-universal OS/app convention for Redo -- an action this app has none of, so claiming that chord too would silently eat a gesture aimed at a nonexistent feature. Deliberately NOT scoped to `viewMode === "table"` (unlike the main j/k/x/d effect), since the undo window (`UNDO_WINDOW_MS`, 5 seconds) can still be open after switching to board or calendar view following a delete. Ported the identical fix to `codegen.ts`'s own `EntityView.jsx` (plain JS, no readOnly concept in the exported standalone app at all, so no equivalent guard was needed there). Added the new row (`Ctrl+Z` / "Undo the last delete") to both `ShortcutsPanel.tsx`'s own `SHORTCUTS` array and `EDITOR_ONLY_KEYS` set, and to `codegen.ts`'s hardcoded-English `SHORTCUTS` array, bumping both cheat-sheets from 13 to 14 rows. Also proactively fixed a stale doc comment above `EDITOR_ONLY_KEYS` that cited exact `EntityPanel.tsx` line numbers which had already drifted from earlier insertions this and prior rounds -- rewrote it to describe the readOnly-guard mechanism itself rather than citing fragile line numbers.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one new real-DOM test: deletes a row via the keyboard, confirms Ctrl+Shift+Z does NOT undo it (proving the Redo-chord exclusion is real, not just documented), then confirms Ctrl+Z restores the row at its original index and that the real DELETE request never fires, and that pressing Ctrl+Z again with nothing pending is a safe no-op. `codegen.test.ts` gained the equivalent real-rendered-component test against the generated `EntityView.jsx`. `ShortcutsPanel.test.ts`'s three existing row-count assertions were updated from 13 to 14 (and from "6 remain for a read-only viewer" confirmed unchanged, since undo-delete is itself editor-only); `codegen.test.ts`'s own "renders every one of the live preview's own 13 keyboard-shortcut rows" test was updated to 14 and the new description added to its expected-rows list.

**Verification**: both regression-proof cycles -- genuinely changing the matched key from `"z"` to `"y"` (not commenting out the line, per the round-719 lesson about comment-outs leaving literal text intact) in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts` -- failed with their exact expected messages (`waitForCondition: condition never became true` for the live app's real-DOM test; `Ctrl+Z must restore the deleted row / 1 !== 2` for codegen.ts's) before being restored clean. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran clean: `apps/api` 651/651; `apps/web` 1037/1037 (no flake this run). `npm run build` clean for the full monorepo. Commit `e594744`.

### Round 724: automation_runs grew forever, with no deletion path short of deleting the whole rule or project

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug, independently re-verified before implementing: every single automation-rule firing added a permanent row to `automation_runs` that nothing would ever read again past the most recent 20.

**The gap**: `packages/db/src/automations.ts`'s `recordAutomationRun` does a bare `INSERT INTO automation_runs` on every rule firing (schedule, record_created, field_equals), with no cap and no cleanup. The table's only reader, `listAutomationRuns`, caps itself at `limit = 20` -- its own doc comment already states the design intent ("AutomationsPanel only ever shows 'did this rule recently misbehave,' not a full archival log"), and confirmed via grep that the one real call site (`routes/projects.ts`'s `GET /projects/:id/automations/:ruleId/runs`) never passes a different limit. The only rows ever deleted are via `deleteAutomationRunsForRule`/`deleteAutomationRunsForProject`, fired only when the whole rule or project is destroyed. A long-lived "schedule" rule (a daily WhatsApp reminder) or a busy `record_created`/`field_equals` rule on an active entity accumulates one row per firing forever -- thousands of rows nothing reads again, never deleted either. This table is strictly worse-off than its two siblings with the same "log that only ever grows" shape: `whatsapp_messages` and `checkpoints` each at least got a manual, user-initiated single-row delete (`deleteWhatsAppMessage`, `deleteCheckpoint`); `automation_runs` had no deletion path at all short of destroying the whole rule. Not previously flagged in any prior round's roadmap entry.

**The fix**: `recordAutomationRun` now prunes `automation_runs` down to a new `AUTOMATION_RUNS_RETENTION_LIMIT` (20, matching `listAutomationRuns`'s own default exactly) immediately after every insert, via a `DELETE ... WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id ... ORDER BY triggeredAt DESC, rowid DESC LIMIT 20)` -- the identical `ORDER BY` `listAutomationRuns` itself already uses (including the `rowid DESC` tiebreak for same-millisecond timestamps), so "the rows that survive" and "the rows any current reader would ever see" are provably the same set; pruning can never discard a row anything still reads. No schema change, no transaction needed (this codebase's db layer uses node:sqlite's synchronous API with no transaction wrapping anywhere else either, so a plain sequential second statement is consistent with its existing style). Scoped by `(projectId, ruleId)` in the same WHERE shape every other scoped automation-runs query already uses, so pruning one rule's history can never touch another rule's or another project's.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed NOT needed -- grepped `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` for "automation" and found only one unrelated comment; the exported standalone app has no automations feature at all, so this is a live-preview/server-only concern.

**The tests**: `automations.test.ts` gained one new test that queries the real underlying row count directly via `SELECT COUNT(*)` (bypassing `listAutomationRuns`'s own `LIMIT` entirely, so it can't be fooled by the read path hiding excess rows) after 50 firings of one rule, confirming the real table stays at exactly 20 rows; confirms pruning one rule's history never touches a second rule's single surviving row; and confirms the 20 rows that do survive are the true 20 most recent (not an arbitrary 20), via a direct `triggeredAt`-ordered row count. The existing "caps at its own limit" test already covering 25 firings still passed unchanged -- its assertion (`listAutomationRuns(...,20).length === 20`) remains equally true now for a different underlying reason (only 20 rows exist at all, not merely that the read path stops at 20), so no update was needed, per this routine's own "an existing assertion that's still accurate needs no touching" convention.

**Verification**: regression-proofed by genuinely changing the prune statement's bound parameter from the real `AUTOMATION_RUNS_RETENTION_LIMIT` to a literal `999999` (not commenting out the statement) -- failed with the exact expected message (`the real row count for a busy rule must never exceed the retention cap... 50 !== 20`) before being restored clean and re-confirmed green. Only `packages/db` changed this round; its full suite ran clean both before and after the regression-proof cycle: 210/210. `apps/api`'s own full suite (which also exercises `recordAutomationRun` via `app.test.ts`, well under the new cap at only 2 calls) was run too since it depends on `@forge/db` directly: 651/651 clean. `npm run build` clean for the full monorepo. Commit `a353777`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 725: the exported app's own README told users to "back it up like any file" while deploying it on a plan that wipes it on every redeploy

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible data-loss-risk bug, carried over from an earlier round's survey and independently re-verified before implementing: the generated `README.md` (`apps/api/src/codegen.ts`, shipped inside every exported Forge AI project) told users "the free plan works for this" in its "Deploy it" section and, separately, "`data.sqlite` — your data. Back it up like any file" -- with zero mention that Render's free plan (the one the README itself just recommended) runs on an ephemeral filesystem wiped on every redeploy or restart. "Back it up like any file" actively implies ordinary persistence, the exact opposite of what happens on that plan.

**The gap**: confirmed by direct contrast -- this repo's own root `README.md` already gets this right for the *live* Forge AI app (its own "Notes:" line: "its storage isn't permanent -- a redeploy or restart resets everything back to a fresh start"), but the *generated* README that real end users actually deploy had never been given the same caveat. Checked `codegen.test.ts`'s existing render.yaml/README tests (`generateExportFiles includes a real render.yaml...`) -- they only assert structural Blueprint validity and the presence of a "Deploy it" heading, never the accuracy of the persistence claim, so nothing was locking in the misleading text.

**The fix**: added the same warning the root README already uses, in both of the two places that needed it, in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s README template: a new paragraph right after the "Deploy it" section's existing free-plan mention, explaining the free plan's disk isn't permanent and naming the three real fixes (a persistent Disk in Render's dashboard, one of Render's paid plans that includes one, or an external database); and the `data.sqlite` bullet itself, which keeps its original "back it up like any file" sentence (so a host that genuinely does persist storage isn't told backups are pointless) but now adds "and if you deployed this on Render's free plan, back it up *before* every redeploy or restart, since that plan's disk doesn't survive one." No `render.yaml`/schema change -- this round deliberately scoped to the documentation-accuracy fix rather than also deciding whether to add a paid Disk stanza by default, which would change the generated Blueprint's real deploy cost and needs its own product call.

**codegen.ts parity**: this IS the codegen fix itself -- not applicable in the usual two-file sense, since the live Forge AI app isn't deployed via this generated README at all (the gap only ever existed in the exported copy).

**The tests**: `codegen.test.ts` gained one new test asserting the real generated README contains both warnings' exact substance (the "storage isn't permanent on the free plan" claim, the "redeploy or restart wipes it back to empty" consequence, the "persistent Disk" remedy, and the data.sqlite bullet's own "back it up *before* every redeploy" addition) while still keeping the original "Back it up like any file" sentence intact. Caught one test-authoring mistake immediately via the test's own first run: a regex assumed the "every redeploy or restart" phrase was on one line, but the actual generated text wraps across a literal newline inside the template string -- fixed by widening the regex to `\s+` between the two halves, then re-ran clean.

**Verification**: regression-proofed by genuinely flipping the claim's polarity (changing "isn't permanent" to "is permanent" in the real template, not commenting it out) -- failed with the exact expected message (`The input did not match .../storage isn't permanent on the free plan/i`) and only that one test, before being restored clean. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its full suite ran: 651/652 on the first pass, with one unrelated failure (`a real vite build of the exported app actually serves the manifest...`, an `EADDRINUSE` port collision) confirmed clean in isolation at 241/241 in the same file with zero other process on that port (`ps aux` showed nothing held it once re-checked) -- a known flake shape this routine has hit before (round 720's roadmap entry), not a regression from this round's change. `npm run build --workspace=@forge/api` clean. ### Round 726: a Table-view row selection became a stale, invisible, unreachable "N selected" claim the instant you switched to Board or Calendar view

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, reproducible bug, independently re-verified before implementing: select rows in Table view, switch to Board or Calendar, and the toolbar's Copy/Export-CSV/Print-list buttons permanently show "N selected" with no way to see which records, and no way to clear it short of switching back to Table.

**The gap**: `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` keeps `selectedIds` as view-mode-agnostic top-level state, but the only UI that can ever *set* it -- the per-row checkboxes, the table header's select-all checkbox, and the "x" keyboard shortcut -- lives entirely inside Table view. `BoardCard` and the calendar day cells have no selection checkbox or `selectedIds`-aware styling at all. Meanwhile the toolbar's Copy/Export-CSV/Print-list buttons read `selectedIds` unconditionally in every view mode, switching their own label to "Export N selected" regardless of `viewMode`. The entire bulk-actions bar -- including its own "Clear selection" button -- and the `Escape`-clears-selection keyboard shortcut both live inside a `useEffect`/JSX branch gated on `viewMode === "table"`, so once a selection existed and the user left Table view, there was no way back to empty without switching back first. **The fix**: a new `useEffect` keyed on `[viewMode]` that clears `selectedIds` the instant `viewMode` is no longer `"table"`. This is safe precisely because nothing outside Table view can ever populate `selectedIds` in the first place (confirmed via grep across the whole component: every call to `setSelectedIds`/`toggleSelected`/`toggleSelectAllVisible` is reachable only from Table-view-only code paths), so the fix can never discard a selection the user actually made from a view that's still showing it. This was deliberately scoped narrower than giving Board/Calendar their own selection UI (a larger, more design-laden feature this round didn't attempt) -- since selection is currently a Table-only concept end to end, making it vanish the moment you leave Table keeps the toolbar's own already-unconditional buttons honest without inventing new UI. ### Round 727: board view cards were missing two of the table row's five per-record actions -- Print and Send WhatsApp

Wired the call site to pass `onPrint={() => setRecordToPrint(record)}`, `phoneField`, and `onSendWhatsApp` -- all three already in scope at the component level, reused verbatim from the table row's own wiring. Ported the identical Print-only fix to `codegen.ts`'s exported `BoardCard` (no readOnly concept there at all, so no gating needed; no WhatsApp, since the exported app has none).
