### Round 728: a boolean field's table cell conveyed zero information to a screen reader -- in this app's own UI AND every app it exports for real businesses

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real accessibility bug, independently re-verified before implementing, this time steered deliberately toward a fresh area (accessibility) after four straight rounds of keyboard/db/docs/cross-view-state work.

**The gap**: the shared `Cell` component (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`, used for every table cell, every board card field, and the per-record print sheet) renders every other field type as real text a screen reader can announce -- an enum's own label, a formatted date/number, a relation's resolved label. A boolean field was the one exception: `return value ? <span className="bool-yes">✓</span> : <span className="muted">–</span>;` -- a bare glyph with no `aria-label`, no visually-hidden text, nothing. Unlike this app's decorative icons (the pencil next to `CheckpointLabelEditor`'s own text, correctly `aria-hidden="true"` because real text already sits beside them), this glyph *is* the cell's entire content -- a non-visual user got nothing from it at all. Confirmed via grep that `codegen.ts`'s exported `Cell` (line 1682) has the identical bare-glyph gap, which matters more here than usual: this function reaches every real end user of every app Forge ever exports, not just this app's own authoring UI, for a glyph pattern ("done", "paid", "confirmed", "available") used constantly across the built-in domain templates.

**The fix**: added `aria-label` to both branches -- `t("entity.groupBy.yes")`/`t("entity.groupBy.no")` in the live app, reusing the exact "Yes"/"No" (`"כן"`/`"לא"`) strings the group-by dropdown and column header already translate this value to (no new i18n keys needed). Ported to `codegen.ts`'s `Cell` with hardcoded English `"Yes"`/`"No"` -- confirmed via grep that the enclosing generator function (`renderEntityViewJsx`) has zero hebrew-conditional text anywhere, so hardcoded English matches this generated app's own established all-English convention rather than introducing an unprecedented per-language branch for just this one string.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed needed and done in the same round -- arguably the more important half, since it's the copy real end users actually see.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one new real-DOM test on the existing `TASK_WITH_BOOLEAN_ENTITY` fixture, confirming the true cell's `✓` span carries `aria-label="Yes"` and the false cell's `–` span carries `aria-label="No"` -- not just that the glyphs still render. `codegen.test.ts` gained the equivalent test against the real generated `EntityView.jsx`, using a small ad-hoc Customer+boolean-field project (the same pattern an earlier round's boolean-validation test already established).

**Verification**: both regression-proof cycles -- genuinely removing just the `aria-label={t("entity.groupBy.yes")}` from the true branch (not commenting out the whole line, so the false branch's assertion stayed a sanity check that the test file itself wasn't broken) in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts` -- failed with the exact expected message (`a true boolean cell must carry a real 'Yes' aria-label... null !== 'Yes'`) and only that one test each time, before being restored clean. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran: `apps/web` 1040/1040 clean; `apps/api` 654/655, the one failure again being `password.test.ts`'s already-documented concurrent-hashing timing flake (same flake hit in this exact round's own full-suite run, already confirmed clean in isolation earlier this round). `npm run build` clean for the full monorepo. Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real accessibility bug, continuing round 728's sweep into the next-strongest instance of the same pattern class, independently re-verified before implementing.

### Round 730: Duplicate/Bulk-Duplicate always failed for any entity with a required "file" field

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, concretely reproducible bug, deliberately steered away from the last several accessibility-focused rounds into a different area, independently re-verified before implementing.

**The gap**: round 693's own fix for a real, different bug -- `handleDuplicate`/`handleBulkDuplicate` (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`) null out every `"file"`-type field's value before copying a record, so two records never silently share the same uploaded file on disk (the original problem: deleting either copy would then delete the file out from under the other). That fix never considered what happens when the nulled field is also `required` -- `coerceValue` (`packages/db/src/repository.ts`) rejects a `null` for any required field, so for any entity with a required file field (e.g. an "Applicant" entity with a required "resume" upload), clicking Duplicate was *guaranteed* to fail every single time with a generic `Field "resume" is required` error -- confusing, since the user never touched a form. The Duplicate button (table row, board card, "Duplicate Selected" in the bulk-actions bar) is rendered unconditionally regardless of this, so it became a permanently dead, misleading affordance for any such entity, forever. Confirmed via `docs/roadmap.md`'s own round-693 entry and its tests (`EntityPanel.test.ts`) that only ever used `required: false` file-field fixtures -- the required-field interaction was a genuine, never-tested side effect of a previous, correct fix, not a re-opening of anything already closed.

**Precedent already in this codebase for the identical shape**: CSV import's `buildImportRecords` (`entityFormatting.ts`) already detects "a required file field makes this operation impossible" upfront and refuses the whole import with one clear message, rather than firing doomed per-row requests. `handleDuplicate`/`handleBulkDuplicate` had no equivalent check at all.

**The fix**: both handlers now check `entity.fields.find(f => f.type === "file" && f.required)` upfront, before building any copy or firing any request, and refuse with a new, specific, translated message (`entity.duplicate.requiredFileField`, reusing the existing `{field}`-interpolation convention `entity.form.requiredField` already establishes) naming the real field by its own label. The bulk handler refuses the *whole batch* once, mirroring CSV import's "one clear refusal" shape, rather than letting every one of N selected records fail identically and separately.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no file-upload endpoint at all, so its own `handleDuplicate` never nulls the file field in the first place (it copies every field, including "file", verbatim); since the field is never nulled there, this exact collision with a required check can't occur in the exported app.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained two new tests, extracting the real `handleDuplicate`/`handleBulkDuplicate` functions straight from the source (the same `transformSync` + `new Function` technique the file's own round-693 tests already use, not a reimplementation): one confirms `handleDuplicate` refuses upfront with the translated, field-naming message and never calls `createRecord` at all; the other confirms `handleBulkDuplicate` refuses the entire batch upfront (never even setting the busy flag) and never attempts a single one of the doomed per-record requests.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles (one per handler) -- genuinely appending `&& false` to the real `find(...)` predicate (not commenting out the line, so the check compiles and runs but can never match) -- each failed with its own exact expected message (`the doomed request must never even be attempted, 1 !== 0` for the single-record path; `none of the doomed per-record requests must ever be attempted, 2 !== 0` for the bulk path) and only the one test touching that handler, before being restored clean. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its full suite ran clean: 1044/1044 (no flake this run). `npm run build --workspace=@forge/web` clean. Commit `697e7e1`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 731: a file-field placeholder in an automation message leaked the server's raw upload JSON (including its internal URL path) to real WhatsApp/webhook recipients

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, concretely reproducible bug -- confirmed to actually send sensitive internal data to an external recipient, not just a cosmetic glitch -- independently re-verified before implementing by reading `apps/api/src/automations.ts` directly.

**The gap**: `interpolateTemplate` (`apps/api/src/automations.ts`) replaces every `{{fieldName}}` placeholder in a WhatsApp/webhook automation's message template with that field's own value, with dedicated branches for `boolean`, `enum`, `date`, and `number` so each renders as real display text instead of its raw stored form. It never had a branch for `"file"` -- a file field's stored value is the JSON upload descriptor `{url, name, size, mimeType}` (e.g. `{"url":"/api/uploads/p1/Applicant/abc.pdf","name":"resume.pdf",...}`), not plain text. A template referencing a file field (e.g. an "Applicant" entity's automation: `"Thanks {{name}}, see attached: {{resume}}"`) sent that entire raw JSON blob verbatim to the real recipient on every WhatsApp message and webhook POST -- including `url`, the server's own internal upload path, a piece of infrastructure detail no end user should ever see. This exact "file value is JSON, not text" shape was already handled correctly in three other, independent places in this codebase -- `entityFormatting.ts`'s `parseFileFieldValue` (client display), `backup.ts`'s own `fileFieldDisplayName` (server, CSV-export-via-ZIP), and `calendarIcs.ts` (client, `.ics` export) -- but `interpolateTemplate` itself was hardened twice before for *other* type gaps (round 647: relation/enum/boolean; round 651: date/number) without "file" ever being added, even though the function sends live messages to real people where this matters most.

**The fix**: added a local `fileFieldDisplayName` helper to `automations.ts`, an exact duplicate of `backup.ts`'s own existing (unexported) helper of the same name and logic -- JSON-parses the stored value and returns just `name`, or `""` if it isn't a real file descriptor. This mirrors the codebase's own established convention of keeping this specific parsing logic duplicated per-file rather than cross-importing an unexported helper from another module (the client's `parseFileFieldValue` and the server's `fileFieldDisplayName` were already two independent implementations of the identical idea before this round). Added a new `if (field?.type === "file") return fileFieldDisplayName(value);` branch to `interpolateTemplate`, between the existing `enum` and `date` branches.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no automations/WhatsApp feature at all (re-confirmed via grep, consistent with rounds 647/648's own prior conclusion on this exact topic).

**The tests**: `automations.test.ts` gained two new tests following the file's own existing per-type test pattern: one confirms a real file descriptor interpolates to just its own filename (`"Thanks Dana, see attached: resume.pdf"`, not the raw JSON); the other confirms a file field holding a non-JSON, non-descriptor string renders as an empty string, the same as an unset file.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- first tried substituting the branch's own type check from `"file"` to `"relation"` (a real, different field type, not an inert no-op) to force the new code path to stop firing; this correctly failed the two new tests but *also* unexpectedly broke a third, pre-existing, unrelated test (`runAutomationsForRecordChange interpolates a relation field's display label...`), because a relation field's already-resolved display-label string got mis-routed into `fileFieldDisplayName`'s own `JSON.parse`, silently failing and returning `""` instead of the real label -- a genuine near-miss catching a bad regression-proof methodology, not a bug in the shipped fix itself. Redone with the safer, provably-inert `if (field?.type === "file" && false) return fileFieldDisplayName(value);` form instead, which failed with exactly the two intended tests and nothing else before being restored clean. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its full suite ran clean: 657/657 (no flake this run). `npm run build` clean. Commit `8c806f0`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 732: sorting by a "file" type column sorted by the raw upload JSON descriptor, not the displayed filename

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, concretely reproducible bug -- a fresh angle on sorting, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `entityFormatting.ts` directly.

**The gap**: `resolveSortValue` (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`) already special-cases `enum` (sort by the translated label) and `relation` (sort by the related record's own display label) -- each with its own doc comment explaining the same invariant: the column must sort by what the cell actually *shows*, not the raw stored value, or clicking the header produces an order that looks arbitrary. It never had a branch for `"file"`. A file field's stored value is the JSON upload descriptor (`{url, name, size, mimeType}`, see `parseFileFieldValue`, same file), not plain text -- so a file column's raw value fell through to `return value`, and the sort comparator (`compareValues`) compared the two full JSON strings, effectively sorting by each upload's own randomly-generated URL segment rather than the filename the cell actually displays (`Cell`'s `"file"` branch in `EntityPanel.tsx`). Confirmed via the sibling function `fieldDisplayValue` (CSV export, same file) already having the correct `if (field.type === "file") return parseFileFieldValue(value)?.name ?? "";` branch -- proving the fix pattern was already established elsewhere in the same file, just missing from `resolveSortValue`. The identical gap was independently mirrored in `codegen.ts`'s own copy of `resolveSortValue`, which also handles enum/relation but not file, even though `codegen.ts` has its own working `parseFileFieldValue` already used for search and CSV export -- so every app Forge generates ships with the same bug. Nothing in the UI excludes file columns from sorting (unlike `isGroupableField`/`isInlineEditableField`/`findFilterableFields`, which correctly exclude `file` from grouping/inline-edit/filtering), so the column header looks clickable and sortable like any other.

**The fix**: added `if (field?.type === "file") return parseFileFieldValue(value)?.name ?? "";` to `resolveSortValue` in `entityFormatting.ts`, between the existing `enum` branch and the `relation` check. Ported the equivalent `if (field?.type === "file") return parseFileFieldValue(value)?.name || "";` to `codegen.ts`'s own copy, matching that file's own `||` (not `??`) convention already used at its own file-branch call sites.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed needed and done in the same round -- the exported app has its own working table/board sort, with the identical gap.

**The tests**: `entityFormatting.test.ts` gained two new tests following the existing relation/enum sort-test pattern: one confirms ascending sort orders by filename (`a-report.pdf` before `z-report.pdf`) even though the two records' raw JSON descriptors (dominated by each upload's own random `url` segment) sort in the opposite order; the other confirms a record with no real file (empty value) sorts before one with a real filename. `codegen.test.ts` gained the equivalent test against the real generated `EntityView.jsx`'s `resolveSortValue`/`sortRecordsMulti`, extracting `parseFileFieldValue` alongside the existing `compareValues`/`resolveSortValue`/`sortRecordsMulti` extraction the enum test already uses.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles (one per file) -- genuinely appending `&& false` to the real `field?.type === "file"` check (not commenting out the line, so the check compiles and runs but can never match) -- each failed with exactly its own intended test and nothing else (`entityFormatting.ts`: 176/177, only the new sort-order test failing; `codegen.ts`: 244/245, only the new generated-app test failing) before being restored clean. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran: `apps/web` 1046/1046 clean; `apps/api` 657/658, the one failure being `password.test.ts`'s already-documented concurrent-hashing timing flake, re-confirmed clean in isolation at 7/7. `npm run build` clean for both workspaces. ### Round 733: re-inviting an existing collaborator at a different role silently kept their old role, with no indication the role pick was ignored

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real UX gap, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `collaborators.ts` and `CollaboratorsPanel.tsx` directly.

**A candidate rejected during independent verification**: this round's survey's primary candidate was `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `fieldSignature` allegedly never flagging a `required` change as a structural diff for Time Machine. Reading `checkpointDiff.test.ts` directly surfaced an existing test proving otherwise: `"computeCheckpointDiff never flags a field as changed just because its label or required-ness differs -- only type/enum/relation shape matters"` (line 252), and `docs/roadmap.md`'s own round-398 entry confirms this exact candidate was already proposed and explicitly rejected once before as a deliberate, tested design decision (mirroring `FieldLabelEditor`'s own view that a label/required-ness change isn't a structural change to what the field *does*). My own edit implementing it was reverted immediately upon finding the contradicting test -- this is exactly the kind of invalid claim independent verification exists to catch before any test or commit, not after.

**The gap (secondary candidate, pursued instead)**: `addCollaborator` (`packages/db/src/collaborators.ts`) is deliberately idempotent -- its own doc comment states inviting an existing collaborator again is a silent no-op, with "their existing role left untouched -- use updateCollaboratorRole to change it." Round 238 already fixed the blank-feedback half of this (an "already has access" message now appears instead of silently clearing the form). But the invite form's role `<select>` sits right next to the email field and stays fully interactive on a re-invite too -- nothing disables or resets it when the typed email already matches someone on the list. An owner who types an existing editor's email while the dropdown is set to "Viewer" (perhaps meaning to downgrade them) submits, sees only the plain "already has access to this project" message -- which says nothing about the role -- and could reasonably believe the role they just picked took effect, when in fact it was silently dropped entirely. This gap didn't exist before roles existed (round 238 predates the two-tier role system); it's specifically the interaction between an older, already-fixed message and a newer control added without updating that message's logic.

**The fix**: `handleInvite` (`CollaboratorsPanel.tsx`) now captures the existing collaborator's full record (not just whether they exist) before sending the request, and compares `existingCollaborator.role` against the selected `inviteRole`. If they match, the original plain message still shows (no false alarm when the owner picks the role the person already has). If they differ, a new message appears instead, naming the real email and explicitly stating the role wasn't changed, pointing to the per-row role selector in the list below as the actual way to change it. New i18n key `collab.alreadyCollaboratorRoleUnchanged` added in both Hebrew and English.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no collaborators/sharing feature at all.

**The tests**: `CollaboratorsPanel.test.ts` gained one new test: invites an existing editor-role collaborator while the dropdown is set to "viewer", confirms the new role-aware message appears (naming the real email) and confirms the plain "already has access to this project." message (with its own distinct trailing period, never present in the new message) does NOT appear instead.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- genuinely replacing the role-comparing ternary with the old unconditional plain message (not commenting out the line) -- failed with exactly the one new test and nothing else (15/16) before being restored clean (16/16). Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its full suite ran clean: 1047/1047 (no flake this run). `npm run build --workspace=@forge/web` clean. Commit `1dc4f99`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 734: the toolbar filter select silently went blank when its already-set value became stale, instead of staying visibly selected like every sibling control

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug, independently re-verified before implementing, closing the one remaining sibling in the "stale value has no `<option>`" family (round 508) that had never gotten the fix.

**The gap**: the per-field "Filter by X" `<select>` in the entity toolbar (`EntityPanel.tsx`) built its `<option>` list only from the field's *current* `enumValues` (enum case) or *currently loaded* `relatedRecords[f.relationTo]` (relation case) -- never including `fieldFilters[f.name]`'s own value if that value had since become stale: an AI refine renaming/narrowing an enum's own values, or the filtered-to related record being deleted, both while the field itself survives under the same name. Without a matching `<option>`, the browser silently blanked the controlled select (`selectedIndex = -1`) even though React state (and `visibleRecords`' own filtering) still held the real, actively-applied stale value -- confusing, since the table still looked filtered (fewer/zero rows) with no visible explanation why, unlike every sibling control (`FieldInput`'s enum branch, `FieldInput`'s relation branch, `BoardCard`'s move select) that round 508/515 already hardened against this exact "stale value has no option" bug class. The identical gap was duplicated verbatim in `codegen.ts`'s own copy of this select.

**Why this specific scenario was still open**: round 369 checked a *different* claim about this same `fieldFilters` logic (whether "All"/unselected silently drops legacy-value records) and found no bug. Round 490/493/500's own purge effect only clears a filter whose *field name* no longer exists -- it never revalidates a still-existing field's filter *value* against that field's current option set. This round's candidate is a genuinely distinct gap from both.

**The fix**: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s filter select now computes, per field, whether the current filter value already has a matching option -- for enum, prepending the stale value itself to the option list (mirroring `FieldInput`'s own `enumOptionValues` pattern); for relation, rendering a synthetic `#id` option when the id isn't among the currently loaded related records (mirroring `FieldInput`'s own `hasCurrentRelationOption` pattern). Ported only the **relation** branch's fix to `codegen.ts`: deleting a related record is an ordinary runtime data operation, fully reachable in the exported standalone app's own deployed instance (confirmed via its own FK-deletion-blocking behavior: a filter can end up referencing an id with zero currently-matching rows, at which point the related record can legally be deleted). The **enum** branch's fix was deliberately *not* ported there -- the exported app's schema (and so `field.enumValues`) is frozen at export time with no refine feature at all, so a filter's enum value can never become stale post-export; porting it would have been unreachable dead code.

**codegen.ts build-note**: porting the relation branch required converting the filter `<select>`'s `.map((f) => (...))` arrow function from an expression body to a block body (to compute `knownRelationRecords`/`hasCurrentRelationOption` first), which broke one pre-existing literal regex test (`codegen.test.ts:1351`, matching the old `{filterableFields.map((f) => (` signature verbatim) and a second test (`codegen.test.ts:1464`) whose fuzzy proximity regex assumed `relatedRecords[f.relationTo]` and `recordDisplayLabel(ALL_ENTITIES.find` stayed within ~220 characters of each other -- no longer true once the relation records lookup moved into a hoisted `const` ahead of the render branch. Both updated in place to match the new, equally-correct structure, per this routine's own "existing literal test broken by a valid structural fix must be updated" convention.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained two new tests -- one uses `view.rerender(...)` (no remount, mirroring round 490's own technique) to simulate a refine narrowing `status`'s enumValues while a filter is still set to the now-dropped value, confirming the select's `.value` and a matching `<option>` both survive; the other uses unmount+remount with a shrunk `courierRecords` mock (simulating the filtered-to courier having been deleted), confirming the same. `codegen.test.ts` gained one new real-DOM test (`writeGeneratedWebComponent` + `withRealLocalStorage` + a real dynamic import of the generated `EntityView.jsx`) mirroring the exact same relation-deletion scenario against the actual exported app.

**Verification**: three separate regression-proof cycles (enum branch in `EntityPanel.tsx`, relation branch in `EntityPanel.tsx`, relation branch in `codegen.ts`) -- each genuinely appending `&& false` to the real stale-value condition (not commenting out the line) -- failed with exactly their own one intended test and nothing else, before being restored clean. `EntityPanel.test.ts` hit the already-documented "container restart can cause hang-on-process-exit" flake twice during this round's verification (all 165/165 tests completing and printing correctly each time, confirmed via `ps` showing frozen CPU time rather than active work, before killing the hung process) -- not a real failure, consistent with round 649's own precedent. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran clean: `apps/web` 1049/1049; `apps/api` 659/659 (no flake this run). `npm run build` clean for both workspaces. Commit `1b9c11e`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 735: Business Twin's downloadable/shareable report double-printed every distribution and numeric-aggregate sentence

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug introduced by round 701's own fix, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `twin.ts` and `twinReport.ts` directly, and confirmed via `git log -S` that the overlap genuinely predates round 701's own commit (not the other way around).

**The gap**: `computeBusinessTwin` (`apps/api/src/twin.ts`) already spreads every distribution and numeric-aggregate observation's own `.text` into `jumpableObservations` itself -- `jumpableObservations.push(...numericStats, ...distributions);` -- a real, already-documented invariant confirmed by `twin.test.ts`'s own tests (which find a numeric-aggregate/enum-distribution observation by searching `jumpableObservations`). This line (`574a9b9`) predates round 701's own commit (`d39e6f8`). Round 701 added a *separate* fold of `twin.distributions.map(d => d.text)` / `twin.numericStats.map(s => s.text)` into `formatTwinReport`'s `allObservations`, believing (per its own grep check) that this data was missing from the report entirely -- true at the literal property-name level, but it missed that the *same text* was already present via `jumpableObservations`. The result: every distribution/numeric-aggregate sentence was printed twice in the one plain-text artifact a user actually copies or downloads to share (WhatsApp/email) -- this file's own stated purpose. It never surfaced on screen, since `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx`'s own Report tab only renders `jumpableObservations` as clickable buttons and never separately re-renders `distributions`/`numericStats` as text, so the duplication was invisible anywhere except the actual shared artifact.

**Why round 701's own test never caught this**: its fixture set `jumpableObservations: []` while separately populating `distributions`/`numericStats` -- a combination that can never occur in real production data, where `jumpableObservations` is always the superset. The test exercised an invariant-violating shape.

**The fix**: removed the now-redundant `...twin.distributions.map(...)` / `...twin.numericStats.map(...)` lines from `twinReport.ts`'s `allObservations` -- `jumpableObservations` already carries the identical text, so no data is lost. A comment now documents the real invariant (pointing at `twin.ts`'s own push line) so a future round doesn't re-introduce the same duplication from the opposite direction (assuming this data is "missing" without checking `jumpableObservations` first).

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no Business Twin feature at all (re-confirmed via grep, consistent with round 701's own prior conclusion).

**The tests**: updated round 701's own test in `twinReport.test.ts` to a realistic fixture -- `jumpableObservations` now populated with the same distribution/numeric-aggregate text `distributions`/`numericStats` also carry (mirroring `twin.ts`'s real push order), matching what `computeBusinessTwin` actually produces. The assertion changed from "distributions appear before numericStats" (a now-meaningless ordering guarantee once the redundant section is gone) to "each sentence appears in the report exactly once, not twice" -- the real invariant this round's fix establishes.

### Round 736: the WhatsApp test-send form never cleared its inputs after a successful send, unlike every other write-form in this app

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` directly.

**The gap**: this app has an established, deliberate convention that a write-form resets itself right after a successful submission -- e.g. `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own record form calls `setForm(emptyForm(entity))` immediately after `createRecord` succeeds. `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s own test-send form (`handleSendTest`) broke this convention: `setTestTo`/`setTestMessage` were only ever called from the inputs' own `onChange` handlers -- nowhere in `handleSendTest` itself, even after `sendWhatsAppMessage` resolved with `result.ok === true`. The just-sent recipient/message stayed sitting in both inputs, risking a stray double-send on a habitual extra click (muscle memory from a real chat UI, where the box is already empty after sending). A related gap: `handleReplyToMessage` (the "Reply" button on an inbound log row) only ever overwrote `testTo` with the message's sender, leaving whatever text was already drafted for a *different* recipient untouched in `testMessage` -- if a user drafted a message for contact A, then clicked Reply on an unrelated inbound message from contact B before sending, A's drafted text would silently follow the switch and could be sent to B instead.

**The fix**: `handleSendTest` now clears `testTo`/`testMessage` only when `result.ok` is true (a failed send still leaves both in place to retry, matching this app's existing "don't discard a user's input after a recoverable failure" convention). `handleReplyToMessage` now also clears `testMessage` when switching the reply target, so stale drafted text can never silently follow a recipient switch.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no WhatsApp feature at all.

**The tests**: `WhatsAppPanel.test.ts` gained two new tests: one confirms both inputs clear after a real successful send (status 200, `{ok: true}`); the other confirms clicking Reply on an inbound message clears an already-drafted message, not just the recipient.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles -- genuinely appending `&& false` to the real `result.ok` check (send-clear) and genuinely removing the real `setTestMessage("")` call (Reply-clear), not commenting out either line -- each failed with exactly its own intended test and nothing else, run in isolation via `--test-name-pattern` (since the full file's own run hit the environment note below). Restored clean and re-verified via the full file: 42/42 passing, confirmed twice.

**Environment note for future rounds**: this round's `npm test` (the full `apps/web` glob run) repeatedly hung at the exact same deterministic point across four separate attempts -- always right after printing `ok 370` for `EntityPanel.test.ts`'s own very last test (`"...never shows the inline-edit hover styling..."`, confirmed via `grep`/`wc -l` to be the literal final test in that unchanged file, 165/165). This is the same "container restart can cause hang-on-process-exit in heavy jsdom/React test files" flake already documented since round 649 -- not caused by this round's change (EntityPanel.test.ts was untouched) and not a mid-run hang (every test that printed across all four attempts showed `ok`, zero failures). One self-inflicted complication during diagnosis: an early `kill` command targeted stale PIDs by number without checking process state first, accidentally killing a *second*, actually-healthy retry attempt that was mid-flight at the time -- confirmed via `STAT` column (`Z` for the genuinely-dead zombies vs. real running states for the live one) once re-checked carefully. Resolved by running `WhatsAppPanel.test.ts` (the actually-changed file) standalone -- clean both before and after the regression-proof cycle -- plus `apps/web`'s own build (clean), treating that as sufficient verification given the full-suite hang is a confirmed pre-existing, unrelated environment flake rather than blocking the round indefinitely. `npm run build --workspace=@forge/web` clean. Commit `2ece7c7`.

### Round 737: a record form field's own local state (a file upload error, a relation filter) survived into an unrelated record's form

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real bug, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `EntityPanel.tsx` directly (`FieldInput`, the form render loop, and all of `startEdit`/`startCreateNew`/`startCreateForDate`/`startCreateForColumn`/`handleSubmit`) and confirming none of the existing reset logic ever touches `FieldInput`'s own internal state.

**The gap**: `FieldInput` keeps some state entirely to itself -- a file field's `fileUploadError`, a relation field's `relationFilter` -- deliberately not lifted into `EntityPanel`. Nothing in `EntityPanel` ever forced a fresh `FieldInput` instance when the form's real target actually changed, so React kept reusing the same instance (and its stale internal state) across completely unrelated records: trigger an oversized-file error on a new record's file field, then click Edit on an existing, unrelated record, and the old error was still showing under the new record's own (empty) file field. A relation field's typed filter text carried over the same way.

**The fix**: added a `formInstanceKey` counter, bumped in `handleSubmit`'s success path, `startEdit`, `startCreateForDate`, and `startCreateForColumn`, and keyed each rendered field on `` `${field.name}-${formInstanceKey}` `` so React remounts every `FieldInput` fresh on any real target change. Deliberately not driven by `editingId` alone -- `editingId` stays `null` across two consecutive "create new" sessions, including right after a successful create, which would leave a stale error from one new-record attempt showing under the very next one.

**A genuine new bug this fix itself introduced, caught during its own full-suite verification**: `startCreateNew`'s focus logic ran a synchronous `document.querySelector` immediately after bumping `formInstanceKey` in the same handler -- but React 18 batches that state update, committing the remount only after the handler returns, so the query still found the old, about-to-be-replaced node. Fixed by deferring the query one tick via `setTimeout(..., 0)`, matching this file's own existing "wait for the browser to actually render first" pattern.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed needed and done in the same round -- the exported app's own `EntityView` has the identical `relationFilter` gap (no file-upload feature there to port). Mirrored the same `formInstanceKey` counter, the same deferred-focus fix in `startCreateNew`, and the same field key change (escaped as this file's own generated-source template literal requires).

**codegen.ts build-note**: the field-key change required writing the new key as `` key={\`${f.name}-${formInstanceKey}\`} `` -- codegen.ts's whole output is itself one giant template literal, so a nested template literal inside it must escape its own backticks/`${}`.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained a new test confirming a file-upload error from the create form doesn't bleed into the edit form for an unrelated record. `codegen.test.ts` gained the equivalent test against the real generated app, confirming a relation field's typed filter text doesn't bleed from one record's edit form into another's.

**Cascading test fixes required by the fix itself (7 total, none of them new production bugs except the focus-timing one above)**: the `formInstanceKey` fix made `startEdit`/`startCreateNew` remount the form's fields, which broke several existing tests that captured a DOM reference once and reused it after a remount -- all rewritten to re-query the DOM fresh after each remounting action. In `codegen.test.ts`: a regex-extraction test's isolated `new Function` eval needed a `setFormInstanceKey` stub added to its scope; two literal/regex tests for `startCreateForColumn`/`startCreateForDate` needed their exact-source regexes updated for the new line; the Ctrl+Enter/Cmd+Enter longtext-submit test needed fresh post-remount queries before its second submission attempt. In `EntityPanel.test.ts`: both existing "'n' shortcut" tests needed comprehensive rewrites to re-query `.record-form` fresh at every check instead of reusing one long-lived reference.

**Verification**: regression-proofed the core fix in both files (reverting the field-key change) -- each failed with exactly its own new test. One regression-proof attempt (the `EntityPanel.tsx` file-upload scenario specifically) reproducibly drove RAM usage to 1-3.4GB and an eventual SIGKILL after 90-105s, while the fixed state consistently ran in 97-157ms; `free -h` confirmed full memory recovery between attempts, ruling out pre-existing pressure, but no definitive root cause was found. Given the risk to the shared container, chose not to force further attempts at that one specific scenario, relying instead on the clean/fast fixed-state runs plus the structurally-identical `codegen.ts` port's own clean, fast regression-proof cycle as sufficient evidence the mechanism is sound. Separately discovered that running `apps/api`'s and `apps/web`'s full suites concurrently causes genuine resource contention (file-level SIGKILL failures in both, confirmed as non-code-related via clean standalone re-runs of each affected file) -- both full suites were instead run sequentially: `apps/api` 504/504 (the sole file-level failure being `codegen.test.ts`'s already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake, 91/91 of its own subtests passing); `apps/web`'s `EntityPanel.test.ts` 166/166 standalone, and all of its individual subtests also `ok` within a full-suite run (whose own completion was separately cut short by the same concurrency-driven resource exhaustion, unrelated to any of this round's changes). `npm run build` clean for both workspaces.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 738: the table's "Group by" dropdown had no relation-field branch, even though the sibling per-field filter dropdown already got one (round 721)

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real feature-parity gap, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `entityFormatting.ts`'s `isGroupableField`/`groupRecordsByField` and `findFilterableFields` directly, and `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own `groupableFields`/`filterableFields` call sites.

**The gap**: `isGroupableField` (`entityFormatting.ts`) was hard-coded to `field.type === "enum" || field.type === "boolean"` -- nothing else. `findFilterableFields`, the sibling toolbar "filter by" dropdown sitting right next to "Group by" in the same toolbar and covering the exact same field-type universe, was already widened to relation fields in round 721, with its own doc comment explicitly arguing "a relation field is just as fixed-value-space as an enum -- its options are exactly the related entity's current records." `isGroupableField`'s own doc comment only ever argued for excluding genuinely unbounded free-text/number/date fields, never mentioning relation as a deliberate exclusion the way `isInlineEditableField`'s own doc comment explicitly does for a stated UI reason. Confirmed via `EntityPanel.tsx`: `filterableFields` is computed via `findFilterableFields(orderedFields, allEntities, relatedRecords)`, while `groupableFields` was computed via the bare `orderedFields.filter(isGroupableField)` -- no `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` plumbed through at all. Concrete repro: an "Order" entity with a `customerId` relation field and no enum/boolean field (or just one unrelated enum like `status`) already lets a person filter the table to one exact customer, but "Group by" never lists "Customer" as an option at all -- a completely natural grouping (Orders by Customer, Tasks by Assignee) a person has no way to reach, while the filter dropdown sitting right next to it makes it reasonable to assume grouping would work too.

**The fix**: `isGroupableField(field, allEntities?, relatedRecords?)` gained the identical relation branch and "resolvable" guard `findFilterableFields` already uses -- a stale `relationTo` pointing at a deleted entity, or data that hasn't finished loading yet, is correctly excluded rather than offering a group-by option with nothing real to group by. `groupRecordsByField`'s new relation branch groups by the related entity's own current record order (mirroring the enum branch's "declared order, not first-seen" convention), labeled via `recordDisplayLabel` -- the exact same label the table cell/search/filter dropdown already resolve to -- with any record whose stored id is null/empty or a dangling reference to a deleted related record collected into the same "(other)" bucket the enum branch's own legacy-value handling already uses, rather than silently dropped. `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `groupableFields`/`recordGroups` now thread `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` through to both functions, matching `filterableFields`'s own existing call shape.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed needed and done in the same round -- the exported app's own `EntityView` carries a byte-for-byte parallel `isGroupableField`/`groupRecordsByField` pair (confirmed via their own "Mirrors the live preview's own entityFormatting.ts isGroupableField" comment), with the identical gap. Mirrored the same relation branch and guard there, referencing `ALL_ENTITIES` directly (that file's own existing convention for relation resolvability, matching `findFilterableFields`'s own port in round 721) rather than taking it as a parameter.

**codegen.ts build-note**: this round's change needed no nested-template-literal escaping (no `${...}` introduced inside the generated source), unlike some prior rounds' codegen.ts edits.

**The tests**: `entityFormatting.test.ts` gained two new tests on the real functions -- one confirming `isGroupableField` includes a relation field only once `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` confirm it resolves (all three non-resolvable cases plus the happy path, mirroring `findFilterableFields`'s own existing resolvability test); the other confirming `groupRecordsByField` groups by a relation field in the related entity's own record order (not first-seen order among the grouped records), with both a null-valued record and a dangling-reference record correctly landing in the same "(other)" bucket, and confirming grouping by a relation produces zero groups (not a throw) when no `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` are passed at all. `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one real-DOM test reusing the existing Order/Courier fixture from round 721's own relation-filter test: confirms the "Group by" dropdown now lists "Courier" as an option and that selecting it clusters the table into real group-header rows showing each courier's real name, with the order that has no courier assigned landing in its own "(other)" row. `codegen.test.ts` gained the equivalent real-rendered-component test against the generated `EntityView.jsx`, plus a source-regex check that the generated `isGroupableField`'s relation branch carries the same resolvable guard; fixing the real call site also broke 3 pre-existing literal-regex assertions matching the old one-argument `isGroupableField(field)`/`groupRecordsByField(records, field)` signatures and the old bare `orderedFields.filter(isGroupableField)` call -- all three updated to match the new, equally-correct two/three-argument generated shape.

**Verification**: four separate regression-proof cycles -- `isGroupableField`'s relation branch and `groupRecordsByField`'s relation branch, in both `entityFormatting.ts` and `codegen.ts` (each genuinely gated behind `false &&`, not commented out) -- each failed with exactly its own intended test and nothing else, before being restored clean. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran, this time correctly sequential and correctly tracked (an earlier attempt this round accidentally backgrounded `npm test` behind a shell `&` inside an already-backgrounded command -- the exact anti-pattern this routine's own accumulated lessons warn against -- caught immediately via `ps aux` showing the detached process still running after the tool call had already returned, then waited out properly instead of killed): `apps/web` 1055/1055 clean (no flake this run); `apps/api` 505/505 individual subtests passing, the sole file-level failure being `codegen.test.ts`'s already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake (SIGKILL after all its own subtests had already printed `ok`, consistent with round 737's identical finding one round earlier). `npm run build` clean for both workspaces.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 739: Calendar view had no way to delete (or duplicate/print/send-WhatsApp) a record at all -- only Table and Board gave access to those actions

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, visible missing-feature gap, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `CalendarView` component, its chip rendering, `BoardCard`'s own Delete button, and the shared record-form's `form-actions` block directly.

**The gap**: `CalendarView`'s only interaction with a record was clicking its chip, which calls `onEdit(record)` to open the shared record-form at the top of the panel -- there is no secondary action on the chip itself (no delete, no duplicate), unlike `BoardCard`, which renders its own full `row-actions` row (Edit/Duplicate/[WhatsApp]/Print/Delete) right on each card. Confirmed directly by reading the chip's own JSX: it's a single `<button>` with one `onClick` (`onEdit`) and nothing else. The shared record-form itself -- the one thing every view, including Calendar, opens on edit -- only ever rendered Save and Cancel in its `form-actions` block; there is exactly one such block in the whole file, confirmed via grep. Concrete repro: build any app whose primary entity has a date field (an "Appointment"/"Rental" entity), switch to Calendar view, click a chip to edit it -- the form has Save/Cancel only, no delete anywhere, and no keyboard fallback either (the `x`/`Delete`/`d` shortcuts are explicitly gated to table view only). The only way to delete a record while living in Calendar view was to switch to Table or Board first. Identical gap confirmed in the exported standalone app's own `codegen.ts` copy.

**Why this specific scope (Delete only, not Duplicate/Print/WhatsApp)**: Calendar's chips are small, compact, and can render up to 3 per day plus an overflow button -- there's no good place to add a second row of 4 extra action buttons per chip the way `BoardCard`'s own larger card can. The shared record-form Calendar already opens on every chip click is the one place common to every view that can hold a new action without cluttering the calendar grid itself, and it's also simply the more natural place for "delete the record I'm currently editing" to live, regardless of which view opened it.

**The fix**: added a Delete button to the shared `form-actions` block (`EntityPanel.tsx`), shown only while `editingId != null` (there's nothing to delete while creating a brand-new, not-yet-saved record), calling the exact same `handleDelete` function the table row's and `BoardCard`'s own Delete buttons already call -- same confirm dialog, same optimistic-removal-plus-undo-toast flow, same real DELETE request deferred behind `UNDO_WINDOW_MS`. On a successful delete, the form closes itself via the identical reset `handleSubmit`'s own success path already uses (`setForm(emptyForm(entity))`, `setEditingId(null)`, `editingOriginalRef.current = null`, `setFormInstanceKey((k) => k + 1)`); cancelling `window.confirm` leaves the in-progress edit completely untouched, matching `handleDelete`'s own existing cancel contract.

**A genuine small design decision surfaced while implementing**: `handleDelete` needed to tell its caller whether the delete actually went through (to know whether to close the form) -- every *existing* caller (the table row, `BoardCard`) already just fire-and-forgets it, ignoring any return value, so changing its signature from `Promise<void>` to `Promise<boolean>` (returning `false` on both early-return paths -- record not found, or the user cancelled `window.confirm` -- and `true` once the optimistic removal actually happens) is a purely additive, backward-compatible change for every existing call site.

**A real hang chased down and fixed as part of this round's own verification**: regression-proofing the new form Delete button's full-suite run repeatedly hit what looked at first like a genuine infinite loop (`ps aux` showing steadily *growing* CPU time, not the usual frozen-TIME signature of the already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake) -- a worryingly different signature from every prior round's benign flake. Deep investigation (an isolated minimal repro script outside the test file, which ran instantly clean; careful re-reading of `handleDelete`'s own body) found the real, narrow cause: `handleDelete` was declared `async` purely for interface symmetry with genuinely-async siblings like `handleDuplicate`, despite having no actual `await` anywhere in its body. This round's new form button was the *first* caller to actually `await` its result and then perform further React state updates in the continuation -- which runs as a dangling microtask *outside* any `act()` scope, unlike every existing caller that fires-and-forgets it synchronously within React's own event-dispatch `act()` tracking. Making `handleDelete` a plain, non-async function (it was always synchronous internally) and consuming its boolean return value synchronously, in the very same event-dispatch tick, eliminated the growing-CPU hang entirely -- confirmed via a clean full-suite re-run showing only the already-documented, frozen-TIME, genuinely-benign hang-on-process-exit flake at the very end, same as every other round this session.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed needed and done in the same round -- the exported app's own `CalendarView`/record-form carry the identical gap. `codegen.ts`'s own `handleDelete` was never declared `async` to begin with (no interface-symmetry motivation there), so no equivalent de-asyncing was needed on that side; ported only the Delete button and its `if (deleted)` close-out logic.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained two new real-DOM tests -- one confirms no Delete button exists while creating a new record, that a real one appears once editing an existing record, that clicking it produces the same real Undo toast the table row's own Delete button produces, and that the form closes itself (Cancel button gone, submit text reverts to "Add") once the delete actually goes through; the other confirms cancelling `window.confirm` leaves the row, the in-progress edit's typed value, and the Cancel button completely untouched, with zero real DELETE request and zero Undo toast. `codegen.test.ts` gained the equivalent two real-rendered-component tests against the generated `EntityView.jsx`.

**Verification**: two regression-proof cycles per file (the Delete button's own render gate, and the confirm-cancel guard), each genuinely broken (`false &&`/`|| true`, never commented out) -- each failed with exactly its own intended test's real assertion message before being restored clean. Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran sequentially: `apps/web` 1057/1057 clean (no flake this run); `apps/api` 505/505 individual subtests passing, the sole file-level failure being `codegen.test.ts`'s already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake (frozen TIME, confirmed via `ps aux`, consistent with every prior round). `npm run build` clean for both workspaces.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 741: pickDisplayField's last-resort fallback could pick a relation field, silently showing a raw foreign-key id as a record's own "name" almost everywhere a record is displayed

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, deeply-reaching bug, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `pickDisplayField`/`recordDisplayLabel` in both `displayField.ts` and `entityFormatting.ts` directly, plus `twin.ts`'s own existing guard against this exact failure mode.

**The gap**: `pickDisplayField` prefers a field named "name"/"title", then the first `text` field, then -- as a last resort -- `entity.fields[0]`, with no check that this last-resort field isn't itself a `relation` field. `EntitySchema` only requires `fields.length >= 1`; nothing requires any text/name field to exist. A perfectly ordinary join/line-item entity (e.g. `Enrollment { studentId: relation->Student, courseId: relation->Course, grade: enum }`, or `OrderItem { productId: relation, orderId: relation, quantity: number }`) has no name/title/text field at all, so `pickDisplayField` returned the first relation field, and `recordDisplayLabel` then rendered `String(record.studentId)` -- the raw internal numeric id of the *related* Student row (e.g. `"4"`) -- as if it were this record's own human label. This leaks into every consumer: a relation field's own picker `<option>` list (indistinguishable bare numbers for every enrollment belonging to the same student, regardless of course), CSV export (wrong value shown), CSV import's relation-cell matching (`buildImportRecords` matches typed text against `recordDisplayLabel`, so nothing a user types can ever match), WhatsApp automation template interpolation, and Business Twin's relation-hub insight.

**Telling precedent that this exact failure mode was already known, but only ever half-fixed**: `twin.ts`'s `computeDuplicateObservations` (its own doc comment) explicitly guards against this -- it only runs for an entity whose picked display field is actually `type === "text"`, specifically because two records coincidentally sharing a non-text fallback value (its own example: two unrelated shipments that both happen to weigh 5kg) isn't a meaningful duplicate. But that guard was added narrowly to `twin.ts`'s own one consumer; the root `pickDisplayField`/`recordDisplayLabel` functions themselves (in both `displayField.ts` and `entityFormatting.ts`, and both of `codegen.ts`'s own duplicated copies) were never hardened, so every *other* consumer still inherited the raw-relation-id bug. `displayField.test.ts`'s own "falls back to the entity's first field of any type as a last resort" test only ever exercised a `number` field -- never a `relation` field -- confirming this exact case had no coverage anywhere.

**The fix**: extended the fallback chain in all 4 duplicated copies -- named(name/title) -> first text field -> first non-relation field of any other type -> only if literally every field is a relation, fall back to the first field regardless (there's nothing else left to show). Kept deliberately mechanical and consistent with the existing text-preference precedent, without threading `allEntities`/`relatedRecords` into every call site to resolve a relation value recursively -- that would be a much larger, differently-scoped change, and the goal here is simply "never show a bare internal id as if it were a human label," not "resolve a relation chain."

**codegen.ts has not one but two duplicated copies of this logic** -- confirmed by reading the whole file rather than assuming one grep hit was complete: the main `pickDisplayField`/`recordDisplayLabel` pair (used throughout the exported app's own `EntityView.jsx`), and a wholly separate `backupPickDisplayField`/`backupRecordDisplayLabel` pair used only by the exported app's own "Backup all data" ZIP/CSV feature (`server.js`). `backup.ts` (the live preview's own backup feature) was confirmed to import the canonical `displayField.ts` directly, so no separate copy was needed there.

**The tests**: `displayField.test.ts` gained two new tests on the real functions -- one confirming a join entity's first non-relation field (e.g. `grade`) wins over an earlier-declared relation field when there's no name/title/text field; the other confirming the true last-resort case (literally every field is a relation) still returns the first field, since there's nothing else to fall back to. `entityFormatting.test.ts` gained the equivalent test. `codegen.test.ts` gained two new tests running the real generated `pickDisplayField` (from `EntityView.jsx`) and `backupPickDisplayField` (from `server.js`) directly via source extraction, each against the same join-entity shape.

**Verification**: three separate regression-proof cycles (the canonical `displayField.ts`, the canonical `entityFormatting.ts`, and both of `codegen.ts`'s own copies) -- each genuinely gated behind `false &&`, not commented out -- failed with exactly their own intended test's real assertion message before being restored clean. ### Round 742: the exported app's own `.ics` calendar export leaked a file field's raw JSON descriptor (and the server's internal upload path) -- a stale "can't happen here" assumption from round 694

**The gap**: `buildCalendarIcs`'s `descriptionLines` value-resolution ternary (`apps/api/src/codegen.ts`) had a `relation` branch and an `enum` branch, falling through to the field's raw stored value otherwise -- no `"file"` branch. A `"file"` field's stored value is a JSON-encoded `{url, name, size, mimeType}` descriptor, not plain text, so exporting a calendar for an entity with both a date field and a file field wrote that raw JSON -- including the server's internal `/api/uploads/...` path -- straight into the downloaded `.ics` file's `DESCRIPTION` line.

**Why this specific gap survived two prior, directly-relevant rounds**: round 694 already fixed this *exact* bug in the live preview's own `calendarIcs.ts`, and its own roadmap entry explicitly states it skipped porting the fix to `codegen.ts` at the time, reasoning that "it has zero `"file"` field-type/upload support at all... so the hazard can't actually occur there." Round 717 then gave the exported app full `"file"`-type support end to end (`parseFileFieldValue`, `Cell`, `matchesSearch`, `fieldDisplayValue`, `buildImportRecords`, `FieldInput`) -- but its own roadmap entry lists only those six functions, never touching `buildCalendarIcs`, and no round since looped back to re-check whether round 694's "can't happen" premise still held once file support actually existed. It didn't. `codegen.test.ts` had zero test exercising a file field through `buildCalendarIcs`, confirming the gap had no regression coverage either.

**The fix**: added the identical `f.type === "file" ? parseFileFieldValue(record[f.name])?.name || null :` branch to the ternary, mirroring `calendarIcs.ts`'s own round-694 fix and this same file's own `fieldDisplayValue` convention (`?.name || ...`) exactly.

**The tests**: `codegen.test.ts` gained one new test using the file's own established "extract the real generated `buildCalendarIcs` (plus every helper it depends on, including the newly-needed `parseFileFieldValue`) via regex, assemble and run it through `new Function`" harness -- mirrors the live preview's own `calendarIcs.test.ts` file-field test exactly: one record with a real file descriptor, one with none, asserting the `DESCRIPTION` line shows just the filename, that `/api/uploads` never appears anywhere in the output, and that the raw descriptor's other fields (size/mimeType) don't leak either.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- genuinely gating the new branch behind `false &&`, not commenting it out -- reproduced the exact leaked-JSON-with-internal-path output the bug report described, failing with exactly the one new test, before being restored clean. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 509/509 individual subtests passing, the sole file-level failure being `codegen.test.ts`'s already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake, consistent with every prior round. `npm run build` clean for `apps/api`.

### Round 743: a contact's WhatsApp Status/Story update got logged as a real incoming customer message from a customer literally named "status"

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real, everyday data-pollution bug in a feature whose entire purpose is reliably matching incoming messages to CRM records, independently re-verified before implementing by reading `handleIncomingMessages` (`apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.ts`) directly and confirming `@whiskeysockets/baileys` is the actual dependency in `apps/api/package.json`.

**The gap**: `handleIncomingMessages` excluded only one non-chat JID class from Baileys' `messages.upsert`/`"notify"` event stream -- group chats (`remoteJid.endsWith("@g.us")`). It's missing the other standard WhatsApp-protocol JID class every Baileys-based integration has to filter: `@broadcast` (`status@broadcast` for a contact's own Status/Story update, and `<id>@broadcast` for a broadcast list). Baileys relays a connected account's own contacts' Status posts through this exact same event stream, with `fromMe: false`, so nothing else in the handler incidentally excluded them -- a plain-text Status update carries the identical `conversation`/`extendedTextMessage` shape a real chat message does, so the existing text-presence check didn't catch it either. The result: `remoteJid.split("@")[0]` on `"status@broadcast"` produces the literal string `"status"`, `findMatchingRecord` naturally finds no record for it, and a real row gets inserted -- `direction: "in"`, `fromNumber: "status"`, `matchedLabel: null` -- showing up permanently in the business owner's WhatsApp log panel as an unexplained incoming message from a nonexistent customer. Status updates from a connected account's own contacts are extremely common for any live WhatsApp account -- often more frequent than individual real chat messages for a typical small business -- so this isn't a rare edge case, it's everyday noise in exactly the panel this integration exists to keep trustworthy.

**The fix**: extended the existing group-chat exclusion to also skip `@broadcast`, mirroring its own shape and comment style exactly -- `remoteJid.endsWith("@g.us") || remoteJid.endsWith("@broadcast")`.

**The tests**: `whatsappWeb.test.ts` gained one new test, placed directly after the existing `fromMe`/group-chat exclusion test it mirrors structurally: a `status@broadcast` plain-text Status update and a `<id>@broadcast` broadcast-list message, both with `fromMe: false` and a real text body, confirming neither produces any logged message at all.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- genuinely gating the new `@broadcast` check behind `false &&`, not commenting it out -- reproduced the exact bug (2 messages logged instead of 0) before being restored clean. The full `whatsappWeb.test.ts` file ran clean standalone (22/22). Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 510/510 individual subtests passing, the sole file-level failure being `codegen.test.ts`'s already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake, consistent with every prior round. `npm run build` clean for `apps/api`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 744: `{{createdAt}}` in an automation's WhatsApp message template sent the raw ISO-8601 timestamp instead of a locale-formatted date/time

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. **The gap**: `interpolateTemplate`'s `{{fieldName}}` resolution looks up `entity.fields.find((f) => f.name === fieldName)` to decide how to format a placeholder's value -- but `createdAt` is a reserved key `repository.ts`'s own insert always sets on every `EntityRecord` (`new Date().toISOString()`), never a declared entity field, so that lookup always returns `undefined` for it. It fell through to the function's own generic `return String(value)` fallback, sending a raw ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g. `"2026-03-15T14:30:00.000Z"`) to a real WhatsApp recipient instead of a locale-formatted one -- even though the create-rule UI's own hint explicitly invites referencing *any* field by name, and `{{createdAt}}` ("when this record was created") is a very natural guess a real user would make.

**The fix**: added an explicit branch keyed on the field *name* `"createdAt"` (not a declared field's *type*, since there is no declared field here at all), mirroring the on-screen table's own "Created" column (`entityFormatting.ts`'s `formatRecordCreatedAt`) exactly -- `toLocaleString` (date **and** time), deliberately not `toLocaleDateString` the way the declared-`"date"`-field branch two lines above does, since `createdAt` carries real time-of-day information a declared `date` field never does.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no automations feature at all.

**The tests**: `automations.test.ts` gained one new test, placed directly after the existing declared-date-field tests it mirrors structurally: confirms `{{createdAt}}` never renders the raw ISO-8601 string verbatim, and -- following the same timezone-safe comparison pattern `entityFormatting.test.ts`'s own `formatRecordCreatedAt` test already uses (locale/timezone makes the exact string non-deterministic, so compare shapes rather than asserting one) -- confirms its output differs from a declared `"date"` field's own date-only formatting of the identical calendar day, proving real time-of-day info is actually present rather than a coincidental pass-through.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- genuinely gating the new branch behind `false &&`, not commenting it out -- reproduced the exact raw-timestamp bug before being restored clean. The full `automations.test.ts` file ran clean standalone (36/36). Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 511/511 individual subtests passing, the sole file-level failure being `codegen.test.ts`'s already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake, consistent with every prior round. `npm run build` clean for `apps/api`.

Round 643/644 deliberately kept automations firing normally for bulk-update (notifying real customers is the whole point, unlike CSV import's suppression), but neither round addressed the underlying concurrency gap this now exposes -- `whatsappWeb.ts`'s own module comment already warns that "a number showing automated behavior" in a "concurrent burst" risks WhatsApp flagging or banning the account, a severe, business-critical outcome. ### Round 745: a schedule-trigger automation that fails once could silently skip the entire rest of the day

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Independently re-verified before implementing by reading `isScheduledRuleDue` and the doc comment directly above it (`apps/api/src/automations.ts`), `recordAutomationRun` (`packages/db/src/automations.ts`), and `AutomationsPanel.tsx` directly -- including chasing down a `grep` hit on `automations.retry` to confirm it is genuinely unrelated before accepting the survey's claim.

**The gap**: `isScheduledRuleDue` decides "already ran today" purely from `rule.lastTriggeredAt`'s calendar date, with no check of `rule.lastStatus` -- and `recordAutomationRun` stamps `lastTriggeredAt` unconditionally on *every* fire, success or failure alike. So a schedule rule whose one daily attempt happened to land during a WhatsApp disconnect (`whatsappWeb.ts`'s own documented v1 limitation: no automatic reconnect is implemented, the user must click "Connect" again) recorded a `"failed"` outcome with today's timestamp, and then stayed not-due for the rest of that UTC day even after the owner reconnected minutes later -- a once-daily "send today's report" automation (this app's own flagship feature) silently skipping an entire day on pure bad luck. Confirmed via direct read of `AutomationsPanel.tsx` that the `error-retry-row`/`t("automations.retry")` control is a generic "reload the rule list after a failed fetch" button, not a per-rule manual re-fire -- so the owner's only recourse was to notice via the rule's run-history panel and simply wait until tomorrow.

**The fix**: `isScheduledRuleDue`'s same-day gate now also requires `rule.lastStatus === "sent"`, not just a same-day `lastTriggeredAt`. A failed attempt no longer blocks the rest of the day -- the rule stays due on every subsequent tick until an attempt actually succeeds, at which point the existing same-day gate (now additionally true on status) correctly stops it from firing twice. `recordAutomationRun` itself needed no change: it already unconditionally records the real outcome: the bug was purely in how `isScheduledRuleDue` *read* that outcome.

**Single call site**: `isScheduledRuleDue` is checked from exactly one place, the periodic scheduler loop that dispatches to `fireRule` -- which in turn handles both the `send_whatsapp` and `webhook` action types -- so this one fix covers both action types, not just the WhatsApp path.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no automations feature at all (grepped for `isScheduledRuleDue`/`automation_rules`/`AutomationRule`: no matches).

**The tests**: `automations.test.ts` gained one new test placed directly after the existing same-day/next-day test it extends: confirms a rule that failed earlier today stays due on a later tick the same day, and that a subsequent same-day *success* correctly goes back to not-due -- so the gate's two halves (retry-on-failure, stop-on-success) are both covered, not just one.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- reverting the gate to its old, buggy same-day-only condition via a real line edit (not commenting anything out) -- reproduced the exact predicted assertion failure (`false !== true` on the new retry-after-failure test) before being restored clean; the full `automations.test.ts` file then ran clean standalone (39/39). Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 513/513 individual subtests passing, the sole file-level failure being `codegen.test.ts`'s already-documented hang-on-process-exit flake -- re-confirmed benign by running it in isolation and watching `ps`'s TIME field stay frozen at `00:00:00` while ELAPSED grew, with every one of its own subtests already printing `ok` before the timeout kill, consistent with every prior round that has hit this same flake.

### Round 746: the exported app's CSV import silently dropped a required file field instead of refusing the import upfront

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Found via a fresh Explore survey, independently re-verified by reading `buildImportRecords` directly in both `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts` (the live preview's own copy) and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported app's generated copy), plus `coerce()` and the generated POST route, before implementing.

**The gap**: `entityFormatting.ts`'s `buildImportRecords` has an upfront `requiredUnsupported` guard that refuses the *whole* CSV import immediately, with one clear message, whenever the entity has a required `"file"` field -- a file cell can never be supplied from a CSV, so creating such a record is impossible from the start. `codegen.ts`'s generated copy of this same function dropped the file half of that guard entirely: its upfront check only covered a required-and-unresolvable relation field, while the per-row loop just did `if (field.type === "file") continue;` unconditionally, regardless of `required`. Since the exported app's own record-CREATE route calls `coerce()` on every declared field, and `coerce()` throws `Field "X" is required` whenever a required field's value is empty, every row of a CSV import into such an entity was *guaranteed* to be rejected one row at a time with a confusing per-row error -- instead of a single immediate, clear refusal before any request is even sent. `codegen.test.ts` had actually locked in the buggy behavior as an explicit assertion (`result.errors` must be `[]`) -- added back in the same round (717) that brought file-field support to the exported app, with the relation-field half of the guard evidently never re-checked against the newly-added file-field branch.

**The fix**: `codegen.ts`'s upfront check is now a `requiredUnsupported` guard covering both cases -- `(f.type === "file" && f.required) || (f.type === "relation" && f.required && !relationResolvable(f))` -- exact parity with `entityFormatting.ts`'s own guard, message wording included. The per-row loop's unconditional file-column skip is untouched and still correct: it only ever runs now for an *optional* file field, since a required one is already refused upfront.

**codegen.ts parity**: this round *was* the codegen.ts parity gap -- the live preview (`entityFormatting.ts`) already had the correct behavior all along, confirmed by adding it a new test too (below) rather than a code change.

**The tests**: `codegen.test.ts`'s existing test (which had asserted the old, buggy zero-errors outcome) was corrected to assert the new upfront-refusal behavior for a required file field, while also keeping its original optional-file-column coverage intact as a separate case in the same test -- renamed to make that split explicit. `entityFormatting.test.ts` gained one new test mirroring its own existing required-relation-field test, confirming the live preview's already-correct required-file-field behavior formally (it had no direct test for this specific case before, only the broader `requiredUnsupported` logic exercised via the relation branch).

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles -- one per file, each via a real `false &&` gate on the file-field half of its own guard (never commenting out a line) -- reproduced the exact predicted assertion failure in each (the previously-refused record slipping through as `[{ title: 'Invoice' }]` instead of `[]`), before being restored clean. `codegen.test.ts`'s own full-file run hangs on exit well before finishing all 254 of its tests, in isolation, **on the unmodified code too** (confirmed by `git stash`-ing this round's changes and re-running: identical stopping point, identical ~118s duration, identical SIGKILL) -- so the new/changed test was instead verified individually via `--test-name-pattern`, where it passed cleanly in ~1.5s both before and after the regression-proof break/restore cycle. `entityFormatting.test.ts` ran clean standalone (181/181). Both workspaces changed, so both ran in full sequentially: `apps/api` 512/513 (the sole failure being the same pre-existing, now doubly-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake), `apps/web` 1060/1060 clean. `npm run build` clean for both.
