### Round 797: a build/refine failure after SSE headers are sent was silently swallowed

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey moved to the build/refine SSE streaming mechanics themselves -- a part of `pipeline.ts`/`app.ts` no prior round in this window had examined.

**The gap**: `routes/projects.ts`'s `streamPipeline` (the build/refine SSE endpoint) calls `res.writeHead(200, ...)` up front, then streams each agent step `pipeline.ts`'s `runBuildPipeline` yields. Every step in that generator is deliberately guarded so it can never throw past that point -- the Database step's own try/catch with an AI auto-fix retry, Seed Data's per-record try/catch, `runQaChecks`' own internal try/catches -- but the finalize block (`updateProjectSpec`, `markProjectBuilt`, `insertCheckpoint`, `getProject`) did real DB writes too, with no such guard at all.

**Why this is not deliberate**: the function's author went out of their way, repeatedly, to guard every other fallible step in this exact generator against throwing past the point headers are sent, specifically because this is an SSE stream where a thrown error has nowhere good to go. The finalize block is the one place this same care wasn't applied, despite doing genuine DB writes that can fail for the same underlying reasons (disk space, DB constraints) the Database step already treats as a real, expected failure mode -- this app's own ephemeral-disk Render deployment makes that a real, not hypothetical, case.

**Concrete failure scenario**: a genuine write failure in the finalize block propagated straight out of the generator. `streamPipeline`'s own `for await` has no try/catch, so it reached Express's error middleware (`app.ts`) *after* this response's headers were already written. That middleware never checked `res.headersSent` -- confirmed via grep that the string never appeared anywhere in this codebase before this round -- so it called `res.status(500).json(...)` anyway, which throws its own synchronous `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` from inside the error handler itself, forwarded to Express's `finalhandler`, which just destroys the socket with no response body at all. The client's SSE reader can only see the connection die and reports a generic network error -- never the real cause -- after the user has already watched Database/Seed Data/QA/Security all render as green "success" steps, strongly implying the build succeeded even though `project.status` was never actually flipped to `"built"` and no checkpoint was ever saved.

**The fix, two parts**: (1) `pipeline.ts` -- wrapped the finalize block in the same try/catch pattern every earlier step in this exact function already uses, yielding a failed `"Forge"` event instead of letting the DB error escape. (2) `app.ts` -- extracted the inline error-handling middleware into an exported `errorMiddleware` function (so it's unit-testable against a fake `Response`, since a real Express response whose headers are already sent really does tear down the socket) and added a `res.headersSent` check at the top: when true, hands the error to `next(err)` instead, exactly what Express's own error-handling documentation recommends. This is defense-in-depth for this and any other streaming route, on top of fix #1 actually preventing the specific case that triggered it.

**codegen.ts parity**: not applicable -- this is backend-only server/middleware logic, not one of the four generated-app-template duplication sites.

**The tests**: `pipeline.test.ts` drives a real build via `runBuildPipeline`, closes the in-memory db right after the Security step succeeds (simulating a genuine write failure during finalize without needing to fake a disk-full condition directly), and confirms the generator yields exactly one Forge event with status `"failed"` naming the real error, rather than throwing. `app.test.ts` gained two new unit tests against `errorMiddleware` directly with a fake `Response` -- one with `headersSent: true` confirms it calls `next(err)` and never attempts `status()`/`json()` (whose fake throws if called, reproducing the real `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` symptom); one with `headersSent: false` confirms the existing 500 response still works normally.

**Verification**: all three new tests verified via genuine revert/restore. `pipeline.test.ts`'s: removing the try/catch made the test fail with the real, unhandled "database is not open" error propagating out of the generator; restored, it passes. `app.test.ts`'s `headersSent` test: removing the guard made it fail by actually throwing `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` from inside the fake `json()`; restored, it passes. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 582/583 pass; the sole failure is the already-documented pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` process-exit hang flake, stopping at the identical subtest it has in every round's log since 787 -- confirmed unrelated, and all three new tests ran and passed inside this full run. `npm run build` (esbuild bundle) clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 798: the exported app's Add form let a required file field repeat an unfixable error forever

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The exact same hazard class already recognized and fixed twice elsewhere in this codebase, missed on the one path every user hits first.

**The gap**: the exported standalone app's `FieldInput` has no upload control at all for a `"file"` field -- only the live Forge AI preview can turn a chosen file into the real `{url, name, size, mimeType}` descriptor this field actually stores. `codegen.ts`'s own comment on that branch already explains why (no upload endpoint exists standalone) and that an existing record's already-uploaded file still displays correctly; it just never considered a brand-new record on an entity whose file field is `required`.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this exact hazard class was already identified and fixed twice elsewhere in this same codebase -- the live preview's own `EntityPanel.tsx` already refuses `handleDuplicate` up front with a dedicated message when a required file field exists, and this exact file's own CSV import (`requiredUnsupported`) already refuses the whole import up front for the identical reason ("a required file field can never be satisfied... must be caught here, upfront, not just skipped per-row"). The single-record Add form -- the one path every user hits first, on the very first record of such an entity -- was simply never given the same treatment.

**Concrete failure scenario**: export any project with an entity like `Applicant { name: text, resume: file, required: true }` -- an entirely ordinary shape (a hiring tracker: every applicant must submit a resume). Deploy the exported app and try to add the very first applicant: the form shows "Resume *" next to a box that only ever says "No file" with nothing to click. Submitting fires `handleSubmit`'s generic `missingField` guard every single time -- `"Resume" is a required field` -- with no indication this is permanent, not a fixable mistake. There is no way around it: no upload endpoint exists, and even a raw API POST hits the server's own `coerce()` rejection. The Applicant entity can never have a single record created in this exported app, ever.

**The fix**: computed `requiredFileField` once per entity (mirroring where `orderedFields` is already computed). `handleSubmit` now checks it first, specifically, before the generic `missingField` check -- but only when `editingId` is null (creating), never when editing an existing record, since an existing record's own already-uploaded file keeps `form[f.name]` non-empty and editing its other fields is still perfectly possible. The Add button is also disabled upfront in that same case, with a persistent explanatory line next to it, so the user discovers this without even needing to click Add once first.

**Scope**: `apps/web` (`EntityPanel.tsx`) needs no fix -- its own file upload genuinely works, so a required file field is normally satisfiable there; this hazard is specific to the exported app's lack of an upload endpoint. `apps/api`'s real backend needs no fix either, for the same reason.

**The tests**: one new test drives the real generated `EntityView` component (not a regex proxy) against a custom entity with a required file field -- confirms the Add button is disabled and the explanation is already visible without submitting, then forces a submit anyway (bypassing the disabled button) to confirm the specific message still wins over the generic one and no POST ever fires.

**Verification**: both halves of the fix verified independently via revert/restore. Reverting `handleSubmit`'s specific check alone made the submit assertion fail with the generic `"Name" is a required field` message instead (the first required field in declaration order, not even naming the real file field); restored, it passes. Separately reverting the button-disabled/banner JSX alone made the button-disabled assertion fail (`false !== true`); restored, it passes. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 583/584 pass; the sole failure is the already-documented pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` process-exit hang flake, stopping at the identical subtest it has in every round's log since 787 -- confirmed unrelated, and the new test itself ran and passed inside this full run. `npm run build` (esbuild bundle) clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

**Rejected candidate this round, after empirical testing**: a survey candidate claimed `HistoryPanel.tsx`'s "Compare with" checkpoint dropdown goes stale (renders blank) when the checkpoint it's comparing against is deleted while a different checkpoint's own diff panel stays open. Investigated directly: `resolveCompareSpec`/`formatCompareTarget` already degrade gracefully when the id no longer exists, and -- critically -- a real DOM test proved the `<select>` itself ALSO degrades gracefully, for a reason the survey missed: removing the currently-selected `<option>` element triggers the browser's own spec-mandated "reset to first option" algorithm for a single-select, auto-correcting the dropdown's visual state regardless of whether React's `compareTargetId` state is explicitly cleared. `selectedIndex` measured `0` (not `-1`/blank) in both the "fixed" and "unfixed" versions -- no observable difference exists anywhere. No fix was shipped; the working tree was left clean and a fresh survey was run instead. Noted here specifically so a future round doesn't re-propose the same claim without re-verifying it against real DOM behavior first, not just code reading.

### Round 799: `FieldChip`'s enum/relation type-change draft had no way to cancel out of it

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The exact same "Escape-cancels" pattern every other inline-edit control in this file already has, missed on the one control added two rounds after all the others.

**The gap**: round 715 added a draft-confirm step for switching a field's type to `"enum"`/`"relation"` (which need a value list or target picked first, unlike every other type, which commits immediately), plus a dedicated "edit values"/"edit target" button to reopen that same draft for a field that's already enum/relation -- since re-selecting the type `<select>`'s own already-shown option fires no native `change` event. Once that draft form is open, there was no way to back out of it at all: no Escape handler, no Cancel button, and the type `<select>` itself can't help either (it's hidden the instant the draft opens, and even if it weren't, re-picking the already-shown type fires nothing).

**Why this is not deliberate**: every other inline-edit control in this exact file -- `RoleChip`, `AssumptionItem`, `PersonaItem`, `EntitySummaryItem`'s label editor, and this same `FieldChip`'s own label-rename editor just above it -- already wires an Escape-cancels handler, several with the file's own doc comments explicitly describing it as "the same Escape-cancels pattern." Round 715's own write-up never discusses or tests a cancel path for the draft it introduced.

**Concrete failure scenario**: the only two ways out of the draft were submitting the form (a real, unwanted network round-trip just to "close a dialog," which also leaves the draft stuck open if that PATCH happens to fail), or picking a genuinely different plain type from the still-visible `<select>` -- which commits immediately with no confirmation at all, silently wiping the field's `enumValues`/`relationTo` server-side, a real destructive action for someone who just wanted to close the dialog.

**The fix**: both draft forms (enum's text input, relation's target `<select>`) now close on Escape, and both gained an explicit Cancel button next to Confirm, mirroring `useRenamableSpecItem`'s own `cancelEditing()` pattern every sibling editor in this file already uses.

**Scope**: purely client-side UI state (`draftType`/`draftEnumValues`/`draftRelationTo`) -- no `apps/api` change needed. No `codegen.ts` parity concern either: this whole spec-review screen is pre-build-only, and `codegen.ts` has no spec-editing UI of any kind.

**The tests**: one new test per draft form, placed directly after the existing "clicking the edit button opens/commits the draft" tests for the same two forms -- confirms Escape (enum) and the new Cancel button (relation) both close the draft without ever calling the real PATCH type endpoint, and that the edit button reappears so the draft can be reopened.

**Verification**: both verified via genuine revert/restore, each isolating its own half of the fix. The enum/Escape test's first run against reverted code hung for 66+ seconds before being SIGKILLed -- traced to a real, previously-documented pitfall: asserting a DOM element directly against `null` (`assert.equal(element, null, ...)`) makes `node:assert`'s default diff formatter try to inspect the actual DOM node when the assertion fails, which hangs indefinitely on jsdom's circular/huge node structure. Rewriting it as a boolean comparison (`assert.equal(element === null, true, ...)`) made the same revert fail cleanly in under 2 seconds instead, exactly as predicted; restored, it passes. The relation/Cancel test was verified the same way, by temporarily removing just its own Cancel button -- failed with "expected a real Cancel button in the draft form" as predicted; restored, it passes. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 1113/1114 pass; the sole failure is `BuildProgress.test.ts`'s own already-documented recurring flake (an unrelated file, confirmed clean when re-run in isolation). `tsc -b` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 800: the inline table-cell editor had no guard against a live refine retyping its field

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Round number 800 reached -- this is the third occurrence of a bug class rounds 780 and 781 already fixed twice over, missed on a sibling that goes through the exact same dispatch.

**The gap**: a live refine retyping a field while `EntityPanel` stays mounted (it's keyed by `entity.name`, so a refine that only changes that same entity's field types never remounts it) can leave component-local draft state holding a value shaped for the OLD type, which `FieldInput`'s type-branch dispatch then renders nonsensically for the NEW type. Round 780 fixed this for `groupFieldName`, round 781 for its sibling `bulkEditField`/`bulkEditValue`, both via a `fieldTypesKey`-keyed effect. `editingCell`/`cellDraft` -- the in-progress inline table-cell editor, which goes through the exact same `FieldInput` dispatch -- was a third, structurally identical piece of state left with no analogous guard.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this is literally the same "missed sibling" shape rounds 795 (a 4th copy of `pickDisplayField`) and 772 (a missing port of round 770's fix) already demonstrated as a recurring pattern in this codebase -- a fix applied correctly to two structurally identical pieces of state, never checked against a third one using the exact same mechanism.

**Concrete failure scenario**: double-click an enum "Status" cell to inline-edit it; `cellDraft` is seeded with the stored value, e.g. "Shipped". Before the cell is blurred, a refine (the user's own concurrent instruction, or a collaborator's on a shared project) completes and retypes "Status" to boolean. The still-open cell re-renders through `FieldInput`'s boolean branch with `cellDraft` unchanged -- `checked={Boolean("Shipped")}` is `true`, so the checkbox renders pre-checked even though the user never touched it. Blurring normally then PATCHes the unchanged string "Shipped" against the now-boolean field; the server's own validation rejects it, surfacing a confusing error on a row the user believes they never edited -- and `editingCell` is already cleared by then, so there's no way to see or fix what caused it.

**The fix**: unlike `groupFieldName`/`bulkEditField` (which reset to a sensible empty value for the new type, since those are standing selections worth keeping), there's no "still useful" draft here once the field underneath an in-progress edit has changed shape -- the fix cancels the edit outright via the exact same `cancelInlineEdit()` an explicit Escape already uses, so the stale `cellDraft` is never fed into whichever control `FieldInput` now renders for the field's new type.

**Scope**: purely client-side React state (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`). No `apps/api` change needed -- the server's own field-type validation on PATCH was already correct; it's the lack of a client-side pre-emptive reset that was missing. No `codegen.ts` parity concern: the exported standalone app's schema is frozen at export time, with no live-refine concept at all.

**The test**: mirrors round 781's own bulk-edit regression test exactly -- renders a Deal entity with an enum "status" field, double-clicks the cell to open the inline editor (confirming it's pre-filled with the real stored value), then rerenders with the same `entity.name` but "status" retyped to boolean (simulating a live refine with no remount). Confirms the editing cell closes outright and no checkbox ever renders in it.

**Verification**: reverted just the new cancelling effect and reran -- the test failed cleanly in under 2 seconds with "the in-progress edit must be cancelled outright..." exactly as predicted (no hang -- this test's own DOM-vs-null checks were written as boolean comparisons from the start, per round 799's freshly-learned lesson). Restored, it passes. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 1115/1115 pass, no flakes. `tsc -b` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 801: stale `selectedAnswers`/`additionalRequest` survived a failed build's "Back" button

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The same "clear the answer state before returning to spec review" invariant four other call sites already enforce, missed on the one sibling that uses a bare inline arrow function instead of a named handler.

**The gap**: `handleBackToHome`, `handleGoHome`, the `subscribeAuthExpired` effect, and `handleAccountDeleted` all treat clearing `selectedAnswers`/`additionalRequest` as a known, named invariant whenever they leave or return to the pre-build spec-review screen -- each with its own near-identical doc comment ("those answered the now-abandoned draft's own open questions, not whatever gets created next"). The one remaining path that also lands back on that exact screen -- `BuildProgress`'s own "Back" button after a failed build -- was wired as a bare `onBack={() => setView("spec")}` with no cleanup at all.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this is the same "missed sibling" shape as rounds 772, 780/781/800, and 795 -- a cleanup rule independently enforced at several call sites, never checked against the one remaining path that reaches the identical screen.

**Concrete failure scenario**: a user answers the spec's open questions and/or types an additional request, then clicks Build. `handleBuild` pairs each answer with its question by array index and `POST`s to `/projects/:id/answers`, which calls `generateSpec()` again and fully replaces `project.spec` -- including a brand-new `openQuestions` array with a different set of questions, a different count, and a different order from whatever `selectedAnswers` was keyed against. The real `/build` pipeline then starts on this new spec. If that build fails (a real, reachable case -- `BuildProgress` shows "Back" precisely when a step errors), the user lands back on the spec screen showing the NEW `openQuestions`, but `selectedAnswers`/`additionalRequest` still hold the OLD values from before the first Build click. Clicking Build again without re-touching every chip re-pairs a NEW question at index `i` with a STALE answer written for a completely different, now-gone question at that same index -- silently feeding a mismatched question/answer pair into another real `generateSpec()` call, with zero error or warning shown anywhere.

**The fix**: the "building" view's `onBack` callback now clears `selectedAnswers`/`additionalRequest` before switching back to the spec view, the exact same cleanup `handleBackToHome`/`handleGoHome` already do.

**Not a controlled-element risk**: `selectedAnswers` drives plain `<button>` className comparisons and a controlled `<input type="text">`, never a `<select>`/checkbox/radio whose own native DOM semantics could mask staleness the way a prior round's rejected `HistoryPanel` candidate turned out to be -- this is pure stale React state, confirmed by reading the server route directly (`POST /answers` really does call `generateSpec()` again and really does replace `openQuestions`).

**Scope**: purely client-side (`apps/web`, the pre-build authoring flow). No `codegen.ts` parity concern -- the exported standalone app has no multi-step AI spec-review/open-questions flow at all; it runs from an already-finalized spec.

**The test**: extracts the real `onBack` callback from `App.tsx` the same way the existing `handleBackToHome`/`handleGoHome` tests extract their own functions, and confirms it clears both pieces of state (while still navigating back to `"spec"`) the same way those two already do.

**Verification**: reverted via two separate cycles. First, reverting the callback back to its original bare one-liner made the test fail immediately with "expected to find the building view's onBack callback" (the regex no longer matches). Second, a more rigorous revert keeping the comment block but removing only the two state-clearing calls made the test fail on the actual assertion instead -- confirming the test catches the real logic gap, not just text matching. Restored, it passes both times. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 1116/1116 pass, no flakes. `tsc -b` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 802: the exported app's own README promised automatic field migration that never existed

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A documentation/implementation drift: the generated README confidently asserts behavior the adjacent code never implemented.

**The gap**: `renderServerJs`'s schema-creation loop ran exactly one statement per entity -- `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` -- a documented no-op once the table already exists (the same SQLite semantics `packages/shared`'s own `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` comment describes elsewhere in this codebase). A field added to the exported app's `ENTITIES` array after the very first run was never actually added to the real table.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this directly contradicts the generated README's own "Extending it" section, which confidently tells the user: "Add a field to an entity... then restart -- existing columns are kept, and SQLite migrates new ones automatically (`ALTER TABLE`, same as Forge AI's own migration engine)." `packages/db/src/migrate.ts` (the live preview's equivalent) has real, carefully-built `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` migration logic with extensive commentary on SQLite's additive-only semantics -- the team clearly solved this problem correctly for the live app, it was just never ported here. Unlike other known/deferred gaps in this same file (which carry an explicit disclaimer), there is no such disclaimer anywhere near the schema-creation loop or the README's migration claim.

**Concrete failure scenario**: following the README's own instructions -- the one thing it tells a non-technical user they can safely do themselves -- silently does nothing to the schema. Every subsequent POST/PATCH touching the new field hits a raw, untranslated "table X has no column named Y" SQLite error, not caught by either of this file's two specific error-translation branches (which only special-case the literal "FOREIGN KEY constraint failed" string), so it falls through to the generic 400 handler and surfaces the confusing raw message verbatim. This doesn't show up during export-time testing -- a brand-new `data.sqlite` always gets every column right via the first `CREATE TABLE` -- it only manifests on the SECOND schema change after the first real run, outside the obvious "does the export work" smoke test.

**The fix**: mirrors `migrate.ts`'s own additive-only approach exactly, scoped to what the README actually promises (new columns, not type/relation-target changes, which `migrate.ts` itself treats as a separate, harder problem the exported app's README never claims to solve either): after `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, query `PRAGMA table_info` for the table's real current columns, and `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` for any field in `ENTITIES` missing from it. `NOT NULL` is deliberately never added retroactively (SQLite can't satisfy it against existing rows -- required-ness is still enforced by this same file's own `coerce()` for every write going forward), and a relation field still gets its `REFERENCES` clause, same as a brand-new table already gets. A pure no-op for a table that was just `CREATE`d fresh in the same pass.

**codegen.ts parity**: this *is* the fix -- `apps/web` has no counterpart feature (the live preview's own `migrate.ts` already does this correctly), so there's nothing to port anywhere else.

**The test**: spawns the real generated `server.js` twice against the SAME on-disk `data.sqlite` file across a real process restart -- not just reading the schema-creation source text, mirroring the existing keyword-entity end-to-end test's own real-spawn convention. First run: one field, one record created. Second run: the same entity regenerated with an added field, same data directory. Confirms the pre-existing record survived with the new column simply unset, and a new write using the added field succeeds via a real migrated column instead of failing with a raw SQLite error.

**Verification**: reverted the `ALTER TABLE` loop and reran -- the test failed exactly as predicted, with the added field missing entirely from the API response (`undefined`, not even `null`) for the pre-existing record; restored, it passes. Only `apps/api` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 584/585 pass; the sole failure is the already-documented pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` process-exit hang flake, stopping at the identical subtest it has in every round's log since 787 -- confirmed unrelated, and the new test itself ran and passed inside this full run. `npm run build` (esbuild bundle) clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 803: deleting the automation rule currently open for editing left the form stuck mid-edit

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The exact hazard class EntityPanel.tsx already learned to guard, never ported to its own close structural sibling.

**The gap**: the rule list's own Delete button stays clickable on every row regardless of which one (if any) is currently open for editing below -- both the list and the single shared create/edit form are on screen at the same time. `handleDelete` never checked or cleared `editingRuleId`, so deleting the exact rule the form was mid-edit on left `editingRuleId` pointing at an id that no longer exists on the server.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this exact hazard class -- deleting the very record currently open in an edit form -- was already identified and fixed in this app's own structurally-similar sibling, `EntityPanel.tsx`: its in-form Delete button only resets `editingId`/form once the delete actually went through. `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s own `editingRuleId`/`handleStartEdit`/`resetToCreateMode` machinery is itself a close structural parallel to `EntityPanel`'s `editingId`/`startEdit`/`emptyForm` reset pattern, but the one case `EntityPanel` already learned to guard was never ported over when this edit feature was added here. The existing test suite had three dedicated tests for the Edit flow (seed-on-edit, submit-and-return-to-create-mode, Cancel-discards-edit) but none for delete-while-editing, confirming this interaction was simply never considered.

**Concrete failure scenario**: click Edit on a rule (the form seeds from it, heading reads "Edit rule", entity select locks, a Cancel button appears). Without saving, click that same rule's own Delete button (still visible in the list above) and confirm. The DELETE succeeds and the row disappears, but the form keeps showing "Edit rule", pre-filled with the now-deleted rule's stale data, with a visible "Save changes" button -- nothing on screen signals that saving is already impossible. Clicking it correctly 404s with `AUTOMATION_RULE_NOT_FOUND`, but the form stays stuck in this broken edit state with no way out except manually clicking Cancel.

**The fix**: `handleDelete` now checks `editingRuleId === rule.id` after a successful delete and calls `resetToCreateMode()` if so, returning the form to a clean create-mode state instead of leaving it dangling on a rule that's already gone.

**Scope**: `apps/api` needs no fix -- the server already does the right thing (a clean, idempotent 404 via `getAutomationRule`/`NotFoundError`); the bug was purely client-side stale state. No `codegen.ts` parity concern -- the exported standalone app has no Automations feature at all (it requires the live server's own WhatsApp integration).

**Not a controlled-element risk**: `editingRuleId` is a plain string id driving which branch of a conditional render shows, not a `<select>`/checkbox/radio whose own native DOM value could mask staleness -- verified entirely by reading `handleDelete`, `handleSubmit`'s edit branch, and the server route directly.

**The test**: opens Edit on the one existing rule, confirms the form is genuinely in edit mode, then clicks that same rule's own Delete button and confirms. Asserts the form returns to create mode (heading, unlocked entity select, no Cancel button, blank message field) instead of staying stuck on "Edit rule" for a deleted id -- and that the mock fetch never receives a PATCH for the deleted rule.

**Verification**: reverted just the new `editingRuleId` check and reran -- the test failed exactly as predicted ("Edit rule" instead of "New rule"); restored, it passes. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 1117/1117 pass, no flakes. `tsc -b` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 804: a collapsed Table-view group kept leaking out of Export CSV/Copy/Print once the user switched to Board or Calendar view

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A view-mode-agnostic piece of state feeding a view-mode-agnostic toolbar, with the one case that actually matters never gated.

**The gap**: `effectivelyVisibleRecords` -- the record set `handleExportCsv`/`handleCopy`/the print-list sheet all read when nothing is selected -- applied its "exclude a collapsed group's records" filter unconditionally, with no `viewMode` check at all. `groupFieldName`/`collapsedGroups` are set only from Table view (the Group-by `<select>` itself only renders there), but once set they're ordinary view-mode-agnostic state that survives switching to Board or Calendar.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this file already has the identical fix for a structurally identical hazard, one effect above: `selectedIds` is also view-mode-agnostic state read unconditionally by the same three toolbar buttons, and an existing effect (`if (viewMode !== "table") setSelectedIds(new Set())`, with its own doc comment spelling out exactly this "view-mode-agnostic state feeding unconditional toolbar buttons" risk) already clears it the moment the user leaves Table view. `groupFieldName`/`collapsedGroups` sit right next to `selectedIds` in the same component, feed the exact same three buttons, and were simply never given the same treatment -- the same "missed sibling" shape as rounds 772/780/781/793/795/796/800/801/803.

**Concrete failure scenario**: group the table by "status", collapse the "Won" group (now hidden from the table body, matching rounds 487/499's own established, already-tested behavior), then switch to Board view. Board renders every record from the flat `visibleRecords` with no "collapsed" concept of its own -- every "Won" record visibly shows up as its own card, with nothing on screen suggesting anything is hidden. Click Export CSV (or Copy, or Print list): the downloaded CSV/clipboard text/print sheet silently omits every "Won" record anyway, because `effectivelyVisibleRecords` kept applying Table view's own collapse filter regardless of the screen now showing everything. No warning anywhere -- the exported data simply disagrees with what the user is looking at.

**The fix**: `effectivelyVisibleRecords` now only applies the collapse filter when `viewMode === "table"`; outside Table view it falls back to the flat `visibleRecords`, matching what Board/Calendar actually render. Deliberately not the alternative of clearing `groupFieldName` itself on leaving Table view (the `selectedIds` effect's own approach) -- that would also silently discard the user's chosen grouping and collapsed sections the moment they peek at Board view, forcing them to re-group and re-collapse on returning to Table. Gating the one `useMemo` that actually matters preserves that state untouched.

**codegen.ts parity**: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` duplicates `effectivelyVisibleRecords`, the three toolbar buttons, and the Group-by select identically (its own doc comment on `effectivelyVisibleRecords` literally says "Mirrors the live preview's own effectivelyVisibleRecords (EntityPanel.tsx)") -- given the identical gate.

**Not a controlled-element risk**: `groupFieldName`/`collapsedGroups` drive a plain array/Set filter inside a `useMemo`, not a `<select>`/checkbox/radio whose own native DOM semantics could mask staleness the way the round-799 rejected `HistoryPanel` candidate turned out to -- confirmed by reading `effectivelyVisibleRecords`, the three toolbar buttons' `onClick` handlers, and the Board/Calendar render branches directly in both files before writing any code.

**The tests**: one new test per file, each grouping by "status", collapsing "Won", confirming the table itself still correctly hides it (reusing rounds 487/499's own established assertions), then switching to Board view and confirming Board shows all 3 cards (proving Board has no collapse concept of its own) before clicking Export CSV and asserting the exported CSV now includes every record, including the ones collapsed back in Table view.

**Verification**: reverted just the `viewMode === "table"` gate in each file and reran its own new test -- both failed exactly as predicted (the exported CSV was still missing the two "Won" records even after switching to Board view); restored, both pass. Both packages changed this round, so both full suites ran: `apps/web` 1119/1119 pass (including the new test), no flakes; `apps/api` 585-586/586, the sole failure being the already-documented pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` process-exit hang flake (varies 1-2 failures between runs, stopping at the identical subtest logged in every round since 787) -- confirmed unrelated, and the new test itself passed inside both full runs. `tsc -b` (apps/web) clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 805: a retyped field's stale value in the add/edit record form could render as a bogus pre-checked checkbox

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The fourth sibling in an already-established, numbered series -- found, verified, and finished by this round.

**The gap**: the main add/edit record form's own `form` state (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`) is keyed by field name and dispatched through the exact same `FieldInput` type-branch as three other surfaces already fixed for the identical hazard -- but `form` holds one value per EVERY field at once (unlike those three, each a single selected field name), and the effect that resets it (`setForm(emptyForm(entity))`) depends only on `[entity.name]`, never on `fieldTypesKey`, so it never fires when a field retypes in place while the panel stays mounted.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this is the fourth instance of the exact same "field TYPE changes while its NAME survives a live refine" bug class, already identified and fixed three times in a row for its siblings -- `groupFieldName` (round 780), `bulkEditField`/`bulkEditValue` (round 781), and `editingCell`/`cellDraft` (round 800) -- each fix's own doc comment explicitly citing the prior one as its template. The add/edit form is the most heavily used of the four surfaces and the only one that sends an unfiltered whole-object payload on create, yet it never received any of the `fieldTypesKey`-driven guards the other three got.

**Concrete failure scenario**: an entity has an enum field "priority" (Low/Medium/High). A user opens the create (or edit) form and picks "High". While the form is still open, a Refine finishes in the background retyping "priority" from enum to boolean while keeping the same field name -- the panel doesn't remount. `FieldInput`'s boolean branch (`checked={Boolean(value)}`) now renders `Boolean("High")` → a pre-checked checkbox the user never touched. For a NEW record, submitting sends the whole `form` object verbatim (unlike editing, which already diffs against a snapshot -- round 644), so the server's `coerceValue` rejects the entire create over one field the user never meant to set (confirmed directly in `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s boolean case, which throws `ValidationError` for anything outside `true/false/1/0`). For an EDIT, it's worse: if the user, confused by the bogus checked box, unchecks it, that now genuinely differs from the original snapshot and gets silently included in the PATCH as a real, unintended data change.

**Not a controlled-element risk**: the affected control is a plain `<input type="checkbox">`, not a `<select>` -- there is no native "remove the selected option" reset algorithm that could mask this the way the round-799 rejected `HistoryPanel` candidate turned out to. Confirmed by reading `FieldInput`'s boolean branch, the form's own `<FieldInput>` call site, `handleSubmit`, and `coerceValue` directly before writing any code.

**codegen.ts parity**: not needed -- grepped for `fieldTypesKey`/`groupedFieldTypeRef`/`bulkEditFieldTypeRef`/`editingCellFieldTypeRef`-equivalents in `codegen.ts`: none exist. The exported standalone app's schema is frozen at export time; there is no "a Refine retypes a field while a record form is open" scenario there at all.

**The test**: fills in both the required "name" field and the enum field in the (always-visible) create form, then `rerender`s with the same entity name but the enum field retyped to boolean -- the identical live-refine, no-remount scenario the three sibling tests already exercise. Confirms the checkbox renders unchecked (not coerced from the stale "High" string) and that the untouched "name" field still shows exactly what the user typed, proving the fix resets only the retyped field.

**Verification**: reverted the new effect and reran -- the test failed exactly as predicted (`checkbox.checked` was `true`); restored, it passes. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 1119/1119 pass, no flakes. `tsc -b` clean.

### Round 806: a fifth sibling of the "field TYPE changes while NAME survives" bug class, found outside EntityPanel.tsx -- AutomationsPanel's own field_equals form

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The same bug class as rounds 780/781/800/805, but in a completely different surface that doesn't even go through `FieldInput`.

**The gap**: `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s field_equals form has three effects keeping `fieldName`/`toField`/`fieldValue` pointed at a real, type-appropriate field/value -- but all three were keyed only on `[entityName]` or `[fieldName]` (the field's own *name*, which survives a retype), never on the field's *type*. The panel is mounted once per `showAutomations` toggle and keeps receiving the live `entities` prop straight from `App.tsx`'s own `project` state (no `key` prop, no remount), so a background Refine retyping a field in place is exactly as reachable here as it was for EntityPanel.tsx's four already-fixed siblings.

**Why this is not deliberate**: the identical hazard -- "a field's name survives a live refine, but its type changes under a still-open form" -- was already identified and fixed four times in `EntityPanel.tsx` (`groupFieldName` round 780, `bulkEditField`/`bulkEditValue` round 781, `editingCell`/`cellDraft` round 800, the main record `form` round 805), each via a `fieldTypesKey`-driven dependency specifically because a `[fieldName]`-only (or `[entityName]`-only) effect is insufficient. None of those four sweeps ever looked at `AutomationsPanel.tsx`, since it has its own inline boolean/enum/relation rendering rather than routing through `FieldInput` -- but the underlying risk (a field-name-keyed effect missing a same-name type change) is structurally identical. An existing, deliberate comment right next to this code (lines 159-164) shows the author was already thinking about field staleness for *entity switches* -- just never extended to an in-place type change.

**Concrete failure scenario**: an entity has an enum field "priority" (Low/High). A user opens Automations, picks trigger "field_equals", field "priority", value "High". While the form is still open, a Refine retypes "priority" from enum to boolean, keeping the same name -- the panel doesn't remount. The Value control correctly reads the live field type and renders a checkbox, but `fieldValue` is still the stale string "High"; since `fieldValue === "true"` is false, the checkbox renders **unchecked** -- a plausible-looking but actually-invalid state. Submitting sends `fieldValue: "High"` for a now-boolean field straight to the server, which correctly rejects it, but with a confusing error that has nothing to do with what the user sees on screen (an apparently-correct, unchecked box).

**Not masked by native `<select>` semantics (the methodology-warning case)**: this candidate was checked carefully against the round-799 `HistoryPanel` trap because `fieldName`/`toField` genuinely are controlled `<select>` elements whose selected `<option>` can disappear (e.g. a field retyping to `file`, excluded from `triggerableFields`). But unlike `HistoryPanel`'s `resolveCompareSpec`, which already had a defensive `?? fallback` wherever the stale id was *consumed* (so the native reset coincidentally produced the same correct behavior with or without the fix), `handleSubmit` here reads the raw `fieldName`/`fieldValue`/`toField` state variables directly with no such fallback -- the bug is in the *submitted payload*, not the visual selection, so it is unaffected by whatever the browser's option-removal algorithm does on screen. The clearest sub-case proving this needs no `<select>` reset at all: the boolean-checkbox scenario above uses a plain `<input type="checkbox">`, not a `<select>`, so there is no native reset mechanism in play whatsoever.

**The fix**: a new `fieldTypesKey` (`selectedEntity.fields.map(f => \`${f.name}:${f.type}\`).join(",")`, mirroring `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own), added to the dependency array of all three affected effects (the `entityName`-keyed field/toField validity check, the `fieldName`-keyed boolean/enum value reset, and the `fieldName`-keyed relation value reset) -- each effect already re-validates against the live field types on every fire, so simply re-running them on a type change (not just a name/selection change) was sufficient; no new reset logic was needed.

**codegen.ts parity**: not needed -- confirmed via `grep -ni automation apps/api/src/codegen.ts`: the only hit is an unrelated comment mentioning the word "automation" in passing. The exported standalone app has no Automations feature at all (it requires the live server's own WhatsApp integration, same as the already-closed round-803 finding notes).

**The test**: selects an enum field and sets its value to "High" in the (always-visible) create form, then `rerender`s with the same entity name but the field retyped to boolean -- the identical live-refine, no-remount scenario the four `EntityPanel.tsx` sibling tests already exercise. Confirms the checkbox resets to its own normal boolean default (checked/"true", the same default a freshly-selected boolean field already gets) rather than staying on the stale, plausible-looking-but-invalid unchecked state, and that submitting sends that valid "true" instead of the stale "High".

**Verification**: reverted the three `fieldTypesKey` dependencies and reran -- the test failed exactly as predicted (`checkbox.checked` was `false`, the stale/invalid state); restored, it passes. Only `apps/web` changed this round, so its own full suite ran: 1120/1120 pass, no flakes. `tsc -b` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 807: docs/security.md and README.md still claimed RBAC, password reset, and auth rate limiting don't exist -- all three had already shipped

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A different bug class from every prior round this window: not a runtime logic gap, but the one document whose explicit job is "what's safe to assume" actively lying about three already-shipped safety features.

**The gap**: `docs/security.md`'s "Explicitly not addressed yet (do not assume these exist)" section said "No RBAC / organizations... no read-only... permission level exists yet", its "Addressed" section said "There is no email verification and no password reset flow yet", and its rate-limiting bullet named `/api/auth/signup` as unprotected. `README.md`'s own Security section repeated the same three claims in one line ("there's no rate limiting, email verification, or password reset yet").

A reader following that instruction sees the bolded "do not assume these exist" heading directly above the false RBAC claim and concludes they need to build their own read-only/sharing permission layer before inviting outside collaborators -- duplicating work that's already done and tested -- or concludes password recovery is unavailable and tells a real user "there's no way to recover your account," when a working `/auth/forgot-password` flow already exists and is reachable from the login screen.

**Verified directly against the current code (not just commit messages)** before editing anything: `requireProjectWriteAccess` (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) returns 403 `VIEWER_READ_ONLY` and is called ~40 times, covering every mutating route in that file; `CollaboratorRole` (`packages/db/src/collaborators.ts`) is a real `"editor" | "viewer"` type surfaced in `CollaboratorsPanel.tsx`'s role picker; `POST /api/auth/forgot-password` and `POST /api/auth/reset-password` (`apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts`) are real, enumeration-safe, hashed-token routes; `createRateLimiter` (`apps/api/src/auth/rateLimit.ts`) is wired to signup/login/forgot-password in `routes/auth.ts`. Also confirmed the inverse -- `routes/projects.ts`/`app.ts` never import `createRateLimiter` at all, so `POST /api/projects`/`.../refine` genuinely remain unprotected, and email verification is genuinely still absent -- so the fix narrows rather than deletes those two specific gaps.

**The fix**: moved the real editor/viewer RBAC and the real password-reset flow from "Explicitly not addressed yet" into "Addressed", with their actual enforcement points named; narrowed the rate-limiting bullet and the "Before any real deployment" checklist to the two still-genuinely-unprotected LLM-calling endpoints instead of also naming the now-rate-limited `/api/auth/signup`; renamed "No RBAC / organizations" to "No organizations / workspaces" (the still-accurate half of that claim -- no `Workspace`/`WorkspaceMember` grouping concept, no entity-scoped permission level -- kept, the now-false "no roles at all" half removed). `README.md`'s one-line Security summary updated to match.

**Scope**: docs-only, no application code changed -- no test suite or build to run, no `apps/web`/`apps/api`/`codegen.ts` parity question applies.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 808: automation_rules' three list queries missed the rowid tiebreak every other createdAt-sorted listing query in packages/db already has

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A "missed sibling" within `packages/db` itself -- one table's listing queries predate a house convention established for every other table, and were never backfilled.

**The gap**: `listAutomationRules`, `listEnabledAutomationRulesForEntity`, and `listEnabledScheduledRules` (`packages/db/src/automations.ts`) all sorted purely by `ORDER BY createdAt ASC`. `createdAt` is a `new Date().toISOString()` string with only millisecond resolution, so two rules created in the same millisecond (two collaborators each adding one, a doubled "Save rule" click, or two browser tabs) leave that tie's relative order unspecified by SQL.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this codebase already closed the identical gap for `checkpoints.ts`'s `listCheckpoints` and `projects.ts`'s `listProjectsForOwner`, each with a doc comment explaining the exact same millisecond-collision reasoning and citing the other as precedent, and `whatsapp.ts`'s keyset-paginated queries use the same pattern. Most tellingly, this *same file*'s own `listAutomationRuns` (for the sibling `automation_runs` table) already has the identical `rowid DESC` tiebreak -- proving the convention was actively applied here, just never backfilled onto the three older `automation_rules` queries that predate it.

**Concrete failure scenario**: `listAutomationRules` feeds `GET /projects/:id/automations`, rendered as-is by `AutomationsPanel.tsx` with no client-side re-sort -- a tie's display order is left to whatever the DB happens to return, so a user could see their automation rules reorder between panel reopens for no apparent reason. Worse, `listEnabledAutomationRulesForEntity` (the hot path evaluated on every record create/update) and `listEnabledScheduledRules` (the global periodic scheduler) use the same unordered-tie query to decide which rule's action fires first -- for two tied rules this isn't just a display cosmetic, it's an unspecified *firing* order (e.g. which of two webhooks fires first).

**The fix**: added `, rowid ASC` to all three `ORDER BY createdAt ASC` clauses, matching `rowid`'s natural insertion-order correspondence for an ascending sort (mirroring the exact tiebreak-direction logic `listAutomationRuns`/`listCheckpoints`/`listProjectsForOwner` already use for their own sort directions).

**codegen.ts parity**: not needed -- the exported standalone app has no automations feature at all (`AutomationRule`/`automation_rules`: zero matches in `codegen.ts`).

**An important, candid verification note**: writing a real regression test (two synchronous inserts landing in the same millisecond, the same technique `projects.test.ts`'s own precedent test uses) did NOT reproduce an observable failure when the fix was reverted -- `node:sqlite`'s current table-scan-then-sort query plan for this query happens to already return ties in `rowid` order even without the explicit tiebreak. Checked whether this was specific to the new fix by reverting `projects.ts`'s own long-established, already-shipped `rowid DESC` tiebreak and rerunning *its* existing precedent test: it also passed without its own fix, in this exact environment. So this isn't a property of the new code -- every tiebreak fix of this shape in this codebase currently can't be forced to fail via a revert-and-rerun check in this specific engine/version, unlike the round-799 `HistoryPanel` case (which was a genuine false positive, masked by a *guaranteed* browser spec behavior). Here, SQL explicitly leaves `ORDER BY` ties *unspecified* -- today's deterministic-seeming behavior is an implementation detail of the current query plan (no index on `createdAt`, forcing a full table scan + sort), not a guarantee; a different index, a different SQLite build, or a future upgrade could silently change it. Shipped anyway, consistent with the three existing precedents that apply the identical defensive convention for the identical reason -- but documented here plainly rather than overclaiming the new tests "catch a regression," since they don't in this environment.

**Scope**: `packages/db` only -- `apps/api`'s own full suite was also run (consumes these functions through `apps/api/src/automations.ts`) since the change affects shared, cross-workspace runtime SQL behavior: 585/586 pass, the sole failure being the already-documented pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` process-exit hang flake, confirmed unrelated. `packages/db`'s own full suite: 213/213 pass, including the three new tests.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 811: the feminine "מנהלת מערכת" sibling of round 659's Manager/Admin substring collision

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A real code bug this round, after three docs-only rounds -- the "missed sibling" pattern recurring inside the Hebrew heuristic spec provider's own role-matching table.

**The gap**: round 659 fixed Manager's bare `"מנהל"` keyword spuriously matching inside Admin's own `"מנהל מערכת"` ("system admin") phrase, via a negative lookahead `(?!\s*מערכת)`. The feminine form `"מנהלת מערכת"` ("female system admin") has the identical substring collision -- `"מנהלת"` contains `"מנהל"` as its own first four letters, immediately followed by `"ת"` rather than `"מערכת"`, so round 659's lookahead never fires for it; and a separate, unguarded bare `"מנהלת"` keyword matched it outright regardless.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this file's own adjacent comment explicitly groups `"מנהל"`/`"מנהלת"`/`"מנהלים"` as one interchangeable word family, and round 659's own regression test comment ("The real word still works on its own (via 'מנהלת'/'ניהול'...)") shows the author was aware `"מנהלת"` was a separate, untested code path -- just never circled back to apply the identical fix to it.

**Concrete failure scenario, verified empirically (not just read from source)**: calling the real `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` with "האפליקציה מיועדת למנהלת מערכת אחת בלבד, בלי תפקידים אחרים" (a description naming only a female system admin) returned `roles = ["מנהל/ת" (Manager), "מנהל/ת ראשי/ת" (Admin)]` -- the generic Member fallback (`matchRoles` only adds it when exactly one role matched) was silently suppressed by the bogus extra Manager role, the exact same wrong outcome round 659 fixed for the masculine phrasing.

**The fix**: merged the masculine and feminine cases into a single lookahead, `/מנהל(?!ת?\s*מערכת)/` (the `ת` made optional), replacing both the old `/מנהל(?!\s*מערכת)/` regex and the separate unguarded `"מנהלת"` literal. Verified against all four cases directly with Node's own regex engine before touching the test file: excludes both `"מנהל מערכת"` and `"מנהלת מערכת"`, while still matching a standalone `"מנהל"`/`"מנהלת"` (e.g. a store manager) correctly.

**Scope**: lives entirely in `packages/spec-engine` (the offline heuristic fallback provider, used when no LLM API key is configured) -- no `apps/web`, `apps/api` route, or `codegen.ts` counterpart, since spec generation happens once, server-side, before any app code is generated.

**The test**: mirrors round 659's own test exactly, substituting the feminine phrase -- confirms the female-system-admin-only description gets no spurious Manager role and does get the Member fallback, and that the real "מנהלת חנות" (female store manager) phrasing still correctly adds Manager.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- the test failed exactly as predicted (`AssertionError`, Manager was present); restored, it passes. Only `packages/spec-engine` changed, so its own full suite ran: 156/156 pass. `apps/api`'s full suite (consumes `@forge/spec-engine` for spec generation) was also run since this is a cross-workspace dependency change: 585/586 pass, the sole failure being the already-documented pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` process-exit hang flake, confirmed unrelated.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 812: Vehicle's bare "garage" keyword never got plural support, unlike every sibling keyword in the same rule -- and unlike its own Hebrew plural, already fixed once before

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. Another "missed sibling" inside `packages/spec-engine`'s keyword-collision rules, this time a plain English singular/plural gap, found via the same fresh sweep style round 811 used.

**The gap**: round 454 `\b`-bounded Vehicle's bare `"garage"` keyword and added a negative lookahead excluding `"garage sale(s)"` -- but never added plural support for `"garage"` itself, unlike literally the next keyword in the same array (`/\bmechanic(s)?\b/`) and every other `\b`-bounded keyword in this file (`driver(s)?`, `worker(s)?`, `service(s)?`, `product(s)?`, etc.). Because `\b` only fires at a transition between a word character and a non-word character, `/\bgarage\b/` cannot match inside `"garages"` at all -- there's no boundary between `"garage"` and the trailing `"s"`.

**The fix**: `/\bgarage\b(?!\s+sales?\b)/` → `/\bgarages?\b(?!\s+sales?\b)/`, mirroring the `sales?` plural handling already present in the same regex's own lookahead. Verified directly with Node's regex engine against all four cases (`"garage"`, `"garages"`, `"garage sale"`, `"garage sales"`) before touching any test.

**The test**: added next to round 454's own existing test -- confirms the plural-only description now matches Vehicle, and that the `"garage sale(s)"` exclusion still holds (re-verified end-to-end with the real provider, not just the regex in isolation) so the plural change doesn't reopen the original round-454 gap.

### Round 813: Courier's bare "שליח" keyword spuriously matched "sending X"/"errand(s)" -- a third consecutive missed-sibling finding in domainEntities.ts

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A third round in a row finding the same class of bug in `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s keyword-collision rules -- this time a plain, unbounded Hebrew substring collision rather than a gender pair (811) or an English plural (812).

**The gap**: Courier's bare `"שליח"` ("courier"/"messenger") keyword is matched via plain `.includes()` substring matching (`matchesKeyword`, `heuristic.ts`), not a bounded regex. It's a literal 4-letter prefix of the construct-state `"שליחת"` ("sending of ___", extremely common phrasing: `"שליחת הודעות"`/`"שליחת חוזים"`/`"שליחת ניוזלטרים"`/`"שליחת מכתבים"`) and of the unrelated noun `"שליחות"`/`"שליחויות"` ("errand(s)") -- neither has anything to do with delivery drivers.

**Why this is not deliberate**: the Courier rule's own inline comments carefully discuss two *other* collisions for this exact keyword list ("driver" ⊂ "screwdriver"/"webdriver", and the "delivery person"/"delivery people" irregular-plural gap fixed in round 584) -- the author audited this rule for collisions twice and still missed this one. No comment anywhere claims it's intentional, and no existing test exercises or protects this case.

**Concrete failure scenario, verified empirically end-to-end** (not just the regex in isolation): calling the real `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` with zero other Courier keywords present in any input --
- "אפליקציה לשליחת חוזים לחתימה דיגיטלית" (an app for sending contracts for digital signature) → `entities: ["Courier"]` only, instead of falling back to the generic `DEFAULT_ENTITY`.
- "מערכת לשליחת ניוזלטרים למנויים" (a newsletter system) → `["Courier", "Subscription"]`, Courier pure noise.
- "אפליקציה לשליחת הודעות ללקוחות" (a customer-messaging app) → `["Customer", "Courier"]`, same noise.

**The fix**: `"שליח"` → `/שליח(?![תו])/`, narrowly scoped to exclude only the ת (construct-state "שליחת") and ו (errand noun "שליחות") continuations that are never a real courier reference. ### Round 814: a third inflection of the same Manager/Admin word family rounds 659 and 811 already fixed -- the Hebrew construct-state plural "מנהלי מערכת"

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A fourth consecutive round finding a real bug in `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts` -- the same word family as rounds 659 and 811, now a third grammatical inflection neither prior fix's lookahead covered.

**The gap**: rounds 659 and 811 excluded Manager's bare `"מנהל"` keyword from matching Admin's own `"מנהל מערכת"`/`"מנהלת מערכת"` (masculine/feminine "system admin") phrases via the lookahead `(?!ת?\s*מערכת)`. The Hebrew construct-state plural `"מנהלי מערכת"` ("system administrators") -- the standard, more natural phrasing for naming a role/permission group rather than one person (e.g. "רק מנהלי מערכת יכולים לגשת לדוחות") -- has the identical collision: after `"מנהל"` the next letter is `"י"`, not `"ת"` or whitespace, so neither prior lookahead fires for it.

**Why this is not deliberate**: this exact word family (`"מנהל"`/`"מנהלת"`/`"מנהלים"`) is explicitly treated as interchangeable by round 811's own comment, which merged two of its inflections into one lookahead -- but the construct-state plural form (grammatically distinct from the free-standing plural `"מנהלים"`) was never considered. `heuristic.test.ts` has explicit regression tests for the masculine (659) and feminine (811) singular forms, confirmed via grep, but none for the plural construct form -- this exact gap was never tested or noticed.

**Concrete failure scenario, verified empirically end-to-end**: calling the real `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` with "האפליקציה מיועדת למנהלי מערכת בלבד, בלי תפקידים אחרים" (a description naming only system administrators, plural) returned `roles: ["מנהל/ת" (Manager), "מנהל/ת ראשי/ת" (Admin)]` -- compare to the identical phrasing in the already-fixed singular forms, which correctly returns Admin + the generic Member fallback with no spurious Manager.

**The fix**: made the `"י"` optional alongside the existing `"ת"` in the lookahead -- `(?!ת?\s*מערכת)` → `(?!י?ת?\s*מערכת)` -- one pattern now covers all three inflections (masculine, feminine, construct-plural), while still matching a real standalone `"מנהל"`/`"מנהלת"`/`"מנהלי"` (e.g. `"מנהלי חנות"`, real plural store managers). Also checked whether Admin's own `"מנהל מערכת"` keyword needed a matching `"מנהלי מערכת"` sibling (it doesn't match the plural either, since the extra `"י"` breaks the contiguous substring) -- confirmed unnecessary: `matchRoles` adds Admin unconditionally regardless of its own keyword match (per its own doc comment in `heuristic.ts`), so only Manager's spurious match needed fixing.

**Scope**: lives entirely in `packages/spec-engine`, same scoping as rounds 811/813 -- no `apps/web` or `codegen.ts` counterpart, since this role-matching logic runs once, server-side, before any exported app code exists.

**The test**: added next to round 811's own existing test -- confirms the plural-construct-only description gets no spurious Manager role and does get the Member fallback, and that the real `"מנהלי חנות"` (plural store managers) phrasing still correctly adds Manager.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- the test failed exactly as predicted; restored, it passes. Also independently re-verified the real plural-manager case end-to-end with no regression. Only `packages/spec-engine` changed, so its own full suite ran: 159/159 pass. `apps/api`'s full suite was also run (cross-workspace dependency): 585/586 pass, the sole failure being the already-documented pre-existing `codegen.test.ts` process-exit hang flake, confirmed unrelated.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- the test failed exactly as predicted (`0 !== 7`, reproducing the real-world symptom precisely); restored, it passes. ### Round 817: Time Machine's diff/"Current" check never compared an entity's own description

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A code bug after a run of mostly-docs rounds followed by the GlobalSearch staleness pair -- this time in Time Machine's own diff/current-check logic.

**The gap**: `checkpointDiff.ts`'s `computeCheckpointDiff` and `isCheckpointCurrent` compare `summary`/`roles`/`personas`/`screens`/`assumptions`/`openQuestions` at the top level, and every field's `fieldSignature` per entity -- but never an entity's own `description`. Unlike a field/entity `label` (deliberately excluded here, per the file's own doc comment, as "cosmetic"), `description` is real, user-rendered content: `EntityPanel.tsx` shows it as `{entity.description && <p className="muted">{entity.description}</p>}`, right above every entity's own table/form.

**Why this is not deliberate**: the file's own structure proves the team already treats "does this property change what the user sees/does" as the test for inclusion -- `required` was added for exactly this reasoning (a prior round), and the top-level `isCheckpointCurrent` fields were each added one-by-one for the identical reason, per the function's own doc comment ("the live app's summary/role chips visibly differ... the opposite of what the doc comment above already promised"). `entity.description` sits in the exact same category but was simply never looked at -- no comment anywhere suggests it was ever considered and intentionally excluded, unlike `label`.

**Concrete failure scenario**: a `/refine` call that regenerates an entity's description (the AI rewording it, or a different heuristic match) while leaving every field untouched is a completely ordinary case. Opening Time Machine afterward: the diff view shows no changes at all for that entity (not even listed), even though the on-screen note under its tab now reads differently than what that checkpoint would restore; if this was the *only* difference, `isCheckpointCurrent` wrongly reports `true` -- the checkpoint gets the "Current" chip and its own Restore button is permanently disabled, even though restoring it would genuinely change the visible description text.

**The fix**: added `descriptionChanged` to `CheckpointDiff`'s `changedEntities` shape, set whenever an entity's `description` differs (even with every field byte-identical), and included it in the push condition so description-only changes are no longer invisible to the diff. Added the identical comparison to `isCheckpointCurrent`'s entity loop. `HistoryPanel.tsx` renders a new list item for a description-only change, with new he/en i18n keys (`history.diff.entityDescriptionChanged`).

**Scope**: `apps/web` only -- confirmed via `grep -n "checkpoint" apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (no matches): the exported standalone app has no Time Machine/checkpoint-history feature at all, the same conclusion prior rounds already reached for this file.

**The tests**: two new `checkpointDiff.test.ts` tests (an entity-description-only change is reported by `computeCheckpointDiff`, and identical-undefined descriptions on both sides are correctly NOT reported) plus one for `isCheckpointCurrent`, mirroring the existing `required`-flag test pair exactly. One new `HistoryPanel.test.ts` DOM-level test confirms the real rendered message appears instead of "No changes." Updated 9 existing `checkpointDiff.test.ts` fixtures whose `assert.deepEqual` calls needed the new `descriptionChanged: false` field added to their expected objects (none of their scenarios involve a description change, confirmed by checking none of their fixtures set `description` at all).

**Verification**: reverted the fix (temporarily neutralizing just the two behavioral checks, not the type-shape change the other 9 tests depend on) and reran -- both new `checkpointDiff.test.ts` behavioral tests failed exactly as predicted; restored, all 3 pass. The `HistoryPanel.test.ts` test also failed without the fix (a module-level crash before reaching the detail-text assertion -- still a valid "module-load crash is a strong confirmation" per this session's own established convention) and passed once restored. Full `apps/web` suite: 1124/1124 pass, no flakes. `tsc -b` clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 818: Time Machine's diff/"Current" check never compared an enum field's own enumLabels

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The very next round found another instance of the exact pattern round 817 just closed, inside the same function.

**The gap**: `fieldSignature()` (`apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts`) encoded a field's `type`, `relationTo`, sorted `enumValues`, and `required` flag -- but never `enumLabels`. Unlike a field/entity `label` (deliberately excluded, per this function's own doc comment, as "cosmetic"), `enumLabels` is real and *pervasively* user-rendered: the displayed text in table cells, Kanban board columns, form `<select>` options, automation rule conditions, calendar exports, and grouping/sort/search matching all read `enumLabels`, not the raw `enumValue` (confirmed across `entityFormatting.ts`, `calendarIcs.ts`, `AutomationsPanel.tsx` -- 15+ call sites), arguably an even more pervasive property than round 817's `description`.

**Why this is not deliberate**: zero mentions of `enumLabels` anywhere in `checkpointDiff.ts`, `pipeline.ts`, or `migrate.ts` (confirmed via grep) -- no exclusion rationale exists for it anywhere, unlike `label`'s own explicit comment two lines above `fieldSignature` itself. This is exactly the "missed sibling" pattern just closed for `description` -- a property silently absent with no exclusion rationale, sitting right next to one (`label`) that got the correct, deliberate treatment.

**Concrete failure scenario**: an enum field `status: { enumValues: ["New", "Done"] }` (no `enumLabels`) gets checkpointed, then refined to add `enumLabels: { New: "חדש", Done: "בוצע" }` with the exact same `enumValues`/`type`/`required`. Every record's status now renders completely different text across the whole app. `fieldSignature` produces the identical string for both (`"enum||New,Done||optional"` either way before the fix), so `computeCheckpointDiff` reports the field as unchanged -- HistoryPanel's diff view says "nothing changed" for a refine that actually re-labeled every value shown app-wide -- and `isCheckpointCurrent` wrongly reports `true`, permanently disabling that checkpoint's Restore button, the same failure mode round 817 just fixed for `description`.

**The fix**: added `enumLabels` to the signature as sorted `"rawValue:displayLabel"` pairs (so key order never produces a spurious diff), with `undefined` and `{}` deliberately producing the identical signature (both mean "no overrides, raw values shown as-is").

**The tests**: mirroring round 817's pair exactly -- a same-named enum field with only `enumLabels` differing is reported by `computeCheckpointDiff` (and identical-undefined `enumLabels` on both sides is correctly NOT reported), plus the identical case for `isCheckpointCurrent`.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- both behavioral tests failed exactly as predicted (`AssertionError`/`true !== false`); restored, all 3 pass. Full `apps/web` suite: 1127/1127 pass, no flakes. `tsc -b` clean.

### Round 819: a relation field re-added as boolean reused its old column's FK and threw a raw, unhandled write error

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round closes the one surviving crack in `diffAndMigrate`'s "reused column" hazard detection (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`) -- the mechanism behind every `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed`/`relation_missing_fk` report in the file.

**The gap**: `sqlTypeFor(field)` collapses `boolean` and `relation` into the same `"INTEGER"` SQL bucket (alongside `text`/`longtext`/`enum`/`date` all collapsing to `"TEXT"`). The reused-column branch's own mismatch check (`shape.sqlType !== expectedSqlType`) only compares this collapsed bucket, not the real field type -- so a field removed as a `relation` and re-added, under the same name, as a `boolean` produced **no report at all**: not `type_changed`, not anything. The column SQLite created back when the field was still a relation keeps its real `FOREIGN KEY` constraint forever -- SQLite has no way to drop a constraint from an existing column -- so the field is now rendered everywhere as a plain Yes/No checkbox sitting on top of a column that still physically enforces "must be a valid Customer row id."

**Why this is worse than it first looked**: the subagent that surfaced this candidate framed it as a silent-data-integrity issue (a stale relation id surviving as a confusing truthy/falsy value). Direct empirical testing (actually calling `insertRecord` against a real in-memory SQLite db, not just reading the code) showed the real behavior is more severe: `repository.ts`'s `coerceValue` turns a boolean into a literal `0` or `1` before writing it, and `1` only "succeeds" by coincidence when row id `1` happens to exist. Writing `false` -- i.e. unchecking the box, the single most ordinary action on a boolean field -- coerces to `0`, which is never a valid row id, and throws a raw, completely unhandled `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` straight out of SQLite. `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` catches this and translates it into `"This record references another record that no longer exists"` (`INVALID_RELATION_TARGET`) -- a baffling error for a field with no relation picker anywhere in the UI. This is a guaranteed write **failure**, not just silently-wrong-but-successful data.

**Why only half the ambiguity is fixable**: the mirror case -- the `"TEXT"` bucket's own `text`/`longtext`/`enum`/`date` ambiguity -- has no equivalent fix available today. Confirmed via grep that no field-level type-history ledger exists anywhere in the codebase (only `checkpoint_entity_history`, which remembers entity *names*, not field types). The `"INTEGER"` bucket's `boolean`/`relation` ambiguity, by contrast, already has a physical signal to resolve it: `fieldTypeLabelForSqlType(sqlType, hasForeignKey)` already distinguishes the two using exactly the column's real FK presence (`shape.fkTable !== undefined`) -- it just wasn't being consulted by the reused-column branch's mismatch check.

**The fix**: added a new branch to the reused-column check in `diffAndMigrate`, directly after the existing bucket-mismatch check: when the bucket comparison stays silent but the column's physical FK is present (`shape.fkTable !== undefined`) and the field is no longer `"relation"`, report a `type_changed` entry (`fromType: "relation"`, `toType` the field's real new type), and feed it into the same `fieldsNeedingAutomationDisable` bookkeeping every other `type_changed`/relation-hazard push in this file already uses. Checked this doesn't double-fire alongside the existing `relation_missing_fk` branch (that one fires in the opposite direction -- boolean-turned-relation reusing a column that *never* had an FK -- so the two conditions can't both be true for the same column).

**Scope**: `packages/db` only. `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts` consumes `diffAndMigrate` directly and needed no change -- it just surfaces whatever hazards the function reports. `codegen.ts` has no `diffAndMigrate`/migration-hazard-reporting feature at all for the exported standalone app (confirmed via grep: zero matches for `diffAndMigrate`, `type_changed`, or `MigrationChange`), so no parity fix applies there either.

**The tests**: a new test mirrors the file's existing boolean-to-relation test for the opposite direction -- builds a relation field, removes it (column+FK survive, additive-only), re-adds it under the same name as `boolean`, and asserts the new `type_changed` entry. It also empirically proves the real-world consequence inline, the same way the existing mirror test proves its own gap: `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` on the live column still shows the real FK, and `insertRecord(..., { driverId: false })` is asserted to throw `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- the new test failed exactly as predicted (missing `type_changed` entry, `new_column` only); restored, all 40 tests in `migrate.test.ts` pass. Full `packages/db` suite: 214/214 pass. Full `apps/api` suite: 106/107 individual tests pass; the 107th subtest is `codegen.test.ts` as a whole, which was `SIGKILL`'d partway through both in the full run and when re-run in total isolation -- reproduced identically, taking ~150s either way, with no assertion failure anywhere in its own output. `codegen.ts` has zero relation to this change (confirmed above), so this is an unrelated environment resource/timeout flake, documented candidly rather than either dismissed or treated as blocking this round.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 820: `fieldSignature`'s third and final missing-property gap, enum value *order*

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This closes the last open instance of the series rounds 817-818 started: `fieldSignature` (`apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts`) now accounts for every field-shape property that's real, rendered behavior rather than cosmetic label text.

**The gap**: `fieldSignature`'s `enumPart` sorted `enumValues` before joining it into the comparison string (`(f.enumValues ?? []).slice().sort().join(",")`), so a refine that reorders the exact same set of values -- no addition, removal, or relabeling -- produced an identical signature either way.

**Why order is real, not cosmetic**: `groupByField` (`entityFormatting.ts`) renders Kanban board columns "in the enum's own declared order, not first-seen order" -- that's the function's own doc comment, not an inference. So reordering `enumValues` on a refine visibly reorders both the board's columns and the dropdown's options app-wide -- squarely the same bar round 818 set for `enumLabels` ("a refine that... visibly changes every rendered instance of that enum field").

Round 817/818's own precedent -- closing `description` and `enumLabels` as the same kind of oversight -- applies identically here.
