**Scope**: `apps/web` only -- `fieldSignature` is private to `checkpointDiff.ts`, consumed only by `computeCheckpointDiff`/`isCheckpointCurrent` within this file. No `apps/api`/`codegen.ts` parity applies (same reasoning as rounds 817/818: no checkpoint-diff feature exists there at all).

**The tests**: three new tests mirroring the exact structure of round 818's `enumLabels` trio -- a same-named enum field with only value *order* differing is reported by `computeCheckpointDiff`; identical order (and set) on both sides is correctly NOT reported; and `isCheckpointCurrent` is `false` when only the order differs.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- both order-sensitive tests failed exactly as predicted (`[]` instead of the expected changed-entity entry; `true !== false`); restored, all 50 tests in `checkpointDiff.test.ts` pass. `tsc -b`: clean. Full `apps/web` suite: 1130/1130 pass (one run was mistaken for a hang after stalling at the same test count twice in a row under tight time budgets -- isolating `EntityPanel.test.ts` alone confirmed it's simply the suite's slowest file, not a real hang: a longer background timeout let the full run finish cleanly in ~302s, and `EntityPanel.test.ts`/`.tsx` have zero references to `checkpointDiff.ts` regardless, confirming this had nothing to do with the change).

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round closes a gap in `effectivelyVisibleRecords` (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` and its duplicate in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`) -- the same value rounds 487/499/804 already hardened for Table view's own group-collapse mechanism.

**Concrete failure scenario**: switch an entity to Board view, collapse one column (e.g. "Won") via its toggle chevron -- its cards visibly disappear from the screen. The exported/copied/printed output still contains every record from the collapsed "Won" column, despite the screen showing none of them -- a silent mismatch between what's on screen and what gets exported, exactly the class of bug round 804 fixed for the opposite direction (stale Table collapse leaking into a Board/Calendar export that has no collapse concept of its own at all). This time the collapse state belongs to the very view the export happens from.

**Why not intentional**: round 804's whole premise was "exported/copied/printed output must match what the screen currently shows" -- Board's own collapse deliberately hides cards from the screen, so by that same established contract the export should exclude them too. No test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` exercised Export/Copy/Print while a Board column was collapsed (checked via grep before writing the fix) -- the existing `collapsedBoardColumns` tests only covered rendering and the toggle's own state, never export. Present identically in `codegen.ts`, including the same incorrect "no collapsed concept of their own" comment -- confirming this is a parity-complete but functionally incomplete mechanism, not a Table-only design decision.

**The fix**: added a `viewMode === "board" && boardField` branch to `effectivelyVisibleRecords` in both files, alongside the existing `table` branch -- grouping `visibleRecords` by the board field and filtering out any column `collapsedBoardColumns` already hides. `groupByField` is called without its optional translator argument in `EntityPanel.tsx` since only column membership (`value`/`records`) is needed here, never the "(other)" bucket's display label.

**Scope**: both `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` needed the identical fix -- confirmed via grep that both files declare `effectivelyVisibleRecords`, `boardField`, and `collapsedBoardColumns` the same way, and both toolbars' Copy/Export-CSV/Print-list buttons read `effectivelyVisibleRecords` unconditionally.

**The tests**: one new test per file, both modeled directly on round 804's own test structure -- enters Board view, collapses the "Won" column via its toggle chevron, confirms the cards disappear from the screen, then exports and asserts the collapsed column's records are absent from the CSV while the never-collapsed record is still present. `apps/api`'s version exercises the real generated `EntityView.jsx` end-to-end (via `generateExportFiles`/`writeGeneratedWebComponent`), matching every other codegen integration test in this file.

**Verification**: reverted each fix independently and reran its own new test -- both failed exactly as predicted (`Beta Inc`/`Gamma LLC` present in the exported CSV despite the column being visibly collapsed); restored, both pass. Full `apps/web` suite: 1130/1131 pass, the lone failure (`BuildProgress.test.ts`'s already-documented recurring timing flake, unrelated to this change) reproduced clean in isolation. Full `apps/api` suite: 586/587 pass, the lone failure is `codegen.test.ts`'s whole-file `SIGKILL` -- the same recurring environment flake first seen in round 819, confirmed unrelated to this round's change since the new test (`ok 398`) passed before the file itself was killed partway through.

### Round 822: the exported app's Board "+" button and calendar day-click never scrolled the create form into view

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` only, this time -- a textbook "missed sibling": a fix applied to 1 of 3 structurally identical call sites within the same file.

**The gap**: `startCreateForColumn` and `startCreateForDate` were each one line away from their third sibling, `startCreateNew`, which already calls the shared `scrollIntoViewRespectingMotion` helper right after resetting the form (`setEditingId(null)` / `setForm(...)` / `setFormInstanceKey(...)`). **Concrete failure scenario**: the exported app's record form renders above the Board and Calendar views in the layout (same as the live preview). The form state is correctly pre-filled with that column's value or that date, but the viewport never moves -- the user is still looking at the Board/Calendar and sees no visible effect at all, with no indication a form is now waiting for them off-screen. Exactly the UX regression `scrollIntoViewRespectingMotion` exists to prevent for the general create button.

**Why not intentional**: a mechanical omission, not a design choice -- both functions sit a few lines from `startCreateNew` in the same file, already importing and using the exact same helper for the exact same "reset form, scroll it into view" purpose. No comment near either function explains a deliberate skip, unlike every other deliberate web-vs-codegen difference in this file, which is always explained inline.

**The fix**: added the identical `scrollIntoViewRespectingMotion(document.querySelector(".record-form"), { behavior: "smooth", block: "start" })` call to both functions, matching `startCreateNew`'s own call exactly.

**Scope**: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` only -- the live preview's `EntityPanel.tsx` already had the correct behavior on all three siblings, confirmed by direct comparison before writing the fix.

Also added a new test executing the real generated `startCreateForColumn` the same way, asserting the scroll helper is actually invoked once -- not just present in the source as dead code, which the pre-existing regex-only test couldn't rule out on its own.

### Round 823: changing an enum field's declared values left its old labels permanently orphaned

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s field type-change route (`PATCH .../fields/:fieldName/type`) already had the right instinct for two sibling derived fields but missed a third, one level deeper.

**The gap**: this route's own doc comment states it "deliberately clears whichever of `enumValues`/`relationTo` no longer applies" when a field's type changes -- and the code does exactly that. But `enumLabels` (line 2169, before the fix) was kept completely verbatim whenever the *new* type stayed `"enum"`, with no check against whether `enumValues` itself had actually changed. `SpecListItemRemover.tsx`'s "edit values" pencil button (`openDraftFor`) is the one sanctioned, pre-build UI for editing an *existing* enum field's value list -- it pre-fills the textbox from the field's current `enumValues.join(", ")`, lets the user edit it, and resubmits to this exact route with `type: "enum"` (unchanged) and the edited list. Renaming or removing a value went through this same "type stays enum" path the fix needed to cover.

**Concrete failure scenario**: a project built from the CRM template ships a `Deal.stage` enum field with `enumValues: ["lead","qualified","proposal","won","lost"]` and matching Hebrew `enumLabels` for every one of the five. Editing the value list to drop `"lost"` and add `"archived"` kept the *entire old* `enumLabels` object unchanged: `enumLabels.lost` survived permanently orphaned (a value that no longer exists), and the new `"archived"` value got no label of its own. Every render path using the pervasive `field.enumLabels?.[value] ?? value` fallback -- table cells, board cards, calendar chips, print sheets, CSV/ICS export -- would show the raw English value instead of a translated label for `"archived"`, for the lifetime of the project, since there is no other UI that can ever touch `enumLabels` directly.

**Why not intentional**: this exact block's own comment shows the author was actively thinking about which derived fields to invalidate on this edit ("deliberately clears... rather than leaving it stranded on a field whose type no longer calls for it") -- `enumLabels` simply wasn't included in that thinking. No comment anywhere near the `enumLabels` line explained a deliberate skip. `apps/api/src/app.test.ts`'s own existing type-change test only ever starts from a field with no pre-existing `enumLabels` at all, so this path had never been exercised.

**The fix**: filters `enumLabels` down to just the keys still present in the new `enumValues` list -- the identical "stale derived data must not outlive the data it was derived from" rule the route's own comment already states for `enumValues`/`relationTo`, just applied one level deeper. A value that survives the edit unchanged keeps its real label; a brand-new value simply has none yet (the same state any freshly-created enum field is already in).

**Scope**: `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts` only. `apps/web/src/api.ts` just calls this route over HTTP with no server-side logic duplicated client-side, and `codegen.ts`'s exported standalone app has no pre-build spec-editing feature at all (this route only exists before a project is built) -- confirmed via grep before closing, no parity fix applies anywhere else.

**The tests**: a new integration test creates a project from the real CRM template (whose `Deal.stage` field ships with genuine, non-trivial Hebrew `enumLabels` for all 5 values -- not synthesized by the test itself, so it also incidentally exercises the real heuristic/template data), edits the stage field's values to drop one and add another, and asserts the orphaned value's label is gone, the brand-new value has none, and every value that survived unchanged kept its own real label.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- failed exactly as predicted (`'lost'` label of `"אבדה"` still present instead of `undefined`); restored, passes. Full `apps/api` suite: 588/589 pass, the lone failure is `codegen.test.ts`'s whole-file `SIGKILL` -- the same recurring environment flake from rounds 819/821/822, confirmed unrelated since this round never touched `codegen.ts` at all and the new test (`ok 146`) passed cleanly. `npm run build`: clean. Only `apps/api` was touched this round.

### Round 824: `listCollaborators` broke a same-millisecond tie on `userId` instead of insertion order

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. `packages/db/src/collaborators.ts` was the one remaining `createdAt`/`addedAt`-sorted listing query in this package that hadn't received round 808's own fix.

**The gap**: `addedAt` is set via `new Date().toISOString()` -- millisecond resolution, identical to every other timestamp column in this package. `listCollaborators`'s query tiebroke a same-millisecond tie with `ORDER BY ... userId ASC` -- an essentially random string unrelated to insertion order. `checkpoints.ts`'s `listCheckpoints`, `projects.ts`'s `listProjectsForOwner`/`listProjectsForUser`, and `automations.ts`'s three list queries all already guard against this exact hazard with an explicit `rowid` tiebreak (round 808), each with a comment explaining why. `collaborators.ts` had no such comment, and `project_collaborators` is a plain rowid table (no `WITHOUT ROWID`) exactly like all of them -- the same fix was simply never applied here.

**Concrete failure scenario**: a project owner invites two collaborators in quick succession -- two browser tabs, a script looping over an invite list, or two fast concurrent `POST /projects/:id/collaborators` requests. The insert path (`addCollaborator`) has only a synchronous `INSERT OR IGNORE` between request and commit, so landing both within the same millisecond is entirely reachable. If the second-added collaborator's `userId` happens to sort alphabetically before the first-added collaborator's, `CollaboratorsPanel.tsx` (which renders `listCollaborators`'s return order directly) displays them in the wrong order -- the collaborator invited second appears above the one invited first, with no indication anything is off.

**Why not caught earlier**: the existing ordering test (`"listCollaborators resolves each collaborator's real email... and orders by when they were added"`) happens to use a `user1`/`user2` fixture where the user added first *also* sorts first alphabetically -- so a `userId` tiebreak and a `rowid` tiebreak were indistinguishable in that fixture, and the bug slipped past it undetected.

**The fix**: `ORDER BY project_collaborators.addedAt ASC, project_collaborators.rowid ASC` instead of `userId ASC` -- the identical fix shape round 808 already applied to every sibling query in this package.

**The tests**: a new test deliberately reverses the relationship between insertion order and alphabetical order (`"zed"` added first, `"amy"` added second) -- the one case the existing fixture couldn't exercise. Unlike round 808's own `automation_rules` tests (which only *pin* intended behavior, since that query's plan happened to already preserve `rowid` order even with no explicit tiebreak at all), this test genuinely distinguishes the fix from its absence: the old code's tiebreak was an explicit, always-applied `userId ASC`, not a missing guarantee a query plan might coincidentally satisfy anyway.

**Scope**: `packages/db` only. `codegen.ts`'s exported standalone app has no collaborator-management feature at all (confirmed via grep), so no parity fix applies.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- failed exactly as predicted (`["amy","zed"]` instead of `["zed","amy"]`); restored, passes, along with all 15 tests in `collaborators.test.ts`. Full `packages/db` suite: 215/215 pass. Full `apps/api` suite (consumer of `listCollaborators` via `CollaboratorsPanel`'s backing routes): 588/589 pass, the lone failure is `codegen.test.ts`'s same recurring, already-documented, unrelated whole-file `SIGKILL`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 825: Employee's bare "צוות" keyword spuriously matched "מצוות" (commandments)

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round needed two survey passes -- the first's top candidate (a claimed gap in `calendarChipLabelField`'s relation-field handling) did not survive independent verification: direct tracing through `pickDisplayField`/`calendarChipLabelField` shows a relation-typed field can never reach the label role whenever the entity has a date field (which `calendarChipLabelField`'s own caller guarantees), and round 778 already closed the fallback-path version of this exact bug class with explicit test coverage, including a near-identical fixture. The survey's second candidate was a real but purely cosmetic stale doc comment near an access-control route (naming the wrong helper function in a comment, with the actual access control correct and consistent) -- too thin to carry a round on its own. A second, redirected survey (pointed at genuinely unexplored files) found this round's real fix.

**The gap**: `domainEntities.ts`'s `Employee` entity rule (`DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`) and `ROLE_RULES.Employee` both included bare `"צוות"` ("team"/"staff") in their Hebrew keyword lists. `"צוות"` is a plain substring of `"מצוות"` ("commandments"/"mitzvot") -- an entirely ordinary word in a religious-observance tracker or bar/bat-mitzvah planning app description, with nothing to do with staff management. `matchesKeyword` (`heuristic.ts`) does a plain `.includes()` for a string keyword, with no word-boundary awareness -- and JS's `\b` doesn't bound Hebrew in the first place, so even an explicit boundary wouldn't have helped.

**Concrete failure scenario**: a description like "אפליקציה למעקב אחר קיום מצוות ומנהגים" (an app for tracking observance of commandments and customs) -- never mentioning staff, team, or employees -- matched bare `"צוות"` as a substring inside `"מצוות"`. `matchEntities` fabricated an `Employee` entity (fields name/role/email/active) with no basis in the description, and `matchRoles` fabricated an `עובד/ת` role alongside Admin, suppressing the generic Member-role fallback (which only applies when exactly one role matched) -- producing an entirely wrong entity/role/screens set for a project about religious observance.

**Why not intentional**: this exact file already fixed the identical "מ + root" collision shape at least 15 times over (documented inline for order/stock/driver/patient/deals/worker/courses/stripe/חיוב/מנוי/מלאי/מוצר), and -- critically -- the very same keyword array already carries this exact fix for `עובד`/`עובדת`/`עובדים` (round 565, excluding the pu'al "מעובד" prefix collision) with `"צוות"` sitting bare in the very next array slot, no exclusion, no comment explaining why it would be different. No existing test exercised `"מצוות"` or `"בר מצווה"` as a negative case.

**The fix**: replaced bare `"צוות"` with `/(?<!מ)צוות/` in both `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`'s `Employee` rule and `ROLE_RULES.Employee`, keeping them in sync -- the identical lookbehind pattern this file already uses for `עובד`/`עובדת`/`עובדים`/`מלאי`/`מוצר`.

**Scope**: `packages/spec-engine` only -- this logic is consumed purely server-side at spec-generation time; confirmed via grep that neither `ROLE_RULES` nor `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` are referenced anywhere in `apps/web`/`codegen.ts`, so no parity fix applies.

**The tests**: a new test mirrors round 565's own `עובד`/`מעובד` test exactly -- confirms a commandments-themed description no longer spuriously adds the `Employee` entity or `עובד/ת` role, while real usage (`"הצוות שלנו"`, with the definite-article "ה" prefix rather than "מ") still matches both.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- failed exactly as predicted (`'מצוות'... must not spuriously match Employee` assertion failed); restored, passes. Full `packages/spec-engine` suite: 160/160 pass. Full `apps/api` suite (consumes spec-engine at build time): 588/589 pass, the lone failure is `codegen.test.ts`'s same recurring, already-documented, unrelated whole-file `SIGKILL`.

### Round 827: `WorkOrder`/`Case`/`Task` seed data silently reused Deal's sales-pitch titles

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. `packages/db/src/seed.ts`'s `textSeedValueFor` -- the function that generates believable demo-record values per field name -- had the exact same "shared field name needs per-entity dispatch" shape its own `"name"` case was already written to handle, just never applied to the sibling `"title"` case a few lines above it.

**The gap**: `case "title"` returned `pick(isHebrew ? DEAL_TITLES_HE : DEAL_TITLES_EN, index)` unconditionally, with zero `entityName` check -- unlike `case "name"` immediately below it, which dispatches through `CATALOG_NAME_ENTITIES`/`MenuItem`/`Project`/`Event`/`Course`/`Pet`/`Vendor` before falling back to a person name, and `case "description"`, which dispatches on `Expense` before falling back to a generic placeholder. `domainEntities.ts` has exactly four entities declaring a `"title"` field: `Deal` (the pool's original and only intended owner), `Task`, `WorkOrder`, and `Case` -- confirmed via grep before writing the fix.

**Concrete failure scenario**: build any app whose spec includes `WorkOrder` (a "field service/repair" description) or `Case` (a "law firm case management" description). Verified empirically via direct `generateSeedRecords()` invocation before implementing anything: a fresh `WorkOrder`'s or `Case`'s very first demo rows showed `title` values like `"Annual contract"`/`"Service upgrade"` -- plausible as a sales deal, nonsensical as a repair job description or a legal matter's subject. `Task`'s titles were similarly off (`"Plan expansion"`/`"Initial setup"` read as deal stages, not to-dos), though less jarring.

Since the bug's actual symptom was a *wrong but non-placeholder* value (a real Deal title string), that assertion passed cleanly every single time, silently masking the gap.

**The fix**: added dedicated `WORK_ORDER_TITLES_HE/EN`, `CASE_TITLES_HE/EN`, and `TASK_TITLES_HE/EN` pools, and dispatched `case "title"` on `entityName` the same way `case "name"` already does, falling back to `DEAL_TITLES` only for `Deal` itself (and any custom/non-domain entity reusing the name "Deal", matching every other case's own fallback convention).

**Scope**: `packages/db` only -- confirmed via grep that `seed.ts`'s pools/dispatch aren't referenced anywhere in `apps/web`/`codegen.ts` (seed-data generation is a server-side-only build step).

**The tests**: added a new test asserting `WorkOrder`/`Case`/`Task`'s seeded titles are never one of `Deal`'s own sample values -- the semantic check the existing "not the generic placeholder" test couldn't provide.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- failed exactly as predicted (`WorkOrder`'s title `"Service upgrade"` matched one of Deal's own sample titles); restored, passes. Full `packages/db` suite: 216/216 pass. Full `apps/api` suite: 588/589 pass, the lone failure is `codegen.test.ts`'s same recurring, already-documented, unrelated whole-file `SIGKILL`.

A physical-fitness-assessment app for a gym ("אפליקציה לניהול בדיקות כשירות גופנית במכון כושר") matched only the generic `Service` entity instead of anything fitness-related. Verified the regex behaves correctly in isolation before writing any test: rejects `"כשירות"`/`"כשירותים"`, still matches `"שירות"`/`"שירותים"` bare or with the definite-article `"ה"` prefix.

**Scope**: `packages/spec-engine` only -- this logic is consumed purely server-side at spec-generation time; confirmed via grep that neither `ROLE_RULES` nor `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` are referenced anywhere in `apps/web`/`codegen.ts`.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- failed exactly as predicted (`'כשירות' (fitness) alone must not spuriously match Service` assertion failed); restored, passes. ### Round 831: a Save/Create in flight never blocked the rule list's own Edit/Toggle/Delete buttons -- a real race, not just a UX glitch

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. After four consecutive rounds on the Hebrew keyword-collision pattern, this round deliberately redirected to a fresh area -- and found a real, previously-unfixed client-side race in `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s own form/list interaction.

**The gap**: the rule list's Edit/Toggle/Delete buttons were disabled only by `busyRuleId !== null` (set while a *different* toggle or delete is in flight) -- never by `createBusy` (set while the shared create/edit form's own Save or Create submission is in flight). Nothing stopped clicking Edit on a different rule while an earlier submission was still awaiting its network round trip.

**Concrete failure scenario (real data loss, not a cosmetic glitch)**: a user editing rule A changes its message template and clicks "Save changes" (`createBusy=true`, a real `await updateAutomationRule(...)` in flight). Before it resolves, they click Edit on rule B -- fully clickable, since `busyRuleId` is unrelated and still `null`. `handleStartEdit(B)` immediately overwrites `editingRuleId` and every form field with B's real values. When A's update resolves, the async `handleSubmit` call -- whose own `editingRuleId` reference was captured in its closure at invocation time, so it still correctly PATCHes A, not B -- unconditionally calls `resetToCreateMode()` with no check of what the form is currently showing. This wipes `editingRuleId` back to `null` and every field to blank "create" defaults, silently discarding whatever the user had already typed into B's edit, snapping the screen back to "New rule" with zero warning. A second variant hits the create path: starting a brand-new rule, submitting, then clicking Edit on an unrelated rule Y while the create is in flight -- once it resolves, its own unconditional partial reset (`fieldValue`/`toNumber`/`webhookUrl`/`messageTemplate` all cleared) blanks several of Y's own in-progress edit fields while `editingRuleId` is still correctly pointing at Y.

**Why not already covered**: round 803 (closed) fixed a *different* race in this exact state machine -- deleting the rule currently being edited left the form stuck on a 404-bound edit -- but that fix only touches `handleDelete`'s own conditional reset. It never extended the row buttons' `disabled` condition to include `createBusy`, and `handleSubmit`'s own `resetToCreateMode()`/partial-reset calls remained completely unconditional. Confirmed via grep: no `disabled={createBusy` anywhere except the form's own Save/Cancel buttons; no combined "anything busy" flag exists anywhere in the component.

**The fix**: extended the row buttons' `disabled` condition to `busyRuleId !== null || createBusy` -- mirroring exactly how `busyRuleId` already disables every row during a toggle/delete. This closes the race at its root (the conflicting click can never happen in the first place) rather than trying to detect and repair the damage after the fact, which would have required tracking the *current* `editingRuleId` via a ref (since the in-flight `handleSubmit` closure's own reference is frozen at invocation time and can't observe later state changes) -- a meaningfully larger, riskier change for the same outcome.

**Scope**: `apps/web` only -- confirmed via grep that `codegen.ts` has no Automations feature at all (it requires the live server's own WhatsApp integration), so no parity fix applies.

**The tests**: a new test holds a rule-A `PATCH` deliberately pending (a manually-resolved promise), confirms rule B's own Edit button is disabled for the entire window the Save is in flight, confirms clicking it anyway (defense in depth) leaves A's own in-progress edit untouched, then resolves the PATCH and confirms the form correctly returns to create mode once the submission actually completes.

**Verification**: reverted the fix and reran -- failed exactly as predicted (`rule2's own Edit button must stay disabled... false !== true`); restored, passes. Full `apps/web` suite: 1132/1132 pass.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 832: the exact same createBusy-style race as round 831, one component over -- EntityPanel's record form, not AutomationsPanel's

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A fresh Explore survey found the identical race shape from round 831, independently present in `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own record form.

**The gap**: `handleSubmit`'s success path unconditionally reset `form`/`editingId` back to blank (and remounted the form fields via `formInstanceKey`) once its `updateRecord`/`createRecord` call resolved, with no check that the form hadn't since moved on to editing a *different* record. A slow save for record A resolving after the user had already clicked Edit on record B silently wiped out record B's own in-progress, unsaved edit, snapping the screen back to a blank "Add" form with zero warning -- the same concrete data-loss shape round 831 fixed in `AutomationsPanel.tsx`, in a different component entirely.

**Why round 831's fix doesn't just port over as-is**: round 831 closed its race by *disabling the conflicting UI* -- extending the row buttons' `disabled` condition to also cover `createBusy`, since AutomationsPanel has exactly three entry points into a conflicting action (the rule list's Edit/Toggle/Delete buttons). EntityPanel has far more: the table's own Edit button, the `startEdit`/`startCreateNew`/`startCreateForDate`/`startCreateForColumn` keyboard shortcut and Board/Calendar card handlers, and the in-form Delete button's own reset -- all of which can start a *new* editing session while an earlier save is still in flight. Disabling every one of them individually carries real risk of missing one (exactly the "missed sibling" pattern this window has hit repeatedly in other files). So this round instead reused the file's own pre-existing `refreshRequestId` convention: a plain React state value is frozen in `handleSubmit`'s closure at whatever it was when that specific submit began, so it can't tell the difference between "nothing changed" and "the user has since started editing something else" -- but a `useRef` mirror of that same value *can* be read live, since refs aren't frozen by closures.

**The fix**: added `formInstanceKeyRef`, a ref that mirrors the pre-existing `formInstanceKey` state (originally just a React remount key), plus a `bumpFormInstanceKey()` helper that increments both together. `handleSubmit` captures `formInstanceKeyRef.current` into `formInstanceAtSubmitTime` before its `await`, then only applies the success-path reset (`setForm`/`setEditingId`/`editingOriginalRef`/`bumpFormInstanceKey`) if `formInstanceKeyRef.current` still equals that captured value when the `await` resolves. Every place that starts a new editing session (`startEdit`, `startCreateNew`, `startCreateForDate`, `startCreateForColumn`, and the in-form Delete button's reset) now calls `bumpFormInstanceKey()` instead of the old bare `setFormInstanceKey((k) => k + 1)`, so any of them invalidates an earlier in-flight submit's assumption. `editingId`/`form` inside the already-running `handleSubmit` stay correctly bound to the original record regardless (ordinary closure capture, same as round 831's `editingRuleId`) -- this ref only gates the *cleanup*, never the save itself, so record A's own save still correctly completes and persists.

**Scope**: both files. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s generated `EntityView.jsx` has the identical `startEdit`/`handleSubmit`/`formInstanceKey` structure (confirmed via grep before assuming parity was needed, per this window's standing discipline), so the same fix -- same shape, same six call-site conversions -- was ported there too, with "Mirrors the live Forge AI preview's own EntityPanel.tsx" phrasing in the comment.

**The tests**: `EntityPanel.test.ts` gets a new test holding record A's own `PATCH` deliberately pending (a manually-resolved promise), switches to editing record B while it's still in flight, types into B's field, then resolves A's save and confirms B's in-progress edit survives and the form is still showing "Save" (an active edit), not "Add" (a reset blank form). `codegen.test.ts` gets the same scenario ported to a real generated-`EntityView.jsx` jsdom render (`generateExportFiles`/`writeGeneratedWebComponent`/dynamic import/`render()`/`act()`-polling, the same pattern as this file's existing "Enter shortcut" test), plus three pre-existing tests updated for the `setFormInstanceKey` → `bumpFormInstanceKey` rename: two literal exact-body regex matchers (round 822's `startCreateForColumn`/`startCreateForDate` tests) and one `new Function(...)`-injected-dependency test's parameter name, plus the round-644-port test's inline synthetic harness, whose no-op `setFormInstanceKey` stub needed replacing with a working `formInstanceKeyRef`/`bumpFormInstanceKey` pair matching the new real implementation's shape.

**Two test-authoring mistakes caught and fixed while writing the `EntityPanel.test.ts` version** (useful precedent for future rounds testing any `bumpFormInstanceKey`-remounting flow): (1) a DOM element reference captured once (`const nameInput = ...`) and reused across the `startEdit`-triggered remount is a detached node after the remount -- the fix is a `getNameInput()` helper re-queried fresh on every use, not a single captured `const`. (2) the deferred-PATCH mock's manually-resolved `Response` body was never actually applied to the test's in-memory `store` array, so the subsequent `refresh()`'s own GET call returned stale data -- fixed by mutating `store[0].name` immediately before resolving the mocked PATCH, the same convention the existing round-644 test already uses.

**Verification**: both new tests confirmed failing without the fix (`'' !== 'Beta Inc TYPING'` in both apps/web and apps/api versions) and passing with it, via a stash/run/restore cycle on `codegen.ts` alone (never piping the backgrounded command through tail/head/grep, per round 831's own operational lesson).

**A pre-existing environmental flake surfaced during verification, unrelated to this fix**: the full `apps/api` `codegen.test.ts` suite's 109 individual subtests all pass cleanly every time, but the file-level test wrapper itself gets `SIGKILL`ed near the very end (167-212s elapsed) before the process can exit on its own -- a hang-on-process-exit, not a real test failure. Confirmed via `ps aux` (no memory/CPU pressure) and, conclusively, by stashing all of round 832's changes and rerunning the *original, unmodified* `codegen.test.ts`: it hangs and gets `SIGKILL`ed the exact same way (108/108 subtests pass, then the same wrapper death). This matches the round-649 class of flake already documented in this file ("container restart can cause hang-on-process-exit in heavy jsdom/React test files, unrelated to code, even in full isolation") -- not a regression from this round's change. `apps/web`'s full `EntityPanel.test.ts` suite ran clean: 183/183 pass with no hang.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 834: round 751's own "codegen.ts parity not needed" verdict used a justification that never covered the real reachability path -- the field-RETYPED half of round 570's own bug

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A fresh Explore survey, explicitly told the `formInstanceKeyRef` mechanism closed by rounds 832/833 was exhausted, turned toward a different stale "no port needed" verdict -- a pattern this routine has specifically found fruitful before (round 570 itself was exactly this move, revisiting rounds 490/493/500's own verdicts).

**The gap**: round 570 ported `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `fieldFilters` field-*removed* staleness fix to `codegen.ts`'s `sanitizeFieldFilters`, using the cross-export localStorage reachability path round 509 established: `FIELD_FILTERS_STORAGE_KEY` is a single fixed key, scoped only by entity name with no export-version dimension, so a browser that still holds an older export's persisted filter sees it unchanged against a *newer* export's `entity.fields` -- no live refine needed at all, since this reachability path never requires the schema to change while anything stays mounted. Round 751 (later) added a field-*retyped* half to the live preview's own `fieldFilters` effect (e.g. a `status` field going from `enum` to `boolean` via a refine) but explicitly declined to port it to `codegen.ts`, reasoning: *"the exported standalone app's ENTITIES array is baked in once at generation time with no live-refine mechanism at all, so a field's type can never actually change while any component stays mounted there."* That reasoning only rules out a type change happening *within one page load* -- it says nothing about round 509/570's own cross-export path, which never needed a mount-time change for the field-removed half either. The identical path trivially covers a field whose *type* changed between two exports of the same project, and `codegen.ts` has no protection against that half of the exact same bug.

**Concrete failure a user would notice**: export a project whose `Order` entity has `status` as an `enum`, filter the exported app's table by `status = "Shipped"` (persisted to `localStorage`). Refine the spec so `status` becomes a `boolean`. Re-export and reload the app at the same origin (the same reachability round 509/570 already treat as real, e.g. redeploying to the same hosting URL). `sanitizeFieldFilters` kept `{status: "Shipped"}` since `"status"` still exists as a field name -- the boolean filter `<select>` only ever renders `true`/`false` options with no synthetic stale-value option (unlike the `enum`/`relation` branches, which already have one for exactly this reason), so it shows nothing meaningfully selected while `fieldFilters` stays set to `"Shipped"`. `visibleRecords`' own `.every()` check (`String(r[fieldName] ?? "") === value`) then compares every record's real boolean value against the string `"Shipped"`, which can never match -- every record silently vanishes from the table with no visible error.

**Independent verification before implementing**: read `codegen.ts`'s `sanitizeFieldFilters` (name-only check, no type-shape check), the boolean/relation branches of the filter `<select>` rendering, and `visibleRecords`' own filter predicate directly, confirming the exact mechanism. Read `docs/roadmap.md`'s own rounds 509, 570, and 751 entries directly to confirm round 751's stated reasoning and that round 570's own fix already relies on the cross-export path that reasoning fails to address.

**The fix**: extended `sanitizeFieldFilters` with the identical `boolean`/`relation` shape checks `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `fieldFilters` effect already has (a `boolean` value must be exactly `"true"`/`"false"`; a `relation` value must be a plain non-negative integer id) -- an `enum` field needs no such check, for the same reason round 751's own doc comment gives: any stored string is a plausible (if stale) enum value, and that staleness is exactly what the filter `<select>`'s own existing synthetic-option guard already surfaces visibly.

**The test**: one new test in `codegen.test.ts`, placed directly after round 570's own field-removed test, mirroring its structure but building a locally-scoped `Project` whose `Customer.status` field is `boolean` (standing in for the "newer export" side of the cross-export path) while seeding `localStorage`'s `forge_field_filters` with `{Customer: {status: "Won"}}` (standing in for the "older export's" stale enum-shaped value) -- confirming both records still render instead of the table going empty with no visible cause.

**Verification**: confirmed failing without the fix (0 rows rendered instead of 2, via a `git stash push -- apps/api/src/codegen.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, test file left unstashed) and passing with it restored, both via an isolated `--test-name-pattern` run.

**A significant verification-process discovery this round, important for every future round touching `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts`**: this file has grown to **283 total `test()` calls**, but a full, unfiltered run of it (`npx tsx --test src/codegen.test.ts`, no pattern) consistently gets `SIGKILL`ed after only **~111-112 tests complete** -- reproduced identically at both default concurrency and `--test-concurrency=1` (ruling out a scheduling/ordering explanation), with `NODE_OPTIONS` carrying `--max-old-space-size=8192` and observed RSS climbing past 10GB mid-run pointing to a real memory ceiling (almost certainly this environment's own container/OS memory limit, not a V8 heap-exhaustion crash, since the kill is a plain `SIGKILL` with no JS heap-OOM stack trace). This round's own new test (the file's 234th `test()` call in declaration order) landed well past that point, so it never appeared in any "full suite" log at all -- not as a failure, not as anything: no `# Subtest:` line, no `ok`/`not ok` line, nothing. This means **every prior round's "full apps/api suite ran clean" claim for this specific file has, in practice, only ever verified roughly the first third of it** -- wherever that round's own new test happened to land early enough to survive. Rounds 832 and 833's own new tests both landed early in the file (lines ~100-1650) and so were genuinely covered; this round's happened to land much later (line ~13281) and was not, purely by file position, with no indication of that in the log's own superficially-clean-looking summary (`pass: 111, fail: 1`, the "1" being only the known hang-on-exit wrapper, never hinting that 170+ further tests were silently never reached). **Going forward**: a new `codegen.test.ts` test's own correctness must be verified via a targeted `--test-name-pattern` isolation cycle (fail-without/pass-with), never assumed-covered by a "full suite" run of this specific file; and any claim that "the full apps/api suite ran clean" for this file specifically should be treated with suspicion unless the log's own total subtest count is checked against the file's true `test()` count (283 as of this round, grep `^test(` to recheck as it grows) -- a mismatch means most of the file silently never ran. `apps/web`'s `EntityPanel.test.ts` does not have this problem at its current size (it ran fully clean, 185/185, in this session's own rounds 832/833) -- this is specific to `codegen.test.ts`'s own size and its unusually heavy concentration of full jsdom-render integration tests (`generateExportFiles`/`writeGeneratedWebComponent`/dynamic `import()`, each of which permanently caches a distinct generated module in the process's memory for the run's lifetime, never reclaimed).

A fresh Explore survey turned toward the `orderedFields` convention itself -- not to find another missed render-path sibling (that six-instance family, rounds 615/621/670/678/684/686, is fully closed), but to check whether some genuinely different kind of export surface had been missed entirely.

**The gap**: every one of this app's export/output surfaces already follows a user's drag-reordered column order (`apps/web/src/columnOrder.ts`'s `getColumnOrder`/`applyColumnOrder`, persisted per project+entity in localStorage): the on-screen table, the per-entity "Export CSV" and Copy actions, both Print sheets, the Columns menu, board cards, the add/edit form, the bulk-edit/filter/group-by field pickers, and the calendar `.ics` export (round 686). `apps/api/src/backup.ts`'s `entityToCsv` -- the per-entity CSV builder inside the "Backup all data" ZIP -- never received or applied it, iterating `entity.fields` in their raw declared order instead.

**Why this is architecturally distinct from the already-closed `orderedFields` family**: every one of the six prior fixes was inside `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` (or a direct per-feature port), where `orderedFields` was already computed client-side in the same render and simply wasn't threaded into one more call. `backup.ts` is a different shape of problem entirely: it's a pure server-side `GET /projects/:id/backup` route with no request body at all -- the server has *no mechanism* to learn the client's localStorage-only preference without new plumbing. This is exactly why it was never swept into the six-instance audit (which only ever looked at `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own render paths) and never separately investigated on its own terms, despite `backup.ts` having been mined four other times for unrelated bugs (a header label-collision fix, a `csvEscape` leading-apostrophe guard, a missing `"file"`-type value branch, a WhatsApp-log CSV Hebrew-header fix).

**Independent verification before implementing**: read `backup.ts`'s `entityToCsv`/`generateBackupZipEntries` directly (confirmed: no ordering parameter anywhere), `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own identical copy (confirmed: the same gap, for the exported app's own backup route -- scoped out of this round, see below), `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s `handleBackup` and `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `backupProject` (confirmed: no column-order data was ever sent), and `columnOrder.ts`'s `applyColumnOrder` algorithm directly (to mirror it exactly server-side, per `backup.ts`'s own stated convention of duplicating rather than importing small formatting helpers per surface). Grepped `backup.test.ts`/`codegen.test.ts` for any `columnOrder`/`orderedFields` reference near `entityToCsv` -- confirmed zero existing coverage.

**Concrete failure a user would notice**: drag a table's columns into a new order -- the on-screen table and every other export surface now reflects it. Click "Backup all data" expecting a consistent file, and the downloaded CSV inside the ZIP lists columns back in the entity's original declared order -- the one export surface in the whole app that doesn't match what the user sees everywhere else.

**The fix**: `apps/web/src/App.tsx`'s `handleBackup` now gathers each entity's persisted column order (`getColumnOrder(project.id, entity.name)`) into a `Record<string, string[]>` and passes it to `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `backupProject`, which encodes it as a single JSON `columnOrders` query param on the backup GET request (a plain query param, since this is a GET download with no request body -- `downloadBlob`'s own fetch-with-Authorization-header mechanics already made this a real `fetch()` call under the hood, not a browser-navigated `<a href>`, so attaching a query param was trivial). `apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`'s backup route parses it via `backup.ts`'s new `parseColumnOrdersQueryParam` (defensive: any malformed shape -- invalid JSON, not a plain object, a non-array value -- silently falls back to an empty map rather than throwing, since a stale or malformed localStorage value making it onto the wire must never break the backup) and passes the result to `generateBackupZipEntries`, which applies `backup.ts`'s new `orderedFieldsFor` (an exact mirror of `columnOrder.ts`'s `applyColumnOrder`: a field the order mentions keeps its persisted relative position; anything the order doesn't mention -- a new field, or an order saved before this entity existed -- is appended at the end in the entity's own declared order) before building each entity's CSV header and rows.

**Scope**: deliberately limited to `apps/web` + `apps/api/src/backup.ts` (the live preview's own backup route) this round. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has the identical gap in its own copy of `entityToCsv` and its exported app's own `/api/backup` route, but that app's own backup trigger is a plain `<a href="/api/backup" download>` tag, not a fetch-based `downloadBlob` call -- it needs a different client-side approach (computing the `columnOrders` query string inline from the exported app's own `getColumnOrder` per entity and setting it as the anchor's `href`, since a plain anchor has no JS-constructed request to attach anything to otherwise) and its own separate test-verification cycle (subject to `codegen.test.ts`'s own newly-documented full-suite-can't-complete limitation from round 834). Rather than rushing a parity port into this same round, it's flagged as a concrete, already-identified candidate for round 836.

**The tests**: four new tests in `backup.test.ts` -- `generateBackupZipEntries` honors a passed-in column order (confirmed via both the CSV header and a real inserted row's own values reordering identically); falls back to the entity's declared order when no order was ever persisted for it; falls back the same way when the persisted order only names a field the entity doesn't have (never dropping a real field); and `parseColumnOrdersQueryParam`'s own defensive parsing of six different malformed-input shapes. One new test in `api.test.ts` confirms `backupProject` builds the exact expected `columnOrders` query param from a given map.

**Verification**: confirmed failing without the fix -- not a soft assertion mismatch but a clean module-load crash (`SyntaxError: The requested module './backup.js' does not provide an export named 'parseColumnOrdersQueryParam'`), via a `git stash push -- apps/api/src/backup.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle (every other changed file, including the test files, left unstashed) -- and passing cleanly with the fix restored. Full suites green: `apps/api`'s `backup.test.ts` 23/23 (19 + 4 new); `apps/web`'s `api.test.ts` 31/31 (30 + 1 new) and `App.test.ts` 82/82 (unchanged, confirming `handleBackup`'s own internals change broke nothing); `apps/web` typecheck clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 838: round 780's own ref-based "Group by" type-staleness fix never covers a remount -- only a continuous live-refine-while-mounted path

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A fresh Explore survey, pointed away from every mechanism closed through round 837, found a genuine gap in a mechanism that itself was closed as recently as round 780: a different *reachability path* into the exact same bug round 780 believed it had fully fixed.

**The gap**: round 780's own fix (`apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`) added `groupedFieldTypeRef`, an in-memory `useRef` that remembers the type of whichever field `groupFieldName` currently names, cleared via the existing round-462 path the instant that type changes while the component stays mounted. This genuinely closes the "live refine while the user is looking at this exact table" path. But `App.tsx`'s own `project.spec.entities.filter((e) => e.name === activeEntity).map(...)` means switching to a *different* entity tab doesn't just hide `EntityPanel` -- it fully unmounts it, wiping the ref. If a refine retypes the grouped field (e.g. `status` from `enum` to `boolean`) while that entity's tab is *not* the active one, the persisted `groupFieldName` ("status") survives in `groupByPreference.ts` exactly as designed -- but the ref that round 780's fix depends on has nothing to compare against on the fresh mount that follows reopening the tab, since it starts at `null` every time. `groupRecordsByField`'s boolean branch then runs `Boolean(r.status)` against the real records' still-unconverted legacy enum strings, landing virtually every record under one confidently-labeled "Yes" group with real, fabricated per-group subtotals -- the identical "silently wrong results presented as correct" hazard round 780's own fix describes, reached a different way. Round 780's own test explicitly only exercised a rerender of the same mounted instance, never an unmount+remount, so this path was never covered.

**Independent verification before implementing**: read `groupedFieldTypeRef`'s exact code and the mount-time load effect directly in `EntityPanel.tsx`, confirming the ref starts fresh (uninitialized) on every mount with nothing to compare against; read `App.tsx`'s own `.filter((e) => e.name === activeEntity)` directly, confirming `EntityPanel` is genuinely unmounted (filtered out of the render tree entirely, not merely hidden) when its tab isn't active; read `entityFormatting.ts`'s `groupRecordsByField` boolean branch directly, confirming it has no legacy-value guard the way the enum branch's own `"(other)"` bucket does.

**A key independent finding that ruled out one of the survey's own two suggested fix directions**: the survey proposed either (a) persisting the field's type alongside its name and validating on load, or (b) giving `groupRecordsByField`'s boolean branch a legacy-value guard, mirroring the enum branch's own `"(other)"` bucket. Reading `packages/db/src/repository.ts`'s `rowToRecord` directly revealed that option (b) is not actually implementable: every single record returned by `listRecords` already runs `field.type === "boolean" ? Boolean(value) : value` **server-side**, unconditionally, based on the field's *current* type in the entity spec -- so a legacy enum string like `"Shipped"` is already coerced to `true` long before it ever reaches the browser. The client never sees the raw string at all; the information a client-side guard would need to distinguish "genuine boolean" from "legacy leftover" is already destroyed one layer below. This made option (a) -- closing the gap in the persistence/validation mechanism itself -- the only viable fix.

**The fix**: `groupByPreference.ts` gains a new sibling store (`getGroupByFieldType`/`setGroupByFieldType`/`purgeGroupByFieldTypeForProject`, same keying convention as the existing plain-string `getGroupByField` store, deliberately kept as a *separate* store rather than changing the existing store's shape -- the existing store's plain-string API and every test already asserting against it stay completely untouched). Rather than threading a new write call through every one of `EntityPanel.tsx`'s four `setGroupByField` call sites (the user's own pick, round 780's live-refine clearing path, round 462's jump-to-record clearing path, and the mount-time load path), the existing `groupedFieldTypeRef`-setting effect (already keyed on `[groupFieldName]`, already fires on every single change regardless of which call site caused it) was extended to also persist the type -- one change point instead of four. The mount-time load effect now validates the loaded `groupFieldName` against the type recorded for it the moment it was last chosen; a mismatch (or a field that no longer exists at all) clears the selection the same way round 780's own live-refine path already does. A choice persisted from before this round shipped (no recorded type at all) is trusted as-is, same as before -- this only changes behavior going forward from the first time a type is actually recorded.

**The test**: a new `EntityPanel.test.ts` test groups a `Deal` entity's table by an enum `status` field, calls `.unmount()` on that render (not `.rerender()` -- a genuine unmount, mirroring `App.tsx`'s own tab-switch behavior), then calls `render()` fresh with the identical entity now retyped to boolean, confirming the "Group by" dropdown resets to "no grouping" and the table renders flat with no fabricated "Yes" group -- the same assertions round 780's own test already makes, just reached via a real remount instead of a rerender. **A self-caught test-authoring bug along the way**: the test's own second `waitForCondition` initially checked a bare `tr` count, which the very bug this test exists to catch also breaks -- with the stale grouping still active (the unfixed case), the table renders extra group-header `<tr>` elements with no `data-record-id`, so a bare count never equals the expected number and the wait times out instead of failing on a real assertion. Fixed by counting `tr[data-record-id]` specifically, a useful precedent for any future test exercising this same "stale grouping still active, extra rows present" failure mode.

**Verification**: confirmed failing without the fix -- first a timeout from the test-authoring bug above (caught and fixed), then a clean assertion failure (`'status' !== ''`) -- via a `git stash push -- apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx apps/web/src/groupByPreference.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, and passing cleanly with both files restored. `groupByPreference.test.ts` (6/6) and `projectPreferenceCleanup.test.ts` (1/1) both ran clean, confirming the existing plain-string store's own API and `purgeGroupByFieldForProject`'s now-expanded purge (it also clears the new type store) broke nothing. The full `EntityPanel.test.ts` suite ran clean this time with no hang-on-exit: 187/187 pass.

**Scope note**: this round did not touch `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`. The survey's own secondary note flagged a related but distinct gap there (`getPersistedGroupField` has no type-tracking at all, not even round 780's own ref-based mechanism) as "a closely related follow-up once the root cause's fix shape is decided" -- this round's fix shape (a new persisted sibling store) now answers that question, but porting it is left as a flagged, concrete candidate for a future round rather than rushed into this one.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

### Round 842: `collapsedGroups`/`collapsedBoardColumns` had the related-but-distinct field-VALUE staleness gap round 841's own note flagged -- and unlike the last three rounds, it was open on BOTH files, reachable without any export/reload at all

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round picked up the exact fourth candidate round 841's own roadmap note named: `collapsedGroups`/`collapsedBoardColumns` are keyed by the grouped/board field's raw stored *value* (an enum value, or the literal strings `"true"`/`"false"` for boolean), not by a field *name* the way the three now-closed stores (`groupFieldName`, `viewMode`, `sortKeys`) are. A fresh survey confirmed this really is a distinct, open gap -- and, unlike every one of rounds 838-841, found it unfixed symmetrically on **both** `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` and `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` at once, not as a missed sibling on one side only.

**The gap**: `groupRecordsByField`/`groupByField`'s own enum branch (in both `entityFormatting.ts` and `codegen.ts`) collects any record whose stored value no longer matches a currently-declared `enumValue` into a synthetic `"(other)"` bucket, keyed via `otherGroupKey()` -- a key deliberately constructed to differ from every real enum value, past or present. A refine renaming or removing an enum value (e.g. `"won"` -> `"done"`) never touches existing records' own stored `"won"` strings (migrations are additive-only, an established fact this codebase already relies on elsewhere -- `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`'s own enum-narrowing logic disables automation rules for exactly this reason). Those records' group simply moves from a key named `"won"` to the `"(other)"` bucket's key -- one the stale `"won"` entry in `collapsedGroups`/`collapsedBoardColumns` never matches again. The dead entry then sits in the persisted store forever: no UI control can ever reach or clear a value that no longer exists, and (though more contrived) a stale entry whose literal string a LATER, unrelated refine happens to reuse for a genuinely different value could wrongly force that new group collapsed from the moment it's created.

**A key distinction from the "stale-key-causes-a-visible-regression" framing the survey's own report led with**: independent verification showed the `"(other)"` bucket's own collapse state is unaffected either way by this gap -- it was never previously collapsed (it didn't exist as a bucket before the refine), so it renders expanded regardless of whether the stale `"won"` entry is pruned or kept. The gap's real, concretely demonstrable effect is the dead entry's own indefinite survival in storage (unbounded, unreachable, with the described reuse-collision risk) -- not a live "the user's choice got undone" symptom on the `"(other)"` bucket itself. The fix and its tests target that real effect directly: confirming the dead entry is actually pruned from persisted storage, rather than asserting a DOM-visible collapse-state regression that, on inspection, wouldn't actually differ between the fixed and unfixed code for this exact bucket.

**Why this is reachable without any export/reload, unlike rounds 838-841's own fixes**: `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`'s own `collapsedGroups`/`collapsedBoardColumns` load effects were keyed only on `[projectId, entity.name, groupFieldName]`/`[projectId, entity.name, boardFieldName]` -- never on anything derived from the field's own `enumValues`. Since EntityPanel doesn't remount when a refine mutates the currently-active entity's own fields in place (an established fact this file's own `groupFieldName`/`viewMode` effects already rely on), and since `groupFieldName`/`boardFieldName` themselves don't change when only a field's `enumValues` are edited (not its name or which field holds the role), neither effect ever refired to re-validate the stale value -- the bug was live-reachable in a single continuous session, not just across a reload the way the three previous rounds' own cross-export-only gaps were.

**The fix**: on `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`, added a `groupFieldEnumValuesKey`/`boardFieldEnumValuesKey` `useMemo` each (an enum field's `enumValues.join(",")`, or `""` for a non-enum field), added to the existing load effects' own dependency arrays so they now re-fire the moment a field's declared values actually change. Each effect now filters the loaded set against the field's current `enumValues` (boolean fields have a fixed, never-stale two-value space, so only the enum case needs filtering), persisting the pruned result back via the existing `setCollapsedGroupsPreference`/`setCollapsedBoardColumnsPreference` setters when anything was dropped -- the same validate-and-filter-with-write-back shape rounds 838-841 already established, just via a continuously-revalidating effect (this file's own established style for in-place-mutable state) rather than a lazy initializer.

**The test**: two new `EntityPanel.test.ts` tests (one per store), each building a custom `Deal` entity with an enum field, collapsing a real group/column via the actual UI, confirming the real persisted value via `getCollapsedGroups`/`getCollapsedBoardColumns`, then calling `view.rerender(...)` with a second entity object whose field renames that same enum value -- mirroring the established "EntityPanel doesn't remount for an in-place field edit" rerender pattern already used by round 435's own sibling test for a related defect. Confirms the dead entry is pruned from the real persisted store once the rerender completes, with no remount needed.

**Verification**: confirmed both tests failing cleanly without the fix -- `deepStrictEqual` failures showing the dead entry (`['won']`/`['high']`) still present where `[]` was expected -- via a `git stash push -- apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, and passing with the fix restored (one transient "React is not defined" failure immediately after the `stash pop` was investigated and confirmed to be an unrelated tsx/esbuild module-cache fluke, not a real regression -- a clean immediate re-run passed both tests normally). All 15 existing `collapsed`/`collapse`-matching tests in `EntityPanel.test.ts` passed clean alongside the two new ones. `apps/web`'s own full build (`tsc -b && vite build`) and its full 1140-test suite (`npm test`) both ran clean -- no hang-on-exit this run, exit code 0.

**Status**: shipped and pushed. Left for a future round, as a deliberately bounded scope decision (matching round 835/836's own precedent of splitting a both-files fix across rounds when the fix itself, not just a parity port, needs writing twice): porting this same fix to `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own `getPersistedCollapsedGroups`/`getPersistedCollapsedBoardColumns`, which the survey confirmed carries the identical gap.

### Round 844: `buildZip`'s own entry-count overflow guard had a missed sibling in the SAME function -- the entry-name-length field

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A fresh Explore survey, explicitly steered away from the now-exhausted stale-persisted-preference family (838-843), moved to a genuinely different area and found a smaller-scoped but textbook instance of the "fixed one instance of a bug class, missed the sibling instances in the very same function" pattern: `apps/api/src/zip.ts`'s `buildZip` -- a minimal, dependency-free ZIP writer with no Zip64 support, used by both the code-export and "Backup all data" routes -- already has one explicit, well-commented guard (`if (entries.length > 0xffff) throw ...`) protecting the one 16-bit fixed-width field someone had clearly thought through: the end-of-central-directory record's own entry-count field. But the local/central file headers write a SECOND 16-bit field per entry -- the file-name length -- via the exact same `Buffer#writeUInt16LE` mechanism, completely unguarded.

**The gap and why it's reachable**: nothing upstream caps an entity or field name's length at all -- `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s `EntitySchema`/`FieldSchema` both declare `name: z.string().min(1)` with no `.max()` anywhere. A long enough entity name (e.g. created directly via the API, not necessarily through any UI control that might otherwise discourage it) survives `backup.ts`'s own `sanitizeZipEntryName` (which only swaps out unsafe characters, never truncates) and reaches `buildZip` as a ZIP entry path. Without a guard, that failed deep inside `Buffer#writeUInt16LE` with a generic `RangeError: The value of "value" is out of range...` -- the exact same unhelpful, un-actionable failure shape the existing entry-count guard's own doc comment was written specifically to avoid, just for a sibling field inside the same function that never got the same treatment.

**Scope decision -- independently verified and deliberately narrowed**: the survey's own report additionally flagged two further unguarded 32-bit fields in the same function: a single entry's own content length (`dataBuf.length`, written via `writeUInt32LE`) and the cumulative running `offset`/`centralDirectoryOffset` across all entries. Both are real, equally-unguarded instances of the identical pattern -- but confirmed, by directly reading `buildZip`'s own code, that proving either one empirically (per this routine's own "regression-proof must fail without the fix" discipline) would require constructing an entry whose content, or whose cumulative total across entries, approaches the ~4GB 32-bit boundary -- an allocation large enough to risk this environment's own memory ceiling (the same one round 834 documented SIGKILLing `codegen.test.ts` around 10GB RSS). Rather than ship an unverified change, this round's fix was deliberately narrowed to just the one gap that's both genuinely reachable AND cheaply, safely testable: the 16-bit file-name-length field. The 32-bit `dataBuf.length`/cumulative-`offset` guards are left as a named, explicit, NOT-yet-implemented candidate for a future round (the same "split across rounds when full verification isn't practical in one" discipline rounds 835/836 and 842/843 already established).

**The fix**: `buildZip`'s per-entry loop now checks `nameBuf.length > 0xffff` immediately after computing `nameBuf`, throwing the same style of clear, actionable error (naming the offending entry's own path and byte count) the existing entry-count guard already uses, before any `Buffer#write*` call can fail with the raw, generic version.

**The test**: a new `zip.test.ts` test mirroring the existing entry-count overflow test's own exact structure and assertion style (`assert.throws(..., /Zip64/i)`, matching specifically on the word "Zip64" to distinguish the intended descriptive error from the raw Buffer RangeError's own coincidentally-similar wording) -- one entry whose `path` is 70000+ bytes long must throw the new error, while a name landing exactly at the 65535-byte boundary must still succeed (confirming the guard isn't overly strict).

**Verification**: confirmed failing without the fix -- the raw, undescriptive `RangeError: The value of "value" is out of range... Received 70004` the fix exists to replace -- via a `git stash push -- apps/api/src/zip.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, and passing with the fix restored. The full `zip.test.ts` suite (5/5) ran clean. The full `@forge/api` suite (`npm test`) reported 597/598 passing, with the one reported failure being `src/codegen.test.ts` itself getting `SIGKILL`ed after ~177 seconds -- confirmed, by reading the actual log line (`signal: 'SIGKILL'`), to be round 834's own previously-documented environmental memory-ceiling limitation (unrelated to this round's change, which never touches `codegen.ts`), not a regression; re-running the full suite a second time, capturing complete output directly rather than relying on the background-task tool's own truncated capture, reproduced the identical single `codegen.test.ts`-only failure, confirming it as a pre-existing, already-known fact about this file rather than something introduced by this round's zip.ts fix. `apps/api`'s own build (`esbuild src/server.ts ...`) ran clean.

**A reinforced lesson from this round's own verification process**: the background-task tool's "completed" notification for a long `npm test` run, when the command is launched via `cmd > log 2>&1 &` *combined with* the Bash tool's own `run_in_background: true`, fires on the OUTER wrapper script finishing (which only launches the real process and returns almost immediately) -- the exact double-backgrounding trap documented since round 833, hit again here. Confirmed via `ps aux` that the real `tsx --test` process was still running well after that false "completed" notification, and switched to the `Monitor` tool (`while kill -0 <pid>; do sleep 3; done; echo PROCESS_EXITED`) to wait for the real process's own exit instead of trusting the misleading notification.

**Status**: shipped and pushed.

**What makes this one notable beyond a plain missed port**: `codegen.test.ts` already has a dedicated parity test for this exact pair of functions (`"the exported app's embedded buildZip sets the UTF-8 flag and rejects more than 65535 entries, matching the live zip.ts"`), whose own doc comment EXPLICITLY reasoned that neither the UTF-8-flag nor the entry-count gap it was fixing "was reachable through this app's own backup endpoint (entity names are always plain ASCII identifiers -- see codegen.ts's own `assertSafe` -- and a real project has nowhere near 65535 entities), so it was never a live bug." **Independent verification before implementing**: read `codegen.ts`'s own `buildZip` (lines 570-642) directly, confirming the entry-count guard (578-580) exists but the entry-name-length guard does not, with the unguarded `writeUInt16LE(nameBuf.length, 26)`/`(..., 28)` writes at lines 601/616. Read the generated `/api/backup` route (lines 826-845) directly, confirming `entity.name` flows straight into `path: \`${entity.name}.csv\`` with no intermediate length check, then into `buildZip(zipEntries)`.

**The fix**: added the identical guard round 844 added to `zip.ts`, ported into `codegen.ts`'s own embedded copy, including matching backtick-escaping discipline for the throw statement's own template literal (this function's source is itself embedded inside one of `codegen.ts`'s giant backtick-delimited template-literal strings).

**The test**: a new `codegen.test.ts` test reusing the existing parity test's own regex-extraction technique (pulling the real generated `CRC_TABLE`/`crc32`/`DOS_TIME`/`DOS_DATE`/`buildZip` source out of `generateExportFiles(...)`'s `server.js` output and executing it via `new Function(...)`, not a reimplementation) -- confirming a 70000+ byte path throws the new `/Zip64/i`-matching error, and a name landing exactly at the 65535-byte boundary still succeeds. No multi-gigabyte buffers needed, the same reason round 844's own 16-bit guard was practically testable where its deferred 32-bit siblings aren't. Also updated the existing parity test's own doc comment to record that round 844 invalidated its "never a live bug" reasoning, rather than leaving a now-incorrect justification sitting next to a test that no longer fully reflects reality.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix -- the identical raw, undescriptive `RangeError: ... Received 70004` round 844 already fixed on the `zip.ts` side -- via a `git stash push -- apps/api/src/codegen.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, and passing with the fix restored. Re-ran, via targeted `--test-name-pattern` (never a full-suite claim for this file, per round 834's documented SIGKILL-ceiling finding), both `buildZip`-related tests plus the `/api/backup` route tests plus the esbuild syntax-validity check -- all 6 pass clean, confirming no template-literal escaping mistake and no regression in the existing parity test. `node --check` on `codegen.ts` and `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` (untouched this round, run as a sanity check) both came back clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed. Both of this file's independently-duplicated `buildZip` copies now guard both of their reachable fixed-width-field overflows (entry count, entry-name length) identically. The 32-bit `dataBuf.length`/cumulative-`offset` guards remain the one still-open, explicitly-deferred candidate in this function, on both copies, pending a genuinely new, safe testing strategy.
