### Round 865: entityTabOrder.ts was the one per-entity preference store round 853's own sweep never reached, because it's keyed differently from its 9 siblings

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey went back to `entityPreferenceCleanup.ts` itself -- the round-853 sweep that purges a dropped entity's stale preferences out of 9 separate localStorage stores -- and found a 10th store that sweep never touched, for a structural reason rather than an oversight in the obvious sense: it doesn't match the shape the other 9 share.

**The gap**: `entityTabOrder.ts` persists a project's entity-tab display order, but unlike every other store `purgeEntityPreferences` already sweeps (each keyed by `${projectId}:${entityName}`, so a dropped entity's whole entry can just be deleted), this one is keyed by `projectId` alone, with the entity names living *inside* its `string[]` value. `purgeEntityTabOrderForProject` (whole-project deletion) already existed and is exercised by `projectPreferenceCleanup.test.ts`, but there was no equivalent for removing just one name from inside that array -- and `entityPreferenceCleanup.test.ts` never mentioned `entityTabOrder` at all, confirming this was never a tested, intentional exclusion.

**Why this is reachable, not theoretical**: dragging the entity tab bar into a custom order is an ordinary, advertised interaction (`App.tsx`'s `setEntityTabOrder` calls). A user who reorders tabs, then refines the project in a way that drops one of those entities, then refines again *reintroducing an entity with the same name* (a materially common real-world case -- "actually, add Deal tracking back" after an earlier "remove deals tracking") sees the reintroduced entity's tab silently snap back into whatever position the old, unrelated entity occupied -- instead of landing at the natural end the way a genuinely new entity does via `applyColumnOrder`'s own "ignore unknown names" fallback (`columnOrder.ts`), which has no way to know a surviving name now refers to something unrelated. This is exactly the "stale preference silently reapplied to a new, unrelated entity" hazard `entityPreferenceCleanup.ts`'s own doc comment already names as the whole sweep's motivation -- this store just didn't match the `${projectId}:${entityName}` grep pattern the sweep's original author used to find its siblings. Independently of the stale-reapply angle, the dropped name also simply leaks in that project's localStorage entry forever for a long-lived, frequently-refined project -- the identical unbounded-growth shape rounds 390/392/399/401/853 each closed elsewhere.

**The fix**: added `purgeEntityNameFromTabOrder(projectId, entityName)` to `entityTabOrder.ts` -- filters the one dropped name out of the stored array (a no-op, not an error, when the project was never reordered or the name isn't present) -- and wired it into `purgeEntityPreferences` alongside the existing 9 calls. No change needed in `App.tsx`'s `handleBuildComplete`: it already calls `purgeEntityPreferences` once per dropped entity name, so the new call reaches it for free.

**The tests**: two new `entityTabOrder.test.ts` unit tests for the new function directly (removes exactly one name, leaves a sibling project's own order -- including its own same-named entry -- untouched; a true no-op on an unreordered or absent name), plus extended the existing comprehensive `entityPreferenceCleanup.test.ts` test with a tab-order seed for both the dropped and surviving project, asserting the dropped name disappears while the sibling entity's position and an unrelated project's own order (including its own identically-named entry) survive fully intact.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix -- via a `git stash push -- apps/web/src/entityTabOrder.ts apps/web/src/entityPreferenceCleanup.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle (keeping both test files in place) -- the comprehensive test's new assertion failed with the stale `"Customer"` entry still present, and `entityTabOrder.test.ts` failed to even load (`SyntaxError: no export named purgeEntityNameFromTabOrder`), both passing cleanly with the fix restored. The full `apps/web` suite ran clean both times (1144 tests before this round's two new cases were added, 1146 after). `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` ran clean both before and after the stash cycle.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/entityTabOrder.ts` + `apps/web/src/entityPreferenceCleanup.ts` only -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no entity tab bar / multi-entity nav of its own at all (a single exported app per project, confirmed via grep), so there is no sibling to port this to.

### Round 866: restoring a Time Machine checkpoint dropped entities just as routinely as a refine does, but never ran the same localStorage sweep -- a second code path round 853/865's own fix never reached

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. With `handleBuildComplete`'s own entity-drop sweep now covering all 10 per-entity-keyed stores (rounds 853/865), this round's survey asked the obvious next question -- is `handleBuildComplete` the ONLY place an entity can disappear from a project's live spec? -- and found a second, structurally separate answer: restoring an older checkpoint.

**The gap**: `App.tsx`'s `onRestored` callback (the sole handler `HistoryPanel`'s `handleRestore` invokes after a successful checkpoint restore) only ever did `setProject(restored)` / `setActiveEntity(...)` / `setBuildWarning(null)` / `setShowHistory(false)` -- no entity-drop detection, no `purgeEntityPreferences` call at all. A repo-wide grep confirmed `purgeEntityPreferences` had exactly one call site before this round: `handleBuildComplete`.

**Why this is reachable, not theoretical**: `routes/projects.ts`'s own restore-checkpoint route comment already explicitly names this as an expected, normal outcome -- restoring an older checkpoint "can easily ... simply [be] missing an entity/field the user has been actively using with real data in it." The everyday flow: build a project with entities A/B/C, customize column widths/order/hidden fields/filters/group-by/collapsed board columns/collapsed groups/sort keys/view mode/recent searches/tab order for entity C, open Time Machine, restore an earlier checkpoint predating C. C's tab disappears from the UI, but every one of its ten localStorage entries is left behind permanently -- and per `entityPreferenceCleanup.ts`'s own doc comment, several of those stores have no type-check against the live entity shape at all, so a LATER refine or restore that reintroduces an entity literally named "C" with a different field shape would silently reapply the stale preference (a `groupByField` naming a field that no longer exists, `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference`'s stale enum values) to the new, unrelated entity -- a genuine correctness bug, not merely an unbounded-growth leak.

**The fix**: mirrors `handleBuildComplete`'s own drop-detection exactly -- captures the pre-restore entity names from the current `project` state (closed over before `setProject` overwrites it, the identical pattern `handleBuildComplete` already uses, with the identical reason: it has to run before the state update, not after), diffs against `restored.spec.entities`, and calls `purgeEntityPreferences(restored.id, entityName)` for each name missing from the restored checkpoint. No shared helper was extracted -- the three-line diff is inlined in both places, matching this codebase's own established preference (seen repeatedly in `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s "mirror, don't import" convention) for keeping small, surface-specific logic duplicated rather than introducing a premature abstraction for two call sites.

**An existing test needed updating, caught by directly running the suite rather than assuming success**: `App.test.ts`'s pre-existing extraction-based `onRestored` test (round 469, confirming the callback clears a stale `buildWarning`) uses `new Function(...)` with an explicit parameter list -- the exact "new free variable breaks extraction test" fragility this routine has hit before (round 853). Adding `project`/`purgeEntityPreferences` as new free variables inside the callback required adding both to that test's own parameter list and call-site arguments (a real `project` fixture via `makeProject`, a no-op purge stub) before it would even load.

**The test**: a new `App.test.ts` test mirroring `handleBuildComplete`'s own round-853 purge test exactly -- a restore dropping two of three entities must call `purgeEntityPreferences` once per dropped entity with the restored project's own id, and never for the one that survived.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix -- the new purge test recorded zero calls where two were expected, while the pre-existing build-warning test (updated for the new parameters, but exercising a different code path) still passed unaffected -- via a `git stash push -- apps/web/src/App.tsx` / run / `git stash pop` cycle (keeping `App.test.ts` in place), and passing with the fix restored. The full `apps/web` suite ran clean both times (1146 tests before this round's one new test, 1147 after). `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` ran clean both before and after the stash cycle.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/App.tsx` + `apps/web/src/App.test.ts` only -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no Time Machine / checkpoint-restore feature of its own at all, so there is no sibling to port this to.

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. The relation-hub insight is hit twice over: its own target entity's label, AND every source entity's label inside its per-target breakdown, both independently unguarded. `twinReport.ts`'s Copy/Download companion reproduces the identical raw text, carrying the ambiguity into the downloaded artifact too, not just the live screen.

The full `twin.test.ts` suite (38 tests, up from 34) and the full `apps/api` suite (497 tests, every file except the SIGKILL-prone `codegen.test.ts`) both ran clean. `apps/api`'s build ran clean.

### Round 868: the message-template field advertised {{fieldName}} interpolation for schedule rules, which fireScheduledRule never actually performs

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey found a gap in `AutomationsPanel.tsx`'s own create/edit-rule form: the message-template textarea's placeholder example and hint text advertised `{{fieldName}}` interpolation unconditionally, for every trigger -- but one trigger's own backend path never honors it.

**The gap**: `apps/api/src/automations.ts`'s `fireScheduledRule` -- the handler for schedule-triggered rules -- has its own doc comment stating the reasoning plainly: "a schedule rule has no triggering record at all ... no {{field}} placeholder could ever resolve to anything," and sends `rule.messageTemplate` completely raw (`whatsapp.sendMessage(project.id, to, rule.messageTemplate)`, with no `interpolateTemplate` call at all) for both the WhatsApp send and the webhook action type the same message field is shared across (`fireWebhookAction` only interpolates when `entity && record` are both non-null; `fireScheduledRule` always calls it with both `null`). This is deliberate, already-tested backend behavior, not something this round needed to touch. `AutomationsPanel.tsx` itself already knows this for the DESTINATION half of a schedule rule -- its own `toMode` picker is forced to `"static"` the moment "schedule" is chosen, with a comment explaining there's no record to read a `toMode:"field"` destination from -- but the message-template field right below it never got the same treatment.

**Why this is reachable**: `CreateAutomationRuleSchema`/`UpdateAutomationRuleSchema` place zero restriction on a schedule rule's `messageTemplate` content, so nothing blocks saving one containing `{{...}}` syntax. A user picking the "Schedule" trigger for an everyday use case (a daily 9am reminder, say) reads the form's own instructions and example text -- both still showing `{{customerName}}` -- and reasonably writes something like "Good morning {{customerName}}, your appointment is today!" Every time that schedule fires, the real WhatsApp recipient (or webhook consumer) receives the literal, unsubstituted text `"{{customerName}}"` -- a visibly broken, unprofessional message sent to an external party, with nothing anywhere in the product warning this would happen.

**The fix**: a new schedule-specific hint/placeholder pair (en/he), swapped in the moment `trigger === "schedule"` is chosen -- mirroring the `toMode` picker's own existing conditional right above this field. The new hint explains the message is sent exactly as written since there's no record to read a value from; the new placeholder example contains no `{{...}}` syntax anywhere, so it can never model a pattern the backend will silently fail to honor.

**The test**: a new `AutomationsPanel.test.ts` test confirming the default placeholder/hint still advertise `{{fieldName}}` for every other trigger, swap to the schedule-specific pair (no `"{{"` anywhere) the instant "schedule" is chosen, and swap back once a non-schedule trigger is chosen again -- proving this is live, reversible UI state tied to the trigger selector, not a one-way mistake.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix -- the placeholder never dropped its `"{{"` after choosing "schedule" -- via a `git stash push -- apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.tsx apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle (keeping the test file in place), and passing with the fix restored. The full `AutomationsPanel.test.ts` suite (38 tests, up from 37) and `i18n/language.test.ts` (including its own automated "every `t(...)` key used by a component exists in both languages" scan) both ran clean, as did the full `apps/web` suite (1148 tests, up from 1147) and `apps/web`'s `tsc -b`.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.tsx` + `apps/web/src/AutomationsPanel.test.ts` + `apps/web/src/i18n/language.ts` only -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no automations feature of its own at all, so there is no sibling to port this to.

### Round 869: Order's keyword list spuriously fired on the common English idiom "in order to", injecting a spare Order entity into completely unrelated apps

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey went back to `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts`'s keyword-matching rules -- already the subject of a long, documented history of substring/idiom collision fixes (Deal's removed "pipeline", Appointment's removed "schedule", Order's own earlier `\b`-bounded fix for "disorder"/"recorder"/"border") -- and found a different pitfall the earlier `\b`-bounded fix never reached.

**The gap**: Order's keyword list used a plain `\b`-bounded `/\border(s)?\b/` regex. That bound correctly rejects "disorder(s)"/"recorder(s)"/"border(s)" (the substring-collision shape its own comment documents), but it still matches "order" as a genuinely standalone, correctly-spelled word inside "in order to" -- one of the most common connector phrases in ordinary English. This is the exact same idiom-co-occurrence shape (pitfall 1b) Deal's "pipeline" and Appointment's "schedule" keywords were already removed for, just never checked for Order's own "order".

**Confirmed empirically before fixing**, per this routine's own standing discipline not to assume a regex fix transfers without a real repro: ran `HeuristicSpecProvider`'s actual `matchEntities` against "An app for a yoga studio to manage class schedules, in order to help instructors plan their week" and "A tool to track employee certifications in order to stay compliant" -- both spuriously matched `Order`, with nothing else in either description remotely e-commerce-related. (A third phrasing, "An app to manage work orders for our maintenance team," also co-fires `Order` alongside the correct, dedicated `WorkOrder` entity -- noted but deliberately left unaddressed, since fixing it would require either dropping the bare keyword outright or a much broader exclusion, and the "in order to" idiom alone is overwhelmingly more common across ordinary app descriptions.)

**Why this is reachable**: `HeuristicSpecProvider` is Forge AI's documented, zero-configuration fallback provider -- used by any project built with no Anthropic API key configured. A spurious match flows straight into `ProductSpec.entities`, producing a real "Order List"/"Order Form" screen pair, a real SQL table with a customerName/total/status/items/courierId schema the moment Build is clicked, a nonsensical extra tab in the live app preview, and (via `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES`, which includes `"Order"`) a wrongly-flipped "needs Stripe" payment recommendation for an app that has nothing to do with selling goods.

**Why this isn't a simple keyword removal**: unlike "pipeline"/"schedule" (which Deal/Appointment's own other keywords already covered without the bare word), two existing `heuristic.test.ts` tests rely on bare "order" matching a genuine standalone use ("Place an order for pickup.", "order-management"), and Order's other keywords (purchase/checkout/delivery) don't cover every legitimate order-tracking description on their own. Dropping the keyword outright would have been a real regression, not a clean fix.

**The fix**: narrowed the match to exclude only the exact three-word idiom itself -- "in" immediately before AND "to" immediately after the very same "order(s)" occurrence -- rather than either half alone. Verified via a standalone repro script against nine hand-picked phrasings (including the tricky "ship customer orders to their destinations," a real logistics sentence that a cruder "exclude whenever followed by to" fix would have wrongly rejected too) before writing the regex into the file, confirming the precise combination was necessary and sufficient.

**The test**: a new `heuristic.test.ts` test confirming both unrelated-domain descriptions no longer spuriously match `Order`, a real "orders to their destinations" logistics phrase still matches, and a real "orders" mention elsewhere in the same text as the idiom still matches too (proving the exclusion doesn't suppress a genuine co-occurring match).

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix via a `git stash push -- packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, and passing with the fix restored. The full `heuristic.test.ts` suite (92 tests, up from 91) and the full `@forge/spec-engine` suite (164 tests, up from 163) ran clean, as did the full `apps/api` suite (497 tests, every file except the SIGKILL-prone `codegen.test.ts`) and `apps/api`'s build.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts` + `packages/spec-engine/src/heuristic.test.ts` only -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no spec-generation feature of its own at all, so there is no sibling to port this to.

### Round 874: isCheckpointCurrent wrongly marked a checkpoint "Current" and disabled its own Restore button when only an entity's or field's own LABEL had been renamed since

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. A first survey attempt this round proposed a plausible-looking entity-vs-entity ZIP path collision in `backup.ts`'s `generateBackupZipEntries` -- but tracing through `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s own `ProductSpecSchema` turned up a guard that already structurally prevents it: `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` rejects any spec where two entity names collapse to the same string under a BROADER, case-insensitive character-replacement set than `backup.ts`'s own narrower, case-sensitive `sanitizeZipEntryName`. Since the narrow set is a strict subset of the broad one, any pair that could ever collide in the backup ZIP is already rejected before the project can reach "built" status at all -- proven both mathematically and empirically (ran the real schema against several colliding name pairs; every one was rejected). Not shipped, since there was nothing left to fix -- a second survey, explicitly warned off this trap, found a genuine gap in `checkpointDiff.ts`.

**The gap**: `isCheckpointCurrent` answers a stricter question than its sibling `computeCheckpointDiff` -- not just "would restoring lose anything" but "is this EXACTLY what's on screen right now," per its own doc comment, which already explains why `summary`/`roles`/`description` all needed explicit byte-exact equality checks for that reason (rounds 773 and 817). `fieldSignature` (used for the entity/field structural comparison) deliberately excludes a field's own `label` -- reasonably, since a pure rename isn't a "structural change" worth flagging in `computeCheckpointDiff`'s diff summary -- but `isCheckpointCurrent` never added its own separate label check the way it already does for `description`, leaving the identical class of gap open for both entity and field labels.

**Confirmed empirically before fixing**: ran the real `isCheckpointCurrent` against two specs identical in every property except `entity.label` ("Customer" vs "Client") and `field.label` ("Name" vs "Full Name") -- it returned `true`, when it should have returned `false`.

**Why this is reachable**: entity/field label renames (`routes/projects.ts`'s `PATCH .../entities/:entityName/label` and `.../fields/:fieldName/label`) do a direct `updateProjectSpec` write with no new checkpoint ever inserted -- checkpoints only ever come from `pipeline.ts`'s build/refine flow. So every pre-existing checkpoint keeps the OLD label forever while the live spec shows the new one. `HistoryPanel.tsx`'s `isCurrent` directly disables that checkpoint's own Restore button (`disabled={... || isCurrent}`) -- since the restore route replaces the entire spec including labels, restoring it would genuinely revert the rename, but the UI falsely claimed "this is already what you have" and blocked the one action that would actually undo it.

**The fix**: added explicit `entity.label`/`field.label` equality checks inside `isCheckpointCurrent`'s own entity/field loops, mirroring the existing `description` check right next to them -- the same precedent this function already established for non-structural-but-rendered content.

**The test**: a new `checkpointDiff.test.ts` test covering both an entity-label-only change and a field-label-only change, each with every other property byte-identical.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix via a `git stash push -- apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, and passing with the fix restored. The full `checkpointDiff.test.ts` suite (48 tests, up from 47) and `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` ran clean, as did the full `apps/web` suite (1151 tests, up from 1150).

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.ts` + `apps/web/src/checkpointDiff.test.ts` only -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no Time Machine / checkpoint-restore feature of its own at all (established in round 866), so there is no sibling to port this to.

### Round 875: GlobalSearch's Enter key hijacked a freshly-edited query to a stale, previously arrow-selected result group instead of submitting it

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey found a real, user-reachable keyboard-interaction bug in `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`, with zero existing test coverage for the exact sequence that triggers it.

**The gap**: `selectedIndex` (which result group is arrow-key-highlighted) was only ever reset to `null` inside `runSearch` itself -- once for the empty-query early-return, once when real results arrive -- never the moment the query text changed, before that new search ever ran. The input's own `onChange` did nothing to it. `handleInputKeyDown`'s Enter branch only checked `selectedIndex !== null`, never that it still corresponded to the text currently in the box.

**Reachable sequence**: type a query, submit, get results; press ArrowDown to highlight the first result group; without pressing Enter yet, edit the query to something unrelated; press Enter. Because `selectedIndex` is still non-null from the old search, `e.preventDefault()` fires and `onJumpToEntity` is called with the OLD entity name -- the form's `onSubmit` (which would run the new search) never runs at all. The user's new query is silently discarded and the panel instead navigates to an unrelated, stale entity tab. This directly contradicts the component's own doc comment ("Enter with nothing highlighted still submits the form as a normal search, so this never changes behavior for someone who just types and hits Enter once") -- the comment's premise (no highlight survives into a new query) turned out to be false.

**Confirmed empirically before fixing**: wrote a real jsdom/Testing-Library repro using the actual component (not a reimplementation) -- searched "widget", ArrowDown-selected the first group, changed the input to an unrelated string, fired a real `keydown Enter`. `onJumpToEntity` was called with the stale entity instead of `[]`.

**The fix**: a single `useEffect(() => setSelectedIndex(null), [query])`, keyed on the query text alone rather than patched into each individual handler -- covers every way the text can change (typing, the existing Escape-to-clear branch, the separate "clear query" button) in one place, rather than three scattered resets that could drift out of sync later.

**`apps/api/src/codegen.ts` had the identical, independently-duplicated copy** of this component (`GlobalSearch.jsx`, per this codebase's established per-surface duplication pattern) with the byte-for-byte same bug -- confirmed by reading its own `handleInputKeyDown`/`runSearch`/`onChange` directly. Same fix applied there.

**The tests**: a new `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` test (real DOM interaction) and a new `codegen.test.ts` test rendering the real generated `GlobalSearch.jsx` end to end (not an extracted function, since the bug lives in the interaction between the input's `onChange` and the keydown handler, not in either alone).

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix -- via two independent `git stash` / run / `git stash pop` cycles, one per file -- recording the stale jump instead of an empty array, and passing with each fix restored. The full `GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` suite (25 tests, up from 24) and `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` ran clean, as did every GlobalSearch-related `codegen.test.ts` test (28, up from 27, run targeted since the full file SIGKILLs). The full `apps/web` suite (1152 tests, up from 1151), the full `apps/api` suite (497 tests, every file except the SIGKILL-prone `codegen.test.ts` itself), and `apps/api`'s build all ran clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` + `apps/web/src/GlobalSearchPanel.test.ts` + `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` + `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts`.

### Round 876: a refine that loosens a field away from a typed value left any field_equals automation rule on it enabled, with its stale type-shaped fieldValue becoming a coincidental free-text match hazard

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey found a real, verified gap in `diffAndMigrate`'s own automation-rule safety sweep -- the exact mechanism that already protects against several other refine-caused staleness hazards (field removal, enum narrowing, relation retargeting) had one direction of its own type-change check missing.

**The gap**: the `type_changed` branch's automation-disable condition only ever checked the NEW field type (`field.type !== "text" && field.type !== "longtext"`), correctly catching a field TIGHTENING from text-like into a typed value (text → boolean, where a free-text fieldValue like "yes" is no longer valid) but missing the mirror-image direction entirely: a field LOOSENING from a typed value (boolean/enum/number/date/relation) into text/longtext.

**Why this matters**: a `field_equals` automation rule's own `fieldValue` is only ever validated against the field's type at creation/edit time (`validateAutomationFieldValue`, `routes/projects.ts`) -- never re-checked by a later refine. `automations.ts`'s `matchesTrigger` does a pure `String(actual) === rule.fieldValue` comparison with no type awareness of its own. So a rule created against a boolean field with `fieldValue: "true"` survived a refine that loosens the field to text fully enabled, and would then match ANY record whose newly-freeform text value happens to literally equal `"true"` -- firing a real WhatsApp send or outbound webhook for a reason with zero connection to the original boolean intent.

**Confirmed empirically end-to-end before fixing**, against the real functions (not reimplementations): built a boolean field, created a `field_equals` rule with `fieldValue: "true"`, refined the field to text -- the rule stayed `enabled: true`, and `matchesTrigger` returned `true` for an unrelated record whose text value happened to literally equal `"true"`. Also independently confirmed the fix closes the real firing path, not just the `enabled` flag cosmetically: `runAutomationsForRecordChange` only ever evaluates `listEnabledAutomationRulesForEntity`'s own results, so a disabled rule is fully excluded before `matchesTrigger` is ever called on it.

**The fix**: a small `isTextLikeFieldType(type)` helper, and the tightening-only condition changed to `!isTextLikeFieldType(prevField.type) || !isTextLikeFieldType(field.type)` -- disabling on either direction of a transition into or out of the text-like bucket, while a pure text↔longtext change (already safe, and already covered by an existing passing test) still doesn't disable anything.

**Two sibling checks with the identical one-sided shape, investigated and left untouched**: `migrate.ts`'s own "new_column reusing a physical column" branch has two more instances of the same `field.type !== "text" && field.type !== "longtext"` pattern. Traced through carefully: by the time that branch runs, any automation rule referencing the field was already created against its CURRENT, correctly-declared type (a rule can't reference a field that doesn't exist yet), so the `type_changed` entry that branch reports reflects a stale PHYSICAL column shape left over from an earlier removed field, not a change to the CURRENT field's own declared type underneath an existing rule. Not a repeat of this round's bug -- left alone rather than over-reaching into an unverified, structurally different scenario.

**The test**: a new `migrate.test.ts` test -- a boolean field with a `field_equals` rule retyped to text, confirming the rule is disabled and the `type_changed` entry is reported.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix via a `git stash push -- packages/db/src/migrate.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle, and passing with the fix restored. The full `migrate.test.ts` suite (43 tests, up from 42) and the full `@forge/db` suite (222 tests) ran clean, as did the full `apps/api` suite (497 tests, every file except the SIGKILL-prone `codegen.test.ts`) and `apps/api`'s build.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `packages/db/src/migrate.ts` + `packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts` only -- `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no automations feature of its own at all, so there is no sibling to port this to.

### Round 877: dropping entity "Foo" silently wiped the unrelated, still-live entity "Foo:Bar"'s own collapsed-board-column/collapsed-group preferences, since entity/field names have no character restriction at all

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey found a real, verified localStorage preference-key collision, reachable because this codebase places no character restriction on entity or field names anywhere.

**The gap**: `EntitySchema`/`FieldSchema` only require `name: z.string().min(1)` -- the only two schema-level refines (`findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames`, `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions`) don't reject a pair like entity "Foo" and entity "Foo:Bar" coexisting in one project. `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` and `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` are the only two of this codebase's many per-entity localStorage preference stores where the entity-drop purge (`purgeCollapsedBoardColumnsForEntity`/`purgeCollapsedGroupsForEntity`) can't do an exact-key delete, since their keys have a third segment (boardFieldName/groupFieldName) unknown at purge time -- `findBoardField`/the grouping field is recomputed fresh from the entity's current fields every render, never passed into the purge call. So both fell back to a colon-joined-string `key.startsWith(\`${projectId}:${entityName}:\`)` scan, and `"proj:Foo:"` is a literal string-prefix of `"proj:Foo:Bar:stage"` -- dropping entity "Foo" wiped entity "Foo:Bar"'s own, completely unrelated, still-live collapsed-column/collapsed-group state too. Every other per-entity store in the codebase (`columnWidths.ts`, `columnOrder.ts`, `columnVisibility.ts`, `fieldFiltersPreference.ts`, `groupByPreference.ts`, `sortKeysPreference.ts`, `viewModePreference.ts`, `entityRecentSearches.ts`, `entityTabOrder.ts`) was checked and confirmed NOT vulnerable: each has only a 2-segment key (project+entity), so its own entity-drop purge is already an exact-key delete.

**Confirmed empirically before fixing**: a throwaway repro (written temporarily inside `apps/web/src/` so Node's module resolution could find `jsdom`, then deleted) used the real `setCollapsedBoardColumns`/`getCollapsedBoardColumns`/`purgeCollapsedBoardColumnsForEntity` functions directly -- seeded "Foo" and "Foo:Bar" each with their own collapsed-column values, purged "Foo", and confirmed "Foo:Bar"'s own entry was wiped too (`getCollapsedBoardColumns("proj1", "Foo:Bar", "stage")` returned `[]` instead of `["archived"]`).

**Why a simple escaping or split-based fix wouldn't fully work**: both `entityName` and `boardFieldName`/`groupFieldName` are themselves unrestricted strings that could contain colons, so neither "escape colons within entityName" nor "split on the last colon" fully resolves the ambiguity from every angle.

**The fix**: both stores now key on `JSON.stringify([projectId, entityName, boardFieldName])` instead of a colon-joined template string. JSON array encoding makes segment boundaries unambiguous regardless of what characters a segment contains, so the purge functions now parse each stored key back into its 3 components and compare them exactly, rather than string-prefix-matching the raw key. This is a one-time reset of these two low-severity UI preferences for any existing user whose browser already has the old colon-joined keys stored (a cost similar in kind to round 861's accepted session-token-invalidation trade-off), accepted since there is no way to migrate an inherently ambiguous old key format forward safely.

**`apps/api/src/codegen.ts` had its own duplicated copy** of these two stores for the exported standalone app (`getPersistedCollapsedGroups`/`setPersistedCollapsedGroups`, `getPersistedCollapsedBoardColumns`/`setPersistedCollapsedBoardColumns`), keyed by `entityName + ":" + fieldName` with no projectId (a standalone app is always single-project) and no purge functions at all (it purges nothing on entity removal). That still left the identical raw get/set collision one level down: entity "Foo" field "Bar:baz" and entity "Foo:Bar" field "baz" both produce the literal key `"Foo:Bar:baz"`, so one entity's collapsed state could silently leak into or get overwritten by the other's. Fixed the same way (`JSON.stringify([entityName, fieldName])`), confirmed by a new test that calls these functions directly with the colliding pair after appending an export statement to the real generated `EntityView.jsx` -- avoiding the need for an entity literally named "Foo:Bar" in a real spec, which would separately break codegen's own unrelated use of raw entity names as JS identifiers in its generated import statements (a distinct, pre-existing gap, noted but out of scope for this round).

**The tests**: a new `entityPreferenceCleanup.test.ts` test seeding sibling entities "Foo" and "Foo:Bar" in the same project and confirming `purgeEntityPreferences("proj1", "Foo")` leaves "Foo:Bar"'s collapsed-board-column/collapsed-group entries untouched; a new `codegen.test.ts` test exercising the raw get/set collision directly against the real generated functions; two existing `codegen.test.ts` tests that inspected the raw stored key format directly updated to the new `JSON.stringify` shape (the UI-driven toggle/collapse tests needed no changes, since they only ever go through the public functions).

**Verification**: confirmed both fixes failing cleanly without their respective change -- via two independent `git stash` / run / `git stash pop` cycles, one for the two `apps/web` files and one for `codegen.ts` -- and passing with each restored. The full `apps/web` suite (1153 tests, up from 1152) and `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` ran clean, as did every affected `codegen.test.ts` test (run targeted, since the full file SIGKILLs) and the full `apps/api` suite (497 tests, every file except `codegen.test.ts` itself) plus `apps/api`'s build.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` + `apps/web/src/collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` + `apps/web/src/entityPreferenceCleanup.test.ts` + `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` + `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts`.

### Round 878: Global Search's own per-entity result-group header never disambiguated two entities that happen to share the same display label

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey found the one surface in the well-established "unguarded-label-collision" family (rounds 635-642, 770, 864, 867) that the prior sweeps never reached: Global Search itself.

**The gap**: `EntitySchema`/`ProductSpecSchema` only enforce uniqueness on an entity's `name` (`findCaseInsensitiveDuplicateEntityNames`/`findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions`), never its display `label` -- so an ordinary project owner can, through the already-shipped Entity Label editor, rename two different entities (e.g. an active-customers table and an archived-customers one) to the identical label "Customers." `entityFormatting.ts`'s `searchEntityRecords` built `EntitySearchResult.entityLabel` as a bare `entity.label ?? entity.name`, with zero occurrence-counting -- unlike every field-label builder in the same file (`fieldDisplayLabel`/`fieldLabelOccurrences`) and unlike `checkpointDiff.ts`/`twin.ts`/`pipeline.ts`'s own entity-level `entityLabelOccurrences`/`entityDisplayLabel` pairs, all of which already disambiguate a shared label elsewhere in this exact codebase. `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s own per-entity result-group header (the live panel opened via Ctrl/Cmd+K or "/") rendered two completely indistinguishable headers for two entities sharing a label, each with its own "Go to tab" button -- no way to tell which group, or which jump target, was which before or after clicking. `searchReport.ts`'s Copy/Download feature inherited the identical ambiguity into its shareable text snapshot, since it just displays whatever `entityLabel` it's handed.

**Why this wasn't caught by the prior sweep**: rounds 635-642/770/864/867 each closed this bug class for a different file/feature (AutomationsPanel, Business Twin's six observation builders, checkpointDiff.ts/pipeline.ts, automationsReport.ts) -- Global Search was simply never named in any of those rounds' file lists, confirmed by grepping `docs/roadmap.md` directly for `searchEntityRecords`/`EntitySearchResult`/`searchReport` and finding no existing entry mentions entity-label disambiguation at all.

**The fix**: added `entityLabelOccurrences`/`entityDisplayLabel` to `entityFormatting.ts` (mirroring the existing field-level `fieldLabelOccurrences`/`fieldDisplayLabel` pair, and the identical pattern `checkpointDiff.ts` already uses for entities), and `searchEntityRecords` now disambiguates `entityLabel` against `allEntities` when given (e.g. "Customers (ActiveCustomer)"). Since `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx` and `searchReport.ts` both just display whatever `entityLabel` they're handed, fixing the one producer fixed both consumers for free -- no changes needed in either file itself.

**`apps/api/src/codegen.ts` had its own duplicated copy** of this feature (`searchAllEntities`, `formatGlobalSearchReport`, the exported `GlobalSearch` component's own render) with the identical gap, keyed by plain `entity.label` with no disambiguation at all. Fixed the same way, by adding the matching `entityLabelOccurrences`/`entityDisplayLabel` helpers to the generated `EntityView.jsx` output and calling them from `searchAllEntities`. **Caught a real bug in this round's own first attempt before it ever shipped**: those two new helpers are defined inside `EntityView.jsx`'s own generated template, but `searchAllEntities` lives in the separate `GlobalSearch.jsx` file -- an initial version left them un-exported, which would have thrown a genuine `ReferenceError` the moment a real user opened Global Search in any exported app, caught only because the full `codegen.test.ts` run (not just the one new targeted test) surfaced three now-failing pre-existing tests complaining `entityLabelOccurrences is not defined`. Fixed by exporting both helpers from `EntityView.jsx` and adding them to `GlobalSearch.jsx`'s own import list -- exactly the same wiring `matchesSearch`/`recordDisplayLabel` already use across these two files.

**The tests**: two new `entityFormatting.test.ts` tests (two entities sharing a label get distinct, name-suffixed labels; a unique label stays bare) proven failing without the fix and passing with it via a `git stash` cycle; a new `codegen.test.ts` test exercising the real generated `searchAllEntities` against two colliding entities, likewise proven failing without the fix; three existing `codegen.test.ts` tests (which sandbox-extract `searchAllEntities`/`runSearch` via regex for direct execution) updated to also extract and include the two new helper functions in their own sandboxed scope, since `searchAllEntities` now depends on them.

**Verification**: confirmed both fixes failing cleanly without their respective change, and passing with each restored, via two independent `git stash` / run / `git stash pop` cycles. All 25 GlobalSearch-related `codegen.test.ts` tests passed after the export/import fix (3 of them had briefly regressed during this round's own work, caught and fixed before commit). The full `apps/web` suite (1155 tests, up from 1153) and `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` ran clean (one unrelated, already-documented `BuildProgress.test.ts` flake in the full run reproduced as a pass in isolation, confirming it wasn't a real regression), as did the full `apps/api` suite (497 tests, every file except the SIGKILL-prone `codegen.test.ts` itself) and `apps/api`'s build.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.ts` + `apps/web/src/entityFormatting.test.ts` + `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` + `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts`.

### Round 879: a successful password reset never actually stripped `?resetToken=` from the URL, contradicting its own doc comment, so a refresh (or re-opening the same emailed link) afterward re-showed the form and failed with a confusing "expired/invalid" error

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey found a real "doc comment asserts behavior the code doesn't actually implement" drift bug in the password-reset flow -- a pattern this codebase has hit before in other files, newly found here in `AuthScreen.tsx`.

**The gap**: the `resetToken` state's own doc comment (`AuthScreen.tsx`) explicitly claims it is "cleared to null (and stripped from the URL)... once the reset actually completes, so a page refresh afterward -- or a second attempt with the same, now-consumed token -- doesn't look like it's still 'pending'." In reality only `handleBackToLogin` (an explicit, voluntary button click) ever did that. `handleResetPasswordSubmit`'s success branch only called `setResetDone(true)`, leaving the token sitting untouched in the URL bar.

**Reachable sequence, confirmed by reading the real route too**: a user follows the emailed `?resetToken=<token>` link, submits a new password, sees the success screen. `apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts`'s `/auth/reset-password` route deletes the token row unconditionally on success (`deletePasswordResetToken`, single-use by design) -- correct and intentional. The URL still reads `?resetToken=<token>`. Before clicking the page's own "Go to login" button, the user does something completely ordinary: refreshes, or re-opens the same emailed link a second time (webmail preview + mail app both opening it, a second device, or just habit after any form submit). `AuthScreen` remounts: `resetToken` re-reads the same non-null token from the URL, `resetDone` resets to its default `false`, and the component renders the reset-password FORM again instead of the success message. Submitting it now fails server-side, since the token row was already deleted -- a `401 RESET_TOKEN_INVALID` "This reset link has expired or is invalid" error, confusing for someone who had, in fact, already succeeded.

**Confirmed empirically**: read `AuthScreen.tsx`'s render gate (`resetToken ? (resetDone ? success : form) : normalLogin`) directly, and `routes/auth.ts`'s `/auth/reset-password` route, confirming the token deletion is unconditional on success with no idempotent "already used, but by you" special case. The existing `AuthScreen.test.ts` reset-flow test only ever exercises the happy path through clicking "Go to login" -- zero coverage either way for a refresh/remount before that click, consistent with this being a genuine miss rather than a deliberately accepted tradeoff.

**The fix**: `handleResetPasswordSubmit`'s success branch now strips the URL's query param immediately (the same one-liner `handleBackToLogin` already used) -- but deliberately *without* also nulling the in-memory `resetToken` state, which would flip the `resetToken && resetDone` render-gate back to the login screen and vanish the very success message this call is about to show. A subsequent refresh now mounts with a clean URL and lands on the normal login screen instead of re-showing a form for an already-dead token. This also finally makes the existing doc comment true.

**The test**: a new `AuthScreen.test.ts` test submitting a real reset through real DOM events, then asserting `window.location.search === ""` immediately after success -- before "Go to login" is ever clicked -- confirmed failing without the fix (URL still carried `?resetToken=abc123`) and passing with it, via a `git stash` cycle. `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported standalone app) has no auth/login feature of its own at all, so there is no sibling to port this to.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix and passing with it restored, via a `git stash push -- apps/web/src/AuthScreen.tsx` / run / `git stash pop` cycle. All 3 reset-password-related `AuthScreen.test.ts` tests passed together. The full `apps/web` suite (1156 tests, up from 1155) and `apps/web`'s `tsc -b` ran clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `apps/web/src/AuthScreen.tsx` + `apps/web/src/AuthScreen.test.ts` only.

### Round 880: MenuItem's bare "menu"/"תפריט" keyword spuriously fired on ordinary software UI chrome ("navigation menu", "hamburger menu", "dropdown menu", "menu bar"), fabricating a restaurant entity into completely unrelated app specs

Still no genuine reply from שלומי. This round's survey found a sibling of round 871's own "dish(es)" fix within the exact same `MenuItem` domain-entity rule -- a keyword never checked, and arguably far more reachable than the idiom collisions rounds 869-871 already closed.

**The gap**: `domainEntities.ts`'s `MenuItem` rule matched the plain substring `"menu"`/`"תפריט"` via `matchesKeyword`'s bare `lower.includes(kw)` (`heuristic.ts`), with zero word-boundary or disambiguation guard -- unlike this exact rule's own `"dish(es)"` keyword (round 871) and every one of this file's seven other keyword-collision fixes. `"menu"` is ubiquitous software UI vocabulary, not a niche idiom: "navigation menu", "hamburger menu", "dropdown menu", and "menu bar" all contain the literal substring and spuriously matched. `matchEntities` adds the WHOLE `MenuItem` entity (price/category/available fields) the instant any one keyword matches, with no secondary confirmation or threshold.

**Confirmed empirically before fixing**, against the real `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate` (not a reimplementation): "Build a task manager app with a navigation menu and a dashboard to organize my personal projects." produced entities `["MenuItem", "Project", "Task"]` -- a restaurant entity with zero connection to the app. "A simple note-taking app with a hamburger menu for settings and a list of notes." produced `["MenuItem"]` *alone* -- the entire spec became a restaurant menu, and the real Note/Item entity never appeared at all. The Hebrew counterpart ("...עם תפריט ניווט...", "...עם תפריט נפתח...") reproduced the identical failure. This is reachable in production, not just a self-hosting edge case: `selectProvider()` returns `HeuristicSpecProvider` whenever `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset (a first-class, documented zero-config mode), AND `generateSpec()` automatically falls back to it whenever a real Anthropic call fails for any reason (network error, rate limit, bad model output) -- so it's also the real runtime fallback for a signed-in user whose build request just happened to hit a transient AI failure.

**The fix**: mirrors the "dish(es)" fix's own exclusion shape (round 871) rather than dropping the keyword outright, since every existing test already pairs "menu"/"תפריט" with "cafe"/"restaurant"/"dish"/"מסעדה" -- excludes "menu" when immediately preceded by a UI-chrome qualifier (navigation/nav/hamburger/dropdown/drop-down/side/context/settings) or immediately followed by "bar"; excludes "תפריט" when immediately followed by ניווט/נפתח/צד (Hebrew's modifier-follows-noun word order puts the qualifier after the noun, the mirror image of English). Confirmed via a quick script against both the regex in isolation and the real provider that every exclusion phrase now falls through to no `MenuItem` match, while "manage its menu and daily dish specials"/"אפליקציה לניהול תפריט ומנות למסעדה" still correctly match.

**The test**: a new `heuristic.test.ts` test alongside the existing "dish" exclusion test, covering all four English UI-chrome phrasings plus the two Hebrew ones, and re-confirming the genuine restaurant phrasing (both languages) still matches.

**Verification**: confirmed failing cleanly without the fix and passing with it restored, via a `git stash push -- packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts` / run / `git stash pop` cycle. All 6 MenuItem-related `heuristic.test.ts` tests passed together, as did the full `@forge/spec-engine` suite (167 tests). Grepped every other apps/api/apps/web test file for "menu"/"תפריט" and confirmed none of the matches are spec-generation-related (UI-menu component tests and unrelated code comments only), so no other suite needed re-running. `apps/api`'s build (which bundles this shared package) ran clean.

**Status**: shipped and pushed, `packages/spec-engine/src/domainEntities.ts` + `packages/spec-engine/src/heuristic.test.ts` only -- this lives entirely in the shared spec-engine package; `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no spec-generation feature of its own at all, so there is no sibling to port this to.
